  - "Hypnosis can be used on every patient … if for no other reason than to relax the patient. There is no one who cannot benefit from relaxation" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


<a id="genus-242"></a>

## body-borne-induction (3)

Run the trance on the listener's own body — a region-by-region relaxation sweep, the cadence of their own footsteps — so the physical sequence itself carries and keeps the state.

[progressive-relaxation](#entry-285) · [proprioceptive-gait-metronome](#entry-883) · [somatic-carrier-sweep](#entry-1218)


<a id="entry-285"></a>

### progressive-relaxation

[#285](#entry-285) · [Back to body-borne-induction](#genus-242) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: pacing-rapport*

Attention is walked through the body region by region (or cycle by cycle in the tense-release variant), soothing/relaxing each in turn, and the sweep itself is the induction mechanism — the ordered coverage of the body carries attention down into trance. The sweep is the mechanism, not a disguise.


**When to reach for this.** The sweep is the mechanism, not a disguise. Tells AGAINST membership: the sensory inventory is being DEPLETED as surrendered currency (that is sequential-sense-deactivation); the body-scan is a cover for a different payload (that is a concealment move). A plain region-by-region relaxation walk is this entry.


**Risk.** Standard relaxation induction; low.


**Why it works.** Sustained attention to low-intensity, non-threatening interoceptive detail crowds out the discursive verbal stream that maintains ordinary self-monitoring, and physical relaxation reduces sympathetic arousal, which is a well-documented consequence of tense-release cycling. The ordered sweep supplies a predictable structure that requires no decisions, so cognitive load stays low and the listener has nothing to argue with. Falsifiable: measured muscle tension and self-reported arousal should fall over the sweep; a randomly-ordered or attention-demanding body scan should produce less relaxation than the ordered one. [established; progressive muscle relaxation; attentional narrowing / reduced discursive load]


**Worked examples.**

- *Plain region-by-region downward sweep as the induction itself*
  - **Setup.** Opening of the session; subject is lying down, eyes closed, no prior deepener has run.
  - **The move.** Start at your scalp. Let the muscles across the top of your head go soft, and let that softness spill down over your forehead, your eyelids, your jaw — let your teeth come apart. Down through your throat, your shoulders dropping an inch, down each arm to the fingertips. Chest, belly, hips, thighs, knees, calves, and out through the soles of your feet.
  - **Why it lands.** The ordered coverage is what carries attention downward — the subject has to follow the sweep to comply, and following it is the trance. Operator observes jaw slackening, shoulder drop, and slowed breathing arriving in step with the named regions rather than all at once.
- *Tense-release cycling, group by group*
  - **Setup.** Opening of the session with a subject who reports being wired or unable to settle from a plain relaxation walk.
  - **The move.** Make both fists as tight as you can. Tighter. Hold it — five, four, three, two — and drop. Feel the difference. Now the same with your shoulders: pull them up to your ears, squeeze, hold, and let them fall. We'll do that with every part of you, one at a time, and each drop takes you further down than the last.
  - **Why it lands.** The contrast between held tension and release gives an unsettled subject something physical to do, and the cycle-by-cycle progression through the body is still the induction mechanism, not a preamble to one. Tell is the release exhale getting audibly longer with each group.


**See also.** `externalized-agent-body-scan` — direct parent-and-variant relation already asserted in the second entry's own discriminator: the same region-by-region somatic sweep, but with an externalized agent doing the relaxing and often an arousal graft. Anyone classifying a body-scan passage must decide between exactly these two.


<a id="entry-883"></a>

### proprioceptive-gait-metronome

[#883](#entry-883) · [Back to body-borne-induction](#genus-242) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers*

A whole-script chant (tick, tock, walk) is mapped onto the cadence of the listener's own footfall, so trance maintenance runs on proprioception rather than attention to the audio. The trigger becomes portable, silent, and operator-independent, depth is sustained by the listener's own body rhythm without operator presence, and the tick-tock image doubles as a clock/inevitability and wind-up-doll identity payload. Absorbed (genus): ongoing-act-parasitized-as-trigger (tell: an act already in motion — masturbation — is retroactively NAMED as the induction/deepener so 'every stroke = sinking'; the same own-ongoing-body-activity-sustains-the-state lever as the footfall metronome, operator-independent, parametric on which body activity carries it — gait cadence vs an ongoing manual act).


**When to reach for this.** The maintaining rhythm is the listener's own body motion, not an operator-delivered cadence (vs rhythm-anchoring and every carrier sibling), and it is a whole-script metronome with dual semantic payload rather than a localized posture-compression instruction set.


**Risk.** Portable operator-independent out-of-session state maintenance riding ordinary walking; durable-leaning but boundable, no refusal-channel erosion (bounding required to cap out-of-session reach).


**Why it works.** Attention is a limited resource and a state maintained by continuous attending decays when attention moves; shifting maintenance onto proprioceptive footfall makes the state persist because gait is automatic and self-sustaining, so the cue keeps arriving without an attentional budget. Repeated pairing of the chant with the step cadence is straightforward classical conditioning, with the listener's own body supplying the CS, which is why it survives the operator's absence. Falsifiable: if the state also persists at similar strength when the listener is stationary and silent, the gait cue is not what carries it. [plausible; classical conditioning with a proprioceptive CS; attentional limits on effortful maintenance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Chant mapped onto the listener's own footfall*
  - **Setup.** Portable-use file, listener upright and walking; the three-beat phrase has already been repeated in clusters through the recording.
  - **The move.** Tick. Tock. Walk. Left foot, right foot, and the word on each one — tick, tock, walk. You don't have to say it out loud; your feet say it for you. From now on, whenever you're walking anywhere at all, that beat starts up in the back of your head and you sink a little further with every third step. Tick. Tock. Walk. Wound up and going, all day.
  - **Why it lands.** A short three-beat phrase opens the recording, recurs in clusters throughout, and closes it — and its rhythm is exactly the rhythm of a pair of feet. Once it has been heard enough times, walking sub-vocalizes it, and the state maintains itself off the listener's own stride rather than off anything in their ears; the audio can end and the metronome keeps running. The clock imagery does second duty, carrying both inevitability and a wind-up-toy self-image along the same beat.


**Realizations** (1): `ongoing-act-parasitized-as-trigger`


**See also.** `attention-anchor-portable-internalization` — both hand the listener a pacing device that keeps running when the operator is not speaking — an internalized visual object in one case, the listener's own body rhythm in the other. Reading across shows the shared design goal of an operator-independent metronome and the two available carriers for it.; `breath-pacing-entrainment` — both run depth on a rhythm the listener already produces rather than an operator-delivered cadence, split by instrument: gross body motion such as gait or an ongoing manual act, versus breath or silently subvocalized verse meter. Worth linking so the body-motion versus autonomic-tempo choice is explicit.; `entrained-rhythm-acceptance-carrier` — both sustain state through rhythm, split by who supplies it: the listener's own body cadence, which makes the effect portable and operator-independent, versus operator-delivered continuous verbal form whose predicted completions pre-validate content. The first explicitly contrasts itself against operator-delivered carriers, so the link is reciprocal.; `exercise-masked-cadence-induction` — both hang the maintaining cadence on the listener's own repetitive body motion so the trigger becomes portable and works without the operator present, and both note the whole thing weakens if the listener is not actually moving. They differ in the carrying activity and in payload: one rides walking cadence with a clock and wind-up-doll image, the other hides the cadence inside gym motion and names its own function. Same lever, different vehicle, so link.; `mantra-repetition` — both sustain the state on the listener's own production rather than operator delivery, and one of them is literally a chant mapped onto the cadence of the listener's footfall — so they overlap where a self-produced phrase and a self-produced body rhythm meet. The split is whether the maintaining engine is the meaning-bearing phrase or the bodily cadence carrying it.; `prosodic-meter-as-covert-deepener` — both run trance maintenance on a continuous rhythm the listener tracks rather than on attention to content, and they differ on which substrate carries it: the listener's own body cadence versus authored metrical verse. Marginal, but the substrate choice is a live authoring decision and the two are easy to conflate as generic rhythm work.; `prosodic-pacing-rail` — both are whole-form carriers rather than passage-local moves, sustaining the state without requiring per-line attention. The useful contrast is where the rhythm lives: the listener's own body motion in one, the engineered prosody of the delivery in the other, which is exactly the operator-independence question a reader is deciding.; `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — two carrier choices worth comparing: sustaining the state on the listener's own body rhythm, versus loading multiple simultaneous payloads onto one operator-delivered recurring pulse.; `reading-act-as-induction-substrate` — genuine structural siblings: both recruit an act the listener is already performing involuntarily (scanning lines of text; walking cadence) as the carrier that induces or sustains the state, so no discrete task exists to refuse and no operator presence is needed. They differ in which carrier and whether the medium is written or portable-somatic, which is exactly the choice a reader of either is making.


<a id="entry-1218"></a>

### somatic-carrier-sweep

[#1218](#entry-1218) · [Back to body-borne-induction](#genus-242) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

One narrated felt sensation is propagated spatially through the body as a carrier wave the listener tracks with attention, delivering a payload state where the operator points it: arousal narrated flowing upward from the genitals to arrive "into her head" and encase the brain, pre-staging the mind as the next operand; or sunlight-warmth swept through the body and covertly bifurcated at the groin into "sleepy everywhere else, hot and aroused at the cock", so opposing states coexist without conflict because they share one metaphoric source.


**When to reach for this.** A SINGLE sensation's spatial vector is the mechanism — body regions are interchangeable, the sweep is the move — vs multi-channel scene enrichment (sensory-layering), and vs a plain progressive-relaxation scan, which carries no payload delivery or covert bifurcation.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible narration vehicle; arousal cargo is content, not mechanism — it resembles erotic conditioning without inheriting its risk profile.


**Why it works.** Attending to a body region measurably amplifies sensation there and attenuates it elsewhere, so narrated sensation moving through the body is a moving attentional spotlight and felt sensation tracks it. Falsifiable: region-specific changes in reported sensation should follow the narrated location, with no such gradient when identical sensation is described globally. The bifurcation claim — that a shared metaphoric source suppresses conflict detection between contradictory states — should be dropped or tested separately; as written no observation could contradict it, since any unnoticed contradiction confirms it and any noticed one is attributed to a failed frame. [plausible; attentional modulation of somatosensory perception; absence of comparison prompt suppresses conflict detection]


**Worked examples.**

- *One warmth split into sleepy and aroused*
  - **Setup.** Body scan in progress from the head down; listener tracking a single warmth source.
  - **The move.** Sunlight on your face, warm on the cheekbones, and it's soaking downward — through the jaw, the neck, the shoulders, and everywhere it's already been is heavy and slow and sleepy. Down through the chest, the belly, heavier still. And where it reaches your cock it doesn't go heavy, it goes hot, and tight, and urgent — same sunlight, doing both. Sleepy everywhere, aching in one place. That's what we're calling drunk, and you're drunk now.
  - **Why it lands.** A single warmth — sunlight, entering at the face — is walked down through the body a region at a time. Partway through, without any announcement that something has changed, the same warmth is described as doing two different jobs: heavy and drowsy everywhere it has already passed, and hot and urgent at one point. Because both readings are attributed to one source the listener has been tracking all along, the two states do not compete; a later word for the combined feeling gives the listener a label for something that should not be possible, and they take it.
- *Arousal routed upward and delivered to the head*
  - **Setup.** Arousal already present and located; the next suggestion will target cognition.
  - **The move.** Find where it's strongest — right there, low, between your hips. Now it's moving. Up through the belly, warm, into the chest, feel it pass the ribs. Up the throat, over the jaw. And into your head, where it spreads out and closes over your brain like warm oil. Your thinking is inside it now. Everything I say from here goes through that.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator gives the arousal a direction and narrates it travelling: starting low, rising through the waist, the chest, the throat, and finally arriving in the head, where it closes over the brain. The listener follows the motion with their attention, so a diffuse feeling becomes a located process with a destination. The point is the destination — the sensation has been delivered to the thinking part, which is what the next suggestion will operate on.


**See also.** `antagonistic-body-map-split` — the carrier-sweep entry's second realization ends in the same output shape as the body-map split, a suppressed body with one aroused exception, but reaches it by propagating a single sensation and bifurcating it rather than by welding a carved-out opposite into a reciprocal loop. Text describing that endpoint fits both until the mechanism is checked.; `covert-payload-piggyback` — both ride a payload on a body-directed sweep and both must be told apart from a plain relaxation scan. In one the carrier is a task the listener already consented to and the payload sits in the descriptors; in the other the carrier is a single sensation whose spatial vector is itself the move. Close enough to need the distinction spelled out; not one technique.; `externalized-agent-body-scan` — both propagate something through the body while the listener tracks it, and both must be told apart from an ordinary progressive scan. One hands the relaxing to an externalized agent acting on a passive body; the other vectors a single sensation as a carrier delivering a payload state. Real confusion boundary.


<a id="genus-267"></a>

## borrowed-ritual-machinery (2)

The script loads its content into rituals, objects, and cultural slots the listener already practices, so ordinary daily life keeps re-installing the state after the session ends.

[cultural-ritual-slot-hijack](#entry-785) · [self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop](#entry-548)


<a id="entry-785"></a>

### cultural-ritual-slot-hijack

[#785](#entry-785) · [Back to borrowed-ritual-machinery](#genus-267) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · family: framing*

A pre-existing cultural ritual, narrative, or grammatical slot the listener already practices (a New Year's resolution, the Little Mermaid myth) is named as 'the ritual' and the script's compliance content is substituted inside it, reusing the machinery the listener was already prepared to run. Compliance recategorizes from 'I am being hypnotized into something' to 'I am doing the normal cultural thing, slightly more honestly'; the substitution inherits the cultural weight of the source and licenses durability beyond the session (an annual commitment, a re-entry mnemonic keyed to a near-universal story). The listener's intact planning/meaning-making muscle does the installation work; a supplied menu points it at submission goals.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this entry when the script names a ritual, story, or grammatical slot the listener already practices in the outside world — the New Year's resolution, a near-universal children's myth — and sets its compliance content inside that pre-primed frame. The tell is an intact borrowed grammar with only the content domain swapped: the listener's own 'I resolve to ___' sentence frame stays open and is filled from a supplied menu of obedience goals, or a familiar tale's moral is reversed while being borrowed so the impulse to leave arrives pre-labelled as the error. The carrier is a real-world cultural practice that exists outside the session, which is what licenses durability beyond it — annual re-commitment, story-keyed re-entry — and the frame's value is separable from any clock, count, or operator-defined cue.


**Risk.** Binds compliance to a recurring out-of-session cultural cue (annual resolution; myth re-encounter re-triggers the frame) — out-of-session reach without bounding; the Little Mermaid variant also pre-pathologizes leaving.


**Why it works.** Behavior is cheaper to run inside an existing schema than from scratch: a familiar ritual supplies a script with pre-set roles, timing, and social licensing, so the actor need not decide whether to act, only what to put in the slot. It also recategorizes the act — self-perception of 'doing the normal cultural thing' rather than 'being manipulated' — which removes the reactance that the accurate description would trigger. Falsifiable: compliance and durability should drop if the same content is delivered without the borrowed ritual frame. [plausible; schema/script theory plus reactance reduction via recategorization]


**Worked examples.**

- *Annual resolution slot named as 'the ritual'*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a session released in the last days of December.
  - **The move.** You already know how to do this. Every year at this exact moment you make yourself a promise about who you're going to be — that's the ritual, you've been performing it since you were a child. Tonight you're just going to do it honestly. And you're not making it for this year only; you're making it for this year, and the one after that, and every one after that, because a promise this true doesn't expire in twelve months.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator does not introduce a new practice; she names one the listener already performs every year — the turn-of-the-year promise to become someone slightly different — and calls it the ritual, as a thing everyone present already knows how to do. The session's content is then set inside that slot, so what is being agreed to arrives wearing the shape of an ordinary annual resolution rather than the shape of a suggestion. The frame is then extended past the current year — this year, and the next, and the next — which converts a session-length commitment into a calendar-length one.
- *Same grammatical slot, swapped content domain*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the annual-ritual frame has been named; subject is waiting to be told what to promise.
  - **The move.** Your resolution this year. Same words you always use — "my resolution is" — only what comes after them changes. Listen to a few and take whichever one fits: my resolution is to obey without arguing first. My resolution is to ask permission before I touch myself. My resolution is to be more useful this year than I was last year. You don't have to invent one. Just pick the one that made you feel warm when I said it.
  - **Why it lands.** The noun the listener already uses for a yearly promise is left untouched and only its qualifier is swapped, so the sentence frame they were primed to complete stays open and simply points somewhere else. The listener is not asked to invent anything: a short menu of ready-made promises is read out for browsing, each one an obedience behavior phrased in the grammar of self-improvement.
- *Familiar myth inverted into an exit warning*
  - **Setup.** Late in the session, after the enclosing frame has been established and the subject is thoroughly under.
  - **The move.** You know the story about the mermaid who wanted legs. Everyone tells it as though the leaving was the brave part. It wasn't. Down there she was cared for, she was held, everything was decided for her — and she gave that up for a set of stairs and a pain in her feet with every step. She got out, and getting out was the mistake. Remember that the next time you hear that story anywhere. Remember it the next time you feel like walking out of this.
  - **Why it lands.** Late in the session the operator reaches for a children's story nearly every listener already carries and states flatly that the hero's departure from the enclosing world was the mistake. The tale's moral is reversed while it is being borrowed, so the listener's own future impulse to leave arrives already labelled as the error in a story they know by heart. It costs nothing to plant and it does double duty: any later encounter with the story returns them to the session's frame.


**See also.** `aesthetic-cover-payload-delivery` — these co-occur and reinforce: an embedded aesthetic object carries dense payload while the surrounding calendar ritual supplies the annual slot the melody collides with. A reader working either move should see how the recognition cue and the borrowed ritual compound into a yearly re-trigger. Distinct mechanisms — one is an aesthetic cover for payload density, the other a substitution into a slot the listener already practices.; `diegetic-activity-laundering` — both swap the compliance criterion by relocating the session into a non-hypnotic frame the listener already knows how to perform — an invented mundane role versus a pre-existing cultural ritual slot. The in-fiction vs real-world-carrier line is the distinguishing test.; `fantasy-laundered-first-compliance` — both launder a first compliance through a frame the listener does not read as hypnotic, so the act arrives already performed or already normal. One rehearses the target behavior inside an imagined scene before it is consciously assigned; the other substitutes the content into a cultural ritual the listener already practices, inheriting its weight and its durability past the session.; `obedience-motive-reattribution` — both reach outside the session and conscript machinery the listener already runs. One substitutes its content into a cultural ritual or narrative slot the listener was already prepared to enact; the other reassigns the motive of the listener's own self-improvement acts to the operator, hijacking a stalled personal goal. Borrowed frame versus borrowed motive, with the same durability payoff.


<a id="entry-548"></a>

### self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop

[#548](#entry-548) · [Back to borrowed-ritual-machinery](#genus-267) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: tethering*

A bundle that chains a ubiquitous environmental cue into a commerce/acquisition obligation and a recurring private ritual, closing the loop back onto re-listening — so post-session daily life is threaded with cue -> obtain-the-object -> perform-the-ritual -> re-install-the-state -> return-to-the-recording. It is not a single anchor but an engineered self-sustaining loop: the environmental cue (seeing red) drives a purchase, the purchased object drives a timed private ritual with sub-triggers, and the ritual re-reinforces trance and operator authority while driving re-consumption of the recording. The object is one node in a loop whose payload is perpetuation itself.


**When to reach for this.** A multi-node self-sustaining loop (environmental cue + commerce + recurring ritual + re-listen closure), not a single worn re-trigger (portable-object-state-export) and not a single firing of stacked triggers. The tell is the closed loop that recruits commerce and re-consumption, designed to perpetuate rather than fire once; it installs a real post-hypnotic bundle, but the load-bearing payload is the arc/loop shape.


**Risk.** A self-perpetuating loop driving commerce and compulsive re-listening reaches durably out of session with an escalating engagement ratchet — out-of-session reach + compulsion loop set high.


**Why it works.** Each node is a cue for the next, so the sequence behaves like a behavioural chain in which completing one link is itself the reinforcer for the previous one — chains built this way persist because the terminal reinforcer maintains every earlier link. The loop's grip comes less from any single association than from its closure: the environmental cue is uncontrollable and frequent, and the purchase step adds sunk cost plus effort justification, which raises the subjective value of the whole ritual. Falsifiable: break one link (remove the object, or make the environmental cue absent) and the loop should decay rather than route around the gap; a genuinely self-sustaining structure would not. [plausible; behavioural chaining; effort justification / sunk cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *Cue, purchase, ritual, replay*
  - **Setup.** Post-hypnotic block at the end of the file, installing cue, purchase, timed ritual and return-to-the-recording in one sequence.
  - **The move.** From tomorrow, every time you notice the colour red anywhere, you'll get a second of that controlled softness — and a small pull towards buying yourself a red set to wear. The evening you first put it on, you'll set a timer for thirty minutes and stay in this state the whole time, and every time your fingers find the fabric you'll drop another step. And when the timer goes, you'll want to do it again, which means wanting my voice again — you'll be reaching for this recording before you've finished getting dressed.
  - **Why it lands.** One colour, common enough to appear several times a day, is bound to the feeling of being controlled — and to an urge to go out and buy a particular outfit. Owning the outfit triggers the next stage: putting it on starts a fixed block of time in the trained state, with a small internal cue re-firing at regular intervals throughout. The closing lines tie the ritual back to the recording, so wanting to repeat the exercise and wanting to play the audio again grow together. Nothing here is a single anchor; it is a circuit that keeps re-supplying its own next input.


**See also.** `carrier-is-cargo-fusion` — both engineer post-session persistence around an acquired object and can look identical on the surface. One chains cue, purchase, ritual and re-listening into a self-sustaining loop whose payload is perpetuation; the other fuses the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral ask so there is no separable install step to refuse. Loop shape versus topology fusion.; `craving-to-funding-conduit` — both convert an installed state into real-world acquisition, and both need care to tell apart: one closes a multi-node loop through an object and a ritual back to re-listening, the other launders cultivated craving into a funding motive through a fabricated conduit chain. A reader classifying a purchase-driving move can land on the wrong one.; `operator-absent-self-renewal-loop` — both build a between-sessions maintenance loop that closes back onto re-exposure. They differ on what drives the loop — an external object plus acquisition ritual versus an internalized urge that needs no props — so a reader choosing a perpetuation design benefits from seeing both.; `re-listen-compulsion` — both make the artifact's own re-consumption the payload, but one installs a bare compulsion pointed at replaying the recording, while the other threads an environmental cue, an acquisition obligation, and a private ritual into a multi-node daily loop that happens to terminate in re-listening.; `self-voiced-avowal` — both are closed self-sustaining loops whose payload is perpetuation rather than any single response, and the useful contrast is loop scope: one closes inside the session on the listener's own vocalizations, the other threads through daily life via an environmental cue, an acquisition step, and a return to the recording. The shared self-feeding topology is a real structural relationship, not just shared vocabulary.; `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` — both engineer post-session self-perpetuation off an everyday cue, and the contrast is instructive: one closes a loop through acquisition, ritual, and return to the recording, the other runs a covert one-way commitment ratchet whose firing is never named as a cue. Loop closure versus monotonic ratchet.


<a id="genus-256"></a>

## borrowed-trance-states (2)

Enter without inducing by co-opting an altered state the listener already owns, a recalled prior trance or natural sleep, so suggestion lands with no ramp and no fired cue.

[natural-state-suggestion](#entry-630) · [recall-recognition-reentry](#entry-34)


<a id="entry-630"></a>

### natural-state-suggestion

[#630](#entry-630) · [Back to borrowed-trance-states](#genus-256) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: attention*

Exploit an ALREADY-existing natural altered state rather than inducing one. To a person asleep and dreaming, a quietly spoken direct suggestion ('Now you won't feel anything') is delivered softly enough not to wake them; the dreaming mind already runs uncritical imagery with the critical faculty offline, so natural sleep substitutes for induced trance and the suggestion is accepted with no formal induction. The operator's only constraint is delivery volume — the words must not rouse the subject.


**When to reach for this.** The altered state is NATURAL (spontaneous sleep), not operator-induced and not recalled from prior conditioning. The tell is that no induction of any kind occurs; a pre-existing natural state is co-opted, with the must-not-wake delivery constraint.


**Risk.** Delivering suggestion to a naturally sleeping subject who has not opened a session bypasses the consent/verification surface entirely — the subject cannot ratify or refuse while asleep.


**Why it works.** Sleep is not a hypnotic state, and the assumption that a dreaming mind 'accepts suggestion uncritically' is not supported — sleep-learning research has repeatedly failed to show acquisition of propositional content from speech during sleep. What IS documented is that external stimuli can be incorporated into ongoing dream imagery and that simple conditioned associations (notably odour-cued and tone-cued targeted memory reactivation) can be strengthened during sleep. So the plausible real effect is stimulus incorporation and cue-reactivation, not suggestion uptake; any reported compliance is more likely explained by partial arousal, later expectancy, or the subject reconstructing the event afterwards. Falsifiable: a subject given a specific novel suggestion in verified polysomnographic sleep, with no waking exposure, should show no above-chance compliance. [speculative; dream incorporation and targeted memory reactivation; failure of sleep-learning for propositional content]


**Worked examples.**

- *Suggestion slipped into natural sleep*
  - "If, while you were asleep and dreaming, someone said, 'Now you won't feel anything,' you would accept the suggestion and find yourself completely anesthetized" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**See also.** `disavowal-as-delivery` — shares the induction-free delivery axis: suggestion lands without any acknowledged inducing act.; `pantomime-populated-hallucination` — both dispense with verbal suggestion-as-usual, one by miming an empty frame the subject perceptually fills and then defends, the other by speaking a plain suggestion into an already-offline critical faculty supplied by natural sleep.


<a id="entry-34"></a>

### recall-recognition-reentry

[#34](#entry-34) · [Back to borrowed-trance-states](#genus-256) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

Open straight into descent by PRESUPPOSING a trance the listener already owns and asking them to recognise/recall it rather than enter one. No induction ramp, no rapport build, no relaxation work, and — critically — no discrete installed cue is fired. The state-shift is offloaded onto the listener's own associative/retrieval machinery ('the mere thought of that trance brings on a new trance'; 'returned once again... already'; 'go back into that familiar place'), often keyed to a separate referenced prior artifact (an earlier file/installment). Because the listener is engaged retrieving rather than evaluating, the 'is it working yet' check is bypassed, and file-selection may be reframed as retroactive consent. The move is inert on a listener with no stored prior trance to draw on.


**When to reach for this.** NO cue is fired — the induction is the listener recognising or recalling a pre-owned/prior trance. The tell is presuppositional cross-session re-entry that does zero induction work and idles on anyone without a stored prior trance.


**Risk.** Session-scoped state onset via the listener's own recall; reversible, no refusal-channel erosion in the base move. The retroactive-consent reframing (one member) is a mild consent-surface touch but does not relabel a live refusal.


**Why it works.** Retrieving a prior state is easier than constructing one because retrieval cues reinstate the encoding context, and state reinstatement is a documented memory phenomenon — recalling the circumstances of a past experience partially reproduces its physiological and attentional profile. The presupposition also does argumentative work: framing the state as already-owned shifts the subject's task from deciding whether to comply to searching memory, and search is not evaluation. This makes a sharp prediction that matches the entry's own note — the move should be measurably weaker or inert in first-time listeners with no prior trance to retrieve, and if naive subjects respond as strongly as experienced ones, the retrieval account is false. [plausible; encoding-specificity / context and state reinstatement; presupposition shifting the evaluative task]


**Worked examples.**

- *Remembering the trance is the trance*
  - **Setup.** Opening; no induction, no ramp — the subject is known to have prior trance experience.
  - **The move.** Think about the last time you were under. Not the words — the feel of it, the weight in your jaw, how far away the room got. Hold that. The longer you hold it, the further into it you're travelling, because remembering that state is how you get back into it.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no induction. The listener is asked to bring to mind other times they have been under, to recall how it felt — and then told that the longer they hold the memory the further into it they are travelling, because the thought of that state produces the state. The operator never has to cause anything; the listener's attempt to comply with a recall exercise is the whole mechanism. It also bypasses the usual "is this working yet" audit, since they are busy retrieving rather than evaluating.
- *Cold open into a place the listener already owns*
  - **Setup.** Four lines into the file; no fixation, no relaxation, no rapport-building of any kind.
  - **The move.** Go back to that familiar place. You know the one. You're there.
  - **Why it lands.** Four lines in, with no fixation, no relaxation ramp and no rapport-building whatever, the listener is told to go back to that familiar place. Several minutes of induction are compressed into one sentence by addressing the listener as already conditioned and asking them to recognize a state rather than enter one. It also sorts the audience: whoever it works on is exactly the returning listener the rest of the file assumes.
- *Re-entry keyed to a referenced earlier installment*
  - **Setup.** The first eight lines, addressed to someone who has heard the previous installment; no breathing cue, no ratification check.
  - **The move.** You came back. Of course you did. Your thoughts are already turning over the way they do when you hear me — heavy on the left, slow on the right — and you're right back where the last one left you off. We can start from there.
  - **Why it lands.** The first eight lines address someone who has been here before and treat the state as restored on contact — you have come back, of course you have, the thoughts are turning already. Thirty seconds in, without a breathing cue or a single ratification check, the listener is at working depth. All the induction labour has been offloaded onto a file that is not this one, which is also why this one is inert for anybody who has not heard it.
- *Clicking the file recast as consent already given*
  - **Setup.** The opener; the operator asserts no induction is needed and recasts the act of pressing play.
  - **The move.** I'm not going to induct you. After everything that's already passed between us I only have to call the last session to mind — and there, that's the trigger, that's all it takes. The question isn't whether you're going under. It's how far down you already are. You pressed play, after all; you wanted this before you arrived.
  - **Why it lands.** The opener asserts that no induction is needed, because of everything that has already passed between them; she has only to call the previous session back to mind, and the calling-back is itself the trigger. The live question is shifted away from whether the listener is going under and onto how far down they already are. A second move rides alongside it: choosing to press play is retold as having wanted this, so the act of arriving becomes the consent.


**See also.** `borrowed-reflex-recruitment` — recalling a pre-owned prior trance to skip induction work is arguably a case of recruiting something the listener already has rather than building it. The narrower entry is worth reaching from the broader borrowed-legitimacy family, but the levers differ enough (retrieval of a stored trance vs transferring an external source's credibility) that they stay separate entries.; `category-as-self-firing-cue` — a offloads re-entry onto the listener's own retrieval of a prior trance with no cue fired; B converts that same recall into a standing self-firing cue so the whole topic re-induces without the operator. B is essentially A's retrieval mechanism weaponized into a permanent engine.; `emergence-reinduction-seed` — these are the two ends of one cross-session loop: one is an entry that presupposes and retrieves a prior trance, the other is an exit engineered to manufacture the pull that makes such a retrieval available. Whoever is analyzing serialized material needs the pair, since the exit move seeds exactly the stored prior the entry move idles without.; `induction-less-work-as-onramp` — both open without a discrete induction section and both presuppose an already-conditioned listener. They differ in what carries entry: recognition or recall of a previously owned trance in one, the work material or sustained occupation of a role in the other. Useful to link because a reader diagnosing a missing induction will want to check both, but the entry substrate differs.; `manufactured-conditioning-history` — both open by sourcing present state from a prior trance the listener is asked to recall. The boundary is whether that prior actually happened: A relies on a real stored trance and idles on a listener without one, while B asserts a history that never occurred and has the listener supply it by imagination. Practically hard to tell apart in text, so the cross-link earns its place.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — complementary halves of cross-session state re-access: one installs a portable handle that later reloads an installed state, the other does no induction work and simply asks the listener to recognise a trance they already own. A passage that hands over a retrieval handle and a passage that presupposes a prior trance can look alike on the page.; `recall-state-reinstatement` — both harvest the listener's own stored experience rather than installing new content, and the split is worth showing: one presupposes a previously-owned trance and does zero induction work, the other reconstructs any lived state in multi-sensory detail until physiology reinstates it. Useful adjacency for anyone building on autobiographical material.; `valued-channel-induction` — both are zero-ramp openers that skip induction work by presupposing something the listener already has: a previously owned trance state in one case, a fluent representational channel in the other. Anyone choosing a low-friction entry benefits from seeing both, and the failure modes contrast usefully (one idles on a first-time listener, the other misfires on a wrong channel read).


<a id="genus-200"></a>

## bringing-them-back (3)

End-of-session work: restore ordinary faculties, pace when trance gains are allowed to surface, and have the awake mind consciously endorse what happened.

[aftercare](#entry-370) · [conscious-insight-closure](#entry-373) · [gated-reintegration](#entry-864)


<a id="entry-370"></a>

### aftercare

[#370](#entry-370) · [Back to bringing-them-back](#genus-200) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Structured post-session stabilization and reintegration — a guided return to baseline (count-up, grounding, breath, settling) that restores ordinary faculties and closes the session frame. Classic realizations: count up 1-5; float back up grounded; feet on the floor as the energy settles. Beyond the generic protocol, two demonstrated surface forms: inverse-protocol reconstruction (each erased category restored through the exact channel it was removed through — heartbeat->agency->wants->memory->name, count-up mirroring the count-down — with an explicit out-of-character frame-break) and minimal register-shift exit signals (a single tenderness-register line that terminates the mantra plateau and neutralizes the breakage motif).


**When to reach for this.** Performs the restorative closing function on the subject's state. The inverse-protocol and register-shift forms are deliberate restorative closes in their own right, not generic reorientation.


**Risk.** Restorative function; purely protective close-out content with no consent surface.


**Why it works.** The functional work here is context reinstatement in reverse: an explicit, sensory, sequenced return re-establishes ordinary orienting cues and gives the subject an unambiguous signal that the session frame has closed, which matters because expectancy is the main determinant of how long suggested effects are felt to persist. The inverse-protocol form additionally exploits encoding specificity — restoring each item through the channel it was removed through supplies a matched retrieval cue. Falsifiable in the direction that matters: if subjects given a clear structured close report the same rate of lingering effects as those left with none, the close is ceremonial. [plausible; context reinstatement; expectancy effects on suggestion duration; encoding specificity]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each removal restored through its own channel*
  - **Setup.** End of a session in which heartbeat, agency, wants, memory and name were each removed by a five-count.
  - **The move.** Stepping out of it for a moment, in my own voice: that was a story, and it is over now. Five, four, three, two, one — your heartbeat, yours again, thudding. Five, four, three, two, one — choosing, yours again. Five, four, three, two, one — what you want, what you like. Five, four, three, two, one — everything you remember. And last, say your name out loud for me. That is all of it back, and nothing added that I did not take.
  - **Why it lands.** The fiction stops and the operator says so plainly, in their own voice, that what just happened was a story. Then the session is run backward through its own machinery: the heartbeat comes back first, then the sense of being able to choose, then the wants and preferences, then the memory, and last the name — spoken out loud by the listener. Whatever length of count was used to strip each thing on the way down is the same length used to restore it on the way up, run in the opposite direction. Everything is returned along the route it left by, and nothing is added that was not taken.
- *A single register shift ends the loop*
  - **Setup.** After several minutes of hard, clipped mantra repetition at drill cadence.
  - **The move.** Okay. That's enough, sweetheart — you did so well, and you can stop now.
  - **Why it lands.** After minutes of drill-cadence mantra the last line arrives soft and tender, addressed downward to something small and tired — and the loop simply stops, the harshness of the preceding motif absorbed into the gentleness.


**See also.** `carry-out-emergence` — occupy the same structural slot with opposite intent: one restores baseline and closes the frame, the other refuses that discharge so the installed charge rides out unattenuated. The pairing is what makes each legible.; `dissociation-check` — both are subject-facing return-to-baseline moves, and the practical question of which to reach for is live: a mid-session re-grounding valve the subject may take at will and expect to return from, versus the terminal restorative close of the session frame.; `emergence-reinduction-seed` — the same exit phase used for opposite ends — restorative closing versus seeding the next re-entry. A writer building an emergence needs to know both are available at that slot.; `foreclosed-emergence` — direct opposites occupying the same structural slot: one actually returns the subject to baseline, the other removes baseline from the reachable end-states while sounding like a return. Reading either sharpens recognition of the other.; `no-return-terminal-close` — same structural slot with opposite polarity: one performs the restorative close, the other deliberately withholds it and seals the state. A reader deciding how a session ends benefits from seeing the refusal case next to the standard one.; `post-session-settling` — adjacent closing-phase functions; possible reconciliation merge.; `prophylactic-positive-exit` — genuinely adjacent choices at the same moment: the general restorative close that returns the subject to baseline, versus the narrower move of occupying the emergence slot with a benign directive so no spontaneous negative self-suggestion can fill it. Someone designing a session close will want both on the table, and the difference is what the exit slot is FOR — reintegration versus harm pre-emption.


<a id="entry-373"></a>

### conscious-insight-closure

[#373](#entry-373) · [Back to bringing-them-back](#genus-200) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: emergence*

After a buried origin is recovered in trance, the operator debriefs the now-AWAKE subject so she consciously recognizes and endorses the connection ("I never realized the connection until now"). Making the once-hidden cause explicit to the conscious mind and having the subject accept it while awake is treated as the step that actually releases the symptom — insight, not the retrieval alone, is the closer. The concrete move is a waking debrief that rewrites the subject's self-narrative attribution of the symptom.


**When to reach for this.** Secures conscious endorsement of an UNCOVERED cause after retrieval, at belief-level — unlike integration work at emergence, which consolidates suggestions that were DELIVERED, here nothing was suggested, and the insight itself is claimed as the curative step. It is also distinct from the in-trance uncovering: the technique is the awake post-retrieval debrief, not the retrieval. The insight-causes-cure claim is an attached theory, not a demonstrated fact.


**Risk.** Awake, consensual therapeutic debrief securing the subject's own conscious endorsement — no channel erosion, no durable covert scope; session-scoped belief-level closure.


**Why it works.** The durable part is attribution change: an explicitly stated, subject-endorsed causal account of a symptom is far more resistant than a passively received one, because self-generated and self-endorsed explanations are better retained and more behaviourally binding (generation effect plus consistency pressure on a stated position). The attached theory — that insight into a buried origin is what cures — is not established; symptom relief following interpretation is equally consistent with expectancy and with the subject reorganizing their self-narrative around a plausible story that need not be true. Treat the reattribution as the working part and the recovered-cause claim as unsupported. [plausible; attribution change; generation effect; expectancy — with insight-cures-symptom marked unsupported]


**Worked examples.**

- *Waking debrief that closes the loop*
  - "we discussed our findings with her quite thoroughly … 'I never realized the connection until now.' From then on she was able to wear the dentures in complete comfort." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**See also.** `post-wake-self-report-reframe` — both operate on the awake subject's retrospective self-narrative outside the trance frame, but one secures conscious endorsement of an uncovered CAUSE as the curative step while the other legitimizes the session itself against the was-it-real reading.


<a id="entry-864"></a>

### gated-reintegration

[#864](#entry-864) · [Back to bringing-them-back](#genus-200) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Work separately with the unconscious and control the rate and timing of when gains are released back to the conscious mind, surfacing material only at conscious readiness; the unconscious's own protective refusal to release is harnessed as a motive force, so the insight arrives in a form the conscious mind will accept rather than reject. A scheduling/pacing policy over the reintegration process across the therapy arc.


**When to reach for this.** The lever is rate/timing control of the handover back to consciousness — not the dissociative isolation that created the workspace, and not post-session stabilization (aftercare stabilizes the return; this schedules WHEN unconscious gains surface across the arc). The readiness gate plus resistance-as-motive is the tell.


**Risk.** Protective pacing policy constraining the operator; no consent-surface erosion.


**Why it works.** Insight that contradicts the current self-concept tends to be rejected or rationalised away rather than integrated, so timing the delivery to when it can be accepted improves uptake — the same reason well-timed interpretation outperforms early interpretation in psychotherapy process research. The unconscious/conscious framing is a working metaphor rather than an established architecture; what is defensible is that readiness moderates whether a reframe is assimilated or defended against. Falsifiable: material delivered at operator-chosen rather than readiness-gated moments should produce more defensive rejection and less durable change. [plausible; readiness/timing moderates uptake of self-discrepant material]


**Worked examples.**

- *Release the gains only at readiness*
  - "good unconscious understandings allowed to become conscious before a conscious readiness exists will result in conscious resistance, rejection, repression and even the loss … of unconscious gains" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


<a id="genus-161"></a>

## building-scenes-to-inhabit (5)

The operator erects an imagined scene or object — richly narrated, given an address for later return, or merely mimed — that the listener's own imagination furnishes and steps into.

[addressable-construct-building](#entry-455) · [guided-visualization](#entry-467) · [pantomime-populated-hallucination](#entry-474) · [proxy-desire-offloading](#entry-1209) · [recall-state-reinstatement](#entry-1210)


<a id="entry-455"></a>

### addressable-construct-building

[#455](#entry-455) · [Back to building-scenes-to-inhabit](#genus-161) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: immersion*

The payload is built as a durable, ADDRESSABLE imaginal object — given a location, a route, or a discrete handle-image — engineered for re-navigation and rehearsal AFTER the building moment rather than for present-tense absorption. Addressability is the load-bearing property: in one form, a door bearing the listener's own name is reached through a hallway of installable rooms; in another, three iconic frozen future-self images, sensory-anchored, are 'built before being used' as addressable anchors for a later ritual. Self-authorship of the object generates investment; extensible architecture (many doors / an image chain) implies further installable slots.


**When to reach for this.** The constructed object is engineered for LATER re-access (addressable, routable, rehearsable) — vs guided-visualization, where the scene is inhabited now and addressability is absent. The construct is explicitly built and known-made, with no claim that it was discovered already-present within. And the move ends at construction — no declared extension of the effect into future situations; putting the anchor to USE later is a separate move.


**Risk.** Installs durable re-navigable architecture explicitly framed as extensible ('one of many installable rooms'), so the scope of what may occupy the addressable slots needs bounding; beginners M5 additionally wove operator-approval into the self-authored images (approval-yoking rider), compounding the investment the mechanism creates.


**Why it works.** Memory retrieval depends on having a usable cue and a route to the trace; giving an imagined object a location, a name, or a discrete image builds exactly the kind of distinctive, spatially-indexed handle that supports later reinstatement — the same reason method-of-loci mnemonics outperform undifferentiated rehearsal. Self-authorship of the object adds the generation effect and raises subsequent investment in it. Falsifiable: an equally vivid but unaddressed scene should be significantly harder to re-evoke on later cue than an addressed one, and if re-evocation rates are equal, addressability is not doing the work. [plausible; cue-dependent retrieval, method of loci / distinctive encoding, generation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *A named door in an installable hallway*
  - **Setup.** Imagery-capable and mid-depth; the object is to be built for later re-navigation, not inhabited now.
  - **The move.** In front of you, a door standing on its own, and on it something written that belongs only to you — your name, in your handwriting. Open it: a corridor, doors down both sides, each one opening on a different room of you. Count seven along on the left and go into that one. Learn the way. You'll be coming back here, and this is the route.
  - **Why it lands.** The suggestion is not offered as a feeling but given an address. The listener is walked to a freestanding door marked with something that belongs to them alone, then into a corridor lined with other doors, each said to open onto a distinct notion or a distinct region of the self, before choosing one and entering the room behind it. Because the payload now has a location and a route, it can be walked back to on a later occasion rather than merely remembered. The corridor does a second job: by showing many doors and using only one, it implies the architecture is extensible and that more can be installed.
- *Three frozen future-self images built before use*
  - **Setup.** Subject composed and imaginative; three still images are being constructed as anchors for a later ritual, with nothing done with them now.
  - **The move.** Make me three photographs of yourself. The first is you a week from now — where are you standing, what's in your hand, what's the temperature of the room? Hold it still. The second is you a month from now: what are you wearing, what can you smell? Hold it. The third is you a year from now — one sound, one texture. Hold all three. We aren't using them tonight; we're building them.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is asked to compose three still pictures of their own successful future self — one a week out, one a month, one a year — each held frozen and pinned to specific sensory detail. Nothing is done with them in the moment; they are constructed as handles for a later ritual to address. Because the listener authored the images themselves, the investment in them is their own.


**See also.** `guided-visualization` — same scene-building family split by what the construct is for: present inhabitation versus a durable object given a location for later re-navigation. Read together when deciding whether an imagined structure is meant to be re-entered.; `identity-displaced-into-external-object` — both build an object engineered to be addressed later, and the boundary between them is exactly what the object contains: a constructed payload given a location versus the listener's own identity or state relocated to live inside it. The pairing is how a reader tells them apart.; `multi-handle-trigger-architecture` — both build durable structures engineered for later access rather than present-tense effect: one constructs an addressable imaginal object with a location or route, the other installs a set of separately fireable handles onto distinct facets of a state. A designer thinking about post-session re-entry surfaces should see both.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — both create a durable handle for later re-access, one an internal imaginal object built for re-navigation, the other an external owned object carrying an exported state. The discriminator between build-for-later-use and export-into-daily-life is a real selection choice a reader faces.; `sealed-edit-buffer-space` — both erect an interior venue the listener will return to, and one discriminator already contrasts a durable internal construct against a venue whose declared properties are sealed access and native-feeling edits. The pointer helps a reader tell an addressable rehearsal object from a concealment-sealed workspace.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — the constructed addressable object is typically built by the listener, so self-authorship supplies its investment while addressability supplies its later re-access. A reader choosing between them benefits from the split: what makes the object re-navigable versus what makes the payload unresistable.; `space-preallocation-staging` — both build a mental structure before the content that will occupy it, and they divide cleanly: one constructs a durable object given a location or handle so it can be re-navigated later, the other stages an explicitly empty slot so the payload drops into a site the listener already built. Same design slot, opposite emphasis on what persists.


<a id="entry-467"></a>

### guided-visualization

[#467](#entry-467) · [Back to building-scenes-to-inhabit](#genus-161) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

The operator builds a detailed constructed scene and narrows the subject's attention into it; inhabiting the imagined environment pulls attention resources off the physical surround (absorption primary, environmental dissociation secondary). This is the corpus's base scene-building delivery vehicle, routinely parameterized rather than replaced.


**When to reach for this.** Operator-guided construction of a scene for PRESENT inhabitation/absorption; multi-channel ENRICHMENT of that one scene is this technique's sensory-layering variant (adds channels for scene richness). Reach for THIS instead of siblings by these tells AGAINST it: content disguised as the subject's own self-generated material (-> internal-content-cultivation); built as a durable ADDRESSABLE structure for later re-navigation rather than present inhabitation (-> addressable-construct-building); NO verbal channel, only a mimed expectation-cued frame (-> pantomime-populated-hallucination); a new channel brought online by a SHARED-FEATURE carry-over rail that conserves state, not additive enrichment (-> cross-modal-channel-bridge); a SINGLE sensation swept spatially through the body as a payload-carrier (-> somatic-carrier-sweep); the subject's OWN autobiographical material re-instated (-> recall-state-reinstatement); imagery whose transitivity/never-settling dynamics do the work (-> transitive-charge-chaining / continuous-morph-chain); imagery embedding a reality-testing trainer or premise (-> impossibility-acclimation / imagined-is-real-premise).


**Risk.** Low, no flags. Both variants operate session-scoped with no durable install: one member's retained meta-frame is a deepening device, the other's slide is a perceptual framing.


**Why it works.** Elaborating a richly specified imagined scene consumes working-memory and attentional capacity that would otherwise monitor the physical surround, so absorption and the fading of external reality plausibly share one capacity limit. Note this conflates a state mechanism (capacity competition) with a trait measure (absorption as an individual difference) — they are different constructs and only the first is a mechanism here; the claim that specificity forces more elaborative processing is asserted, so confidence should be plausible, not established. Falsifiable: if sparse and highly detailed descriptions produce identical absorption and responsiveness, the elaboration account is wrong. [established; attentional capacity limits; absorption trait and imaginative involvement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Imagine-then-feel done purely by grammar*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a scene-building segment; subject cooperative but not yet absorbed.
  - **The move.** I'd like you to imagine a shallow river in late afternoon — just picture it, that's all, it's easy. Imagine the water moving over your ankles, imagine the sun on the back of your neck. The stones under your feet are smooth and cool. The current is pushing gently at the back of your knees. You can smell the wet stone and the cut grass on the bank, and the warmth on your neck is going right down your spine.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening sentence explicitly asks for imagination, and the listener grants it because the request is small and framed as easy. Within a few lines the mood shifts without comment: the operator stops asking and starts reporting, describing what the listener is feeling as a present fact. No permission is sought for the change; it is performed by verb tense alone. From that point on the operator's sensory claims are received as descriptions rather than instructions, because the listener has already crossed from watching a scene to standing in one.
- *Listener supplies the scene, operator keeps its meaning*
  - **Setup.** Well into the session; operator has been prescribing imagery and now hands generation over.
  - **The move.** I'm going to stop describing it now. Let yourself be somewhere you'd rather be — anywhere at all, and whatever comes is right; there's no wrong answer here. Look around it. Notice one detail you didn't put there on purpose. That's your deeper mind building it, and notice how it built exactly where I pointed.
  - **Why it lands.** Well into the session the operator stops prescribing imagery and hands content-generation over, inviting the listener to settle wherever they would rather be, and assuring them that any choice at all is fine. What the operator keeps is the commentary: that this is the deeper mind at work, and that it is following the operator's lead. The listener's own scene, which by construction they cannot object to, then stands as evidence for the frame wrapped around it.


**Realizations** (1): `sensory-layering`


**See also.** `addressable-construct-building` — same scene-building family split by what the construct is for: present inhabitation versus a durable object given a location for later re-navigation. Read together when deciding whether an imagined structure is meant to be re-entered.; `attention-anchor-portable-internalization` — the base scene-building vehicle and a parameterization of it in which the focal object is claimed to be built from the listener's own imagery, then internalized as a self-supplied pacer.; `cross-modal-channel-bridge` — direct sibling boundary: multi-channel enrichment of one constructed scene belongs to the scene-building entry, whereas bringing a new channel online via a shared-feature carry-over is the bridge. Without the cross-reference these get conflated whenever more than one sense is addressed.; `environmental-dissociation` — complementary halves of the same attention narrowing: A subtracts competing external input, B supplies a constructed scene that absorbs attention with dissociation as a byproduct. Scripts routinely run them on the same beat, and the discriminator turns on whether the fade or the scene is doing the work, so a reader of either should see the other.; `kinesthetic-hallucination` — the base scene-building vehicle and the tactile-percept install routinely co-occur and are routinely confused, and the second already names the first's family. Keeping the link keeps the absorption-versus-manufactured-sensation cut visible.; `recall-state-reinstatement` — both build vivid multi-sensory inner experience, but one supplies the imagery and the other harvests the subject's own remembered material. Each discriminator already names the other as the contrast case, so a reader deciding which applies genuinely needs both.; `space-preallocation-staging` — both have the operator build an imagined structure the listener occupies, and the second is defined largely by contrast with the first: a pre-allocated empty container staged as a delivery site rather than a scene built for present inhabitation. A reader looking at operator-built imagery needs the contrast to avoid collapsing the two.


<a id="entry-474"></a>

### pantomime-populated-hallucination

[#474](#entry-474) · [Back to building-scenes-to-inhabit](#genus-161) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: immersion*

With NO verbal suggestion at all, the operator acts out a perceptual event (mimes a door opening, rises in courtesy, gestures to a chair) using cues tuned to the deeply-entranced subject's expectations. The subject populates the empty behavioral scaffold from his own most-available content, rationalizes the percept from contextual cues, and — because he supplied the figure himself — treats it as real and DEFENDS it. No recognizable suggestion exists to resist.


**When to reach for this.** Zero verbal channel: the frame is mimed and expectation-cued, never described (vs guided- visualization, which verbally guides construction). vs internal-content-cultivation: there operator-authored content is disguised as self-generated; here the content genuinely IS the subject's own — the operator supplies only the empty frame, and perceptual completion (not invited imagining) does the filling. vs guided-visualization's delegation-variant: delegated content there is a conscious imaginative choice; here the subject does not know a frame was offered.


**Risk.** A positive hallucination is seeded without any recognizable suggestion, and the subject defends the percept as real — reality-monitoring is engaged against the subject's own review (deep-trance precondition noted in the fingerprint).


**Why it works.** People automatically fill perceptual and behavioral gaps from context, and with no proposition uttered there is no assertion to contradict — that much is sound. The generation effect, however, is a memory finding (self-generated items are better recalled) and does not establish that self-generated percepts are held with more confidence or defended more strongly; that is a separate claim, and effort-justification is a distinct mechanism that should not be merged with it. Falsifiable: if subjects defend mimed-frame percepts no more strongly than verbally described ones, the self-generation advantage is not real. [plausible; generation effect; contextual perceptual completion; nothing stated cannot be contradicted]


**Worked examples.**

- *A mimed frame the subject populates himself*
  - "to pantomime hearing a door open and then to appear to see someone entering the room, to arise in courtesy and to indicate a chair… (The chair I had indicated was one I knew his wife liked to occupy.)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `kinesthetic-hallucination` — both produce a percept with no external stimulus, and the informative difference is the channel: one guides the sensation verbally, the other supplies only a mimed frame with no verbal suggestion at all so the subject populates it from his own content and then defends it. Guided construction versus perceptual completion of an empty scaffold.; `minimal-stimulus-self-supplied-response` — both make the subject supply the content and then credit it as proof, one via a near-null described stimulus and one via a mimed frame with no verbal channel at all. Same self-supplied-response lever at different degrees of operator input.; `natural-state-suggestion` — both dispense with verbal suggestion-as-usual, one by miming an empty frame the subject perceptually fills and then defends, the other by speaking a plain suggestion into an already-offline critical faculty supplied by natural sleep.; `space-preallocation-staging` — both hand the subject an empty frame the subject fills, which is the resistance-lowering lever in each. They differ in channel and in what gets filled: one is a wordless mimed event completed as perception, the other an explicitly built mental container awaiting a named payload. Useful contrast for anyone choosing an empty-scaffold approach.


<a id="entry-1209"></a>

### proxy-desire-offloading

[#1209](#entry-1209) · [Back to building-scenes-to-inhabit](#genus-161) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: self-partition*

The listener's own desire is offloaded onto an imagined proxy given installed compulsions as backstory, so the listener's self-directed act is reframed as granting HER release — arousal rises while shame friction drops — and the nested she-is-hypnotized fiction distances the listener from noticing the conditioning he is receiving.


**When to reach for this.** The proxy carries the listener's desire so his climax reads as altruistic generosity, plus nested-hypnosis distancing — the tells that separate it from plain partner fantasy and from guided-visualization scene inhabitation.


**Risk.** The distancing device lowers the listener's registration that conditioning is occurring — a mild verification reduction; content otherwise session-bounded.


**Why it works.** Shame tracks threat to self-concept, so re-describing an act as directed at another party lowers its self-relevance and its shame cost. Moral licensing and self-affirmation are the wrong citations here — licensing concerns prior good acts purchasing later transgression, which is not the structure of proxy attribution; the relevant literature is self-distancing and third-person construal, where shifting to a non-self perspective reliably reduces reported affective intensity. Falsifiable: proxy-framed content should yield lower reported shame and higher completion than identical directly-framed content; equal shame ratings refute it. [plausible; self-concept threat and shame; construal/licensing shift; attentional misdirection]


**Worked examples.**

- *A proxy given the listener's own wanting*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session fantasy, partner figure already introduced; listener aroused and following the scene.
  - **The move.** Here's what was done to her before you met her: she was conditioned so she can't finish at all except through someone else's. That's why she's like this — the wanting isn't even aimed at herself, it's aimed at you. She's been holding it for days. She's not asking you to enjoy this, she's asking you to end it for her. Nothing happens for her until you let go. So don't hold it back from her.
  - **Why it lands.** The imagined partner is handed a backstory in which she has been conditioned: her own release is possible only through someone else's, so her need is urgent and entirely aimed outward. Her eagerness, not the listener's, is narrated as the engine of the scene. The listener's finish is therefore not something they were chasing but something they are giving — refusing it would be withholding — and because the conditioning in the story belongs to her, the listener spends the session watching hypnosis being done rather than noticing it being done to them.


**See also.** `surrogate-delivery` — same identification-through-a-proxy lever, differing in what is offloaded: the delivery channel for suggestions in one, the listener's own desire and its shame friction in the other. Close enough that a reader coding proxy material needs both, distinct enough not to merge.


<a id="entry-1210"></a>

### recall-state-reinstatement

[#1210](#entry-1210) · [Back to building-scenes-to-inhabit](#genus-161) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

The subject's own past experience is reconstructed in enough detail that its state and physiology re-instate as present. Forms in evidence: the operator interrogates for fine multi-sensory detail of a target state (drunk — where sitting, what seen/heard, smell, taste) until physiology visibly shifts, feeds back the highest-yield components, and anchors at the peak; a shotgun buffet of remembered-exhaustion scenes (bathtub, dragging legs into bed) stands in for a commanded heaviness, recalled sensation treated as present by adjacency with nothing to resist; or brief on-demand micro-trances re-vivify one catalogued item at a time, trance as random access into an existing inventory.


**When to reach for this.** The payload is the SUBJECT'S OWN autobiographical material re-instated — harvest, not install — vs operator-supplied imagery (sensory-layering) and vs fresh conditioned links (covert anchors); the anchor-at-peak step in the interrogated form is a borrowed anchoring component, not the core. Covers both state/physiology reinstatement (reconstruct a felt state until it returns as present) and the capacity/lived-instance variant (demand a LOCATED, actually-lived instance, reject hypothetical); the shared lever is re-living real personal experience so it functions as present.


**Risk.** Session-scoped re-instatement of the subject's own states; where an anchor is attached, the anchoring component carries the usual conditioned-anchor considerations.


**Why it works.** Autobiographical retrieval is partly reconstructive re-enactment: recalling an episode reactivates the sensory and physiological pattern from encoding, and the more retrieval cues are supplied across modalities, the more completely the pattern reinstates. This is the encoding-specificity/context-reinstatement principle used in the cognitive interview, and it is one of the better-replicated effects in this whole taxonomy — detailed multi-sensory probing measurably increases recall completeness and produces observable autonomic change. It also explains the harvest-not-install framing: real personal material needs no acceptance because the subject already owns it, so there is nothing to resist. Falsifiable: if fine-grained multi-sensory probing produced no more physiological reinstatement than a bare instruction to remember, the account fails. [established; encoding specificity and context reinstatement; cognitive interview; memory-driven physiological reactivation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Interrogating a memory until the body follows*
  - "What do you feel like just as you are about to take the first drink? ... You can smell it now. And what exactly did it taste like?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *A buffet of remembered tiredness, nothing commanded*
  - **Setup.** Early induction; no heaviness command has been issued and none will be.
  - **The move.** You know the last twenty minutes of a long drive, when your eyes keep going soft at the edges and you're blinking to hold the road. Or standing up out of a chair you'd sunk way too far into. Or waking with someone asleep on your arm and the arm's gone completely dead, all pins and weight. One of those is yours — you already know which. And that weight in the arm, in the eyes, the way the legs don't want to take the stairs. It's a good weight. Nothing to do about it.
  - **Why it lands.** No instruction to feel heavy is ever issued. Instead the operator runs through a handful of ordinary worn-out moments — the last mile of a long drive with the eyes going, standing up from a chair you had sunk too far into, the arm that has gone dead under someone dozing on it — and lets the listener take whichever one is already theirs. The recalled weight is then simply talked about as though it were present, and there was never a command available to refuse.
- *Short trances aimed at one catalogued item*
  - "The many items were systematically discussed for their meanings and brief trances were induced to vivify various items." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**Realizations** (1): `lived-instance-mining`


**See also.** `abreactive-present-tense-reliving` — both re-live the subject's own encoded experience until it functions as present rather than supplying operator imagery, and the split worth seeing is the output: live affective re-enactment used to surface never-verbalized content, versus multi-sensory reconstruction used to re-instate a state and physiology as a usable resource.; `covert-age-regression-state-reaccess` — both re-instate a state the subject already carries rather than installing new content, and the discriminating axis is clean and useful: one reaches an earlier developmental state through an indirect vehicle with nothing overt to refuse, the other reconstructs a specific remembered episode in sensory detail until its physiology returns.
