A reader working with subject-supplied material benefits from seeing the covert-access and detailed-reconstruction routes side by side.; `fabricated-recovered-memory-retrieval` — both make a produced memory-experience function as present fact, and a writer will confuse them. The split is provenance: one fabricates material wholesale and frames it as recovery, the other reconstructs the subject's own genuine autobiographical episode until its state re-instates. Harvest vs. manufacture.; `guided-visualization` — both build vivid multi-sensory inner experience, but one supplies the imagery and the other harvests the subject's own remembered material. Each discriminator already names the other as the contrast case, so a reader deciding which applies genuinely needs both.; `recall-recognition-reentry` — both harvest the listener's own stored experience rather than installing new content, and the split is worth showing: one presupposes a previously-owned trance and does zero induction work, the other reconstructs any lived state in multi-sensory detail until physiology reinstates it. Useful adjacency for anyone building on autobiographical material.; `state-capture-anchor` — both work on already-present subject material rather than operator-supplied content, and one explicitly borrows the anchor-at-peak step from the other. Worth the pointer so a writer picks correctly between anchoring a live spontaneous reaction as an inspectable handle and reconstructing past autobiographical experience until it re-instates as present.


<a id="genus-180"></a>

## capture-attention-without-asking (4)

Capture the listener's focus without ever issuing a refusable focus-command — recruiting whatever attention state they're already in, hiding the fixation inside fiction or gesture, or crediting the object with the pull.

[adverse-attentional-state-recruitment](#entry-22) · [fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset](#entry-25) · [fixation-object-agency-displacement](#entry-27) · [intervention-ecology-correction](#entry-720)


<a id="entry-22"></a>

### adverse-attentional-state-recruitment

[#22](#entry-22) · [Back to capture-attention-without-asking](#genus-180) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: attention*

Rather than fighting an adverse attentional state, the operator recruits the subject's CURRENT attentional posture — whichever way it fails the conventional induction — as the working vehicle, so no attentional failure-state remains available and the exit-justification is deleted. Two opposite presenting states, one move: (a) drift/distraction recruitment — the operator names the divided or wandering attention the listener is already in (half-listening while doing a background task) and relabels it as the session's substance, never asking them to stop or close their eyes, so distraction becomes proof it's working; or the wandering-mind failure is named BEFORE it happens and its recovery pre-prescribed (bring attention back to the voice) so drift becomes a self-correcting re-bind rather than a trance-breaking event; (b) effort/strain recruitment — the operator cancels the expected relaxation frame and swaps in an effortful focus task, or inverts a let-go induction into deliberate conscious control ('be very mindful' before mindless), or sets an engineered-unresolvable target so failure is recoded as insufficient focus and drives more attending, or equates any lapse of focus with falling into trance, or commands 'pay attention' as a defense against influence so obeying IS the trance-producing narrowing. Either way the framing pre-defines every attentional posture as trance so both compliance and resistance deepen.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the listener is ALREADY in an attentional state that would normally break the induction (drifting, distracted, effortfully straining, jaded) and you want to convert that exact state into the vehicle — the payload is deleting the exit ('I'm too distracted / this is too much effort for this to work'). Choose it OVER fixation and cognitive-quieting, which install a NEW narrowing or emptying; here nothing new is installed, the present posture is relabeled. Drift-recruitment (make wandering attention the substance / pre-prescribe its recovery) and effort-recruitment (recruit sustained effort with a no-win frame where both compliance and resistance deepen) are the two poles of this one relabel-the-current-posture move.


**Risk.** Drift/distraction recruitment alone is low (session-scoped relabel, no durable reach). Lifted to MEDIUM by the absorbed effort-recruitment realization: the pay-attention-as-defense trap collapses compliance AND resistance so no engaged response is a non-deepener — a soft foreclosure of the exit. Session-scoped with no out-of-session reach, but the no-exit framing is the reason it is not pure low.


**Why it works.** Whether an internal state counts as success or failure depends on the label available for it, and people generally accept a plausible label supplied by a credible source rather than generating their own. Relabelling the state the listener is already in also removes the specific counterargument ('I'm too distracted for this') that would otherwise license quitting, and pre-prescribing the recovery converts a lapse into a scripted step rather than a breach. Falsifiable: if listeners in a distracted state dropped out at the same rate whether or not their distraction was pre-labelled as the vehicle, the recruitment does nothing. [plausible; misattribution/relabelling of internal states; expectancy; removal of a counterargument]


**Worked examples.**

- *The listener's divided attention named as the method*
  - **Setup.** Opening move; subject has the audio on while doing something else, attention flipping between the two.
  - **The move.** You've got this on while you're doing something else, haven't you — and your attention keeps flicking, over to the dishes, back to me, over, back. Don't stop. Don't close your eyes. That flicking is the whole thing; every time it comes back to my voice you're a little further in than when it left.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening move is to describe the state the listener is in right now: you have this playing while you get on with something else, and your attention keeps flipping between the two. No instruction to stop, no instruction to close their eyes — the other task is kept and enlisted as one end of the swing. Having been named as an ordinary observation, the flipping is then quietly relabelled as the mechanism itself. The usual excuse — my attention is too split for any of this to land — is no longer available, because the splitting is now the thing that is working.
- *Wandering named early, recovery prescribed in advance*
  - **Setup.** Early, before the subject has actually drifted anywhere; recovery must be prescribed in advance.
  - **The move.** In a few minutes your mind is going to wander off somewhere. That's fine, that's expected. When you notice it's happened, just come back to my voice — and coming back is what takes you down.
  - **Why it lands.** Well before anyone has actually drifted, the operator names drifting as a thing that will happen and hands over the fix in the same breath: notice it, come back to the voice. Executing that recovery is itself another act of binding to the voice, so a moment that would have cost depth now adds to it. Say it after the listener has already gone and it arrives too late to catch them.


**Realizations** (1): `effortful-attention-as-vehicle`


**See also.** `attention-as-evidence-loop` — both convert the listener's existing behavior into confirmation rather than installing anything new; one relabels the current attentional posture, the other accumulates the ongoing act as evidence. The boundary is fine enough to warrant the link.; `capacity-saturation-overload` — adjacent inductions that are genuinely confusable when the listener presents as strained or effortful. The test is whether anything new is imposed: one RELABELS the attentional posture already present (drift or strain) so no failure-state remains as an exit excuse; the other IMPOSES concurrent or flooded demand beyond the processing budget. The effort-recruitment pole sits closest to the load form, which is why the pointer earns its place.; `engineered-failure-harvest` — both take whatever the listener actually does and score it as success, and the discriminators already contest the boundary: one relabels a present attentional posture, the other engineers a task outcome and cashes it. The engineered-unresolvable-target form sits right on the seam, which is exactly why the pointer earns its place.; `ironic-process-delivery` — shares the recruitment of the listener's attentional failure state as the script's working vehicle.; `recruited-or-foreclosed-quieting` — both avoid issuing a refusable instruction and leave no exit justification: one relabels the attentional posture already present, the other engineers the emptying so no directive exists to refuse. Neighbouring solutions to the same resistance problem.; `response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure` — the same anticipatory pre-claiming applied specifically to attentional postures, where the presenting failure-state is recruited as the working vehicle.; `tension-release-induction` — both break the assumption that entry runs through relaxation, and either can be reached for when a listener is strained rather than calm. The split matters: one relabels the attentional posture already present so no failure state remains available, while the other manufactures a genuine physiological tension spike and labels the release rebound as trance. Nothing new is installed in the first; a real body-state change is engineered in the second.


<a id="entry-25"></a>

### fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset

[#25](#entry-25) · [Back to capture-attention-without-asking](#genus-180) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: attention*

Fixation is delivered so the subject never receives (or cannot refuse) an explicit, recognized 'focus on this' instruction. The focal capture is either diegetic (justified by the fiction so the subject is already attending), disguised inside a socially-expected gesture (a handshake folding in observation, rapport, and eye-fatigue), structurally undeliverable (an audio-only 'spiral' the listener must hallucinate or accept, with 'you can't look away' unfalsifiable), borrowed from a caretaker frame (a casualty-opener plea landing fixation while the listener is in rescuer mode), or forced onto the body prior to any decision (a head physically tipped to the target so looking is a body-fact). In every case the choose-to-attend frame conventional inductions rely on is removed, lowering awareness of being inducted and foreclosing 'choose to look away' as an exit.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from plain fixation by the absence of a recognized, refusable focus command. Separated from agency-displacement (there the induction is overt but the object is credited; here the recognition itself is suppressed or the choice is removed). The unifying rule is delivery that denies the subject the recognize-and-refuse juncture.


**Risk.** The forced-witness member (one realization) stages a non-consensual body-first onset removing the choice-to-look; that erodes the refusal juncture for that realization, lifting the cluster off pure low. Most members are covert but session-scoped.


**Why it works.** Refusing an instruction requires first recognising that an instruction was given; delivery that hides the instruction inside a fiction, a social routine, or a physical positioning never presents the recognise-and-refuse juncture, so no refusal is generated. Socially scripted gestures such as a handshake are especially effective because the automatic completion of the script leaves no decision point at all. Falsifiable: deliver the identical fixation with an explicit 'focus here' framing; if compliance and reported awareness of being inducted are unchanged, covert delivery is not the lever. [plausible; automatic execution of social scripts; reactance requires perceived influence attempt]


**Worked examples.**

- *Fixation folded into an ordinary handshake*
  - "the handshake is a gesture of friendship. It creates an immediate rapport which is essential… bringing the left hand down over the profile of the patient's face is a technique for tiring the eyes quickly." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *A fixation object the listener cannot actually see*
  - **Setup.** Audio-only recording, no visual component exists; opening fixation.
  - **The move.** Look at the spiral on the screen. Watch the arms of it turn, in, and in, and in. Stare right into the middle of it — and now you find you can't look away.
  - **Why it lands.** This is an audio recording with no picture, and the operator keeps telling the listener to look at a spinning shape on the screen, to watch it turn, to stare into it — and then that they cannot look away. There is nothing there. Either the listener builds the shape in their head, which is effortful and absorbing, or they simply accept the claim without checking, which is compliance. And the instruction cannot be falsified, because there is nothing to look away from.
- *The head turned to the target before any decision*
  - **Setup.** First exposure to the focal pattern, delivered as narrated action on the body; no offer, no choice point.
  - **The move.** Her hands take your head, one on each side, and tip it back until the pattern on the ceiling fills everything. "Eyes up." You're already looking before you decide to.
  - **Why it lands.** The first exposure is not offered. Hands take hold of the narrator's head and angle it toward the pattern above, with a two-word order attached, and the body complies before the will has caught up. Because the looking was never elected, the usual exit of electing to stop is not available either; there was no decision anywhere in the sequence that could be reversed.
- *Fixation delivered as a plea to a rescuer*
  - **Setup.** The opening seconds; operator presents as the casualty of her own botched working and the subject is holding the object that could undo it.
  - **The move.** No — put the pendant down, please, just set it on the table, I can't think with it swinging. I've done something stupid and I need — look at me. Look at me, please, just at my eyes, I can't get the words straight unless you look at me.
  - **Why it lands.** The speaker opens as the casualty of her own botched working — disoriented, fumbling with the paraphernalia she has just misused — with the listener cast as the competent one holding the object that could undo it. Her first move is not a command but a request that the listener set that object aside, followed by a flustered, repeated appeal for their eyes. It removes the listener's leverage and lands clean fixation in the same breath, and it is evaluated in rescuer mode, before anything registers as an induction at all.


**See also.** `covert-frame-entry` — both remove the recognize-and-refuse juncture at the entry seam — one by making the focal capture unrecognizable as an instruction, the other by presenting the whole session under a false benign frame. A writer choosing an unresisted entry needs to see both.; `disavowal-and-masking` — genuinely adjacent: both disarm the defense by removing the recognize-and-refuse juncture rather than by overpowering it. One narrows that to the fixation onset specifically, where no refusable focus instruction is ever delivered; the other covers denial or concealment of the operation as a whole. A reader working on covert onset should know the general family.; `fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer` — sibling departures from plain fixation, each altering a different property: removal of the recognize-and-refuse juncture, versus manufacture of a real physiological event that ratifies the suggestion. A reader deciding which departure is present benefits from seeing both.; `reading-act-as-induction-substrate` — both remove the recognize-and-refuse juncture at induction: one delivers fixation without any recognized focus command, the other makes the involuntary act of reading the compliance so there is no discrete task to decline. The second explicitly recruits and exceeds ordinary fixation, so the link is a real containment relationship rather than a coincidence.


<a id="entry-27"></a>

### fixation-object-agency-displacement

[#27](#entry-27) · [Back to capture-attention-without-asking](#genus-180) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: authorship-shift*

A fixation object is not merely attended but is credited with the causal agency for the attention or the trance itself, shifting the subject's locus of control off the self and onto an operator-controlled artifact. The pull is attributed to the object ('it simply pulls you in', 'catches the eyes like a net'), or the object is framed as the cause of obedience, or the induction labor is exported to an external self-running loop the voice merely narrates, or the effect is credited to a launched program while the operator's voice 'recedes', or the pull is sourced from the listener's own folk-model of hypnosis the operator only 'confirms'. Once agency is displaced, any wandering attention reads as the object working rather than as failure, so no resistance signal is observable and residual skepticism finds no target.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from plain fixation (there the object is inert) by the causal attribution: the object/artifact is credited as the cause. Separated from covert-onset variants (there the subject does not recognize the induction; here the induction is overt but the AGENCY is relocated). Separated from function-inversion (the object's role stays 'cause of attention' throughout; it is not repurposed into an aperture or descent vehicle).


**Risk.** Session-scoped and reversible; displacing agency onto an object disarms skepticism but does not erode the refusal channel or reach out of session.


**Why it works.** Relocating causal attribution for a state onto an external object exploits the same attribution machinery that produces misattribution of arousal: people infer the cause of an internal state from the most salient available explanation rather than from privileged introspective access. Crediting the object also makes the claim unfalsifiable from the subject's side — drifting attention confirms 'it's working' and sustained attention confirms it too — so no observation counts as disconfirmation and skepticism has nothing to attach to. This predicts that subjects given an external causal frame report less sense of personal effort and volition than subjects given the identical fixation instruction with no attributed agency; if effort ratings are unchanged, the account is wrong. [plausible; causal misattribution / attribution of internal states to salient external cues]


**Worked examples.**

- *The object credited with doing the pulling*
  - **Setup.** Fixation on a pattern; the subject's attention has started to wander for the first time.
  - **The move.** See how it pulls? You're not holding it — it's holding you, catching your eyes like a net. Same as a screen across a room with nothing on it, and your gaze goes anyway. And when your attention drifts, that's it working; it just draws you back.
  - **Why it lands.** Attention is never described as something the listener is doing. The pattern pulls, the pattern catches the eye, the pattern draws you back — and the operator borrows a familiar involuntary experience to prove it, the way a screen across the room takes your gaze even when there is nothing on it. Once the pulling belongs to the object, drifting attention stops being failure and starts being evidence the thing is working, which leaves no observable signal that anyone is resisting.
- *The induction exported to a self-running visual*
  - **Setup.** A separate looping animation is already running on the subject's screen; the voice's job is narration, not causation.
  - **The move.** The loop is doing this, not me — watch it swell, and hold, and swell again. Breathe in when it opens, out when it closes. In. Out. And the word at the centre of it is "obey," once every breath, and I don't have to say it because it's already there.
  - **Why it lands.** A separate looping animation is running on the listener's screen, and the recording's job is not to cause anything but to narrate what that animation is already doing. Breathing is then tied to its pulse, so the artifact is also pacing autonomic state. Because the voice is not spending itself on relaxation patter, it can spend the whole runtime on content instead — and the word pulsing at the centre doubles as both the thing being stared at and a command getting one repetition per breath.
- *The pull sourced from the listener's own expectations*
  - **Setup.** Fixation established; the subject has some prior folk-model of what hypnosis is supposed to be.
  - **The move.** You already know what this does — the watch on the chain, the swinging, the machine that takes your mind. You've known since you were a kid. That belief is where all of its power comes from, and you were right about it the whole time.
  - **Why it lands.** Rather than claiming the image is hypnotic, the operator invokes what the listener already believes hypnosis looks like — the swinging watch, the machine that takes your mind — and says that these beliefs are what give the thing its power. Then the only remaining step is agreeing that they were right all along. The pull now belongs to the listener's own model rather than to anything the operator did, and disputing it means disputing themselves.


**Realizations** (1): `authorship-relocation-to-object`


**See also.** `attention-anchor-portable-internalization` — both build a fixation object, but the levers differ: one launders operator-authored content as the listener's own imagery and internalizes it as a self-supplied pacer; the other credits the object with causal agency for the trance. A writer picking a fixation move benefits from seeing both options.; `causal-attribution-to-external-agent` — both relocate causation onto something outside the listener so volition has nothing to push against; the split is what the external thing is credited with — the attentional pull toward a fixation object versus the state-change itself, by a non-consumed agent. The second entry already names the first as the neighbour to pick instead, which is precisely the case a cross-reference should carry.; `fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer` — two fixation moves that a practitioner will confuse in the wild, and they resolve each other cleanly: one manufactures a real physiological event and reframes it as suggestion success, the other credits the object itself with causing the attention or the trance. Both define themselves against inert fixation, so reading either benefits from seeing the other.; `identity-displaced-into-external-object` — both shift something onto an external object. One credits the object with causing the attention or trance; the other makes the object the residence of the listener's identity or state. Read together to pick between agency-attribution and identity-relocation.; `operator-agency-disavowal` — two destinations for the same relocation. Agency for the trance is moved off the self either onto an operator-controlled artifact or onto the listener themselves, and in both cases resistance loses a target. Anyone classifying an agency-displacement passage has to choose between these two, so the pairing is a real disambiguation aid.; `single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer` — both relocate an arbiter of behavior/truth to an external locus (object vs operator-via-anchor); `withheld-completion-dependency` — both relocate who is driving attention away from the subject, and contrasting the destination is the payoff. One credits the fixation artifact with causal agency for the pull; the other saturates with pointers and then withholds the next one so the subject leans in waiting to be directed. Object as cause versus operator as cause.


<a id="entry-720"></a>

### intervention-ecology-correction

[#720](#entry-720) · [Back to capture-attention-without-asking](#genus-180) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

The operator treats observed feedback (subject resistance, or the aftermath of a successful removal) as a signal to re-orient the intervention's AIM or ECOLOGY rather than to add force — a design constraint on the change's fit, not a subject-state push. In the resistance-as-targeting-feedback form, stalling or refusal is read not as an obstacle to push through but as evidence the operator is aiming at the wrong object: abandon the defended presenting symptom and redirect onto its substrate or secondary gains (the conditions that make the symptom necessary), so removing the need leaves the symptom nothing to defend — the lever is operator-side search re-orientation, not increased force. In the post-removal ecology-check form, after a technique strips an overgeneralized protective response, deliberately verify that ordinary adaptive caution survived and re-task some of the freed-up energy as a guardrail in the newly-open context, preventing the change from overshooting into recklessness (the useful core of the removed protection is confirmed intact and the liberated energy is redirected to safeguard). The shared lever is feedback-driven operator-side correction of the intervention's aim/ecology.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for intervention-ecology-correction when observed feedback tells the operator to ADJUST the intervention's aim or ecology (not its force) — a design constraint on the change's fit, with no consent channel touched and no struggle engaged in-frame. Tells: resistance re-aims the search onto the symptom's substrate; a post-success check confirms adaptive caution survived and redeploys freed energy as a guardrail.


**Risk.** Operator-side search heuristic; no direct channel erosion or durable scope on the subject.


**Why it works.** Pushing harder against a defended symptom triggers reactance — the perceived threat to freedom makes the defended behaviour more attractive, so added force predicts worse outcomes. Re-aiming at secondary gains works instead because the symptom is being maintained by a reinforcement contingency; remove the contingency and the maintained behaviour extinguishes without needing to be attacked. The ecology check reflects the fact that learned protective responses generalize by similarity, so stripping an overgeneralized one predictably removes adaptive instances too unless they are separately re-established. [plausible; psychological reactance; operant maintenance by reinforcement; stimulus generalization]


**Worked examples.**

- *Resistance read as aiming at the wrong target*
  - "Clients don't resist… All they ever do is demonstrate that you are on the wrong track… 'Hey! Not there! Over here!'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (1): `redeploy-liberated-energy-into-caution`


<a id="genus-208"></a>

## change-through-others (3)

Route the influence through other people — peers yoked to the target's outcomes, models silently re-weighting what's normal, third parties recruited as the reinforcement engine.

[peer-mediated-contingency](#entry-2) · [social-reinforcement-recruitment](#entry-534) · [vicarious-modeling-installation](#entry-169)


<a id="entry-2"></a>

### peer-mediated-contingency

[#2](#entry-2) · [Back to change-through-others](#genus-208) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: social-topology*

Recruit a peer GROUP as auxiliary change-agents by yoking its reinforcement topology to the target behavior and posting each member's status publicly, so peers monitor, pressure, and coordinate with each other atop the operator's direct contingency. The yoking structure is the parameter — VARIANTS: (a) general public-status substrate [peer-mediated] — public/consequential status alone recruits peer pressure regardless of how rewards are yoked; (b) all-or-none interdependent [interdependent-group] — reward hinges on a collective criterion (group total/mean), 'all earn or none do', with an optional defensive individual-overlay to neutralize defectors; (c) dependent 'hero-gates-all' [dependent-group] — one member's performance gates the whole group's reward, converting peer hostility into positive attention on the 'hero'. All three ride the same peer-as-change-agent graph; pick the yoking that fits who should gate whose reward.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a co-present GROUP under a shared contingency can be turned into reinforcers of each other — the lever is peer monitoring/pressure yoked to reward, and you choose the yoking (public-status substrate / all-or-none / hero-gates-all). NOT belonging-recruitment (social-proof-belonging-enrollment — membership pull of a converted cohort, no reward-yoking) and NOT peer-authored-target-selection (peers author the agenda, they do not gate the reward).


**Risk.** Recruits social/peer pressure as an added control source over the subject; bounded, but the multi-agent pressure surface is more than a session-scoped operator-subject contingency.


**Why it works.** Peers who can observe your performance and whose own outcomes depend on it become a live audience with a stake, and humans adjust behaviour far more under observation with consequences than under private instruction alone. Public status posting adds accountability and normative comparison; yoking reward to a collective or single-member criterion converts indifferent bystanders into active enforcers because their payoff now moves with the target's behaviour. Falsifiable: if compliance rates under public+interdependent contingencies were no higher than under an identical private individual contingency, the account fails. [established; group contingencies in applied behaviour analysis; audience/accountability effects; normative social influence]


**Worked examples.**

- *Public shared contingency recruits peers as change agents*
  - "a group contingency can capitalize on peer influence or peer monitoring because this type of contingency sets the occasion for peers to act as change agents" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (2): `dependent-group-contingency`, `interdependent-group-contingency`


**See also.** `social-reinforcement-recruitment` — both convert third parties into the maintaining reinforcement source, but peer-mediated contingency yokes a co-present group's shared reward to the target behavior so members police each other, while social recruitment works agent-by-agent on the setting's existing people without any group-level yoking.


<a id="entry-534"></a>

### social-reinforcement-recruitment

[#534](#entry-534) · [Back to change-through-others](#genus-208) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: contingency-engineering*

Route the maintaining reinforcement through another AGENT whose delivering behavior is itself the engineered variable — convert the subject's social environment into the reinforcement engine. Operator-side forms: inform capable-but-dormant people in the setting of the value of their attention and explicitly ask them to watch for and reinforce any reasonable effort (awakening an asleep community so gains persist after the trainer leaves); or, where ABC narrative data reveal caregivers/staff reinforcing the wrong endpoint (e.g. the end of an escalation chain over appropriate bids), directly reverse that agent's contingency (reinforce appropriate responses, extinguish the escalation endpoint, shape delay tolerance). Selection-side form: choose a proxy target behavior specifically because its payoff changes how significant others treat the subject, recruiting a named third-party causal path. Subject-side form: the subject self-evaluates against a criterion and, on meeting it, actively recruits praise/feedback from an authority, engineering the conditions under which that person reinforces them (raising the authority's own praise rate as a collateral change). Includes the dosing layer: calibrate recruiting rate and topography to the setting's tolerance so the recruited contingency stays net-positive and the reinforcing agent is not flipped into a punisher.


**When to reach for this.** The maintaining consequence is delivered by another social agent whose attention or response is recruited or redirected. Recruitment may be operator-led, mediated by target selection, or taught to the participant as criterion-based feedback seeking. Unlike peer-mediated group contingencies, another member’s reward need not be yoked to the target’s performance.


**Risk.** Out-of-session engineering of third-party reinforcement around a possibly-unaware subject; no refusal-channel erosion (two members).


**Why it works.** Attention and approval from significant others function as powerful social reinforcers, and unlike an operator they remain in the setting, so recruiting them shifts maintenance onto a source that persists. Reversing a caregiver's contingency works because whichever behavior in an escalation chain reliably produces the payoff is the one that gets strengthened — reinforcing the wrong endpoint teaches escalation directly. The dosing layer reflects that reinforcer delivery is itself behavior under its own contingencies: a recruiter who overdraws makes attending aversive and the agent stops delivering. Falsifiable: if recruited third-party reinforcement produced no better post-operator maintenance than operator-delivered reinforcement, the account fails. [established; social attention as reinforcer; contingency reversal; recruiting reinforcement / behavioral trapping]


**Worked examples.**

- *Waking the dormant reinforcing community*
  - "The contingency is there, but dormant. One solution… is to inform key people in the generalization setting of the value and importance of their attention… and ask them to help." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Proxy target chosen for its third-party payoff*
  - "not because of their direct benefit…but because of an important indirect benefit" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (1): `reinforcing-agent-engineering`


**See also.** `peer-authored-target-selection` — both route the operative move through the surrounding group rather than the subject, and one already names the other as a contrast. The distinction worth preserving is what the peers supply: reinforcement delivery versus authorship of the target list itself.; `peer-mediated-contingency` — both convert third parties into the maintaining reinforcement source, but peer-mediated contingency yokes a co-present group's shared reward to the target behavior so members police each other, while social recruitment works agent-by-agent on the setting's existing people without any group-level yoking.; `public-avowal-third-party-propagation` — both route maintenance through people outside the operator-subject pair, but one arranges third parties to deliver reinforcement while the other uses an audience's self-consistency pressure and recruitment. Read together when deciding whether the social environment is being managed or being made the propagation vector.; `self-administered-contingency` — same who-administers-the-contingency axis with the role routed into recruited others rather than the self.


<a id="entry-169"></a>

### vicarious-modeling-installation

[#169](#entry-169) · [Back to change-through-others](#genus-208) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · bounded · family: social-topology*

Showing the target others performing (or NOT performing) an act — even on film, with no instruction to imitate — silently re-weights what the viewer treats as available and appropriate and shifts their own subsequent rate of that act; valence is set entirely by what is modeled (the same channel cures phobia or transmits aggression). VARIANTS by carrier/direction: (a) in-person/film depiction [vicarious-modeling] — mere observation of a model raises the behavior, no live plurality/instruction/prohibition; (b) media-scale one-way [publicized-modeling-contagion] — wide broadcast of a similar other's act (e.g. publicized suicides) raises the base rate population-wide among identifiers, differing from (a) only by scale and carrier; (c) inaction/mutual-visibility [pluralistic-ignorance-freeze] — among co-present strangers each reads the others' calm non-response as evidence nothing is wrong and suppresses their own, a recursive freeze that yields less help than a lone witness (broken by singling one person out).


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when mere OBSERVATION of a model shifts the viewer's own rate — no belonging is offered, no operator required, nothing suggested/triggered/scheduled. Pick the variant by carrier (in-person/film vs media-scale) and direction (action-raising vs inaction-freeze). NOT social-proof-belonging-enrollment (membership/conformity is the lever, not rate-shift-by-exposure) and NOT two-track-relational-delivery (a foreground RELATION carries the payload via identification, not a bare modeled behavior).


**Risk.** Durable behavior-baseline shift delivered without felt instruction and out of session, but no refusal-channel erosion, countervailing prohibitions at action time still work (stated in source).


**Why it works.** Observational learning is well established: observers acquire and increase behaviours they see modelled, without reinforcement or instruction, with effects strongest when the model is similar to the observer. Vicarious extinction of phobia and modelled-aggression transfer are both replicated, which is why valence is set by what is modelled rather than by the channel. The bystander variant rests on separately replicated findings that helping declines as the number of co-present witnesses rises, and that ambiguity plus others' visible inaction is read as evidence of non-emergency. Falsifiable throughout: each variant predicts a measurable rate change against a no-model or lone-witness control. [established; observational learning / vicarious modelling; bystander effect and pluralistic ignorance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Watching a model shifts the watcher's own rate*
  - "these children were significantly more harmful toward another child than were children who had watched a nonviolent television program… held true for the two age groups… and for both girls and boys" — Cialdini (1984), Influence


**Realizations** (2): `pluralistic-ignorance-freeze`, `publicized-modeling-contagion`


**See also.** `manufactured-consensus` — same-chapter social-proof genus, different lever (live headcount certification vs observational installation); reconciliation may raise a shared principle.


<a id="genus-160"></a>

## changing-what-pays-off (5)

Behavior is shaped by rearranging its consequences: cut the payoff, hand the reward out free, suspend privileges, or make relief from discomfort the wage of compliance.

[negative-punishment-timeout](#entry-876) · [negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance](#entry-1026) · [noncontingent-reinforcement](#entry-430) · [reinforcement-extinction](#entry-432) · [scaffold-fade-control-transfer](#entry-1129)


<a id="entry-876"></a>

### negative-punishment-timeout

[#876](#entry-876) · [Back to changing-what-pays-off](#genus-160) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Immediately contingent on the target behavior, the operator withdraws the subject's opportunity to earn positive reinforcers or removes access to currently-available ones for a bounded interval; the subject ends the interval only by waiting it out or meeting exit criteria. Future frequency of the producing behavior drops because the moment of misbehavior reliably costs a window of good things. No new skill is taught — the lever is pure suppression, and it works only when the time-in environment is already reinforcing and the withdrawal is immediate and contingent. Defined by its suppressive effect, not by any topology.


**When to reach for this.** Withdraws the opportunity to earn or access reinforcers for an interval, distinct from response cost which levies a fine against already-held reinforcers. If the producing behavior's future frequency does not drop, it is not punishment at all — that effect-defined suppression is the tell versus any surface-similar removal.


**Risk.** Bounded, reversible aversive-adjacent suppression contingent on behavior; no channel erosion and no durable identity scope, but it withdraws access to reinforcement and must ship inside a host that supplies the reinforcing time-in and a defined exit.


**Why it works.** Removing access to reinforcement contingent on a response lowers that response's future rate, provided removal is immediate, reliable, and the time-in environment is genuinely reinforcing. State the prediction in advance rather than defining it post hoc: measure baseline rate, apply the contingency, and predict a drop. If the rate does not fall, the note is wrong — do not rescue it by reclassifying the operation as 'not punishment'; report which precondition (delay, inconsistency, unrewarding time-in) failed and treat that as a testable follow-up. [established; operant conditioning — negative punishment / timeout from reinforcement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Withdraw the chance to earn, for a set interval*
  - "the immediate response-contingent withdrawal of the opportunity to earn positive reinforcers or the immediate loss of access to positive reinforcers for a specified time" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `response-cost-token-economy` — textbook siblings inside subtractive suppression, separated by whether a not-yet-earned opportunity is withheld for an interval or a reinforcer the subject already holds is debited per instance. Each already defines itself against the other, so the cross-link is load-bearing.


<a id="entry-1026"></a>

### negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance

[#1026](#entry-1026) · [Back to changing-what-pays-off](#genus-160) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Make TERMINATION (escape) or prevention (avoidance) of an already-present aversive condition contingent on a target response: the subject raises the response to turn the aversive off or keep it from onset, and the reinforcer is the RELIEF itself, not an added reward. Severity scales effort (relief from a strong aversive can outweigh a comparable positive reward). The operator selects WHAT aversive the response escapes. REALIZATIONS by aversive source: (escape-from-aversive-reinforcement) the base case — a pre-existing aversive the response terminates/prevents; (escape-based-compliance) make the INSTRUCTION itself aversive by escalating instructional pressure (prompts, re-issue, error-correction) on non-response, so complying brings relief (the operator may run this without recognizing it); (aversive-antecedent-contingency) open a mild social-aversive interval (awkwardness, a pending obligation to respond) that responding terminates and not-responding worsens, compliance experienced as escape; (coercive-demand-form-selection) cast the want as a COMMAND supplemented with an added aversive whose removal negatively reinforces compliance — the coercive pole of demand-form selection (defined by the backing contingency, not the imperative grammar; the willing-listener pole is a praise-reinforced request with no aversive).


**When to reach for this.** Reach for NEGATIVE REINFORCEMENT / ESCAPE COMPLIANCE when the response is maintained by RELIEF from an already-present aversive (the response turns it off or prevents it), not by an added reward. Choose it over: positive reinforcement (adds a reward — here nothing is added, an aversive is removed); punishment (reduces a behavior — this INCREASES the target response by relieving an aversive); response-cost / time-out (subtract or withhold a positive — here an aversive is added-then-escaped). The realizations differ only by the aversive SOURCE (a pre-existing aversive / escalating instructional pressure / a social-awkwardness interval / an aversive backing a command). Often unrecognized — the operator may believe they are reinforcing positively while running an escape contingency.


**Risk.** Arranging an aversive the subject works to escape is durable behavior-shaping with a coercive edge; severity-scales-effort can drive hard compliance. Bounded, requires a host supplying entry/exit.


**Why it works.** Negative reinforcement is one of the best-replicated findings in operant psychology: response rate rises when the response reliably terminates or postpones an aversive stimulus, and escape-maintained behaviour is notoriously persistent because every occurrence is immediately and unfailingly reinforced by relief. Its danger here is that relief is not experienced as reward, so both parties can misread coerced compliance as willing consent. Falsifiable at the individual level: if removing the aversive contingency left response rate unchanged, the behaviour was not escape-maintained. [established; Negative reinforcement / escape-avoidance conditioning (Sidman avoidance, functional analysis)]


**Worked examples.**

- *The response turns the aversive off*
  - "consists of the removal or termination of an aversive condition that is already present." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (3): `aversive-antecedent-contingency`, `coercive-demand-form-selection`, `escape-based-compliance`


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation` — directly complementary: one maintains a response by relief from an aversive condition, the other neutralizes or dissolves that same aversive antecedent so there is nothing left to escape. Reading the escape contingency without knowing the upstream edit that abolishes it leaves the practitioner with only the consequence-side half of the pair.; `noncontingent-reinforcement` — contrasting contingency structures worth reading together: one delivers the maintaining reinforcer on a clock with no behavioural contingency, the other makes relief from an aversive contingent on responding. Both are commonly confused in practice with positive reinforcement, and the selection question genuinely runs between them.; `relief-monopoly-dependency` — the relief-monopoly entry is an applied case of the escape contingency: distress is manufactured or intensified, then compliance is made the unique route to relief, so the response is maintained by relief rather than an added reward. Naming the underlying schedule helps a reader see why the monopoly form is so durable.; `resistance-penalty-contingency` — both make an aversive do the work, but one attaches a penalty specifically to resisting, thinking, or waiting so the exit path costs, while the other maintains a target response by relieving an already-present aversive, regardless of whether resistance was in play. Punish-the-exit versus relief-as-reinforcer is a genuine selection question.


<a id="entry-430"></a>

### noncontingent-reinforcement

[#430](#entry-430) · [Back to changing-what-pays-off](#genus-160) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering*

Deliver the maintaining reinforcer on a fixed-time schedule INDEPENDENT of the behavior, so the reinforcer the problem behavior used to produce is now free on the clock and the behavior loses the motivation to produce it. In the escape variant, breaks from a demand are handed out pre-emptively on a fixed-time schedule before the subject acts out, decoupling escape from misbehavior so the task is experienced as interruptible-by-default (compliance rises, disruptive escape falls). ABSORBED GUARD (ncr-competition-discrepancy): for NCR to actually suppress, the free source must OUT-COMPETE the earned one — increase amount/quality and densify the schedule so it exceeds baseline rate, and typically pair with extinction; if free and earned reinforcement merely MATCH, the subject keeps working for the earned one and NCR does nothing (the named failure mode).


**When to reach for this.** Versus extinction (removes the reinforcer) and DRO (reinforces omission); the tell is the maintaining reinforcer is still DELIVERED but on a time schedule with no behavioral contingency. The escape variant's tell is that the free reinforcer is scheduled task-removal, not an appetitive item.


**Risk.** Free delivery of a benign reinforcer; no channel erosion, reversible.


**Why it works.** If the reinforcer that maintained a behaviour arrives freely on a clock, the behaviour no longer produces anything the subject does not already have — both because the response-reinforcer contingency is degraded and because free delivery satiates, lowering the reinforcer's momentary value. Which of those two does the work is not fully settled, but the practical consequence is well replicated. The competition guard is the falsifiable core: the account predicts that NCR fails whenever the free source does not out-compete the earned one in rate, amount or quality, and that failure mode is exactly what is observed when schedules merely match. [established; contingency degradation; satiation / abolishing operation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Free breaks on the clock, not on the behavior*
  - "the therapist used an initial FT 10-sec schedule for escape, meaning that the student had a break from the instructional requests every 10 seconds" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (1): `ncr-competition-discrepancy`


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement` — sibling behavioral-schedule techniques that each name the other as the choice to rule out: one reinforces something other than the target behavior, the other delivers the maintaining reinforcer on a time schedule with no contingency at all. The contingency-versus-no-contingency fork is exactly the decision a reader needs.; `function-based-extinction` — same maintaining-reinforcer axis run the other way: the reinforcer is delivered free on a clock schedule so the behavior stops purchasing it.; `negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance` — contrasting contingency structures worth reading together: one delivers the maintaining reinforcer on a clock with no behavioural contingency, the other makes relief from an aversive contingent on responding. Both are commonly confused in practice with positive reinforcement, and the selection question genuinely runs between them.; `reinforcement-leak-proofing` — two disjoint levers on the same arranged contingency that are routinely deployed together: closing every unintended path by which the maintaining reinforcer can still be obtained, and delivering that same reinforcer freely on a time schedule. The second is explicitly noted to need the first to work.; `removal-from-reinforcement-timeout` — both are reinforcement-schedule procedures defined largely against each other and against the same siblings (extinction, response-cost): one delivers the maintaining reinforcer free on a time schedule so the behavior stops producing it, the other withholds access to reinforcement for a contingent period. A practitioner picking a reductive procedure needs the pair side by side.


<a id="entry-432"></a>

### reinforcement-extinction

[#432](#entry-432) · [Back to changing-what-pays-off](#genus-160) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Reduce a behavior by breaking the response-reinforcer contingency: once the maintaining reinforcer is identified, arrange the environment so the behavior no longer produces it, so with no payoff the rate declines toward its pre-reinforcement baseline. Nothing aversive is delivered — the lever is removal (not punishment), and partial reinforcement undermines it. The move spans every reinforcer channel and carries its own integrity rules: withhold a positive reinforcer with no alternative; enumerate and withhold ALL maintaining sources at once (one live source only thins the schedule and can leave the behavior intact); block escape so a negatively-reinforced response no longer terminates the aversive (escape extinction); restate the contingency flatly and disengage to deny an attention/conflict payoff; break the contingency at the sensory channel when the reinforcer is the behavior's own self-produced sensation (sensory masking). Route targeting through a functional assessment ('just ignore it' is the named anti-pattern) so the identified reinforcer is the one cut. Anticipate the extinction burst and hold the line consistently through it (relenting reinforces an intensified response); optional accelerants engineer extra evoking occasions to raise non-reinforced trial density, titrate a caregiver's tolerated ignoring duration upward so the procedure is actually sustained, and guard NCR delivery timing so a scheduled free reinforcer never coincides with a just-emitted problem behavior. PROCEDURAL FIDELITY: hold the contingency steady through the predictable side-effect cascade (burst, response variation, spontaneous recovery, resurgence, emotional/aggressive outbursts) treating these as expected, and critically do NOT let an emergent burst topography contact reinforcement — caving to an escalation trains a new, worse behavior to do the old job (topography substitution is itself the consistency failure). CHAIN-STRUCTURED SUPPRESSION (breaking a chain via its reinforcer structure): (chain-link severing) pay the LATE response of a two-response chain unconditionally so the intermediate stimulus stops predicting reinforcement and loses SD/conditioned-reinforcer value — only the EARLY link decays, surgical vs broad suppression; (chain collapse) strip the value of the chain's TERMINAL payoff so decline cascades BACKWARD through every upstream link — an extinction route (withhold the terminal consequence, the most immediate breaker) or a satiation route (an abolishing operation devalues it — the same abolishing-operation move as motivating-operation engineering).


**When to reach for this.** Reach for EXTINCTION to reduce a behavior by REMOVING its maintaining reinforcer so the rate declines to baseline (no aversive delivered). Choose it over: punishment (delivers an aversive); noncontingent reinforcement (still delivers the reinforcer, free on a schedule); differential-reinforcement rerouting/DRA (preserves the reinforcer and redirects it to a sanctioned channel); differential reinforcement of absence/low-rate (reinforces omission, not full removal); graded-support-withdrawal / transfer-of-control (there withdrawal is engineered so the GAIN persists; extinction removes support so the response dies); motivating-operation engineering (the chain-collapse SATIATION route here is its twin — extinction WITHHOLDS the payoff, satiation DEVALUES it). The chain-structured facets split by whether one link is surgically severed (unconditional late-response payment) or the terminal payoff is removed so the whole chain cascades backward. Variants also split by reinforcer channel (positive / escape / attention / automatic-sensory) and by integrity/acceleration rule (complete-enumeration, burst-integrity, trial-density, graduated-ignoring, NCR timing-guard). Fidelity trap (folded from reinforcement-leak-proofing): inconsistent withholding does not merely slow extinction — a single lapse installs an intermittent schedule and REVERSES the direction of change, making the behavior more resistant — so the reinforcer must be withheld consistently across every agent and occasion, bundling instructions, alternative reinforcement, and recruitment of significant others to close multi-agent leaks.


**Risk.** The escape-extinction variant holds an aversive demand in place regardless of the subject's response, eroding the exit/refusal channel; sustained removal of reinforcement can be aversive and, at scale, coercive. The mechanism is reversible and channel-local, so it ships bounded.


**Why it works.** Behaviour persists because it produces a consequence; break that relation and the rate declines toward baseline — this is the most heavily replicated finding in operant work. The characteristic side effects fall out of the same account: the burst and response variation are what an organism does when a previously reliable contingency stops paying (try harder, try differently), and partial reinforcement histories slow extinction because the subject has already learned that non-payment does not mean the contingency is gone. The account is falsifiable at the point that matters operationally — it predicts extinction fails if any maintaining source is left live, which is why incomplete enumeration reliably produces no decline at all. [established; operant extinction; extinction burst; partial-reinforcement extinction effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Withhold all reinforcement for the response*
  - "Extinction (withholding all reinforcement for a previously reinforced behavior) produces a decrease in response rate to the behavior's pre-reinforcement level." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Enumerate every source before withholding any*
  - "withholding one source of reinforcement may have minimal or no effect on behavior." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Block the exit so escape stops paying*
  - "placed on extinction (escape extinction) when those behaviors do not produce a removal of the aversive stimulus, meaning that the individual cannot escape from the aversive situation" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Break the contingency at the sensory channel*
  - "adding lima beans to the vomit... the vomit did not taste as good, and the positive sensory consequence was masked." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (6): `behavioral-extinction-of-refusal`, `chain-collapse-terminal-payoff-removal`, `chain-link-severing`, `extinction-procedure-fidelity`, `function-based-extinction`, `sensory-extinction`


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation` — both reduce a behavior once its maintaining function is known, but extinction acts on the CONSEQUENCE side (withhold the reinforcer the response already produces) while antecedent editing acts upstream so the occasion, motivation, or motor possibility never arises and there is nothing left to consequate.; `behavior-chaining` — one assembles a multi-step sequence by exploiting each link's dual reinforcer-and-cue role; the other's chain-structured facets attack that same link structure in reverse, severing a link or collapsing the whole chain from its terminal payoff — build and teardown of one architecture, and the teardown only makes sense to a reader who holds the build.; `chain-link-severing` — extinction genus carrying the chain-structured-suppression facet this entry matured from.; `counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening` — adjacent behavior-reduction procedures that each name the other as the alternative to choose against - removing the reinforcer that maintains an operant versus pairing an incompatible state against an eliciting cue. Practitioner-facing selection depends on reading both.; `function-based-extinction` — genus entry for the same withhold-the-maintaining-reinforcer move, spanning every reinforcer channel plus integrity and chain-structured facets.; `functional-analysis-methodology` — worth reading in sequence: turning a suspected variable on and off proves what maintains a behavior, and removal of that identified reinforcer is the intervention that consumes the proof. The assessment is exactly the routing step whose omission is the removal move's named anti-pattern; they are separate moves because one only changes what the operator knows and the other changes the behavior.; `response-cost-token-economy` — sibling behavioral suppression routes a writer chooses between: one removes the maintaining reinforcer so the rate decays, the other debits a reinforcer the subject already holds per instance. Each discriminator already contrasts against the other's family, so the cross-link is doing real selection work.; `sensory-extinction` — genus extinction entry whose sensory-masking channel this entry matured out of.


<a id="entry-1129"></a>

### scaffold-fade-control-transfer

[#1129](#entry-1129) · [Back to changing-what-pays-off](#genus-160) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

Establish or MOVE stimulus control by installing a temporary support that reliably produces the target response, then removing that support GRADUALLY so control transfers to the natural cue with few or no errors and no lasting dependence. The common lever is graded withdrawal of ONE assistive dimension rather than a cold handoff; the non-negotiable second half is that the support must be faded or the gain becomes prompt/dimension dependence (the named failure mode). The realizations differ by which dimension is attenuated. Response-prompt strength: an added antecedent — verbal instruction, demonstration/model given a prior imitative repertoire, or graded assistance hierarchies (most-to-least, graduated guidance, least-to-most) — is reinforced while present, then faded. Stimulus-side errorless fading: the antecedent STIMULUS's own form is exaggerated-then-faded, or an artificial shape is morphed into the natural target, so at completion no separable prompt remains. Time-delay transfer: only the TIMING gap between an unchanged prompt and the cue is stretched, so the learner responds in anticipation and beats the prompt. Graded support withdrawal: an artificial support (token system, chemical dose, dense free-reinforcer schedule) is withdrawn along a planned graded schedule, each step subthreshold for relapse — the gain-preserving/maintenance facet, optionally migrating the function to a portable substitute first. Model-reinforce-fade teaching: present the object, model the response, reinforce the echo, then fade the model so the object alone evokes the tact. Errorless superimposition-plus-fading (superimpose a new dimension on an already-controlling one, then fade the old) is the shared errorless craft.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for TRANSFER-OF-STIMULUS-CONTROL (prompt/errorless fading) when a support currently produces the response and you must hand control to the natural cue WITHOUT errors or dependence — the defining act is the engineered FADE of that support. Choose it over: shaping (grades successive approximations of the RESPONSE with no external support carrying it); discrimination training (builds cue control by a reinforce/extinguish history, not by fading an added support). The realizations differ only in WHICH dimension fades — response-prompt strength, stimulus form, prompt timing, or an artificial support schedule; all share the one transfer-by-attenuation lever and the 'leaving the support in = dependence' failure mode.


**Risk.** Antecedent-field arrangement to teach a target response with a fade plan; environmental contingency shaping, no refusal channel or identity scope acted on. The modeling form installs nothing durable and gates on prior skills.


**Why it works.** A response reliably occasioned by an added prompt does not thereby come under control of the natural cue; control transfers only if the prompt is attenuated gradually enough that the response continues to occur and be reinforced in the prompt's near-absence. Fading works because the learner never experiences the error, and the extinction of the prompt's discriminative function is gradual rather than abrupt. The failure mode is a direct prediction of the same account: leaving the support in place means the support retains stimulus control, which is exactly what prompt dependence is. Falsifiable: an abrupt withdrawal should produce more errors and lower retention than a graded one, holding total training constant. [established; transfer of stimulus control; errorless learning / prompt fading]


**Worked examples.**

- *Add a prompt that evokes the response, then fade it*
  - "Prompts are supplementary antecedent stimuli used to occasion a correct response in the presence of the natural SD" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Errorless transfer by superimposing then fading*
  - "first superimposing a white vertical line on the green light (SD)... Finally, the amplitude of the red and green lights was reduced gradually until only the vertical and horizontal lines remained" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (8): `differential-reinforcement-teaching`, `graded-fade-stimulus-control-transfer`, `graded-prompt-fading-transfer`, `graded-support-withdrawal`, `prompt-fade-scaffolding`, `prompt-then-fade-to-natural-antecedent`, `stimulus-side-errorless-fading`, `time-delay-prompt-transfer`


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — the same graded-fade lever applied to different objects: withdrawing an added support so the natural cue takes control, versus handing over authorship of the contingency itself until the subject is both parties. The first is the general craft the second specializes.; `descriptive-functional-assessment` — sibling off-axis ABA procedure; measurement vs contingency arrangement; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — adjacent halves of stimulus control: one builds cue control through a reinforce-in-presence, withhold-in-absence history; the other moves existing control to the natural cue by fading an added support. Anyone selecting between them needs the pair.; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — both concern where control of a response sits and how it moves. One has the subject manufacture their own antecedent cue; the other fades an operator-supplied support until the natural cue takes over. A reader choosing a control-transfer route benefits from seeing both handoff shapes.; `shaping-successive-approximation` — an explicitly paired design contrast already stated on both pages: one differentiates the response while holding the antecedent fixed, the other holds the response fixed and fades an added support. Practitioners routinely confuse the two, and each entry's discriminator names the other as the thing to choose against.


<a id="genus-302"></a>

## charging-key-words (2)

Specific words — the subject's own terms or a captured pet word — are pre-loaded with meaning so every later use carries the payload without re-consent.

[own-language-echo-reframe-durability](#entry-1164) · [semantic-referent-capture](#entry-1173)


<a id="entry-1164"></a>

### own-language-echo-reframe-durability

[#1164](#entry-1164) · [Back to charging-key-words](#genus-302) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

The operator first gathers the subject's exact terms for their intention — their nominalizations, unspecified verbs, and idioms — then re-uses those same terms when describing the NEW behavior, rather than inserting operator vocabulary. Because nothing foreign is imposed, agreement is anchored in the subject's own frame and the reframe does not later flip into a reaction against inserted content. The lever is a linguistic quality-control move for reframe durability: own-language echo prevents a delayed polarity backlash.


**When to reach for this.** Not general rapport-matching or pacing — that is rapport, not language-reuse. The tell is the specific gather-then-reuse of the subject's exact nominalizations/idioms to describe the NEW behavior, aimed at preventing a delayed polarity flip.


**Risk.** A linguistic QC craft move on how a reframe is worded; session-scoped, reversible, no consent surface or channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Reusing the subject's own terms works because those words carry the subject's private referents rather than the operator's, so the described new behaviour is evaluated against meanings the subject already endorses and generates fewer counter-arguments — self-generated framing is reliably more persuasive and more durable than externally supplied framing. The claim about preventing a delayed reversal is the weaker half: it is plausible that operator-inserted vocabulary becomes a salient cue for later reactance, but the specific delayed-backlash prediction is not well evidenced. Testable: reframes described in the subject's own language should survive longer at follow-up than the same reframes in operator vocabulary. [plausible; self-generated persuasion; reduced counter-arguing to self-owned framing]


**Worked examples.**

- *The subject's own words reused for the new behavior*
  - "if you use that same set of nominalizations and unspecified verbs and idioms… you will match what he is trying to do at the unconscious level… That will avoid the polarity problem." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `commitment-before-restructure-sequencing` — both are quality-control moves aimed at the same later failure — a delayed 'this was imposed on me' backlash — but one banks a congruence-checked commitment to self-change before the content is revealed, while the other reuses the subject's exact terms so nothing foreign is inserted to react against: sequencing versus vocabulary.; `intervention-fit-doctrine (prefer shed-to-existing)` — technique-level instance of the doctrine's content-validity and congruence clauses: fit the subject's own terms to prevent the polarity backlash.; `referent-pre-alignment` — both are pre-work language moves that align the subject's terms with the operator's before a payload depends on them: one reconciles what the target state means, the other harvests the subject's own phrasing and reuses it for the new behaviour. Genuinely useful as a pair; the difference is aligning a referent versus preventing a later polarity flip.; `representational-system-matching` — both reuse the subject's own words back at them and both aim at suggestions registering as self-originated. The split is what surface is harvested and to what end: exact intention-terms reused to keep a reframe from flipping, versus sensory-modality vocabulary read as a channel index and matched covertly. Easy to conflate without the link.


<a id="entry-1173"></a>

### semantic-referent-capture

[#1173](#entry-1173) · [Back to charging-key-words](#genus-302) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

The operator captures a repeated word so they become its sole referent. By floating both readings of a word ("bunny" as animal vs "a cute bunny girl") then offering herself as the referent and inviting the listener to notice which image jumped to mind, she installs herself as what the word means. Every later benign-sounding use of that word ("pet", "take care", "bunny deserves") then carries the person-load without re-consent; the frame is self-authored, lowering later resistance.


**When to reach for this.** Covert equivocation captures a vocabulary item so subsequent benign uses smuggle in a relational obligation the listener never re-agreed to. vs a simple pet-name introduction — no equivocation, no captured referent. vs seeding expectancy for the session — that primes what the session will feel like; this captures the meaning of a word for later reuse.


**Risk.** Ordinary nickname association is limited; this entry specifically analyzes equivocation that imports unagreed relational obligations. A lexical association does not supply agreement to those obligations.


**Why it works.** Repeated pairing of a word with a particular referent shifts which meaning is retrieved first, and once one reading dominates, later uses of the word activate it automatically without the listener re-evaluating the choice. Having the listener notice which image came to mind converts this into self-perception evidence — she infers her own stance from her own reported response, so the association feels self-authored and resists correction. Testable: after the capture, response times and interpretations for that word should shift toward the installed reading, and the effect should be weaker if the listener is not asked to report which reading surfaced. [plausible; semantic priming / dominant-meaning selection; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *A word captured so the operator is its meaning*
  - **Setup.** Pre-induction, conversational register; subject alert, no trance yet, the word will be reused throughout the session.
  - **The move.** Say the word kitten. Now — which one came to mind first, the small animal, or a girl on her knees called kitten? Whichever one it was, you noticed something, and that noticing is your answer. From here, when I say kitten, this is who I mean. And a kitten gets looked after, doesn't she. A kitten gets fed, and told when to sleep, and a kitten belongs to somebody.
  - **Why it lands.** Before any trance work, the operator picks one soft, harmless noun that has both an innocent everyday sense and a person-shaped one, and asks the listener which came to mind first. Whichever the listener notices, the noticing itself is treated as the answer, and the operator then offers herself as the thing the word points to. From that moment the word has one referent. Every later cosy, unobjectionable sentence built on it — who looks after whom, what is owed — carries a claim about a person that the listener never separately agreed to, and it feels like a meaning they supplied themselves.


**See also.** `covert-referent-migration` — two forms of covert referent manipulation under a stable surface word: one migrates the grammatical seat that names the listener, the other captures a shared vocabulary item so the operator becomes what it means. Both defeat resistance by removing the marked boundary where an objection could fire; the difference is which referent moves.


<a id="genus-227"></a>

## climax-as-leverage (3)

The climax is expropriated as a control asset: loaded as the maximal-imprint moment, or withheld behind compliance gates so the mounting drive itself enforces the terms.

[banked-reward-escrow](#entry-299) · [orgasm-as-imprint-window](#entry-275) · [orgasm-release-gating](#entry-277)


<a id="entry-299"></a>

### banked-reward-escrow

[#299](#entry-299) · [Back to climax-as-leverage](#genus-227) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

TECHNIQUE (banked/escrowed lever): rather than delivering reward in the moment, WITHHOLD and BANK it so it accumulates, then discharge it later on a condition — converting a diffuse pairing into a high-stakes reflex. The pleasure is 'kept from you', stored, and detonated all at once only when a command is obeyed (tested via a hand raise/lower), so each act of obedience becomes disproportionately rewarding and a standing post-session trigger keeps releasing the reservoir. Realizations: pleasure withheld-accumulated-detonated on an obeyed command (the core escrow); a pre-signed consent token — an unpriced, open-ended 'I would trade anything for it' CONSENT lever, ratified in the subject's own first-person voice and banked before any specific ask exists, for later withdrawal. The through-line: the value (reward or consent) is stored now and drawn against later, not spent live.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the defining move is withhold-accumulate-and-discharge-later (a stored reservoir or a pre-signed lever), NOT in-the-moment reward (-> direct-reward-linkage). The escrow/banking step is the tell; the consent-lever variant also borders the manufactured-consent family.


**Risk.** Installs a standing post-session trigger that keeps releasing banked pleasure on future obedience — durable and out-of-session, but reward-positive and self-supplied with no refusal-channel erosion, so medium.


**Why it works.** Delaying and concentrating a reinforcer raises its momentary value at delivery, and one large reinforcer contingent on a single identifiable act produces sharper response–reinforcer contiguity than the same amount dribbled out — the accumulation is effectively a motivating operation inflating the reinforcer's effectiveness. The pre-signed consent variant runs on a different lever: a commitment made when it costs nothing is cheap to give, and the consistency principle then makes it expensive to withdraw once a specific ask is attached. Falsifiable: banked-then-discharged reward should produce faster acquisition of the target act than continuous equivalent reward; and subjects who gave an open-ended early commitment should comply more with a later specific request than subjects asked cold. [established; motivating operations / deprivation; foot-in-the-door and commitment-consistency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reward stored up and detonated on obedience*
  - **Setup.** Pleasure established and then explicitly withheld; the subject's hand is resting where the operator can test it.
  - **The move.** I'm not handing you that feeling as it comes — I'm keeping it, stacking it up, and none of it is yours until you do as you're told. Raise your right hand for me. There — all of it at once, every bit you were owed; and from now on, each time you do what I say, the whole stack pays out again.
  - **Why it lands.** Instead of paying out the good feeling as it arises, the operator announces that it is being held back and stockpiled, and that it will be released in a single lump for one thing only: doing as told. A trivial test instruction follows — a small gesture performed on cue — and the stored reservoir is said to discharge on completion. The same rule is then extended past the session, so every later act of compliance draws on the same reservoir. What would have been a diffuse pairing becomes a high-stakes payout, and each small obedience is rewarded far out of proportion to its cost.


**Realizations** (1): `pre-signed-consent-token`


**See also.** `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — real boundary friction: one entry's banked open-ended consent token is close to the other's cited-back agreement artifact. The pointer should carry the split — a discrete retrievable agreement replayed to suppress live refusal, versus a stored value drawn down on an arbitrary later command.; `orgasm-gated-recurrence` — both withhold something now to spend it later, one gating a real physical release behind re-consuming the operator's material, the other banking a diffuse reward or a pre-signed consent token for discharge on a later command. Adjacent withhold-and-draw-later structures with different held goods.; `orgasm-release-gating` — both recruit an unspent reward as the compliance lever, but one holds a live discharge behind a met-able key so mounting drive enforces the condition, while the other accumulates a reservoir and detonates it on an arbitrary later command; a writer choosing between them is choosing whether the subject can see the key.; `perpetual-obligation-ledger` — both hold value across time as leverage rather than spending it live. One withholds and banks a reward or a pre-signed consent lever for later discharge on a condition; the other keeps a relational debt balance permanently open by over-repaying. Stored reservoir versus never-settled balance.; `reciprocity-ledger-seeding` — both bank a lever now for withdrawal later, and the escrow entry's pre-signed open-ended consent token is the same shape as an obligation seeded long before any specific ask.
