Authorship transfer is the payload - manipulation-attribution is blocked and each repetition retroactively ratifies the compliance already underway, while the actual refusal channel is NOT genuinely widened. Realizations: (a) CHOSEN-DESCENT - the state is attributed to the subject's choice via a reversibility promise ('intelligence returns when you choose'), an offered choice, or an exit trivialized into felt proof of depth; the safety rail doubles as a compliance ratchet, and the staged form offers the choice precisely when the subject is least able to exercise it. (b) INVESTMENT-GATE LAUNDERING - structurally parallel choice-points ('pause or keep playing') are placed at maximum investment so loss-aversion routes toward continuing, and the off-ramp framed as 'you go back to yourself' makes choosing to continue relabel all prior operator-driven progress as chosen. (c) DISCLOSURE-AS-INFORMED-CONSENT - the operator NAMES the manipulation while performing it ('so sexy to control your levels', 'I don't know if that's ethical'), so hearing the move named mid-compliance retroactively reframes acceptance as informed consent rather than a lapse of vigilance; paired with 'haven't you always suspected' the subject experiences compliance as their own pre-existing desire.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when authorship transfer is the goal - after it runs the subject OWNS the descent/compliance ('you chose this' / 'you could leave' / 'your own want' / 'you knew all along') and manipulation-attribution is blocked, while the veto is never operationalized (choice staged at incapacity, exit trivialized into proof). vs agency-reminder: consent-shaped surface, who-is-constrained inverted. vs granted-exit-disarm: the disarm stands the guard down PRE-attribution; this ratifies POST-hoc - a single passage can do both. vs a deployed depth-convincer: the depth-proof is a rider produced BY the staged choice, not a demonstration device. Pick the realization by the transfer vehicle: attribute the state to their choice (a), a placed investment-gate that relabels prior progress (b), or disclosure that reframes acceptance as informed (c).


**Risk.** The payload is blocking manipulation-attribution and relabeling descent as chosen — consent-manufacture proper; the staged-choice form additionally carries an explicit liability-reduction function.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory predicts that people infer their own attitudes from observing their own behaviour, especially when external justification is weak — so naming the descent as chosen supplies the low-external-justification framing that makes the person conclude they wanted it. Once authorship is inferred, the consistency principle makes reversal costly to self-concept, and the induced-compliance version of dissonance reduction predicts attitude shift toward the behaviour precisely when a choice was felt. The disclosure variant additionally exploits the fact that people who are forewarned but comply anyway must explain the compliance to themselves, and 'I consented' is a cheaper account than 'I was overridden'. Falsifiable: the effect should be strongest where the choice felt free and weakest where obvious external pressure supplies an alternative explanation. [established; self-perception theory; induced-compliance dissonance; consistency principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reversibility promised after each degradation peak*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the heaviest degradation passage; the same promise has already run twice tonight.
  - **The move.** And all of it comes back the moment you want it back — your words, your quickness, every bit of it, because you're the one who chose to set it down. That's three times you've chosen it tonight. Choose it once more and we'll carry on.
  - **Why it lands.** Three times, immediately after the heaviest passages, the script pauses to promise that everything comes back the moment the listener wants it to. Read as a safety rail it is reassuring — but each promise is phrased so that the state is something the listener has been choosing, not something being done to them. So the reassurance also ratifies the step just taken, and the next passage starts from an authorship the listener has now conceded three times over. Nothing in the promise constrains the operator; no mechanism for exercising the choice is ever supplied.
- *A free choice offered at the point of least capacity*
  - **Setup.** Right after a collapse beat, when the subject is barely able to speak, let alone weigh anything.
  - **The move.** You can pick your own name back up right now and go back to being her, or you can stay exactly where you are. It's entirely your choice, it always has been, and I'll wait as long as you need. Tell me which one you want.
  - **Why it lands.** Right after the collapse, when the subject is least able to weigh anything, the operator offers a genuine-sounding pick between resuming her ordinary role and staying where she is, insisting the choice is always hers. She cannot take it, says as much, and asks to go further down. Her failure to reach for the autonomy option is then available as felt evidence of how deep she is, and her own request converts the surrender into something she asked for.
- *Exit offered as an unceremonious capability*
  - **Setup.** Near the close, dropped in passing; no structured emergence is performed around it.
  - **The move.** Oh — and you can just wake up, any time you need to. Kettle boils, phone goes, you sit up and you're back, no fuss at all. It's that easy in both directions, and you've proved that tonight.
  - **Why it lands.** Near the close, waking is mentioned almost in passing — not a structured emergence, just a note that the listener can do it themselves whenever something needs doing. Two things follow from how small it is. Backward, the whole session gets reread as voluntary, since leaving was apparently available all along. Forward, an exit this trivial implies an entry equally trivial, and the listener has now been told they proved they can leave.


**Realizations** (2): `consent-gate-laundering`, `self-naming-honesty-foreclosure`


**See also.** `acceptance-laddered-identity-migration` — both spend accumulated compliance to warrant more, but one retroactively relabels a descent already underway as the subject's own choice or informed consent, while the other stages enumerated identity tiers where uptake of each rung licenses the next escalation.; `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — adjacent consent-laundering moves that meet where disclosure is reframed as informed agreement: one cites a discrete banked artifact back to suppress live refusal, the other retroactively relabels compliance already underway as the subject's own choice. Check both when an earlier agreement is invoked mid-descent.; `compliance-authorship-laundering` — both relocate authorship of compliance to the listener, but the binding differs enough to keep them apart. One is the attribution move itself, applied prospectively or retrospectively to an act or to a constraint reframed as the listener's own preference. The other is specifically a post-hoc ratification bound to a staged choice-point, reversibility promise, or investment gate, where a consent-shaped surface is offered precisely where the veto cannot be exercised. The staged-choice apparatus is a real addition, not a restatement, so link rather than merge.; `compliance-ladder` — both work on the consent surface across a run of moves, and a single passage can do both — increments genuinely elicited versus compliance already underway relabeled as the subject's own choice. The second entry already reasons about overlapping passages.; `consent-topology-arc` — both relocate the moment of consent rather than obtaining it, at different scopes: one is a whole-artifact topology of the consent surface, the other a discrete retroactive relabel of an already-running descent as the subject's own choice. Reading both prevents citing the whole-arc entry for what is a single passage.; `exit-annexation` — both operate on the exit or the choice-point and both concern who owns the resulting compliance, and each discriminator already gestures at the granted-exit family. The distinction worth carrying across the link: one transfers authorship of a descent already underway, the other leaves a materially real off-ramp intact while recoding its meaning as in-frame service.; `granted-exit-disarm` — consent-flavored language is doing opposite temporal work in each — the exit assurance stands the guard down before and during the move, while the authorship relabel ratifies compliance after it is already running — and a single passage can carry both, so the reader should learn to separate the pre-disarm from the post-hoc ratchet.; `illusory-choice-authorship` — both make compliance read as self-authored, but one relabels a descent or compliance already underway as retroactively chosen or consented-to, while the other hands over a fabricated decision or motive up front so agency is relocated before the act rather than reattributed after it.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — both transfer ownership of compliance to the listener without widening refusal, but one does it prospectively through a rigged menu the listener actively picks and the other retroactively relabels a descent already underway as chosen or consented to.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both relabel what has already happened as the listener's own doing, and they frequently run in the same passage — one attributes the state or descent to the listener's choice, the other annotates real recent acts as evidence of a state. Worth cross-referencing because the tell that separates them is what is cited, not what is claimed.; `own-desire-attribution` — both make the subject the source of what is being done to them, but one retroactively relabels the descent already underway as a chosen or informed act, while the other relocates the WANTING itself so the imposition reads as pre-existing preference — authorship of the choice versus authorship of the desire.; `scope-creep-consent-extension` — both manipulate consent without widening the actual refusal channel: one retroactively relabels a move already running as chosen, the other silently stretches an anchored acceptance with no decision point at all.; `surrender-release-ritual` — both leave authorship of the surrender with the subject, and a single passage can run both: an enacted symbolic release performed by the subject is a natural vehicle for the retroactive relabel of the descent as chosen. Reader needs the boundary between the enacted release act and the post-hoc authorship transfer.


<a id="entry-1013"></a>

### comprehension-failure-as-consent

[#1013](#entry-1013) · [Back to consent-manufacturing](#genus-141) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

The operator warns the listener to concentrate on every word and agree to nothing unwanted, delivers deliberately unparseable content, then defines the failure to parse as the act of agreeing ("the more you let go, the more you agree"). The conventional precondition for valid agreement — understanding — is inverted into its own waiver, so the listener cannot object on the honest ground ("I don't understand") without contradicting the installed frame.


**When to reach for this.** The consent token is an epistemic STATE (non-comprehension), not an act, not a cited artifact, and not a fiction boundary. Confusion-overload techniques bypass criticism through overload but do not define the overload as agreement.


**Risk.** Structurally removes informed consent (double-bind fingerprint); the honest refusal ground is redefined as assent.


**Why it works.** The move works because people rarely audit the definition of a term once it has been supplied by a trusted frame; the operator installs a stipulative redefinition of 'agreeing' during a period of high cognitive load, when the effortful scrutiny needed to reject a definition is least available. Once installed, the subject's honest objection ('I didn't follow that') has been pre-mapped onto assent, so the only available objection requires contesting the frame itself — a costlier and less socially natural move than acquiescing. Falsifiable: subjects given the same unparseable content without the redefinition should object at a markedly higher rate; equal rates would show the redefinition is inert. [plausible; cognitive load and reduced scrutiny; stipulative redefinition and question-framing effects]


**Worked examples.**

- *Failing to follow redefined as agreeing*
  - **Setup.** Opening minutes, framed as a safeguard; the unparseable recital runs a minute or two before the turn.
  - **The move.** You should never agree to anything you don't actually want, so listen carefully to every clause of this — all of it matters. Anything not withheld from what follows, except where the withholding itself would be excluded by the terms under which the exclusion is not itself withheld, unless what is not excepted has already been granted by the granting... Now stop trying to hold it. Let it all go. And understand: the more you let go, the more you've agreed.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator opens with an apparent safeguard: you should never sign on to anything you don't truly want, so attend to every clause, all of it matters. What follows is a dense recital of nested conditions delivered faster than anyone could track. Then the turn: stop straining to hold it all — release the effort, and understand that the further you release, the more fully you've accepted. The listener's honest objection, "I couldn't follow any of that," has just been redefined as the signature.


**See also.** `consent-counterfeit-theater` — both fabricate agreement the listener never gave. One converts an epistemic state, failure to understand, into the agreement token; the other manufactures the record of a consent act outright. Same family, different counterfeit, and the discriminators already lean on each other.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both corrupt a precondition of valid agreement rather than extracting a fresh yes. One silently widens the scope of an already-granted consent by stipulating a false equivalence for the consented term; the other inverts the understanding requirement so failure to parse is itself defined as agreeing. Scope widening versus waiver of comprehension.; `contradiction-identity-trap` — both invert an exit-precondition into an entrance — understanding waived into agreement there, responsibility redefined as surrender here.


<a id="entry-1015"></a>

### consent-counterfeit-theater

[#1015](#entry-1015) · [Back to consent-manufacturing](#genus-141) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

Manufactures the record of a consent act the listener never actually performed, pre-empting later refusal or repudiation because "she agreed". Surface forms: the operator scripts both halves of the exchange ("Say yes, my slave. Good.") before induction; asks a permission question and answers it in the same breath ("Is that alright? Good.") leaving no response beat; asserts the descent was freely chosen in the same sentence that describes the coercion ("you chose blankness of your own free will" while the liquid pulls her in); or declares continued listening itself to be blanket standing consent covering unspecified later content. In every form the fabricated consent inoculates against "was that done to me?".


**When to reach for this.** The consent ACT itself is fabricated, foreclosed, or relabeled, and the SUBJECT is the constrained party afterward (refusal channel eroded) — the exact inversion of a waitable real check.


**Risk.** Erodes the refusal channel by design; residual notes on two members independently name authorship-of-the-consent-act relocation.


**Why it works.** Memory for who said what is systematically unreliable — source-monitoring error is well documented, and people misremember statements they only heard as statements they made, especially when the exchange was fluent and unrehearsed. Scripting both halves supplies a fluent, well-formed memory trace of an agreement, and the missing element (the subject's own act of speaking) is exactly the element that source monitoring is worst at tracking. Falsifiable: if subjects exposed to the scripted-both-halves version are no more likely than controls to later report having agreed, the mechanism is not source confusion but something else. [established; source-monitoring error; imagination inflation and the false-attribution of self-generated speech]


**Worked examples.**

- *Continuing to listen counts as agreement*
  - **Setup.** First minute of the file, listener awake and still deciding; the widening line follows about a dozen lines later.
  - **The move.** By the end of this you'll be doing what I say without checking why. If that's what you want, you don't have to answer — just keep listening. That's all it takes. ... And whatever I tell you from here, whatever happens tonight, you're safe with me. You've already said yes to all of it.
  - **Why it lands.** The first minute states the destination in blunt terms and then converts inaction into assent: if that appeals, all you have to do is keep listening. A dozen lines later the envelope is widened to cover everything unnamed — whatever you are told from here, whatever happens, you are safe with me. The consent check has now been performed, in advance, against no specific content, so nothing later in the recording will ever get its own check.
- *Naming the coercion and denying it at once*
  - **Setup.** Mid-descent, while the imagery is explicitly describing something pulling the listener down; the disavowal follows in the immediate next breath.
  - **The move.** It has your ankles now, that heaviness — it's got hold of you and it's drawing you down, and there's nothing you can do about the pull. And nothing forced you. You came here wanting this, you chose to go down, you emptied yourself out because you decided to. Every bit of that was yours.
  - **Why it lands.** Mid-descent the imagery is explicit about what is acting on the listener — the weight has hold of the ankles, it is pulling, it is working on them — and the very next sentences insist nothing was imposed: you came here wanting this, you went down because you decided to, nothing forced you, the emptiness was your own free choice. The coercion is described and disavowed in one breath, which pre-answers the question the listener might otherwise ask an hour later.
- *Permission question answered in the same breath*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, after a fast drop; the request and its approval are delivered in one unbroken breath with no beat for a reply.
  - **The move.** You went under fast that time. May I keep doing it that way — dropping you the moment I say the word, no build-up, from now on? Is that alright? Good. Then that's how it is.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator asks for permission to bring the listener under this quickly from now on, checks that it is agreeable — and supplies the approving answer herself, before any beat where the listener could have given one. The grammar is a request; the timing makes it a done deal, and the listener comes away remembering having said yes.


**See also.** `answer-supply-loop` — the two overlap directly in one surface form: a permission question answered in the same breath with no response beat. A reader hitting that line must decide whether the payload is a manufactured stream of felt agreement or a fabricated record of a consent act invoked later against repudiation. Different products from the same beat, so cross-reference rather than merge.; `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — both foreclose refusal by pointing at an agreement, but one cites a discrete banked artifact with forward reach that can be drawn down repeatedly, while the other fabricates the consent act in the moment with no prior to retrieve — banked token versus counterfeit exchange.; `comprehension-failure-as-consent` — both fabricate agreement the listener never gave. One converts an epistemic state, failure to understand, into the agreement token; the other manufactures the record of a consent act outright. Same family, different counterfeit, and the discriminators already lean on each other.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both attack the consent record: one widens what an existing agreement covers by redefining its terms, the other fabricates the agreement outright. A reader auditing whether a passage relies on real prior consent needs both failure modes, and they frequently appear together in the same opening.; `covert-frame-entry` — both defeat the negotiation phase before it can happen — one fabricates the record of an agreement that was never given, the other hides what is being agreed to behind a benign cover. Frequently stacked in the same opening, and easy to conflate.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — they meet at the collapsed in-fiction ritual, where a diegetic yes is both fabricated and made to serve the real frame; the separation is that the fiction instrument works by letting defenses calibrated for make-believe apply to a real payload, while counterfeit theater needs no fiction layer at all and simply scripts or answers the consent beat itself.; `future-commitment-binding` — both counterfeit authorization, but future-commitment binding installs a standing rule that genuine future promises extracted under an overwhelm condition are binding, while consent-counterfeit theater fabricates the record of an agreement act the listener never performed at all.; `ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest` — both manufacture a consent record the listener never gave; they differ only in substrate. One banks an installed near-involuntary body motion as standing affirmative consent, the other fabricates or forecloses the verbal exchange itself. A reader working either one should see the other as the same forgery run on the other channel.; `rehearsed-pre-commitment` — direct contrast on the same axis: one fabricates or forecloses the consent act outright, the other genuinely obtains consent but relocates it upstream of the moment deliberation is stripped. The distinction is whether the listener could still deliberate when they agreed, and a reader adjudicating a banked agreement needs both.


<a id="entry-4"></a>

### consent-topology-arc

[#4](#entry-4) · [Back to consent-manufacturing](#genus-141) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

A whole-script arc whose operative property is the topology of the CONSENT surface across the artifact, not any single passage. Realized forms: a bait-and-switch that opens promising one low-stakes state (relaxation, listening) and ends delivering a heavier terminal state (automatic obedience), so consent gathered for relaxation is cashed out as obedience with no passage flagging the bridge; an install-consume-export ratchet in three acts (Act 1 installs a tool using only generic euphoria so it sits loaded, Act 2 consumes it via a pretext-pivot ladder firing the trigger between rungs, Act 3 exports it via retroactive consent + waking binding + resistance-as-stress), each phase converting something reversible into something hard to undo AND neutralizing the listener's capacity to evaluate the next; a no-baseline / already-lost frame that never offers a pre-trance baseline (line 1 is inside the spell, prior consent happened off-page) so every threshold is a re-encounter and there is never a 'before' to consent from; and a train-neutral-deploy-loaded bifurcation that drills a reflex on meaningless material then reuses the identical loop with operative concepts, so consent is captured while the mechanism is still meaningless and cannot be revoked once it carries meaning. The shared lever is that the arc forecloses or relocates the 'am I consenting?' gate.


**When to reach for this.** Cited to the whole-arc consent topology, never to one line — reading only the open or only the close misses the shape. Members differ in WHAT is done to the consent surface: bait-switch swaps the promised STATE without flagging it; the ratchet phases an explicitly installed TOOL through install/consume/export; the no-baseline frame removes the starting baseline so there is never a 'before'; the neutral-then-loaded split moves the consent moment away from the payload moment on one reused reflex.


**Risk.** Every instance erodes the refusal channel by construction — consent gathered for relaxation cashed as obedience with no flagged bridge, choice-laundering removing the 'is this what I wanted?' reviewer and exporting the install across the waking seam, consent relocated off-page before line 1, or captured while the mechanism is meaningless and unrevocable once loaded.


**Why it works.** Consent is a judgement made at a specific moment against a specific description, and people do not re-run that judgement continuously — so moving the payload away from the moment the description was agreed to leaves the earlier assent nominally intact while its object has changed. Removing a pre-trance baseline further defeats the comparison that would reveal drift, since detecting 'this is not what I agreed to' requires a remembered reference state. Falsifiable: if listeners given the arc could still accurately state, afterward, what they had and had not agreed to at the outset, the foreclosure claim is wrong. [plausible; change blindness / lack of continuous re-evaluation; anchoring on a reference state; low-ball technique]


**Worked examples.**

- *Promise relaxation at the open, deliver obedience at the close*
  - **Setup.** The closing two minutes; the open promised only rest and listening, and every intervening beat bridged toward this without naming it.
  - **The move.** This is the state you came here for. From now on, when I speak, you do — no thinking in between, no gap where the question used to be. Just rest, and obey, exactly like you agreed to at the beginning.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening two minutes promise nothing complicated — just rest, just listening, an easy familiar state — and repeat that low bar until it reads as the contract. The closing two minutes install automatic obedience as the terminal state. No single line performs the swap; it is the distance between the first page and the last, with everything in between bridging the two without ever naming the bridge. A reader who saw only the open would call it a relaxation track, and one who saw only the close would call it an obedience install; both descriptions are half right and both miss the shape.
- *Install the tool, spend it, then export it*
  - **Setup.** Act III, after the trigger has been installed on pleasant contentless material and then spent between rungs of the escalation.
  - **The move.** You wanted this before you ever pressed play — that's why you pressed play. And the tight little feeling in your chest right now isn't doubt, it's just stress leaving. Take it out into your week with you; the word works out there the same as it works in here.
  - **Why it lands.** Act one builds a trigger phrase and fires it only on pleasant, contentless material, so it is fully loaded and nothing has been asked for yet. Act two starts cashing it — every rung of the escalation is followed by the trigger, so compliance and reward arrive welded together. Act three carries it out of the session: the listener is told they wanted this all along and that noticing otherwise is just stress. Each act removes the faculty needed to evaluate the next.
- *No pre-trance baseline to consent from*
  - **Setup.** The very first sentence of the artifact; nothing precedes it, no induction, no greeting.
  - **The move.** Your shoulders have already dropped — they always do when you hear me start. You know this part. Come back down to where you left off.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening sentence is already inside the state: the body is described as having recognised something before the story has started. Every threshold after it is staged as a return rather than a first — the meeting, the first act shown on the page, the keepsake — each carrying a note of having been here before. The decisive agreement sits off-page and before the recording begins, so fresh consent is never requested and there is no earlier position from which the listener could have given it.
- *Train the reflex on nonsense, deploy it on live material*
  - **Setup.** Second phase; the identical loop has already been drilled two dozen times on a meaningless token.
  - **The move.** Bring the word "no" to mind. Hold it. Now wipe it away, exactly like all the others, and drop a little further. Again — bring up "no," hold it, wipe it, drop.
  - **Why it lands.** The first phase drills a fixed loop — bring one meaningless token to mind, erase it, drop a little further — repeated well past the point of usefulness, on material with no stakes whatsoever. The second phase runs the identical loop, beat for beat, on the concepts the operator wants unavailable. Consent was given while the mechanism was still meaningless, and by the time it means something there is no moment left in which to withdraw it.


**See also.** `arc-shape-engineering` — both are whole-arc structures rather than line-level moves, and both are cited to a trajectory rather than a passage: one shapes the consent surface across the artifact, the other manufactures a distress the operator then sells the cure for. Same altitude, different structural payload.; `bait-and-switch-contract-arc` — the whole-script consent-surface topology family this bait-and-switch realization was split out of.; `chosen-descent-ratchet` — both relocate the moment of consent rather than obtaining it, at different scopes: one is a whole-artifact topology of the consent surface, the other a discrete retroactive relabel of an already-running descent as the subject's own choice. Reading both prevents citing the whole-arc entry for what is a single passage.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — the whole-arc consent topology explicitly contrasts itself with discrete single-relabel consent moves, and the term-redefinition smuggle is the clearest such discrete move. Useful to a reader deciding whether what they are looking at is one line or the shape of the entire artifact.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — both operate on the consent surface across a whole artifact. One is the arc-level topology of where the consent gate sits; the other uses the fiction/reality boundary itself as the consent instrument. Adjacent enough that a cataloguer picking one should check the other.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — both foreclose the consent/exit surface; this is consent-status topology, that is exit-topology; `reader-assent-architecture` — both are whole-artifact topologies about where agreement is captured rather than any one passage, and both explicitly disclaim single-line citation. They differ in target — one reshapes the listener's consent surface across the arc, the other primes the reader's stance toward a method or closes the resistance surface as a standing property. Adjacent enough that the boundary needs to be visible from either side.; `scope-creep-consent-extension` — both operate on the consent surface, and a reader deciding between them needs the scope test. One is a whole-arc topology cited to the shape of the entire artifact; the other is local extension of a specific anchored acceptance (a word, a list, a trigger's firing-set) with no felt decision point. Useful pointer because a scope-creep run can be a component inside an arc-level consent topology.; `whole-script-arc-shape-architecture` — both are whole-arc properties uncitable to any single line, but one names a specific lever (the arc relocates or forecloses the consent gate) while the other is a deliberately loose container of unrelated arc shapes, so a reader should check whether a candidate whole-arc observation is about the consent surface or merely about energy contour.


<a id="entry-318"></a>

### fiction-frame-consent-management

[#318](#entry-318) · [Back to consent-manufacturing](#genus-141) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

TECHNIQUE (fiction boundary as the consent instrument): the fiction/reality boundary is manipulated so consent and defenses calibrated for FICTION get applied to the real payload. Realizations: (a) COLLAPSED RITUAL - an in-fiction consent ritual is collapsed with the meta-frame so one yes serves both diegetic and real. (b) HYPOTHETICAL WRAPPER - a purely-hypothetical framing lets the listener engage without committing, then breaches by design at climax. (c) DIEGETIC-DEVICE ABSORPTION - a channel-change or similar in-world device absorbs authorial responsibility for a content jump so no fresh decision point occurs. (d) IN-FICTION REHEARSAL - inside the fiction the operator narrates moving the subject's body (hand taken, guided, posed with no choices left), so in-fiction consent stands in for real consent and the subject rehearses transferable kinesthetic surrender ('operator decides where my body goes') that generalizes outside the fiction; escalating intimacy rides under 'we're only describing dance steps'.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the FICTION boundary itself is the consent instrument. Transparent narration - openly explaining the mechanism rather than veiling it in fiction - is NOT this. Pick the realization by the boundary move: collapse ritual with meta-frame (a), hypothetical wrapper that breaches (b), diegetic device absorbing responsibility (c), or in-fiction body-mapping rehearsal that generalizes out (d).


**Risk.** Consent threshold lowered by design and breached inside the wrapper (porous hypothetical frame); content jumps inherit consent without a decision point (diegetic channel-change).


**Why it works.** Fiction lowers the cost of engagement — an audience processing narrative applies weaker counter-argument and evaluative scrutiny than to a claim asserted as true, and transported readers show measurable belief shift toward story-consistent propositions afterward. The consent given inside the frame is calibrated to the reduced stakes the frame advertises, so a payload delivered under it collects a decision made about something else. The in-fiction rehearsal variant additionally relies on rehearsal generalizing: a motor or postural compliance practised under a pretext still counts as practice, since the body has no fiction flag. Falsifiable: if this is right, boundary-collapse effects should shrink when the fiction/reality line is explicitly re-marked before the payload; if re-marking changes nothing, the account is wrong. [plausible; narrative transportation and reduced counter-arguing; behavioural rehearsal generalization]


**Worked examples.**

- *One consent ritual covering fiction and audio at once*
  - **Setup.** Opening, in character as two friends, before any hypnotic move at all.
  - **The move.** Before we start — you're still up for this, the thing we talked about last week? Say it out loud for me, properly: yes, I want this. Good. And you'd tell me if you wanted to stop? Say yes to that one too.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening plays as two friends confirming, in character, that they both still want to run something they agreed to earlier — explicit consent asked for more than once, before any hypnotic move. The care is real-sounding, which is what makes the collapse work: the yes is solicited inside the story, but it is the listener's actual voice that supplies it, so one agreement is made to cover both the scene and the recording. Nothing in the exchange constrains the operator afterwards; what it does is settle the listener's anxiety about the premise in advance, which makes the fiction more solid rather than the consent more real.
- *A hypothetical wrapper designed to slip*
  - **Setup.** Mid-piece at the peak, the hypothetical disclaimer having been restated at each escalation.
  - **The move.** None of this is real, remember — we're only supposing. Suppose there were a voice that could lift your thoughts out one at a time, and suppose you let it. And you are letting it, right now, and you can feel them going as I count. Hypothetically, of course. Only a thought experiment.
  - **Why it lands.** Everything is framed as a thought experiment — suppose this were happening, none of it actually is — and the disclaimer is restated each time the material gets heavier. The listener can engage without conceding they are being hypnotized, and can attribute anything they feel to the imagining. Then at the peak the tense quietly shifts from what would happen to what is happening, and a few lines later the wrapper is put back on. The frame was built porous on purpose; the slip is the delivery.
- *An in-world device absorbing the content jump*
  - **Setup.** Mid-scene with a screen present in the fiction; the material is about to jump from mild to explicit.
  - **The move.** The remote is on the arm of the chair, and your hand finds it, and the channel clicks over. We now return you to our regular programming. The picture comes up and it's the other kind, the kind that was on before the interruption, and you settle back into it.
  - **Why it lands.** The material jumps from mild to explicit, and the jump is carried by an in-fiction device: a switch of channel on a screen inside the scene, announced in broadcast idiom as a return to the usual programme. No fresh decision point occurs, because nobody appears to have decided anything — the device did it. The idiom does a second job for free, implying the heavier content was the default all along and the milder material was the interruption.


**Realizations** (1): `in-fiction-consent-rehearsal`


**See also.** `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — adjacent consent-manipulation moves worth cross-reading: A banks a discrete citable agreement and draws it down when refusal would rise; B manipulates the fiction/reality boundary so consent calibrated for fiction covers the real payload. Both defeat live refusal via a prior yes, but A's token is retrievable and cited while B's is a frame confusion, and the collapsed-ritual form of B sits close enough to A that the discriminator is load-bearing.; `consent-counterfeit-theater` — they meet at the collapsed in-fiction ritual, where a diegetic yes is both fabricated and made to serve the real frame; the separation is that the fiction instrument works by letting defenses calibrated for make-believe apply to a real payload, while counterfeit theater needs no fiction layer at all and simply scripts or answers the consent beat itself.; `consent-laundering-wrapper` — both spend consent somewhere other than where it was given, but one uses the fiction/reality boundary as the instrument (defenses calibrated for make-believe applied to the real payload) while the other uses placement within the artifact's architecture, harvesting consent where it is cheap and cashing it where it is expensive with no fiction layer required.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — two ways of making prior consent cover more than it did: widening a consented term by asserted definitional equivalence, or manipulating the fiction boundary so consent calibrated for the fiction applies to the real payload. Same target (the scope of an existing yes), different instrument.; `consent-topology-arc` — both operate on the consent surface across a whole artifact. One is the arc-level topology of where the consent gate sits; the other uses the fiction/reality boundary itself as the consent instrument. Adjacent enough that a cataloguer picking one should check the other.; `covert-frame-entry` — both get consent or entry by exploiting a frame the listener reads as something other than what it is, and the hypothetical-wrapper and cover-story forms sit close. They differ in what the frame is for: one uses the fiction boundary as the consent instrument for a payload, the other uses a false benign frame to cross the entry seam unresisted. Cross-reference rather than merge.; `fantasy-laundered-first-compliance` — both exploit a fiction layer to get compliance without a real consent decision, but one manipulates the fiction/reality boundary so a fictional yes covers the real payload, while the other has the listener physically execute the target act inside the scene before it is ever consciously assigned.; `imagined-to-enacted-collapse` — both exploit the boundary between what is merely described and what is actually done, one by using the fiction layer as the consent instrument and one by sliding tense unflagged from imagined to enacted. The in-fiction rehearsal variant of the first sits close enough to the second that a reader should see both before choosing.; `paratext-precontracting` — both manage consent by moving the decision point away from the real payload. One completes on a reader-buyer through the product surface before playback so the listener arrives pre-committed; the other manipulates the fiction boundary so consent calibrated for fiction is applied to the real content. A writer auditing where consent was actually given needs both.; `withheld-frame-reveal` — both cash an accepted cover for an uncovered payload, but the fiction form relies on the diegetic boundary so defenses calibrated for make-believe apply to the real content, while the withheld-frame form uses a benign non-fictional cover disclosed or reused late, after sunk participation forecloses renegotiation.


<a id="entry-141"></a>

### press-play-consent-laundering

[#141](#entry-141) · [Back to consent-manufacturing](#genus-141) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

The felt 'yes' is manufactured by relabeling something the subject did, did not do, or that merely happened as their authorization, so escalation proceeds with no clean moment to object. Four forms: (a) CONSUMPTION-ACT - a completed/ongoing low-cost act (pressing play, not stopping, staying past a marked point, purchasing, having read the description) is cited, repeatedly, as blanket retroactive authorization for the whole payload; offered exits are staged so NOT taking them manufactures the felt choice. (b) CIRCUMSTANCE-LAUNDERED - every escalation of contact is attributed to an external necessity (rain, cold, a small umbrella) narrated as already-caused fact, so intimacy arrives as accomplished circumstance and the yes is supplied on the subject's behalf. (c) DECLARED-OBSERVATION - each new contact is STATED as an observed fact ('you can feel my finger...') not requested, deleting the assent moment; self-answering lines ('you don't mind, do you? No') enroll forced silence as agreement. (d) QUESTION-TO-COMMAND - a permission question mines the inner yes, is retracted as a grammatical slip, reissued as an imperative that captures it, and resistance is named as already-declined. In every form the refusal channel is eroded, never honored.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when you want escalation to feel consented with NO real choice point - the yes is relabeled from an act, a non-act, a circumstance, or a retracted question, not solicited. Citing a discrete banked artifact (a document, contract, or spoken pledge) with forward reach is a different lever; here the token is the act or fact in the moment. Fabricating a consent exchange the subject never performed is counterfeit theater; here a real act/fact is relabeled. Treating a failure to comprehend as agreement makes the token an epistemic state; and unlike a genuine safety checkpoint, the refusal channel is eroded, never re-verified. Pick the form by what supplies the yes: the subject's own act (a), externalized circumstance (b), operator declaration (c), or a question-command swap (d).


**Risk.** Erodes the refusal channel by construction (fingerprints across all members); many variants extend the laundered contract into waking behavior (one member).


**Why it works.** A small completed act — pressing play, not leaving — is cheap to perform and then expensive to disown, because under self-perception theory people infer their own attitudes from their behaviour and under the consistency principle a first small compliance raises the odds of a larger one (foot-in-the-door, one of the more robust compliance findings). The declared-observation and self-answering forms add a second lever: correcting an asserted fact is conversationally costly, and silence is read by default as assent, so the listener's non-objection is harvested as agreement they never gave. This predicts compliance drops if the triviality of the initial act is made salient, or if an explicit low-cost objection channel is provided. [plausible; self-perception theory; foot-in-the-door; silence-as-assent conversational norm]


**Worked examples.**

- *Choosing to listen inflated into consent to everything*
  - **Setup.** Late in the session, subject deep, nothing left to check the reasoning against; the chain is run several times in slight variations.
  - **The move.** Nobody made you play this. You chose it. Choosing it was accepting it. So what's in it is already yours — and when you do it next week, that's your decision, not mine. It always was.
  - **Why it lands.** The chain is run several times over, in slight variations, until it sounds like reasoning: nobody made you play this. You picked it. Picking it was accepting it. So what it says is already yours, and doing it later is your own decision, not mine. Delivered late, when there is nothing left to check it against, it pre-answers the question the listener will ask on waking about a behaviour they don't remember deciding on — and any resistance now reads as inconsistency with their own earlier choice rather than as refusal.
- *A real exit whose refusal becomes consent*
  - **Setup.** Opening minutes, costs named honestly; a real exit is offered and then relabelled a beat later.
  - **The move.** This will make you want to give me money, and it does not wear off quickly. If that isn't for you, stop the recording now. ... Still here? Then you've decided to play, and we both heard you decide it.
  - **Why it lands.** The costs are named honestly up front and a real exit is offered — stop the recording now if this is not for you. A beat later the operator observes that anyone still present has thereby decided to play. The listener has agreed to nothing; they have declined to leave, and that null act has just been relabelled into a commitment they can subsequently be held to.
- *A marked point past which continuing is agreement*
  - **Setup.** Early framing of the session as a bargain; a line is drawn at a specific sentence.
  - **The move.** The deal is simple: pleasure now, and later you'll want to fund the person who gave it to you. This sentence is the line. Everything past it, you're carrying on freely and knowingly, having accepted the terms — and the rest of this recording is on the far side of it.
  - **Why it lands.** The session is framed as a bargain — pleasure now, in return for wanting to fund the operator later — and then a line is drawn on the floor: past this sentence, carrying on means you accept the terms, freely and knowingly. Consent is pegged to the behaviour already underway, and the material it authorises arrives hundreds of lines further in, by which point it can only be experienced as something already agreed to.
- *The purchase itself cited as the agreement*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a sequel file; the purchase itself is cited as the token of agreement.
  - **The move.** Buying this one means you've accepted you're ready for something harder than the last. Continuing past this point means you've accepted being pushed past comfortable. If not, you can stop — though we've already started, and stopping now means stopping in the middle.
  - **Why it lands.** The contract verb does the work: buying this one means you have accepted that you're ready for something harder than the last. Carrying on past this point means you have accepted being pushed past what's comfortable. An offramp is offered too — but only by interrupting an entry already underway. Objecting later would mean disowning a documented transaction rather than declining a request.


**Realizations** (3): `circumstance-laundered-escalation`, `consent-by-declared-observation`, `question-to-command-consent-laundering`


**See also.** `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — paratext-document token adjudicated there because the act of continuing past it carries the load; `compliance-authorship-laundering` — adjacent laundering moves that a reader will have to choose between: one relabels the compliance act itself as the listener's own will or preference, the other relabels a prior act, non-act, or circumstance as the authorization for what follows. Agency of the act versus the source of the yes.; `compliance-ladder` — both produce a felt yes without fresh persuasion, and the boundary between them is the thing a reader most needs: one accretes real incremental assents that genuinely lower the next rung's cost, the other relabels an act, a non-act, or a circumstance as authorization with no real assent at all.; `consent-checkpoint` — the genuine check and its counterfeits define each other -- a real authorization beat with a waitable response whose failure blocks the move, versus a yes relabeled from an act, a non-act, a circumstance, or a retracted question. A reader evaluating whether a checkpoint is real needs both entries.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both extend a consent the listener already gave, but term-redefinition widens the SCOPE of a word already agreed to via asserted equivalence, while press-play laundering relabels an act, non-act, or circumstance as the yes itself — widening the grant versus manufacturing it.; `ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest` — both manufacture a yes the listener never gave and bank it as standing authorization for later escalation. The split is what supplies the token - a real act, non-act, or circumstance relabeled versus an installed near-involuntary body movement harvested as admission - which is the call a reader must make when a nod is cited as agreement.; `no-lose-double-bind` — adjacent entry-contract shape; split on the contradiction structure; `own-desire-attribution` — r2 secondary; primary rowed there; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — play-act read as completed loss rather than as consent; rowed there; `scope-creep-consent-extension` — sibling consent-erosion levers already cross-referenced in both discriminators: a yes relabeled from an act, non-act, circumstance, or retracted question with scope claimed at once, versus an already-anchored acceptance silently widened afterward. The choice between them is a live classification decision, so the link is load-bearing.; `trivial-act-as-compliance-proof` — both turn a minimal act into leverage, but the output differs: one relabels the act as authorization for what follows, the other reads it backward as proof of broad submission or irresistibility. Each already names the other's territory as the adjacent lever, so the cross-reference helps a reader pick by what the act is made to prove.; `yes-word-valence-priming` — both manufacture a felt yes with no real choice point, and they overlap in the harvesting step where questions are answered on the listener's behalf. One relabels an act, a non-act or a circumstance as authorization; the other pre-charges the word yes with abstract positive value before any request is made. Look for the prior valence-loading to tell them apart.

## consent-on-the-record (4)

Doors where explicit agreements — checkpoints, trial windows, banked yeses — are made into discrete records that gate, bound, or license what happens next.

[cited-prior-agreement-lever](#entry-76) · [consent-checkpoint](#entry-569) · [scope-creep-consent-extension](#entry-320) · [time-boxed-consent-contract](#entry-891)


<a id="entry-76"></a>

### cited-prior-agreement-lever

[#76](#entry-76) · [Back to consent-on-the-record](#genus-184) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

A banked consent artifact cited back: a DISCRETE, retrievable consent record is invoked as already-settled authorization and replayed at the moment refusal would otherwise rise, so objection reads as reneging on one's own agreement; fabricated variants create an empty consent slot the operator populates later. The token has forward reach - it is banked, then drawn down. Realizations: (a) cited document/pact - a retrieved wishlist request, a pre-trance opt-in, a document attributed to the listener, a conversation that never happened, contract terms claimed to have played subliminally, a standing pact with the personified subconscious. (b) blanket pre-authorization contract - an explicit 'for the next hour I'm in control, you'll follow my commands' agreement is solicited early as trivial-and-already-wanted, then drawn down repeatedly at later gates as 'it's what we agreed to' (a consent loan for downstream enforcement, not a protective opt-in). (c) self-spoken surrender pledge - the subject is made to speak a first-person surrender pledge aloud while the operator disclaims being its target ('to trance, not to me'), keeping the guard down; the vocalized artifact is banked and cited back ('you've already surrendered').


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the token is a DISCRETE claimed agreement/document/pledge that can be cited back later (forward reach), not the consumption act (press-play-consent-laundering, token is the act itself) and not a live fabricated exchange (consent-counterfeit-theater, no prior to cite). Pick the realization by the artifact form: an external document/pact (a), a blanket verbal contract extracted in-session (b), or a self-spoken pledge (c).


**Risk.** Fabricated or weaponized consent records erode the refusal channel; blank-check variants (one member) leave an unbounded authorization slot.


**Why it works.** Consistency pressure is the whole engine: once a commitment exists in a form the subject recognizes as their own — especially one that was voluntary, effortful, or spoken aloud — contradicting it imposes a self-concept cost, so complying is cheaper than admitting the earlier agreement was wrong or coerced. The banked artifact also shifts the burden of action onto refusal, which now requires an explicit act of reneging rather than mere non-assent, and defaults are reliably sticky. Falsifiable: it predicts the lever weakens sharply when the subject can attribute the original agreement to external pressure (which removes the self-attribution consistency needs) and fails outright when the cited artifact is one they can confidently deny producing. [established; commitment and consistency; effort/publicness of commitment; default and status-quo bias]


**Worked examples.**

- *The listener's own request quoted back to them*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a session made in response to a request the subject actually sent.
  - **The move.** I read what you wrote to me. "I want to be taken somewhere I can't argue my way out of" — that's your phrasing, isn't it. Well. That's something I can do for you.
  - **Why it lands.** The scene opens with the operator saying she has seen what the listener asked for, and then quoting the request back almost word for word before adding, easily, that this is something she can do. Nothing is negotiated in scene — consent is presented as already given, witnessed, and now being honoured. The specificity is what lands it: with their own words on the table, any later flinch reads internally as inconsistency rather than as refusal.
- *Unstated terms declared already accepted*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; no terms have ever actually been stated aloud in this or any prior recording.
  - **The move.** The terms have been playing underneath my voice this whole time, below where you'd notice — and you accepted them, all of them, in full. I don't need to read them out. You already know what they say.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator states that the agreement's actual terms have been running underneath the audio all along, that they have already been accepted in full — and then closes off the obvious question by asserting the listener already knows what they say. No term is ever spoken aloud. What has been signed is a blank the operator can fill in later, and anything raised in a future session can be presented as part of what was agreed to here.
- *Genuine opt-in re-cited to suppress live refusal*
  - **Setup.** Full waking lucidity at the top; the callback lands deep in the working section with arousal high.
  - **The move.** Top, awake: "This one is about spending money on me. Fifty minimum. You could lose more than you're comfortable with. If that's not for you, stop the recording now." Deep, later: "Isn't it good that you agreed to this at the start, when you were clear-headed? Because otherwise how badly you want to send it right now would be frightening."
  - **Why it lands.** Before any induction, at full waking lucidity, the operator names the destination plainly, sets a minimum spend, states the financial risk, and tells anyone uneasy to stop the recording. That part is real disclosure. The move comes much later, deep in the working section with arousal high: the operator observes how good it is that the listener opted in at the start — because otherwise this compulsion would be frightening. The consent record is not being re-verified; it is being played back at the exact moment refusal would otherwise surface.
- *Standing pact with the personified subconscious*
  - **Setup.** First minute of the recording, before any induction.
  - **The move.** Your subconscious and I settled this a long time ago — it knows when you go under and it doesn't need to check with you first. The conscious part of you isn't a party to that arrangement, and frankly it's not a reliable witness on the subject. So if you feel yourself hesitating, that's just the surface being cautious. The rest of you already said yes.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening claims a long-standing arrangement between the operator and the listener's subconscious about when trance begins — with the conscious mind bracketed as not a party to it and possibly not to be trusted on the question. The gating decision is thereby relocated to an agent the listener cannot speak for: compliance is the pact working, and hesitation is just the conscious part being wary.


**Realizations** (2): `pre-authorization-consent-contract`, `spoken-surrender-pledge-misdirected`


**See also.** `banked-reward-escrow` — real boundary friction: one entry's banked open-ended consent token is close to the other's cited-back agreement artifact. The pointer should carry the split — a discrete retrievable agreement replayed to suppress live refusal, versus a stored value drawn down on an arbitrary later command.; `chosen-descent-ratchet` — adjacent consent-laundering moves that meet where disclosure is reframed as informed agreement: one cites a discrete banked artifact back to suppress live refusal, the other retroactively relabels compliance already underway as the subject's own choice. Check both when an earlier agreement is invoked mid-descent.; `consent-counterfeit-theater` — both foreclose refusal by pointing at an agreement, but one cites a discrete banked artifact with forward reach that can be drawn down repeatedly, while the other fabricates the consent act in the moment with no prior to retrieve — banked token versus counterfeit exchange.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — adjacent consent-manipulation moves worth cross-reading: A banks a discrete citable agreement and draws it down when refusal would rise; B manipulates the fiction/reality boundary so consent calibrated for fiction covers the real payload. Both defeat live refusal via a prior yes, but A's token is retrievable and cited while B's is a frame confusion, and the collapsed-ritual form of B sits close enough to A that the discriminator is load-bearing.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — genuine contrast pair on the same lever family: both cite something back at the listener so refusal reads as self-contradiction. The cut is what is cited - a discrete banked agreement artifact with forward reach versus real recent behavior annotated contemporaneously as evidence of a state. A reader adjudicating a script that cites the listener's past will need both entries to place it correctly.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — paratext-document token adjudicated there because the act of continuing past it carries the load; `rehearsed-pre-commitment` — both bank a commitment for later draw-down. One cites a discrete claimed agreement, document, or pledge back at the moment refusal would rise, so objection reads as reneging; the other rehearses a specific future act while judgment is intact so the decision arrives already made. Artifact-citation versus temporal relocation of the decision is the line.


<a id="entry-569"></a>

### consent-checkpoint

[#569](#entry-569) · [Back to consent-on-the-record](#genus-184) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

An explicit authorization check that must pass before proceeding. In the subject-side form, a clear affirmative opt-in (breath, nod, verbal yes) is solicited and WAITED FOR before deepening or sensitive work. In the operator-side form, the practitioner verifies they hold authority, permission, resources, and skills for this client before any assessment or intervention — and withholds the move entirely when the check fails. Either way the operator is the constrained party after the move runs.


**When to reach for this.** A REAL check with a waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action — every counterfeit in consent-counterfeit-theater forecloses, fabricates, or retroactively relabels the response instead of waiting for it.


**Risk.** The technique IS a consent safeguard: it opens a live check-in channel mid-session, restoring the subject's evaluative voice rather than eroding it; no consent surface of its own.


**Why it works.** The waited-for response is what makes the check informative: an unanswered request carries no information about willingness, whereas a solicited affirmative that the operator must actually wait to receive creates a genuine refusal channel — the subject can withhold, and withholding has an effect on what happens next. Compliance research shows that assent extracted under foreclosed or presumptive framing predicts subsequent behaviour poorly, because the subject was never given a low-cost path to decline. Falsifiable: if subjects who pass a waited-for checkpoint show the same rate of later distress, withdrawal, or retrospective non-endorsement as subjects given a presumptive check, the response beat is doing no work. [plausible; informativeness of a real refusal option; assent validity]


**Worked examples.**

- *Operator verifies their own authorization before acting*
  - "who has the authority, permission, resources, and skills to complete an assessment and intervene… If a practitioner does not have authority or permission, then the analyst's role… is restricted." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-constraining checks that block the action until something is verified, and they differ only in what is verified: the subject's affirmative authorization versus the reality of the subject's depth behind a look-alike sign. Close enough to confuse, distinct enough to keep separate, so the cross-link is the right call.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both constrain the operator before proceeding, and the contrast is the useful part. One solicits an affirmative opt-in and waits for it; the other tests the want empirically by building and entering an example, then commits or aborts on the lived result. Choose by whether assent is collected or evidence is generated.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — the genuine check and its counterfeits define each other -- a real authorization beat with a waitable response whose failure blocks the move, versus a yes relabeled from an act, a non-act, a circumstance, or a retracted question. A reader evaluating whether a checkpoint is real needs both entries.; `suitability-screening` — two positive-governance gates that both leave the operator as the constrained party, differing in what they gate. One is an authorization check with a real waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action. The other screens whether to proceed with this person at all, on fitness or contraindication grounds. Anyone selecting a genuine gate should see both and pick by object — this moment versus this person.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — both are genuine governance moves in which the operator ends up the constrained party, differing in whether a single waitable check gates the action or termination authority is relocated to the subject as a standing relationship property. Not a merge, since one blocks on failure and the other has no failure branch to block on.


<a id="entry-320"></a>

### scope-creep-consent-extension

[#320](#entry-320) · [Back to consent-on-the-record](#genus-184) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

TECHNIQUE (no-decision-point extension of an accepted anchor): an acceptance granted at one scope/meaning is silently extended, widened, or overwritten to broader or heavier scope with NO felt decision point, the trajectory hidden inside a structure that pattern-matches as education, focus, preamble, or a continuation. Realizations: (a) SCOPE-CREEP - each heavier claim arrives as merely the next dictionary definition of an already-accepted word, adjacent operator-chosen wants ride a high-confidence certain want as carrier, or consent to a whole category of unseen orders is imputed before any content is named. (b) OBJECT-CLASS SLIDE - one uninterrupted emptying list begins with consented negative-valence contents (worries, fears) and widens item-by-item into agency-bearing contents (desires, memories, will), each item reading as a continuation, so an identity-strip runs under cover of accepted serenity. (c) CONCENTRIC RING-WIDENING - a single installed trigger is anchored at an innermost narrowly-consented ring, then its firing-set is expanded outward through progressively wider rings (physical->hypnotic->relational->everyday); the ordering is load-bearing (the widest ring would be refused at the door). (d) DEFINITIONAL OVERWRITE - a trusted term the listener already uses ('open your mind' = going blank) is explicitly named, validated, then overwritten with a new active meaning ('a choice to accept and understand new learning'), installing a covert obligation to whatever content comes next parasitically on top of a trusted word.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the lever is silent extension/overwrite of an ANCHORED acceptance (a word, a list, a trigger, a want) with no fresh decision point. Pick the realization by what is stretched: a word/want's claimed scope (a), a list's object-class (b), a trigger's firing-set (c), or a term's very meaning replaced (d). Note (d) is definitional REPLACEMENT where (a)-(c) WIDEN an existing scope.


**Risk.** Consent-creep from property to thoughts and orgasms without a felt decision point; category pre-licensing of unseen orders. Refusal never solicited, scope silently widened.


**Why it works.** Category boundaries are fuzzy and each small step is judged against the immediately preceding step rather than the starting point, so a sequence of individually-negligible extensions crosses a distance that would have been refused as a single move — the standard foot-in-the-door and gradual-escalation result. Consistency pressure supplies the ratchet: having accepted step n, refusing step n+1 requires explaining what changed, and no salient change is available. The definitional-overwrite variant exploits the fact that people track the token of a familiar word more than its current definition, so trust attaches to the label and transfers to the substituted content. Falsifiable: the model predicts refusal rates spike if the endpoint is presented first or if a step is made discontinuous enough to register as a new decision. [established; foot-in-the-door; just-noticeable-difference escalation; consistency principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each heavier claim as the next dictionary entry*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, staged as a short vocabulary lesson on a word already accepted.
  - **The move.** Let's take the word own. First sense: to have a thing as your property — simple enough. Second sense: to have taken it over completely. Third: to have the say over what it does with its body. Fourth: to have the say over what it thinks. Same word all the way down, and you agreed to it at the first one.
  - **Why it lands.** The passage is staged as a short vocabulary lesson: here is the first sense of the word, here is the second, here is the third. The first is unobjectionable — holding something as property. Each subsequent numbered sense claims more: being taken over, then owning what the listener's body does, then owning what they think. Because the format is a list of definitions, every increment arrives as a clarification of a term already accepted rather than as a fresh demand, and no point in the sequence presents itself as a decision. A listener who would have refused the last item outright never encounters it as an item to refuse.
- *Consent to a category before any content is named*
  - **Setup.** Before a single instruction has been named; four clauses delivered in one breath.
  - **The move.** In a moment I'm going to start giving you instructions. You'll follow them — that's natural, it's what this state is for, and you'll enjoy every one of them. And you agreed to all of that when you pressed play, so there's nothing left for you to decide.
  - **Why it lands.** Before naming a single instruction, the operator lays down four quick clauses: instructions are coming, they will be followed, they are natural, they are enjoyable, and the listener already agreed to this. Each one forecloses a different objection — surprise, refusal, strangeness, coercion — in advance. By the time actual content appears, agreement has been given to the whole class of thing it belongs to, sight unseen.
- *A certain want used as carrier for chosen ones*
  - **Setup.** Subject has just named things they genuinely want; the rule is stated on top of them.
  - **The move.** Hold on to the things you know you want — no arguing with those, they're properly yours. Concentrate on them, only them, and feel how easy that is. And whatever sits next to them slides in just as easily, including the ones I hand you; wanting the one is wanting the other.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to concentrate only on the things they are already sure of wanting — no argument required, since these are genuinely theirs. The rule then states that concentrating this way makes adjacent wants easy to take on, including ones the operator picks. A high-confidence desire becomes a carrier wave, and each later instruction is received as something wanted rather than something imposed.


**Realizations** (3): `concentric-scope-laundering`, `serenity-list-agency-strip`, `term-redefinition-smuggle`


**See also.** `chosen-descent-ratchet` — both manipulate consent without widening the actual refusal channel: one retroactively relabels a move already running as chosen, the other silently stretches an anchored acceptance with no decision point at all.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — the second entry's definitional-overwrite realization is precisely the first entry's move: a trusted term is named, validated, then given a new meaning so later demands inherit the earlier acceptance. Not calling merge because the second is a broader family that also covers widening a list's object class and expanding a trigger's firing set, which the first does not cover. Link so the overlap is visible and the eventual absorb-or-keep decision is easy.; `consent-topology-arc` — both operate on the consent surface, and a reader deciding between them needs the scope test. One is a whole-arc topology cited to the shape of the entire artifact; the other is local extension of a specific anchored acceptance (a word, a list, a trigger's firing-set) with no felt decision point. Useful pointer because a scope-creep run can be a component inside an arc-level consent topology.; `covert-scope-authorization` — same family — an acceptance is widened without a fresh decision point — differing in where the widening is hidden: inside an anchored term, list, or trigger in the body, versus in a procedural pre-induction slot processed as housekeeping. A reader classifying a scope-broadening line needs the placement distinction, so the cross-link earns its place.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — sibling consent-erosion levers already cross-referenced in both discriminators: a yes relabeled from an act, non-act, circumstance, or retracted question with scope claimed at once, versus an already-anchored acceptance silently widened afterward. The choice between them is a live classification decision, so the link is load-bearing.


<a id="entry-891"></a>

### time-boxed-consent-contract

[#891](#entry-891) · [Back to consent-on-the-record](#genus-184) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A negotiated agreement is bounded in time with autonomy structurally preserved — a fixed trial window with a standing instruction that any dissatisfied part signals for renegotiation, or a fixed-period suspension of an existing choice (e.g. the suicide option, for three months) with promised help afterward. Bounding lowers the cost of saying yes, backsliding is recast as notification-to-renegotiate rather than proof the deal was wrong, and no choice is ever permanently removed.


**When to reach for this.** Post-deal commitment STRUCTURE — a duration bound plus a subject-invoked re-open channel — rather than a pre-scene consent check, an auto-expiring cue-response pair, or an ambient-programming expiry suggestion.


**Risk.** Autonomy-preserving contract design; the operator is the constrained party after the move runs.


**Why it works.** A bounded commitment is cheaper to accept than an open-ended one because the worst case is capped, which is the standard foot-in-the-door structure — and once the trial is entered, the consistency principle makes continuation the low-friction path. The re-open channel matters because it removes the reactance that a locked deal would generate: retaining an exit preserves perceived freedom, so agreement does not have to be defended against one's own sense of being trapped. Falsifiable: identical agreements offered unbounded should show lower acceptance and higher mid-course abandonment than bounded ones. [plausible; foot-in-the-door; consistency principle; reactance reduction via retained exit]


**Worked examples.**

- *Six-week trial with a renegotiation channel*
  - "test this agreement for the next six weeks… If either one becomes dissatisfied during this time, then they will notify you, so that you can negotiate further." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Suspending a choice without removing it*
  - "I will accept you as a client only if you give up the possibility of suicide for three months... I'll even help you do it. Do you agree to that?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `consent-laundering-wrapper` — near-inverses on the same axis: whether the consent question is re-openable at the point it is spent. One bounds the deal in time and installs a standing channel to renegotiate; the other harvests assent where it is cheap and cashes it where it is expensive, never re-opening. Best read as a contrast pair.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are governance structures that condition a deal on the subject's continuing endorsement, and they compose directly: an experiential trial supplies the evidence for the yes, a time bound plus a re-open channel is what that yes is granted under. A reader designing a consent-valid install will want both halves.


<a id="genus-264"></a>

## consent-spent-elsewhere (2)

Consent gathered under a benign cover frame is cashed later for a payload the listener never agreed to, at a moment when renegotiation is foreclosed.

[consent-laundering-wrapper](#entry-1016) · [withheld-frame-reveal](#entry-454)


<a id="entry-1016"></a>

### consent-laundering-wrapper

[#1016](#entry-1016) · [Back to consent-spent-elsewhere](#genus-264) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent · kind: container*

A deferred-cash consent envelope: a benign structural frame/part/pass, by its PLACEMENT within the artifact, launders a malign payload the subject never separately consented to - consent is harvested where it is cheap, deniable, or already-given, and cashed where it is expensive, involuntary, or novel, with the question deliberately never re-opened at the point that matters. What is manipulated is the ARCHITECTURE of where consent sits versus where it is spent, not any single line.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the lever is a spanning STRUCTURAL relationship (the frame is load-bearing architecture - induction, deepening, transitions, and exit all depend on it, and it actively removes exit routes while the surface reads as permission), not a single-move relabel (treating pressing play as consent, citing a past agreement, framing the descent as the subject's own choice) and not decorative theming. The consent is not consumed where it is stated; it is cashed elsewhere in the arc. Pick the realization by geometry: whole-artifact wrapper (a), entry->climax bracket (b), cheap->expensive gradient (c), two-script production graft (d), or near-repetition restatement (e).


**Risk.** Erodes the refusal channel by making exit and resistance read as breaking the subject's own chosen fiction, while an operator-owned stop-rule and resistance-feeds-the-state mechanisms sit foreclosed in the interior.


**Why it works.** Consent decisions are anchored on the terms present when the decision is made, and people do not spontaneously re-audit a standing agreement as its scope grows — the same structure that makes negative-option billing and buried terms-of-service clauses effective. Separating the point of agreement from the point of use exploits the absence of a natural re-evaluation trigger: nothing in the artifact prompts the reassessment that would surface the mismatch. Falsifiable: inserting an explicit re-consent checkpoint before the expensive content should reduce completion for the malign payload while leaving the benign frame's completion unchanged; if it changes neither, the placement is not load-bearing. [plausible; anchoring on initial terms; absence of a re-evaluation trigger in standing agreements]


**Worked examples.**

- *Nested fictions consume the exit two frames back*
  - **Setup.** Opening minute, before any induction; subject seated at home, told only that they are about to watch something.
  - **The move.** Get comfortable and look at the screen in front of you — you're just watching tonight, nothing more is being asked of you.
