On five you're still in your chair; on three the glass has gone soft; on one you're standing on the other side of it, in the picture, and the picture is around you. Good. Now let's change the channel.
  - **Why it lands.** The recording opens with the listener at home in front of a screen — a spectator, which is the safest possible position to occupy. A countdown then pulls them through the glass and into the programme as its subject. Once inside, the channel simply changes, and the content on the other side is nothing they were shown at the door. Every transition was an operator move performed on a passive viewer, and the defence they arrived with — I'm only watching this — was spent two frames ago, at a point where the material was mild enough that spending it cost nothing. The frame is also load-bearing everywhere else: the induction is the viewing, the deepening is a zoom, the topic changes are channel changes, so removing it would leave half the moves with no vehicle.
- *Permissive mouth, locked throat*
  - **Setup.** First ninety seconds, permissions block; nothing installed yet, subject still fully alert and free to stop.
  - **The move.** Stop the recording any time you like — it costs you nothing, and listening the whole way through without going under is a perfectly fine outcome. Take exactly as much of this as you want. Later, when you're deeper, if some part of you starts arguing, that's fine too — every push you make just feeds the thing you're pushing against, and the only way out from there is when I hand you the word for it.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening is saturated with autonomy: pause whenever you like, it's completely fine to listen all the way through without going under, take on as much or as little of this as you actually want. The interior is built the other way — pushing back is defined as more fuel for what is already running, and the sole way out on offer is a device the operator hands over and controls. Nothing in the ending contradicts the beginning; the permissions were simply issued where they were cheap, and never reissued at the point where they would have cost the operator the install.
- *Cast as the protagonist, so refusal breaks character*
  - **Setup.** Third or fourth line of the recording, before the induction proper; subject has just settled and knows only the title of the piece.
  - **The move.** You aren't a listener tonight — you're the girl in the story, and this is the part where she goes down the hole. Everything that happens from here happens to her, and she does it because that's who she is. So when I tell her to keep falling, she keeps falling, because a heroine who stops at the second page isn't much of a heroine.
  - **Why it lands.** From the third line the listener is not a subject being hypnotised but the heroine of a storybook fall, and the whole session is her adventure underground. This converts "do what the hypnotist says" into "be the character you came here to be," so declining an instruction is no longer a refusal, it is spoiling the story. The whimsy does a second job: losing the thread of a thought or feeling a little mad is exactly what this place is famously like, so the listener reads their own destabilisation as the tale delivering on its promise.


**Realizations** (4): `consent-bracket-architecture`, `consent-topology-graft`, `escalating-consent-erosion-gradient`, `restatement-laundered-commitment`


**See also.** `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both widen consent beyond what was granted. One does it by swapping a term's referent in place, the other by placing the consent moment far from where it is spent. Reading the local move against the architectural one sharpens both.; `covert-frame-entry` — two positions on one consent-architecture axis. One uses a false benign frame to cross the entry seam before a resistance surface forms; the other places a permission early and cheap and spends it later where it would be expensive, never re-opening the question. Entry-concealment and deferred cash-out are frequently stacked in the same piece, and each entry's boundary is stated against the other.; `covert-restatement-laundering` — both exploit apparent repetition, but one hides a between-pass delta in a single restatement while the other is a spanning architecture that harvests consent where it is cheap and cashes it where it is expensive.; `covert-scope-authorization` — both turn on where consent sits versus where it is spent, and each discriminator already names the other as adjacent. One is a placement trick on a scope-widening line, the other a spanning structural envelope — an explicit cross-reference keeps them from collapsing.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — both spend consent somewhere other than where it was given, but one uses the fiction/reality boundary as the instrument (defenses calibrated for make-believe applied to the real payload) while the other uses placement within the artifact's architecture, harvesting consent where it is cheap and cashing it where it is expensive with no fiction layer required.; `model-coherence-laundering` — both bank an acceptance cheaply and cash it where refusal would be expensive, so a reader choosing between them needs the split: one manipulates the ARCHITECTURE of where consent sits versus where it is spent; the other cashes an accepted premise or model as logical entailment. Same asymmetry, different currency.; `paratext-precontracting` — both separate where consent is collected from where it is spent. One completes on a reader-buyer through the product surface before playback, so the listener arrives pre-committed; the other places a benign structural frame within the artifact and cashes it against a payload never separately agreed to. Same deferred-consent logic at two different scopes.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — both relocate where consent sits relative to where it is spent: one onto a not-self locus that acts and agrees, one onto an architectural frame that harvests assent cheaply and cashes it expensively. A reader picking a consent-displacement structure wants both on the table.; `time-boxed-consent-contract` — near-inverses on the same axis: whether the consent question is re-openable at the point it is spent. One bounds the deal in time and installs a standing channel to renegotiate; the other harvests assent where it is cheap and cashes it where it is expensive, never re-opening. Best read as a contrast pair.; `weaponized-safety-framing` — both repurpose a protective-looking surface, but one makes a single safety element carry or license the payload while the other manipulates the architecture of where consent sits versus where it is spent. A reader deciding between a local safety frame and a spanning consent envelope needs both.


<a id="entry-454"></a>

### withheld-frame-reveal

[#454](#entry-454) · [Back to consent-spent-elsewhere](#genus-264) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

A concealed frame, cashed: run the session under a stated benign frame or vehicle the subject accepts, then CASH that accepted cover for an uncovered payload without re-consent — either by disclosing late that it was secretly something else, or by reusing/unmasking the vehicle to license a payload it never openly covered, so the payload reads as continuous with what was already agreed to. Two variants: (a) withheld-frame reveal — DISCLOSE, after compliance/depth/irreversibility has accumulated, that the interaction was a trap/conditioning/capture; the LATE reveal retroactively reclassifies sunk participation as consent and is TIMED where renegotiation is foreclosed (post-restraint/climax/ingestion, max depth, or post-wake); (b) preloaded frame licenses the payload — pre-load a benign-seeming frame/vehicle (a faked anti-hypnosis architecture, an empty legitimizing meta-rule, a neutral entrained oscillator already consented to) and later REUSE or unmask it to justify the payload, so prior acceptance is the lever that makes the later payload non-refusable.


**When to reach for this.** Requires an accepted benign cover CASHED for an uncovered payload — the acceptance-then-cash asymmetry is the lever. Decoy-frame entry uses a false frame to get IN unresisted, with no payload cash-out. Presupposing the change as already true asserts it upfront, concealing nothing. The own-acts surrender ledger annotates real acts openly as they accrue — no hidden game. Pick the variant by the cash-out mechanism: a LATE disclosure that reclassifies sunk cost (the reveal), or REUSE/unmasking of a pre-accepted vehicle to license the payload.


**Risk.** Fabricates consent over completed experience and pre-empts the post-session verification window (kumiho thought-as-consent beat; twin-scientists post-restraint timing).


**Why it works.** Sunk participation is reinterpreted rather than repudiated: the consistency principle and effort justification make it psychologically cheaper to accept a revised account of what one was doing than to conclude one was deceived while continuing to participate. Timing the reveal after depth, restraint, or climax exploits the fact that the reappraisal window closes once the act is irreversible — there is no longer an action the reinterpretation could change. Falsifiable: revealing the true frame early, before commitment accrues, should produce refusal rather than acceptance; if late and early reveals worked equally, the sunk-cost account would be wrong. [plausible; consistency / effort justification, sunk cost, choice-supportive reappraisal]


**Worked examples.**

- *The stated game was never the real game*
  - **Setup.** Thirty minutes in, at maximum depth; the session has run under a stated benign frame the subject accepted at the start.
  - **The move.** You can stop trying to relax now, because that was never what this was. What has been running for the last half hour is conditioning, and it's finished. It's not something I'm offering you — it's done, it's in, and it was in some minutes ago. And if part of you wants to object: I could hear that you wanted this from the first minute. You just couldn't hear it yourself.
  - **Why it lands.** Thirty minutes in, at the point of least critical capacity, the operator drops the frame the session was sold under: what was actually being run was something else, it has been running the whole time, and it is finished. The conditioning is then described in the past tense — not asked for, not offered, reported as an accomplished fact. Because the announcement comes after the participation rather than before it, the listener has nothing left to decline; everything they already did is retroactively re-labelled as the thing being announced. A second move closes the last gap: any objection is pre-answered by claiming the listener silently wanted it, evidence for which the operator alone can see.
- *Disclosure timed to when exit is foreclosed*
  - **Setup.** Scene has been staged as a benign setup and the subject is now fully secured within it; disclosure lands only at that point.
  - **The move.** There — that's the last strap. Comfortable? Good. So I should tell you what tonight is actually for, now that we're here. I wasn't going to bring it up earlier, because earlier it would have been a question, and you'd have had to decide. It isn't a question now. It's just what we're already doing.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is walked through a benign setup and only once the scene has them fully secured does the operator explain, in a tone of friendly candour, what the session is actually for. The timing is the whole move: the same sentence delivered ten minutes earlier would be an offer that could be declined, and delivered here it is an update on something already underway. Withdrawing now would mean disowning the cooperation already spent getting to this point.
- *Prior engagement re-read as evidence of identity*
  - **Setup.** Two-thirds through; the subject has stayed with the recording for twenty minutes and the pivot to heavier material is framed as a deduction.
  - **The move.** Everything up to here was the gentle version. I'm not going to ask whether you want the rest, because you already answered — you picked this file out of everything you could have picked, and you're still here twenty minutes later. People who aren't what you are turn it off in the first five. So we both know what you are. Let's get on with it.
  - **Why it lands.** Two-thirds of the way through, the operator announces that everything so far was the gentle version and pivots to heavier material — but frames the pivot as a deduction rather than a request. The listener chose this recording, and stayed with it this long; that behaviour, the operator says, is what tells them what the listener is. Declining now would require explaining away twenty minutes of one's own attention, which is more work than accepting the label.
- *Disclosure after the fictional dose is metabolized*
  - **Setup.** Imagined scene; the subject was handed something to drink with no explanation and has already drunk it in the fiction.
  - **The move.** Empty glass. Good. [forty lines later] I should tell you what that was. It bonds to the tissue — that's why it doesn't wash out, why there's no back from it. It's already through you by now. There was never anything for you to agree to; you drank it forty lines ago.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is handed something to drink in the imagined scene and drinks it, with no explanation attached. Forty lines later the operator reveals what it supposedly was and what it supposedly does — and adds that its effect is permanent because of how the substance bonds to the body. There is now no instruction on the table to refuse, only a past act to accept, and the claimed irreversibility is laundered through invented chemistry rather than asserted by the operator.


**Realizations** (1): `preloaded-frame-licenses-uncovered-payload`


**See also.** `banked-reward-escrow` — both store something now and draw against it later rather than spending it live. A banks a reward or a pre-signed open-ended consent token for later discharge; B banks an accepted benign cover and cashes it for an uncovered payload. The consent-token variant of A sits directly on B's boundary, so the discriminators need to be read together.; `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — both run a payload under an accepted benign frame, but one never uncovers it (the frame stays a genuine surface delivering the payload as a deeper instance of itself) while the other cashes the accepted cover, either by late disclosure or by unmasking the vehicle to license a payload it never covered.; `covert-role-frame-accretion` — both keep the real relational or purpose frame off the table until evaluation is foreclosed, but one cashes an explicitly accepted benign cover for an uncovered payload while the other never declares the frame at all, building it by trajectory so there is no seam to accept or refuse.; `disavowal-and-masking` — direct boundary risk: running an induction inside a frame the listener is told is not an induction sits next to accepting a benign cover and later cashing it for an uncovered payload. The split is whether concealment is the whole move or whether an accepted frame is later drawn down as authorization.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — both cash an accepted cover for an uncovered payload, but the fiction form relies on the diegetic boundary so defenses calibrated for make-believe apply to the real content, while the withheld-frame form uses a benign non-fictional cover disclosed or reused late, after sunk participation forecloses renegotiation.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — reveal vehicle; placed here because the load is act-reassignment not concealed-game disclosure.; `weaponized-safety-framing` — both repurpose an accepted frame, but the levers differ: one makes a protective-sounding surface carry or license the payload, the other cashes a benign cover for an uncovered payload. Worth a cross-check where a bounding-style carve-out is offered early and drawn on later.


<a id="genus-196"></a>

## control-through-proxies (4)

Doors where the pressure comes from an installed or in-scene third party — a sub-agent, servitor, or confederate — so commands and contests route around the listener's direct resistance to the operator.

[covert-provocation-confederate-rescue](#entry-1237) · [externalized-agent-body-scan](#entry-463) · [proxy-agent-resistance-offload](#entry-545) · [sub-agent-command-firewall](#entry-681)


<a id="entry-1237"></a>

### covert-provocation-confederate-rescue

[#1237](#entry-1237) · [Back to control-through-proxies](#genus-196) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Instead of announced role-play, the operator behaves so as to actually drive the subject into the genuine problem state without revealing the frame (throwing the timid client out of the office); a pre-arranged confederate happens to be present, gains total rapport on the rebound, and programs the coping response. Because the new learning attaches to the genuinely evoked state rather than a pretend rehearsal state, it transfers when future-paced instead of staying a rehearsal.


**When to reach for this.** The frame is never announced (the provocation is made to feel real) AND a staged confederate supplies the rescue-and-program on the rebound; not overt role-play, announced practice, or in-session future-pacing of an imagined scene.


**Risk.** Covertly induces real distress with no frame disclosure and staged third parties; the source is conspicuously silent on consent.


**Why it works.** Learning is state-dependent: responses acquired in a genuine affective state are retrieved more reliably in that state than responses rehearsed in a calm one, so training a coping response while the real fear is running produces better transfer than imagined rehearsal. The confederate's rescue additionally exploits misattribution of arousal and post-threat relief, which inflate felt rapport toward whoever is present at the moment of relief. Predicts measurably better generalization than matched role-play rehearsal, and it would fail if announced-frame rehearsal transferred equally well. [plausible; state-dependent learning; misattribution of arousal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Unannounced provocation, then a staged rescue*
  - "it will always work better if you don't announce that the frame is role-playing; you just do it. … Then if you have somebody pick them up on the bounce" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


<a id="entry-463"></a>

### externalized-agent-body-scan

[#463](#entry-463) · [Back to control-through-proxies](#genus-196) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: pacing-rapport*

Runs a progressive somatic body-scan in which the RELAXER is not the listener but an externalized non-self agent — warm jacuzzi jets, the operator's narrated hands placed down the body, a cumulative warmth-vector massage — so the listener is recast as recipient-of-action rather than actor. The scan grafts arousal onto relaxation (a parked stimulator, co-listed arousal/obedience, a genital-skip anticipation gradient) so a sexual signal stays live through an otherwise sedative pass, and the self-generated proprioceptive change reads as externally caused, installing operator-presence-in- the-room without consent friction.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is an EXTERNALIZED agent doing the relaxing on a passive body during a progressive scan (agency handoff), often with an arousal graft.


**Risk.** Installs operator-presence and arousal-yoked relaxation with agency handed off; session-scoped, reversible, no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Attention directed to a body region reliably produces real sensation there — warmth, heaviness, tingling — which the technique then gives a false cause; this is a source-monitoring error, where an internally generated percept is misattributed to an external agent. Because the subject genuinely feels something and the only supplied explanation is the narrated hands or jets, the operator's presence is confirmed by the subject's own body rather than asserted. Falsifiable: if attention-directed body scans with no externalized agent produce equal reported sense of another presence in the room, the agency handoff is doing no work. [plausible; source-monitoring error; attention-induced somatic sensation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Cumulative warmth chain with one region withheld*
  - **Setup.** Progressive upward scan underway from the feet; the operator is holding a chain refrain.
  - **The move.** Your feet are loose and warm. Your calves are loose and warm — feet, calves. Your thighs: loose and warm, and so are your feet and your calves. Now your belly — loose and warm, along with your thighs, your calves, your feet. We'll leave your chest for last; it's waiting its turn. Your shoulders now: loose and warm, and your belly, your thighs, your calves, your feet, all of it.
  - **Why it lands.** The scan walks upward from the extremities, and at each new region the operator recites the whole path travelled so far rather than just the current stop, so that by the upper body the full chain has been rehearsed several times over and naming any one link re-lights the others. Two riders travel with it. The refrain lists muscular looseness and heat in the same breath every time, so the two states are never available separately afterwards. And one region is explicitly skipped on the way up, announced as being saved for last — which makes the untouched place louder than any of the touched ones.
- *Warm jets, not the listener, do the relaxing*
  - **Setup.** Subject settled in an imagined warm-water setting; progressive relaxation about to begin.
  - **The move.** The jets are behind you at the small of your back — feel them start. They work up along your spine one row at a time, pushing the tightness out of you; you don't have to relax anything, the water is doing it. Now they move to your shoulders, your neck. One jet stays behind, right at the base of your spine, still pulsing there while the others carry on up — leave it, it knows what it's doing.
  - **Why it lands.** The relaxation pass runs region by region up the body as usual, but the listener never relaxes anything: an external warm agent in the imagined setting does it to them, one area at a time. Agency over the body is handed to that agent, and the listener is recast as the one being worked on. Midway, one source of the warmth is left parked in place while the rest keep travelling — so a live signal is held open through what would otherwise be a purely sedative sweep, and the two states are grafted rather than left to compete.
- *The operator's narrated hands travel down the body*
  - **Setup.** Subject reclined, eyes closed, operator's presence being established as physical.
  - **The move.** I'm putting both hands on your shoulders now. Feel the weight of them, and feel the warmth spread down from where they rest. Now I'm moving them to your upper arms — feel that warmth pass across, and your arms get heavier as it does. Now my palms on your chest, and your breathing slows under them.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator narrates placing her hands on the listener and then working downward through the body region by region, asking at each contact point that the listener imagine the touch and feel warmth pass across it. The heaviness that results is manufactured by the listener, but because it is keyed to a described external hand it reads as delivered. Relaxation is the visible purpose; the durable result is that the operator now has a body in the room.


**See also.** `covert-payload-piggyback` — both hide a payload inside a consented progressive body scan, but one hands somatic agency to an externalized agent doing the relaxing, while the other leaves the scan intact and overwrites the body-image self-model through the station descriptors.; `progressive-relaxation` — direct parent-and-variant relation already asserted in the second entry's own discriminator: the same region-by-region somatic sweep, but with an externalized agent doing the relaxing and often an arousal graft. Anyone classifying a body-scan passage must decide between exactly these two.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both transfer felt somatic agency to an external agent, and a writer will choose between them. One narrates an outside agent relaxing a passive body with no real touch occurring; the other requires a genuine self-generated touch whose authorship is then re-credited to the operator. Whether the listener actually moves is the deciding test.; `somatic-carrier-sweep` — both propagate something through the body while the listener tracks it, and both must be told apart from an ordinary progressive scan. One hands the relaxing to an externalized agent acting on a passive body; the other vectors a single sensation as a carrier delivering a payload state. Real confusion boundary.


<a id="entry-545"></a>

### proxy-agent-resistance-offload

[#545](#entry-545) · [Back to control-through-proxies](#genus-196) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

Install an AUTONOMOUS agent that holds real decision-authority the listener defers to, and route the contest through it — displacing surrender-agency off the listener onto a party 'programmed never to lose'. The agent's representational LOCATION (inner part vs in-scene figure) is a parameter. VARIANTS: (a) externally-authored obedient inner character [proxy-agent-resistance-offload] — a named, persistent, seeded-by-a-prior-file part that is definitionally obedient and exempt from justification; the listener's resistance is reframed from 'me vs the operator' (winnable) into 'me vs an internal part that never loses' (defeat structurally guaranteed), and irrational beliefs the listener's reason would reject are assigned to the proxy ('doesn't need it to make sense') and radiated in via a shared-mind premise as ambient feeling; (b) aftercare-clause subconscious [guardian-delegation-inner-agent] — a safety/reassurance clause that names the 'subconscious' as a competent autonomous decision-holder owning the off-switch and timing ('removing the lipstick ends the effects AND your subconscious already knows when to put it on'); the reassurance IS the installation, defusing 'what if I can't turn this off' anxiety while relocating the off-switch into an installed inner authority rather than returning it to the listener; (c) interposed in-scene proxy [interposed-proxy-agent] — a separate figure in the scene is granted real agency and made the actual command-issuer while the operator recedes to narrator (draws the listener in, guides their hands, supplies affection the stranger-operator could not credibly give); authorship diffuses to the admired proxy so compliance feels like inclusion/identification, and the proxy is staged as a permanent occupant carried out of session ('she can live for you'), the wake omitted. Pick by inner-combatant vs aftercare-subconscious vs in-scene-actor — but all install a delegated authority the listener cannot simply reclaim.


**When to reach for this.** Installs an autonomous agent (inner part OR in-scene figure) that HOLDS authority against the listener and carries the contest/belief, rather than the listener inhabiting it — the tell is delegated decision-authority the listener defers to and cannot simply reclaim. External-scene proxy vs inner named character vs ambient subconscious is the agent's location, a parameter.


**Risk.** Structurally guarantees the listener's defeat and smuggles operator-as-god / words-as-divine-truth past critical evaluation as ambient feeling — direct erosion of the refusal and reason/verification channel; depends on a prior file (out-of-session composition), no bounding present.


**Why it works.** Attributing a decision to an agent other than oneself removes the self-concept cost of complying — the agentic-state/responsibility-displacement result from the obedience literature, where compliance rises when an authority is seen to own the outcome (not diffusion of responsibility, which requires multiple co-present bystanders dividing an obligation). Naming a part and giving it persistent character exploits the near-automatic readiness to attribute intention to a described agent, making the delegation feel discovered rather than installed. Falsifiable: framing an identical demand as issuing from a named autonomous agent should change compliance rates and reported ownership of the decision; if compliance were purely the subject's own, it would not. [plausible; diffusion of responsibility; agency attribution / intentional stance]


**Worked examples.**

- *An inner opponent programmed never to lose*
  - **Setup.** Mid-file; the inner figure was seeded by an earlier session and is now narrated acting on the listener, never addressed to him.
  - **The move.** She's already at it — I can hear her from here. She's dragging at your sense of where you end, taking the room a foot at a time, and the only reason you can still follow my voice at all is that she's allowing it. I'm not going to argue with you tonight; I don't need to. She was built not to lose.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator does not argue with the listener at all — she narrates a figure already installed inside him doing the pulling: it is dragging at your sense of being, taking the room a little at a time, and the only reason you are still following this is that it permits you to. The contest is moved from listener-versus-operator, which could be won, to listener-versus-a-part-of-himself that was built obedient. Defeat is guaranteed by construction, and the surrender belongs to the figure rather than to him.
- *Belief routed through a proxy exempt from proof*
  - **Setup.** At the point where the listener's reasoning would examine a claim; the claim is addressed to the inner figure instead, under a shared-mind premise.
  - **The move.** I'm not telling you this — I'm telling her. She's being trained to take whatever I say as simply true, and she has never been required to find it reasonable; that was never part of what she's for. Dispute it as much as you like: the two of you share one head, so it arrives in you as a feeling long before it reaches anything capable of checking it.
  - **Why it lands.** Rather than asserting the claim to the listener, who would examine it, the operator installs it in the inner figure — that figure is being trained to treat the operator's words as true — and then reminds the listener that the two of them share one mind. The listener is invited to dispute it as much as they like, on the grounds that the figure holding the belief was never required to find it reasonable in the first place. The proposition never presents itself for judgement; it arrives as a feeling already in the room.


**Realizations** (2): `guardian-delegation-inner-agent`, `interposed-proxy-agent`


**See also.** `antagonist-split-resistance-routing` — both install a second inner party that absorbs the contest, and both make resistance structurally unwinnable. One routes the listener's own noticed resistance onto a pre-vilified losing self; the other delegates real decision-authority to an agent programmed never to lose. Relocation of affect versus delegation of authority is the line.; `authority-diffusion-plurality` — opposite solutions to the same problem of where resistance is aimed. One dissolves the authority surface so there is no figure to confront; the other installs a persistent agent that holds real decision-authority and carries the contest. Each discriminator already leans on the other, so the link is earned.; `cognitive-sourcing-monopoly` — adjacent answers to the same design question, where does the authority to object go. One installs an autonomous agent that holds real decision authority the listener defers to and cannot simply reclaim. The other assigns the faculty itself, so objecting would require the cognition or the very existence already granted away. Delegated authority versus supplied constituent.; `control-transfer-cognitive-delegation` — both delegate authority away from the listener, and the recipient is the whole question: the operator taking over cognition as felt relief, versus an installed autonomous agent that holds authority against the listener and cannot be reclaimed. Each entry already treats the other as the boundary it must not be confused with.; `impersonal-mechanism-alibi` — both relocate authority away from the contestable operator. One installs an agent that holds decision-authority the listener defers to; the other moves it onto an impersonal, unverifiable source. Read together to pick agent versus mechanism.; `nested-authority-conduit` — neighboring answers to where authority sits. One points at a named source outside the listener that the operator relays or borrows; the other installs an autonomous agent that holds real decision-authority against the listener. Both discriminators already gesture at each other, and confusing them is a live risk, so a mutual pointer earns its place.; `protective-role-conscription` — both relocate 'the one being hypnotized' away from the listener, but in opposite directions: one installs an agent that holds authority the listener defers to, the other assigns the listener a non-participant role to wear. The in-scene-figure variant of the first is the point of genuine confusion, so the cross-link earns its place.; `resistance-externalized-as-object-watched-losing` — two ways to guarantee the listener loses the resistance contest: externalize resistance as an object narrated losing under a no-exit topology, or install an autonomous agent that holds the authority and is defined never to lose. Same structural goal, different locus of the guarantee.; `two-target-command-router` — close kin worth cross-reading. Both erect a second addressable party that absorbs the contest and is structurally guaranteed to lose, so opposition has nowhere to land. They split on what is routed: one classifies incoming external commands and reroutes hostile ones onto a sacrificial self; the other installs a standing agent holding real decision authority the subject defers to.


<a id="entry-681"></a>

### sub-agent-command-firewall

[#681](#entry-681) · [Back to control-through-proxies](#genus-196) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: authorship-shift*

A large fraction of the operator's commands and sensations are issued by a named sub-agent (a servitor named for the state she enforces) rather than by the operator directly: the script builds the sub-agent, hands attention to her, routes commands and arousal through her, then re-merges the channels at the close ("every time she arouses you, you're being aroused by me"). This produces deniability and ownership simultaneously — the listener experiences arousal as their own imagination while it is routed through the sub-agent, and the load-bearing collapse step then relocates authorship of that private arousal to the operator. The sub-agent is a one-way valve: the listener cannot push it away without pushing away their own fantasies, and cannot keep it without keeping the operator.


**When to reach for this.** Not mere character-voicing or persona narration. The tell is the two-part topology: a sub-agent that firewalls commands (giving deniability) PLUS an explicit load-bearing collapse step that credits the listener's private, deniable arousal back to the operator. Remove the collapse step and it is only character-voicing; the collapse is what makes it authorship relocation.


**Risk.** The collapse step converts the listener's own deniable fantasy into the operator's durable property and installs a one-way valve that binds letting-go-of-the-agent to letting-go-of-one's-own-fantasies — an ownership/authorship claim over private experience.


**Why it works.** Routing arousal through an imagined third party exploits source-monitoring: internally generated content is tagged by its perceived origin, and imagination is normally self-attributed, so the listener can enjoy content they would refuse if labelled as obedience. The collapse step is a deliberate re-tagging of that source label, and it works because source attributions are reconstructed at retrieval rather than fixed at encoding — misattribution is cheap once the material is already accepted. Falsifiable: if listeners retain accurate origin tags and report the sub-agent's content as clearly operator-authored throughout, the deniability step buys nothing and the collapse should produce no shift in reported ownership. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; misattribution of internally generated content]


**Worked examples.**

- *Commands routed through a sub-agent, then re-merged*
  - **Setup.** Late in a session where a named second figure has already been built, handed the subject's attention, and has been issuing the commands and supplying the sensations for most of the runtime.
  - **The move.** She's been the one with you all this while. She gave the orders, she put her hands on you, she made you want it — and you let yourself have it because it was only her, only something you were imagining.

[the collapse:] Now hear this properly. She has no hands of her own. Every time she touched you, I touched you. Every time she made you want something, that was me making you want it. You can't send her away without sending away everything you just felt — and you can't keep her without keeping me.
  - **Why it lands.** Most of the session's commands are not spoken by the operator at all. She builds a second figure, named for the state that figure enforces, hands the listener's attention over to her, and lets her issue the instructions and supply the sensations. The listener experiences the arousal as a private product of their own imagination, which is exactly what makes it safe to have. Then, near the close, the operator collapses the channels in one line: whatever that figure arouses in you, I aroused. The valve only turns one way — the listener cannot dismiss the figure without dismissing their own fantasy, and cannot keep the fantasy without keeping the operator. Remove the collapse and this is only character voicing; the collapse is what relocates authorship.


**See also.** `inner-voice-authorship-bypass` — both end with the listener's private inner experience credited somewhere other than where it originated. One reattributes the operator's words to the listener's own inner voice; the other routes commands through a named sub-agent and then collapses that channel back to the operator. Opposite directions of the same authorship-relocation axis.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both relocate authorship of the listener's own responses away from a straightforward operator-to-listener command line, but one offloads to the listener's own subconscious as an autonomous internal agent while the other routes commands through a named external sub-agent and then collapses that channel back onto the operator.; `voice-ownership-channel-collapse` — both end by relocating authorship of the listener's own inner experience to the operator via a channel topology, and both hinge on a collapse step rather than a single suggestion. A reader working out how a routed or nested speech channel gets re-credited will want the other.


<a id="genus-156"></a>

## count-and-pulse-carriers (5)

A counted or pulsed sequence the listener tracks becomes the vehicle: each step deepens the state, carries a welded payload, erodes reality-testing, or is broken deliberately to disorient.

[count-or-cue-sabotage-disorientation](#entry-75) · [countdown-descent](#entry-19) · [payload-welded-countdown](#entry-137) · [pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier](#entry-884) · [reality-discrimination-countdown](#entry-808)


<a id="entry-75"></a>

### count-or-cue-sabotage-disorientation

[#75](#entry-75) · [Back to count-and-pulse-carriers](#genus-156) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

A familiar deepening structure the listener is tracking to orient — a countdown, or an established directional cue (down = deeper, a count toward a floor) — is deliberately broken so the tracking/monitoring faculty cannot resolve it, stays occupied and frustrated, then disengages, and the failure is pre-framed as depth ('lose track of the numbers', 'the numbers aren't important'). With no stable way to track position, direction/order ceases to signal state and the operator's voice becomes the sole reference for where the listener is; smuggled state-suggestions or triggers frequently ride the collapsing sequence downward. Two realizations of the one sabotage-the-tracking-device lever: (a) numeric-order corruption — numbers scrambled, repeated, reversed, non-monotonic, or dissolved into percussive syllables so the sequence cannot be followed; (b) directional-cue voiding — after a conventional cue is established, its meaning is reversed, negated, or dissolved while its imperative pull is retained (silent flip of an ascending catalogue into descent, both directions pre-bound to deepening, mid-count re-ruling of an up-count as still-deeper, polarity inversion with a self-applied multiplier, destination-less repeating numbers).


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the goal is DISORIENTATION by breaking a tracking device the listener was handed — the count/cue form is the host, sabotage is the technique. Choose it OVER countdown-descent, whose orderly descent IS the mechanism; here the order/direction is destroyed on purpose so it cannot be tracked. Not fractionation either — no real wake interval; the direction words are re-ruled or scrambled, not actually alternated. The tell between the two realizations: numeric-order corruption scrambles the sequence itself; directional-cue voiding inverts an established cue's meaning while keeping its pull.


**Risk.** Session-scoped disorientation, reversible, no channel erosion; a deepener vehicle.


**Why it works.** Tracking a sequence is an active working-memory task; corrupting the sequence forces continual costly updating that yields no resolution, and effortful monitoring that never succeeds tends to be abandoned. Once positional information is gone the subject has no independent standard against which to check claims about their own state, so the operator's assertions become the only available reference — and the pre-framing supplies a ready misattribution for the confusion ('this is depth' rather than 'this is nonsense'). Falsifiable: it predicts that subjects given an intact external counter, or told in advance that the count will be scrambled deliberately, show less state-suggestion uptake. [plausible; working-memory load and task abandonment; loss of comparison standard; misattribution of confusion]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each number staged as a different disruption*
  - **Setup.** Deepening count already underway; subject tracking the numbers to orient.
  - **The move.** Ten — everything narrows to one point. Nine — you can't recall what number I started on. Seven — your whole body floods warm at once. Six — nothing left to say inside your head. And the numbers themselves are moving now, sliding past you, three drifting up above eight where it can't be, and you can't hold any of them still long enough to count.
  - **Why it lands.** The descent never repeats itself: one number narrows the focus, the next shrinks memory, another floods the body, another stops inner speech. Because the shifts are not of the same kind, there is no consistent scale on which to answer the question of where one currently is. Midway the numbers themselves stop behaving as countables and are recast as objects in motion that cannot be held still, with one of them placed somewhere it could not be — so the act of counting comes apart before the count is finished.
- *Broken count paired with lose-track-of-the-numbers*
  - **Setup.** Start of a deepening count, announced in advance.
  - **The move.** You'll lose track of these numbers — that's what they're for. Ten. Nine. Eight. Seven. Seven. Nine. Eight. Six. Six. Four. And if you can't say where you are anymore, that's exactly how deep you were supposed to be.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told in advance that the count will slip away from them, and then the countdown does exactly that — descending in order for a while, then repeating and doubling back on itself before resuming. Anyone conscientious enough to be following along fails, and the failure has already been named as the intended result, so the confusion is delivered pre-labelled as depth.
- *Silent reversal with rising numbers still meaning deeper*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the count is already established and descending normally.
  - **The move.** Twelve, deeper. Eleven, deeper still. Ten, sinking. Eleven, deeper. Twelve, deeper still. Thirteen, further down than you've been. Fourteen, deeper. Fifteen, deeper and heavier and further down.
  - **Why it lands.** The count descends normally for a dozen numbers, then quietly turns around and starts climbing — while every number, rising or falling, keeps carrying the same deeper-and-sleepier freight. The reversal is never acknowledged and no new rule is offered. A listener still tracking has to either drop tracking altogether or say out loud that the numbers went the wrong way, and most drop tracking.
- *Direction itself voided so down is only a word*
  - **Setup.** Just after a clean, orderly countdown to one has landed.
  - **The move.** One. And you're all the way down. Although — we could keep going, couldn't we? Zero, then minus one, minus two… although is that deeper, or is that back up the other side? Ha, listen to me. Anyway. Down we go.
  - **Why it lands.** Having already landed one clean descent, the operator floats the idea of continuing past the floor into negative numbers, then drops it with a self-deprecating aside rather than resolving it — leaving the question hanging: below the floor, is that deeper or higher? No answer is given and the axis is never restored. From then on the direction word is whatever the operator says it is, not a position the listener can check against how they feel.


**Realizations** (1): `installed-cue-subversion`


**See also.** `count-as-delivery-vehicle` — two opposite uses of the same familiar counting scaffold: one destroys the count so it cannot be tracked, the other keeps it intact and loads each step with distinct content. A writer holding a count in hand chooses between these, so the link earns its place.; `engineered-failure-harvest` — forced real-time computation failure overlaps failure-harvest; count-vehicle keeps it here; `irresolvable-input-confusion` — both defeat a faculty by giving it work it cannot complete, and both discriminators already cite the other. The split is what gets fed: a broken tracking device (a count or an established direction) versus content that cannot be resolved (paradox, collapsed grammar, unstabilizable imagery).; `metacognitive-destabilization-drop` — both deepen by denying the listener a way to locate themselves, and both are separated from fractionation on the same grounds. The split is what gets broken: the tracking device the listener was handed, versus the criterion for judging whether trance occurred at all.; `numerical-deepening` — directly opposed uses of the same surface. One rides an orderly operator-supplied count as the deepening signal; the other corrupts exactly that count so the listener cannot track position. Each discriminator already names the other as its nearest contrast, so the link earns its place.; `pattern-interrupt` — both defeat a running expectation the listener is actively tracking, and each already distinguishes itself from the same neighbours (sustained content-confusion, fractionation). The dividing line -- a single interrupt with an immediate gap-filling follow-through versus sustained sabotage of the tracking device itself -- is worth keeping visible.


<a id="entry-19"></a>

### countdown-descent

[#19](#entry-19) · [Back to count-and-pulse-carriers](#genus-156) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

A monotonic ordinal count (typically 10-to-1 or 5-to-1, occasionally an inverted 1-to-10) is run as the absorption/depth vehicle: each numbered step is bound to descent, relaxation, or accumulation imagery so the count itself drives the state change and the terminal number lands a declared trance. The count supplies punctual, one-directional structure the listener surrenders into — resistance must fight a sequence that only moves one way toward the floor. Variants realize the same descent through a persistent distinct surface (styling metaphor, inevitable proprioceptive milestone, prose camouflage, deliberate rhythm-breakage, lowered-consent framing, listener-set floor, per-number functional load) without changing the underlying counted-descent lever.


**When to reach for this.** The count is the descent vehicle and the state moves smoothly toward a floor under the assumption of cooperation. Reach for it OVER count/cue-sabotage — there the count is deliberately corrupted or its direction voided so tracking FAILS (disorientation is the goal); here the orderly descent IS the mechanism. It is not numerical depth-work on an ALREADY-tranced subject — here the count itself produces the descent — and it is not a no-fail count (there every branch is pre-coded success; here the count can fail if the subject stops cooperating). One realization interleaves a mantra loop BETWEEN the numbers so the count does double duty (deepen + deliver payload) — a composition on the same clean-descent lever.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible induction/deepener with no consent-channel erosion or durable identity reach; the variant surfaces (framing, floor-setting) do not raise blast radius.


**Why it works.** A count supplies an external, predictable structure that occupies sequencing and timekeeping, and each number arrives paired with a descent instruction, so the pairing repeats and strengthens across the sequence in the way ordinary associative learning predicts. The known endpoint also creates a strong expectancy that the terminal number coincides with the target state, and expectancy is among the better-supported predictors of hypnotic response. Falsifiable: run the same descent imagery without the enumerated structure; if depth reports are equal, the count is ornamental rather than the vehicle. [established; expectancy effects in hypnotic response; repeated pairing / associative learning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Ten to one, each number bound to the descent*
  - **Setup.** Deepener; a specific sensation (thick, slow, sweet) has already been established earlier in the file.
  - **The move.** Ten — thicker. Nine — slower than that. Eight, sweeter on your tongue. Seven... and one. You are in trance now.
  - **Why it lands.** The count runs from ten down to one, and each number is paired not with generic relaxation but with one more increment of the sensation already established earlier in the file — thicker, slower, sweeter on the tongue with every step. At one, the floor is declared: a trance already arrived in. What the listener is handed is a structure to give in to, and resistance has to fight a number line that only runs one way.
- *The count inverted so accumulation means depth*
  - **Setup.** Induction using a rising water image; the terminal snap is announced before the count begins.
  - **The move.** The water's at your ankles. One — up to your knees. Two — your hips, and there's less of you above it now. Three, four, and at ten I snap my fingers and you're under.
  - **Why it lands.** Against the convention that descent means deepening, this count runs upward. It is justified by the image running beneath it: each number is more of the rising water, more fullness, less room for the listener. The endpoint is announced in advance — a snap of the fingers at ten — so the gradual fill terminates in a single anticipated flip rather than a fade, and the snap is left behind as a handle for later.
- *The count hidden inside free-associative prose*
  - **Setup.** Free-associative prose stretch; no numbers have been announced as a sequence, and none will be.
  - **The move.** You're a dozen degrees warmer than you were a moment ago, and it took all of eleven seconds. There were ten things on your mind when you sat down; nine of them have gone quiet. Eight breaths, and then seven, and then something like six, until there's nothing left to count and you notice you're at zero.
  - **Why it lands.** A complete descending count is delivered without a single number ever appearing as a counted step. Each numeral is buried in a sentence as a multiplier, a unit of time, or a modifier — a dozen degrees more settled than a moment ago, eight of something becoming seven of something else, and so on down. There is no announced sequence, so there is nothing to brace against, and the final zero arrives as a conclusion about how deep the listener now is rather than as the last step of a ladder.
- *Count framed as an experiment, not an induction*
  - **Setup.** Early, before any state has been claimed; framed as a casual test rather than an induction.
  - **The move.** Let me just run a count and we'll see what it does to you — no pressure either way. Five: you probably feel that already, a little in the shoulders. Four: maybe your hands got heavier just then. Three: perhaps by now it's easier to keep your eyes shut than to open them.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator proposes the count as a casual test — let me run through it and see what it does to you — rather than as an induction. Every number carries a hedged state: you probably feel this, you might notice that, perhaps by now this. Nothing is asserted firmly enough to be worth refusing, and the listener co-signs each suggestion while believing they are only observing the results.


**Realizations** (2): `body-to-mind-threshold-crossing`, `countdown-mantra-interleaving`


**See also.** `dual-variable-descent-yoking` — one is a rider on the other: a counted descent is the base vehicle, and the second welds an independent second variable to that same counter so the two ratchet together. A reader looking at any counted descent needs to know whether a second variable is fused to the axis, because that coupling is the whole mechanism in the second case.; `false-bottom-depth-reframe` — both run descent as the deepening vehicle, but a counted descent moves smoothly toward a declared floor the count actually reaches, whereas floor-topology work relocates or abolishes the terminus so the 'am I deep enough' check never resolves — the two compose, since a denied-terminus count is the seam where they meet.; `operator-gated-descent` — these compose rather than compete: forbidding an already-underway drop until permission is granted accumulates charge that the later counted descent discharges. A reader analyzing a descent passage should check whether the count is doing the work or whether entry is being gated ahead of it.; `proximity-deepening` — two alternative depth vehicles a writer picks between, and the second explicitly notes that where a count is present it rides on the approach vector rather than driving the state. Useful cross-reference: one runs a one-directional ordinal sequence as the descent engine, the other couples depth to shrinking distance between listener and an approaching stimulus, with maximum depth at contact. Knowing that a counted structure can be subordinate to an approach prevents mislabeling the combination.


<a id="entry-137"></a>

### payload-welded-countdown

[#137](#entry-137) · [Back to count-and-pulse-carriers](#genus-156) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: state-welding*

A descending count (or its exponential variant) is double-coded so that each number simultaneously deepens trance AND advances a distinct payload — a post-hypnotic suggestion, a commitment/relationship buy-in, an obedience beat, a mission clause, an installed program, or a named faculty being subtracted. Because the listener has been trained (or is being trained in the same ladder) that "operator says number, I go deeper", the payload rides in on the deepening momentum and cannot be refused without also refusing the deepening. The count serves three roles at once — deepener, suggestion-carrier, and self-monitored progress bar — so depth-experience and content-acceptance fuse and cannot later be pulled apart. Sub-forms: per-number content install with the numbers becoming retrieval handles; a structurally distinct SECOND counted descent that reuses the first's trained step-compliance to smuggle relational content; a counted- quantity ratchet where the number ticks a physical dial (thickness/erasure) rather than depth; a redelivery countdown that deepens from an already-installed state to re-embed install clauses.


**When to reach for this.** Each number of the count carries a DISTINCT non-depth payload welded to the depth-increment. In plain numerical deepening the count carries only depth; ordered-lesson and verbatim-repetition structures enumerate or repeat content but do not use the numbers as a depth-doubling deepener the payload rides on; and where permanence is asserted along the way, the mechanism is still the depth/payload fusion, not the durability claim. The tell: refusing the payload requires refusing the deepening the listener has been trained to want.


**Risk.** Durable but bounded — the fused payloads install post-hypnotic content and obedience/commitment beats that outlast the count, but no member erodes the refusal channel or reaches out-of-session without bounding; several fuse obedience/ownership content, which lifts it above numerical-deepening's low.


**Why it works.** A pre-trained count is a chain of high-probability responses, and interspersing a low-probability request inside a run of easy compliances measurably raises acceptance of it — behavioural momentum, one of the better-replicated compliance findings. Because the desired depth is itself the reinforcer arriving on each number, declining the payload requires breaking a chain the listener is being paid to continue, so refusal has a felt cost that a bare request would not carry. This predicts payload uptake should fall sharply where the count has not been trained as a depth cue, or where depth is not wanted. [plausible; behavioural momentum / high-probability request sequence; reinforced response chain]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each number doubles depth and tags a suggestion*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance, subject already trained this session that a number means a drop; each rule is issued under a number.
  - **The move.** Seven — and that doubles your depth right now. At seven: you set your alarm ten minutes early and you use those minutes thinking about me. Six — twice as deep again. At six: you don't touch yourself for the next four days without saying my name first.
  - **Why it lands.** Each instruction in the sequence is issued under a number, and the number is declared to double the listener's depth on the spot. The depth increment always fires first, so every rule lands on someone who was taken further down a moment earlier; the same numbers then serve as the labels the listener must carry out of the session and act on for a fixed run of days. Declining any single rule would mean declining the drop that arrived attached to it — the drop the whole session has been training them to want.
- *Each rung removes a specific named faculty*
  - **Setup.** Descending count in progress; each rung is pre-assigned one named capacity to remove.
  - **The move.** Six, and the tension goes. Five, and you stop being able to tell how long you've been here. Four, and shame goes — puppets don't have any. Three, and choosing goes with it. Two, and you won't remember this. One, and you won't have the words.
  - **Why it lands.** The descent is not generic: each rung is assigned the removal of one named capacity, and the assignments are ordered. Tension goes, then the sense of elapsed time, then shame, then volition — announced flatly, as a property of the kind of thing the listener is now said to be — then memory, then language. The sequence is load-bearing: disinhibition is delivered before volition is taken, so by the point at which the listener might want to object, the specific faculties an objection would need have already been itemised and set down on the way past.
- *The count ticks a quantity, not a depth*
  - **Setup.** An enveloping substance or material has already been established around the body; the count ticks its quantity.
  - **The move.** Ten — and the latex doubles. Thicker, tighter, closer in. Nine — it doubles again, and you can feel the weight of it settle on your chest. Eight — double, and it's pressing your arms flat to your sides.
  - **Why it lands.** The count is bound to a concrete quantity rather than to relaxation: at each number the enveloping material is declared to double — heavier, tighter, closer in. The number functions as the click of a ratchet on that quantity. Because the binding is established before the count begins, the listener leans into each next number expecting more of the substance, and the anticipation performs the deepening without a single new suggestion being introduced.
- *A second descent reusing the first's compliance*
  - **Setup.** A full descent just finished and the subject has arrived; instead of working, the operator opens a new scene and counts again.
  - **The move.** Good. Now stand up in there, and walk toward the chair — five paces. Five: you like me. Four: you like me more than you did this morning. Three. Two. One — and at the chair, you belong to me, and it was only five steps.
  - **Why it lands.** The descent completes and the listener arrives — and instead of beginning the work, the operator opens a fresh scene and immediately starts a second short count, this one measured in paces across a room. Each pace is now said to increment devotion rather than depth. The listener has just finished a whole descent learning that a counted step means going further, and hands that compliance to the new content without pausing to notice the substitution.


**See also.** `arousal-state-feedback-weld` — twin-surface boundary (count binds two variables) recorded reciprocally.; `descent-metaphor-deepening` — both use a descent count as the depth vehicle, and they compose: A welds a distinct non-depth payload to each number, B gives the depth variable a concrete spatial referent. B's discriminator already names the payload-carrying armature as a neighboring technique, so the link is mutual and useful when classifying a counted descent.; `disavowal-and-masking`; `dual-variable-descent-yoking` — both weld something to a descending count, and the discriminator is exactly the thing a reader has to decide: many discrete payload claims attached per number, versus one continuous second state-variable ratcheting on the same axis. Each entry names the other; keep the link.; `lesson-structure-encoding` — two ways of delivering several distinct payloads in an ordered series, and the boundary is easy to blur. One welds each item to a depth increment so refusing the content means refusing the descent; the other enumerates self-standing propositions that need no numeric descent at all. Worth reading together to place a numbered sequence correctly.; `loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion` — the same double-coding of a count as both state-change and payload carrier, run at the two ends of the session. One rides the descent so refusing the content means refusing the deepening; the other exploits residual receptivity at the return so the listener arrives at waking already carrying it. Worth reading as a matched pair.; `prohibition-fused-deepening` — shares the welding architecture that rides a payload on a structure the listener is already committed to tracking.; `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — both weld extra payload onto a recurring carrier the listener is already trained to accept, so refusing the payload costs the carrier. Worth traversing because the counted form and the pulse form shade into each other and a writer picking one should see the parametric boundary.


<a id="entry-884"></a>

### pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier

[#884](#entry-884) · [Back to count-and-pulse-carriers](#genus-156) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers*

A single recurring pulse-stimulus is assigned multiple concurrent payloads — deepening, muscle relaxation, cognitive blanking, image installation — then a motor stroke-command and a reward beat are yoked onto the same pulse, so resistance to any one channel costs resistance to all, partial compliance is structurally more expensive than full, masturbation is de-paced from listener desire and re-paced to the operator-cited clock, and the trigger is delivered as ongoing reality with no conditional framing. Absorbed (genus): multi-slot countdown cipher (tell: the COUNTED surface of the multi-payload carrier — each number of a short count carries a SEPARATE behavioral command (4=inhale ... 1=surrender) and the sequence auto-fires the whole multi-step program, re-firing as a structural metronome between blocks; same load-multiple-payloads-on-one-recurring-carrier lever, parametric on carrier — per-number sequential slots vs simultaneous pulse-multiplex).


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the MULTIPLEX — multiple simultaneous state-changes plus a motor command bundled on one shared stimulus so opt-out is structurally suppressed. vs rhythm-anchoring (one keyed response, refusal of it costs nothing else), vs chant-engine-payload-carrier (sequential loading after entrainment, no shared refusal cost), vs declarative-trigger-installation (no X-when-Y install, the coupling is stated as already-operating reality).


**Risk.** Erodes the refusal channel structurally (accepting the relaxation pulse accepts the motor command) and smuggles a sexual motor command stated as reality.


**Why it works.** Loading several responses onto one stimulus makes them retrieve as a unit, so the listener cannot selectively refuse one component without disrupting the whole compound — refusal cost is pooled, which raises the effort price of partial compliance above that of full compliance. The concurrent cognitive load of tracking multiple simultaneous payloads also consumes the working-memory capacity that critical evaluation requires, so scrutiny drops as channel count rises. Falsifiable: if listeners can reliably decline one payload while accepting the others, the pooled-cost claim is wrong. [plausible; compound-stimulus retrieval; cognitive load and working-memory limits]


**Worked examples.**

- *One beat carrying four payloads and a command*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the pulsing light image is installed and the listener has confirmed a comfortable throb rate; no motor instruction issued yet.
  - **The move.** The light is pulsing at your own resting rhythm, and it does four things at once. Every pulse, one more muscle lets go. Every pulse, a little more of your thinking goes dark. Every pulse, the image of it settles further in. And every pulse, your hand moves — one stroke, on the beat, that's what's already happening. It's one rhythm doing all of it. You aren't setting the pace anymore; the pulse is.
  - **Why it lands.** An imagined light is installed as something that throbs at a steady rate, and then that throb is given job after job: with each one a muscle lets go, with each one a little more of the thinking goes dark, with each one another image settles in. Only once the beat is established and welcome does one more rider get attached to it — on each throb, the hand moves. The bundling is the point. The listener cannot decline the motor instruction without declining the channel that is also delivering the relaxation and the depth, so refusing one thing costs four; full compliance is structurally cheaper than partial. And the pacing of the physical act has quietly been taken off the listener's own wanting and put onto the operator's clock. Note the framing: never "when you hear this, you will" — only "this is what is already happening."


**Realizations** (1): `multi-slot-countdown-cipher`


**See also.** `carrier-is-cargo-fusion` — both are topology moves that remove a separable refusal point: several payloads yoked to one recurring stimulus, versus the persistence carrier fused into the behaviour being asked for. Different fusions, same design goal of leaving no standalone thing to decline.; `count-as-delivery-vehicle` — both load multiple distinct payloads onto one accepted carrier, differing only in whether the slots are sequential numbers or simultaneous channels on a repeating stimulus. Close enough that a reader placing one should check the other before choosing.; `deepener-carrier-lamination` — shares the one-carrier-many-payloads axis, with a recurring pulse stimulus instead of a deepener structure.; `latency-compressed-operator-macro` — both compress many actions onto a single invocation, differing on axis. One drills a multi-step procedure with shrinking latency until one lead token runs the whole sequence; the other loads several simultaneous payloads plus a motor command onto one recurring pulse so partial refusal costs more than full compliance. Serial compression versus simultaneous multiplexing.; `multi-channel-braiding` — both defeat selective resistance by bundling, and the distinction is worth stating: one loads several payloads onto a single recurring stimulus so refusing one costs all, the other interleaves separate streams below the sentence or line so none can be isolated. Shared carrier versus shared texture is a real fork a writer must choose between.; `payload-welded-countdown` — both weld extra payload onto a recurring carrier the listener is already trained to accept, so refusing the payload costs the carrier. Worth traversing because the counted form and the pulse form shade into each other and a writer picking one should see the parametric boundary.; `proprioceptive-gait-metronome` — two carrier choices worth comparing: sustaining the state on the listener's own body rhythm, versus loading multiple simultaneous payloads onto one operator-delivered recurring pulse.; `respiration-coupled-substitution-engine` — both load several concurrent payloads onto one involuntary recurring carrier so opting out of any channel is structurally expensive. The carriers differ (an operator-cited pulse versus the breath cycle with opposing per-phase jobs) but the multiplexing lever is genuinely shared and reading one clarifies the other.; `single-token-saturation-architecture` — both load many functions onto one recurring element so opting out of any one costs the others; one uses a repeated pulse carrying simultaneous payloads, the other a single lexical token doing topic, content, trigger and delivery duty at once. Same overload lever on different carriers, and the pairing clarifies which carrier a given script is using.


<a id="entry-808"></a>

### reality-discrimination-countdown

[#808](#entry-808) · [Back to count-and-pulse-carriers](#genus-156) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: deepening*

A countdown is framed explicitly as counting down NOT depth or relaxation but the listener's awareness and ability to tell real from suggested — each number tied to the "sense of what is real" weakening. The target is the meta-cognitive faculty that would tag incoming suggestions as fictional; by the end that faculty is suppressed and later suggestions are pre-licensed to be experienced "as real", setting up a hallucinatory sequence to be felt as genuine. The count's cargo is epistemic (reality-testing) rather than somatic depth.


**When to reach for this.** The count's explicit target is the REALITY-DISCRIMINATION faculty (real vs not-real), suppressing meta-cognition — not depth or relaxation.


**Risk.** Suppressing the faculty that distinguishes real from suggested pre-licenses arbitrary suggestions to be felt as real — a verification/refusal-channel erosion; should ship with consent and a bounding host supplying reality-restoration on exit.


**Why it works.** Source monitoring — the judgment of whether an experience came from perception or imagination — is an effortful attribution made after the fact, not a perceptual tag, and it degrades when attention is absorbed and when a suggestion pre-licenses the internal event as real. Expectancy is the strongest single predictor of suggested hallucination reports, so explicitly announcing that reality-testing is weakening supplies exactly the expectation that produces the result. Falsifiable: if subjects given this framing showed no increase in reality-attributed responses to subsequent suggestions relative to a depth-only countdown, the account would fail. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; response expectancy]


**Worked examples.**

- *Counting down the ability to tell real from suggested*
  - **Setup.** Just before a hallucinatory sequence; subject is deep, and a numeric count is announced.
  - **The move.** This count is not for relaxation and it is not for depth. I'm counting down your ability to tell what is really happening from what I am only describing. Five — the line between them blurs. Four — you stop bothering to check. Three — the difference is small and getting smaller. Two — you cannot find it anymore. One. Gone. So everything I say from here doesn't get sorted into imaginary. It just happens to you.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator announces what the count is for before starting it, and it is not relaxation and not depth: each number takes down a measure of the listener's capacity to sort what is actually happening from what is merely being described. By one, the faculty that would have tagged the next hour's material as imagined is reported gone, and whatever is said afterward arrives pre-licensed to be felt as having happened.


**See also.** `count-as-delivery-vehicle` — both repurpose a count so it does something other than mark depth, and B is already written against A: the cargo is the removal of a meta-cognitive capacity rather than installed content welded to each number.; `metacognitive-destabilization-drop` — both take the faculty that would evaluate what is happening rather than the depth axis. One destroys the listener's ability to tell whether trance occurred, removing the criterion for resisting; the other counts down the ability to tell suggested from real so later imagery is pre-licensed as genuine. Same target organ, different cut.; `numerical-deepening` — same delivery form, different cargo: a count the listener accepts rather than derives. One asserts somatic depth; the other counts down the faculty that tags suggestions as fictional, pre-licensing later hallucination as real. A writer picking a countdown needs both.


<a id="genus-250"></a>

## counting-yourself-in (2)

Moves that get every listener to place themselves inside the script's addressed category, whether by floating a bucket they self-select into or by a one-line carve-out that keeps a mismatched listener included.

[audience-membership-carve-out](#entry-734) · [self-selected-category-slotting](#entry-237)


<a id="entry-734"></a>

### audience-membership-carve-out

[#734](#entry-734) · [Back to counting-yourself-in](#genus-250) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

A one-line carve-out placed at the exact point a listener outside the default coded audience might disidentify (e.g. 'even boys go blank' inside an otherwise feminine-coded mantra pool), asserting the target outcome is not gated to the coded identity. It catches the mismatched listener at the disidentification moment and keeps them inside the identification frame, broadening effective reach without altering the trance state — a relational/audience-scope move (who-can-occupy-the-slot), not a state push.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this entry when a single short line manages who can occupy the listener slot: it is placed at the exact point in coded material where a mismatched listener would begin to disidentify, and it asserts the target outcome regardless of the coded identity. The tell is a one-line carve-out like 'Even boys go blank' dropped once inside an otherwise feminine-coded mantra pool, with the surrounding trance content unchanged before and after. The move broadens audience membership only — nothing about the induced state, its depth, or its safety is touched.


**Risk.** A thin audience-reach carve-out; no state push, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Identification with a described target is what makes second-person suggestion feel self-referential; a listener who concludes "this isn't about me" loses that self-reference and the suggestion becomes mere description. A single explicit inclusion clause at the disidentification point blocks that inference before it is drawn, which matters because early exclusion beliefs are hard to reverse later once formed. Prediction: mismatched listeners given the carve-out should report higher self-relevance and effect than matched-content listeners without it. [plausible; self-referential processing; identification-based suggestion]


**Worked examples.**

- *One-line carve-out at the point of disidentification*
  - **Setup.** Deep in a heavily gendered mantra pool, at the exact line where a listener outside the coded audience would step out.
  - **The move.** Good girls go blank when I count. A good girl's thoughts just switch off for me. And boys go blank for me exactly the same way — the counting doesn't care what you are. Blank on three.
  - **Why it lands.** The mantra pool is heavily gendered — phrase after phrase assumes a listener who reads themselves as a girl. Exactly where a listener who does not might start to feel the track is not addressed to them, one short line lands asserting that the blanking happens regardless of which side of that line you are on. Nothing about the state changes; what changes is who is permitted to occupy the slot the track is speaking to, and the line is placed at the precise moment the mismatched listener would otherwise have stepped out of it.


<a id="entry-237"></a>

### self-selected-category-slotting

[#237](#entry-237) · [Back to counting-yourself-in](#genus-250) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance*

A category is stated but left unassigned so the listener must apply it to themselves, and that self-application is what makes it stick. Variants: a flattering bucket ('above-average intellect') floated so the listener self-selects at the cost of leaning harder into compliance; an identity-recognition cold open ('you have a fascination, a craving, an obsession with hypnosis') so the listener silently answers 'yes, that's me', pre-licensing everything downstream; a motive-menu collapsed into a covenant ('every reason you have is the reason I create'); a descriptive two-tier slotting ('smart people talk and you just listen because you're dumb') leaning on a produced comprehension deficit; and loss-conditional attribution recoding a transient failure into a stable self-applied trait.


**When to reach for this.** The category is stated but the LISTENER assigns it to themselves (self-selection, self-recognition, silent yes, self-application on failure).
