A reader who mislabels the deferred install as an activation will look for a firing that is not there.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are serial-position moves about what a file leaves behind unfired. One carves an installed trigger out of an otherwise complete wake so it survives as part of the restored self, the other installs a receptor whose payload is deliberately deferred to a later file. Useful together for anyone reading the end-of-file region, where the defining property is placement rather than content.


<a id="entry-1299"></a>

### declarative-trigger-installation

[#1299](#entry-1299) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers*

The operator binds a specified cue to a specified future response so a persistent conditioned pair fires outside the installing moment. The cue is external to the subject's own cognition — an operator-verbal phrase, a typographic/all-caps token, an everyday object or image, a class of objects, an everyday high-frequency word, the file's own title, or a guaranteed public/calendar event — and the response is a discrete future state-change or behavior ('when you hear/see/encounter X, Y happens'). The install grammar runs in several authored refinements that stay inside the one mechanism: the cue is engineered as a broad, self-expanding ambient surface so it fires in ordinary life without the operator present (a whole clothing class, a title-as-trigger keyed to anyone saying it or the subject's own thought of it, common high-frequency words); the response is specified to strengthen per firing (growth-clause rider: multiplicative per-firing growth, or an additive driveable accumulator); the install labels rather than creates, cashing conditioning already drilled unmarked across the runtime so the trigger arrives with a built-in response history (retroactive arming — saturate-then-consecrate ordering, a pre-flooded word, an already-drilled command phrase, narrating the response as inevitable fact, state-synchronous drilling, a sleep-cue built into a reflex); the install is asserted as already-done in an earlier unauditable session so denying it works would require denying one's own past (presupposed-conditioning — a voice-register claimed as long-conditioned, a back-dated everyday word, past arousals recoded as prior installs); and the anchored cue is chosen to double as its own content-meaningful term plus a belief-conversion payload so each riding assertion is silently accepted while the trigger survives audit as plain deepener talk (deniable-belief-converter — e.g. an anchored term like 'surrender'). Two more cue-surface/register variants of the same install lever: an open-narrated install — the conditioning is narrated OPENLY in procedural language as it happens, transparency-as-disarm lowering scrutiny; and a somatic-anatomical cue — an imagined object is implanted at a named body-site so later mention of its name fires a felt body-SENSATION, the cue-surface being a body location rather than a word/object/image.


**When to reach for this.** Declarative cue->response binding for a discrete future state/behavior, the cue external to the subject's cognition. Tells AGAINST: the cue is the subject's own metacognitive/self-reference act consumed by the response (-> self-referential-cue-install); the response is valence/reward delivery only (that is conditioning territory, not a trigger install); the install works by temporal stimulus-pairing with no verbal contingency declaration (-> respondent-stimulus-pairing); the install ACT itself is concealed/disguised at delivery time (-> covert-install-under-cover); the install target is an open content-unknown slot inheriting conditioned weight (-> deferred-content-slot-install); the installed topology is a closed self-referential ring whose response re-summons the cue source (-> closed-loop-operator-binding); an object is given ambient symbolic meaning with no discrete fired response (no cue->response pair ever fires, so it is not a trigger install at all). The ambient-surface, growth-clause, retroactive-arming, install-by-assertion, and deniable-dual-function forms are all VARIANTS of this one install lever — twists on the cue-surface, the response-magnitude, the install-timing, the install-veridicality, or the cue's semantic doubling, not distinct moves.


**Risk.** Durable waking-life cue-response pair, medium risk at baseline. The camouflaged-unavoidable-cue and ambient-surface variants fire on cues the subject cannot avoid, pushing toward requires_bounding=true at variant level; the deniable-belief-converter variant bypasses evaluative consent to each riding claim and reads higher.


**Why it works.** Post-hypnotic suggestion is a well-documented and replicable phenomenon: a declared cue-response contingency does produce the response later, in high-suggestibility subjects, often with the response reported as involuntary. Expectancy is a large part of it — telling someone what will happen raises the probability it happens and shapes how they interpret ambiguous internal events — and the ambient-surface refinement simply raises the base rate of cue exposure, while retroactive arming and presupposed-conditioning exploit source-monitoring error to borrow a response history that may never have existed. Falsifiable throughout: response rates should track measured suggestibility, and a cue declared but never encountered should produce nothing. [established; post-hypnotic suggestion; expectancy effects; source-monitoring error]


**Worked examples.**

- *Saturate the phrase first, name it after*
  - **Setup.** Count has reached the bottom of the descent; the phrase has not yet been named as a trigger.
  - **The move.** Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Drop for me. Those three words are a spell now — you have been doing it for the last minute. Hear them anywhere, and you go straight down.
  - **Why it lands.** First the phrase is repeated a dozen-odd times back to back with nothing at all in between, right after the count has reached bottom, until it has stopped meaning anything and is only a sound. Only then does the operator define it: these words are a spell; hear them and you go straight down. The conditioning is already finished before the trigger is announced, so the install reads as labelling something the listener has plainly been doing, not as a request. The chosen phrase is itself an order, so each later utterance narrates the response and produces it in the same breath.
- *Cue chosen as a wide ambient surface*
  - **Setup.** Deep, persona content already established; the operator is defining the out-of-session cue surface.
  - **The move.** Anything you'd call lingerie is a switch now — you decide what counts, and that list only ever gets longer. The moment the strap touches your shoulder she comes forward, every time, and once it has started you cannot interrupt it. You will simply be dressing, and then you will be her.
  - **Why it lands.** The cue named is not one garment or one act but a whole fuzzy category of clothing, so the listener's own sense of what counts decides the boundary — and that boundary can only widen. The operator adds that the switch throws the moment dressing begins, cannot be interrupted, and always works. The persona-change stops needing an operator at all: the wardrobe is now the induction surface, and clothes have gone from things worn to switches that cannot be left unpressed.
- *Each firing specified to add to the last*
  - **Setup.** Arousal established, subject deep; the phrase is being bound with its accumulator clause.
  - **The move.** When you hear denied for me, your body is certain it has gone a full week without release, and every time I say it again it adds another week on top. Denied for me. Denied for me. Denied for me. Denied for me. That's a month, and I have not touched you once.
  - **Why it lands.** The response is written with an accumulator built into it: hear the phrase and the body is told it has gone far longer without release than it has — and every further utterance adds the same increment again on top. Having established the rule, the operator simply repeats the phrase several times over in quick succession, stacking a great deal of imagined deprivation in well under a minute. The felt shortage is now a number the operator can drive at whatever rate she likes, entirely detached from what the body has actually done.
- *Install asserted as an already-old fact*
  - **Setup.** Mid-script; the operator has just shifted into a lower, slower vocal register.
  - **The move.** Listen to how I'm speaking to you right now — this softer register, right here. You learned this one over the earlier recordings, so you'll notice your body already knows what it means: it means trance is close. You may not remember the session where you picked it up, but your shoulders remember.
  - **Why it lands.** Mid-script the operator stops to comment on the way she is speaking at that moment: this particular register, she says, is a cue you picked up over the earlier files — it means trance is close. Nothing is installed in front of the listener and nothing can be checked; the claim is about a register they are hearing right now and about sessions they may or may not remember precisely. Whatever settling follows gets attributed to the voice, and denying the trigger would mean denying one's own past listening.


**Realizations** (2): `imaginal-to-somatic-anchor`, `transparent-narrated-install-with-resistance-route`


**See also.** `ambient-yes-reflex-conditioning` — both bind everyday objects and acts as cues that keep firing outside the installing moment.; `bundle-install-single-anchor` — one is the baseline cue-to-response install with its enumerated variants; the other loads several distinct effects onto a single freshly-minted cue in one pass. The bundle case is the nearest sibling of the baseline and its discriminator turns on how many payloads ride one anchor, so the reader needs both.; `context-generalization` — directly complementary and frequently sequential: one binds a cue to a response, the other takes an already-installed response and widens where it fires. The confusable case is an install whose cue is engineered broad from the outset versus a later scope-widening of an existing payload, and a reader hitting that case should see both.; `implementation-intention` — strong overlap on the core act — binding a named external cue to a named future response that fires outside the session — but one is a large consolidated install-grammar entry carrying many authored refinements (cue-surface breadth, per-firing growth clauses, retroactive arming, install-by-assertion, deniable dual-function terms) while the other is the plain one-directional conditional with variation only in cue and payload surface. The narrower one looks absorbable, but a merge would fold a small entry into a very large one, so link them and let a dedicated pass decide absorption rather than; `internal-event-keyed-trigger` — both bind a cue to an installed response, but the general install keys on an operator-supplied or environmental token while the self-referential form keys on the listener's own act of thinking or self-reference, which makes it operator-free and untestable because checking is itself the cue.; `named-trigger-persona-swap` — the toggle install is built from paired trigger installs but the entry is the two-state identity machine and its engineered bias (one-sided amnesia plus a per-activation growth clause), which no single cue-to-response pair models.; `procedural-routine-install` — both attach something to a cue; the difference is the payload's size and kind. One drills a multi-step executive procedure at decision-point granularity as the product; the other binds a cue to a discrete future state-change or behavior. Compare when a trigger appears to fire a whole routine rather than a single response.; `rule-governed-behavior-install` — real discrimination need: both state a contingency in words in advance, and both use the same when-X-then-Y surface. The split is whether behavior comes under the control of the verbal description itself, bypassing trial and error, or whether a cue is bound to a specified future response that later fires. Easy to mislabel without the contrast.; `template-reuse-install` — the declarative cue-response install grammar whose spotlight/tool phrasing is the very template this entry's content swap reuses.; `trigger-stacking` — stacking presupposes single installs already exist: the declarative install builds each cue-response pair, stacking then composes several under one cue. Reader arriving at either genuinely needs the other to know whether they are installing a pair or composing pre-installed ones.


<a id="entry-1300"></a>

### deferred-content-slot-install

[#1300](#entry-1300) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers*

Builds a locked structure of conditioned words, then installs an OPEN slot in it: the listener pre-commits, at peak suggestibility (orgasm as the binding agent), to treat future content-unknown words — whatever they turn out to be, delivered live or in other recordings — as equivalent to the existing conditioned set, inheriting its full weight. The actual filler words are never cleanly delivered; the install target is a VARIABLE, not a value — a future-tense backdoor on the conditioning that the operator can re-enter and fill arbitrarily.


**When to reach for this.** The install target is an open, content-unknown slot pre-authorized to inherit existing conditioned weight. vs declarative-trigger-installation: there a fixed, known cue-response pair is declared at install time; here nothing bound is known at commitment time. The orgasm is the binding agent, not a conditioned response — this is not arousal-to-cue conditioning. And the concealment is NON-DELIVERY of the filler content, not an amnesia wrapper around a delivered command. Not a growth-clause variant: growth clauses strengthen a KNOWN response; the slot defers WHAT is installed, not how strongly.


**Risk.** A consent-scope breach by construction — content is unknown at commitment time yet pre-authorized to inherit full conditioned weight, re-fillable across future sessions and recordings; scope bounding and explicit consent are the minimum viable containment.


**Why it works.** The consistency account is right but the label is not: low-balling is agreeing to a SPECIFIED deal whose cost is then worsened, which is not what happens when a subject commits to unspecified future content. This is a blank-check commitment — the consistency principle binding people to the commitment act itself rather than its content — and should be cited as commitment-consistency, not low-balling. Choosing peak arousal exploits attentional narrowing under high arousal (Easterbrook-style), though the transfer from the lab arousal literature to trance/sexual arousal is an extrapolation and should be marked as such. Falsifiable: if subjects who pre-committed to unknown content accepted it at the same rate as subjects hearing it cold, the slot mechanism is inert. [plausible; consistency principle / commitment before terms (low-balling); arousal-driven attentional narrowing]


**Worked examples.**

- *A blank slot pre-authorized at the peak*
  - **Setup.** At the edge of climax; eleven conditioned words already drilled into a closed set.
  - **The move.** You have eleven words, and they are locked. Now, before you go over: two more words will be added to that set at the moment you come, and whatever those two words turn out to be, they belong to the set with everything the other eleven carry. Say yes to that now, while you're right at the edge — yes to two words you haven't heard yet.
  - **Why it lands.** Eleven words have been drilled into a locked set. At the edge of climax the operator asks for one more commitment: two further words will be added at the moment of release, and whatever they turn out to be, they will belong to the set with all its accumulated weight. The listener agrees to a value they have not heard — the pledge is to a variable. In the recording itself the two words are never delivered cleanly; the climax dissolves into repetition. The slot stays open, and the operator can return later, in this catalogue or live, and fill it with anything she likes.


**See also.** `emptied-window-install` — both engineer a slot for content that escapes evaluation, but emptied-window-install disables the objecting tools first and then states known content into that narrow window, while deferred-content-slot-install leaves the content itself unknown at commitment time so future arbitrary words inherit the conditioned weight.; `future-commitment-binding` — both pre-authorize content that does not exist at commitment time, which is a real boundary: one binds arbitrary future verbal commitments extracted under a stated condition, the other installs an open slot that future unspecified words inherit weight through. A reader classifying an open-ended pre-authorization needs both to pick correctly.; `meta-suggestibility-conditioning` — both install a capacity rather than a value, which is a real structural kinship: one conditions general receptiveness to whatever the next file does, the other installs an open slot pre-authorized to inherit existing conditioned weight from content not yet delivered. A reader assessing what a file leaves usable for later needs both, and the distinction (disposition versus named empty variable) is worth stating.; `open-slot-attachment-frame` — both install a frame with a deliberately empty slot and let the slot's vacancy carry the payload, which makes them easy to confuse. They differ in who fills it and when: one leaves the slot open so the listener's own associations attach during the session, the other pre-commits the listener to accept whatever the operator later drops in. Not one technique twice — the filler and the power that fills it are different.; `self-supplied-order-hook` — two ways of installing a variable instead of a value. One leaves the order content blank at emergence so the listener fills it from a prior install and certifies their own compliance; the other pre-authorizes an open slot to inherit existing conditioned weight so the operator can fill it later. Who fills the blank, and when, is the distinguishing axis.


<a id="entry-1192"></a>

### derived-relations-installation

[#1192](#entry-1192) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

For a verbally/relationally capable learner, arrange a training history so that teaching a proper SUBSET of a repertoire causes an untaught, larger repertoire to EMERGE with no direct instruction — the target function/class/relation is never itself taught, paired, or labeled; it falls out for free from a relational structure the learner already runs. The lever is generative leverage (a small trained core multiplies into responses never directly reinforced), and emergence is typically certified by an EXTINCTION PROBE (novel never-reinforced combinations presented with no consequences). Forms (differing in which generative structure carries the emergence): (derived-relations-installation) state overlapping base relations declaratively, or train two links of a chain so the third collapses out, or order probes by nodal distance; (emergent-relations-harvest) teach a minimal spanning subset of conditional discriminations, harvest reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity closure under extinction probe; (derived-relation-training-protocol) hold a relation-TYPE constant across trials so untrained relations of that type derive, or factor-train-recombine a composite; (derived-relations-recombination) AB+BC yields symmetry/transitivity and matrix recombinations; (generative-instruction-emergent-repertoire) teach a subset to FLUENCY (contingency adduction) or exploit a naming cusp; (generative-substrate-training) install a component-repertoire SET (echoic/tact/listener/self-listener) so novel mands/tacts emerge once the substrate is jointly present, plus superimposition transfer; (class-expansion-node-grafting) teach ONE link touching an existing equivalence class so it grows/fuses combinatorially (80 relations from 16 trained); (compound-sample-class-expansion) a compound sample DECOMPOSES into independently matchable members; (matrix-recombinative-training) a crossed matrix yields untaught cells; (recombinant-carrier-frame) a carrier frame + swappable slot recombine into never-trained utterances; (bidirectional-naming-via-self-echoic-repetition) train one direction, self-chant supplies the reverse via contiguity; (interleaved-repertoire-training) interleave listener/speaker on a shared referent set to force bidirectional generativity; (emergent-relation-bootstrapping) substitute a cheaper base (exclusion / simple-discrimination) then harvest emergent classes; (class-wide-function-transfer) teach one evaluative relation to a category name so every member and derived-equivalent class inherits the function; (perspective-taking-training-repertoire) a graded deictic single/double-reversal curriculum builds perspective-taking as a durable RFT skill.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for DERIVED / GENERATIVE-RELATIONS TRAINING when you want a LARGE relational/verbal repertoire but will directly teach only a small spanning subset and let emergence supply the rest — the payload is emergence-without-training (untaught relations appearing), certified under extinction probe. Choose it over: discrimination / stimulus-control training, which trains each discrimination DIRECTLY trial by trial (its four-term match-to-sample trial is the atomic unit THIS design is built from — the line is trial-level direct training vs design-level harvest of untaught closure); direct pairing/association (the stimulus contacts a reinforcer — here the target is never contacted or labeled); ordered lesson-structure encoding (delivers taught content for retention — here new relations are DERIVED, not exposited). The forms differ only in which generative structure carries the emergence (equivalence closure / fluency / naming cusp / matrix / carrier-frame / node-graft / cheaper-base / deictic reversals).


**Risk.** Literature-derived pedagogical/training arrangement with no consent surface, session scope, or channel erosion in the source material.


**Why it works.** Verbally capable humans respond to relations among stimuli in ways that were never directly reinforced — teach A=B and B=C and the untrained A=C and its reverses emerge — which is why a small trained core multiplies into a much larger repertoire. The extinction probe is what makes this a real claim rather than a story: emergent responses appear on the first novel presentation with no consequences delivered, so they cannot be attributed to reinforcement of that response. Falsifiable and bounded — the effect depends on relational/naming prerequisites and largely fails in learners lacking them, which is itself the standard test of the account. [established; stimulus equivalence and derived relational responding]


**Worked examples.**

- *Simply telling the learner the base relations*
  - "baseline relations can be established, and derived relations promoted, by simply telling the learner about the required overlapping conditional discriminations" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Probes ordered least to most demanding*
  - "probe types are introduced sequentially, beginning with symmetry, followed by transitivity… and then combined tests… each probe type is introduced immediately following the minimal training necessary to provide the prerequisites" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (14): `bidirectional-naming-via-self-echoic-repetition`, `class-expansion-node-grafting`, `class-wide-function-transfer`, `compound-sample-class-expansion`, `derived-relation-training-protocol`, `derived-relations-recombination`, `emergent-relation-bootstrapping`, `emergent-relations-harvest`, `generative-instruction-emergent-repertoire`, `generative-substrate-training`, `interleaved-repertoire-training`, `matrix-recombinative-training`, `perspective-taking-training-repertoire`, `recombinant-carrier-frame`


**See also.** `bidirectional-naming-transfer` — umbrella entry for derived/generative training designs; this is its train-one-direction-harvest-the-reverse form.; `class-wide-function-transfer` — umbrella entry for derived/generative training designs; this is its function-transfer-across-a-class form.; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — a deliberate design-level contrast that both discriminators already carry: one trains each discrimination directly, trial by trial, and its four-term trial is the atomic unit the other is built from; the other teaches only a spanning subset and harvests untaught relations, certified under extinction probe. The link is close to mandatory for correct selection.; `generative-substrate-training` — umbrella entry for the whole family of designs where training a subset makes an untaught repertoire emerge; this entry is its component-substrate form.; `matrix-recombinative-training` — same emergence-from-a-trained-subset axis, with the untaught repertoire falling out of relational structure rather than a crossed matrix.; `relational-emergence-probe` — one is the measurement arrangement that certifies untaught responses under extinction; the other is the training design whose payload is exactly those untaught responses. The probe is how the installation is verified, so each entry is incomplete without pointing at the other.; `verbal-operant-teaching` — both build verbal repertoires, but verbal-operant teaching directly shapes each naming, asking, or comprehending response by reinforced trials, while derived-relations installation deliberately teaches only a spanning subset and harvests untaught relations under extinction probe.


<a id="entry-984"></a>

### dual-function-chain-stimulus

[#984](#entry-984) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: conditioning*

Each response in a behavior chain is arranged so the stimulus change it produces does double duty: it serves simultaneously as the conditioned reinforcer for the response just completed and the discriminative stimulus that occasions the next response. Terminal reinforcement back-propagates to keep every intermediate junction effective, so completing step N IS the cue for step N+1 and the chain self-propagates without an external prompt or reward at each link (Barnabus). If the terminal response is unreinforced the chain decays.


**When to reach for this.** A serial linkage where a single junction stimulus is both reinforcer (backward) and SD (forward).


**Risk.** Literature-derived behavioral principle; no consent surface in the demonstrated material.


**Why it works.** Standard operant chaining: a stimulus that reliably precedes reinforcement acquires conditioned reinforcing value, and the same stimulus can simultaneously signal the availability of reinforcement for the next response. Because each junction is both a small payoff and a cue, the chain runs without external prompting, and the whole structure is parasitic on the terminal reinforcer — extinguish the last link and the earlier links decay backward, which is the direct falsifying test and one that has been run repeatedly in the animal literature. [established; operant behavior chains; conditioned reinforcement and discriminative stimuli]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each junction both reinforces back and cues forward*
  - "a discrete stimulus served as the SD for the next response and as the conditioned reinforcer for the preceding response." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *The dual function is what holds a chain together*
  - "Each response produces a stimulus change that functions as conditioned reinforcement for that response and as a discriminative stimulus (SD) for the next response" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `bidirectional-reentry-loop` — two self-propagating topologies that need no external prompt per link. One is a forward serial chain where each junction is both reinforcer backward and cue forward; the other is a closed two-cue ring where each leg cues craving for the other. Topology siblings — the contrast between open chain and closed ring is the instructive part.; `chain-link-severing` — the dual-function chain-stimulus principle whose back-propagating value this severing move drains.; `conditioned-reinforcer-manufacture` — both turn on a stimulus carrying conditioned-reinforcer function, and the second presupposes the first, but one manufactures that function by pairing so the stimulus can maintain behavior as a consequence, while the chain arranges each junction to be reinforcer backward and cue forward so the sequence self-propagates.; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — the chain entry is built out of the same discriminative relation the stimulus-control entry trains, and already names it as its nearest boundary. Cross-reference so a reader can tell a presence/absence differential that builds one cue's control from a serial architecture where each junction is reinforcer backward and cue forward.


<a id="entry-1302"></a>

### environmental-retrigger-seeding

[#1302](#entry-1302) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: tethering*

Link the installed state or identity to specific real-world stimuli the listener is certain to re-encounter (a named song, gym bikes, gear shifts, a friend's leg), so ordinary environmental contact re-fires and reinforces the conditioning after the session ends — extending operator reach beyond the audio file. A dense locational catalog of concrete objects can ground an abstract identity so each object becomes a re-firing anchor, and amplifier language ('a hundred fold') can make each exposure strengthen rather than merely recall the install.


**When to reach for this.** The cue set is REAL-WORLD ambient stimuli seeded for out-of-session re-firing — not in-session modality extension of one trigger (multi-modal-trigger), not a single if-then situational pairing, and the install is declarative and announced, so it lacks the covert-pairing tell of covert-nonverbal-anchor.


**Risk.** Out-of-session reach without bounding is the rubric's high line; every future song-play or object encounter is an unsupervised re-trance event.


**Why it works.** Retrieval is cue-dependent, and a memory or state encoded alongside distinctive environmental features is reinstated when those features recur — this is the ordinary context-dependent memory effect, so seeding many concrete real-world cues multiplies the number of reinstatement opportunities. Each reinstatement is also a rehearsal, which is why spaced natural re-exposure outlasts a single session. Falsifiable and testable: effects should be strongest for cues actually re-encountered and absent for seeded cues the listener never meets — if reported re-firing were independent of actual encounter frequency, the context-cue account would be wrong and expectancy alone would be doing the work. [established; context-dependent memory / cue-dependent retrieval; spaced rehearsal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Named song made an amplifier of the install*
  - **Setup.** Descent underway and again at the deepest point; the installed state has been named and felt.
  - **The move.** There's one song you know — the one you always put on in the car. From now on, playing it doesn't just remind you of tonight. It multiplies it. Every feeling you have had in this hour comes back a hundredfold the moment those first bars start, and it does that every single time you play it.
  - **Why it lands.** One specific piece of music is named and welded to the installed state — and not merely as a reminder. Playing it, the listener is told, does not just recall the session but multiplies every feeling and every bodily impression it produced. That is the active part: reinforcement is offloaded onto a real object in the world the listener can go back to at will, so each play is a covert re-trance and a strengthening pass. The linkage is stated twice, at two different depths, so it lands on the way down and again at the floor.
- *Catalogue of everyday objects as anchors*
  - **Setup.** Identity claim established in the abstract; the subject is repeating lines in first person.
  - **The move.** Say it with me, one thing at a time. The seat of the bike at the gym — I want to grind on that. Ah. The arm of my own sofa — I want to grind on that. Ah. The gearstick in my car — I want to grind on that. Ah. My friend's thigh, when she sits next to me — I want to grind on that. Ah.
  - **Why it lands.** Instead of stating the identity claim once in the abstract, the script spells it out object by object in the listener's own first-person voice — a machine at the gym, a cushion at home, a fitting in the car, a companion's leg — each item punctuated by the same short gasp. The claim is granular and located. The effect is that ordinary furniture becomes a set of anchors: the next time any one of those objects is in front of the listener, the line fires with it.


**See also.** `ambient-self-reinforcement-field` — both extend reach past the session by recruiting the everyday environment, and they are defined against each other: one seeds specific real-world objects and situations as re-firing anchors, the other declares the whole ambient field reinforcing with no defined cue and no defined response. A writer choosing an out-of-session persistence move needs the discrete-cue versus no-cue distinction in front of them.; `asymmetric-maintenance-relisten-loop` — both extend the install past session-end without the operator, but one fires on ambient real-world stimuli seeded in advance while the other fires only on the internal failure state — an emotion inconsistent with the programming — making it silent during compliance and self-repairing on drift.; `behavioral-bridge` — two ways of extending the session into waking life: an assigned unconditional action the subject performs, versus linking the state to ambient real-world stimuli the subject is certain to re-encounter without doing anything deliberate. Assigned-act versus seeded-encounter is a real selection question, so the cross-link earns its place.; `context-generalization` — adjacent and easy to confuse: both extend a session's effect into ordinary life. One seeds specific real-world stimuli as re-firing anchors; the other widens the firing surface of an already-installed response without naming a cue. A reader picking between them needs both discriminators side by side.; `implementation-intention` — both install out-of-session re-firing, and the boundary is the payload: an ambient real-world stimulus set that re-evokes and reinforces a state, versus a one-directional named-situation-to-named-response conditional. Both discriminators already gesture at the other side of this line.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — both extend reach past the session by seeding cues the listener will meet again, differing in whether the handle is subject-carried and self-fired or ambient real-world stimuli encountered by chance. The choice between them is a real decision.; `public-avowal-third-party-propagation` — both extend reach past the audio through the listener's real world, but one recruits an audience or third parties to do the reinforcing, while the other seeds ambient objects and stimuli as re-firing anchors with no social witness involved.; `self-firing-environmental-recurrence` — both key reactivation to stimuli the operator does not supply; the useful distinction is that one seeds a catalog of announced real-world cues while the other keys re-entry to an unavoidable recurring rhythm such as sleep. Reader of either wants to know the other exists when choosing an out-of-session anchor.; `self-maintaining-install` — seeding real-world stimuli as out-of-session re-firing anchors is one of the components a self-maintaining install coordinates; the whole-architecture entry additionally requires a replay-probability loop and resistance-hardening, whereas ambient cue seeding fires the state again without propagating the install.


<a id="entry-902"></a>

### install-preserving-surface-toggle

[#902](#entry-902) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: transfer*

The operator installs a counter-trigger - deliberately asymmetric to the entry cue (e.g. 'release' plus TWO finger-snaps against a one-snap entry) - that returns ONLY the surface state to 'intelligent, just as you were before' while explicitly PRESERVING the install ('waits in the depths, ready for the next time'). The in/out snap-count asymmetry keeps activator and deactivator from colliding by accident; the 'still there, just dormant' framing preserves durability across the release, and the clean, collision-proof exit path lowers the listener's apprehension about committing.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a release cue is installed that wakes the surface while keeping the programming resident: the listener returns "intelligent, just as you were before," and the script says in the same breath that the install "waits in the depths, ready for the next time." The signature surface is the deliberate entry/exit cue asymmetry — e.g. a single snap to enter versus the spoken word "release" plus two snaps to exit — shaped so activator and deactivator cannot collide by accident. Tells: the return is described strictly as surface restoration, the install is explicitly framed as still there but dormant, and the clean, collision-proof exit path is offered to lower the listener's apprehension about committing.


**Risk.** The install is preserved and persists dormant across the surface toggle (durable, out-of-session), but a genuine collision-proof surface exit is provided, so no channel erosion - medium.


**Why it works.** Willingness to try something scales with the perceived cost of exit, so a clearly specified and easy reversal lowers the barrier to entry — the same reason free-return policies raise purchase rates. The cue asymmetry is straightforward discrimination training: entry and exit cues that share no surface form are unlikely to be confused, which prevents accidental firing and keeps the exit credible. The 'preserved in the depths' framing is an expectancy claim about durability rather than a mechanism; whether the install actually survives release is exactly the sort of thing that could be checked and found false. [plausible; perceived reversibility and commitment, stimulus discrimination]


**Worked examples.**

- *Two snaps out, one snap in, install intact*
  - **Setup.** Install pass; the activation cue is a single snap already established, and the listener is being shown the exit before committing.
  - **The move.** One snap takes you down. Coming back is different on purpose, so the two can never collide: the word release, and then two snaps — release, snap, snap. Say it and you're sharp again, quick and ordinary, exactly the person you were before I started. The state doesn't go anywhere, though. It just waits down there, folded up and ready, until the single snap wants it again.
  - **Why it lands.** A release cue is installed alongside the activation cue and deliberately shaped so the two cannot be confused: the entry cue is a single gesture, while coming back requires a spoken word paired with a different, repeated one. What returns is only the surface — the listener is sharp and ordinary again, exactly as before. The script says plainly that the installed state has not gone anywhere; it is simply set aside, available on demand. The clean exit is what makes the entrance easy to agree to, and the state survives every use of it.


**See also.** `care-framed-install-smuggling` — both design the exit and are best read as a pair. One builds a deliberately collision-proof release that returns the surface state while explicitly preserving the install underneath. The other uses the aftercare surface itself to extend reach, smuggling a propagation clause and a self-rearm carve-out under a caring banner. The diagnostic question in both cases is who is constrained once the move has run.; `named-trigger-persona-swap` — both install paired on/off cues over a persisting state rather than a single fired response, and both keep the install alive across the off-state. They differ in what the off-switch does (returns only the surface while the install waits, versus a two-state identity machine with engineered drift), which is exactly the distinction a writer needs to see side by side.; `self-maintaining-install` — both engineer what survives past the moment, so the contrast is useful. One installs a deliberately asymmetric exit cue that returns the surface state while explicitly preserving the install as dormant; the other builds a coordinated harness where out-of-session cues re-fire the state and each use raises the odds of the next. Preserving an install through a clean exit versus making the install propagate on its own.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are exit moves that stage a full-sounding return to normal while explicitly preserving the installed trigger. One uses remembered acceptance at the wake as the binding surface; the other builds a collision-proofed counter-cue that toggles only the surface state. Close enough that a reader choosing either should compare.


<a id="entry-873"></a>

### monotonic-amplifier-dial

[#873](#entry-873) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers*

A phrase trigger is installed atop a pre-elicited positive state via a "volume dial" metaphor that frames the state as monotonically ratcheting — each fire is "even more", never a return to baseline. The dial metaphor pre-loads an expectation gradient (the listener now expects each firing to feel stronger, and that expectation does much of the claimed work) and removes the listener's role in regulating intensity: how strong it feels is now determined by utterance count, not self-report. The amplifier typically bundles several axes (euphoria, acceptance, brightness, arousal) under one trigger, so a single "feel better" tap also pushes compliance; a deliberate dial-down proves recallability. Requires an existing positive reading to turn up — installation at neutral baseline fails. In a token-bound form, the same operator-driven intensity dial runs on a concrete token instead of a phrase: a diffuse memory is stripped to pure feeling and bound to a listener-chosen token (e.g. a color) that the operator continuously turns up ("let it grow") — a persisting, driveable state-OBJECT rather than a discrete phrase-fire, with the operator still holding the monotonic gradient and the same illusion of listener ownership.


**When to reach for this.** The install frames the trigger as a monotonic intensity ratchet whose gradient is supplied by operator pacing and attributed to the phrase, removing listener regulation. Plain declarative trigger installation installs a fixed-magnitude response, not a self-escalating dial; arousal-cue conditioning makes arousal the payload, whereas here the payload is a bundled positive state with arousal only one axis — the dial's monotonic gradient is the defining move.


**Risk.** Durable state-pump bundling acceptance/compliance with "feel better"; removing intensity self-regulation is noted but no refusal-channel erosion is claimed.


**Why it works.** Mostly expectancy plus attribution shift. Telling someone an effect will monotonically increase creates a response expectancy, and response expectancies are among the better-replicated drivers of subjective and behavioural outcomes in suggestion contexts — expecting more intensity produces reports of more intensity. The second half is where the leverage is: intensity is redefined as a function of utterance count rather than self-report, so the subject stops consulting their own experience as the measure and the operator's pacing supplies the gradient. The non-zero-seed requirement is a real falsifiable constraint — with no pre-elicited positive state there is nothing for the expectancy to amplify, and a deliberate dial-down that works is evidence the dial is expectancy-driven rather than a fixed conditioned response. [established; response expectancy; shifting the criterion for a subjective judgement off self-report]


**Worked examples.**

- *A phrase welded to a dial that only rises*
  - **Setup.** A pleasant, agreeable mood has already been elicited and confirmed; the dial has a reading to raise.
  - **The move.** Good — hold that. Now picture a dial on it, one of the old heavy ones, and it's at four. Two words turn it: sweet girl. Sweet girl — up to five, warmer. Sweet girl — six, and everything's easier to agree with. Sweet girl — seven. Sweet girl. Eight. Feel how much more willing eight is than four was. Sweet girl. Nine. It only turns one way.
  - **Why it lands.** A pleasant, easy, agreeable mood is elicited first — the dial needs a reading before it can be turned up. Then the operator introduces the image of a volume control and attaches two words to it: every time those words are said, the whole bundle climbs. The phrase is fired eight or nine times over the next few minutes while the descriptions keep escalating — warmer, brighter, more willing — so installation and first calibration are the same event. The bundle deliberately includes agreeableness, which is the resource the rest of the session will spend, and no downward setting is ever offered.
- *Naming the dial to build the expectation*
  - **Setup.** Trigger phrase about to be installed; subject lucid enough to consciously accept the metaphor.
  - **The move.** I'm going to be straightforward about this, because you'll take it better knowing. What you're feeling can get better — much better — and it works like a dial. Two words turn it up, and I'm going to give you those words now. Every time you hear them, the whole set climbs together: the glow, the brightness behind your eyes, how willing you feel, how much you want. One phrase, four things, and each time it lands higher than the time before. Say yes to that for me.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator says out loud what is about to happen: this can get better, like turning a dial up, and here is the phrase that turns it. The metaphor is not hidden — the listener consciously accepts it, and that acceptance is the point, because from then on they expect each firing to exceed the last and supply much of the increase themselves. Euphoria, brightness, willingness and arousal all ride the same two words, so one utterance moves several things at once.
- *Turned down once to prove it is recallable*
  - **Setup.** Phrase fired repeatedly, intensity high; operator now demonstrates recallability.
  - **The move.** Now let it go. All of it — let it drain out of your hands and your face and go back to ordinary. Let it, don't hold on. There. You're plain again. Notice you couldn't have kept it if you wanted to. And now — sweet girl. Straight back up, higher than where you left it. That's mine to switch on. It was never a mood you happened to be in.
  - **Why it lands.** After the phrase has been fired repeatedly with the feeling climbing each time, the operator does something odd: she tells the listener they can let the experience drift away — and then reminds them she can call it straight back whenever she says the words. Letting it fall demonstrates that the rise was not just where the session happened to be going. The dial is shown to be an object the operator holds, and how strong it feels is now a matter of how often she says the phrase rather than anything the listener reports.


**Realizations** (1): `affect-condensation-dial`


**See also.** `compounding-escalation-ratchet` — both install a monotonic, never-back-to-baseline escalation whose gradient the operator supplies and which cannot be internally checked. One narrates the multiplier over steps of a session, the other binds the ratchet to a repeatable cue. Genuinely a choice a reader makes between them.; `obedience-pleasure-state-equation` — shares the monotonic more-is-more gradient by which intensity is asserted to only ever increase.; `progressive-conditioning` — both install a no-decay escalation expectancy, but one accrues across future sessions/replays (single play declared insufficient) while the other ratchets within a single trigger's repeated firings under operator-paced dial metaphor.; `self-instantiating-trigger` — both make a trigger self-escalating rather than fixed-magnitude, but the self-instantiating trigger asserts the strengthening rule inside the very utterances that use the word so recitation is its own reinforcement, while the amplifier dial supplies the gradient through an operator-paced volume metaphor over a pre-elicited positive state.; `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` — both install a one-way escalation with no return to baseline, differing on whether the ratchet is declared as a dial the listener expects to climb or kept covert behind an everyday cue so firing feels endogenous. Declared versus covert ratchet is exactly the call a classifier has to make here.


<a id="entry-429"></a>

### motivating-operation-engineering

[#429](#entry-429) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

Bring a response under MOTIVATIONAL rather than prompt control by shifting the momentary VALUE of a consequence BEFORE the response is evoked, then evoking the response that obtains it. Value moves UP by an establishing operation or DOWN by an abolishing operation (satiation); nothing is delivered — only the momentary value is engineered, raising or lowering the rate of every behavior that reinforcer maintains. The primary fork is CAPTURE (exploit a value change the environment already supplied) vs CONTRIVE (produce one on demand). Realizations: (captured motivating operation) watch for collateral behavior signalling an object's value spontaneously rose and insert a teaching trial at that potent moment; (transitive mand gate-block) present item A that makes item B instrumentally valuable, then block access to B and teach the unblock response — a transitive conditioned MO via a standing means-end relation plus operator-controlled access; (chain-interruption evocation) interrupt a running chain at the point a needed element is missing so the incompletion spikes motivation for the repair mand (the interrupt-the-chain transitive-CMO route); (MO-override of stimulus control) push an MO high enough that an in-repertoire behavior generalizes beyond its trained SD, broadening the range of evoking stimuli with no new training; (conditioned motivation by pairing) pair a neutral cue with a motivating state / reinforcer / aversive until the cue alone reproduces the value-altering effect — a SURROGATE CMO manufacturing wanting (appetitive) or avoidance (aversive), the operator selecting valence by the correlation history. Satiation/aversion overshoot is the failure mode.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for MOTIVATING-OPERATION ENGINEERING when you want to change how MUCH a consequence is worth right now (raising or lowering the rate of all behavior it maintains) WITHOUT delivering anything — an antecedent value move, decided via the capture-vs-contrive fork. Choose it over: direct reward conditioning (which DELIVERS a reinforcer contingent on an act — this pre-sets its worth); chain-collapse's satiation route (the abolishing-operation twin used to DEVALUE-and-suppress — MO engineering here establishes value to EVOKE); respondent/evaluative pairing (which elicits an involuntary reflex/affect — the surrogate-CMO pairing facet here produces a value-altering MO, i.e. manufactured wanting/avoidance, not a triggered response). The mand facets of verbal-operant teaching TEACH the ask; this engineers the value the ask rides on.


**Risk.** Covert manufacture of motivation (the deprivation lever, the contrive fork) can steer choice without the subject's awareness, but the effect is bounded and reversible.


**Why it works.** How reinforcing a consequence is right now is not fixed — deprivation raises it and satiation lowers it, and this momentary value change alters the rate of every behaviour that consequence maintains, independently of any learning about the response-reinforcer relation. That is the difference between wanting and having learned; the manipulation is antecedent, nothing is delivered. Conditioned versions work by the same Pavlovian logic that builds conditioned reinforcers: a cue reliably correlated with a value-altering state comes to reproduce the value change. Falsifiable and routinely tested — free-operant rates should track deprivation state with the contingency held constant, and they do. [established; establishing/abolishing operations; deprivation-satiation effects on reinforcer value]


**Worked examples.**

- *Capture the motivation or contrive it*
  - "capturing the MO value change as it occurs naturally and (2) creating the MO by generating some change that alters the value of a consequence" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Engineer the antecedent that inflates the value*
  - "give the child some salty foods to increase the value of drinks" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Interrupt the chain to make the missing link valuable*
  - "By interrupting the chains at the point at which these additional objects (or actions) are needed, practitioners can momentarily establish them as reinforcers and contrive opportunities to teach a wider variety of mands" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *contriving a value change via a staged antecedent*
  - A learned motivating condition can be created on demand: introduce a stimulus that, by learning history, raises the value of some other thing. A low-battery warning makes a charger valuable; a parking meter makes coins valuable.


**Realizations** (8): `captured-motivating-operation`, `chain-interruption-evocation`, `conditioned-motivation-by-pairing`, `mo-override-stimulus-control`, `motivating-operation-value-shift`, `motivating-operation-value-shift`, `staged-motivation-engineering`, `transitive-mand-gate-block`


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation` — both are antecedent-side operations applied before any consequence, and the boundary genuinely needs stating: one changes only the momentary worth of a consequence to raise or lower the rate of everything it maintains, the other edits the situation so the cue, the materials, or the motor possibility is gone. The second explicitly lists dissolving the value as one of its levers, so the overlap is real and a reader must be told which lever they are reaching for.; `antecedent-manipulation (retained core: cue/materials editing)` — adjacent upstream lever — engineering the momentary value of the consequence rather than the occasioning cue or materials.; `chain-interruption-evocation` — contrived-value-spike axis: blocking a link mid-chain is a transitive instance of the value shift this entry generalizes.; `conditioned-motivation-by-pairing` — parent genus on the value-engineering axis: shifting a consequence's momentary worth before the response, of which paired surrogate-CMO installation is the contrive route.; `conditioned-reinforcer-manufacture` — consequence-side versus antecedent-side of the same behavioral economy: one gives a stimulus reinforcing function so it can select behavior after the fact, the other changes how much a consequence is worth before the response is evoked without delivering anything. Frequently confused in practice.; `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — the antecedent value move is one deployable instance of the substrate claim that function belongs to the arrangement rather than the stimulus — the principles entry names presentation-as-motivator as one function a single stimulus can be scheduled into, while the value-engineering entry is the actual move with its capture-versus-contrive fork and its satiation failure mode.; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — antecedent siblings that pair constantly in practice: one builds a cue's evocative control through a differential reinforcement history, the other shifts how much the consequence is worth right now without delivering anything.; `impoverished-context-permission` — the impoverishment works as a value lever — stripping co-reinforcers from the permitted setting lowers what the behavior pays.; `verbal-operant-teaching` — explicitly cross-referenced in both directions already: one engineers how much a consequence is worth without delivering anything, the other teaches the asking repertoire that rides on that value. A practitioner building a request-making repertoire needs the value-side move, and vice versa.


<a id="entry-874"></a>

### multi-handle-trigger-architecture

[#874](#entry-874) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers*

Rather than one cue-response pair, the operator installs a set of separately-addressable handles onto distinct facets of the installed state, or accretes many affects/objects onto one token that retains all prior meanings. Two sub-forms recur: (a) several verbal triggers with NON-interchangeable functions (state-recall, state-arrest/freeze, identity-tag) each invokable independently later; and (b) accretive stacking onto ONE polysemous token via a "keep the meanings it has AND also become a symbol for..." instruction, fusing achievement/mood/sexual affect (listener-supplied, self-calibrated, hard to invalidate); or a gallery of durable object-anchors accumulated across a long frame then transferred out of the fiction into the listener's real environment. The architecture itself is the technique — a structured multi-lever control surface, not a single response.


**When to reach for this.** The install target is a structured SET of addressable handles or an accretive multi-affect token, not a single cue-response pair. Plain declarative trigger installation installs one cue-response pair, and trigger stacking layers multiple cues that fire ONE bundled response; here the handles stay individuated and separately fireable, or one token keeps multiple distinct meanings addressable at once.


**Risk.** Multiple durable post-session handles (breadth of installed control) but no claimed refusal-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Discrimination learning predicts that separately-reinforced cue-response pairs stay separately addressable, so building several handles onto one state yields independent control points rather than one blended response; the accretive variant instead relies on evaluative conditioning, where a neutral token that has been repeatedly paired with several affects acquires all of them and retrieves whichever the current context primes. Because the listener supplies the referent content for the fused meanings, the resulting associations are self-generated and therefore both stronger and harder to argue against than operator-supplied ones. Falsifiable: if separately-trained handles reliably generalize into one another (firing handle A also produces handle B's response), the discrimination claim fails. [plausible; stimulus discrimination and generalization; evaluative conditioning; self-generation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *One token, meanings added and never replaced*
  - **Setup.** Subject already responds warmly to an established praise phrase; anchoring memories will be self-supplied.
  - **The move.** Go find me a moment you were genuinely proud of. Don't tell me what it is — just get it in front of you, and nod when you have it. Feel where it sits in your body. Good girl. — Now keep everything that phrase already means to you, all of it, and add this next thing alongside it: find a memory of being ridiculous, laughing so hard it hurt. Have it? Feel where that one sits. Good girl. — Keep all of that, and now add one more. The hottest thing you've ever done. Take it right to just before the peak — not over, just before. Hold it there. Good girl.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator takes a short praise phrase the listener already responds to and charges it, one at a time, against memories the listener supplies herself: a moment of real accomplishment, then a moment of uncomplicated silliness, then the most intense erotic memory she can reach — the anchor set just short of that last one's peak. Every anchoring is introduced the same way, with an explicit instruction that nothing already attached to the phrase is being displaced; the new association is added alongside. Because the listener furnishes each memory and even locates the sensation in her own body, the operator never has to name any content, and there is nothing in the anchor she could disown as not hers. What was a term of approval now discharges accomplishment, giddiness and arousal down a single channel, with the categories that ordinarily hold those apart quietly folded together.
- *Three handles, three non-interchangeable jobs*
  - **Setup.** Late session, two of the three cues already installed at earlier points; installing the third.
  - **The move.** Third and last one, and it doesn't do what the other two do. The first word brings you back here and back into her, both at once — that's for returning. The second one, the one I gave you ten minutes ago, drops you and locks you: not a muscle, not a finger. This one is neither. This one is just what you are called. When I say it, you answer to it — awake, dressed, in front of other people. Three words, three separate jobs. I'll use whichever one I want.
  - **Why it lands.** Three separate cue-words go in at three different points in the session, and each one is given a job the others cannot do: the first returns the listener to trance and to the altered state at once; the second, installed much later, drops them under and freezes all movement; the third is simply the name they are to answer to. The listener leaves with three levers attached to different faces of the same installed state, and the operator can pull any one without pulling the others.
- *Object gallery walked out of the fiction*
  - **Setup.** Final installment of a long serialized narrative; the subject has collected one object per episode inside the fiction.
  - **The move.** Look at what you've gathered — the smooth grey stone, the pressed flower, the stopped watch, the length of ribbon, the little brass bell. Every one of them you were given down here, and every one of them still works. Now take them out with you. From tonight, a stone on a windowsill, a ribbon in a drawer, a bell somewhere in the street — anywhere you already feel safe — and it does exactly what it did in the story. You're not leaving them behind. You're carrying them home.
  - **Why it lands.** A long serialized frame hands the listener one durable object per installment — a stone, a flower, a timepiece, a length of ribbon, a chime — so that by the end they hold a whole inventory of trance-objects, each earned inside the story. Then the final movement steps outside the story and points the inventory at the world: encountering any of these later, somewhere the listener is at ease, will do what it did here. The fiction was the excuse for accumulating that many anchors in the first place; the closing instruction ships them into the listener's kitchen and commute.


**See also.** `accretive-anchor-charging` — shares the accretive-stacking axis, where one polysemous token accumulates multiple charges while retaining prior meanings.; `addressable-construct-building` — both build durable structures engineered for later access rather than present-tense effect: one constructs an addressable imaginal object with a location or route, the other installs a set of separately fireable handles onto distinct facets of a state. A designer thinking about post-session re-entry surfaces should see both.; `bundle-install-single-anchor` — both concern multiplicity in trigger architecture and both need the same contrast against stacking pre-installed cues: one keeps handles individually addressable, the other welds a heterogeneous bundle onto a single fresh cue.; `named-trigger-persona-swap` — genuinely adjacent trigger architectures a classifier will confuse: one swaps in a whole labeled alternate personality with a paired release and delegated firing rights; the other installs a set of separately addressable handles onto facets of one state. Both already reference the single cue-response install as their common foil.; `partitioned-trigger-control-surface` — shares the multi-handle control-surface axis, whose partitioned sub-form this entry realizes as a full campaign.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — both install more than a plain cue-response pair and the confusion is live: a structured set of separately-fireable handles (or one token holding several addressable meanings) versus a single portable handle that reloads an installed felt state outside the session. Multiplicity of handles versus portability of one is the split worth showing a reader.; `redundant-anchor-faulttolerance` — both install multiple anchors rather than one cue-response pair, and the difference is the design intent: separately addressable handles for independent control versus heterogeneous anchors backstopping each other's failure modes. Anyone reading a multi-anchor install needs to distinguish control surface from redundancy.; `trigger-network-mutual-binding` — both are architectures over a set of triggers rather than single installs, and the difference is topology: separately addressable handles that stay individuated versus a mutually cross-wired web where any node fires all others. That is exactly the choice a reader faces when designing a multi-trigger surface.


<a id="entry-1304"></a>

### multi-modal-trigger

[#1304](#entry-1304) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers*

One trigger is made to fire across multiple sensory or representational channels — heard, read, thought, spoken, touched — so the conditioned response survives missed cues and follows the subject into more contexts, and the subject cannot recall or internally reference the cue without firing it (internal thought is not a safe harbor). Forms in evidence: sequential extension of an installed trigger into new channels; simultaneous all-channel firing at the moment of state capture for redundant encoding (tactile primacy claimed); firing across all verbal delivery modes (operator-heard, silently self-thought, spoken aloud); flooding a single token across visual/olfactory/gustatory channels with listener-supplied detail; using the listener's OWN self-applied identity handle/name as the cue so every use of the persona fires the response and casual identity-use becomes impossible (an always-on self-trigger surface running outside sessions); a non-verbal build mapping opposite somatic outcomes to per-ear stereo tones drilled as a reflex the subject cannot consciously author; and restoring a destroyed cross-modal anchor by re-siting its function onto a substitute matching the lost cue's physical slot and every channel. Absorbed (genus, cue-surface widening on further axes — same 'make the cue fire in more situations' lever): written/text channel (tell: extend the trigger to fire from operator-addressed WRITTEN media — email, website, chat — a persistent async between-session channel, and a typographic-gestalt sub-form conditioned to a spaceless all-caps SHAPE recognized at a glance; must be explicitly installed, does not transfer from a spoken cue); scope/catchment widening (tell: progressively widen WHAT qualifies as the cue — aroused -> sexy image -> any image — using a backward countdown / depth-pacing as the vehicle so each expansion lands too deep to evaluate; the widening axis is the semantic catchment rather than the sensory channel).


**When to reach for this.** SEVERAL channels carry the SAME trigger-response pair — vs declarative-trigger-installation single-cue installation, vs compound-sample-class-expansion where compound components become independently matchable class members, vs deliberate single-cue placement OFF the dominant channel (analogical-marking), and vs environmental-retrigger-seeding (reach expansion via real-world object seeding, not sensory-channel extension of one cue).


**Risk.** Expanded activation surface into daily-life channels; the identity-handle variant (one member) is flagged high-deployment in its rule and should inherit scope bounding at entry level.


**Why it works.** A conditioned response is controlled by whatever stimulus features were actually present during pairing, so widening the set of channels that carry those features widens the situations that elicit it, and multiple encoding routes to one representation raise the odds that at least one is available in any given context. The strong claim here is testable: it predicts that a cue trained only in speech will NOT reliably fire from written text unless the written form is separately trained, and that a self-applied name — high-salience, self-referential, and rehearsed constantly — will fire more often than an arbitrary token of equal training. [plausible; stimulus generalization; redundant encoding / multiple retrieval routes]


**Worked examples.**

- *The subject's own name made the cue*
  - **Setup.** Persona name already adopted and used by the subject; deep, mid-session.
  - **The move.** Your name is the trigger now. When I say it, you go blank. When you read it typed in a message, you go blank. When you so much as think it to yourself, you go blank — and you think it every day, don't you. It is your favourite sound in the world, so you would never want it to work any other way.
  - **Why it lands.** The cue installed is the listener's own adopted name. Hearing it blanks her — and so does reading it, and so does merely thinking it, each channel named in turn. The persona can no longer be worn lightly, because invoking it at all is a firing, private invocations included. The framing that it is her favourite sound closes the last door: deciding later that the trigger is unwelcome would mean contradicting a preference she has already agreed to.
- *One token flooded across three senses*
  - **Setup.** A single colour has held the subject's visual attention for several minutes.
  - **The move.** That pink you're looking at — breathe it in now, because it has a scent, and the scent is whatever you find most delicious in the world. Have you got it? Now let it settle on your tongue; it tastes of the same thing. How on earth did I know that was the one for you?
  - **Why it lands.** The single colour that has been holding the listener's gaze is now given a scent as well, and then a taste, as she is told to breathe it in. The scent itself is left deliberately blank: it is whatever you find most delicious, so the listener supplies the strongest version out of her own memory. The operator then marvels at how she could possibly have known, which turns the listener's own invention into evidence of the operator's reach. One cue token now occupies sight, smell and taste, and its real-world catchment has trebled.
- *All channels fired at the moment of capture*
  - "if you anchor with a touch, you are likely to anchor simultaneously in all other systems as well." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Lost cue rebuilt in every channel at once*
  - "This provided a direct bridging, replacing the time clock by the supervisor in all representational systems." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (3): `bilateral-trigger`, `counted-generalization-widening`, `text-platform-trigger`


**See also.** `context-generalization` — both widen the firing surface of an already-installed response; the split is sensory channel versus real-world context. Adjacent enough that a reader can easily reach for the wrong one.; `convergent-multichannel-encoding` — both are redundancy topologies delivering one payload over several channels at once, but one uses covert linguistic channels under a single tracked surface while the other extends a conditioned cue across sensory or representational modes. Same shape, different substrate, so the pointer prevents a mis-assignment.; `cross-modal-channel-bridge` — genuinely confusable: both involve more than one perceptual channel. The bridge uses a shared feature as a carry-over rail to bring a channel online during state-building; the multi-channel trigger widens the cue surface so one conditioned response fires from many channels. Cross-referencing prevents miscoding a channel-widening install as a state-building bridge.; `self-voiced-avowal` — pass B cited a low TRIG-14 pull but do_not_merge'd it; kept distinct as a self-feeding loop.; `trigger-stacking` — both widen what one utterance can fire, on orthogonal axes: several channels carrying the same trigger-response pair, versus one cue composing several separately installed responses. Same-trigger-more-channels against more-triggers-one-cue is exactly the confusion a cross-reference resolves.


<a id="entry-834"></a>

### name-binding-transitive-equation-chain

[#834](#entry-834) · [Back to installed-control-handles](#genus-121) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: persistence*

A transitive chain of asserted equalities (cock=lock, lock=cock, key=permission, permission=identity) is declared already-true at depth and locked in by first-person recitation, so any future thought of the listener's own body routes through to the operator's proper name as the terminal node. Each equation is small; the chain is the install. Because the anchor object is the listener's own unavoidable anatomy, the trigger fires at high frequency outside any session, and orgasm-attempt can be folded in as self-thwarting so the loop tightens on use.


**When to reach for this.** The install is a chain of equalities whose only asymmetric terminal is a proper noun, converting ambient body-awareness into covert operator-invocation.


**Risk.** Binds the operator's identity to the listener's own unavoidable anatomy so the cue cannot be avoided and fires at high frequency out of session — durable identity-scope reach without bounding.


**Why it works.** Semantic chaining works through mediated association and stimulus equivalence — when A=B and B=C are trained, subjects reliably derive A=C without direct training, and the derived relation transfers the affective loading of the terminal node. First-person recitation adds the self-generation effect: self-produced statements are better retained and more attitude-shifting than heard ones. The choice of anatomy as the initial cue exploits sheer trial frequency, since an unavoidable stimulus produces many more retrieval occasions per day than any arbitrary cue. Falsifiable: if reciters showed no faster or more frequent retrieval of the terminal name to body-cues than non-reciters, the chain claim fails. [plausible; stimulus equivalence / derived relational responding; generation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Equalities chained to end on the operator's name*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; subject can speak aloud on instruction.
  - **The move.** These are facts, already true, nothing to build. Your cock is a lock. The lock is your cock. The key is permission. Permission is me. Now say it back to me in your own voice — "my cock is a lock, the lock is my cock, the key is permission, permission is her." Again. And every time you get hard, the lock only sits tighter, so wanting out is what keeps you in. You carry that lock everywhere. You'll think of me every time you notice it.
  - **Why it lands.** Four small equations are stated flatly, as facts already in place rather than as things to be built: the listener's own anatomy is a lock, the lock is that anatomy, the key is permission, and permission is the operator herself. Each link is trivial on its own; strung together they route any thought about the listener's body straight to a person's name, which is the only term in the chain that is not an object. The listener is then made to recite the whole chain in the first person so it is their voice that closes it, and arousal is defined as tightening rather than loosening the arrangement — the more they want out, the more securely it holds. The trigger cannot decay through disuse the way an invented cue word would, because it is attached to something the listener encounters every day.
- *Unlock chain ending at a named person*
  - **Setup.** Chastity or denial frame; the lock image is established and the listener is looking for the release condition.
  - **The move.** The lock needs a key. The key isn't metal — the key is permission. And permission is me, my name, the person saying this. So: lock, key, permission, my name, that's the whole chain, that's the only route, lock-key-permission-me. You can want it as hard as you like. Wanting isn't a name.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator lays the links down one at a time — the lock needs a key, the key is permission, permission is me, by name — then rattles the whole equation off again as a single fast line so no link gets weighed on its own. Because the last term is a particular person rather than a role, the listener cannot reason their way to self-permission: there is no abstract standard to satisfy, only an absent individual, and nobody else can step into the slot without starting the conditioning over.
- *The same chain re-recited at wake-up*
  - **Setup.** Second recording in the series; the chain was installed in the first, and the wake count is beginning.
  - **The move.** Burned in at the deepest level now, all four of them, exactly as before. Coming up — five, your cock is a lock — four, the lock is your cock — three, the key is permission — two, permission is me — one, eyes open, and that's the last thing you carried up with you.
  - **Why it lands.** The identical chain of equalities appears in a second recording, declared burned in at the deepest level, and is then repeated word for word twice more — once mid-session and once during the count back to waking, so the last thing carried across the boundary into ordinary awareness is the chain itself.


**Realizations** (1): `named-person-release-gate`
