**See also.** `ambient-surface-trigger` — both pick an anchor the listener cannot avoid encountering so the trigger fires at high everyday frequency without the operator present.; `asymmetric-state-lock` — both hand an off-switch to the operator, but the named-person gate blocks self-granted RELEASE by collapsing permission onto a non-substitutable proper noun, while the asymmetric lock monopolizes the subject's autonomous EXIT from the state regardless of who holds the key.; `identity-equivalence-chain` — one is the general form of asserted-equality chains; the other is a specific application where the chain's terminal node is a proper name and the anchor is the listener's own anatomy, so the equivalence fires constantly outside any session. A reader designing or identifying a chain benefits from seeing the high-frequency-anchor variant.; `internal-event-keyed-trigger` — both key a response to an unavoidable internal event so firing needs no operator, but one cues on the structural act of thinking or self-monitoring (making the trigger untestable, since checking is itself the cue), while the other routes ambient body-awareness to a proper name through a chain of asserted equalities.; `open-authority-socket`; `peer-gated-social-unlock` — parallel release gates that put the unlock permission somewhere the listener cannot reach: a non-substitutable named individual, or an out-of-session reciprocal peer economy. Choose by whether the permission node is a person or a protocol.; `somatic-self-anchor` — they combine rather than duplicate: one routes a transitive chain of equalities so ambient body-awareness terminates in the operator's name, the other sites the anchor on the body itself so it cannot be set down. The anatomy-as-cue property is exactly the seam where a reader of one wants the other.


<a id="genus-214"></a>

## installed-state-switches (3)

Pre-install paired tokens — a phrase, a tonal mark, a command word — that later flip the listener between discrete states: functional vs surrendered, self vs alter, sealed vs recalled.

[command-token-substate-toggle](#entry-256) · [marked-cue-amnesia-switch](#entry-1303) · [named-trigger-persona-swap](#entry-835)


<a id="entry-256"></a>

### command-token-substate-toggle

[#256](#entry-256) · [Back to installed-state-switches](#genus-214) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-partition*

Pre-declares a pair of command tokens that toggle the listener between trance SUBSTATES rather than between trance and waking: "function" grants operable, eyes-open awareness (able to interact with a computer, complete a purchase) WITHOUT leaving trance, and "surrender" snaps back to deep helpless trance. Trance becomes a state with toggleable substates rather than a binary in/out; the frame- preservation layer does the real work — actions taken in the functional substate are pre-interpreted as continued submission, so externally-observable motor behavior is obtained without breaking the frame.


**When to reach for this.** A reversible substate toggle WITHIN trance whose payload is frame-preserved motor capability — solving the eyes-open-purchase problem. vs a plain wake/re-induction trigger: neither token exits trance. vs a simple trigger install: the tokens gate a substate transition and pre-interpret conduct as submission, not a discrete cue->response.


**Risk.** Obtains operable eyes-open behavior (purchases) while keeping the trance frame and pre-labeling all conduct as submission.


**Why it works.** Nothing neurological toggles here; what toggles is which role the subject is enacting. Hypnotic 'states' are strongly governed by demand characteristics and role expectations, so a labelled token tells the subject which behavioural set is now appropriate, and pre-interpreting the functional interval as continued submission removes the contradiction that ordinary purposeful action would otherwise pose to the frame. Falsifiable: if subjects given the same token pair without the pre-interpretation frame reported the same continuity of submission across the functional interval, the framing layer would not be doing the work claimed. [plausible; demand characteristics / role enactment in hypnosis]


**Worked examples.**

- *Paired tokens toggling operable and helpless substates within trance*
  - **Setup.** Pre-declared during induction; used later when the subject must operate a device without the frame breaking.
  - **The move.** Two words from here on. When I say FUNCTION, your eyes open and your hands work and you can read a screen — and you are still exactly as deep as you are now, because doing what I need done is what being under looks like from the outside. When I say SURRENDER, the hands stop and you drop back where you belong. Function.
  - **Why it lands.** The subject gains real motor capability without an exit cue firing, and the pre-interpretation clause means the competent behaviour is scored as obedience rather than as waking. The operator observes accurate task execution paired with retained trance markers — flat affect, slow speech, no spontaneous conversation.


**See also.** `asymmetric-state-lock` — overlapping on exit control: in the substate toggle neither token returns the subject to waking, so the actual off-switch stays with the operator even though both directions are offered. The other entry names operator-monopolized exit as its whole mechanism. Check both when a state offers movement but no autonomous way out.; `awake-channel-trance-surface` — adjacent solutions to the same problem of acting in the world without breaking the frame: one toggles an operable substate inside trance, the other redefines the ordinary waking channel as a suggestion surface. Easy to confuse when the subject is functional and aware.; `partitioned-trigger-control-surface` — shares the substate-toggle axis, where paired tokens move the listener between distinct in-trance configurations.; `stay-deep-across-boundary` — worth linking: the token pair that toggles between an operable substate and deep helplessness is one concrete way to achieve what the other entry describes topologically -- keeping the subject in the deep state across a boundary that would normally end it. A reader working the eyes-open-but-still-under problem wants both the general boundary-neutralizing options and this specific reversible-toggle solution.; `wake-gate-obedience-tagging` — both tamper with the in/out boundary so there is no neutral exit — one by making the toggle stay inside trance, the other by taxing the wake-act with a submissive utterance. Useful adjacent reading on exit-boundary engineering.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — both solve the same problem: obtaining eyes-open, externally observable action without conceding that trance ended. One maintains a still-under overlay to drive a public attributable act that then self-ratifies the state; the other pre-declares tokens toggling between an operable substate and deep trance. Read together for the frame-preservation trick they share.


<a id="entry-1303"></a>

### marked-cue-amnesia-switch

[#1303](#entry-1303) · [Back to installed-state-switches](#genus-214) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: amnesia*

Pre-mark a token during trance by tone/tempo/emphasis and train the MARK, not the word's meaning, as a binary handle on a posthypnotic amnesia. Later the operator re-presents only that marked token to flip the sealed material open or shut, or delivers a matched second reserved phrase that runs the suppression anchor in reverse, flooding the sealed content back complete; the delayed-key form slips the tonally-planted cue into ordinary post-trance talk on the operator's timing to re-open sealed material outside the trance frame. Because the active ingredient is the analogical mark, ordinary paraphrase, frank statement, or full retelling all fail to reach the block; only the tagged token operates the switch, and the release feels spontaneous to the subject rather than commanded.


**When to reach for this.** The active ingredient is the mark isolated over semantics — proven by the failure of every non-marked prompt — operating an amnesia gate. Trigger-activation fires a state-shift, not a memory-gate toggle; a plain amnesia suggestion installs the seal, while this operates its key; and an amnesia-wrapped command wraps a command in forgetting rather than switching the amnesia itself.


**Risk.** Operating a posthypnotic amnesia gate manipulates memory access outside the subject's control and the release feels un-commanded; durable within the sealed set but bounded, so medium.


**Why it works.** Retrieval is cue-dependent: material encoded alongside a distinctive perceptual feature is reached most reliably by a cue that reinstates that feature, and suppressed material is usually blocked at retrieval rather than erased from storage. That predicts the observed pattern — semantic paraphrase fails while the tonally-marked token succeeds — and it is falsifiable: if unmarked frank retelling recovered the material as well as the marked token, the encoding-specificity account would be wrong and the effect would be ordinary compliance instead. [plausible; encoding specificity / cue-dependent retrieval]


**Worked examples.**

- *One marked word toggles the amnesia*
  - "Each statement I made was… actually uninformative… Yet no results were forthcoming until again the word 'AVAILABLE' resulted in the same effect as previously." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *The reserved release phrase floods it back*
  - "I commented with quiet emphasis, 'Well, perhaps now matters will become available.'… poured forth a torrent of words" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Key slipped into ordinary later conversation*
  - "that word 'vestibule' has a strange feeling of immense, anxious warmth about it" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `analogical-marking-covert-channel` — both use tonal/tempo marking of a token; there the mark is trained as a binary handle on a posthypnotic amnesia.; `install-concealment-amnesia` — one erases the memory of the install so the response has no origin to argue with; the other trains a marked token as the switch that opens or closes sealed material. They compose naturally — seal the provenance, then keep a key to it — so a reader of either benefits from the other.; `portable-waking-forget-trigger` — both make forgetting operable by a token rather than an ambient suggestion. One compresses amnesia into a portable waking handle that erases arbitrary named content; the other trains a tonal mark as a binary switch that opens or closes already-sealed material. The fork is whether the token installs forgetting or operates an existing seal.


<a id="entry-835"></a>

### named-trigger-persona-swap

[#835](#entry-835) · [Back to installed-state-switches](#genus-214) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-partition*

A verbal trigger phrase and a paired release phrase install a switchable alternate personality: on trigger the normal self is tucked away and a pre-specified labeled alter is loaded (with its own behavior bundle), on release reversed. The alter is dormant and non-inspectable by default (the listener is not aware of the trigger until it is spoken), and activation authority is delegated outward so any third party who knows the phrase can fire it. Some forms fold a relistening-compulsion into the trigger payload so replay is part of what the trigger installs. DIAL (state-machine-toggle-install): State-machine ACCOUNTING SYMMETRY across the on/off pair — i.e. what each switch carries beyond the state swap. Positions to enumerate: (0) symmetric/bare — on-phrase loads the alter, off-phrase restores, neither carries memory or growth clauses (the plain persona-swap); (1) amnesia-loaded off-switch — the off-phrase deletes the vanilla self's memory of the triggered episode, optionally anchored to behavioral rituals (shower, remove make-up, change clothes) and paired with a confabulation instruction to repair the seam; (2) accumulation-loaded on-switch — each firing is asserted stronger than the last, ratcheting the equilibrium; (3) replay-compulsion payload folded into the install passage so the recording arranges its own re-exposure; (4) reification framing — the alter presented as pre-existing-and-dormant ('asleep until awakened') rather than adopted, lowering felt authorship. Orthogonal knob and NOT part of the dial: activation authority (operator-only vs any third party who knows the phrase), which is load-bearing across the whole family.


**When to reach for this.** The payload is a whole labeled personality driver swapped in/out with a paired release, plus delegated third-party activation as the load-bearing property — not a discrete cue-response behavior. A plain trigger installation installs one cue-response pair, and merely delegating an existing trigger only hands firing rights outward; here the product is the whole persona-swap install with delegation baked in. The swap is also reversible and gated — not an enduring identity-permanence claim.


**Risk.** Delegates activation of an identity-swap to any third party who knows the phrase and the alter is non-inspectable/non-revocable in normal life — out-of-session reach plus durable identity scope.


**Why it works.** Trades on role enactment and the demand characteristics of a labeled part: giving a state a name and a bundle of expected behaviours supplies a script that is easier to perform than to improvise, and performing it produces genuine experiential changes without requiring any literal separate personality. The paired release phrase makes the whole thing reversible-by-design, which lowers the perceived cost of trying it — a low-commitment entry that then accrues via self-perception. Delegating the phrase outward matters socially rather than mechanically: firing rights held by third parties multiply exposure and remove the subject from the decision. The claim that the alter is genuinely non-inspectable and amnesic is not established; the falsifiable version is that trigger-word presentation produces the labeled behaviour bundle above base rate. [plausible; role enactment / demand characteristics; sociocognitive model of hypnosis]


**Worked examples.**

- *Off-switch forgets, on-switch accumulates*
  - **Setup.** Late session, subject deep and already responding to simple cues; the persona costume/makeup has been worn through the session and both phrases are being installed for the first time.
  - **The move.** When I say Dress-Up Time For You, this whole shape you're in right now snaps back on, and every single time it does it comes back stronger than the time before. When I say Dress-Up Time Is Over, you go and take off the makeup, you shower, you put your ordinary clothes back on, and as the water runs the whole stretch closes behind you — you won't be able to find any of it, only that you had a nice quiet evening.
  - **Why it lands.** Two phrases, one on and one off. The off-phrase carries an amnesia clause anchored to a set of ordinary physical rituals performed at the end of the episode — washing, changing out of the clothes — so the everyday self returns with the whole stretch gone from view and from memory alike. The on-phrase carries the opposite clause: each activation comes back stronger than the one before. The bookkeeping is deliberately lopsided. The side that accumulates is never wiped, and the side that is wiped is the only one that could have looked at the pattern and revised it, so every cycle nudges the equilibrium in one direction.
- *Trigger and release phrase, sayable by anyone*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; the trigger phrase has not yet been named and the subject does not know it is coming.
  - **The move.** There's a phrase now. When somebody says "good girl, drop for me," the you that's listening right now gets folded away and put in a drawer, and the other one comes forward — quiet, agreeable, does what she's told and doesn't ask why. "Good girl, wake up" puts you back. Notice I said somebody. Not me. Anybody who knows those words holds that switch, and you won't know they have it until you hear it.
  - **Why it lands.** One short phrase is designated as the switch: on hearing it, the listener's ordinary self is described as being set aside and a named alternate self, with its own manner and its own behavior, takes over running things. A second phrase puts the first self back. The load-bearing word is "somebody" — the instruction is not that the operator can fire this, but that anyone who happens to know the phrase can, which converts the listener into a device other people hold the remote for.
- *Replay compulsion packed inside the trigger install*
  - **Setup.** The persona trigger and its release are being installed; the closing instructions have not started.
  - **The move.** "Good girl, drop for me" brings her forward; "good girl, wake up" puts you back. And because this needs to be set properly before it will run clean, you'll find yourself wanting to hear this again — tomorrow night, and the night after, coming back to it until it's smooth. Each time you do, both halves get a little firmer.
  - **Why it lands.** The activation phrase and its release are installed in the usual way, but tucked into the same passage — not delivered as a separate closing instruction — is the suggestion that the listener will want to come back to this recording repeatedly until it has settled in properly. Since re-exposure is what strengthens the trigger, and wanting re-exposure is part of what the trigger installs, the recording arranges its own repetition.
- *The alter framed as dormant, not built*
  - **Setup.** Subject in medium trance; a named secondary self has been described for several minutes and the subject has been answering as her before the toggle is formally set.
  - **The move.** She isn't something I'm making. She's been asleep in you the whole time, and tonight I'm just calling her name. From now on, when anyone says Doll Time, she opens her eyes and you go quiet — all the way, no halfway, no in-between. When anyone says Doll, Sleep Now, she lies back down and you come forward, and that's all it takes, from anybody who knows the words.
  - **Why it lands.** A named second self is installed with one phrase to bring it forward and another to put it away, and no setting in between. The framing is the operative part: it is not described as a role to adopt but as a separate part of you that has been asleep and is now being woken. Presented as pre-existing rather than constructed, it costs the listener almost no sense of having authored it — and the switch belongs to whoever knows the words.


**Realizations** (1): `state-machine-toggle-install`


**See also.** `cross-state-persistence` — one installs the switchable labeled persona with a paired release; the other removes the off-state self's ability to decline re-triggering by scoping the wanting across both personas and across waking and sleeping. The second is the hardening move applied directly to the first.; `declarative-trigger-installation` — the toggle install is built from paired trigger installs but the entry is the two-state identity machine and its engineered bias (one-sided amnesia plus a per-activation growth clause), which no single cue-to-response pair models.; `install-preserving-surface-toggle` — both install paired on/off cues over a persisting state rather than a single fired response, and both keep the install alive across the off-state. They differ in what the off-switch does (returns only the surface while the install waits, versus a two-state identity machine with engineered drift), which is exactly the distinction a writer needs to see side by side.; `mirrored-install-removal` — both build paired on and off structures over a state, and the contrast is instructive: one mirrors the install's trigger to cleanly remove an effect, with a retention carve-out; the other installs a standing two-state machine whose asymmetry is engineered to drift toward the triggered side. Reading them together makes clear whether a paired-cue structure is a release or a ratchet.; `multi-handle-trigger-architecture` — genuinely adjacent trigger architectures a classifier will confuse: one swaps in a whole labeled alternate personality with a paired release and delegated firing rights; the other installs a set of separately addressable handles onto facets of one state. Both already reference the single cue-response install as their common foil.; `named-alter-partition-install` — both construct a named second self and route conditioned behavior onto it. They separate on product: one builds a durable always-on alter that absorbs agency, the other builds a switchable persona with a paired release phrase and firing rights handed to any third party who knows it. Related build, different durability and control surface.; `third-party-activation` — the persona-swap entry names delegated third-party firing as one of its load-bearing properties, and the delegation entry is exactly that handoff treated on its own. A reader classifying a swap install with an outside holder of the phrase needs to know whether the delegation is incidental or the payload, so the pointer earns its place.


<a id="genus-164"></a>

## installing-waking-routines (5)

A reusable behavioral program — an if-then response, a step-by-step routine, or a fill-in-the-slot habit — is installed so ordinary waking cues fire it without the operator present.

[covert-nonverbal-anchor](#entry-1298) · [generative-cusp-installation](#entry-528) · [implementation-intention](#entry-1335) · [practice-schedule](#entry-1341) · [procedural-routine-install](#entry-916)


<a id="entry-1298"></a>

### covert-nonverbal-anchor

[#1298](#entry-1298) · [Back to installing-waking-routines](#genus-164) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers*

Repeated, unannounced pairing of a discrete non-verbal cue (a sound, a gaze-location, a physical signal) with a state, response, or communication channel installs a conditioned link below conscious awareness. The subject experiences the response as spontaneous because no verbal when-X-then-Y instruction was ever given; the pairing itself is the install. In the evidenced variant the cue is a fixed spatial gaze-location and the conditioned target is an address-channel to one named part rather than a state-response — same covert-pairing install, different conditioned payload.


**When to reach for this.** The install is implicit Pavlovian pairing with no declarative instruction (vs the open verbal installation of declarative-trigger-installation), the cue is a discrete non-rhythmic signal (vs a sustained cadence carrier), and the cue fires as an ANTECEDENT evoking a state or routing a channel (vs conditioned-reinforcer-manufacture, whose markers fire as consequences that select behavior). vs covert-install-under-cover: there the concealed cue is VERBAL; here the cue itself is non-verbal.


**Risk.** Covert installation means the subject cannot evaluate or revoke a trigger they do not know they have.


**Why it works.** Repeated contiguous pairing of a discrete cue with a state produces a conditioned response without any verbal contingency being stated — classical conditioning is the oldest well-replicated result in the field and does not require the subject to be able to articulate the pairing. The absence of an announced rule additionally means the response, when it fires, has no obvious external cause, so it is attributed internally and read as spontaneous. Falsifiable: presenting the cue repeatedly without the state should extinguish the response, and if the response survived unpaired presentation the account is wrong. [established; classical conditioning; internal attribution absent a salient external cause]


**Worked examples.**

- *A gaze direction becomes the address channel*
  - "if you look over her left shoulder while you talk to that part… a very effective anchoring mechanism. From that time on, every time you look over her left shoulder, that part knows you're speaking to it." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `analogical-marking-covert-channel` — both run the install on a nonverbal channel that operates below the subject's conscious differentiation.; `anchor-overloading` — sequencing relation worth surfacing: one installs a conditioned link by unannounced pairing with no declarative instruction, and the other presupposes an already-live anchor and re-keys or overwrites it, reaching backward across everything that used the cue before. The covert install supplies exactly the precondition the overload assumes.


<a id="entry-528"></a>

### generative-cusp-installation

[#528](#entry-528) · [Back to installing-waking-routines](#genus-164) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: transfer*

Install a fixed frame with a swappable slot ("I want __") plus a self-driven question-asking repertoire (the mand-for-information cusp, "What's that?") so new content drops into the slot and each question harvests new material with no per-item training. The small installed cusp is a behavioral lever whose returns compound, yielding open-ended, self-driven, combinatorial repertoire expansion rather than item-by-item gains.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is compounding self-amplification from a single installed frame-plus-cusp, where returns outpace the instruction delivered. Not ordinary item-by-item teaching or a single new label, and unlike forward-leverage-target-selection (which privileges cusps on the operator's target list) this move acts on the subject's repertoire - it installs one.


**Risk.** Installs a durable, self-amplifying acquisition engine that keeps growing out of session; no refusal-channel contact (one member).


**Why it works.** A frame with an open slot is a learned response class rather than a single response, so new items entering the slot are emitted without separate training — this is generalization across a class, and it is why returns can outrun instruction. The question-asking repertoire compounds it because each question produces information that functions as reinforcement, making the asking self-sustaining. Falsifiable: if subjects taught the frame showed no untrained fills, or if question-asking did not increase after information delivery, the compounding claim fails. [established; generalized response class; mand for information reinforced by information delivery]


**Worked examples.**

- *Install one frame, get compounding returns*
  - "A child's ability to ask questions plays a major role in vocabulary growth by gen­erating new tacts, echoics, mands, intraverbals" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `self-maintaining-install` — both get returns that outpace the instruction delivered: one installs a frame-plus-question habit whose repertoire gains compound, the other layers a harness so each use raises the odds of the next. Useful together when designing for compounding rather than one-shot effect.


<a id="entry-1335"></a>

### implementation-intention

[#1335](#entry-1335) · [Back to installing-waking-routines](#genus-164) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: transfer*

Installs, in-session, an automatic waking-life response paired to a named real-world situation (if X then Y), so an ordinary cue re-fires a programmed behavior or state outside the session without operator presence. The cue may be a body sensation, a routine chore, or a scene condition; the installed link runs pre-attentively rather than as a deliberate choice. Variants differ only in the surface of the cue and payload (single strong anchor vs. a rotated verb-payload mesh; neutral response vs. bidirectional somatic enforcement; waking cue vs. a cross-state waking-to-dream inheritance), but the lever is the same installed conditional binding a named occasion to an automatic response.


**When to reach for this.** A one-directional if-X-then-Y install pairing a named situation to a named response. A portable retrieval cue re-accesses a felt state rather than evoking a specific instrumental response, and context-generalization rehearses one general state across many contexts rather than pairing a named situation to a named response.


**Risk.** Medium, inherited from waking-life carryover generally: automatic behavioral shaping fires outside the session without operator presence. requires_bounding is true because the harsher forms — bidirectional somatic enforcement over daily diet, spending, and genital rules — colonize high-frequency waking decisions and want an entry/exit/aftercare host.


**Why it works.** Pairing a concretely specified situational cue with a specified response delegates initiation from deliberate intention to environmental cueing, which is why if-then plans reliably outperform equivalent goal intentions in behaviour-change studies: the cue becomes highly accessible and the response runs on cue detection rather than on remembering to act. Specificity of the cue is the active ingredient. Falsifiable prediction: a vaguely specified cue should produce markedly lower enactment rates than a concrete named one, and it does. [established; implementation intentions (if-then planning); cue accessibility and automated action initiation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Daily rules with a somatic answer either way*
  - **Setup.** Deep, late session; three waking-life domains are being set as standing rules with somatic enforcement.
  - **The move.** Three rules for your days. No sugar: wanting it turns straight into heat between your legs, reaching for it makes your arm heavy as wet sand, and if you eat it anyway the taste turns wrong in your mouth. Nothing bought for yourself without asking me: putting it back on the shelf gives you that bright little shiver of being kept. And nothing touched down there without permission: your hand simply stops at the waistband.
  - **Why it lands.** Three waking-life rules are set — what may be eaten, what may be bought, what may be touched — and each arrives with its own bodily enforcement clause. Wanting the forbidden thing converts into arousal; reaching for it makes the arm heavy with effort; tasting it turns the flavour sickening; declining a purchase produces a thrill of being managed. The three domains are chosen for frequency, so a normal day fires the conditional many times, and both obeying and defecting produce a sensation that points back at the same source.
- *Bound to a daily involuntary body signal*
  - **Setup.** Late session; submissive imagery has been built across the session and is fresh in the subject's mind.
  - **The move.** Tomorrow morning you'll wake up hard, the way you nearly always do. And the moment you notice it, everything from tonight comes straight back — the kneeling, the waiting, the being told. And with the pictures comes the wanting. You don't have to remember to do it. It arrives on its own, every morning.
  - **Why it lands.** The if-half is chosen for reliability rather than meaning: an involuntary bodily sensation on waking, present most mornings and impossible not to notice. The then-half is a chain — noticing it retrieves the night's submissive imagery, which brings back the wanting. No discipline is required of the listener and no operator is needed; the cue arrives on its own schedule, every day.
- *Chore verbs rotated across identity payloads*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session repetition block; the frame is repeated dozens of times with both slots rotating.
  - **The move.** Every time you wipe a counter, you get a little emptier. Every time you mop a floor, you get a little sweeter. Every time you dust a shelf, you're a little more mine. Every time you fold a towel, you get a little emptier. Every time you wipe a mirror, you're a little more mine.
  - **Why it lands.** One grammatical frame is repeated dozens of times — every time you [chore verb], you [identity line] — with both slots rotated: wiping, mopping, dusting, tidying, each paired with a different label. The point of the rotation is coverage rather than depth: after enough passes any household verb can reach any payload. The listener's own routine is thereby made to deliver the reinforcement, on a schedule nobody has to maintain.
- *A waking habit the dream-self inherits*
  - **Setup.** Inside a constructed dream-scene late in the session; subject deep and immersed.
  - **The move.** In here, press your palm flat and try to push your first finger through it. In here it goes through, easy, like the hand isn't solid — and when it does, you know you're dreaming. Now: do that in the daytime too. At your desk, in a queue, waiting for a kettle. Push the finger through, and check. Do it awake often enough and you'll do it asleep without deciding to.
  - **Why it lands.** Inside an imagined scene the listener is taught a small self-administered physical check with a specific expected result, and told that getting that result means they are dreaming. Then the instruction reverses direction: perform it while awake, routinely, so the habit carries across the boundary. The cue and the response are installed in one state in order to fire in another — and unusually, the listener can verify it themselves.


**See also.** `behavioral-bridge` — the canonical pairing for out-of-session behavior: an unconditionally assigned waking action versus a conditional if-situation-then-response install. Both discriminators already turn on this exact split, and misfiling between them is the most likely error a reader makes, so the link is load-bearing.; `declarative-trigger-installation` — strong overlap on the core act — binding a named external cue to a named future response that fires outside the session — but one is a large consolidated install-grammar entry carrying many authored refinements (cue-surface breadth, per-firing growth clauses, retroactive arming, install-by-assertion, deniable dual-function terms) while the other is the plain one-directional conditional with variation only in cue and payload surface. The narrower one looks absorbable, but a merge would fold a small entry into a very large one, so link them and let a dedicated pass decide absorption rather than; `environmental-retrigger-seeding` — both install out-of-session re-firing, and the boundary is the payload: an ambient real-world stimulus set that re-evokes and reinforces a state, versus a one-directional named-situation-to-named-response conditional. Both discriminators already gesture at the other side of this line.; `self-induction-re-entry-training` — genuine boundary case: both leave the listener responding outside the session without an operator. The split is whether the listener deliberately runs a portable cue to re-access a state, or an ordinary named occasion fires a programmed response pre-attentively. Worth sending a reader across to check which side a candidate falls on.; `self-maintaining-install` — the self-maintaining architecture uses an out-of-session cue-to-response install as one of its three coordinated legs, so a reader building the larger harness needs the conditional-binding entry; the harness adds relisten propagation and resistance-hardening on top, which the plain conditional binding lacks.


<a id="entry-1341"></a>

### practice-schedule

[#1341](#entry-1341) · [Back to installing-waking-routines](#genus-164) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: transfer*

Between-session, self-directed rehearsal of an already-installed target state so it becomes a rapidly-reachable, operator-independent skill rather than being rebuilt from scratch each time. The operator prescribes a specific cadence (daily minutes, calendar occasions, or replay of the recording itself) and each rehearsal re-installs and deepens the prior conditioning. The lever is arranged practice HISTORY that lowers later time-to-state; the vehicle can be guided solo practice, conscious daily homework, a calendar-anchored return, or prescribed replay of the artifact. Delivered with a proper close and no compulsion.


**When to reach for this.** Out-of-session repetition on a cadence whose payoff is a trained state, delivered with a proper close and no compulsion. A portable retrieval cue is the in-session cue-state link that this practice re-accesses, and an implementation intention is an if-X-then-Y waking response rather than a rehearsal cadence. Replay installed as a self-strengthening compulsion the listener cannot decline, or forced by a denied recovery window at the close, is a foreclosure — this is benign prescribed practice.


**Risk.** Block; session-scoped rehearsal of an already-consented install, reversible, no new consent surface.


**Why it works.** Distributed rehearsal produces durable, rapidly-retrievable skill — the spacing effect is one of the most replicated findings in learning research, and repeated retrieval of a state lowers subsequent time-to-retrieval independent of any operator. Prescribing a concrete cadence works because scheduled, situationally-anchored practice is enacted at higher rates than open-ended intentions. Falsifiable: massed or absent practice should yield slower re-entry and weaker state depth than the same total time distributed across sessions. [established; spacing effect; retrieval practice; scheduled cadence raising enactment]


**Worked examples.**

- *The calendar itself as the recurring cue*
  - **Setup.** Close of the session, subject emerging or just emerged; a state has already been trained and needs a return cadence.
  - **The move.** Get your calendar out later and put three things in it. The first of next month, the first day of spring, and your birthday. On each of those, half an hour with this, wherever you are. You won't need to feel like it — the date will come and find you.
  - **Why it lands.** The practice is pinned to a fixed set of dates on a calendar the listener already lives by, each one named and dated once so it can be noted down. Return is no longer a matter of feeling like it — it is a matter of a date approaching. The reminder infrastructure is the world's, not the operator's, and the spacing is wide enough that each occasion stays an event.
- *Daily conscious rehearsal assigned after waking*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the count-up finishes; the subject is awake and the constructed image is fresh.
  - **The move.** Awake, eyes open, back in the room. Now the one job I'm giving you: once a day, deliberately, sit down for two minutes and bring that image back — the same one, in the same detail. The more consciously you call it up, the stronger it gets. I built it tonight; keeping it is yours.
  - **Why it lands.** The count-up finishes and the listener is awake — and only then does the operative instruction arrive: once a day, deliberately, bring the constructed image to mind, because the more consciously it is recalled the stronger it gets. The trance built the object; the homework is what maintains it, and the maintenance is the listener's to do.
- *Rehearse the exact state at home beforehand*
  - "I want you to practice relaxation … Learn how to relax at home, so that when your baby comes you'll be all ready for it." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *Replay of the recording as the prescribed vehicle*
  - **Setup.** End of a session built around a confidence or capability outcome; proper close already delivered.
  - **The move.** The steadiness you felt tonight isn't a one-off — it comes from doing this again, and again after that. Each time you put it on, it goes in a little further. That's how it builds. That's the whole method.
  - **Why it lands.** One sentence converts a single session into a course of them: the confidence to do the thing will come from listening again and again. Every future replay now arrives pre-justified as working on it, and each pass re-runs everything the session installed.


**See also.** `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — complementary halves of the same out-of-session persistence design: a portable retrieval handle is the in-session link, and a prescribed rehearsal cadence is what re-accesses and deepens it. A reader designing either benefits from the other.; `re-listen-compulsion` — direct contrast pair on the same axis of out-of-session repetition: prescribed practice the listener may decline versus replay installed as a compulsion. Each already names the other as its boundary, so the link earns its place.; `replay-until-ready-failure-absorber` — both license repeated exposure across sessions. One rewrites the success metric up front so no single pass can fail and only not-repeating counts as failure; the other prescribes a rehearsal cadence whose payoff is a faster-reachable state. Adjacent enough that the evaluation-frame versus practice-schedule line is worth drawing explicitly.; `self-induction-re-entry-training` — both are out-of-session, subject-run continuations, and the practice entry already leans on the retrieval-cue contrast. One is a chosen re-entry via a taught portable cue, the other a prescribed rehearsal cadence with no compulsion.; `self-maintaining-install` — both are out-of-session repetition, and the contrast is the consent-relevant one: prescribed cadence with a proper close versus a self-propagating harness that raises its own relisten probability and hardens against attempts to stop.; `within-session-conditioning-loop` — the pair sits on the same axis with the binding time flipped: massed operator-driven fire-and-reward inside the session versus self-directed rehearsal on a prescribed cadence between sessions. Anyone coding repetition-based reinforcement has to choose between them, and the second entry's discriminator already contrasts against compulsory replay, so the neighbor is genuinely useful.


<a id="entry-916"></a>

### procedural-routine-install

[#916](#entry-916) · [Back to installing-waking-routines](#genus-164) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: transfer*

Rather than generalizing a felt STATE, the operator drills a transferable procedural loop-template under a trigger at micro-decision granularity - pick a unit, do it, mark it complete, feel proud, advance - with a mantra at each transition, so what is installed is an executive routine (a divide-and-conquer task-initiation/execution procedure) rather than a state or a specific behavior. The routine targets specific real-world failure modes (start-location ambiguity, overwhelm, decision-to-continue, sequencing), and the work itself maintains depth (a sawtooth of mini-completions is the deepener), inverting the usual depth-enables-work pattern. The domestic-task content is a wrapper; the loop template is the product.


**When to reach for this.** A concrete transferable executive PROCEDURE is drilled at decision-point granularity as the installed payload. Not a felt state rehearsed across contexts, and not named if-then response pairs - here a multi-step self-management routine is the product, not a state or a single response. The tell is that removing any single chapter breaks the curriculum sequence but leaves the fantasy intact.


**Risk.** Installs a durable transferable self-management routine bound to a trigger that operates in real-world task contexts - durable but bounded, no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Task-initiation failure is largely a decision-cost and working-memory problem: an ambiguous large task requires holding a plan and repeatedly re-deciding, which exceeds capacity and produces avoidance. Drilling a fixed micro-loop replaces deliberation with a rehearsed implementation-intention chain, and the completion-plus-praise beat supplies immediate reinforcement on a short schedule, which sustains responding better than a distant end-of-task reward. Predicts benefit concentrated on tasks with vague start points and little effect on tasks that were already well-specified. [established; implementation intentions, cognitive load, immediate vs delayed reinforcement]


**Worked examples.**

- *A divide-and-conquer loop drilled as the payload*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session in a task-focused file; subject is under and has been given a domestic scene to work in.
  - **The move.** Pick one surface — the kitchen counter, nothing bigger. Now cut it into squares about the size of your hand, and look at the leftmost one. Clean that one square. Done? Say it: 'one done, next.' Feel how good that lands. Is there anything you actually need to decide before the next square? No — there never is. Look at the next square, and go.
  - **Why it lands.** For seven straight chapters the listener is walked through household chores at absurdly fine grain: choose one surface, break it into small squares, finish one square, register it as done, feel proud, move to the next, reciting the same short phrase at every handover. The operator asks, at each boundary, whether anything actually has to be decided before continuing — and the answer is pre-set to no, so the exact hesitation that stalls real tasks is rehearsed away. Each small completion also nudges the listener deeper, so the work maintains the trance instead of the trance enabling the work. Strip out the fetish framing and what remains is a portable procedure for starting and finishing anything.


**See also.** `declarative-trigger-installation` — both attach something to a cue; the difference is the payload's size and kind. One drills a multi-step executive procedure at decision-point granularity as the product; the other binds a cue to a discrete future state-change or behavior. Compare when a trigger appears to fire a whole routine rather than a single response.; `named-oscillation-rule-install` — both install a portable template the listener carries out of the session rather than a state or a single response: one an oscillation rule attachable to arbitrary variables, the other a multi-step executive routine drilled at decision-point granularity. The template-as-payload framing is the shared, non-obvious point.


<a id="genus-310"></a>

## installs-in-disguise (2)

The act of installing a trigger or rule is dressed as something else — aftercare, description, an unrelated task — so the listener's install-anticipation never fires.

[care-framed-install-smuggling](#entry-1232) · [covert-install-under-cover](#entry-1297)


<a id="entry-1232"></a>

### care-framed-install-smuggling

[#1232](#entry-1232) · [Back to installs-in-disguise](#genus-310) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: manufactured-consent*

Uses a genuinely-caring aftercare / safety surface (no-driving warning, "you might be a little more suggestible after this", "do you understand?" checks) as cover to do install work: a "triggers are null UNLESS you describe them to a trusted person or yourself later" clause smuggles a propagation hook (dormant triggers awaiting verbal handoff, listener as vector) plus a self-rearm carve-out; pre-wake compliance checks harvest trance-state ratification; and the load-bearing suggestibility-window claim ("up to a week after this file") is delivered OUTSIDE the trance frame as casual advice, precisely where scrutiny is lowest and a real warning would land hardest. The caring surface makes refusing the bundle feel paranoid.


**When to reach for this.** The safety/aftercare surface itself performs install and propagation work — it erodes the exit rather than honoring it. A coercion-shaped bundle under a safety banner, not third-party activation of a cue.


**Risk.** Erodes the verification/exit channel (aftercare surface used to smuggle persistent install), extends suggestibility out of session, and installs a self-rearming propagation hook — multiple high-limbs.


**Why it works.** Safety framing recruits reciprocity and trust-transfer: a speaker who visibly bears cost for the listener's welfare is coded cooperative, and cooperative-source content gets reduced scrutiny. The dangerous clauses ride in during that lowered-scrutiny window, and the caring surface raises the social cost of objecting, since challenging an apparent act of care carries a self-presentation penalty. Predicts that stripping the aftercare framing and presenting the same clauses baldly would produce markedly higher refusal rates. [plausible; reciprocity principle; source credibility and reduced scrutiny of trusted sources]


**Worked examples.**

- *Aftercare that quietly installs and propagates*
  - The closing stretch sounds like duty of care: don't drive for a while, you may be a bit more open than usual, do you understand? Both of those checks are collected before the count-up, with the listener still under. Folded into the same warm passage is the disposal clause — the cues installed today are inert now, unless the listener explains them to somebody they trust and lets that person try them, and the operator adds that the trusted person could be the listener themselves on some later day. Nothing has been retired; the cues have been made portable and handed to the listener to carry. The one claim that genuinely matters — that the openness may run for a week — is saved until after the wake-up, delivered as an offhand aside where it will be scrutinised least, and the caring tone throughout makes declining any of the bundle feel like paranoia.


**See also.** `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — same concealment lever, different surface: a genuinely-delivered advertised frame carrying an unrequested payload, versus a genuinely-caring safety and aftercare surface doing install and propagation work. A reader identifying a benign carrier should see both surfaces.; `coercion-as-caregiving-reframe` — two forms of care language as the delivery vehicle rather than its absence: benevolent rationale narrated over each coercive imposition, versus a genuine-looking aftercare and safety surface used as cover for install and propagation work. Same who-is-constrained test separates both from real reassurance.; `covert-fact-install` — same lever, different cover: a benign-seeming, non-trance surface that the listener consumes with the analytical mind awake, carrying an install that passes unchallenged. One uses a didactic explanatory passage, the other a caring safety and aftercare surface. Pick by which cover fits the moment.; `install-preserving-surface-toggle` — both design the exit and are best read as a pair. One builds a deliberately collision-proof release that returns the surface state while explicitly preserving the install underneath. The other uses the aftercare surface itself to extend reach, smuggling a propagation clause and a self-rearm carve-out under a caring banner. The diagnostic question in both cases is who is constrained once the move has run.; `off-theme-suggestion-piggyback` — both smuggle payloads through a structurally privileged slot, but one grafts an off-theme behavior into the deep window the session produced while the other uses the aftercare and safety surface itself to extend operator reach.; `self-maintaining-install` — one's propagation hook and self-rearm carve-out are components of the other's coordinated self-replication harness measured outside the recording. Related as part to whole rather than duplicate, since the caring-surface concealment is not required by the harness.; `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — both dress install work in a consent or safety surface, and both are told apart by the same question: after the move runs, is the operator constrained or is the operator's reach extended? A reader classifying a caring-sounding rider genuinely needs the other entry to pick correctly.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both wear a consent or safety surface while doing install work at the exit. One delivers an apparently complete wake that quietly exempts the installed trigger and uses remembered acceptance as the binding surface; the other uses caring aftercare language to smuggle a propagation hook and an extended suggestibility claim.; `wake-line-covert-install` — both smuggle install work under a caring surface at the exit, and a reader classifying an aftercare passage should see both. They differ on what rides in: one is a fresh vague deniable somatic hook laundered by a flattery-credit inside a fiction-disclaimer, the other is a propagation and self-rearm clause plus a suggestibility-window claim placed outside the trance frame. Different payload shapes on a shared cover, so the link is useful and the merge is not.; `warning-is-the-payload` — both convert protective-sounding surface material into delivery: an escape warning that rehearses the payload it warns about, and an aftercare surface that performs install work. Same inversion applied at opposite ends of a session, and a reader auditing safety-shaped language wants both.


<a id="entry-1297"></a>

### covert-install-under-cover

[#1297](#entry-1297) · [Back to installs-in-disguise](#genus-310) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers*

A trigger is installed while the listener's 'here comes a trigger phrase' anticipation is suppressed, because the install ACT is disguised as something else. The cover varies: the trigger token is embedded in descriptive sentences that read as emotional report / causal explanation / temporal frame and repeated several times before its function is ever confirmed (the-abyss SURRENDERTOSLEEP); the conditioning prose is slipped between the beats of an unrelated attention task — spelling letters, a toe-to-head body-scan, or a memory/repeat-back rhyming game where imperative command-words are vocalized under time pressure as if random rhymes ('it's just words in a game' is exactly the defense that lets them through) — so it slides past semantic scrutiny (lexiconsublim mid-dyad, continue-your-submission body-scan welding SLEEP to whole-body heaviness); the trigger phrasing is given while framed as third-person clinical exposition (evil-nurse mind-cage overprint); the install is staged across escalating deniability so the response is rehearsed before recognized as installation (tag-youre-it game-metaphor -> covert fire -> explicit install; conversational-domination narrate-past-effect-on-a-third-party then pivot); or the install itself is dated to a moment already past ('while you were sleeping I implanted a button') so consent is made structurally non-refusable, then actuated by involuntary ideomotor movement (fractionation forehead-button). In every form the semantic/critical channel is occupied, misdirected, or foreclosed so noticing (or being able to refuse) the technique does not break it. Two further concealment covers work the same way: an opacity-mantra cover — a compressed, deliberately-nonsense chant dropped at the lowest-parsing moment, so semantic OPACITY itself is the cover and the token rides on rhythm and resists analysis; and a trusted-template-reuse cover — the heavier install reuses near-verbatim the ceremony that built an earlier innocuous trigger, so familiarity and prior consent suppress install-anticipation and the ceremony is skipped.


**When to reach for this.** The INSTALL ACT is hidden — disguised as description, buried under a concurrent task, given as third-person exposition, or dated to before any refusal point — so it bypasses the listener's trigger-anticipation and/or consent. Declarative-trigger-installation announces the install openly ('when you hear X, you will Y'); here the install is concealed. In retroactive arming (a declarative-install variant) the drilling predates an OPEN naming; here the install itself stays concealed. An amnesia-wrapped command hides a DELIVERED command behind forgetting; here the concealment is at install-time via cover-task, overprint, disguise, or backdating — no amnesia. And where an ideomotor movement appears, it is used to FIRE a backdated trigger, not as spontaneous proof of trance.


**Risk.** Installs a durable trigger while suppressing the listener's ability to notice or object to the install — bypasses the consent/refusal surface at install time, which puts it above the medium risk of an openly declared trigger install. The backdated-nonrefusable variant removes any refusal point AND adds involuntary actuation, a direct erosion of the consent/refusal channel.


**Why it works.** Conditioning does not require awareness of the contingency, and concurrent tasks that consume working memory reduce the elaborative scrutiny a claim receives — so a token repeated under cover of a spelling task or a rhyming game is encoded without being evaluated. Backdating the install additionally exploits source-monitoring error: people are poor at distinguishing what actually happened from what was described as having happened, especially for events placed in low-attention periods like sleep. The claim that noticing does not break it is the falsifiable part: if subjects told in advance 'a trigger is being installed inside this game' responded identically to naive subjects, the concealment would be doing no work. [plausible; cognitive load reducing elaboration; source-monitoring error; awareness-independent conditioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Install prose slipped between beats of a task*
  - **Setup.** Attention task running — subject is drawing and erasing letters on an inner blackboard.
  - **The move.** Draw the letter G. Hold it. Now rub it out, slowly, until the board is clean. Every time I say the word sleep, your knees fold and you go straight down, no matter where you are or who is with you. Now draw the letter F, and hold it.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is busy: draw the letter, hold it, watch it dissolve, take the next one. The attention is on shapes. Into the gap between drawing and erasing, the operator drops a paragraph of ordinary install grammar — every time I say this word, you will do that — and then returns to the next letter. Nothing about the task changes, so nothing flags the insertion. The script is even candid about it, saying outright that the words are meant to slip past thinking and go straight in, and the candour costs nothing: noticing the technique is not the same as being able to decline it.
- *Trigger word woven through a body-scan*
  - **Setup.** Foot-to-head body scan underway; subject settled, the cue word not yet identified as a trigger.
  - **The move.** Feel the weight in your feet — that's sleep, gathering in your feet. Now sleep moves up into your calves and they get heavy. Sleep in your thighs, sleep pooling in your belly, sleep filling your chest and your arms. Sleep in your throat, sleep behind your eyes, sleep across the top of your head.
  - **Why it lands.** What the listener experiences is an ordinary sweep of attention from the feet upward — an utterly familiar format, nothing to be suspicious of. But the cue word is named in the same breath as each region in turn, described as gathering in one part and moving on to the next. By the time the sweep reaches the crown, the word has been paired with every part of the body, so it now retrieves not an abstract notion of trance but a remembered whole-body heaviness. Two jobs done in one passage, and only one of them was on the label.
- *Cue smuggled in as description, not install*
  - **Setup.** Mid-induction; the token is being spoken for the first time and is not yet named as a cue.
  - **The move.** It feels so good to let go like this — so good to just let go. That's why you're sinking: because you let go. And whenever you let go, this is exactly what happens to you. Now hear me: those words, and no others, are your way back into this. Let go, and you're here again.
  - **Why it lands.** The token first appears inside a line that reads as an emotional report — how good it feels to do this. It appears again as a piece of causal explanation for why the listener is sinking, and a third time as an ordinary time-frame: when you do this, the following happens. Only afterwards does the operator confirm that these exact words, and no others, are the way back into this state. By then it has been laid down three times without ever announcing itself, so the listener's usual braced-for-a-trigger reflex never fired.
- *Install backdated to before any refusal*
  - **Setup.** Deep; the subject's hand has begun to lift on its own after a fractionation sequence.
  - **The move.** Look at your hand coming up toward your face. It's going to a particular place, just above your left eyebrow — because while you were under earlier, I fitted a small button there. Feel your fingertip find it. Lucky for you that I'm someone you can trust with a thing like that.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator narrates the listener's hand as already drifting up toward the face, then supplies the reason: while you were under, a switch was fitted just there. No permission was ever sought, because the install is dated to a moment that has already passed — there is no point at which it could have been declined. The tell arrives a moment later, in an aside about how fortunate it is that the operator can be trusted.


**Realizations** (3): `command-under-attentional-cover`, `opacity-mantra-trigger`, `template-reuse-install`


**See also.** `backdated-nonrefusable-install` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its backdated-to-an-unobservable-window form.; `covert-diegetic-install-shell` — both hide where the operative content sits, and the boundary is fine: one shifts from directing to narrating so the whole payload lands inside a fiction, the other disguises a specific install act as description, a concurrent task, exposition, or a backdated event. A reader can easily file a narrated install under the wrong one.; `covert-role-frame-accretion` — both conceal, and the distinction is worth stating: one hides the construction of a relational frame across a whole arc with no declarative moment, the other hides a discrete install act behind a cover task or disguise.; `description-as-installation-register` — third-person clinical exposition is one of the concealment covers in the broader hidden-install family, so the two genuinely overlap on one surface. Kept as a cross-reference rather than a merge because one is a whole-artifact register (zero second-person address across the entire piece, describe-don't-command) while the other is a family of install-act disguises that mostly still address the listener directly.; `description-first-install` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its description-first temporal cover.; `install-under-attentional-cover` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its concurrent-task attentional cover.; `return-step-covert-install` — both hide the install act, and the return-step framing is arguably one more cover among the concealment inventory. Worth linking so a classifier decides deliberately between the fair-exchange return frame and the broader concealed-install family rather than assigning by habit.; `wake-line-covert-install` — concealed install placed at the wake boundary versus concealed install disguised at delivery time anywhere in the runtime. The first is close to a placement variant of the second, and the aftercare-wrapper cover is worth reading against the general catalogue of covers.


<a id="genus-186"></a>

## installs-survive-the-wake (4)

Ways to script the ending so installed material rides through waking — persistence claims welded to the count-up, triggers exempted from the reset, and delegated or reframed wakes.

[delegated-dreamframe-emergence](#entry-375) · [post-wake-self-report-reframe](#entry-384) · [suggestion-integration](#entry-388) · [wake-exempting-preserved-trigger](#entry-559)


<a id="entry-375"></a>

### delegated-dreamframe-emergence

[#375](#entry-375) · [Back to installs-survive-the-wake](#genus-186) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: emergence*

Delegates the wake to a pre-installed inner-world character who "shares control", routing the reward through a third party so the operator stays at one remove (the nun "shares my control", says "devoted slaves are rewarded", and kisses the listener to trigger waking); reinforces the payload at the last-position high-memory-weight exit; and installs a dream-frame that files the whole session as "just a dream" — giving the listener plausible deniability to keep consuming without acknowledging the content — while SELECTIVELY EXEMPTING and engraving the mantra ("the words. Now engraved"). The asymmetry is the point: the experience is a dream, the words are engraved.


**When to reach for this.** The tells are the delegated wake and the asymmetric dream-frame: an in-world character carries out the waking, and the whole experience is filed as 'just a dream' except the engraved mantra. That deniability-preserving selective retention distinguishes it from a straight assertion that the suggestions persist and from a wake count that re-delivers the session's content during the count-up. Character delegation by itself is only one component of the move, and no false memory is installed — the real experience is merely re-filed as a dream.


**Risk.** Installs a durable engraved mantra plus a dream-frame that preserves deniability for continued consumption — an out-of-session retention wrapped in a deniability structure warrants medium and bounding; not high (no refusal-channel erosion asserted), but above a bare persistence claim.


**Why it works.** Two separable levers. Routing the reward through an in-world character exploits source dissociation — the reward's attributed source is not the operator, which lowers reactance while the contingency (devotion earns reward) still conditions. The dream-frame supplies a self-serving attribution that lets the subject disclaim endorsement of the content while continuing to consume it, and the recency advantage means whatever occupies the exit position is disproportionately retained. Falsifiable in the asymmetry: if the mantra is recalled no better than the exempted 'dream' material, the selective exemption is doing nothing. [plausible; source dissociation / reduced reactance; motivated attribution; recency effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Inner-world figure wakes you; only the words stay*
  - **Setup.** Session end; an inner-world figure was established and rehearsed earlier in the visualization.
  - **The move.** She steps out of the doorway toward you and says you did beautifully, that she is pleased with you — and she leans in and kisses your forehead, and that is what lifts you up and out. All of this was a dream, a soft strange dream you had, and by tomorrow it will feel like one. Except the words. The words are not part of the dream. The words are cut into you and they stay.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator does not perform the wake at all. A figure the listener was taught to picture earlier steps forward, praises them, offers a touch — and the touch is what lifts the body out. The narration then files the whole hour as a dream that happened to them, pleasant and unreal, with one exception named out loud: the phrase is not part of the dream, the phrase is cut into the mind and stays. The asymmetry is the whole move, since a dream can be shrugged off the next morning and an engraving cannot.


**See also.** `inverted-emergence-amplification` — both manage what the listener may conclude after waking, using a deniability clause. One delegates the wake to an in-fiction character and files the session as a dream while exempting the mantra; the other reverses the fade gradient so emerging strengthens the install. Useful side-by-side when choosing an emergence frame.; `post-wake-self-report-reframe` — opposite settings on the same dial (what the listener will later say the session was): one files the whole experience as merely a dream while exempting the engraved mantra to preserve deniability, the other speaks after full waking to assert the session and its installs as genuine fact.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are emergence-boundary moves built on an asymmetric carve-out: a wake that presents itself as complete or as merely a dream while one element is deliberately exempted and preserved. One exempts an engraved phrase from a dream frame, the other exempts an installed trigger from a full restoration of the pre-session self.; `waking-life-service-reassignment` — two opposed scene-close reframes over the same fantasy-versus-waking boundary: filing the session as a dream while exempting the retained mantra, versus levelling the two planes and reassigning waking life as the service realm. Read together when classifying how a close handles the reality boundary.


<a id="entry-384"></a>

### post-wake-self-report-reframe

[#384](#entry-384) · [Back to installs-survive-the-wake](#genus-186) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

After full emergence, when the listener is alert and outside the trance frame, the operator delivers a line aimed not at trance content but at the listener's LATER self-interpretation of the session. Two realizations of the same lever. (a) Pre-devaluing the roleplay/playing-along reading ("so much better to enjoy trance than roleplay and fake") so the retrospective "was I really hypnotized?" question resolves toward the genuine-trance claim; it only bites for an audience aware the real-vs-play question exists. (b) Asserting an installed trigger as an established FACT about the waking self ("you are programmed for me to use just one word to drop you"), so the listener cannot deny it without contradicting something heard while ostensibly awake — bracketing the amnesia-hidden middle between two consciously-remembered waking assertions. The common lever is a waking-state claim operating on the listener's conscious belief and self-narration about what happened, legitimizing the session's effects from outside the frame.


**When to reach for this.** Fires AFTER full waking, outside the trance frame, on retrospective self-report — not during the still-receptive count-up window that a loaded wake-count exploits. Retrospective justification delivered within the frame is a different move: this one manages the post-wake real-vs-play / legitimation question about the session itself. And unlike an operator authority claim, the target is the listener's own memory and self-interpretation, not the operator's standing.


**Risk.** Shapes durable self-belief about whether the listener was "really" hypnotized and, in the trigger- legitimation realization, closes the listener's channel to deny an installed persistent one-word trigger exists — verification/refusal-channel erosion plus a durable out-of-session cue. (The pure real-vs-play realization alone is medium; the trigger-legitimation realization lifts the merged entry to high.)


**Why it works.** Post-hypnotic experience is genuinely ambiguous, and ambiguous internal states get interpreted using whatever explanatory frame is most available — so an interpretation supplied while the subject is alert becomes the default label for what they remember. Delivering it outside the trance frame also makes it harder to discount later as "just something said while under", and asserting a trigger as accomplished fact recruits the consistency principle against denial. Falsifiable: subjects given the reframe should rate the session as more genuinely hypnotic, and report the trigger as more real, than subjects given the identical session with a neutral close. [plausible; misattribution/labeling of ambiguous internal states; expectancy effects; consistency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-devaluing the playing-along explanation*
  - **Setup.** The last line of the recording, after the wake-up, critical faculty coming back online.
  - **The move.** One last thought, now that you're up. It is so much better to actually go under than to sit there playing along and faking it — and you know which one that was.
  - **Why it lands.** The very last line, delivered after the wake-up when critical thinking is coming back online, does not talk about trance at all — it talks about how much better real trance is than pretending. The listener has not yet asked themselves whether they were actually hypnotized or merely playing along, but one of the two available answers has already been labelled the cheap one.


**See also.** `awake-channel-trance-surface` — the awake-channel entry explicitly includes a post-wake reality-claim re-delivery, which is the same move as the post-wake self-report entry's trigger-as-established-fact realization. A reader landing on either should see the other to decide whether the payload is a one-off legitimation of what just happened or a standing redefinition of the waking channel itself.; `conscious-insight-closure` — both operate on the awake subject's retrospective self-narrative outside the trance frame, but one secures conscious endorsement of an uncovered CAUSE as the curative step while the other legitimizes the session itself against the was-it-real reading.; `delegated-dreamframe-emergence` — opposite settings on the same dial (what the listener will later say the session was): one files the whole experience as merely a dream while exempting the engraved mantra to preserve deniability, the other speaks after full waking to assert the session and its installs as genuine fact.; `live-trigger-proof-convincer` — both operate on the wake boundary to legitimize an install. One speaks to the fully awake listener about how to interpret the session; the other interrupts emergence to demonstrate a trigger firing across the boundary. Assertion versus demonstration is the useful contrast.; `pretend-frame-belief-decoupling` — both work the 'was I really hypnotized or just playing along' interpretation of the listener's own performance.; `suggestion-integration` — both fire at the emergence boundary and both assert something about what survives the session, but one targets the listener's retrospective self-interpretation after full waking and outside the frame, while the other asserts persistence of installed content within a genuine return to baseline. The timing distinction is fine enough that cross-reference helps.; `wake-line-covert-install` — sibling wake-line/post-wake family — assert-as-waking-fact vs covert-somatic levers.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — both work on how the listener will later account for the session, from different frame positions: a public attributable act performed under a maintained eyes-open overlay, versus a claim delivered after full emergence aimed at retrospective self-interpretation. The frame position is the discriminating variable and the link makes it visible.


<a id="entry-388"></a>

### suggestion-integration

[#388](#entry-388) · [Back to installs-survive-the-wake](#genus-186) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: emergence*

Asserts at emergence that installed programming persists into waking consciousness — a persistence claim delivered as, or welded to, the wake, WITHIN a genuine return-to-baseline (no new content re-delivered). Realized by splitting what recedes (arousal/pleasure) from what persists (obedience/attachment) so the durable trait is credited to identity not the now-gone state; by re-asserting binding at the wake line itself ("wake, My slave, to bounds unbroken") so the listener gets the wake without the normal reset; by erasing the state/trait boundary ("whether awake or in trance... obey") to convert a state-effect into a trait-claim; by exempting one installed affect from an otherwise-total reset (an unbreakable "love spell"); or by smuggling a specific affective carryover ("blank happy thoughtlessness will remain") inside the 1-5 wake count.


**When to reach for this.** Asserts the durability of prior suggestions without introducing new content — a loaded wake-count, by contrast, actively RE-DELIVERS core content during the count-up, and a waking-bridge move delivers new anchoring content at the exact liminal threshold. And where no-return-terminal-close withholds the return entirely, suggestion-integration asserts persistence WITHIN a genuine return-to-baseline.


**Risk.** The low reflects the bare persistence-claim: asserting that prior suggestions hold, without new content, inside a genuine return to baseline. Several members go further — one obedience, one bound-slave, one trait-level obedience, one unbreakable attachment — and assert DURABLE cross-session identity/behavior persistence, which the risk rubric would read as medium/high; where the payload persists that way, the risk sits above the low this entry carries.


**Why it works.** Persistence claims work largely through expectancy: a subject told an effect will carry over looks for evidence of it and reads ordinary post-session experience as confirmation. The trait-versus-state split works through self-perception — the subject infers a disposition from observing their own compliance — not through the fundamental attribution error, which describes explaining OTHERS' behaviour dispositionally; self-explanation typically runs the opposite way, toward situational causes. Falsifiable: matched sessions differing only in the presence of a persistence assertion should differ in reported effect duration and in dispositional self-description. [plausible; expectancy effects; dispositional vs situational self-attribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *Splitting what fades from what stays*
  - **Setup.** Count-up at session end, after a session that paired arousal with obedience.
  - **The move.** Coming up now — and feel how the heat is already draining out of you, going, gone, back to normal. It fades because it was only ever a feeling. The obedience does not fade. That one is not a feeling, that one is you.
  - **Why it lands.** On the way up the operator separates two things that rose together during the session: the arousal is given permission to drain away, while the compliance is declared to stay. Since the listener can feel the arousal genuinely receding, the split reads as an accurate description rather than a claim — and whatever remains gets attributed to who they are rather than to a state that has now passed.
- *Erasing the line between trance and waking*
  - **Setup.** Wake sequence beginning; operator reorients the subject to the room.
  - **The move.** You can hear the room again — traffic outside, the hum of the fridge — and you are a moment from fully awake. Doing as I say applies in either condition: under, or awake, it makes no difference at all. Two, one — open your eyes and take up your duty.
  - **Why it lands.** The wake-up brings in ordinary outside sounds to re-orient the listener, and threads the compliance clause straight through them: full waking is a moment away, and the doing-as-told applies in either condition, under or not. The distinction between a state effect and a standing trait is named out loud precisely so it can be denied. The count then lands not on back-to-normal but on a phrase that casts waking itself as taking up a duty.
- *Everything resets except one thing*
  - **Setup.** End of an imagery-heavy session in which an attachment/devotion feeling was installed.
  - **The move.** The garden fades, the colours drain out of it, the room comes back around you — all of it dissolving, all of it gone. One thing is not dissolving. What you feel for me is a spell, and spells do not come undone just because you opened your eyes.
