Keep separate, link strongly.; `identity-labeling` — both make an identity label land as recognition rather than assignment, but one paces a state the subject is already having and names it in the same breath, while the other is a cross-phase ordering move that manufactures the referent through content-free drill or objectifying groundwork before naming it in a separate later phase.; `identity-uncertainty-gap` — both concern preparing the slot before an identity claim lands: one manufactures not-knowing with the operator as sole resolver, the other lays groundwork that pre-slots the listener as a thing before the label arrives. Genuine complementary setup moves for the same later payoff.; `install-then-repossess-agency-theft` — the second is a sharp special case of the first's ordering logic: build an experiential referent, then re-label it. Here the referent is a voluntary behavior deliberately installed so it can be revoked, and the label is a loss rather than a claim about the listener's nature. Reading the general ordering entry alongside clarifies why the theft is one mechanism spanning two phases rather than two installs.; `layered-identity-claim-with-immunity` — both are multi-phase architectures in which earlier steps prepare a later identity claim to land as recognition rather than assertion. One manufactures an experiential referent and only then names it; the other partitions the listener, inserts a lower layer, claims it, and welds on an immunity clause. Closest contact is the pre-slotted-identity form, where groundwork readies the slot before the label drops.; `manufacture-problem-sell-cure-iatrogenic-arc` — both order manufacture before framing, so the operator's frame arrives as a description of what the listener already experienced.; `model-coherence-laundering` — both are cross-phase ordering moves in which something is banked early and cashed later, so the payload lands as recognition rather than assertion. The difference is what gets banked: a manufactured felt experience in one case, an accepted premise or model in the other.; `obedience-demonstration-as-proof` — both split a manufactured referent from the claim made about it, but at different scopes: one is a whole-script ordering where a fabricated experience precedes the label that interprets it, the other is the local validation beat where a single obeyed act is cited straight back as evidence. The demonstration move is the most common thing the ordering schedules, so a reader working on one wants the other.; `pre-staged-apparatus-relabeled-automatic` — both work by producing a real state or arrangement first and naming it later, so the later claim reads as description rather than assertion. Useful cross-reference on the ordering lever; they differ in what is pre-made (a manufactured experiential referent inside trance versus a physical setup consented to while waking).; `presupposed-conditioning-fire` — both let a just-manufactured experience stand as the evidence for a claim delivered afterward, so the claim reads as description rather than assertion.; `rehearsable-impairment-template` — instructive contrast on seam width. One deliberately splits produce and label into separate phases so the later claim reads as recognition of what was just experienced; the other performs and names the deficit in the same breath, collapsing the seam entirely. Reading them together makes the ordering variable visible.; `retroactive-subject-disclosure` — adjacent whole-arc ordering moves that both delay naming until commitment exists. One manufactures an experiential referent and then labels it, so the claim lands as a description of what just happened; the other withholds the script's own declared subject until accumulated self-evidence makes objecting read as the predicted symptom. The boundary is what is withheld: the label for a produced experience, versus the topic itself.; `unifying-frame-overlay` — both are whole-artifact ordering architectures in which the sequencing of groundwork and claim, not the claim's content, does the persuading.; `verdict-before-perception` — temporal inverses on the same axis of ordering experience against interpretation: manufacture the referent then name it, versus land the appraisal before any perception can form.


<a id="entry-448"></a>

### own-acts-surrender-ledger

[#448](#entry-448) · [Back to make-real-then-rename](#genus-183) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: framing*

The operator enumerates or annotates the listener's genuine recent acts — purchasing, browsing, fetching a garment, adopting a posture, obeying setup instructions, sustained engagement, even a single compelled motion — and re-labels each as an instance of the target state (surrender, obedience, vulnerability, love, devotion), openly and contemporaneously. Because the cited proofs are the listener's own real behavior they are hard to repudiate; the perceived baseline shifts from zero to already-surrendered, future resistance now feels like self-contradiction (sunk-cost/complicity), and skeptical mode becomes harder to enter. Registers span retrocausal compliance/surrender ledgers, posture-as-consent ratchets, waking-compliance relabeled as automatic-obedience, a compliance act laundered into "natural" baseline desire, a symptoms-to-diagnosis interpretive frame, a single compelled motion re-narrated as a chain of consensual obedience acts, and a lure-reveal that rebinds self-generated pursuit to the operator.


**When to reach for this.** Requires REAL acts openly annotated as EVIDENCE OF A STATE as they accrue. Not a yes-set — this commits the listener to a causal story about just-performed behavior, not to verbal agreements.


**Risk.** Session-scoped convincer that hardens skeptical entry (one member's fingerprint); no direct refusal-channel deletion.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory: people infer their own attitudes by observing their behaviour, especially when internal cues are weak or ambiguous — which trance deliberately produces. Because the cited acts genuinely happened, the subject cannot dispute the evidence, only the label, and the consistency principle then makes contradicting the inferred state costlier than continuing to act on it. Falsifiable: the technique should fail or backfire when the cited acts have an obvious situational explanation the subject can point to, since a salient external cause blocks the dispositional inference. [established; self-perception theory, consistency principle, discounting by situational attribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *Recent real acts annotated as prior surrender*
  - **Setup.** A few minutes in; the subject has genuinely bought the recording, reacted to the first number, and followed one small setup instruction.
  - **The move.** Three things you already did tonight. There was a flicker when you paid for this — that was you surrendering. You reacted to the very first number I said, before I'd done anything — that was you surrendering. And you moved your hands where I told you without a pause — that was you surrendering. I'm not asking you to start. I'm telling you what you've already been doing.
  - **Why it lands.** Minutes in, the operator lists back three things the listener genuinely just did — the flicker of arousal while buying the recording, the reaction to the very first number spoken, the readiness with which a small setup instruction was obeyed — and labels each one, retroactively, as an episode of the state being installed. None of them were framed that way at the time. The listener now holds an evidence file about themselves that did not exist five minutes earlier, built entirely from their own behavior, which is much harder to dismiss than a claim the operator merely asserted. The state is presented as already true and simply being pointed out.
- *Consumer behavior flattened into acts of power transfer*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the subject has a real history with the material — site visits, free files, a download, a followed instruction.
  - **The move.** Count them with me. You found the site: that was you handing over a piece of power. You listened to the free ones: another piece. You downloaded this: another. You took your clothes off when I told you to, ten minutes ago: another. Look at how much of it is already mine. You're not deciding whether to start — you're a long way in.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator reads out a list of things the listener has done — visiting the site, watching the free material, downloading the file, following the undressing instruction — and attaches the same clause to every item: each one was an act of handing over power. Ordinary consumer behavior sits in the list alongside deliberate submission, undifferentiated. The listener is told to realize how far along they already are rather than to decide anything, so the next request is framed as continuing rather than starting.
- *Waking setup compliance relabeled as a trait*
  - **Setup.** Pre-induction, subject fully awake; a fetch instruction, a posture instruction, and a hand-placement instruction have all just been completed.
  - **The move.** Stop a moment. You got up and fetched it because I asked. You arranged yourself the way I described. Your hands went where I put them. All of that with your eyes open and nothing in your head but my voice on a speaker — no trance anywhere. That's not something I did to you. That's just how you work.
  - **Why it lands.** Before any induction the listener is sent to fetch a small item, then told how to arrange themselves and where to put their hands. Once all of it is done the operator stops and points out that every one of those instructions was followed at once, with no trance involved at all — which is offered as proof that compliance is simply how this listener works. A baseline is thereby established before any depth exists, and everything that follows only deepens something the listener has already accepted as a fact about themselves.
- *One compelled motion renarrated as many obediences*
  - **Setup.** Imagined journey through thresholds and stairs; the initial motion was framed as a compulsion the subject did not choose.
  - **The move.** You're already walking — you didn't decide to, you just noticed you were. Through the first door. Down the stairs. Through the second. [at the destination] Now look back at how you got here. Every doorway was a separate instruction, and you chose to follow every one of them. Twelve times you said yes tonight. That's the only way anyone arrives in this room.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told they are already moving before they noticed deciding to — a single compulsion, openly described as such. The journey then passes through a series of doorways and stairs. At the destination the operator re-narrates the whole trip: every threshold, she says, was a separate command the listener chose to follow, and only that repeated obedience could have brought them here. One instruction has become a remembered chain of a dozen consented acts.


**See also.** `absurdity-as-proof-obedience-task` — both harvest a real performed act and re-read it as evidence about the listener, but one annotates ordinary accrued behavior as state-evidence while the other engineers a deliberately costly absurd task so the cost itself is the proof. Useful as a cost-axis contrast, not the same move.; `acceptance-laddered-identity-migration` — both spend the listener's own prior behavior as warrant for a larger claim, and the split is what the accrued acts buy: evidence that a state is already present versus a license for the next identity tier. Close enough to be mistaken for each other.; `attention-as-evidence-loop` — both convert the listener's own behavior into evidence of an installed state, but one annotates discrete completed acts as accruing proof of a named state while the other runs on mere inertia — continuing to listen, sitting in silence — where the disconfirming move is pre-framed as already-failed.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both turn the listener's own performed act into unarguable material, but the ledger annotates real acts as EVIDENCE OF A PRESENT STATE (you are already surrendered), while the self-sealing proof runs the act as a LOGICAL PREMISE that forecloses a larger future commitment the listener has not yet made.; `chosen-descent-ratchet` — both relabel what has already happened as the listener's own doing, and they frequently run in the same passage — one attributes the state or descent to the listener's choice, the other annotates real recent acts as evidence of a state. Worth cross-referencing because the tell that separates them is what is cited, not what is claimed.; `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — genuine contrast pair on the same lever family: both cite something back at the listener so refusal reads as self-contradiction. The cut is what is cited - a discrete banked agreement artifact with forward reach versus real recent behavior annotated contemporaneously as evidence of a state. A reader adjudicating a script that cites the listener's past will need both entries to place it correctly.; `compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting` — both harvest the listener's real performed acts as evidence, but the ledger annotates many genuine acts contemporaneously to shift the perceived baseline to already-surrendered, while the single deferred callback targets one frictionless act much later to prove a specific thesis about manufactured wanting.; `concession-gated-kinesthetic-proof` — both cite evidence back to the listener as proof a state has already been entered, and the instructive contrast is the nature of the evidence: genuinely performed real acts annotated as they accrue, versus a suggested two-vector body sensation read as confirmation that a concession was accepted.; `covert-public-behavior-install` — both manufacture ongoing self-proof of an identity out of the listener's own behavior; the fork is whether the acts already happened and are merely annotated, or are newly installed as plausibly-invisible public behaviors under a secrecy frame. Close enough that a passage can read as either.; `decision-rights-revocation-ladder` — both present an itemized ledger that shifts the perceived baseline to already-surrendered, and both make later resistance feel like self-contradiction. The items differ in kind: one enumerates named decision-authorities and reassigns them in the past tense, the other annotates the listener's genuine recent behavior as evidence of a state. Choose by whether the ledger rows are fictive authorities or real acts.; `epistemic-authority-capture` — two routes to evidence the listener cannot rebut: claiming direct perception of their interior, or annotating their genuine recent acts as proof of the target state. Both strip standing to deny, one by asserted telemetry and one by the listener's own undeniable behavior.; `fantasy-laundered-first-compliance` — both convert a performed act into commitment before the listener can treat it as a decision, and the boundary between them is clean enough to be worth stating: one annotates the listener's genuine real-world acts as evidence of an already-present state; the other has the listener execute the target act inside a fantasy before it is consciously assigned. Real-act annotation versus fiction-laundered first execution.; `ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest` — both harvest the listener's own performed behavior as unrepudiable evidence, differing on whether the act is an installed near-involuntary motion banked as consent or genuine prior acts annotated as evidence of a state. Neighboring enough that a writer picks between them.; `irreversible-autobiographical-binding-act` — both cite the listener's own real behavior back as self-evidence. The distinction is act type and time axis: reversible acts annotated contemporaneously as evidence of a present state, versus one irreversible deed creating a permanent autobiographical fact. Real risk of misassignment when a script does both in sequence.; `own-desire-attribution` — both close the disavowal exit by making the listener the author, but retrospective attribution relocates the want into an asserted past history, while the ledger cites the listener's genuine just-performed acts as contemporaneous evidence of the state.; `pace-mirror-agency-proof` — both manufacture evidence that a state or role is already true before the doctrine is stated, and both work by the listener reading the proof as their own. They differ on whether the cited acts are real behavior openly annotated or a fabricated mirror loop, which is the call a reader has to make.; `pacing-leading` — both bank verifiable present truths to build unrepudiable agreement; the split is whether the accepted material is the listener's own real acts read as state evidence or observable statements coupled to an unverified lead.; `physical-compliance-proof-posture` — real overlap worth marking: adopting a posture appears among the acts one entry annotates as evidence of a state, while the other treats an elicited display posture as the proof device in its own right. The boundary is whether the act is elicited and then read back, or already-performed behavior annotated as it accrues. Keep both, and keep the pointer.; `pre-induction-compliance-ratchet` — both bank the listener's real physical acts as compliance capital, but the pre-induction ratchet is defined by BINDING TIME (waking, eyes open, before any trance language, before reactance mobilizes) while the ledger is defined by the ANNOTATION — enumerating acts as evidence of a state, at any point in the session.; `trust-capital-banking` — both convert something already banked into leverage on later asks: real acts relabeled as evidence of a state, versus a foreclosed verification of past trustworthiness banked as spendable capital. Same forward-spending logic on different collateral.; `withheld-frame-reveal` — reveal vehicle; placed here because the load is act-reassignment not concealed-game disclosure.


<a id="entry-145"></a>

### reciprocity-ledger-seeding

[#145](#entry-145) · [Back to make-real-then-rename](#genus-183) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: framing*

A future extraction is converted into a present desirable identity via a reciprocity / "good deal" frame, with the cost side named vaguely and low-friction while the benefit side is concrete and emotional, so the obligation is pre-installed as something the target WANTS rather than owes. Long before any trance, a transaction is stated as already agreed (she gives cuteness/availability, he "takes care of everything") and phrased as generosity toward him ("such a great deal", "all you have to do is take care of me"), seeding a ledger that later moves cash out. The lever is that the obligation is disguised as a cute deal — overt in content, covert in function; the target sees generosity, not an obligation contract.


**When to reach for this.** Installs a reciprocity ledger / provider-obligation as a desirable present identity via a "great deal" frame — off the v6.9 identity-labeling map (labels an identity, not an obligation). Not an explicit contract; the tell is the disguised cost side and concrete benefit side.


**Risk.** Pre-installs a real-world provider obligation (money/goods) cashed out later; durable and out-of-session in consequence but seeded as identity, not channel-eroding. Medium.


**Why it works.** The reciprocity norm makes an accepted benefit feel like an obligation, but the framing asymmetry is what makes the deal acceptable at seeding time: concrete, vivid benefits are weighted heavily in evaluation while vague, temporally distant costs are discounted, so the ledger is agreed to before its price is representable. Once agreed as an identity rather than a debt, later collection is defended by consistency rather than resisted as a new demand. This predicts that stating the cost side concretely and immediately at the seeding moment should measurably reduce acceptance. [plausible; reciprocity norm; vividness and construal-level asymmetry between concrete benefit and vague cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *A future obligation seeded as a great deal*
  - **Setup.** Pre-trance, conversational and light; the arrangement is stated as though already settled.
  - **The move.** So here's how we work: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and all you have to do is take care of me. That's your whole side of it. Honestly, it's a wonderful bargain for you.
  - **Why it lands.** Long before any trance, the arrangement is stated as if already settled and as if the favour runs toward the listener: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and looking after me is the only thing on your side of it. Isn't that a wonderful bargain for you? The benefit is concrete and emotional; the cost is a vague everything-I-need. The listener adopts the provider role as a flattering identity rather than an obligation, and the ledger it opens is cashed out much later.


**See also.** `banked-reward-escrow` — both bank a lever now for withdrawal later, and the escrow entry's pre-signed open-ended consent token is the same shape as an obligation seeded long before any specific ask. Useful contrast: one disguises the cost side inside a fairness frame, the other withholds and accumulates a reward or a consent claim to discharge on a condition.; `front-end-gift-directed-obligation` — same reciprocity lever run at two ranges: one seeds an obligation ledger far in advance as a desirable identity, the other renders an immediate free service and collects while the debt is live. A reader identifying an obligation play benefits from seeing both the pre-seeded and the front-loaded form, and from the repayment-channel boundary condition.; `identity-labeling` — both are off-map pre-commitment seeding; boundary is temporal-buffer-self-label vs reciprocity-ledger. Reconciliation may co-home them.; `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` — both manufacture felt indebtedness rather than stating a debt: one seeds a provider-obligation as a desirable present identity via a 'great deal' frame, the other stages a theatrical costly concession so an unchanged offer is revalued as a favor. Different install routes to the same reciprocity lever, so a reader designing an obligation move gains from seeing both.


<a id="genus-174"></a>

## make-them-need-it (4)

Diagnose a deficit, invoke an owed obligation, or weld the ask to a prized self-image so the payload arrives as something the listener's own identity demands.

[identity-congruence-leverage](#entry-1156) · [manufactured-deficit-remedy](#entry-118) · [old-self-discreditation](#entry-125) · [relational-repair-disclosure-lever](#entry-764)


<a id="entry-1156"></a>

### identity-congruence-leverage

[#1156](#entry-1156) · [Back to make-them-need-it](#genus-174) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

Compliance is welded to a prized self-image, value, or interest the listener already owns — being a real man, smart and careful, self-improving, the winner, the keeper of privileged knowledge — so the directed behavior installs as identity-congruent and self-chosen and refusal reads as failing one's own self-concept. The leverage point is volunteered or presumed positive identity, not shame and not a manufactured deficit.


**When to reach for this.** Positive self-image as the lever — unlike manufactured-deficit-remedy (a deficit is built first), old-self-discreditation (the past self is mocked), or compliance-authorship-laundering (agency relabeled with no identity-congruence test). Even where the win-frame licenses third-party use, the lever is still the listener's own prized self-image — a laundered bargain, not a governed delegation of control.


**Risk.** plugplaydaddyissues M6 licenses third-party use through the win-frame — out-of-session reach that requires bounding; other members are session-scoped reframes.


**Why it works.** Once a self-concept is salient, people act to remain consistent with it, and behaviour framed as expressing a valued identity is performed at higher rates than the same behaviour framed as a request — identity-framing effects of this kind replicate across domains from voting to honesty. Refusal then carries a self-concept cost rather than merely a social one, which is why it feels self-chosen. Falsifiable: the effect should vanish or reverse if the invoked identity is one the listener does not in fact hold, which distinguishes it from generic flattery. [established; consistency principle and identity/self-concept framing effects]


**Worked examples.**

- *A rigged binary makes obedience the smart choice*
  - **Setup.** Opening frame, before induction; subject chose to start the recording themselves.
  - **The move.** You should never obey blindly — anyone who demands that from a stranger has earned your suspicion. The other kind is the authority you picked, deliberately, after thinking it over. Nobody made you press play on this; you went looking for it. And obedience here doesn't mean going slack — it means paying close attention and getting it exactly right, the way a careful person does. Stopping now would mean overruling the choice you already made when you were thinking clearly.
  - **Why it lands.** Two kinds of authority are laid out: the bad kind, which you should never follow blindly, and the good kind, which you picked for yourself. The listener's guard is invited to fire at the first category — and then the operator points out that the listener chose to press play, which files this voice under the second. A second definition follows: paying close attention and getting things exactly right is what being obedient means. Compliance now sits inside two things the listener already values, being discerning and being careful, so stopping would mean taking back their own earlier choice.
- *The subject's prized self-image made the test*
  - "Do you think you have the ability to show her your love before she even asks for it? Is that a challenge you are man enough to meet?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Surrender counted as a win the listener scores*
  - **Setup.** Escalation segment; a pleasure/reward loop has already been installed and the subject has stated they want it to continue.
  - **The move.** Let's be clear about the scoreboard. Every time you go quiet for me, that's a point to you. Every time I use you, that's a point to you. You told me earlier you wanted that warmth to keep coming — this is how it keeps coming, so you're the one collecting on the deal you set. I win, you win, and you win twice, because you picked the terms.
  - **Why it lands.** Winning is redefined so that each thing given up scores a point: going quiet is a win, being used is a win, and it is stated as a win for everyone at once. Because a reward loop was installed earlier, the listener already has a stated condition of their own — keep the reward coming — which the escalation is then made to satisfy. The result reads back to the listener as a bargain they set the terms of rather than an imposition they accepted.
- *Exposure recoded as privileged secret knowledge*
  - **Setup.** Late session, an installed public-facing behaviour has already been agreed; the subject is anticipating social cost.
  - **The move.** Yes — people will hear you say it and think you've misspoken. Let them. They see a slip; you know exactly why the word came out that way, and you're the only person in the room who does. There's a particular pleasure in standing there straight-faced with a secret running underneath, and it belongs to you. Every time it happens in front of someone, you get that again.
  - **Why it lands.** The obvious cost of the installed behaviour — sounding foolish in front of other people — is picked up and handed back as an advantage: they see one thing, you know the truth, and only you know the gap is there. The listener is given words for enjoying it, so the social hit becomes the point of a private game. Every time the behaviour fires in public it now confirms the flattering self-image instead of denting it.


**See also.** `illusory-choice-authorship` — adjacent levers for making compliance feel self-chosen: relocating agency onto the subject versus welding the ask to a self-image the listener already prizes. One entry already names the other as a boundary case, so the pointer is earned rather than a category coincidence.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — both are self-supplied-lever moves that neighbor closely enough to be confused: one welds compliance to a prized self-image the listener already holds, the other relocates authorship of the payload to the listener outright. The tell that separates them - identity congruence versus genuine authorship - is only legible when both are in view.


<a id="entry-118"></a>

### manufactured-deficit-remedy

[#118](#entry-118) · [Back to make-them-need-it](#genus-174) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

The operator fabricates or diagnoses a deficit the listener is induced to own - a lifelong self-tyranny, shame driving resistance, constitutional weakness, always disappointing solo orgasms, a self that wants emptying, a lost-and-confused baseline, an unbearable bind - then positions the payload (surrender, dependency, the assigned task, the offered identity) as its remedy. The diagnosis is generic enough to feel personal, delivered where pushback is impossible, and often hardened by leading questions that manufacture confirming memories the listener then owns.


**When to reach for this.** The problem is built first and the payload sold as relief; separates from retrospective-desire-attribution (want asserted as already present, no deficit installed), from old-self-discreditation (past self mocked to close the return path, no remedy sold), and from identity-congruence-leverage (prized self-image leveraged, not a deficit).


**Risk.** Installs durable pathologizing self-beliefs and dependency framing (one member's lifelong-trait backdating); bounded hosts required for the deficit installs.


**Why it works.** Generic self-descriptions are readily accepted as personally accurate, so a fabricated deficit is owned rather than disputed, and once owned it creates a felt problem the operator alone has framed a solution for. Leading questions compound this by prompting the listener to generate confirming instances from memory, which are then held with the confidence of self-generated evidence. Falsifiable: if listeners rejected the generic diagnosis as not applying to them, or if compliance did not track how strongly they endorsed the deficit, the account fails. [established; Barnum/Forer effect; self-generated argument; leading-question memory distortion]


**Worked examples.**

- *A lifelong self-tyranny named as the real enemy*
  - **Setup.** Subject already down and unable to interrupt; the operator delivers a life history the subject did not supply.
  - **The move.** You learned to be ashamed young, and you've been managing it ever since — working too hard, apologising in your head, punishing yourself quietly for things nobody else noticed. That's what's been holding you back in here tonight. It was never me you were resisting. It was that. And you can put it down.
  - **Why it lands.** Once the listener is down, the operator delivers a biography they did not write: the shame that arrived early, the years spent managing it, the overwork, the guilt cycles — all of it named as one continuous campaign the listener has been waging against themselves, and named as the true source of every hesitation they have ever felt here. The phrasing is universal enough that almost anyone finds something that fits, and recognition does the rest. Resistance has now been relocated: it is no longer between the listener and the operator, it is between the listener and their own history — which makes handing over control a form of liberation rather than a concession. It also functions as insurance, since any future reluctance can be filed under the same old enemy.
- *Leading questions manufacture a confirming memory*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the operator asks rhetorically, waits a beat, then treats the answer as settled fact a few minutes later.
  - **The move.** When you do it on your own, it always promises more than it gives you, doesn't it. A little flat by the end, every time — wouldn't you say. ... And since you already know first-hand how thin it is by yourself, listen: with me, it doesn't do that. Not once.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is forbidden outright. Instead the operator asks, gently and rhetorically, whether it has not always been the case that on their own it promises far more than it ever delivers — a little flat every time, wouldn't they say. The listener is recruited as a witness against their own history, and whatever they actually remember, the frame supplies the reading. Minutes later the operator refers back to it as settled fact, citing what the listener supposedly knows first-hand, and offers itself as the remedy for the deficiency it installed on the way past.
- *A disoriented pre-state declared, never measured*
  - **Setup.** First lines of the session; nothing has been asked, nothing checked, no question posed.
  - **The move.** You've been adrift lately, haven't you. A bit helpless with it. Not quite able to hold a thought all the way to the end of itself. That's all right — that's exactly what this is for. Sit back and let me sort it out for you.
  - **Why it lands.** Before anything has been asked, the listener's current condition is announced to them: you've been adrift, haven't you, a bit helpless, not quite able to think straight. No question was posed and nothing was checked. The session then offers itself as the way out of that state, so the settling that follows registers as relief the operator produced — and the baseline it improved on was supplied, not measured.
- *Constitutional weakness backdated over a whole life*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after a suggestion test where the subject felt their own will fail to assert itself.
  - **The move.** Notice you couldn't stop that. That wasn't something I did to you — that's what you are. A mind built like yours was never going to hold out; minds like yours take their direction from outside, that's simply how they're made. You need this. You have always needed it. Tonight is only the first time anyone told you so.
  - **Why it lands.** Immediately after the listener has felt their own will fail to assert itself, the result is explained to them — not as something the session did, but as something they are: a mind built this way was never going to hold out, and minds of that sort require their direction from outside. Then the tense shifts and does the real work: you need this, and you have always needed it. A single session's state has been converted into a standing trait with a history attached, and the dependency being offered arrives as the sensible response to a fact about the listener rather than as a demand.


**See also.** `identity-uncertainty-gap` — both open a hole and install the operator as filler, but one fabricates a deficit the listener owns and sells the payload as its remedy, while the other manufactures identity not-knowing specifically so a later identity-label drops into a prepared slot and feels self-discovered.; `manufactured-insufficiency-ratchet` — both manufacture a shortfall the listener owns, then trade on it. One installs a deficit up front and sells the payload as remedy; the other renders an insufficiency verdict at the moment of likely success on a standard that cannot be satisfied. Reading both clarifies whether the shortfall is a diagnosis or a moving standard.; `manufactured-insufficiency-treadmill` — deficit-driven pair: one fabricates a shortcoming and sells the payload as its remedy, the other grants a success then revokes its sufficiency so no stable done-state exists. The second is effectively the repeating form of the first, and a writer needs to know whether the deficit is installed once or refreshed each cycle.; `old-self-discreditation` — resolve twins also feed an admission demand; deficit reading rejected because failure is real not fabricated; `own-desire-attribution` — pass B variant_of FRAM-03 overturned to deficit-first reading per fingerprint; `relief-dependency-couple` — both run on a problem-and-relief structure and they are ordered opposites, which is exactly why they get confused. One fabricates or diagnoses a deficit first and sells the payload as its remedy; the other delivers genuine felt relief on emergence and couples that relief to dependency and to a pending compliance ask. Whether the problem or the relief comes first is the discrimination.; `relief-monopoly-dependency` — complementary halves of one dependency build: a fabricated deficit the listener is induced to own, then a single source positioned as the only route out with relief kept deliberately incomplete. They frequently run together, and the second is the natural next move after the first.; `self-generated-failure-as-identity-proof` — both manufacture the evidence that justifies the payload, but one asserts a deficit for the listener to own and sells the payload as its remedy, while the other has the listener ENACT a failure in real time and converts the performance into identity proof.


<a id="entry-125"></a>

### old-self-discreditation

[#125](#entry-125) · [Back to make-them-need-it](#genus-174) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-model-surgery*

The listener's prior self - its beliefs, failed resolutions, ordinary relational demands, autonomous self-improvement attempts - is named, mocked, pathologized, or renounced (often in the listener's own first-person voice) so the return path closes: when the old position resurfaces it has already been self-disavowed, future protest of that shape is pre-tagged as the rejected wrong self, and failure history is inverted into evidence for the offered identity or into a credential for admitting need.


**When to reach for this.** Operates on the listener's self-narrative about who they WERE; no remedy is sold (manufactured-deficit-remedy) and no present want is asserted (retrospective-desire-attribution). The payload is closure of the exit back to the prior self.


**Risk.** Durable identity scope - autobiographical revision that pre-closes return to prior beliefs (gratitude M4, new-you M3 unfalsifiable identity-evidence flip).


**Why it works.** People infer their attitudes partly from their own utterances, so speaking the disavowal in first person makes the rejection self-attributed rather than imposed and thereby resistant to later retraction. Once the old position is on record as one's own repudiated error, its return arrives pre-labelled as the discredited self, which is a dissonance cost rather than a fresh option. Falsifiable: if self-spoken disavowals showed no more durability than operator-spoken ones, the self-attribution mechanism is not doing the work. [established; self-perception theory; counter-attitudinal advocacy; cognitive dissonance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Failed resolutions recoded as diagnostic proof*
  - **Setup.** Early, pre-trance or light trance; conversational, therapeutic register, before any suggestion is offered.
  - **The move.** Think back to the promises you made yourself in January. Can you even name them now? That blank is the first sign — not that you're weak, but that you were never built to run yourself. Those promises failed because keeping them meant impersonating a kind of person you are not.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator asks the listener to call up the promises they made themselves at the turn of the year, and then whether they can even name them now. That blank, she says, is the first sign. It is not weakness — they were simply never built to run themselves, and those promises failed because keeping them meant impersonating a kind of person they are not. A near-universal history of quitting is renamed as evidence for the offered identity, in therapeutic vocabulary, so the listener experiences it as insight rather than as a claim. Nobody can deny the premise without lying; accepting it routes straight into the conclusion. Afterwards the frame cannot be disproved — every future lapse counts as further confirmation.
- *First-person renunciation of the prior self*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session mantra block; subject is told to say each line along with the operator, two beats per line.
  - **The move.** Say it with me. There was a time I thought I could work things out for myself — ridiculous. There was a time I told my friends to stand up for themselves — ridiculous.
  - **Why it lands.** The lines are written to be recited along with, in two beats each. There was a time the speaker believed they could work things out for themselves — and the second beat dismisses it as ridiculous. There was a time they told their friends to stand up for themselves — ridiculous again. In the second person this would land as an attack; in the listener's own voice it lands as confession, and the belief has been written off by the only person whose verdict on it counts.
- *Ordinary life voiced as petty complaint*
  - **Setup.** Mid-flow, deep; operator drops into a whining register for a few seconds, then drops it again without comment.
  - **The move.** "Put that down. You promised. It's my turn to pick. Why is a screen more interesting than me?" ... Anyway. Down you go.
  - **Why it lands.** Mid-flow the track breaks into a whining register and performs the listener's ordinary life as a string of small grievances — put that down, you promised, it's my turn to choose, why is a screen more interesting than me. Then it drops the register and moves on. Nothing is argued against; the objection that there is a real life outside this has simply been played back as something small and shrill.
- *Weakness renamed as the strength of admitting need*
  - **Setup.** Subject has just been walked through their history of failed self-discipline and is braced for a scolding.
  - **The move.** That kind of willpower simply isn't in you, and that's fine — it isn't weakness, it's the other kind of strength, the kind that knows what it actually needs. No more play-acting. Every time you tried before, that's all it was.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator tells the listener that this kind of willpower simply is not in them — and that this is fine, because it is not weakness but a different sort of strength, the kind that consists of knowing what you actually need. No more play-acting, she says: every attempt they made before was play-acting. The listener arrived braced to be told to try harder and is instead told the trying was never real, which recasts every past act of self-direction as pretence and makes asking to be run the honest move.


**See also.** `identity-origin-erasure` — both close the exit back to who the listener was, so a reader hunting for return-path foreclosure will hit both. The means are different and worth contrasting: one discredits or renounces the prior self so future protest is pre-tagged as the rejected wrong self, the other deletes the baseline outright by rewriting the timeline so there is no before to locate.; `manufactured-deficit-remedy` — resolve twins also feed an admission demand; deficit reading rejected because failure is real not fabricated; `temporal-self-relocation` — both operate on the prior self to close the return path — one by discrediting and disavowing it, one by asserting an accomplished identity discontinuity that puts it out of reach. Different tone (mockery vs. dispassionate assertion), same target.


<a id="entry-764"></a>

### relational-repair-disclosure-lever

[#764](#entry-764) · [Back to make-them-need-it](#genus-174) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: authorship-shift*

A silent or withholding part is treated as an insulted relationship: the subject goes inside, apologizes for years of fighting it, and states sincere intent. Where the part still hides its function, the operator inserts themself as sole arbiter of usefulness and invokes a manufactured obligation, moving judgment and accountability off the part so its disclosure risk drops — extracting a response that direct asking could not get. The impasse is recast as a repairable relationship problem.


**When to reach for this.** The explicit apology/relational-injury framing plus accountability-transfer and manufactured-obligation levers — not merely re-asking nicely, and not manufactured authority that raises the COST of withholding (claimed infallibility); here the lever LOWERS the risk of disclosing.


**Risk.** Arbiter-insertion plus manufactured obligation pressure a withholding channel; session-scoped parts-work, but the operator takes judgment authority.


**Why it works.** Disclosure is governed by perceived risk, so lowering expected cost raises disclosure more reliably than raising the cost of silence. Apology and stated benign intent are cheap signals, not costly ones — they work by reducing anticipated judgement, and shifting the usefulness call onto the operator removes the subject's accountability for what is revealed. Falsifiable: if disclosure rates after apology-plus-accountability-transfer matched rates after simple repeated asking, the risk-lowering account fails. The internal-parts framing is a therapeutic convention, not evidence of separate agents. [plausible; disclosure risk calculus; reciprocity norm applied to a personified internal agent]


**Worked examples.**

- *Apologize to the silent part, then take the blame*
  - "go inside and apologize and tell it that you misunderstood its intentions… nine times out of ten he'll get a response." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `reciprocity-leverage` — the repair-disclosure move explicitly recruits a manufactured obligation, which is the same social-exchange lever, applied inside a parts-negotiation frame to lower the cost of disclosing rather than to buy compliance. Worth the cross-read to see the lever transplanted.


<a id="genus-217"></a>

## making-it-stick (3)

Moves that close the road back: changes declared permanent, the neutral baseline deleted from the state map, and leaving priced as abandoning who you are.

[identity-exit-tax](#entry-587) · [neutral-state-deletion](#entry-589) · [permanence-declaration](#entry-590)


<a id="entry-587"></a>

### identity-exit-tax

[#587](#entry-587) · [Back to making-it-stick](#genus-217) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: state-welding*

Fuses compliance to the listener's real self, worth, progress, or gendered identity so that non-compliance changes category: leaving stops being "I choose differently" and becomes "I abandon who I am." Refusal is thereby recoded as self-erasure or self-betrayal rather than a preference-level choice, recruiting self-consistency and identity-protection against future autonomy. The self-model is held FIXED and welded to a behavior (contrast self-model-surgery, which restructures the model): the mechanism is the cost-structure imposed on exit, not the durability of any installed content. In one script realization, self-worth is made entirely dependent on being "that perfect GOOD GIRL," making the whole trigger system load-bearing for identity. In a variant, the contingent condition is REMAINING IN a state ("Good girls stay / Underwater"), converting the trance state into an identity-membership rule so exiting trance forfeits good-girl status.


**When to reach for this.** The move prices EXIT at the identity level. It is not a durability claim — asserting that installed content endures is permanence-declaration; this is a contingency structure, not a permanence claim. It is not the identity-was-always-real reframe that conceals installation — that edits the history of the self, not the cost of leaving. It is not direct identity labeling, which applies a label with no conditionality. It is not deletion of the exit DESTINATION from the state map — neutral-state-deletion is map surgery that removes where you'd go; exit-tax leaves the map intact and prices the crossing. And exit taxed with DISTRESS rather than self-betrayal is the affective-level analogue, a separate move.


**Risk.** Directly erodes revocation capacity: when refusal reads as self-erasure, the subject's exit channel is taxed at the deepest available level. Anchored by demonstrated evidence (one member with dim_residual=true/high; another demonstrated as an in-script keystone).


**Why it works.** The move changes what refusal costs by changing what refusal means: once compliance is defined as an expression of who the subject is, declining is no longer a preference-level choice but an inconsistency with a self-concept, and self-consistency motivation makes such inconsistency aversive to act out. Self-perception dynamics compound it — the subject has already behaved compliantly, has an identity label available to explain that behaviour, and infers the identity from the behaviour, so each act of compliance strengthens the premise that makes exit expensive. Making the contingency state-membership rather than act-compliance extends the same pricing to remaining in the state at all. Falsifiable: the account predicts that exit rates fall specifically when the identity framing is present and that subjects offered a face-saving non-identity-implicating reason to stop will exit at markedly higher rates; if a neutral exit ramp does not restore exit rates, identity cost is not the operative mechanism. [plausible; consistency principle and self-concept maintenance; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Refusal recoded as abandoning who you are*
  - **Setup.** Late working phase, after the subject has complied readily with several instructions and the compliance is visible.
  - **The move.** This is not a habit you picked up. This is who you actually are, and every time you do as I say you are being more yourself than you have ever been. The person who argues, who hesitates, who needs a reason first — that was the smaller, older version, and every step away from me is a step back into her.
  - **Why it lands.** Compliance is welded to the listener's real self rather than to a preference: doing as told is described as being who they truly are, and any drift from it as sliding back toward a lesser, earlier version of themselves. The move never argues that the instruction is good. It changes what declining means — no longer a matter of preferring otherwise, but of giving up the person one has become. Self-consistency, which normally protects a person's judgement, is turned around to guard the operator's install instead.
- *Self-worth made wholly contingent on obeying*
  - **Setup.** Closing block, after a full trigger set has been installed and rehearsed.
  - **The move.** Listen carefully, because this is the ground you stand on now. You are worth something when you obey. That is where it comes from — not from being clever, not from being kind, not from anything else you have ever counted on. There is no good version of you that says no to me. That person does not exist.
  - **Why it lands.** The closing lines stop presenting the pleasant feeling as a reward for obeying and present it as the only ground on which the listener has any worth at all. There is no longer a version of them who disobeys and is still a decent person — that person has no defined existence in the frame. Every earlier trigger becomes load-bearing for selfhood rather than optional.
- *Staying in the state made a membership rule*
  - **Setup.** Mid-descent, between two stretches of imagery; delivered once, quietly, at the same pace as the surrounding scenery and never returned to.
  - **The move.** The light gets greener the further down you go, and the weeds move very slowly here. Good girls stay under. Sand on the bottom, cool and pale, and the surface is a long way up now.
  - **Why it lands.** One quiet line, dropped between two stretches of scenery and never repeated, states that the well-behaved remain down here — so leaving the trance now costs a title rather than merely ending a session.


**See also.** `affect-fused-identity` — two ways of making an identity label defend itself. One welds the label to a self-firing affect so membership is intrinsically rewarding; the other leaves the self-model fixed and prices exit as self-betrayal. Frequently co-occurring and easy to confuse, so the contrast is worth carrying.; `asymmetric-state-lock` — both price or foreclose leaving, at different layers: one makes exit cost the self, the other structurally removes the subject's autonomous off-switch and hands release to an operator condition. Since scripts commonly stack the identity cost on top of the structural monopoly, a reader auditing exit routes should see both. Not one technique — a contingency structure is not a monopolized off-switch.; `exit-annexation` — both price the off-ramp rather than removing it: one recodes refusal as self-betrayal, the other recodes using the exit as an act of service inside the same frame. The exit stays materially available in each; the capture is in what leaving means. Real contrast value for a writer choosing how to close an exit without blocking it.; `identity-clothing-hysteresis` — the garment entry prices exit at the identity level too, but binds the identity to a physical worn state with a deliberately costly named escape. That is close enough to the exit-tax structure that the boundary needs stating: a persistent physical cue with hysteresis versus a general cost-on-leaving contingency.; `neutral-state-deletion` — complementary exit-closure moves that each define themselves against the other: one prices the crossing at the identity level while leaving the state map intact, the other deletes the destination from the map so there is nowhere neutral to return to. Reading either without the other invites misattributing map surgery to cost structure.; `no-exit-state-braid` — both eliminate a clean exit, but the exit tax prices leaving at the identity level while leaving the state variables independent, whereas the braid makes depth, arousal and obedience co-move so no single-variable exit route exists at all.; `operator-removal-self-policing-closure` — the operator-free closure names self-worth staked on compliance as one of its interlocking components, and that component is exactly the identity-priced exit. Reader of the whole-script architecture gains from the discrete move that supplies its identity-cost limb; reader of the discrete move gains from seeing the end-state it is usually built toward.


<a id="entry-589"></a>

### neutral-state-deletion

[#589](#entry-589) · [Back to making-it-stick](#genus-217) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-model-surgery*

After two opposing triggers exist, the operator closes the listener's state-space to exactly those triggered states and names ordinary functioning as no longer available ("these are your only two states... no other options"). The move operates on the self-model's available-states INVENTORY: the neutral baseline is deleted from the map, so every post-session moment is framed as one of two triggered states and the "I'll just go back to normal afterwards" exit is foreclosed by removing "normal" as a destination. The binary metaphor (light bulb: on/off, no third state) does real work. This is not a movement on any continuous dimension — it is a state-space topology change: the A/C/D/R/T dimensions describe motion within a reachable space; this move redefines what the reachable space contains.


**When to reach for this.** Edits the AVAILABILITY MAP, not the machinery and not the price. The triggers themselves already exist — installing them is a different move; this one forecloses the third state. Pricing exit at the identity level while the map stays intact is identity-exit-tax, the complementary exit-closure move. Routing all listener RESPONSES to one outcome is action routing (foreclosure), not map surgery. Deleting a session-trajectory ENDPOINT (no wake count, no bottom) operates on arc-level completion states; here the deleted object is a self-state with waking-life scope — an identity-map edit. There is no amnesia wrapper, no new cue-response pair, no waking behavioral assignment, and states are removed, not moved.


**Risk.** Deletes the neutral baseline with waking-life scope — forecloses return-to-normal, which structurally attacks any revocation protocol whose endpoint is "back to baseline." Demonstrated evidence, dim_residual=true/high.


**Why it works.** Choice is made from the options a person can actually represent, not from the options that exist; by supplying an explicit two-item inventory the operator exploits the fact that unlisted alternatives are far less likely to be retrieved and considered (an option-generation and choice-set framing effect). Falsifiable: if listeners given the closed two-state framing are no less likely to spontaneously report or select a third neutral state than listeners given the same triggers without the closure line, the mechanism is doing nothing. [plausible; choice-set / option-generation framing effects; consideration-set restriction]


**Worked examples.**

- *Only two states exist — normal is off the map*
  - **Setup.** Both opposing triggers already installed and tested; subject responsive and near the close.
  - **The move.** So now you have two states and that is the whole list. Trigger one: mindless and open. Trigger two: sharp and eager. There is no third setting — you are a switch on a wall, and a switch is up or down, it is never somewhere in between. Whatever you are doing tomorrow afternoon, you are in one of those two, because there is no longer anywhere else for you to be.
  - **Why it lands.** With two opposed triggers already installed, the operator names them as the listener's complete inventory: these two, and nothing besides. A simple two-position device carries it — a mechanism with one setting or the other and no third position, which the listener is invited to identify their mind with. Nothing is added to either trigger and no new cue is created; what changes is the map of available states. The ordinary self that would simply resume afterwards is not forbidden, argued against, or taxed — it is quietly deleted as a destination, so the reassurance a listener would normally reach for afterwards has nowhere to point.


**See also.** `asymmetric-state-lock` — both close the return to baseline, and the distinction is the one a reader most needs: one deletes the neutral state from the map of available states, the other leaves an exit intact but hands its operation to an operator condition. Map surgery versus monopolized off-switch.; `eternal-present-frame-deletion` — both remove a vantage point rather than moving the subject along one, and seeing them together shows two different objects deleted: one strikes ordinary functioning from the inventory of reachable states so there is no baseline to return to, the other strips past, future and identity so there is no standpoint from which to evaluate the present.; `foreclosed-emergence` — both edit reachability rather than move the listener along a dimension: one deletes the neutral baseline from the waking-life state inventory, the other deletes clean waking from the set of end-states at the close. Same topology surgery at different scopes.; `identity-exit-tax` — complementary exit-closure moves that each define themselves against the other: one prices the crossing at the identity level while leaving the state map intact, the other deletes the destination from the map so there is nowhere neutral to return to. Reading either without the other invites misattributing map surgery to cost structure.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — both close off the route back to ordinary functioning, but one is a whole-arc property of the reachable response space while the other is a discrete edit to the inventory of available self-states. Useful for telling an arc-level design property from a single map-surgery line.; `switching-state-machine-topology` — near-inverse edits to the same object — the inventory of reachable states. One builds a two-state machine that requires the return to baseline and protects it; the other deletes the neutral baseline from the map so only the triggered states remain. A designer choosing between a re-runnable switching topology and a closed two-state space benefits from seeing both.


<a id="entry-590"></a>

### permanence-declaration

[#590](#entry-590) · [Back to making-it-stick](#genus-217) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: persistence*

Installs the belief that installed content — identity, conditioning, state, or body-image change — endures beyond the session and resists decay. The base move is a declarative durability assertion ("permanent, irreversible, the way it will be from now on"), but the corpus shows a family of delivery vehicles for the same belief: an anticipatory pre-frame issued BEFORE the payload is named, so everything that follows is received as durable-by-default; an event-gated commit that binds the permanence-fix to a specific physiological moment (orgasm framed as a save-checkpoint), pre-announced so anticipation amplifies it; an autonomous self-refiring maintenance process ("wipers") that engineers persistence rather than declaring it, shifting the model from "I was changed" (an event) to "something keeps me changed" (ongoing, no off-switch); a physical-inscription rendering ("engraved on your brain") declared tamper-proof and applied to already-deposited content; a listener-spoken chant with permanence tied to repetition count; and a compounding re-listen hook. Two structural observations recur: permanence claims are over-engineered redundantly — layered across timescales and across mutually-incompatible frames — so no single puncture releases the listener; and the claim is frequently carried across the trance boundary by a deliberately non-discharging wake. A further delivery vehicle: once cognition is suspended, name the state with a deliberately TERMINAL/mortal metaphor ("the silence of death", "the deep death of trance", the conscious mind "gone, given way") rather than a neutral "rest" — the mortal framing lowers the listener's expectation that the conscious mind will reassert and pre-establishes that the original self has "died", so a later identity-replacement frame has somewhere to land. The metaphor is the durability claim's vehicle, not a separate tool.


**When to reach for this.** A claim (or engineered process-expectation) about the DURABILITY of installed content. Not a rigged verification channel: a fait accompli asserted to pre-empt the "did this work?" check is a seal (self-sealing-frame), not a duration claim. Not identity-exit-tax, which prices EXIT at the identity level rather than claiming endurance. Not comfort conditioned onto PERCEIVING permanence or closure-of-exits — that is an affect-routing move. Not the claim that conditioning deepens progressively across future sessions: a re-listen hook here is one facet of a present permanence declaration, not a standalone multi-session claim. Not the identity-was-always-real reframe, which edits the past rather than asserting the future. Not the repetition that encodes the content in the first place, and not the amnesia payload the claim sometimes rides beside. Terminal-metaphor tell: if the state is given a final/mortal framing chosen specifically to DISCOURAGE re-emergence, that is a durability claim and belongs here — naming an empty/blank state neutrally to deepen, or personifying the mind as resting, describes depth/rest without an anti-re-emergence durability payload.


**Risk.** Strengthened relative to the plain declaration: the broadened scope adds engineered no-decay maintenance processes (one member) and event-committed locks (another member) that explicitly deny natural decay — a revocation-protocol requirement is MORE load-bearing under the broadened mechanism.


**Why it works.** Expectancy is a strong determinant of hypnotic and placebo response, so an explicit durability claim can act as a self-fulfilling prediction: a listener expecting persistence attributes ordinary post-session feelings to the install rather than to baseline variation. Falsifiable: matched sessions differing only in the presence of the permanence assertion should differ in measured persistence and in attribution of ordinary states to the install. (Dropped the 'redundant layering across incompatible frames adds robustness' clause — it predicts robustness under every outcome and was given no test of its own; if retained it needs its own falsifier, e.g. single-frame vs multi-frame versions differing in resistance to a targeted counterexample.) [plausible; response expectancy; placebo/expectancy effects; confirmation bias in self-attribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *Durability declared before the payload is named*
  - **Setup.** Start of the suggestion phase, before any specific content has been named.
  - **The move.** Everything I am about to give you holds. Not for tonight, not while the file is playing — it holds tomorrow at your desk, it holds next month. This is not imagination and it is not a game you put down at the end. It is simply how things are for you from now on. Now, here is the first of it.
  - **Why it lands.** Before a single specific change has been described, the operator states flatly that whatever follows will hold — outside the session, later in the day, not as imagery but as how things now are. The listener is told what the coming suggestions will do before being told what they are, so there is nothing concrete yet to weigh the claim against. Every item delivered after that arrives pre-classified as durable. It also closes, in advance, the reassurance a listener normally reaches for afterwards: the dismissal that it was only trance has been sealed before there was anything to apply it to.
- *Climax framed as the moment the change saves*
  - **Setup.** Arousal phase; subject edging under instruction and release has not yet been permitted.
  - **The move.** You are not allowed yet, so listen. Whatever depth you are at when you finish is the depth that sticks. The second you go over, it locks — everything I have put in you tonight gets written down permanently at exactly that setting. So take yourself higher first. When I say now, you go, and you save it.
  - **Why it lands.** Well before release is permitted, the listener is told that whatever level they have reached will be fixed at the instant they finish — the peak is recast from a discharge into a commit. Anticipation then does the work the claim cannot: the listener approaches climax knowing it is supposed to be the point of no return, and arrives having half-authored the lock themselves.
- *A background process that keeps re-applying itself*
  - **Setup.** After the primary suggestion has landed and been ratified.
  - **The move.** One more thing goes in underneath it. There is a little routine running in the back of your head from now on — it wakes up whenever any of this starts to loosen, and it tightens it again, and then it goes quiet. You will not notice it working. There is no switch on it. It just runs, the way your heartbeat runs.
  - **Why it lands.** After the main effect lands, the operator installs a maintenance routine on top of it — something that runs quietly on its own schedule, re-doing the work whenever it starts to slip, with no described off-switch. The listener's model shifts from a change that happened once to an upkeep that never stops running, which quietly removes the expectation that any of it should fade.
- *Inscription language plus a tamper-proof claim*
  - **Setup.** Late session, applied on top of material already installed earlier in the same recording.
  - **The move.** Everything you have taken in tonight is not sitting on the surface of you. It is cut into the tissue, scored deep, the way a name is cut into stone. You cannot sand it out. You cannot think your way back over it and change what it says. The wanting stays wanting, and the thought stays the thought, exactly as written.
  - **Why it lands.** Acceptance is described in physical terms — cut into the mind, written into the person — and then declared unalterable: the thought cannot be revised, and the need cannot be lost. It is applied to material already deposited earlier in the session, so it hardens what is there rather than adding content. The practical effect is that the listener's own later doubt is pre-labelled as futile.


**Realizations** (1): `terminal-metaphor-irreversibility`


**See also.** `intrinsic-self-reframe` — adjacent durability claims pointed in opposite temporal directions: asserting the content was always intrinsic, versus asserting it endures forward and resists decay. Passages routinely carry both, so the retroactive-versus-forward split is worth the cross-reference.; `no-return-terminal-close` — the durability entry explicitly notes its claim is often carried across the trance boundary by a non-discharging wake, which is the other entry's whole move. Real dependency: one asserts endurance, the other removes the return event that would otherwise discharge it.; `suggestion-integration` — overlapping payload: both assert installed content outlasts the session. The line worth drawing is placement and scope. One makes the durability claim at the emergence line within a genuine return to baseline; the other is a general durability assertion with many delivery vehicles, not tied to the wake.; `total-permeation` — two axes of the same durability problem: spread across every layer of the self so the trait cannot be bracketed, versus endurance in time so it does not decay. Easy to conflate, and scripts often run both.


<a id="genus-119"></a>

## manufactured-body-sensation (14)

Techniques that make the listener physically feel what the script authors — touch from words, substituted body parts, relocated sensation sources — rather than what the world supplies.

[antagonistic-body-map-split](#entry-1182) · [attribution-capture-of-internal-states](#entry-1271) · [catalepsy-comfort-relabel](#entry-1183) · [coercion-as-caregiving-reframe](#entry-1100) · [cross-modal-channel-bridge](#entry-1190) · [graded-somatic-identity-loading](#entry-466) · [inner-voice-medium-colonization](#entry-1073) · [kinesthetic-hallucination](#entry-473) · [perception-source-substitution](#entry-1253) · [phantom-body-ontological-reversal](#entry-1206) · [progressive-body-substitution](#entry-475) · [sensation-as-cognitive-edit-channel](#entry-813) · [somatic-mirroring](#entry-515) · [words-as-touch-transposition](#entry-488)


<a id="entry-1182"></a>

### antagonistic-body-map-split

[#1182](#entry-1182) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: immersion*

Runs a whole-body heaviness/immobility induction, then carves out one body part (the genitals) and assigns it the OPPOSITE sensation (lightness/buoyancy), then welds the two into a reciprocal loop where lighter-there means heavier-everywhere and a more-excited exception. Splitting the body into an inert majority and one hyper-live exception foregrounds arousal by suppressing everything around it, and the reciprocal weld makes the split self-confirming (denying the lightness means denying the loop), so the listener feels immobilized everywhere except the genitals, which become the only live sensation channel.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is a carved-out antagonistic exception (one part gets the reverse sensation) welded into a self-confirming reciprocal loop with the rest of the body.


**Risk.** Body-map alteration foregrounding arousal via immobility; carries the anti-stuck concern that attaches to induced immobility, session-scoped and reversible, no consent erosion.


**Why it works.** Sensation is judged relative to context, so suppressing the perceptual background makes a single spared region stand out far beyond its absolute signal strength — the same contrast logic that makes a light spot look brighter on a dark field. Attention is also capacity-limited: withdrawing it from the rest of the body concentrates it on the one live channel, and attended body regions are reported as more intense. The reciprocal weld adds a consistency trap in which reporting the lightness commits the subject to the heaviness, but this coupling is the weakest part of the claim. Falsifiable: if a carved-out exception produced no greater reported genital sensation than uniform whole-body heaviness, the contrast account is wrong. [plausible; perceptual contrast, attentional modulation of somatosensory intensity]


**Worked examples.**

- *One part made light while the rest goes heavy*
  - **Setup.** Mid-induction; whole-body heaviness already established and limbs are visibly slack.
  - **The move.** Your arms are lead, your legs are lead, and the chair is taking all of it. Everything except one place — between your legs there's a balloon tied on, tugging upward, light and buzzing and awake. And the harder it pulls up, the heavier the rest of you goes; the heavier your arms get, the more alive that one spot feels. Feel how heavy your hands are right now — that's how much it's floating.
  - **Why it lands.** An ordinary heaviness induction runs over the whole body — arms, legs, everything sinking — and then one region is carved out and handed the opposite sensation, floating and buoyant, as if it were tied to a balloon. The operator immediately welds the two halves into a loop: the more that one place floats, the heavier everything else becomes, and the heavier the limbs get, the more alive that one place feels. The body is now an inert majority with a single live exception, and the exception is the only channel left carrying sensation. Disputing the lightness is awkward, because the heaviness the listener can plainly feel is offered as its evidence.


**See also.** `somatic-carrier-sweep` — the carrier-sweep entry's second realization ends in the same output shape as the body-map split, a suppressed body with one aroused exception, but reaches it by propagating a single sensation and bifurcating it rather than by welding a carved-out opposite into a reciprocal loop. Text describing that endpoint fits both until the mechanism is checked.


<a id="entry-1271"></a>

### attribution-capture-of-internal-states

[#1271](#entry-1271) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

Rather than truthfully describing the listener's present state, the operator seizes the CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION of that state - recoding the listener's own baseline sensations, drift, or inevitable physiological actions as caused by the operator's voice, command, or influence. A maybe-menu ('maybe it's all of those things') or a declared symbol-meaning template ('blue is the colour of relaxation, so you feel it') captures every possible introspective result, including feeling nothing, so whatever the listener finds on introspection confirms the operator's hold; because the 'commanded' effect is one the listener would produce anyway (eyes closing under deepening, ordinary distraction), each landed prediction silently extends apparent causal reach and the listener begins to experience their own drift as obedience-output. REALIZATION: besides linguistic capture, the running state can be captured by REMOVING COMPETING REFERENTS [<-1212 scaffold-collapse-reattribution: after a fully-built imaginal scene has done its work, the operator strips the entire scaffold in a few lines while the relaxed somatic state stays and is renamed as the operator's own doing ('there is nothing but my hypnosis') - pulling the environment after the listener is inside it leaves the state with nothing to attach to except the voice, so it re-attributes directly to the operator].


**When to reach for this.** The tell is causal REATTRIBUTION onto the operator - 'you feel/did/wanted this BECAUSE of me / this proves my hold' - not truthful description of what is. DECODE absorbed: 1212 = capture a running state by demolishing every competing referent (strip the built scene mid-trance) so only the operator's voice remains for the state to attribute to. Direction is listener-to-operator credit - the INVERSE of compliance-authorship-laundering (83, which relocates authorship of the operator's content TO the listener). Distinguish from pacing-leading (states checkable-true facts, never claims to have caused them), from self-validating language (asserts unfalsifiable claims; here real introspective results are captured wholesale), from expectation-seeding (captures already-present states, not previewed ones), and from operator-credit-engineering (128 - arranges EVENTS/successes to harvest credit for operator AUTHORITY; here the listener's own internal states are captured to erode self-attribution).


**Risk.** Erodes the listener's self-attribution of their own internal states — a self-model surface, more than the low-risk pacing baseline — but stays session-scoped and reversible without durable identity install, so medium not high. Two members both make self-observed inattention self-incriminating, a soft refusal-channel pressure.


**Why it works.** People are poor at identifying the causes of their own internal states and readily adopt a plausible cause supplied to them — the standard misattribution finding. Predicting effects that would occur anyway (eyelid heaviness during sustained relaxation, attention drifting) produces near-certain hits, and the menu structure makes any introspective result confirmatory, so the listener accumulates apparent evidence of the operator's causal reach in the same way a Barnum statement accumulates apparent accuracy. Falsifiable in an obvious way: predictions targeted at base-rate-inevitable events should produce more attributed causal reach than predictions of unlikely events, and stripping a scene should raise operator-attribution only if the state persists after the referent is removed. [established; misattribution of causality; Barnum/subjective validation; base-rate exploitation]


**Worked examples.**

- *A maybe-menu that catches every answer*
  - **Setup.** Opening, before any formal induction; the listener has just been told they are in control and may stop at any time.
  - **The move.** You're in charge here. You can stop whenever you like. Well — mostly in charge.

Whatever you're feeling right now: maybe it's just that you're tired, it's late. Maybe there's something still hanging around from the last time you listened to me. Maybe it's simply what my voice does to people. Maybe it's all three at once.

And if you're feeling nothing much, or a bit muddled about which it is — that's the most common one of all. That's how it starts.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator opens by granting the listener full command of the situation, then withdraws it in the next breath — perhaps not entirely. She offers a series of possible explanations for whatever they are currently feeling: that they are simply tired, that something lingered from a previous listen, that this is just the effect her voice has, or that all of it is true at once.
