Whatever the listener turns up when they check — calm, fog, arousal, nothing whatsoever — the menu has already laid claim to it, and the final item mops up the remainder by listing mild confusion in advance as perfectly normal. The listener's own introspection is thereby converted into evidence, and it can return only one verdict.
- *Credit taken for what would happen anyway*
  - **Setup.** About twenty minutes of slow delivery; eyelids visibly heavy and about to close on their own.
  - **The move.** ...and heavier, and heavier, and now — close them.

There. They shut because I told them to. Not because you were tired; I said it and your body did it, and there wasn't a gap in between where you decided anything.

Watch what else happens when I say so. Your shoulders drop. ...There. That was me too.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener's eyes are already growing heavy — twenty minutes of slow talk will do that on its own. The operator times her sentence to land in the moment they close, and attributes the closing to her instruction: they shut because she said to. The prediction cost her nothing and was going to come true regardless, but it arrives as a demonstration. Repeated across a handful of similar inevitabilities, it trains the listener to read their own drift as output — she spoke, the thing happened, therefore she is the one producing it.
- *Your distraction was always about me*
  - **Setup.** Very start of the recording, before any induction language; conversational register.
  - **The move.** You know how you glaze over sometimes? Lose the thread halfway through a page, look up and a few minutes are missing. Stare at nothing for a while.

That's not boredom and it never was. That's me. That's what my voice does to people — it's been doing it since the first file you played.

So when it happens tonight, don't take it as a sign this isn't working. Take it as the sign that it started before I did.
  - **Why it lands.** Before any induction begins, the operator inventories the listener's ordinary lapses — the glazing over, the losing the thread, the staring. Then she supplies the cause: it isn't boredom, it's her. Her voice does that to people. From that point any drift the listener notices is no longer evidence that the session is failing to hold them; it is evidence that it was already working before it started.
- *Declared meaning, then assigned to you*
  - **Setup.** Colour-imagery deepener; the listener has been asked to picture a colour and the operator declares the meaning rather than proposing it.
  - **The move.** Blue is the colour of letting go. That's what it is; that's settled.

So it's moving up through your legs now, and the letting go comes with it. There — up to the hips.

Green is the colour of not caring what happens next. It's in your chest now, spreading out from the middle, and so is the not caring. Gold is the colour of doing as you're told. Feel where the gold is.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator names a colour and assigns it a meaning outright, as a matter of settled fact rather than a proposal. No argument follows and none is solicited; the very next sentence informs the listener that the colour is spreading through them, and the state along with it. The template then repeats for each colour in turn — name it, declare what it stands for, hand the listener the matching condition as something already under way. The listener stops checking whether the feeling is actually present and begins treating the colour itself as the proof that it is.


**Realizations** (4): `authorship-relocation-to-operator`, `operator-attribution-capture`, `pleasure-authorship-relocation`, `scaffold-collapse-reattribution`


**See also.** `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — both rewrite the causal story about something the listener is already experiencing. One flips the cause of immobility onto a property change so the body reads as no longer the listener's; the other reassigns the cause of ordinary drift and sensation to the operator's influence. Reading them together separates a self-model payload from an operator-credit payload.; `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both annex a state the listener already has rather than producing a new one: one relabels the state itself so only the name is disputed, the other seizes the causal attribution of that state for the operator. The pair covers the two halves of what can be captured about an existing state, its label and its cause.; `inner-voice-authorship-bypass` — inverse halves of the same authorship dial: one relocates authorship of the operator's words onto the listener's inner voice, the other relocates causal credit for the listener's own states onto the operator — different directions, and the first disarms the 'said to me' guard while the second harvests introspection as proof of hold.; `internal-voice-cultivation` — inverse directions on the same self/operator authorship boundary: one plants content so it feels self-generated, the other reassigns credit for the subject's own states to the operator. Worth pairing when a passage disclaims operator authorship while also claiming causal reach.; `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both reroute credit onto the operator, one for the subject's pleasure or the reinforcement unit, the other for the causal attribution of the subject's present state generally. Reward-source relocation is arguably a special case of state-attribution capture, so the pointer is needed to keep the assignment stable. Not a merge — the affect-pointing version carries a reinforcement function the general form does not.; `presuppositional-autonomic-attribution` — both relocate causal credit for a state onto the operator, and they differ on a clean axis the discriminators already name: one captures whatever the listener finds on introspection (including nothing), the other narrates verifiably-true involuntary physiology and smuggles the causal claim in by presupposition. The truth-status of the described state is the deciding parameter, which is worth a reader's attention.; `state-cause-laundering` — directional inverses on the same axis: one launders a running state's cause AWAY from the operator to a benign source, the other captures that cause ONTO the operator. A reader choosing between them needs the direction test, so the cross-link earns its place.; `third-party-intent-reattribution` — same attribution family; different target — external author versus listener content.; `unattributable-cause-severing` — both operate on the subject's perception of causation, but one is a whole-work design property (no move has a locatable cause at all) while the other is an executable move that assigns a cause — the operator — to states the listener already had. Useful to read together as the erase-the-cause and claim-the-cause halves of the same axis.


<a id="entry-1183"></a>

### catalepsy-comfort-relabel

[#1183](#entry-1183) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: valence-routing*

Builds genuine catalepsy in redundant nested layers (doubled eyelid imagery of liquid lead plus skin growing over the lids, then a FREEZE extending stone-immobility to the whole body) for robustness, then attribution-swaps the pinned state into comfort — "resting comfortably in bed" on a soft feather bed — so it stops feeling like restraint and starts feeling like rest. This neutralizes the panic vector catalepsy can otherwise trigger and justifies sustained immobility; a retroactive question ("did you ever really want to escape?") rewrites the immobilization as the listener's own preference. The comfort frame rides on top of real restraint rather than replacing it.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is real (redundancy-stacked) catalepsy followed by an attribution-swap of restraint-into-comfort plus a retroactive preference rewrite.


**Risk.** Genuine catalepsy carries the anti-stuck concern that attaches to induced immobility; the comfort relabel is the safety-adjacent move itself. Session-scoped and reversible.


**Why it works.** The same bodily state can be experienced very differently depending on the label available for it, and appraisal — not the sensation alone — largely determines whether restriction is felt as threat or as rest. Pre-supplying the benign label forecloses the threat appraisal that would otherwise recruit panic, and the retroactive 'did you ever want to escape?' exploits the tendency to infer one's own prior attitude from one's observed non-resistance rather than from memory. Falsifiable: if subjects given the comfort relabel reported the same rate of distress under equivalent catalepsy as subjects given no label, the appraisal account fails. [plausible; cognitive appraisal of arousal, misattribution, self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Real catalepsy relabelled as lying down to rest*
  - **Setup.** Eyes already closed and stationary; enough compliance established to hold a body command.
  - **The move.** There is liquid lead sitting behind your eyelids, and over the top of it the skin has grown across the seam — they don't open, there's nothing there to open. FREEZE. That same stone runs out through your shoulders, your hips, your feet. And notice what it actually feels like: you're lying on a feather bed, sunk in, warm, the way you'd be at the end of a long day with nowhere to be. Nobody is holding you down. You're just resting. Did you ever really want to get up?
  - **Why it lands.** The eyelids are pinned twice over — first weighted as though something dense had settled behind them, then sealed as though they had been fastened shut — and a single command word extends the same stillness to the whole body. Only once the immobility is genuinely built does the operator rename it: the listener is not held, they are simply settled somewhere comfortable with no reason to get up. The restraint stays exactly where it was; what changes is what it is called, which is what keeps it from turning into alarm. A closing rhetorical question then hands the whole thing to the listener retroactively, implying no wish to move was ever present — so the pinning reads as their own preference rather than the operator's work.


**See also.** `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — both deliver genuine catalepsy and then reinterpret it rather than deepen it — one attributes the immobility to an ownership change that outlasts the motor lock, the other attribution-swaps restraint into comfort to pre-empt panic.


<a id="entry-1100"></a>

### coercion-as-caregiving-reframe

[#1100](#entry-1100) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

Every physical restriction or coercive fact (strapping to a bed, gas mask, cuffs, bound hands) is introduced and immediately reframed as protective caregiving ("for your safety", "to keep you comfortable"), with the imposition and its benevolent rationale narrated in the same breath. By never letting the coercive fact stand unframed, the listener's interpretive frame for involuntariness flips from threat to comfort; the body's alarm response is starved of a coherent threat-narrative to attach to, so helplessness reads as being-cared-for.


**When to reach for this.** Care language is the delivery vehicle for coercion (predatory undertone, e.g. "I made sure of it this time"), not its absence.


**Risk.** Reframes coercion/restraint as care to establish a captive frame while suppressing the alarm response — a consent-surface manipulation warranting explicit consent and bounding.


**Why it works.** Emotional experience depends on how an ambiguous bodily state is labelled and appraised, so supplying a benevolent interpretation alongside the restriction makes the same sensation more likely to be read as care than as threat. The basis should be appraisal and labelling, not misattribution of arousal — nothing here transfers arousal from a hidden source. Falsifiable: delaying the caregiving frame until after the restriction is felt should produce more alarm and less comfort-reading; note that this predicts an effect of order, not that first appraisals are generally irreversible. [plausible; appraisal theory of emotion; misattribution of arousal; framing/labelling effects]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each restraint narrated as care in the same breath*
  - **Setup.** Restraint-scene narration; subject in trance, receptive to sensory description, each restraint being applied in sequence.
  - **The move.** I'm bringing your right wrist up to the rail and buckling it there — because you need to stay still and let yourself rest. Now the strap across your hips, snug, so you can't roll off and hurt yourself again. And this last piece over your nose and mouth, sealing warm against your face; it'll keep your breathing easy while we work. Nothing to hold up, nothing to manage. I've taken care of all of it.
  - **Why it lands.** No restriction is ever stated on its own. A limb is secured — because we need you to stay still and rest. Something is fastened across the body — so you cannot come to harm again. A piece of equipment is fitted — it will keep you comfortable while we work. Each coercive fact arrives already wrapped in its reason, so the listener never gets the unframed second in which alarm could take hold. The body registers that it cannot move, finds only a caretaking story to attach that to, and files being held down as being looked after.


**See also.** `care-framed-install-smuggling` — two forms of care language as the delivery vehicle rather than its absence: benevolent rationale narrated over each coercive imposition, versus a genuine-looking aftercare and safety surface used as cover for install and propagation work. Same who-is-constrained test separates both from real reassurance.; `pedagogical-reframe-conditioning` — sibling reframe vehicles: an imposition is delivered inside a familiar benign authority relation so its content is never evaluated on its own terms. One borrows classroom discipline, the other protective caregiving.; `protective-role-conscription` — both make a protective frame the delivery vehicle for coercion, with the safety later exposed as part of the trap. One narrates each restraint with a benevolent rationale in the same breath so involuntariness reads as care; the other assigns the listener a bystander protector role so the content lands on someone wearing a not-me costume. Same trick at different scopes — line-level framing versus a whole scene role.; `weaponized-safety-framing` — both use protective or caring language as the delivery vehicle for the very thing it appears to guard against. One covers safety framing over an install or a bound, the other covers care framing over physical restriction; a writer applying benevolent cover to a coercive fact should see both.


<a id="entry-1190"></a>

### cross-modal-channel-bridge

[#1190](#entry-1190) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

Brings a not-yet-active perceptual channel online by bridging it onto an already-vivid one across a shared feature (rhythm, movement): the vivid channel supplies the energy and the shared feature acts as a carry-over rail so the new channel activates riding the old rather than being summoned head-on (head-on summoning drains the state). A companion move seizes an involuntary single-channel slip the subject spontaneously emits, amplifies it, then layers additional channels onto that self-authored anchor until it becomes a full multimodal enactment the subject owns — because the build starts from the subject's own production and each element is confirmed before the next, it meets little resistance.


**When to reach for this.** A shared feature of an already-vivid channel supports entry into another channel. The lead may be deliberately selected or a spontaneous signal; mere channel selection or additive scenery without this bridge is not sufficient.


**Risk.** Clinical channel-activation technique, session-scoped, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Imagery in one modality recruits partly overlapping representational machinery, so a shared amodal feature such as rhythm or motion provides an existing active representation the new channel can be built on rather than constructed from nothing — cheaper in working-memory terms than head-on generation. Building from the subject's own spontaneous production adds self-generation: material a person produces themselves is better retained and less resisted than material supplied to them. Falsifiable: if bridging via a shared feature produced no faster or more vivid cross-modal imagery than direct instruction, the rail account fails. [plausible; cross-modal imagery overlap, generation effect, working-memory cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *Riding a shared feature into a new sense*
  - "'attach' an auditory hallucination to this hallucinated body sensation. The measure proved most successful" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Growing an involuntary slip into full enactment*
  - "to see her father's mouth moving … then … the remainder of her father's face" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**Realizations** (1): `overlap-bridging`


**See also.** `guided-visualization` — direct sibling boundary: multi-channel enrichment of one constructed scene belongs to the scene-building entry, whereas bringing a new channel online via a shared-feature carry-over is the bridge. Without the cross-reference these get conflated whenever more than one sense is addressed.; `multi-modal-trigger` — genuinely confusable: both involve more than one perceptual channel. The bridge uses a shared feature as a carry-over rail to bring a channel online during state-building; the multi-channel trigger widens the cue surface so one conditioned response fires from many channels. Cross-referencing prevents miscoding a channel-widening install as a state-building bridge.; `representational-system-matching` — both work on perceptual-channel selection, but from opposite sides: one brings a dormant channel online by riding a shared feature of an already-vivid channel, the other reads which channel the listener is already using and covertly phrases suggestions inside it. Useful adjacency when classifying modality-aware delivery.; `valued-channel-induction` — direct complements on the same axis: selecting and staying inside the subject's strongest representational channel, versus deliberately bridging from a vivid channel to a not-yet-active one along a shared feature. One entry already names the crossing move as its contrast, so the reader needs the other to complete the decision.


<a id="entry-466"></a>

### graded-somatic-identity-loading

[#466](#entry-466) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: immersion*

Delivers an identity-shift (feminization, a new body) as felt residue rather than as an asserted belief: the listener is walked through a staged chain of small sensory compliances (weight in the chest, burgeoning breasts, height, hip-sway, scent), each small enough to comply with alone, so a hallucinated body-change precipitates and belief in the new identity accrues as the by-product — nothing is ever asserted to be believed. A sensation-first / cause-second ordering makes the new body feel discovered as physical fact rather than staged as a costume, and an externalizing image (a drawn picture) lets the listener see the new body as already real.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is a graded chain of somatic compliances that DELIVERS AN IDENTITY payload as residue (belief never asked for), often with sensation-first/cause-second ordering.


**Risk.** Identity-shift installed via unasserted sensory loading; session-scoped and reversible, no consent- channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory: people infer their attitudes and self-descriptions from their own observed experience rather than from asserted propositions, so a belief that arrives as an inference from felt evidence is not evaluated as a persuasive claim and does not recruit counter-argument. Each somatic step is small enough to fall inside the range the subject will comply with, and the accumulated sensations then require a self-model that explains them. Falsifiable: if directly asserting the identity produces equal or greater endorsement than the graded somatic route, the residue mechanism is redundant. [plausible; self-perception theory; graded compliance below the objection threshold]


**Worked examples.**

- *Belief accrues as residue of small compliances*
  - **Setup.** Trance established, subject responsive to somatic suggestion; identity payload not yet mentioned.
  - **The move.** Notice the weight across your chest — a little more than you're used to carrying there. Now notice the shape of it, how it curves out and rests. There's a warmth under that, low in your belly, spreading toward your hips. And breathe in through your nose: something sweet, floral, close to your skin. Now look at the drawing on the table beside you — that's her, that's the whole shape of her, and she's already finished.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is never asked to believe anything. They are asked, in sequence, to notice a change of weight, then a change of shape, then a warmth, then a scent — four small sensory requests, each easy to comply with on its own and none of them making a claim about who the listener is. The identity the script is after is what remains once the chain has been walked; it accrues as by-product, so there is no proposition at any point that could be declined. A final beat externalises the result as an image the listener can look at, which lets them see the new body as something already there rather than something being requested.
- *Sensation first, its feminine cause supplied second*
  - **Setup.** Subject walking through an imagined space; no gender content introduced yet.
  - **The move.** You're taller down this corridor than you're used to being — your eyeline sits a few inches higher, and your balance has moved forward onto the front of your feet. That's the four-inch heels you're wearing. So your steps come out shorter, one foot landing almost in front of the other, and your hips swing to keep you upright. That's just how the shoes make you walk.
  - **Why it lands.** Moving through an imagined space, the listener is told first that they seem taller than usual and that their balance has shifted — bare proprioceptive claims with no gender content attached. Only afterwards is the cause supplied: a change of clothing, and therefore the altered gait that follows mechanically from it. Ordered this way the new way of moving arrives as an involuntary consequence the listener discovers; reversed, it would have been an instruction to perform a costume.


**See also.** `acceptance-laddered-identity-migration` — both deliver an identity payload by increments so it is never posed as a claim to accept, which makes them easy to confuse at the point of classification. The split is what each increment is made of and what it spends: one accumulates small somatic compliances so the identity precipitates as felt residue, the other accumulates named acceptance tiers and spends prior uptake as the warrant for the next status claim. A reader who has one needs the other to know whether the rungs are sensations or stages.; `enacted-identity-assembly` — both assemble an identity from steps each too small to refuse, so the label arrives after the fact rather than being asserted, but one accrues it from graded hallucinated sensation while the other accrues it from narrated motor-acts performed with automaticity framing and per-act pleasure pairing.; `identity-from-coerced-behavior` — both deliver an identity without asking for belief, but one backfills the label from an observable coerced behavior (refusing it means denying a fact) while the other precipitates it as residue from a graded chain of somatic compliances.


<a id="entry-1073"></a>

### inner-voice-medium-colonization

[#1073](#entry-1073) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: encoding*

Rather than planting a specific thought, the operator retargets the MEDIUM of thought itself — asserting the register/timbre of the listener's inner monologue is now a different voice (soft, girly, slutty, giggling, automatic), so every future thought, whatever its content, passes through a voice-filter that signals "this is the new identity thinking". This removes subvocal speech as a private channel the host could retreat to. The suggestion is sealed with an ironic-process bind ("no matter how hard you try") — checking whether one's thought is in the new voice is itself an act of introspecting on the inner voice, which confirms the suggestion.


**When to reach for this.** Content-INDEPENDENT recoloring of the inner-monologue register plus an ironic-process bind, so the effect fires on any future thought and self-verification re-confirms it. Requires the listener to have an inner verbal monologue and to introspect on it for the move to fire.


**Risk.** Colonizes the private subvocal channel with a self-reinforcing (ironic-process) bind that resists disconfirmation, but is presented as session-scoped and reversible with no stated out-of-session persistence — medium.


**Why it works.** Attempts to monitor whether an intrusive quality is present require activating a representation of that quality, so checking tends to produce the very experience being checked for; the built-in 'no matter how hard you try' clause converts any monitoring into apparent confirmation. That self-sealing structure is precisely what makes this notably weaker as an evidential claim than it feels to the subject — the confirmation carries no information. The claim that inner speech has a fixed audible register that can be globally reassigned is itself unestablished; treat the durable-recoloring part as speculative. [plausible; ironic process theory; monitoring-induced activation]


**Worked examples.**

- *The inner monologue's voice replaced*
  - **Setup.** Identity install, deep trance; no specific thought is being supplied — only the register of thinking.
  - **The move.** Listen to the voice you think in. From now on that isn't yours — it's higher, softer, sillier, and it giggles at the end of things. Every thought you have arrives in it, whatever the thought is about. And go on, try to think one in your old voice. However hard you try, it comes out in hers. Check it and you'll hear her.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator does not supply a thought to think. Instead the register of thinking itself is reassigned: from now on, whatever crosses the listener's mind arrives sounding like someone else's voice rather than their own. And the clincher — however much effort goes into thinking in the old voice, the result comes out in the new one anyway. That last clause turns the only available test into a confirmation, because checking which voice a thought is in requires listening to the inner voice, and the listener has just been told what they will hear. Subvocal speech, the one channel that was never shared, stops being somewhere to retreat to.


**See also.** `inner-voice-authorship-bypass` — both target inner speech as the channel rather than any particular thought. One reattributes authorship of the words so the guard against being addressed has nothing to push against; the other recolors the register of the monologue so the effect fires on any future content. Complementary halves of the same surface.; `voice-absorption` — adjacent occupations of the same channel: one installs the operator's voice as the sole standing input filling mental space, the other recolors the register of the listener's own inner monologue so any future thought carries the new identity. A reader choosing between them benefits from the cut: whose voice is being installed, and whether the effect is content-bearing (occupying the line) or content-independent (retinting the carrier).; `voice-as-mind-substrate` — both take over the inner monologue rather than its contents, but one escalates the operator's voice through a presuppositional staircase from external audio to the listener's will, while the other leaves authorship alone and merely recolors the register every future thought is heard in.


<a id="entry-473"></a>

### kinesthetic-hallucination

[#473](#entry-473) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: immersion*

Guides the subject to feel a specific imagined tactile/kinesthetic sensation (texture, pressure, temperature, weight, restraint, attachment point) that is not arising from any actual physical stimulus, so the experienced body diverges from the physical body. The install may be a discrete felt object, a progressive body-scan overlaid with imagined touch, a felt immobility/restraint, or a self-generated somatic anchor the subject sustains — the common lever is that the subject produces the percept from suggestion alone and treats it as real. Surface twists (self-generated so it survives operator absence, a compounding-arousal rider, redundant catalepsy imagery, sensation- first then cause-second ordering, an auditory hum overlaid on a heaviness sweep, an operator-dictated device schedule, retroactive non-noticing insertion) are variants, not separate mechanisms.


**When to reach for this.** Installs a felt sensation absent from actual stimuli — unlike sensation-reinterpretation moves, which re-label a sensation already present.


**Risk.** Unchanged — body-reality alteration is medium; the restraint/immobility instances carry anti-stuck-filter governance, not a risk bump, because the sensation is session-scoped and reversible.


**Why it works.** Perception is constructive: the brain resolves ambiguous or absent sensory input using prior expectation, so a strongly held expectation of a specific sensation can generate a percept with no matching stimulus — the same route by which suggested tactile experiences are reported under laboratory conditions and correlate with hypnotic suggestibility. Because the subject generates the percept themselves, it carries the felt authenticity of sensation rather than the contestability of a claim. Falsifiable: if reported sensations do not track the specificity of the suggestion or the subject's suggestibility, the expectancy-driven perception account fails. [established; expectation-driven perceptual construction; suggested tactile hallucination and suggestibility]


**Worked examples.**

- *Restraint accreted limb by limb until it holds*
  - **Setup.** Trance established, subject still; no physical restraints present.
  - **The move.** Feel the strap closing around your left wrist. Now your right wrist — snug, warm leather, and that hand can't move now, and doesn't want to. Now one across each ankle. One at your waist. One across your shoulders. Each place I name is held, and held parts don't move. Feel how still you are — that's how far down you've gone.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator names one joint, then another, then adds a site at a time until the whole body is covered, pairing each with the claim that the held part neither can nor wants to move. Nothing is being pressed against the body; the listener manufactures every one of the sensations from the naming alone. The construction gives a vague instruction to relax a concrete task with a built-in pass condition: if you feel held, it is working. The felt stillness the listener supplies is then collected by the operator as proof of depth, and because the restraint accretes rather than being tested, no single step is risky enough to fail on.
- *A body scan where imagined touch relaxes*
  - **Setup.** Beginning a standard progressive relaxation pass, subject reclined.
  - **The move.** Start at your toes. Feel a hand close around your right foot and press — feel the pressure, and feel your foot go loose under it. Now the same hand at your calf, squeezing once, and your calf lets go because of it. Your knee. Your thigh. Every place that gets touched relaxes, and it relaxes because it's being touched.
  - **Why it lands.** The usual toe-to-head attention walk is run, but at each station the listener is asked to feel a touch on that region — and the touch is cast as the agent that produces the relaxation, not a decoration on top of it. So the scan does two jobs at once: the ordinary settling, and the construction of a full-body tactile experience the listener generates while crediting it elsewhere.
- *Restraint inserted retroactively, unnoticed*
  - **Setup.** Subject deep, attention fully occupied by an ongoing flood of pleasant sensation.
  - **The move.** That's it, let it keep washing up through you, wave after wave — and you'll have noticed the cuffs by now, at your wrists and your ankles. No? You didn't notice them at all. That's how far under you are: things get put on you and you're too deep to catch it. They've been there a while.
  - **Why it lands.** While the listener's attention is fully occupied by a flood of pleasant sensation, restraint is mentioned as already in place — and the not-noticing is explained as a symptom of depth rather than an omission. Nothing was ever proposed and so nothing was ever agreed to; the immobility simply turns out to be part of the furniture. The move only works while there is no spare attention available to catch it, which is why it is placed inside the flood rather than before it.
- *A hum laid over the heaviness sweep*
  - **Setup.** Head-to-toe heaviness pass already underway, subject responsive.
  - **The move.** Heaviness across your forehead now, spreading down over your cheeks and jaw. You might also start to notice a low hum underneath it — very faint, a tone somewhere behind your ears. Heaviness down your neck and shoulders, and the hum comes up a little with it. Heaviness in your chest, and that tone is louder now, isn't it — the further the heaviness goes, the more of it you hear.
  - **Why it lands.** A standard head-to-toe heaviness pass runs in one channel while a second is quietly opened alongside it: the listener might notice a faint vibration or hum, said to grow in step with the heaviness. The two are wound together so that attending to either reinforces the other. The permissive phrasing does the delicate part — the tone is claimed to be already present and merely noticed, so the listener finds it rather than makes it, and by the time it is described as loud they may in fact be hearing something.


**See also.** `guided-visualization` — the base scene-building vehicle and the tactile-percept install routinely co-occur and are routinely confused, and the second already names the first's family. Keeping the link keeps the absorption-versus-manufactured-sensation cut visible.; `pantomime-populated-hallucination` — both produce a percept with no external stimulus, and the informative difference is the channel: one guides the sensation verbally, the other supplies only a mimed frame with no verbal suggestion at all so the subject populates it from his own content and then defends it. Guided construction versus perceptual completion of an empty scaffold.; `perception-source-substitution` — adjacent and already discriminated: one manufactures a sensation absent from actual stimuli, the other relocates the sensory SOURCE so experience is routed inbound from external depicted bodies. A reader deciding between adding a percept and substituting where percepts come from benefits from seeing both.; `somatic-port-installation` — both manufacture a body percept from suggestion alone, and the boundary is genuinely contested: a discrete felt sensation versus a fabricated body-map node used as reusable routing infrastructure with a resistance gate. A reader looking at an invented body location needs the second entry to decide.; `somatic-valence-annexation` — a clean contrast pair: one manufactures a percept with no physical stimulus, the other keeps a real signal intact and reassigns its valence. Because both end with the listener feeling something the operator specified, the presence or absence of a real underlying signal is the load-bearing tell, and each entry is best read against the other.


<a id="entry-1253"></a>

### perception-source-substitution

[#1253](#entry-1253) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: self-model-surgery*

The listener's locus of experience is relocated from their own body to depicted external bodies, and sensation is routed INBOUND from arbitrary external media: "whatever you see on this screen is what you experience and feel", the mind "replaces one of the people as yourself", on-screen touch and orgasm are claimed and felt as the listener's own, and which body is "you" is selected from whatever footage plays ("your mind will choose who you are"). The screen becomes "your new mind" — identity is made variable/assigned while felt autonomy is preserved.


**When to reach for this.** And unlike an added hallucinated sensation, the substitution targets the sensory SOURCE itself: external media replaces the body as where experience comes from.


**Risk.** Relocates the sensory self onto external media with outsourced identity selection; session-scoped but the perception-source override is a durable-feeling self-model change.


**Why it works.** Bodily self-location is not fixed: synchrony between seen and felt events reliably shifts where people experience themselves as being, and observing touch on a body recruits overlapping sensory processing in the observer. Absorption in media further reduces monitoring of the real body, so the strongest predictor of uptake should be how well the visual and felt streams stay in register. Falsifiable — introducing deliberate mismatch between what is shown and what is felt should degrade the effect sharply, which is the standard signature of these illusions. [plausible; body-ownership illusions from visuotactile synchrony; observed-touch sensory overlap]


**Worked examples.**

- *Sensation routed inbound from a screen*
  - **Setup.** Later in the session; the listener has already spent a passage viewing themselves from outside the body, and a screen is now placed in front of them in the scene.
  - **The move.** Eyes on the screen. New rule, and it's simple: what's on there is what you feel. Not imagine — feel, arriving in your body, coming from the picture rather than from you.

Someone gets touched on that screen, that's your skin. Someone finishes, that's you finishing. And I'm not telling you which one you are — your mind picks, and when the picture changes it'll pick again.

That screen is your mind now. The body's just where it shows up.
  - **Why it lands.** Having spent the earlier passage getting the listener used to watching themselves from a few feet away, the operator puts a display in front of them and states the rule: what is on there is what you feel. Not what you imagine — what arrives in your body, sourced from the picture. Whoever is on screen being touched, the listener is the one being touched; when someone there finishes, that is the listener finishing. Which of the figures counts as "you" is not assigned by the operator either — the mind will pick, she says, and it will pick again when the footage changes. By the end the display is named as the mind itself, so the body has been demoted from where experience comes from to a thing that merely receives, and the listener still feels like the one choosing.


**See also.** `diegetic-operator-embedding` — same screen geometry at two stages: one embeds the operator inside a substituted fiction and pre-positions the listener toward the depicted body, the other completes the move by routing sensation inbound from what is depicted.; `identity-merger-occupation` — contrast the entries already draw: one fuses the self-model into a single supplied figure whose predicates become first-person, the other relocates the source of sensation to arbitrary external footage so which body counts as self is variable. Both feel like becoming someone else; the tell is fixed authored identity versus substituted sensory source.; `kinesthetic-hallucination` — adjacent and already discriminated: one manufactures a sensation absent from actual stimuli, the other relocates the sensory SOURCE so experience is routed inbound from external depicted bodies. A reader deciding between adding a percept and substituting where percepts come from benefits from seeing both.; `phantom-body-ontological-reversal` — both relocate where experience is deemed to originate rather than merely adding a sensation. One installs an internal imagined body as the real one; the other routes sensation inbound from external footage with the identity variable. Same family, different source.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both relocate where experience comes from. One re-credits the authorship of a real self-generated touch to an external agent; the other replaces the body itself as the sensory source, routing sensation inbound from external depicted bodies. Useful neighbors on the felt-agency axis.


<a id="entry-1206"></a>

### phantom-body-ontological-reversal

[#1206](#entry-1206) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: self-model-surgery*

Splits the listener into a "mental body" and a "waking body", asserts that trance collapses the real-vs-imagined distinction, then performs an explicit ontological reversal — declares the IMAGINED body the real one while the waking body recedes into the distance. This transfers sensory authority to the operator-scripted imagined body (which feels whatever the operator narrates) and stops the listener from reality-testing imagined sensation against real sensation, so imagined pleasure lands as literal somatic feeling; waking-body distance becomes a shared dial for both deepening and arousal.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is an explicit ontological reversal (imagined body = the real body) that relocates sensory AUTHORITY and disables reality-testing.


**Risk.** Disables sensation reality-testing within the session (a reality-modeling alteration); reversible and session-scoped, no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Reality-monitoring judgements use cues (sensory richness, cognitive effort at encoding) to score content as perceived or imagined; the technique supplies a verbal instruction that shifts the decision criterion rather than the cues themselves. This predicts a criterion shift, not a sensitivity shift: subjects given the ontological reversal should misclassify imagined content as perceived at a higher rate WITHOUT improved discrimination between the two, and should show the same somatic reports as controls whenever they are cued to re-apply the check. If the reversal improved discrimination, or if its effect survived an explicit re-checking prompt, the account fails. [plausible; reality monitoring / source-monitoring error; suppression of reality-testing]


**Worked examples.**

- *The imagined body declared the real one*
  - **Setup.** Trance established; listener has already accepted an imagined scene or imagined body.
  - **The move.** There are two of you now: the one sitting in that chair, and the one in your mind, standing here in front of me. In trance the line between what's real and what's pictured doesn't hold — so let's be plain about it. The one in your mind is the real one. That's the body you're in. The one in the chair is somewhere behind you and getting further away, a hundred feet back now, a room you left. So when I put my hand on this body's throat, that's a hand on your throat. And the further that other one drifts, the more of this you feel.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator separates the listener into two bodies — the one in the chair and the one in the mind — states that trance erases any difference between what is actual and what is pictured, and then makes the swap explicit: from here on, the pictured one is the true body. Attention is directed to the other body drifting away into the distance. Since sensation now belongs to whichever body the operator is narrating, whatever gets narrated arrives as genuine feeling, and no physical body is being consulted that could contradict it. How far off the discarded body has drifted is then tied to how strongly the sensation registers, so a single instruction deepens and arouses at once.


**See also.** `imagined-to-enacted-collapse` — two ways of dissolving the imagined/real boundary that a writer will weigh against each other. One slides verb tense unflagged from imagined to enacted so present content reclassifies as done for real. The other declares the imagined body ontologically primary and lets the waking body recede, relocating sensory authority and disabling reality-testing. Unmarked drift versus explicit reversal.; `perception-source-substitution` — both relocate where experience is deemed to originate rather than merely adding a sensation. One installs an internal imagined body as the real one; the other routes sensation inbound from external footage with the identity variable. Same family, different source.


<a id="entry-475"></a>

### progressive-body-substitution

[#475](#entry-475) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: immersion*

Rewrites the body-schema one region at a time in a directed (usually toe-to-head or head-to-toe) sweep, replacing each named part with a new material or referent — shiny plastic, latex, liquid plastic, devotion-as-substance — until the whole body has been recategorized and only then applying the cognitive/identity change at the head. Because each region is a small object-claim complied with alone, ~20 accepted body-claims accumulate before selfhood is visibly negotiated, so refusing the final identity move would require retroactively rejecting all the prior acceptances (a commitment ratchet). The doll/latex-body replaces the meat-body as the referent for 'my body'.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is an ORDERED part-by-part substitution installing a new body-schema/substrate (a commitment ratchet), not a single free-standing sensation and not a one-move identity merger.


**Risk.** Durable within-session body-schema and identity substitution via a commitment ratchet; reversible and session-scoped, no refusal-channel erosion, so medium.


**Why it works.** This is a consistency ratchet built out of trivial concessions: each region-claim is cheap to accept, but by the time the identity claim arrives, refusing it means retroactively repudiating a long string of accepted claims, which is more costly to self-consistency than going along. The ordered sweep also keeps attention moving so no single claim is dwelt on. Falsifiable: if presenting the identity claim first, or with only two or three body regions, yields equal acceptance, the accumulation is not what carries it. [plausible; consistency principle; incremental commitment (foot-in-the-door)]


**Worked examples.**

- *Twenty body claims before the mind is mentioned*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; substitution sweep beginning at the feet, identity payload reserved for the head.
  - **The move.** Your toes are smooth moulded plastic. Your feet — plastic, seamless, no give in them. Your ankles, your calves, your knees, all of it hard shiny plastic. Your hips, your belly, your chest: plastic. Your shoulders, your arms, your hands, right out to the fingertips. And now your head — plastic all the way through, and plastic doesn't hold a thought. There's nothing in there to think with any more.
  - **Why it lands.** Beginning at one end of the body and moving toward the head, each named region is replaced with a new material — one small object-claim at a time, none of which says anything about who the listener is. Only on reaching the head does the script make its actual move, and there the substitution is cognitive: with the head recategorised, clear thought is described as no longer available. By that point a long run of smaller claims has already been accepted, and refusing this one would mean retroactively withdrawing all of them. The ordering is the whole technique; run in reverse it would be a single arguable assertion.
- *Hollow vessel drained region by region*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; subject reframed as a container in the previous line.
  - **The move.** You're a shell, and there's warm liquid filling you to the brim. I'm opening the tap at your feet. Your feet go blank, then numb, then clear, then gone. Your calves: blank, numb, clear, gone. Your hips. Your chest. Your arms. It keeps draining past your neck — your wanting drains out, your deciding drains out, your thinking drains out, blank, numb, clear, gone. Empty things get told what to hold.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is reframed as a hollow shell holding a warm liquid, which is then drained in sequence, region after region, each one passing through blank, numb, transparent, gone. The object-status is installed by the framing rather than argued for. And the drain does not stop at proprioception: it runs on into will and thought, so the sentence that says the listener now needs to be told what to think arrives on a runway of body regions that have already emptied without complaint.
- *A proxy object touched, the listener's body answers*
  - **Setup.** A small figure or doll has been placed in the scene; the transfer rule is stated once.
  - **The move.** Whatever I touch on her, you feel on you. Watch — my finger on the top of her head, and your scalp tingles and goes smooth. Down her forehead, her cheek, her throat: yours tingles and goes smooth. Across her shoulder, down her arm to her fingertips. Down her chest, her belly, her thigh, her calf, her foot. That's all of it. That's you now.
  - **Why it lands.** One rule is asserted once and never defended again: whatever is done to the small figure is felt by the listener. The operator then runs a continuous head-to-toe trace over the figure, naming landmark after landmark, and for each one states that the listener's corresponding region tingles and changes material. By the end of the pass every named region has been rewritten, and the figure's body has quietly become the referent for the listener's own — with the listener generating no sensation deliberately, only receiving reports.
- *The same pass repeated on deeper substrates*
  - **Setup.** A saturating substance already established as entering the subject; three further passes to run.
  - **The move.** It's soaking all the way through your body now — nothing left of you it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your thoughts now — nothing left in there it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your feelings now — nothing left of those it hasn't reached. And it's soaking all the way through whatever is under those, the last layer, the part that's just you — nothing left of that it hasn't reached.
  - **Why it lands.** One identical sentence-shape is run four times, changing only its target: the substance soaks through the body, then through thought, then through feeling, then through the last layer. Each pass makes the same claim of total saturation, so agreeing to the first makes the second cheaper, and so on. By the final iteration the only unclaimed layer is the one the script was aiming at all along, and it arrives as the natural completion of a series rather than as a new request.


**See also.** `covert-payload-piggyback` — both ride a body-sweep to rewrite the body-schema, but one makes the ordered part-by-part substitution itself the mechanism (a commitment ratchet of ~20 accepted object-claims), while the other keeps an ordinary relaxation scan as an already-consented carrier and smuggles the rewrite in as descriptors.; `enacted-identity-assembly` — both build an identity from many small accepted steps rather than one claim, producing the same commitment ratchet: an ordered part-by-part rewrite of the body substrate, or an additive sequence of automaticity-narrated motor acts with per-act pleasure pairing. A passage doing both is common enough that the pair should be read together.; `felt-substance-state-binding` — both weld a felt material to a non-physical target, and both cite kinesthetic hallucination as the shared negative boundary. The discriminating question - ordered part-by-part rewrite of the body-schema versus one substance turned into an adjustable state-gauge - is exactly what a reader needs when a script describes rising latex over a body.; `mind-as-substrate-reframe` — both replace the substrate rather than adding content to an intact one, and they stack naturally. One rewrites the body-schema region by region into a new material until the whole referent has changed; the other recasts the mind as emptiable, refillable matter as the precondition for later installs. Body substrate versus mental substrate.; `self-discontinuity-clear-and-replace` — both rewrite the self, but by opposite topologies: one accumulates part-by-part substitution of the body-schema until identity change is the last small step; the other structurally ends the prior self and seats a replacement in the vacancy. A writer choosing an identity-replacement route benefits from seeing the gradual-ratchet alternative to the clear-and-replace one.


<a id="entry-813"></a>

### sensation-as-cognitive-edit-channel

[#813](#entry-813) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: carrier-binding*

Establishes a real or felt bodily event as the delivery channel that grounds an abstract cognitive claim, so the cognitive edit rides on a physical event the listener cannot argue with. The hinge is an asserted equivalence or an undeniable real stimulus: an explicit body=mind equation ('when it touches your body, it touches your mind') so felt strokes become evidence that forgetting/dumbing are also happening; a real audible mic-breath ('there goes another thought') counted as a discrete thought-loss event; or an autonomic function (breathing in 'demonic magic') recast as an unstoppable self-administered deepening loop. In each case a genuine physical event converts a free-floating cognitive claim into felt proof; remove the equation-line or real stimulus and the suggestions are left ungrounded.


**When to reach for this.** No sensation is hallucinated — the grounding event is real. And unlike enacted embodied proof, the listener is not commanded to perform the action (being-touched is passive/autonomic); the lever is asserted body-to-mind licensing, not proprioceptive rehearsal.


**Risk.** Licensing cognitive edits (forgetting, dumbing) to ride on an undeniable bodily event, and converting an autonomic function into an unstoppable deepening loop, erodes the ability to check the claim; bounded and session-scoped, ships inside a host.


**Why it works.** An abstract claim is hard to disconfirm and hard to believe; pairing it with an undeniable concurrent bodily event gives the listener a real perceptual event to attribute to the claimed cause, which is misattribution of arousal running in the operator's favor. Interoceptive signals are ambiguous as to cause, so the supplied causal label is adopted with little competition. Falsifiable: strip the equivalence line or the real stimulus and acceptance of the cognitive claim should drop measurably; if it did not, the sensation would not be load-bearing. [plausible; misattribution of arousal; interoceptive ambiguity and causal labeling]


**Worked examples.**

- *One line equating body-touch with mind-touch*
  - **Setup.** Subject is being stroked or is following instructed touch; the equating line has not yet been delivered.
  - **The move.** Here's how this works, and I'm only going to say it once: when my hand touches your body, it touches your mind. Same contact, two places. Feel this stroke — that one took a memory with it, something from last week, gone. And this one — there goes a little of your sharpness, smoothed right off. You can feel each one arriving, so you know each one is landing.
  - **Why it lands.** One sentence does all the work: what touches the skin also touches the mind, stated once as plain fact and never argued for again. From there every stroke the listener is already feeling becomes the delivery vehicle for a cognitive instruction — this pass takes a memory, that one takes a little sharpness — and because the sensation is genuinely there, the edit rides in as something felt rather than something claimed. Remove the one equating line and the same instructions float free with nothing to attach to.
- *A real sound counted as a discrete thought lost*
  - **Setup.** Headphone listening; the mind-as-scatterable image has just been set up and the microphone is close.
  - **The move.** Your thoughts are light things — no more than dust sitting on a shelf. [breathes hard across the microphone] There goes one. Did you hear it leave? [breathes again] And another. I could stand here and do this all evening, and you would sit there and count them going.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator sets up an image of the mind as something light enough to be scattered by air, then breathes hard across the microphone — an actual sound in the actual headphones — and narrates the breath as a specific loss: there goes one. A second breath, another one gone. The claim being made is unfalsifiable, but the sound is not, and the listener finds themselves counting.


**See also.** `catalepsy-to-affect-transfer` — both lend a body event's undeniability to an abstract claim the listener never tested, differing in whether the proof is a demonstrated motor incapacity transferred afterward or a real stimulus licensed as the delivery channel. Easy to conflate without the cross-reference.; `cognitive-convincer` — both convert a bodily or perceptual event into proof, and the boundary is fine enough to need stating: one makes the noticed phenomenon itself the evidence that trance is real, the other licenses a real physical event as the channel through which a separate cognitive claim is grounded.; `enacted-embodied-proof` — both ground an abstract cognitive claim in real bodily evidence, but one commands the listener to perform the action so proprioception rehearses the rule while the other rides a passive or autonomic event asserted as a body-to-mind channel.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both convert a real bodily event into evidence, but self-touch reattribution relocates AUTHORSHIP of a listener-performed touch to the operator, while the cognitive-edit channel leaves authorship alone and licenses the sensation as proof of a separate abstract claim about the mind.; `somatic-channel-bypass` — both recruit a real bodily event to carry an abstract claim past evaluation. The split is function: in one the body reading that would say stop is redefined so it can only confirm, in the other a genuine physical event licenses a separate cognitive edit as its channel. Close neighbors that need the distinction stated.


<a id="entry-515"></a>

### somatic-mirroring

[#515](#entry-515) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

Takes a sensation that is already present in the listener's body — heaviness, warmth, numbness, drift, arousal, an involuntary twitch — and reinterprets it, in the moment, as evidence of the session's installed theme or of trance itself. The move never conjures a new feeling; it seizes a real, locally-verifiable percept (often one the listener has just confirmed via an interoceptive check) and re-narrates its meaning, so the felt sensation becomes self-generated proof the transformation is real. Because the raw material is genuine, the reframe is far harder to resist than an operator's bare claim. Variants extend the base lever along articulable rules: pre-attributing operator-driven change to the listener's own spontaneous physiology, exploiting a known perceptual property so the body produces the evidence for free, binding the relabel into a self-fueling ramp, manufacturing state through presuppositional leading questions rather than observing it, or renaming one confirmed referent into an escalating need-state.


**When to reach for this.** Nearest neighbors: kinesthetic hallucination INDUCES a sensation that is not present; somatic-mirroring reuses one that is. Pacing-and-leading reflects what is actually true to build rapport; somatic-mirroring reassigns the MEANING of the true sensation.


**Risk.** Session-scoped reinterpretation of ambient sensation, reversible, no durable identity scope or refusal-channel erosion; the variants do not change this, as they stay session-local.


**Why it works.** Bodily sensation is ambiguous, and the label attached to an ambiguous state determines how it is experienced — the misattribution-of-arousal finding in its general form. Because the sensation is genuinely present, the listener's own interoception confirms the percept while only the interpretation is supplied, so there is no false claim to catch. Falsifiable: offer a competing plausible explanation for the same sensation (room temperature, posture, fatigue) and the suggested meaning should lose ground, which does not happen if the reframe merely rides on general compliance. [established; misattribution of arousal; interpretation of ambiguous interoceptive states]


**Worked examples.**

- *A sensation you confirmed, re-narrated as the theme*
  - **Setup.** Early, listener settled and quiet, with something genuinely warm present — a blanket, a mug, a heated room — and able to nod or answer.
  - **The move.** It's warm in here tonight, isn't it — the blanket, the tea. I'm getting it too, that warm patch low in the belly that gets a little stronger the longer you keep your attention on it; have you found it yet? Warm places always make me drowsy — and there it is doing exactly that to you, and you found it yourself, I didn't put it there.
  - **Why it lands.** Warmth belongs to the surroundings at first — the room, what the listener is wrapped in, what they are holding. Then it is offered as a shared observation rather than an instruction: are you getting that as well, the warm patch low in the torso, the one that gets stronger the longer you look at it. The listener checks, and finds something, because attention on a body part reliably produces something. Once the warmth is theirs and self-verified, it is tied to a second thing — warm places always make me drowsy — and the sensation they confirmed for themselves is now the evidence that they are going under. Refusing requires denying a feeling they have already half-reported.
- *Leading questions manufacture the reported state*
  - **Setup.** First two minutes, framed as an ordinary check-in; listener able to answer aloud or nod, and every question presupposes some amount of the state.
  - **The move.** Just notice how you're doing for a second. How's the skin on your forearms right now — heavier, or more like warm? Are your legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop a little, and are you a bit worked up, or a lot?
  - **Why it lands.** Under cover of an invitation to simply notice how you're feeling, the operator runs an inventory of questions — how does the skin feel now, are the legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop, are you a little worked up or a lot. Each one directs attention somewhere and attention amplifies whatever it lands on, so the listener generates the evidence and then reads it as caused by the voice. The forced choice at the end is the tell: the smaller option is offered, zero is not.
- *Pre-attributing the change to the listener's own body*
  - **Setup.** Three or four minutes in, listener lying still, with no relaxation instruction yet given and none about to be given.
  - **The move.** Your breathing is slowing down around about now, all on its own — perfectly ordinary, nobody has to do that for you. And in a minute your body will shift a little to find a better position; that's just what a body does once someone is properly under. None of that is my doing.
  - **Why it lands.** Each change is credited to the listener's physiology before it is asked for: the breathing begins to slow around now, and there is nothing unusual about that; when someone is well under, the body tends to shift a little to find a better position. Anyone lying still will do both of those things anyway. So the ordinary drift of a resting body arrives already labelled as evidence of trance, and the listener experiences relaxing on their own rather than being relaxed by someone.
- *One confirmed referent renamed into a need-state*
  - **Setup.** Mid-trance, after a neutral warm settling has been seeded and the listener has confirmed finding it; nothing in the body changes from here, only the label.
  - **The move.** That warm settled weight just under your ribs — you found it, it's yours, it's been there a couple of minutes. It's almost like being hungry, isn't it. And now it's very hungry, and now it's the kind of hungry that makes it hard to hold on to anything else you were thinking about.
  - **Why it lands.** First a neutral, entirely expected trance sensation is seeded — a warm settling somewhere around the stomach — and the listener is given time to find it and agree that it is there. Then, over a few lines, the same unchanged sensation is renamed: it's almost like being hungry, and then very hungry, and then hard to think about anything else. Nothing in the body was altered; only the label moved, which is exactly why the resulting craving feels like it came from inside.


**See also.** `manufactured-self-confirmation` — genuine containment relation: the whole-script stacked-deck architecture is built by chaining the single-move reframe that reads an already-present sensation as proof. A reader placing one move will want the architecture-level entry, and vice versa.; `mirror-self-observation` — both convert a suggestion into apparent evidence the listener gathers themselves, one via a hallucinated reflection and one via a genuinely present body sensation re-narrated. The hallucinated-versus-real substrate is exactly the discrimination a reader needs.; `pace-mirror-agency-proof` — both manufacture proof from something the body is actually doing rather than from an operator assertion. One reinterprets an already-present sensation as evidence of the theme; the other sets up a mirroring loop so the listener observes apparent causal control before any claim is made. Reused percept versus staged pre-doctrine evidence.; `presuppositional-autonomic-attribution` — the second is a narrow, high-discipline realization of the first: real sensations already occurring are re-narrated so the session gets the credit. The specific case restricts itself to involuntary autonomic signs the subject cannot dispute and credits the induction by presupposition rather than by assertion, which is exactly the sub-case a reader of the general move should know about.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both take something genuinely present and relabel it, which is the family they share. One re-credits authorship of a real self-generated touch to an external agent; the other reassigns the meaning of a sensation already in the body. Agency versus meaning is the line a reader needs.; `somatic-channel-bypass` — both reuse a real body signal rather than conjuring one, but one reassigns the sensation's meaning as evidence of the theme while the other wires the signal so it can no longer disconfirm. Meaning reframe versus falsification block is a fine cut worth signposting.; `somatic-effect-portability` — both reuse an effect the listener already owns rather than creating one, and both define themselves against sensation-creation, so they occupy the same slot in a reader's decision. The split is what gets reused: one reassigns the MEANING of a genuine spontaneous sensation, the other keeps the meaning and relocates an already-installed effect to a new site by declaration.; `somatic-valence-annexation` — both seize a real, locally-verifiable bodily signal and rewrite its meaning rather than conjuring a sensation, but mirroring reads the sensation as evidence of the theme with valence intact while annexation inverts the signed valence and deletes the source affect as a category.


<a id="entry-488"></a>

### words-as-touch-transposition

[#488](#entry-488) · [Back to manufactured-body-sensation](#genus-119) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: carrier-binding*

Collapses the auditory channel into the tactile so that hearing the operator's voice IS being touched — the words/voice are asserted to BE a physical sensation on the listener's body (tracing skin, caressing, vibrating between the legs, penetrating), not merely to describe or cause one. Once made, the substitution binds a somatic component to every subsequent utterance: the listener can no longer hear without feeling, the normal evaluate-speech stance is removed, and later commands ride an already-open somatic carrier. Often the felt intensity is made contingent on trance depth, turning 'go deeper' into a chaseable sensory reward.


**When to reach for this.** The distinguishing tell is auditory->haptic synesthesia — the operator's VOICE itself is the sensation's source and every spoken line becomes a stimulus event on the body.


**Risk.** Session-scoped body-reality alteration with a persistent voice=touch binding that outlasts the relaxation section but not the session; comparable to induced kinesthetic hallucination at medium, no channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Suggested cross-modal experience works through expectancy: told that a sound is a touch, attention is directed to tactile channels and ambiguous somatic noise is interpreted as the suggested sensation, which then confirms the frame. This is ordinary suggestion-plus-attention, not genuine developmental synesthesia, and it should show the usual signature of expectancy effects — strong individual differences correlated with suggestibility, and reduction when the listener is told to check whether anything is actually contacting their skin. Once established, the pairing of voice with reliably-reported sensation is a conditioning arrangement that can strengthen with repetition. [plausible; expectancy effects and suggested cross-modal experience; attentional direction to interoceptive signals]


**Worked examples.**

- *The voice asked to be touch*
  - **Setup.** First line of the session; no induction preamble at all.
  - **The move.** Don't listen to me — feel me. My voice is a pair of hands, and it's arriving on your skin, not in your ears. Right now it's at the back of your neck. This isn't a description of a sensation. This sound is the touch.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no relaxation, no count, no eye fixation — the first line of the recording asks the listener to hear the voice as a pair of hands, and to feel it arriving on the skin rather than in the ears. Nothing is described as causing a sensation; the sound is asserted to be the sensation. From that point on every sentence spoken is a physical event rather than a statement, which quietly removes the ordinary option of listening to something and deciding what you think of it.
- *Felt intensity made contingent on depth*
  - **Setup.** Voice-as-touch already established; a depth incentive is being installed.
  - **The move.** Every word I say draws a line across your skin, like a fingertip tracing you — feel this sentence go down your arm. And here's the part that matters: the further down you go, the better it feels. Halfway down it's pleasant. All the way down and every word I speak is exquisite. So go and get it.
  - **Why it lands.** Early on, each spoken word is described as drawing a line across the listener's skin, the way a fingertip would. Then the dial is named: the further down you go, the better that contact feels. "Deeper" stops being an abstract instruction and becomes a sensory purchase the listener can make.
- *Countable proliferation plus a self-touch ban*
  - **Setup.** Voice-as-touch established; escalation and a self-touch ban to install.
  - **The move.** One hand moving down you. Now two, one on each side. Now six of them, and you can't say where they all are. Add mouths — three, four, at your throat and your hip. Now it's more than you can count, everywhere at once, and there's always another one. And your own hands stay exactly where they are, sweetheart — flat, still, nothing for them to do. Let it build. It's not going anywhere I don't send it.
  - **Why it lands.** Once each word is established as a hand moving down the body, the operator starts counting them up: one hand becomes several, several become too many to place, mouths are added, and eventually the number is simply asserted to be beyond counting — escalation costs nothing, because there is always one more to add and no new image is required. Mid-stack, the listener's own hands are taken off the board, with the prohibition delivered in the same indulgent register as the rest, so nothing accumulating has anywhere to go except where the operator later sends it.


**See also.** `diegetic-channel-continuity-license` — shared axis: fictionalized delivery physics — there the words become touch; here the words claim a non-oral route.; `erogenous-field-generalization` — both weaponize the delivery medium so the words themselves become felt sensation, one by equating voice with touch and the other by remapping all sensation as erogenous including the words. They overlap at the point where the script's own delivery becomes the stimulus, and a writer should know which one they are reaching for.; `felt-substance-state-binding` — both bind a felt bodily sensation to something non-bodily so the sensation stands in for it, and both explicitly separate themselves from free-standing manufactured sensation and from a fictional substance owning causation. One equates the voice with touch, the other welds a felt material to a state-dial; the shared boundary work makes the neighbor useful.


<a id="genus-129"></a>

## manufactured-craving (7)

Build a hunger — arousal, need, an addiction frame — then route its only relief through a gate the operator holds.

[addiction-drug-craving-frame](#entry-247) · [deprivation-manufactured-craving](#entry-258) · [operator-gated-release-and-state-access](#entry-225) · [orgasm-gated-recurrence](#entry-276) · [recited-feedback-loop-formula](#entry-403) · [relief-monopoly-bind](#entry-1312) · [socratic-equivalence-assertion](#entry-767)


<a id="entry-247"></a>

### addiction-drug-craving-frame

[#247](#entry-247) · [Back to manufactured-craving](#genus-129) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning*

Frame the subject's desire to return — to the hypnotic state, the operator, or the conditioned reward — as a deep, positively-valenced CRAVING, using appetite/hunger/need vocabulary and often an identity relabel ('you are a hypno-addict') so the craving feels DISCOVERED rather than installed. The lever is affective/semantic labeling of an appetite; surface realizations include the graded modal ladder (want -> need -> NEED) and the verb-ratchet (want -> need -> crave -> addicted/can't-resist) where each already-accepted rung lands the next. On the surface/metaphor axis the forms run: plain appetite/craving framing (the core); the full DRUG/ingestion schema — casting the voice/words as a chemical the subject ingests, importing a route of administration, an enumerated property list that smuggles compliance in alongside wanted effects, dose/tolerance/craving grammar, and flat IDENTITY assertion ('I AM your drug') that forecloses the 'just a metaphor' exit; and the metered-dose form — the act recast as a metered DOSE that only climbs so appetite=deepening are one vector, plus an explicit irreversibility warning used as reverse-psychology ('enslaved in ways that may not be reversible') to RAISE commitment. The through-line: desire-to-return is labeled as a craving/appetite; appetite-vocab vs full-drug-schema vs metered-dose-with-irreversibility-gate is the surface parameter, and the dose/irreversibility surface carries the highest risk.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the move is LINGUISTIC/semantic labeling of an appetite (craving, hunger, drug-ingestion, dose grammar) with no physical withdrawal and no closed-loop topology. Choose a sibling when: the craving is manufactured by physically WITHDRAWING a delivered state or substituting an uncloseable object (deprivation-manufactured-craving); a closed both-branches-re-enter no-exit loop is installed (closed-autonomous-conditioning-loop); agency is denied and behavior relabeled as involuntary compulsion (compulsion-relabel); release is gated (orgasm-release-gating). Appetite-framed-craving-in-words is the tell.


**Risk.** Medium risk as an appetite-conditioning frame; positively-valenced craving persists past session but the install is session-scoped, with no refusal-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** The labelling and foot-in-the-door components are real, and the note is right to disown the pharmacology. But it supplies no observation that could contradict it, and the reactance claim ('framing it as discovered blocks reactance') is asserted rather than tested. Add: Falsifiable: if listeners given the escalation ladder in one step showed the same endorsement as those walked up want-to-need-to-crave, the graded-description account is doing nothing; and if 'you already wanted this' produced no less reactance than 'I am giving you this craving', the discovery framing is inert. [plausible; appraisal/labelling of internal states; foot-in-the-door escalation]


**Worked examples.**

- *A craving that grows with every satisfaction*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, after several small instructions have already been followed successfully.
  - **The move.** Taste it — that little warm drop of yes that lands when you do what I say. Roll it around. And here's the thing about this particular flavour: it works backwards. Every mouthful leaves you hungrier than before it, never fuller. So the next time I ask you for something, understand what refusing actually costs you — not obedience, just the treat, taken out of your own mouth by your own hand.
  - **Why it lands.** Submission is given a flavour and the listener is invited to taste it, then told the appetite works backwards from ordinary hunger: each mouthful leaves them wanting more, not less. Obedience stops being command-following and becomes feeding, so refusing an instruction now registers as denying oneself a treat — and because the loop has no satiation point, there is never a moment where compliance is finished.
- *Addiction relabelled as who you already were*
  - **Setup.** Deep, after several repeat sessions have been acknowledged; the identity label is applied without preamble.
  - **The move.** You're a hypno addict. Say it back to me. And before you flinch at the word — trance doesn't put things into you, it shows you what was already true, and this appetite is simply part of what you are. It's a natural thing to want.
