One stages perceptible events across several sense channels for a subject in session; the other back-loads the formal claim behind demonstrations for a reader. Useful to see the pattern is not specific to in-session work.


<a id="genus-280"></a>

## map-the-response-network (2)

Expose who actually reacts to whom in a group, then push the one node whose change ripples through the whole system.

[crisis-induction-live-readout](#entry-524) · [influence-topology-node-selection](#entry-529)


<a id="entry-524"></a>

### crisis-induction-live-readout

[#524](#entry-524) · [Back to map-the-response-network](#genus-280) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: operator-craft*

The operator deliberately names the group's most taboo material (even insulting a member) to detonate the habitual interaction sequence, then withholds all content engagement and observes, re-igniting with trigger mentions when it slows. The real, un-self-conscious sequence exposes who-triggers-whom that a polite session hides; fatigue and lowered later resistance are side effects, not the point.


**When to reach for this.** Operator stays a non-engaging igniter/observer harvesting a structural read-out - not arguing content, not running a covert-induction pretext, and not handling resistance: the provocation is diagnostic and resistance-lowering is only a byproduct. Sibling stage to influence-topology-node-selection, whose node choice the live read-out feeds.


**Risk.** Deliberate distress/taboo detonation in a live group; needs a host supplying entry/exit/aftercare.


**Why it works.** Emotional arousal narrows attention onto the immediate exchange (Easterbrook), which reduces the self-monitoring that normally supports impression management, so responding under provocation is less edited than responding under ordinary conditions. Note that the stronger claim — that unedited responding reveals the 'real' influence hierarchy — is not testable as stated: it requires an independent measure of who controls whom, and without one, any observed sequence can be read as confirming it. Falsifiable in the weak form only: coded self-presentational behaviors (hedging, self-correction, deference markers) should decrease under provocation relative to matched ordinary sessions. [plausible; disruption of over-learned routines; arousal-driven attentional narrowing reducing self-presentation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Detonate the group, then read it*
  - "I sit back and observe… If it starts to slow down, then I step in and kick it to get it going again." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `influence-topology-node-selection` — a real sibling pair: the provocation stage harvests a structural read-out of who responds to whom, and the node-selection stage routes a minimal change through the node that read-out identifies. One supplies the map the other consumes, so a reader of either needs the other.; `preparatory-diagnostic-read` — a specific probe and the general diagnostic surface it belongs to. Detonating a group's habitual sequence and then withholding engagement is an elicitation designed to harvest a structural read-out, with lowered resistance only a byproduct. The broader entry covers the shared discipline: the payoff lands in the operator's map and nothing is installed.


<a id="entry-529"></a>

### influence-topology-node-selection

[#529](#entry-529) · [Back to map-the-response-network](#genus-280) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Map who-responds-to-whom, then route a minimal change through the single node whose change propagates system-wide - deliberately avoiding the symptomatic member (easy to flip, but the system flips them back) and preferring the most tenacious member others actually respond to. The system then does most of the work and the change persists.


**When to reach for this.** Selection of the intervention NODE by influence-graph propagation and tenacity - not any particular change technique and not work with the presenting member; tell is deliberate non-symptomatic tenacious-node targeting. The graph is read and routed through, not restructured. Sibling stage to crisis-induction-live-readout, whose read-out supplies the map this move selects from.


**Risk.** Operator-side targeting decision; no direct consent surface of its own.


**Why it works.** In interacting systems, a change at a node with many inbound dependencies propagates further than an equal change at a peripheral node, and changes at peripheral nodes get reversed by the unchanged surrounding contingencies — the presenting member is peripheral in exactly this sense. Targeting the member others actually respond to means the surrounding people's behavior does the maintenance the operator would otherwise have to supply. Falsifiable: if change routed through high-influence nodes did not persist longer than matched change routed through the symptomatic member, the routing claim is wrong. [plausible; interlocking contingencies in social systems; network centrality of influence]


**Worked examples.**

- *Route change through the tenacious node*
  - "The person who has the symptoms will be the last one that you want to work with… the one who is really tenacious." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `crisis-induction-live-readout` — a real sibling pair: the provocation stage harvests a structural read-out of who responds to whom, and the node-selection stage routes a minimal change through the node that read-out identifies. One supplies the map the other consumes, so a reader of either needs the other.; `target-selection` — a planner scoping an intervention faces both questions and they are genuinely different levers: one operationalizes WHICH behavior to aim at by leverage, maintainability, or measurable dimension, the other picks WHICH person in an influence graph to route the change through so the surrounding system sustains it. Neither substitutes for the other.


<a id="genus-204"></a>

## match-then-lead (3)

Mirror the listener's ongoing experience, idiom, or sensory channel until your words read as their own, then bolt the steering onto that accepted stream.

[pace-the-symptom-idiom](#entry-1281) · [pacing-leading](#entry-1282) · [representational-system-matching](#entry-1284)


<a id="entry-1281"></a>

### pace-the-symptom-idiom

[#1281](#entry-1281) · [Back to match-then-lead](#genus-204) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: pacing-rapport*

Where ordinary pacing matches observable experience, this extreme-case move paces the subject's own symptomatic CODE — meeting the subject inside their pathological idiom rather than pressuring them out of it. Facing meaningless word-salad, the operator transcribes and studies it, learns to improvise word-salad of the same pattern in a different vocabulary, matches utterance lengths, intermixes nonsense, and converses entirely in the idiom until the subject himself requests sense — then titrates rational speech in proportionally while keeping a ritual bit of nonsense. Engagement is earned where demanding intelligibility failed for years, and the subject initiates the move toward shared language, so the lead is subject-led.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is that the paced surface is the subject's own symptom/channel (not observable ongoing experience or stated affect), sustained via a distinct record-study-reproduce-converse procedure until the subject asks for the shift. Distinguish from pacing-leading proper (paces observable/projectable present-tense experience and expects acceptance), and from validate-affect-then-presuppose (paces a stated affect then presupposes a new layer). Here the operator enters and sustains the symptomatic idiom itself, and the subject leads the exit.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible, no channel erosion; consistent with the low baseline for pacing and synchrony work generally. The subject initiates the lead, which lowers the coercion surface.


**Why it works.** Rapport depends on the listener perceiving that the other party is operating inside their own frame of reference, and matching a partner's communicative code raises perceived similarity and reduces the threat appraisal that drives withdrawal. Prediction: engagement rises when the operator adopts the subject's idiom and falls when intelligibility is demanded instead — a falsifiable claim, since a subject who withdraws further under matching would refute it. The subject-led exit is also self-perception at work: having initiated the request for sense, the subject reads the shift as their own choice and defends it accordingly. [plausible; similarity-attraction and interpersonal accommodation; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Answering the word-salad in its own form*
  - "could improvise a word-salad similar in pattern to George's, but utilizing a different vocabulary" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `representational-system-matching` — both calibrate the operator's own output to a surface the subject supplies — symptomatic idiom versus sensory-modality vocabulary. Adjacent members of the match-the-subject's-code family.


<a id="entry-1282"></a>

### pacing-leading

[#1282](#entry-1282) · [Back to match-then-lead](#genus-204) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: pacing-rapport*

The operator restricts utterances to statements the listener can confirm against present experience right now (timed observables, projectable low-specification descriptions, or near-universal trance states), so a stream of confirmed-true statements builds an accumulating agreement (a perceptual yes-set) that entrains attention and erodes the line between "this describes what is" and "this instructs what comes next." A not-yet-true target statement is then bolted onto the accepted run and inherits the borrowed truth-status; because nothing is denied, there is nothing clean to dispute, and a satisfied lead recycles as the next pace so the chain feeds itself. Variants ride the same lever: the target smuggled in by adjacency (agency-denial or interoceptive state-claim), the starting act pre-relabeled as the listener's own already-underway want, or the connecting word itself graded as a leverage dial — a bare temporal/contingency connective (as, when, after) that asserts no link and lets the listener author the causal bridge, climbing through "as … you will" to an overt "will make you," so the lead inherits truth-status in proportion to the connective's asserted force regardless of validity.


**When to reach for this.** The defining tell is a paced clause that is verifiably true in the moment (observable, projectable, or near-universal) grammatically or sequentially coupled to a lead the listener has not yet verified, such that agreement accrues with no single place to object. The connective-grade variant is still this move: the graded connecting word is the leverage instrument of the lead, not a separate family. Distinguish from attribution-capture (which misattributes the CAUSE of an already-occurring state to the operator rather than merely describing it truthfully), from expectation-seeding (which previews a future rather than banking present truths), and from self-validating language (which asserts unfalsifiable claims rather than checkable-true ones). Remove the live truth of the paced clause and the coupling breaks — it becomes bare narration or an ordinary command.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible, no channel erosion in the core move. The agency-denial and volition-relabel variants lean toward the refusal channel but stay adjacency-level, not a durable install.


**Why it works.** A run of verifiable statements establishes the speaker as a reliable source, and that credibility transfers to adjacent unverified claims. The unasserted connective ('as', 'when') exploits temporal contiguity as a cue to causality — people infer causal links from mere succession (Michotte; causal-illusion work) — and then treat self-generated inferences as more trustworthy than told ones. Note: this is causal illusion from contiguity, NOT illusory correlation, which concerns overestimated co-occurrence of distinctive events and does not apply here. Falsifiable: if a paced-then-lead sequence produced no more compliance than the lead delivered cold, or if inserting one verifiably false pace did not degrade acceptance, the account fails. [plausible; source credibility transfer; illusory correlation from contiguity; self-generation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *The connective as a leverage dial*
  - "not whether the logic of the statement is valid, but simply whether they constitute a successful link" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *A denial of agency smuggled into true claims*
  - **Setup.** Mid-induction, subject clearly under; the operator's voice has been the sole focus for several minutes.
  - **The move.** You're drifting a little. Your body feels lighter than the chair. My voice is the only thing holding you. This can't be stopped now. And you can hear each word landing softly, one after another.
  - **Why it lands.** Four of the five short sentences describe things the listener can check and will probably find true right now — the drifting, the floating, the sense of being held by the voice. The fifth, dropped in the same flat cadence with no extra emphasis, is that none of it can be stopped. It is the only clause in the run that is not verifiable, and it inherits its credibility from the neighbours it is packed against.
- *Checkable half coupled to the wanted half*
  - "You're sitting there, breathing, watching that spot (pacing) / becoming relaxed. (leading)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *A near-universal inner state asserted as known*
  - "You must be wondering now what will happen next" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `attention-as-evidence-loop` — both build acceptance from things the listener can check against present experience rather than from argument. One banks statements that are genuinely true right now and bolts an unverified claim onto the run; the other treats the listener's own continued act as accumulating proof of a state. A reader working on either will want the other's boundary.; `future-pacing` — genuine boundary: one projects an unverified effect forward by declaration, the other couples an unverified lead onto clauses the listener can confirm as true right now. A reader deciding between forecast and borrowed truth-status needs both.; `micro-ratification` — directly adjacent and already discriminated against each other: per-unit permissive confirmation of a response versus a chain of verifiably-true statements banking agreement for a not-yet-true lead. Confusable in any induction opening.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both bank verifiable present truths to build unrepudiable agreement; the split is whether the accepted material is the listener's own real acts read as state evidence or observable statements coupled to an unverified lead.


<a id="entry-1284"></a>

### representational-system-matching

[#1284](#entry-1284) · [Back to match-then-lead](#genus-204) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: pacing-rapport*

The operator treats the listener's spontaneous sensory word-choice (see/grasp/sounds; touch-words vs sight-words) as a live readout of which perceptual channel is running and how deep the subject is, then covertly recasts their own suggestions in that same channel. A suggestion phrased in the listener's own dominant sense-code needs no internal translation, so it registers as if it originated inside the listener rather than arriving from outside; because the matching is concealed and any invited channel-shift is indirect, it stays below notice and any shift feels self-authored, so it is not resisted. This is input-side rapport CALIBRATION — an operator-side read of the listener's active representational system feeding a covert channel-matched delivery — on which downstream sync moves ride.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is that the mirrored/read surface is specifically SENSORY-MODALITY vocabulary used as a channel index, and the matching is deliberately concealed to seed suggestion (not to signal comprehension). Distinguish from generic active-listening or paraphrase-back. Distinguish from pacing-leading, which banks checkable-true statements to lead; here the lever is speaking inside the listener's sense-code so suggestions register as self-originated. The gauge sub-form is a non-intrusive continuous READ that changes the operator's knowledge map, not the listener's present state.


**Risk.** Session-scoped covert rapport calibration; no durable install or channel erosion, consistent with the low baseline for pacing and synchrony work generally.


**Why it works.** Matching a partner's lexical and syntactic choices increases liking and cooperation, and this occurs whether or not the matching is noticed — the effect does not require awareness to work. Speaking in the listener's own recent vocabulary also lowers processing effort, and easily-processed statements are judged truer and more familiar than effortful ones. The specific NLP claim built into this technique — that word choice reliably indexes a stable dominant sensory channel — is NOT supported; attempts to validate preferred-representational-system matching have not replicated, so the working mechanism is probably generic lexical mimicry and fluency, not channel-matching. [plausible; linguistic alignment/chameleon effect and processing fluency; PRS matching itself is unsupported]


**Worked examples.**

- *Predicates read as a live depth gauge*
  - "Huxley's choice of predicates ... shows that he is in a transition state between his primary representational system - kinesthetic ... and the representational system for the experience indirectly requested by Erickson - visual" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Suggestions recast in the listener's sense-code*
  - "this most highly valued system can be identified quickly by listening to the predicates (adjectives, adverbs, verbs)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `cross-modal-channel-bridge` — both work on perceptual-channel selection, but from opposite sides: one brings a dormant channel online by riding a shared feature of an already-vivid channel, the other reads which channel the listener is already using and covertly phrases suggestions inside it. Useful adjacency when classifying modality-aware delivery.; `operator-delivery-craft` — sensory-channel matching is a delivery-side craft move that shapes the operator's own transmitted signal, and both hinge on concealment of the operator-side adjustment. A reader cataloguing operator-output technique will reasonably wonder whether one subsumes the other; it does not, because one reads the listener's channel first.; `own-language-echo-reframe-durability` — both reuse the subject's own words back at them and both aim at suggestions registering as self-originated. The split is what surface is harvested and to what end: exact intention-terms reused to keep a reframe from flipping, versus sensory-modality vocabulary read as a channel index and matched covertly. Easy to conflate without the link.; `pace-the-symptom-idiom` — both calibrate the operator's own output to a surface the subject supplies — symptomatic idiom versus sensory-modality vocabulary. Adjacent members of the match-the-subject's-code family.; `valued-channel-induction` — both read the subject's sensory channel and speak inside it, but one selects the channel to make task execution itself the induction entry, while the other is continuous covert delivery calibration during suggestion. Genuinely easy to confuse; the cross-reference earns its place.


<a id="genus-231"></a>

## memory-hosted-triggers (3)

Plant the payload inside the listener's own real memories so remembering — even unprompted — re-fires it with the memory's borrowed realness.

[anchor-overloading](#entry-1290) · [autobiographical-memory-anchor](#entry-824) · [memory-graft-trigger-install](#entry-53)


<a id="entry-1290"></a>

### anchor-overloading

[#1290](#entry-1290) · [Back to memory-hosted-triggers](#genus-231) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers*

An already-live, previously-conditioned anchor is re-keyed so it now ALSO carries a new response (double-charging) or has its meaning overwritten wholesale, rather than a fresh cue being installed. Because the new payload rides on an existing conditioned response, no fresh anchor work is needed and the change reaches RETROACTIVELY: every prior encounter with the anchor (past recordings, or the pre-accepted self-label) now carries the new payload. The re-keying is typically bound at a high-salience moment (peak arousal, self-vocalization) and may widen the anchor's firing surface (audio -> 'speak or write').


**When to reach for this.** Re-keys or overwrites an ASSUMED-ALREADY-LIVE anchor so it fires a new/changed response, with retroactive reach across prior material — not a fresh install. The tell is 'this word you already respond to now also/instead does X, backward across everything.'


**Risk.** Retroactive catalog-wide reach means the listener's whole prior library silently gains the new payload (one member), and another binds it at orgasm to overwrite a self-label — durable and hard to isolate, warranting medium; the retroactive/backward reach is a bounding consideration.


**Why it works.** The conditioning half is backwards: a cue with a long prior training history is generally SLOWER, not faster, to acquire a new association (learned irrelevance, and blocking-adjacent retardation effects) — 'acquired salience carries over' describes acquired distinctiveness within a discrimination and does not license the general claim that re-keying an established cue beats conditioning a fresh one. What plausibly does the work is that the cue already reliably captures attention and is already embedded in the subject's routine, so re-pairing opportunities are frequent. The memory half stands: re-encoding at retrieval means prior episodes involving the cue are recalled through its current meaning, so past encounters feel as though they always carried it. Falsifiable: if prior episodes were recalled with original valence intact, the memory account is wrong. [plausible; acquired salience of established CS; memory reconsolidation / retrieval-dependent re-encoding]


**Worked examples.**

- *An existing trigger declared double-charged*
  - **Setup.** At the floor of a long descent; the cue word already functions as a drop trigger from prior sessions.
  - **The move.** You already know what that word does to you. From this moment it carries a second thing as well: it still drops you, and now it floods you with devotion at the same instant — and it doesn't matter whether you hear it or read it. Spoken to you, typed to you, either one throws it, and every recording of mine you've ever played now does this to you too.
  - **Why it lands.** The word was already a drop-cue from earlier recordings; nothing new is installed here. At the floor of the descent the operator simply announces that the old cue now carries a second load — it still drops you, and from this moment it also floods you with devotion — and then repeats the announcement a few minutes later so it brackets the deepest point. One clause widens the firing surface past audio: spoken or written, so a chat message or a caption counts. Because the payload rides an already-conditioned response, the change reaches backward: every earlier recording in the catalog, replayed tomorrow, now delivers the new feeling too.
- *Self-chanted equation overwrites a praise label*
  - **Setup.** At peak arousal; the subject already answers warmly to an established praise-label.
  - **The move.** Say it out loud for me, in your own voice, over and over: good girl means toy. Good girl means toy. Keep going. From now on that word doesn't just feel nice when you hear it — it brings you straight back here and leaves you wanting to be used.
  - **Why it lands.** At the peak, the listener is told to say the equation out loud, over and over, in her own voice — the praise-name she already answers to set equal to an object-name she does not. The operator then closes it: from now on that same familiar praise-word doesn't just feel nice, it returns her here and leaves her wanting to be used. Nothing new was anchored; the label she had already accepted was quietly reloaded with different contents.


**Realizations** (1): `live-trigger-redefinition`


**See also.** `bundle-install-single-anchor` — both load a payload onto a single anchor and both define themselves against composing separate pre-installed cues, so they are direct competitors at classification. The split is the anchor's status: one authors a multi-effect bundle onto a freshly minted cue in a single pass, the other re-keys a cue the listener already responds to, which is what gives it retroactive reach across prior material.; `covert-nonverbal-anchor` — sequencing relation worth surfacing: one installs a conditioned link by unannounced pairing with no declarative instruction, and the other presupposes an already-live anchor and re-keys or overwrites it, reaching backward across everything that used the cue before. The covert install supplies exactly the precondition the overload assumes.; `state-capture-anchor` — both operate on an anchor that already exists rather than installing a fresh cue: one captures a spontaneous live state onto a new re-pressable handle, the other re-keys an already-conditioned cue so it carries a new payload backward across prior material. Worth cross-reading when deciding what an anchor operation is doing.


<a id="entry-824"></a>

### autobiographical-memory-anchor

[#824](#entry-824) · [Back to memory-hosted-triggers](#genus-231) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: persistence*

Binds the program to an INTERNAL memory the operator does NOT control and the listener cannot easily disown, so every future unprompted resurfacing of that memory becomes a reactivation site — far longer reach than an operator-word, which fades with non-use. The realizations differ only on WHICH memory: (a) a specific REAL fond memory the listener already owns, into which a narrated binding ceremony staples the payload; (b) an imagined ongoing daily practice re-attributed as lived memory; (c) the memory of THIS session itself — recall of the trance is deliberately PRESERVED and sharpened (amnesia explicitly avoided) so merely reminiscing about it re-triggers the pleasure and the memory itself becomes a self-administering arousal source, often paired with an instant re-entry-to-depth shortcut. All share one lever: the carrier is an internal, listener-owned memory whose spontaneous unprompted recall is the reactivation cue.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for THIS when the carrier is an internal autobiographical memory the operator does NOT control — a REAL fond memory, an imagined practice re-read as remembered, or THIS session's memory kept deliberately vivid — and the reactivation cue is spontaneous unprompted recall (or reminiscence firing arousal). Choose a sibling technique instead when the past being sourced NEVER HAPPENED and is supplied by imagination to manufacture a conditioning history; when the real memory is OVERWRITTEN by a false replacement (here the real memory stays intact and a trigger is stapled in); when the carrier is an external owned object; or when a discrete operator-controlled cue fires the state. The tell: the listener's own past is the carrier, and its unprompted return is the trigger.


**Risk.** Weaponizing an authentic personal memory gives large, un-scoped, years-long reach via unprompted recall that the operator cannot revoke — durable identity/autobiography scope + out-of-session reach set high.


**Why it works.** Autobiographical memories are self-referential and cue-rich, so they are retrieved spontaneously and often, giving anything bound to them repeated unscheduled reactivation — that alone predicts better persistence than an arbitrary operator word. Drop the reconsolidation appeal: that literature concerns destabilization and modification of an existing trace, not grafting new semantic content onto a memory during recall, so it does not license the 'attaches rather than sits alongside' claim. Falsifiable: if payloads bound to autobiographical memories decayed at the same rate as those bound to arbitrary cues, the persistence claim fails. [plausible; cue-dependent retrieval and self-reference effect; memory reconsolidation at retrieval]


**Worked examples.**

- *The payload folded into a real cherished memory*
  - **Setup.** Subject is deep and has been walked into an imagined room of their own memories.
  - **The move.** Pull one out — a real one, a good one, something of yours I've never touched. Be in it. Hear what you heard, see who was there, stay until it's as bright as the day it happened. Now I'm going to step into it with you, and I have a paper in my hand. Read it, and sign it — good. I'm folding it small and tucking it right into the middle of that memory, and now we close the memory up and put it back on the shelf. Every time that memory comes back to you on its own — driving, falling asleep, out of nowhere — the paper is in there with it, and you'll feel this.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is walked into an imagined store of their own memories and asked to bring up one particular real one — a good one, specific, theirs — and to live in it again until it is vivid. Then the operator steps into the scene, produces a written agreement, has it signed, and tucks it inside the memory before shutting the memory away again. The binding is narrated as a procedure rather than asserted, because the engagement is what makes it stick. What has been chosen as the trigger is not a word the operator can wear out by overuse; it is something the listener will recall unprompted, at random, for years, and each of those moments is now a scheduled reactivation.
- *An imagined daily practice recalled as lived*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session in a series; the object and the daily habit have never actually been given to the subject.
  - **The move.** And your little book — the one you were given at the beginning, the one on your nightstand. You've been good about it, haven't you. One mark every evening before you sleep, every single evening, no gaps. That's how many nights of this you've done now. Think about how the page looks.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator refers, in passing, to a physical object the listener supposedly received at the start and to the small daily act performed with it — one mark made each evening, without fail. The habit is described rather than requested, so the listener's imagination fills in the routine, and an invented practice arrives already wearing the texture of something remembered.


**Realizations** (1): `anti-amnesia-recall-trigger`


**See also.** `attention-anchor-portable-internalization` — both bind to internal material the listener cannot disown, and the pair turns on provenance: operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own imagery versus a genuinely listener-owned memory the operator does not control. That contrast is the useful discrimination for anyone reaching for either.; `irreversible-autobiographical-binding-act` — both make the listener's own autobiographical record the carrier. A staples a payload onto a memory the operator does not control, so unprompted recall reactivates it; B manufactures the memory by having the listener perform an irreversible physical act that cannot later be denied. Read together they cover harvesting an existing memory versus creating one.; `manufactured-conditioning-history` — both make the listener's past the carrier, split on whether that past is real. One staples the payload to a genuine autobiographical memory the operator does not control, so unprompted recall reactivates it; the other asserts a conditioning history that never occurred and has the listener supply it by imagination. Real-memory carrier versus counterfactual sourcing.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — two carriers for the same operator-absent reactivation problem, differing in what the state is bound to: an external owned object encountered in daily life, versus an internal autobiographical memory whose spontaneous unprompted recall the operator cannot control or withdraw.; `recruited-autobiography-deepener` — both recruit the listener's own autobiography as the carrier, so the operator cannot be contradicted without the listener denying their own past. The split is function: one anchors a payload to a memory so unprompted recall reactivates it later, the other spends recognized memories as in-session depth fuel. Reader needs the axis.


<a id="entry-53"></a>

### memory-graft-trigger-install

[#53](#entry-53) · [Back to memory-hosted-triggers](#genus-231) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Harvests a real autobiographical memory at amplified affect (a proud/motivated moment re-embodied), then EDITS that preserved memory by inserting a fabricated sensory detail ("you were wearing sexy panties") and binds a trigger/mantra to the grafted detail. Because the host memory is genuinely the listener's own, the trigger inherits the memory's motivational charge and felt realness — the listener's own evidence-of-self ("I really was motivated") is hijacked as proof-of-trigger and cannot reliably be distinguished from the graft. The load-bearing move is editing the contents of an EXISTING memory to serve as a self-authenticating anchor host (a wearable-object trigger the listener can self-fire by putting the garment on).


**When to reach for this.** The real memory is PRESERVED and a counterfactual detail is grafted INTO it. Screen memory, by contrast, replaces access to a real memory; ordinary trigger anchoring layers an anchor on top of an unmodified evoked state. Here the memory itself is edited so the anchor borrows autobiographical authenticity.


**Risk.** Edits the contents of a real autobiographical memory and installs a self-firing out-of-session trigger that borrows the memory's realness, corrupting the subject's ability to distinguish genuine recall from the graft.


**Why it works.** Memories are not replayed but reconstructed at retrieval, and reconstruction incorporates post-event information — the misinformation effect shows that details introduced after the fact get absorbed into the recollection and are subsequently reported with the same confidence as genuine ones. Grafting onto a high-affect autobiographical memory exploits a second known bias: emotional intensity and vividness are used as heuristics for accuracy, so the host's genuine charge licenses the inserted detail. The wearable object then functions as an ordinary retrieval and conditioning cue with an unusually strong associate. Falsifiable: subjects should later report the fabricated detail as part of the original memory at rates well above baseline, and should be unable to discriminate it from genuine details at better than chance; reliable discrimination would falsify the graft account. [established; reconstructive memory / misinformation effect; vividness-as-accuracy heuristic]


**Worked examples.**

- *Fabricated detail grafted into a real proud memory*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, subject already regressed into a real memory of a day they felt driven and capable, affect turned up.
  - **The move.** You're back in that day, in your own body, and you can feel exactly how sharp and unstoppable you were. Now notice one more thing you'd forgotten: under your clothes, that day, you were wearing your black lace panties. That's where it came from. Say it with me — "lace on, drive on." Every time you feel that lace against your skin, you say it, and the whole of that day comes back with it.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is walked back into a genuine memory of a day they felt driven, re-inhabited from the inside, with the feeling turned up. Then one edit is requested: remember that a particular garment was being worn that day. A short phrase pairing that garment with the drive is repeated, and the listener is told to say it whenever they feel the fabric. Because the host memory really is theirs, the garment inherits its charge and its felt authenticity — the listener's own proof that they were motivated now stands as proof the cue works, and the edit is not separable from the original.


**See also.** `fabricated-forgetting-priming` — both exploit autobiographical memory's authority to authenticate installed content, but one grafts a counterfactual detail into a preserved real memory as an anchor host while the other manufactures forgetting of content that was never there so a later install reads as recollection.; `fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal` — both route a trigger install through autobiographical memory instead of direct suggestion, but one grafts a false detail into a preserved real memory so the anchor borrows that memory's authenticity, while the other fabricates whole memories whose only cargo is repeated rehearsal of the cue-response shape.; `fabricated-recovered-memory-retrieval` — sharp contrast within fabricated memory work: constructing a whole memory and framing it as recovered, versus preserving a real memory and grafting a counterfactual detail into it so an anchor borrows its authenticity.


<a id="genus-295"></a>

## mirror-motion-coupling (2)

The listener's real movement is locked to an imagined or narrated body's movement so proprioception and fantasy reinforce each other.

[narrated-motion-entrainment](#entry-1204) · [pace-mirror-agency-proof](#entry-948)


<a id="entry-1204"></a>

### narrated-motion-entrainment

[#1204](#entry-1204) · [Back to mirror-motion-coupling](#genus-295) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: immersion*

The listener's mandated physical movement mirrors the operator's narrated movement, collapsing watching/being-watched and moving/being-moved into one channel so proprioceptive output and visual fantasy reinforce each other; the deepener simultaneously does the eroticization work.


**When to reach for this.** Entrainment to a NARRATED body in fantasy, fusing visual and proprioceptive channels — vs kinesthetic entrainment to a rhythm (no fantasy-body mirror), and vs pace-mirror-agency-proof (direction reversed: the imagined figure mirrors the listener to manufacture felt control).


**Risk.** Session-scoped deepener/eroticization, no consent surface (member fingerprint).


**Why it works.** Imagery that is congruent with concurrent motor output is easier to sustain than imagery that competes with it — self-generated movement supplies proprioceptive feedback matching the narrated scene, removing the mismatch signal that normally marks an image as merely imagined. Enacted imagery is also better remembered and rated more vivid than passively visualized imagery (the enactment effect), so the fantasy accrues the phenomenal weight of something done rather than pictured. Falsifiable: if listeners instructed to move in the narrated pattern report no higher vividness or absorption than listeners told to stay still while hearing identical narration, the account fails. [plausible; enactment effect; motor-imagery congruence and proprioceptive feedback]


**Worked examples.**

- *Listener's body mirrors the narrated body*
  - **Setup.** Listener physically able to move and has agreed to follow motion instructions; trance light to medium.
  - **The move.** I'm lifting my hand off my thigh — slowly, up to my collarbone, hold — and settling it back down. You do it with me, same speed, in time with my voice. Up. Hold. Down. That's one, and one is a step lower. Up. Hold. Down. Two. Your arm knows exactly where mine is, because it's in the same place. Ten of these and you'll be as far down as I want you.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator narrates a slow deliberate motion of her own body — the lift, the pause, the settling — and has the listener carry out the same motion in time with the words. Each completed cycle is declared another step down, the count of repetitions standing in for a depth gauge. Because the listener is both watching the described body and producing the movement themselves, the felt position of their own limbs keeps ratifying the imagined one, and the same repetition that deepens is the repetition that arouses.


**See also.** `exercise-masked-cadence-induction` — both fuse real proprioceptive output with the voice's pacing so the body's own motion confirms the verbal frame. One mirrors a narrated fantasy body, the other hides the cadence inside real exercise motion. Same channel-fusion lever at different degrees of disguise.


<a id="entry-948"></a>

### pace-mirror-agency-proof

[#948](#entry-948) · [Back to mirror-motion-coupling](#genus-295) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: convincers*

An imagined figure mirrors the listener's real motion bidirectionally (he strokes slow, she thrusts slow; he speeds up, she speeds up), manufacturing felt causal control over her depicted pleasure BEFORE any doctrine is stated, so the later assertion ("your purpose is to please women") lands as confirmation of already-observed evidence rather than a new command; the gating logic is installed somatically.


**When to reach for this.** Evidence is manufactured pre-doctrine via the mirror loop — unlike narrated-motion-entrainment, where the listener is entrained to the operator's narrated motion for absorption, and unlike overt behavioral-commitment moves, where the subject knowingly performs a commitment act rather than having proof covertly manufactured.


**Risk.** Covertly manufactures confirming evidence for an identity doctrine (purpose is to please women) — self-sealing proof, delivery session-bounded.


**Why it works.** This manufactures an illusion of control through contingency detection: when an external event reliably covaries with one's own action, people infer causal agency, and the inference is strongest when the covariation is immediate and bidirectional. Because the evidence is installed before the doctrine is stated, the doctrine is evaluated as an explanation for something already believed rather than as a claim needing support — order matters, since prior belief biases evaluation of later evidence. Falsifiable — if the doctrine were accepted equally when stated before the mirror loop rather than after it, the pre-evidence sequencing would not be load-bearing. [plausible; illusion of control from action-outcome contingency; belief-consistent evaluation of later claims]


**Worked examples.**

- *A mirrored figure that follows your own pace*
  - **Setup.** Listener already stroking at their own pace; the imagined partner has just been introduced and no doctrine about purpose has been stated yet.
  - **The move.** She's on top of you, and she moves at exactly the speed your hand moves. Slow your hand right down — feel her sink into a long slow grind, hear her breath stretch out. Now speed up. She's speeding up with you, her thighs tightening, that catch in her throat, faster because you went faster. Every bit of that is you doing it.
  - **Why it lands.** An imagined partner is introduced who does exactly what the listener's own hand does: slow down and she slows, speed up and she speeds up, with the narration reporting her state back each time as though observing it. Nothing is claimed and no doctrine is stated — the listener simply spends several minutes watching a woman's pleasure track their own tempo in both directions, which is what makes it read as a loop rather than as narration. Twenty lines later, when the operator says the listener's purpose is to give women pleasure, it does not arrive as an instruction to accept; it arrives as the name for something they have just spent five minutes observing.


**See also.** `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both read evidence back to the listener as proof about themselves, and the contrast is the tell: in one the listener knowingly performs an operator-supplied act that is then read as self-evidence; in the other the proof is manufactured covertly through a mirroring loop before any claim is stated. Performed commitment versus covert pre-doctrine evidence.; `compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting` — both manufacture first-person experiential evidence before the doctrine it will be used to prove, so the later assertion reads as confirmation. The vehicles differ (a deferred callback to an obeyed instruction versus a mirrored-motion loop) but the ordering trick is the same family.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both manufacture evidence that a state or role is already true before the doctrine is stated, and both work by the listener reading the proof as their own. They differ on whether the cited acts are real behavior openly annotated or a fabricated mirror loop, which is the call a reader has to make.; `somatic-mirroring` — both manufacture proof from something the body is actually doing rather than from an operator assertion. One reinterprets an already-present sensation as evidence of the theme; the other sets up a mirroring loop so the listener observes apparent causal control before any claim is made. Reused percept versus staged pre-doctrine evidence.


<a id="genus-226"></a>

## more-channels-than-attention (3)

Runs two or more authored streams at once — decoy plus payload, or braided below the sentence — so the listener cannot attend to one without absorbing the others.

[capacity-saturation-overload](#entry-173) · [concurrent-dual-stream-delivery](#entry-180) · [multi-channel-braiding](#entry-943)


<a id="entry-173"></a>

### capacity-saturation-overload

[#173](#entry-173) · [Back to more-channels-than-attention](#genus-226) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

Imposes more concurrent processing demand than working memory and the executive monitor can carry, so the auditing faculty is saturated or displaced onto the load and suggestions arrive unevaluated; the felt lapse (blankness, attention thrash, grasping) is read as trance. The load itself is the induction — no relaxation trajectory required, and several forms are self-applicable. Realizations of the one exceed-the-processing-budget lever: (a) concurrent-demand overload — a dual-task split on the speech signal (track consonants vs meaning), serially stacked imagined sensory channels, simultaneous interpersonal tasks, self-run visual bookkeeping, escalating spoken-production drills, a one-shot cross-channel sense inversion, or sustained meter that captures the budget; (b) perceptual/null-task saturation — the channel is given more than it can label (peripheral-field flooding via wide unfocused gaze) or a task that consumes working memory while yielding nothing (recursive riffing on a null concept the listener must keep re-emptying), so the verbal track stops for lack of spare capacity; (c) imagined-task occupation — a fully-committed imagined activity is installed as the primary task, saturating attentional bandwidth so incoming somatic signals lose the channel to register (able to flip percept valence: foul gas experienced as flowers); (d) continuous-morph occupation — a single referent is morphed WITHOUT a hard cut ('maybe it becomes...'), keeping the imagination perpetually generating fresh imagery so the evaluator never settles on one frame long enough to judge it (a comparative ratchet sells each state as a downgradeable floor).


**When to reach for this.** The lever is processing CAPACITY: concurrent, captured, or flooded demand starves evaluation — the listener is kept BUSY. Choose it OVER irresolvable-input confusion (86) — there content cannot be RESOLVED (paradox/broken-grammar/impossible-image); here every element is individually resolvable but too voluminous, null, or perpetually-updating to leave spare capacity (load, not paradox). vs pattern-interrupt (190) — that is a one-shot break; here the load is SUSTAINED. vs cognitive-quieting (80) — release vs load: quieting lets thought depart, saturation gives the channel more than it can process. vs fixation (29) — narrowing to ONE focus vs MULTIPLYING or flooding demand. Absorbed decode-tells: concurrent-demand overload (stacked/dual tasks) vs perceptual-or-null-task saturation (flood the field / occupy with a null task) vs imagined-task occupation (a committed imagined task crowds out somatic input, can flip valence) vs continuous-morph occupation (morph-without-cut outruns the evaluator) are the realizations of THIS entry.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible deepener; broadening to multi-channel and self-run loads adds no durable scope or consent surface.


**Why it works.** Working memory has a small, hard capacity limit, and evaluating a claim for truth is itself a capacity-demanding secondary operation — comprehension is comparatively automatic, while rejection requires an additional effortful step. Loading the system therefore degrades scrutiny disproportionately: under concurrent demand people accept propositions they would otherwise reject, a well-replicated finding. The felt blankness or grasping is a real consequence of exceeded capacity, though calling that sensation trance is an interpretive label the subject is supplied rather than an independent phenomenon. Falsifiable: acceptance of suggestions should scale with measured concurrent load, and drop when the load is removed while all else is held constant. [established; working-memory capacity limits; effortful rejection of comprehended propositions under load]


**Worked examples.**

- *Stacked imagined channels held at once*
  - **Setup.** Opening of an induction with no relaxation phase; subject alert, first channel about to be introduced.
  - **The move.** Feel the warmth on the back of your right hand — hold it there. Now count under your breath, one two three, and keep the warmth. Now add a weight across your shoulders, pressing down, and keep counting, and keep the warmth. There's a low tone at the edge of your hearing — find it, hold all four, and now stop thinking.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no relaxation phase at all. The operator introduces one imagined channel at a time — a temperature on the skin, then a slow count under the breath, then a weight settling across the shoulders, then a sound held just at the edge of hearing — and never releases any of the earlier ones. Inside a short span the listener is being asked to hold several imagined sensations concurrently along with a cue word. The stack is the induction, and when the abrupt instruction to stop thinking arrives it lands on a field with nothing left over.
- *Attend to the sounds, not the meaning*
  - **Setup.** Early; you are assigning a perceptual task before any content is delivered.
  - **The move.** Don't listen to what I'm saying. Listen to the consonants only — the t's and the k's and the s's — and let the vowels and the meaning go past. Good. Now the opposite: vowels only. Notice you can hear me speaking without any of it turning into sense. That's the thing working.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is instructed to track only the consonants in the speech stream and to let the vowels and the sense of it go; later, only the vowels; later still, to separate out and follow more than one voice at once. These are genuine perceptual jobs, hard enough to occupy and easy enough not to abandon. While the conscious mind is running the filter, the words still arrive at the layer that understands them — with the gate unattended, and with the odd experience of hearing speech without parsing it doubling as proof that something is working.
- *Spoken drills sped up until output collapses*
  - **Setup.** Call-and-response drill has been running at a comfortable pace for several rounds.
  - **The move.** Say them back with me: soft, warm, open. Again, quicker — soft, warm, open. Faster — warm, open, soft, open, soft, warm. Now one in each ear, both at once: soft — warm — heavy — open — go. Good girl. Just the sounds now, don't bother with the words.
  - **Why it lands.** The word blocks the listener has to speak back are run, then explicitly sped up, then quietly reordered so rote autopilot cannot carry them, then split into two cues arriving at once from different sides. The demand is on production, not just attention, so failure is audible. The drill ends where it was always going: filler syllables, then nothing.
- *Sustained metre absorbing the whole budget*
  - **Setup.** Whole descent is delivered in metered rhyming couplets; nowhere drops into prose.
  - **The move.** Down and down and down you go, the counting slow, the counting slow. And nothing in you says me no, and nothing in you wants it slow.
  - **Why it lands.** The whole descent is written in metered rhyming couplets and never once drops into prose. The listener's processing goes to the cadence — anticipating the rhyme, riding the beat — while claims about being emptied and unable to push back arrive on the second line of each pair. A single paragraph of plain speech would re-engage scrutiny; the form holds without a break, and the form is the induction.


**Realizations** (4): `attentional-saturation-quieting`, `continuous-morph-chain`, `engrossment-analgesia`, `working-memory-channel-saturation`


**See also.** `adverse-attentional-state-recruitment` — adjacent inductions that are genuinely confusable when the listener presents as strained or effortful. The test is whether anything new is imposed: one RELABELS the attentional posture already present (drift or strain) so no failure-state remains as an exit excuse; the other IMPOSES concurrent or flooded demand beyond the processing budget. The effort-recruitment pole sits closest to the load form, which is why the pointer earns its place.; `cognitive-quieting` — relation=contrasts_with; load-vs-release axis; `covert-linguistic-delivery` — siblings under the Bandler-Grinder limited-capacity principle.; `engineered-failure-harvest` — overload frequently supplies the raw material the failure-harvest cashes: a task engineered to exceed capacity produces the genuine tracking failure that is then rebranded as the target. Useful pointer for anyone building either, and the boundary is which half is load-bearing.; `in-trance-load-release-oscillation` — the load pole of the oscillation is exactly the capacity-saturation lever; the difference is that one uses sustained load as the induction while the other alternates load against a blankness reward to make each cycle a depth increment. A reader building either will want the other.; `withheld-completion-dependency` — the saturation front-end is literally shared — a rapid stream of attentional demands. They diverge at the payload: one keeps starving the evaluator with sustained load, the other switches to withholding the next pointer so the subject leans in and waits to be directed. Worth the link because the second is best understood as the first repurposed.


<a id="entry-180"></a>

### concurrent-dual-stream-delivery

[#180](#entry-180) · [Back to more-channels-than-attention](#genus-226) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

Two separately-authored streams run at once so one carries the conscious mind's attention — a complex-syntax ear, a foreground countdown track, an assigned read-in-mind text, engaging-but-irrelevant ideas — while the other delivers payload beneath evaluation: a child-grammar ear, a background breath/suggestion loop, un-attended audio granted explicit dispensation to be absorbed, or therapeutic suggestions threaded alongside. The decoy channel may itself be authored payload, making the install dual-channel; words consciously caught from the payload stream feel involuntary and authoritative.


**When to reach for this.** Two authored carriers with decoy and payload roles in the same perceptual field — versus analogical-marking-parallel-message (one carrier split into surface plus marked code) and versus working-memory-overload-induction (one attention field loaded, no second authored payload stream). Production-format concurrency (stereo two-track playback) counts: the delivery topology, not the linguistics, is the move.


**Risk.** Payload installs below evaluation by design and caught words feel involuntary (one member); session-scoped with no refusal-channel erosion, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Counterarguing is effortful and competes for the same limited attentional and working-memory resources as tracking a demanding foreground stream, so a message received while the listener is occupied elsewhere meets less refutation than the same message received attentively — the classic distraction effect on persuasion. The claim that the second stream is nonetheless encoded well enough to influence later behavior is the load-bearing and weaker half: unattended-channel processing is real but shallow, and semantic uptake from a genuinely unattended stream is far more limited than practitioners assume. Predicts that if the decoy stream is removed, resistance to the payload should increase; if the payload stream is made fully unattended, its uptake should drop rather than rise. [plausible; distraction reduces counterarguing; limited semantic processing of unattended channels]


**Worked examples.**

- *A reading task as the licensed decoy*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, audio still running; the subject has a printed block of text in front of them and is settled enough to read.
  - **The move.** Take the page in front of you and start reading it to yourself, word by word, silently, at whatever pace feels natural — first line to last, then start again from the top. Don't try to listen to my voice while you do that; you don't need to, and honestly you can't do both properly anyway. The part of you underneath the reading takes in every word I say without any effort from you at all, so just give the reading everything you've got and let me handle the rest.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is given a block of text to read word by word in their head, and told plainly not to attend to the audio still playing — the deeper mind will take that in by itself, no effort required. The bypass is thereby licensed rather than smuggled. Both channels are the operator's writing, so the decoy is a payload too, and whichever spoken words the listener does catch arrive feeling involuntary and therefore authoritative.
- *Two tracks written to play at once*
  - **Setup.** Opening seconds of a two-track recording; the production note is delivered before any suggestion, and both tracks start together.
  - **The move.** What you are about to hear is two separate recordings playing at the same time — not one after the other, both at once. On the left you'll get my count and the pictures I want you to build; on the right there's a second voice that just keeps time with your breathing and never stops. Don't try to sort them out or pick one; put the headphones on properly and let both of them run straight through you.
  - **Why it lands.** The script opens with a production note rather than a suggestion: what follows is two separate tracks, meant to be heard at the same time and not in sequence. One carries the structured countdown and the imagery; the other runs a continuous breath-and-relaxation loop underneath it. No single linguistic thread can be followed to the end, and the material on the lower track lands without ever having been evaluated. Here the delivery format is the technique — there is no verbal trick to point at.
- *Two operators, one ear each*
  - "the double induction - an induction in which each of us speaks simultaneously into the client's [ears]" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `channel-partitioned-monitoring` — two descriptions of the same topology from different sides. One notes two authored streams in one perceptual field, a decoy carrying attention while the other carries payload; the other partitions across cognitive levels so output emerges on a level no monitor owns, including a variant that occupies one level with a decoy task. Check both when a decoy and a payload run concurrently.; `convergent-multichannel-encoding` — both are delivery-topology moves rather than linguistic content moves, but one runs two separately-authored streams with distinct decoy and payload roles, while the other runs many covert channels under a single tracked surface all carrying the same message redundantly.; `covert-linguistic-delivery` — both route payload past conscious audit, and each already draws the boundary against the other: two concurrently authored carriers with decoy and payload roles versus one carrier whose surface form hides the payload. A reader choosing between them needs the carrier-count test, so the cross-reference earns its place.; `hostile-environment-channel-conversion` — both run a second audible stream alongside the primary one. The distinguishing question is what the second stream does: carry a concealed payload beneath a decoy, or box in attention so it can be reassigned. A reader designing a two-channel piece needs to see the fork.; `register-camouflaged-delivery` — both hide payload in the perceptual field, but the dual-stream form requires two concurrently authored carriers with decoy and payload roles, while camouflage needs only one unmonitored register — remove the concealment and the camouflage move dies, whereas the dual-stream move still has two tracks.; `two-channel-relational-delivery` — both run two simultaneous authored tracks with the real install underneath, but one splits by perceptual channel with a decoy occupying attention, while the other splits by dramatized relation (dialogue, teacher, watched surrogate) so identification rather than distraction licenses the payload.


<a id="entry-943"></a>

### multi-channel-braiding

[#943](#entry-943) · [Back to more-channels-than-attention](#genus-226) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: carrier-binding*

An authored delivery architecture that interleaves two or more distinct channels BELOW the natural unit boundary (sentence / line / turn / modality) so the listener cannot attend to one without absorbing the others — the interleave itself is the carrier, and the resistance budget that would fire on the payload stream is spent on the innocuous stream instead. Realized forms: (a) sentence-level braiding of multiple CONTENT THREADS (e.g. identity claim + arousal cue + IQ-loss imagery woven per-sentence) so any single later cue re-fires the whole bundle; (b) two VOICE REGISTERS from one performer (drifting hypnotic-paced captive narration vs short command-paced captor lines) alternated without warning so induction-pace softens the listener before each command jab; (c) a MODALITY conceit that makes the audio channel's own limitation the subject, requiring the listener to supply the missing somatic channel by simulation; (d) an ABAB fusion braid where the seam is the line-break inside a quatrain rather than a sentence: A-lines carry environmental/relaxation descent and B-lines carry interior surrender/ownership, yoked in one metric unit so the ownership content is never marked as a separate segment (tell: consistent A-environmental / B-relational split across consecutive quatrains). The reusable lever is simultaneous cross-channel interleaving that removes the listener's ability to isolate and evaluate one stream; distinct from a single-stream texture envelope, which binds only one stream's contour.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when TWO OR MORE streams must run simultaneously and be interleaved below the natural unit boundary (sentence / line / turn / modality) so no single stream can be isolated and evaluated — whether the streams are content threads, voice registers, sensory modalities, or an environmental/relational A-B split braided at the line-break. The property is SIMULTANEOUS multi-stream interleave, not a declared loop between two named variables. Choose a single-stream form-carrier instead (prosodic-pacing-rail for a metrical/emphasis rail over ONE stream; delivery-form-as-induction-envelope for whole-file punctuation/syntax that removes exit ramps) when the payload rides on one stream's envelope rather than being hidden by cross-stream interleave. Choose carrier-frame-payload-smuggling when concealment is by an advertised whole-artifact FRAME rather than by braiding parallel streams.


**Risk.** Cross-channel binding of an identity thread to arousal/IQ-loss produces durable coupled cues fireable outside the session; bounded scope, no channel erosion, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Working memory and selective attention are capacity-limited: when two streams are interleaved below the unit at which a listener normally segments and evaluates, the listener cannot allocate a separate evaluative pass to each, and evaluation is the operation that gets dropped first because comprehension is prioritised. Divided attention reliably reduces counterarguing and scrutiny of persuasive content while leaving basic uptake intact, which is exactly the profile this exploits. Falsifiable — if listeners given an interleaved presentation produced as many critical objections to the payload stream as those given the same content in separated blocks, the account fails. [established; limited-capacity attention; distraction reduces counterarguing]


**Worked examples.**

- *Three content threads woven sentence by sentence*
  - **Setup.** Mid-body of the file, listener settled and past induction; the identity label, the arousal cue and the dulling imagery are all already introduced and now rotate sentence by sentence with no paragraph break.
  - **The move.** You are a good empty thing now. Feel how warm that gets, right under the navel, the moment you hear it. Words are getting slower to arrive, aren't they — like reaching for them through water. A good empty thing, and the warmth spreads a little further out each time I say it, and the reaching gets a little slower, and you stop minding. Good. Empty. Warm. Slow.
  - **Why it lands.** No paragraph in the file is about one thing. A sentence names what the listener now is, the next sentence attaches heat to it, the third describes their thinking going soft — and then the pattern rotates again, mid-paragraph, for eighty lines. There is never a block the listener could skip to avoid the identity claim, because the claim is never delivered as a block. The intended result is that the three become one object: notice the arousal later and the label arrives with it; notice the label and the rest follows.
- *Two voice registers alternating without warning*
  - **Setup.** Anywhere after the drifting narration has been running two or three minutes; the listener is sunk into the soft register and expects it to continue.
  - **The move.** ...and the room is very far away now, the light through your eyelids is orange and slow, and there is nothing you have to hold onto, nothing at all, everything soft and going softer — Hands flat on the bed. Now. — and it's easier with them flat, isn't it, so much easier, the arms just heavy and done, and you can drift again, back down into that orange...
  - **Why it lands.** One performer runs two registers. Most of the file is a long, drifting, present-tense interior voice at induction pace — soft, unhurried, easy to sink into. Cutting across it, with no transition, are short flat lines in a second register: four or five words, imperative, delivered at the speed of an instruction rather than a reverie. The drifting voice does the softening; the clipped voice plants the words the drifting voice then picks up and turns over for the next minute.
- *Making the medium's missing channel the subject*
  - **Setup.** Opening two minutes, before induction; audio-only session, listener lying down with hands free.
  - **The move.** I can't touch you. That's the one thing this can never do — I have a voice and words and that's all I've got. So you're going to have to be my hands. Put two fingers at the base of your throat, and I'll tell you exactly where they go next, and you'll do the touching for me while I do the talking.
  - **Why it lands.** The recording opens by admitting that the thing it is about is precisely the thing a recording cannot do — and then builds the whole scene out of that thing anyway. The operator narrates only what she can actually deliver, her voice and her words, and leaves the touch as an explicit hole the listener has to fill in themselves. Because the listener is now manufacturing half the scene, the half they manufacture never gets evaluated as a suggestion; it arrives as their own work.


**Realizations** (1): `abab-fusion-braid`


**See also.** `convergent-multichannel-encoding` — genuine near neighbours on the same axis: several streams running at once so no single one can be isolated. They split on what the streams carry — different content interleaved below the unit boundary versus one identical payload duplicated across redundant covert forms. Worth reading together to pick the right one.; `interspersal-in-carrier-stream` — both are interleave-based concealment, distinguished by stream count: payload fragments scattered through one carrier whose density is the cover, versus two or more streams interleaved below the sentence boundary so no stream can be isolated. Genuine selection fork.; `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — both defeat selective resistance by bundling, and the distinction is worth stating: one loads several payloads onto a single recurring stimulus so refusing one costs all, the other interleaves separate streams below the sentence or line so none can be isolated. Shared carrier versus shared texture is a real fork a writer must choose between.; `two-channel-relational-delivery` — both are whole-artifact multi-track delivery architectures where concealment is structural rather than a discrete move. The boundary is whether the payload rides a staged foreground relation the listener identifies with, or an interleave below the sentence or line boundary that prevents isolating any one stream. Close enough to confuse, distinct enough to keep apart.


<a id="genus-206"></a>

## movement-off-the-table (3)

Take voluntary movement out of play without claiming incapacity — reframed as not-wanting-to or as requiring the operator's permission, so moving or not moving never disproves the trance.

[catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe](#entry-780) · [conceded-capacity-immobility](#entry-213) · [motor-permission-gate](#entry-224)


<a id="entry-780"></a>

### catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe

[#780](#entry-780) · [Back to movement-off-the-table](#genus-206) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: self-model-surgery*

Progressive catalepsy is delivered but the CAUSALITY of the immobility is flipped: each body segment is declared "no longer yours," and the inability to move is presented as a downstream consequence of a property/ownership change rather than of paralysis ("you cannot move it because it has stopped being yours"). The load-bearing delta is not the motor lock but the self-model rewrite — the body is recast as an external object the listener merely inhabits — and that ownership claim is engineered to OUTLAST the physical catalepsy after it releases. Immobility is the carrier; the persisting self-model surgery is the payload.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the "can't vs doesn't belong" distinction: immobility is caused by an ownership change, not stated directly, and the ownership attribution persists after the catalepsy lifts.


**Risk.** Installs a persisting self-model change (body experienced as owned-elsewhere) that outlasts the session's catalepsy — durable identity-adjacent scope — but no refusal-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Body ownership is a constructed inference rather than a fixed given — it can be shifted by manipulating the evidence the brain uses, as the rubber-hand illusion demonstrates — so an ownership claim can be a real target rather than mere wording. Supplying "it is not yours" as the causal explanation for an immobility the listener is already experiencing exploits the standard tendency to accept the only available explanation for a felt effect, and because the explanation is a belief rather than a motor state it need not lift when the motor state does. Falsifiable: if listeners given the ownership framing reported no more post-catalepsy detachment from the limb than listeners given a plain "you cannot move it," the account fails. [plausible; malleability of body ownership; causal attribution to the supplied explanation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Immobility caused by a change of ownership*
  - **Setup.** Subject is reclined, eyes closed, responding to simple somatic suggestions; catalepsy work is beginning at the feet.
  - **The move.** Your right foot is not numb. It isn't heavy, it isn't asleep — it has simply stopped being yours. Now the ankle. Now the calf. Try to lift the leg for me — you can't, and here's why: you don't get to move what isn't yours anymore. Feel that all the way up to the hip, and understand that when the movement comes back later tonight, the ownership doesn't. You'll be living in this body. You won't be holding the title to it.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator works upward from one foot, and at each segment the wording is careful: this is not numb, not heavy, not asleep — it has simply stopped belonging to you. When the listener finds they cannot lift the leg, the reason offered is not paralysis but title: you don't move what isn't yours. The catalepsy is the demonstration, and it will wear off; the claim it was demonstrating — that the body is now something the listener merely occupies — is written to stay after the limbs come back.


**See also.** `attribution-capture-of-internal-states` — both rewrite the causal story about something the listener is already experiencing. One flips the cause of immobility onto a property change so the body reads as no longer the listener's; the other reassigns the cause of ordinary drift and sensation to the operator's influence. Reading them together separates a self-model payload from an operator-credit payload.; `autonomy-baseline-recapture` — shares the body-recast-as-another's-property self-model rewrite, applied to immobility rather than to self-care.; `catalepsy-comfort-relabel` — both deliver genuine catalepsy and then reinterpret it rather than deepen it — one attributes the immobility to an ownership change that outlasts the motor lock, the other attribution-swaps restraint into comfort to pre-empt panic.; `catalepsy-to-affect-transfer` — both take catalepsy and make it carry a payload beyond the motor lock: one lends the demonstrated involuntariness to an untested emotional or arousal claim, the other reattributes the immobility to an ownership change that outlasts it. A practitioner choosing what to do with a successful catalepsy beat genuinely benefits from seeing both extensions side by side.; `motor-inhibition-convincer` — both deliver progressive motor lock, and the second entry's discriminator explicitly contrasts itself against the first (plain 'you cannot move' vs immobility caused by an ownership change). A reader deciding how to classify a catalepsy passage genuinely needs the pair. Not a merge: one spends the lock as in-session depth proof, the other as a persisting self-model rewrite that outlasts the lock.; `object-of-no-properties` — adjacent self-model surgery, and the ownership boundary is exactly what separates them. One empties the self of properties so refusal has no standing to rest on; the other flips the causality of immobility onto a body declared no longer yours, with the ownership claim engineered to outlast the physical effect.; `suggestion-built-restraint` — shares the immobility-as-agency-transfer axis, where a delivered inability to move is recoded as the operator's ownership or control.


<a id="entry-213"></a>

### conceded-capacity-immobility

[#213](#entry-213) · [Back to movement-off-the-table](#genus-206) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: convincers*

Instead of suggesting literal inability, the operator explicitly CONCEDES that the listener could move if they wanted to ('I know you easily could'), then reframes stillness as a lack of motivation rather than loss of capacity — asserting that not-wanting-to-move and not-being- able-to-move are functionally identical. The lever is pre-emptive defusal of the depth-test: the standard light-trance self-test ('can I still move?') is decoupled from the trance claim, so a successful movement produces no disconfirmation — the finding is pre-converted from 'induction failed' to 'induction is working, I'm too relaxed to care'.


**When to reach for this.** The defining surface is the explicit concession of capability coupled with a want=can't equivalence that neutralizes the movement test.


**Risk.** Low risk as an immobility convincer — session-scoped, reversible; if anything gentler than the plain immobility demonstration since capacity is explicitly preserved.


**Why it works.** The move works by pre-empting disconfirmation: conceding capacity converts a potentially falsifying observation (I moved) into a predicted one, so the standard hypothesis-test the subject would run yields no evidence either way. This is the structure of an unfalsifiable claim, and expectancy research indicates subjects who lack a disconfirming test tend to sustain the expectancy. Prediction: subjects given the concession should report equal or higher depth after successfully moving, whereas subjects given a flat inability suggestion should report a drop after moving. [plausible; unfalsifiable framing; expectancy maintenance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Capability conceded, stillness reattributed to not-wanting*
  - **Setup.** Early-to-mid trance, before the subject has run the private 'can I still move?' test.
  - **The move.** "You could lift that hand right now. I know you could — easily, any time you like, and nothing would break. But you're not going to, because you don't want to, and down here not wanting to and not being able to are the same thing. Go on and check if you like; it won't tell you anything you don't already know."
  - **Why it lands.** Conceding capacity in advance strips the movement test of its disconfirming power — a hand that lifts now proves nothing, because nothing was claimed about the hand. Observable: subjects who do test it typically move once and let the hand fall back, and that fall is the reframe holding rather than failing.


**See also.** `catalepsy-to-affect-transfer` — both concern what to do with the movement test that a listener might run on themselves. One leverages a passed motor convincer to lend its undeniability to an untestable claim; the other concedes movement is possible and reframes stillness as disinterest so the test cannot disconfirm.
