The distinction is whether the cue is a structural cognitive event or the absence of commands, and whether what is installed is a discrete routine or a replacement baseline.; `recruited-or-foreclosed-quieting` — both produce a quiet mind without a refusable instruction, and the discriminators already contrast on the same point: one removes the refusal juncture from the emptying itself, the other conditions when emptiness engages by targeting the uncommanded baseline. Useful adjacency for anyone deciding which of the two a passage actually shows.


<a id="entry-877"></a>

### obedience-to-blankness-coupling

[#877](#entry-877) · [Back to obedience-as-resting-state](#genus-210) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: compliance*

The operator states an overt rule that every obeyed command makes the mind more blank and pushes action toward automaticity, then frames each later motor command as also discharging cognition. This contractually couples compliance to mental quieting so each obeyed command lowers conscious resistance for the next and turns blankness into a reward SIGNAL, ratcheting toward automaticity while the coupling operates covertly across later commands. The listener stops monitoring whether they WANT to obey; obedience and mind-emptying become a self-reinforcing loop that escalates toward automatic action.


**When to reach for this.** And unlike an ambient diffuse-contentment reward, the reward here is a state that also erodes resistance.


**Risk.** Contractually couples obedience to mental blankness so each command lowers resistance for the next and the listener stops monitoring their own consent, ratcheting toward automatic action; erodes the self-monitoring/refusal channel.


**Why it works.** The stated rule sets an expectancy (obeying causes blankness) and the felt quieting after each command confirms it, so the pair becomes a self-reinforcing expectancy loop; simultaneously the blank state is delivered contingent on compliance, which is operant reinforcement of obedience if blankness is experienced as pleasant. Self-perception theory adds the ratchet: the listener observing their own repeated compliance without felt coercion infers a disposition to obey. Falsifiable: if blankness is delivered non-contingently (independent of obeying), compliance escalation should not occur; if it still does, the coupling is not doing the work. [plausible; expectancy effects; contingent reinforcement; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Every obeyed command buys more blankness*
  - **Setup.** Early in the working phase, before any motor commands have been issued.
  - **The move.** Here's the arrangement, and it holds for the whole hour. Every single thing you do because I asked, your mind gets quieter. A little emptier each time, until doing takes no thinking at all. — Curl your toes for me. Good. Feel that? That cost you a thought, and you're emptier for it. — Now lift your right hand an inch off the bed. Good. Emptier. — Lower it. There goes another one. Keep obeying and keep getting that. The part of you that would ask whether you want to is the part you're spending.
  - **Why it lands.** Before any real instruction is given, the operator states the exchange rate out loud: do what I ask and your mind goes quieter, a little emptier each time, until the doing needs no thought at all. Then come the small motor tasks — curl your toes, lift your hand — and each one is narrated as having spent some more of the listener's thinking. Emptiness is now the payout for obeying, which means the listener has a reason to keep obeying that has nothing to do with wanting what was asked; the question "do I want to do this" is the very faculty being cashed in.


**See also.** `compliance-loop-language` — both run compliance as a self-reinforcing loop, but the reward differs: one pays a felt good-state (relaxation, pleasure, praise) while the other contractually pays mental blankness, so each obeyed command also erodes the capacity to evaluate the next.; `content-blind-compliance-preauthorization` — both install a standing rule that lowers per-suggestion scrutiny going forward, one by declaring acceptance content-blind and the other by making each act of obeying reward itself with mental quieting. A reader assessing how a script disables case-by-case evaluation should see both routes to the same end.; `prohibition-fused-deepening` — shares the compliance-coupled-to-depth axis in which each obeyed command advances the installed state.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — both build compliance loops that stop needing the operator to deliver the reward. One contractually couples every obeyed command to increasing blankness, making the state itself the reinforcer; the other transfers reward-generation to the listener while the operator keeps only the framing. Useful to compare when deciding who supplies the reinforcement.


<a id="entry-804"></a>

### operator-absent-self-policing

[#804](#entry-804) · [Back to obedience-as-resting-state](#genus-210) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: compliance*

The operator achieves behavioral control during her own literal absence by deputizing the subject as both subject and warden. Surveillance is externalized into the subject's own conscience: the audio goes silent for a deliberately-undisclosed duration (removing any endpoint to ration patience against), and the subject is made the enforcer of their own failure — if they turn, check a screen, or text, they must themselves stop the recording and forfeit the training. Self-administered forfeiture makes the subject complicit and invested in not triggering it, so total obedience is the only stable state.


**When to reach for this.** Absent-operator control via subject-as-own-warden plus self-administered forfeiture and an undisclosed duration.


**Risk.** Deputizes the subject to police and punish themselves during an undisclosed operator absence with no exit endpoint — the refusal channel is converted into self-forfeiture.


**Why it works.** Self-executed forfeiture recruits consistency and self-attribution: quitting requires an explicit act the subject must own, which passive compliance does not. Undisclosed duration is an unknown-endpoint arrangement, not a variable-interval schedule — VI describes reinforcer timing for a repeated operant, and the extinction-resistance finding belongs to partial/variable-ratio reinforcement; the honest claim is that no visible endpoint prevents effort rationing. Falsifiable: disclosing the duration, or swapping self-forfeiture for an operator-imposed penalty, should reduce compliance. [plausible; consistency/self-attribution plus variable-interval persistence]


**Worked examples.**

- *Subject deputized as their own warden*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; subject is seated, phone within reach, and the silent stretch has not yet started.
  - **The move.** Turn your chair so you're facing the wall — no screen, no phone in your eyeline. In a moment I'm going to stop talking, and I'm not going to tell you for how long. It might be two minutes. It might be much longer. If you turn around, if you check the time, if you reach for that phone — you stop this recording yourself, and you don't get the rest of it. I won't know. You will.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is put in a posture that faces them away from every screen and device, told the conditions of the wait, and told explicitly that its length will not be disclosed. Then the recording simply stops making sound. The enforcement is handed over before the silence begins: break the posture or reach for a device, and the listener is the one who must stop the recording and give up the session — no operator returns to catch them. With no endpoint to measure their patience against and the only penalty being one they administer to themselves, obedience is the sole strategy that keeps the thing they want available.


**See also.** `operator-absent-self-renewal-loop` — two ways control survives the operator's absence — the listener as their own enforcer under threat of self-administered forfeiture, versus a self-renewing loop whose urge to re-run is itself one of the reinforced installs. Enforcement versus renewal is a clean choice a writer actually has to make.; `operator-removal-self-policing-closure` — both make the subject their own enforcer, but one is a bounded in-session forfeiture contract during an undisclosed operator silence, while the other is a whole-script end-state where self-detection, self-reward and self-punishment interlock into a permanently operator-free loop.; `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — both relocate the enforcement role into the subject so control persists with no external agent present, and the contrast is sharp and instructive: one is an autonomy-intact self-run loop the subject owns, the other a self-surveillance and forfeiture contract serving the operator. The pairing is the clearest way to teach that boundary.; `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both install the subject as their own enforcer with no operator present, differing in the enforcement currency: a standing internal deviation detector fed by an identity reward versus a self-administered forfeiture during a deliberately undisclosed absence. Useful adjacency for anyone choosing a self-policing structure.


<a id="genus-270"></a>

## obedience-feels-chosen (2)

A real-feeling choice or freedom is staged so every path executes compliance, and the listener attributes the obedience to their own wanting.

[illusory-choice-compliance-lock](#entry-111) · [illusory-choice-into-obedience](#entry-932)


<a id="entry-111"></a>

### illusory-choice-compliance-lock

[#111](#entry-111) · [Back to obedience-feels-chosen](#genus-270) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance*

Manufactures felt volition while structurally foreclosing refusal: the operator offers a real-feeling choice — a menu of ways to do the task, a rigged binary, or a permissive branch — where every option still executes the underlying compliance OR is pre-bound to the operator's target outcome/state, and no branch leads out of the frame. Because refusing one option is still selecting another, a listener inclined to resist cannot resist this one; ownership of the outcome transfers to the listener (they believe they elected it) so later resistance drops. The compliance variant locks a directive; the outcome variant launders a post-session state or phenomenology through the listener's own volition (e.g. 'each chime either wakes you or takes you deeper'; 'feel heavy or floating'), so any felt state becomes the 'correct' one and the trance-verification loop collapses. The lever is choice-architecture, not accumulated agreement — a single rigged decision, not a ladder of yeses.


**When to reach for this.** The tell: all branches collapse to the same underlying compliance or operator-served outcome, and felt coercion drops because the listener owns the pick. In the state/outcome variant the branches are welded to operator-service and the trance-verification loop collapses so any felt state reads as correct — close kin to self-sealing evidence-rigging, but the lever is an actively-elected bounded menu, not every response pre-labeled.


**Risk.** The refusal channel is structurally closed for the locked task but the targets observed are bounded and session-scoped (body-scan order, silliness, photo-or-worship inside a submissive frame); no durable identity scope or out-of-session reach — bounded, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Perceived choice raises commitment to the resulting behavior and lowers reactance, because reactance is triggered by a felt loss of freedom rather than by the actual constraint on outcomes — a menu whose branches all converge preserves the feeling while removing the freedom. Having selected, the listener attributes the outcome internally by self-perception and defends it as their own, so later resistance would now cost self-consistency. Falsifiable: identical directives delivered as a bare command versus a converging menu should produce measurably different refusal and reactance rates, with the menu lower. [established; reactance theory; perceived-choice and commitment effects; self-perception]


**Worked examples.**

- *Rigged binary with the answer presupposed*
  - **Setup.** Early, subject still analytical; operator poses a genuine-sounding question and answers it before any answer comes back.
  - **The move.** Would you rather I take you properly through the technical side of how all this works — the mechanics, the terminology, all of it — or has that thought already slid off somewhere before you got to the end of the sentence? Mm. That's what I thought. This way's so much less effort for you, isn't it.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator poses it as a genuine question: would the listener rather work carefully through the technical side of all this, or has that thought already drifted off before they could finish it? One arm is described as labour and the other as relief. Then, before any answer has actually been given, she agrees with the one she wanted — that is what I thought, and this way is so much less effort. The choice is genuinely felt, which is what it is for; the architecture had settled it in advance, and the listener now owns the descent as something they elected.
- *A menu whose every option complies*
  - **Setup.** Start of a body-scan relaxation; subject is the type who pushes back at being told what to do, so the order is handed to them.
  - **The move.** You pick where we start. Crown of the head and work down, or the soles of your feet and work up, or one whole side and then the other — or just start with whatever part is loudest right now and we'll go from there. Entirely your call. Tell me where, and we'll release it and move on.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator lays out a menu and hands the listener the pick: perhaps they begin at the crown and work downward, perhaps from the soles upward, perhaps one side and then the other, perhaps starting with whatever is loudest in their head — the order is entirely theirs. The menu is real and the listener genuinely chooses, but every branch performs the same body scan. Someone inclined to push back against being told what to do has nothing to push against, because refusing one option is only selecting another.
- *Both branches keep the listener inside the frame*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session in an established dynamic; a new escalation is offered with the refusal branch pre-named as devotion.
  - **The move.** There's one step further tonight, and it's yours to take or not. Take it, and you please me. Hold back, and you stay where you are and adore me from there — which I'd feel too, you know. Entirely up to you. I trust you to choose what's right for you.
  - **Why it lands.** A new step up is offered with the choice made explicit: you can take it and please me, or you can hold back and adore me from a distance — entirely up to you, and I trust you'll choose what's right for you. Declining is not an exit; it has been pre-named as devotion of another kind. One branch escalates and the other confirms the role, so the felt autonomy is real while the non-submissive option was never on the menu.


**Realizations** (1): `illusion-of-choice-close`


**See also.** `answer-supply-loop` — both manufacture felt agreement while leaving no real refusal window, one by a menu whose branches all execute the same compliance and one by supplying the answer before a response can form. Close cousins a reader would want to compare.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both foreclose refusal, but by different levers: one rigs the branch structure so every option executes the same compliance, the other converts an already-performed small act into evidence that forecloses a larger commitment. They overlap in the rigged-forced-choice form, where a discarded option is pre-counted as fulfillment, and a reader picking between them benefits from seeing where choice-architecture ends and evidence-manufacture begins.; `chosen-descent-ratchet` — both transfer ownership of compliance to the listener without widening refusal, but one does it prospectively through a rigged menu the listener actively picks and the other retroactively relabels a descent already underway as chosen or consented to.; `compliance-authorship-laundering` — two ways to manufacture felt volition: relabel a compliance act or constraint as the listener's own will, versus offer a bounded menu whose every branch executes the same compliance. A writer choosing how to launder volition should compare them.; `compliance-ladder` — pass B saw a faint autonomy-flavored-ladder reading; kept here because the operative move is the rigged both-branches-inside-frame choice, not accumulation. Confirm at reconciliation.; `forced-choice-wake` — the wake-line binary is the emergence-boundary instance of the rigged-menu lever: both branches serve the install, agency is offered as cover. Reader of the general choice-architecture move gains from the specific placement at emergence where one branch fires conditioning past session end.; `graded-concurrent-choice-architecture` — choice-architecture axis: both steer through a menu of live options, one by tilting relative payoffs, one by binding every branch to the same outcome.; `interpretive-closure-meta-command` — both foreclose refusal by handing the listener the appearance of authorship, but at different scopes: one rigs a bounded menu where every branch executes the same compliance; the other installs an open-ended interpretive rule that resolves all future uninstructed choices toward the operator. A reader choosing between a closed rigged choice and an open construction rule benefits from the contrast.; `self-sealing-platform-compulsion` — both work by pre-handling the branch that would have been an exit, so no response leads out of the frame — one via a rigged menu where every option executes the same compliance, the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so even prior compliance feeds the structure. The shared lever is exit-closure architecture, not merely the presence of a choice.; `trivial-act-as-compliance-proof` — both manufacture felt volition without accumulated agreement, and both explicitly separate themselves from the same neighbors. One rigs a live choice so all branches execute the compliance; the other reinterprets an already-performed trivial act as proof of a larger submission. Useful adjacency when picking between prospective and retrospective volition manufacture.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — a mirror pair with a clean test. Both hand the subject a felt sense of control to dissolve resistance, but one offers branches that all collapse to the same compliance or operator-served outcome, while the other transfers narrow termination authority and visibly honors it. Whether the transfer is actually honored is the discrimination.


<a id="entry-932"></a>

### illusory-choice-into-obedience

[#932](#entry-932) · [Back to obedience-feels-chosen](#genus-270) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance*

The operator first stages a genuine-feeling freedom — restores agency, grants a real-sounding choice, and forces the listener to explicitly NOTICE they have the option — then immediately issues a command and reframes the instant compliance as the listener's own irresistible desire. Because the freedom was registered as real, the ensuing obedience gets attributed to wanting rather than compulsion, so control is demonstrated as chosen. The load-bearing step is "notice that you have the option", which is what converts obedience from compulsion into apparent self-authorship.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when obedience is staged to read as self-authorship: the operator first restores real freedom (the arms are released, the choice declared genuinely the listener's), then — before any command — makes the listener pause and explicitly register that the option is real. Only after that noticing beat does the command come, and the instant compliance is narrated straight back as appetite: "you want to obey me so much that you can't imagine making any other choice." The load-bearing tell is the "notice that you have the option" instruction itself — because the freedom was registered as real, the ensuing obedience gets attributed to wanting rather than compulsion, and the proof produced is "you wanted to."


**Risk.** Relabels obedience as self-authored desire, which is a durable self-model touch, but session-scoped and reversible with no explicit channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Choice-induced attitude change: when a behaviour is performed under conditions that feel freely chosen, external attribution is unavailable and the actor infers an internal motive — the insufficient-justification result from dissonance work, and the reason forced-compliance studies find larger attitude shifts under low external pressure. Explicitly noticing the option is what supplies the perceived freedom. Predicts weaker internal attribution if the choice step is removed or the pressure is made salient. [established; perceived choice / insufficient justification; internal attribution of behaviour]


**Worked examples.**

- *Real choice staged, then obedience read as desire*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the subject's arms have been suggested immobile and the operator is about to release them.
  - **The move.** Your arms are yours again — lift them, they move freely. And this next part is entirely up to you: touch yourself or don't, either is fine with me, nobody's making you. Notice that. Notice you could genuinely stop right now, and nothing would happen. Got it? Good. Hands between your legs, now. See how fast that was? Nothing was taken from you — you just didn't want the other option.
  - **Why it lands.** The arms are released and the listener is told the choice is genuinely theirs — act or don't, entirely as they prefer — and then made to pause and register that the option is real. Only once that has been noticed does the command come, and the instant compliance is narrated straight back as appetite: nothing was taken away, they simply had no interest in any other option. Because the freedom was real a moment earlier, obedience gets filed under desire rather than pressure, and the cycle can be run again by returning the hands to where they started.


**See also.** `arousal-isolated-obedience-test` — both stage a beat whose purpose is proving obedience is real rather than borrowed. One halts a high-arousal action so compliance cannot be attributed to momentum; the other stages a genuine-feeling freedom first so compliance is attributed to wanting. Two ways of controlling what the obedience proof is credited to.; `desire-without-obligation` — both stage an apparent freedom in order to make the ensuing compliance read as self-authored desire, differing in placement: one has the listener explicitly NOTICE the option immediately before a command, the other laminates a standing 'you do not have to' disclaimer onto a maximally installed craving. Same laundering logic, and the disclaimer-versus-noticed-option distinction is exactly what a writer needs.; `illusory-choice-authorship` — both manufacture felt authorship over an outcome the operator controls. The first is a specific beat order in which a genuine-feeling freedom is registered first so the ensuing instant compliance reads as wanting; the second is the broader agency-relocation family including converging branches and assigned observation tasks. Species to genus link, not a duplicate.


<a id="genus-254"></a>

## obedience-turned-evidence (2)

Get an easy act obeyed, then cite it back: the listener's own performed compliance becomes felt, hard-to-dispute evidence that the control or the manufactured wanting is real, lowering the bar for the next ask.

[compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting](#entry-693) · [obedience-demonstration-as-proof](#entry-945)


<a id="entry-693"></a>

### compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting

[#693](#entry-693) · [Back to obedience-turned-evidence](#genus-254) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: convincers*

The operator issues an easy, frictionless instruction (breathe in and squeeze), then much later points back at that obeyed act as first-person empirical evidence for the THESIS that the operator can manufacture wants in the listener. The performed compliance is converted into self-evidenced proof of induced desire, so resisting any later command now contradicts something the listener felt themselves do — raising the prior on all subsequent commands. The lever is the deferred callback that reframes the obeyed act as evidence of operator-induced (not self-chosen) wanting.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this entry when an easy, frictionless instruction (draw one slow breath in and hold it) is issued early and then, minutes later, deliberately pointed back at as first-person empirical evidence for a stated thesis: that the operator can manufacture wanting in the listener ('a moment ago you had no interest in that breath'). The observable tell is the deferred callback that relabels the obeyed act — the compliance is harvested to prove that the listener's desire was installed rather than self-chosen, a move on the listener's self-model of where wants come from, so that resisting any later command would contradict something the listener felt themselves do.


**Risk.** Installs a self-evidenced belief that the operator can manufacture the listener's wants, a durable self-model touch that licenses downstream commands; bounded and reversible with no explicit channel install, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** The deferred callback is a misattribution manoeuvre: the listener performed the act for a trivially available reason (it was easy and asked politely), but the reason is not stored with the memory, so a later supplied explanation faces little competition. Once the act is relabelled as evidence the operator manufactured a want, consistency pressure raises the prior on subsequent commands. The delay matters because immediate relabelling would collide with the still-accessible real reason. Falsifiable: if the same relabelling done immediately after the act produced identical downstream compliance, the deferral is not load-bearing. [plausible; misattribution; self-perception; consistency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Obeyed act cited as proof of manufactured wanting*
  - **Setup.** Two beats in one session: an early frictionless instruction, then the deferred callback several minutes later once the subject is under.
  - **The move.** [early] You don't actually know what you want — attention is what makes a want, not the other way round. Now: draw one slow breath in through your nose and hold it at the top. Hold. And let it go.

[much later] Go back to that breath. Thirty seconds before I said it, you had no interest in it whatsoever. I put your attention on it. Then you wanted it. Then you took it. You watched me build a want in you out of nothing and you felt yourself have it. That's the machine we're working with.
  - **Why it lands.** Early on the operator lays out a claim: you do not actually know what you want, and attention placed on a want is enough to create one. Then comes an instruction with no friction to it at all — draw one slow breath in and hold it. Several minutes later she returns to it as evidence. A moment ago you had no interest in that breath; I named it, and then you wanted it, and then you took it. The listener is now holding what feels like their own first-hand data that this voice can install a desire, so declining the next instruction means contradicting something they felt their own body do.


**See also.** `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — very close - both direct an easy act and later read it back as first-person evidence. Held apart on two real differentiators: the deferred callback (the act is harvested much later rather than confirmed on the spot) and what the act is claimed to prove (that wanting is operator-manufactured, rather than that the target state is already present). Link rather than merge until the timing gap is shown to be incidental.; `obedience-motive-reattribution` — both relocate the authorship of wanting rather than issuing a new instruction: one harvests a trivially obeyed act as evidence that desire is manufactured, the other reassigns the motive behind acts the listener already performs on their own. Useful pairing for a reader working on attribution of motive, with the boundary being in-session harvest versus out-of-session motive swap.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both harvest the listener's real performed acts as evidence, but the ledger annotates many genuine acts contemporaneously to shift the perceived baseline to already-surrendered, while the single deferred callback targets one frictionless act much later to prove a specific thesis about manufactured wanting.; `pace-mirror-agency-proof` — both manufacture first-person experiential evidence before the doctrine it will be used to prove, so the later assertion reads as confirmation. The vehicles differ (a deferred callback to an obeyed instruction versus a mirrored-motion loop) but the ordering trick is the same family.; `spend-compliance-receipt-as-attention-anchor` — both harvest an already-performed compliance act and spend it on something other than the act itself, one via a deferred callback that reframes it as proof of manufactured wanting, the other by immediately converting it into an attentional anchor. Same receipt, different disposal, and the timing contrast is instructive.; `trivial-act-as-compliance-proof` — same family: one performed act retroactively reinterpreted as proof of something larger. They differ only in the conclusion harvested — broad submission or irresistibility in one, the thesis that the operator manufactures wanting in the other. Close enough that a writer needs the discriminator.


<a id="entry-945"></a>

### obedience-demonstration-as-proof

[#945](#entry-945) · [Back to obedience-turned-evidence](#genus-254) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: convincers*

The operator elicits an obeyed act (a commanded motion, a triggered response, a stop/resume, a snap-gated shutdown) and then cites the listener's own performance back to them as felt, self-witnessed evidence that control/depth is real — shifting obedience from asserted to demonstrated. The engine is the validation beat: because the listener saw their own body comply, the claim becomes unfalsifiable and the threshold for the next, larger ask drops. Variants stack the demonstrators into a graduated ladder (trivial-to-costly, or arithmetic-competent-off vs dumb-on) or attach an identity reward, but the core lever is the same demonstrated-compliance cited-as-proof.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the validation beat — the obeyed act exists TO be cited back as evidence.


**Risk.** Originally rated low, but the demonstrated scripts here escalate to costly/real-world asks and install portable leashes; the ladder variants raise it to durable-but-bounded compliance capital. Channel not eroded, so not high.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory is the engine: lacking privileged access to their own internal states, people read their own overt behaviour as evidence about themselves, and observing oneself comply supplies exactly that evidence. Citing the compliance back closes the loop by making the inference explicit, and each accepted small demonstration then functions as a foot-in-the-door step that raises acceptance of the next, larger request. Falsifiable — if subjects who performed the act but were not given the validation beat showed identical acceptance of the following larger request, the cited-back-as-proof component would be doing nothing. [established; self-perception theory; foot-in-the-door compliance]


**Worked examples.**

- *The command announced in advance as a demonstration*
  - **Setup.** Deep in the file, after an extended stretch of claiming the body now answers to the operator; listener lying still with eyes closed.
  - **The move.** You don't have to take my word for it. I'll show you. On the next breath out, your right hand turns over — palm up. Now. There. You didn't decide that, and you can't tell me you did, because you weren't the one who thought of it.
  - **Why it lands.** Seventy lines of claiming that the body now answers to her without consulting the listener, and then the operator says, plainly, that she is about to prove it: she will give one instruction, and the body will carry it out. The instruction is short, physical and unambiguous — a single commanded change of position — and the moment it is performed she names what just happened as the evidence. Nothing has been hidden; the whole point is that the listener watched it. Having moved, they have no way left to argue the claim was only talk, because the counter-argument would have to be that they did it themselves — which is precisely the thing they can no longer distinguish.
- *Obeyed act read back as the listener’s own proof*
  - **Setup.** Listener is well into stroking and clearly does not want to break; operator has been building for several minutes.
  - **The move.** Stop. Hands off, right now. ... Good. Now put them back. That was against everything you wanted, and you did it in under a second — you just watched yourself belong to me. Keep going.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator waits until the listener is well into something they want to keep doing, then orders them to stop — and holds the silence a beat before releasing it. The stop is the harder command on purpose: obeying a permission proves nothing, while obeying against an active urge does. The moment the hand comes back she names what just happened as the evidence, and the listener watched themselves supply it.
- *A ladder from trivial to costly under one cue*
  - **Setup.** Early in a compliance sequence; the cue phrase has just been named as meaning "do the thing I said," and no rungs have been climbed yet.
  - **The move.** When I say now be good, you do the thing I just said. Touch your finger to your chin — now be good. Good. Hand in the air — now be good. Good, you're quick at this. Kneel where you are and say thank you out loud — now be good. Look how easy that was for you. You're good at this.
  - **Why it lands.** One short phrase is installed as the cue meaning do the thing I just named, then drilled immediately from nothing: a fingertip to the chin, a hand raised, and onward through the rungs that cost dignity, each success praised and banked as evidence that the listener is good at this. By the time the same cue is attached to something that costs actual money, refusing would mean failing at the one thing the last ten minutes established they were succeeding at.
- *Switching it off and on as install verification*
  - **Setup.** The dumbing state is already installed with an on/off cue; listener responsive and able to speak or think an answer aloud.
  - **The move.** Cue off. Clear head, back to normal — what's seven plus five? Easy, right? You didn't even have to look for it. Cue on. Now: what's six plus six? Is it twelve, or is it a lot, or is it too many numbers? Take whichever one comes. See what I just did to you?
  - **Why it lands.** The operator switches the state off, asks a genuine arithmetic question, and confirms the listener answers it easily. Then she switches it back on and asks a second question of the same size — except this one is rigged so that the only offered answers are the ones the state is supposed to produce, and failing it is pre-framed as the fun part. The contrast between the two answers is the whole demonstration: the listener does not have to be told the switch works, they just compared themselves with it on and off.


**See also.** `arousal-isolated-obedience-test` — a specialized case and its general form. The general one cites any obeyed act back as proof; the specialized one halts a high-arousal action specifically to show obedience was not just riding momentum. Useful for a reader picking the strength of proof they need.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both cite a performed act back as proof, but the proof currency differs. One trades on felt self-witness (you saw your body obey, so control is real); the other trades on a logical tautology that forecloses refusal. Related enough to cross-reference, not one technique.; `enacted-embodied-proof` — two ways a commanded act becomes evidence: one has the body manufacture proprioceptive proof for an abstract claim or rule ('your mind works the same way'), the other cites the bare fact of having obeyed back as proof that control is real — the payload differs (a cognitive claim versus the operator's authority), but both convert a performed action into an unfalsifiable convincer and drop the threshold for the next ask.; `in-session-rehearsal-of-posthypnotic-act` — nested pair with a sharp line between them. One elicits any obeyed act purely so it can be cited back as evidence of control; the other rehearses the exact act a later suggestion will demand, so the body pre-proves that specific suggestion. Anyone reaching for the general proof beat should know the targeted-rehearsal variant exists.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both split a manufactured referent from the claim made about it, but at different scopes: one is a whole-script ordering where a fabricated experience precedes the label that interprets it, the other is the local validation beat where a single obeyed act is cited straight back as evidence. The demonstration move is the most common thing the ordering schedules, so a reader working on one wants the other.; `out-of-audio-compliance-offload` — a demonstrated act cited back as proof of control, versus that same proof beat relocated into a separate medium where the act is materially performed out of band. The second is the channel-transfer variant of the first's validation beat, so a reader of either wants the other.; `physical-compliance-proof-posture` — both elicit an act and cite it back as self-witnessed evidence of the target state. One covers obeyed commands generally, the other is specifically a physical display or exposure posture, usually elicited before any trance language. Keep separate despite the overlap: the body-configuration read-back is its own assignable surface, and this pointer marks the boundary.; `self-generated-failure-as-identity-proof` — same engine, different payload: a self-witnessed performance cited back as unfalsifiable evidence, proving a degraded identity in one case and the reality of control in the other.; `spend-compliance-receipt-as-attention-anchor` — the spent-receipt entry is defined by contrast with the standing proof beat: it is the case where the demonstrated obedience is immediately reversed and converted into an attentional anchor instead of being cited back as evidence. Reading one without the other invites assigning every convincer to the standing form.


<a id="genus-128"></a>

## operator-side-groundwork (7)

Work done to the plan, not the listener: choosing targets, screening subjects, gating interventions, and checking that consequences actually work as intended.

[contingency-discriminability-design](#entry-1116) · [contingency-sign-verification](#entry-1186) · [contingency-space-analysis](#entry-783) · [intervention-gating](#entry-830) · [measurement-confound-mitigation](#entry-500) · [suitability-screening](#entry-583) · [target-selection](#entry-525)


<a id="entry-1116"></a>

### contingency-discriminability-design

[#1116](#entry-1116) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

Set how DETECTABLE a behavior-consequence contingency is to the subject — a single design variable the operator drives to either pole. INDISCRIMINABLE POLE (make the contingency undetectable to force steady responding / prevent gaming): (indiscriminable-contingency) reinforce on a schedule the subject cannot discriminate — randomized delivery (spinners, dice, raffles) spread across many forms of the behavior, many settings, many rewards, so no instance is reliably non-reinforced and the exit ('the game's off, no need to respond') is removed, making the reward-optimizing policy 'act the targeted way across every domain'; (indiscriminable-reinforcement-schedule) a variable (VR) schedule the subject cannot COUNT, eliminating post-reinforcement pauses; (contingency-target-concealment) in a GROUP contingency, randomize/conceal which student/behavior/reinforcer counts (often drawn after performance) to defeat scapegoating and strategic under-responding; (reinforcement-thinning-boundary-erasure) step the schedule down before probes so the learner cannot discriminate training from test by reinforcer presence — an indiscriminability move for MEASUREMENT validity (keeps probe responding from differential extinction). TRANSPARENT POLE (make the contingency maximally discriminable so behavior attaches to the act, not confusion): (contingency-transparency-arrangement) pre-define the response class in observable terms with positive examples AND nonexamples, post the standing rules (duration, exit criteria, escalation) as a continuously-visible discriminative stimulus, and give a terminal transition prompt near the interval's end.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for CONTINGENCY-DISCRIMINABILITY DESIGN when the lever is the subject's ability to DETECT the contingency — set it opaque (VR/randomized/concealed-target/erased-boundary) to force steady responding, prevent counting or gaming, or protect probe validity; set it transparent (defined class + posted rules + transition prompt) so behavior attaches to the act rather than confusion. Choose it over: reward-magnitude moves / multiplier-stacking (which amplify a reward — here the manipulated variable is detectability, not size); a fixed cue-response pairing (a randomizer/visibility choice, not a set pairing). The two poles are the same design variable driven opposite directions; the group-target-concealment variant is the social/anti-scapegoating case, distinct from schedule-level indiscriminability.


**Risk.** Covert, broad, durable behavior installation that removes the subject's ability to detect when the contingency is active; no coercion or refusal-channel erosion, but covert breadth lifts it above low.


**Why it works.** Variable-ratio schedules produce steady high-rate responding and strong resistance to extinction, while FIXED schedules produce post-reinforcement pausing — the pause comes from the fixedness of the requirement, not from the subject counting. The transparent pole works via a different route: clearly defined discriminative stimuli and stated rules reduce ambiguity so behaviour comes under control of the act rather than guesswork. Falsifiable: shifting from a variable to a fixed ratio at matched reinforcement density should introduce post-reinforcement pauses, which distinguishes this account from "randomness is exciting". [established; variable-ratio schedules; partial reinforcement extinction effect; discriminative stimulus control]


**Worked examples.**

- *Spread the payoff so no instance is safe to skip*
  - "When you can't tell which of several green behaviors performed exactly where or when will produce a reward, the best strategy… is acting green in every way, everywhere, all the time" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *A game device decides what pays off*
  - "a game-like procedure for randomly determining which green behaviors, emitted where and when, will earn what rewards" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (4): `contingency-target-concealment`, `contingency-transparency-arrangement`, `indiscriminable-reinforcement-schedule`, `reinforcement-thinning-boundary-erasure`


**See also.** `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — both are contingency-design reference entries rather than subject-facing moves, and the discriminability variable is one of the arrangement properties the substrate principles govern. A designer consulting one will want the other.; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — both are about how a cue or contingency becomes detectable to the subject, and one explicitly manipulates discriminability of the reinforcement schedule while the other builds control by a reinforcement history. A reader designing stimulus control genuinely needs to know that detectability of the contingency is a separate lever they can set opaque or transparent.; `reinforcement-leak-proofing` — both are design levers on the same arranged contingency and are explicitly disjoint: one closes off every path by which reinforcement can arrive outside the arrangement, the other sets how detectable the arrangement is to the subject. Readers arranging a contingency routinely need to place a move on the correct axis.


<a id="entry-1186"></a>

### contingency-sign-verification

[#1186](#entry-1186) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: measurement*

An operator-side monitoring move: the operator watches the rate data to detect whether a procedure intended to reduce a behavior is in fact INCREASING it — i.e. whether the same operation is functioning as reinforcement rather than punishment on this individual — and, on detecting the sign inversion, abandons the procedure and reassigns the subject to an alternative contingency with the intended sign (time-out, DRA). The lever is a function-over-form empirical check on the sign of the contingency, requiring an alternative procedure ready to swap in.


**When to reach for this.** A writer reaches for this entry when an operator running a behavior-reduction procedure watches the rate data specifically to catch the contingency operating with the wrong sign — the imposed cost functioning as reinforcement, the targeted behavior rising under repeated penalty. The observable tell is a function-over-form empirical check on the DIRECTION of the contingency's effect, not on how much progress it is making toward a goal, and what is being verified is the operation's effect on behavior rather than any authorization or license. The move completes with a swap: an alternative procedure with the intended sign (time-out, DRA) is held ready and substituted the moment inversion is detected, as in Cooper, Heron & Heward's instruction that when response cost serves to reinforce, 'the practitioner should stop using response cost and switch.'


**Risk.** A self-correcting monitoring check that catches and replaces a procedure doing harm; literature, protective in effect, no consent surface eroded.


**Why it works.** Reinforcement and punishment are defined by their effect on behaviour rate, not by the operator's intent or the aversiveness of the event — attention delivered as a reprimand functions as reinforcement whenever attention is the maintaining consequence. Rate data is therefore the only valid test of a contingency's sign, and this move exists because the operator's intuition about aversiveness is a known-unreliable predictor. Falsifiable and routinely falsified in practice: procedures intended as punishers are observed increasing target behaviour. [established; functional definition of reinforcement; attention-maintained behaviour]


**Worked examples.**

- *Checking whether the penalty is reinforcing instead*
  - "One occurs when the repeated imposition of response cost serves to reinforce, and not punish, the undesirable behavior. When this situation arises, the practitioner should stop using response cost and switch" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `attribution-hygiene-audit` — both audit the operator's own inference against the data before trusting it — there checking a procedure's sign, here checking the measurement channel itself.; `contingency-space-analysis` — both are operator-side checks on the sign of a behavior-to-consequence contingency using observation data rather than manipulation. They stay separate because one computes a comparison against a base rate and the other watches live rate data and swaps procedures on inversion.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-side empirical checks that block acting on appearances, but the depth gate verifies a subject state before licensing a high-stakes act, while sign verification watches rate data to catch a procedure functioning with the opposite sign and swaps it out — license gating versus function-over-form correction.


<a id="entry-783"></a>

### contingency-space-analysis

[#783](#entry-783) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: measurement*

An operator-side measurement/analytic step. The analyst computes the probability a consequence follows the target behavior AND the probability that same consequence occurs in behavior-absent intervals, then graphs the pair; more-than marks a positive contingency, less-than a negative one, equal a neutral one. The lever is statistical discrimination against a base rate — it separates a genuine behavior-to-consequence dependency from a consequence that is merely ambient, correcting the false signal that raw co-occurrence tallying produces. It requires direct-observation counts for behavior-present and behavior-absent intervals and involves no experimental manipulation of the subject.


**When to reach for this.** Not ABC co-occurrence tallying (its cited sibling M6, which logs raw antecedent and consequence counts) — the tell is the explicit conditional-probability comparison against the behavior-absent base rate. An analytic computation over already-collected observation data, not an elicitation move on a present subject.


**Risk.** A measurement/analytic computation over observation data; no consent surface, no channel erosion, no durable scope change.


**Why it works.** Human and animal learning tracks contingency, not mere contiguity: a consequence that occurs just as often without the behavior produces little or no learning even when it frequently follows it. Comparing p(consequence|behavior) against p(consequence|no behavior) therefore measures the quantity the organism is actually sensitive to, and it is falsifiable — if reinforcement schedules with equal conditional probabilities still produced behavior change as reliably as positive-contingency schedules, the analytic step would be worthless. [established; contingency vs. contiguity in conditioning (Rescorla's truly-random-control finding)]


**Worked examples.**

- *Probability of the consequence against its base rate*
  - "the probability of the consequence following the behavior and ... the probability of the consequence following the absence of the behavior should also be determined ... compared in what is called a contingency space analysis (CSA)." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `contingency-sign-verification` — both are operator-side checks on the sign of a behavior-to-consequence contingency using observation data rather than manipulation. They stay separate because one computes a comparison against a base rate and the other watches live rate data and swaps procedures on inversion.; `descriptive-functional-assessment` — these are sequential steps over the same observation record rather than rivals: one logs antecedent-behavior-consequence triples only when the behavior fires, the other computes consequence probability against behavior-absent intervals. Worth seeing together because the second corrects the false dependency signal the first can produce, and neither manipulates the subject.; `self-monitoring-reactivity` — same operator-side measurement axis: turning a log of behavior events into the operative lever or datum.; `unconditional-antecedent-consequence-logging` — two consecutive steps of one measurement protocol: the unconditional logging protocol produces exactly the behavior-present and behavior-absent counts that the contingency computation consumes. A reader implementing either needs the other to get a usable result. Kept separate because one is a recording discipline and the other an analytic computation.


<a id="entry-830"></a>

### intervention-gating

[#830](#entry-830) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

An operator-side conditional branch that converts 'do X' into a go/no-go (or which-arm/which-form) decision keyed to an assessed precondition, changing the operator's plan rather than the subject's state. Realizations: (a) PRECONDITION-READINESS GATE — check readiness conditions before an advanced program (primary skills strong, learner self-listens, learner can tact her own behavior) and proceed only if all hold, else build the missing prerequisite first; (b) FAIR-PAIR PRECONDITION — block any reduction plan until a same-function adaptive replacement is named and scheduled (elimination is converted into construction, because removing a functional behavior leaves a vacuum); (c) CAUSE-ACCESSIBILITY TRIAGE — test whether the subject can state the cause consciously; if yes run direct suggestion, if no run uncovering first, then correct (a which-arm branch with an explicit failure signature: direct suggestion fails when the cause is unconscious); (d) METHOD/FEASIBILITY SELECTION — pick among methods by a rule keyed to downstream side-effects (default to the error-minimizing method when learning history is unknown or errors evoke problem behavior; escalate complexity only when simpler fails) and covertly gauge whether significant others can actually run the plan, filtering targets by treatment-integrity risk; (e) EFFICACY-AUDIENCE FILTER — an intake prerequisite that admits only a pre-conditioned listener (e.g. familiarity with a prior product) so hotter in-session work can run without onboarding. The gate itself enacts nothing on the subject; it branches the plan on effectiveness or feasibility grounds.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for intervention-gating when the writer's question is 'should this run, in what form, or which arm?' — an assessed-precondition test that branches the plan before/about intervention content, with no authorization surface on the subject. Variant tells: readiness checklist (a), same-function replacement required first (b), conscious-cause test picks the corrective arm (c), side-effect-keyed method/feasibility rule (d), listener-precondition intake filter (e). NOTE on (e): unlike a subject-facing consent or suitability screen, the efficacy-audience filter protects NOBODY — it serves hotter work, not welfare; that purpose-inversion is its tell.


**Risk.** Preparatory operator-side gates on whether to run a program; no move on the subject, no consent or refusal surface — session-external planning. The fair-pair gate is welfare-protective (retains the subject's route to the reinforcer).


**Why it works.** Conditional branching works because intervention effects are moderated by preconditions that are cheap to test and expensive to discover by failure: a plan run on a subject lacking the prerequisite skill, or delivered by a third party who cannot execute it with fidelity, produces near-zero effect regardless of technique quality. The fair-pair variant rests on the matching law and the behavioural vacuum finding — removing a response that reliably produces a reinforcer without supplying an equally efficient alternative tends to yield substitution or resurgence rather than extinction. Falsifiable: if gated and ungated runs on precondition-failing cases showed equal outcomes, or if reduction plans without a same-function replacement showed no elevated substitution rate, the rule would be wrong. [established; treatment-integrity moderation; matching law and response substitution / resurgence]


**Worked examples.**

- *Three prerequisites checked before the program runs*
  - "There are several prerequisite skills are necessary to benefit from a formal autoclitic intervention program: (1) A speaker's existing verbal skills are sufficient... (2) a speaker demonstrates self-listening skills, and (3) a speaker can tact aspects of her own verbal and nonverbal behavior." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *No reduction plan without a same-function replacement*
  - "never plan to reduce or eliminate a behavior…without first (a) determining an adaptive behavior that will take its place (also known as the fair pair rule)" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (3): `cause-accessibility-triage`, `efficacy-audience-filtering`, `operator-side-method-selection`


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side conditional rules that branch or block the plan before anything is done to the subject, with no subject-facing surface. One is a general precondition-branch family, the other a specific hold on altering a load-bearing belief until consequences are foreseeable; the specific case reads as an instance of the general gate and readers should see the relation.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-side gates that block or branch action on an assessed precondition, and a writer looking for one may want the other. The narrower one refuses to infer depth from ambiguous outward signs and forces independent verification before a high-stakes act; the broader family branches the plan on readiness, feasibility, or which corrective arm to run. Gating on verified state versus gating on plan viability.


<a id="entry-500"></a>

### measurement-confound-mitigation

[#500](#entry-500) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: measurement*

An operator-side measurement-design rule that recovers a valid picture of the subject's behavior from an assessment process that would otherwise distort it. Two confounds are managed by the same lever (vary and/or repeat observation): MASKING — a behavior live in one context is absent from a single sample — is defeated by deliberately spreading observation across times, settings, and caretakers so a false-negative target map is caught rather than missed; and REACTIVITY — being watched shifts the behavior — is defeated by minimizing obtrusiveness and repeating observation across days until the novelty-driven reactive transient decays, then reading the stabilized baseline. Both convert a measurement artifact into a managed, validity-protecting arrangement; the move acts on the operator's data, not on the subject's state.


**When to reach for this.** Not an intervention that changes the subject's behavior and not the recording protocol itself; the tell is that the move manages a measurement confound (masking or reactivity) to protect the validity of assessment data.


**Risk.** Assessment-design rule about observation validity; session-scoped, no consent surface, no channel erosion — evidence is the two demonstrated ABA passages.


**Why it works.** Behaviour varies across settings and observers, so a single sample is an unreliable estimate of a rate; aggregating across occasions reduces sampling error and raises the reliability of the estimate — basic measurement theory, not a claim about the subject. Reactivity is a well-documented artifact in which being observed changes the observed behaviour, and it typically attenuates with repeated exposure as the observer's presence loses novelty. Falsifiable and routinely tested: reactivity predicts a systematic difference between early and later observation sessions that should shrink over days. [established; measurement reliability via aggregation; observer reactivity and habituation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Vary time, setting and person to defeat masking*
  - "if data are collected only during morning sessions, at home, or with a specific caretaker, the 'target' behavior may be masked in the afternoon, at school, or with different caretakers" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Repeat observations until reactivity decays*
  - "behavior analysts mitigate reactivity when they make observations as unobtrusive as possible, repeat observations until apparent reactive effects subside" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


<a id="entry-583"></a>

### suitability-screening

[#583](#entry-583) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Before or at the threshold of the working phase, the operator screens whether to proceed at all — delivering contraindication warnings, declining structurally opposed subjects (defiers, skeptics, intimates) on a consent-state premise, reading a receptivity proxy, or aborting the planned route where a contraindication surfaces — narrowing the operator's own license and honoring the subject's fitness/authorization rather than pushing a state. Positive governance: the operator is who ends up constrained.


**When to reach for this.** Gates whether (and on whom) the session runs, for the subject's protection or on a consent premise; the operator's action is blocked/narrowed.


**Risk.** Protective/consent-honoring screening, in the manner of a contraindication prompt advising the subject to consult a professional. The float-relaxation member covertly presupposes a 'subconscious mind' model, noted but not risk-elevating.


**Why it works.** Hypnotic responding varies widely between people and is partly a stable trait, so a screening step exploits real predictive information rather than guesswork — some subjects will not reach the state the procedure assumes, and proceeding anyway spends time and can produce a failure experience that lowers subsequent responding. Independently, contraindication screening handles asymmetric risk: the cost of declining a marginal case is small, the cost of proceeding with a subject for whom the material is contraindicated is not. Falsifiable: if screened and unscreened cohorts show identical adverse-event and non-response rates, the gate is doing nothing. [established; individual differences in hypnotic suggestibility; asymmetric risk of proceeding]


**Worked examples.**

- *Decline the structurally opposed subject*
  - "hypnosis is a consent state and, obviously, the person who defies does not consent" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *Contraindication warning and opt-out before eyes close*
  - **Setup.** Opening seconds, before any settling work; subject fully alert and still in an ordinary deciding frame.
  - **The move.** Before we start, some plain housekeeping. Do not use this if you are driving or operating anything, if you are epileptic or prone to seizures, or if you are in a bad place mentally tonight — and if any of that is you, stop the file here, right now, nothing has happened yet. It will still be here another day, and another day is fine.
  - **Why it lands.** Before any of the settling work begins, the operator names the conditions under which this recording is a bad idea for you and tells you plainly to stop it here if any of them apply — then adds that you can always come back another time. The screen runs while the listener is still in an ordinary deciding frame, and anyone the warning fits has removed themselves before a single instruction lands.
- *A somatic read gates whether to proceed today*
  - "A cold hand says that the person is cold to the subject; a hot, wet hand says that the patient is liable to resist. A warm hand tells you that you should be successful immediately." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *A trauma origin reroutes the planned route*
  - "she is abreacting to the tonsilectomy of twenty-five years ago" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, and they gate on different grounds: subject fitness and consent state versus the operator's foreknowledge of downstream fallout. Reading one raises the natural question of what else can hold a session back, which the other answers.; `consent-checkpoint` — two positive-governance gates that both leave the operator as the constrained party, differing in what they gate. One is an authorization check with a real waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action. The other screens whether to proceed with this person at all, on fitness or contraindication grounds. Anyone selecting a genuine gate should see both and pick by object — this moment versus this person.; `context-gate` — complementary pre-induction gates that block the session on different axes. One rules on whether the listening situation is safe enough to proceed; the other rules on whether this person should be worked with at all. Both narrow the operator's license rather than pushing a state, and both commonly appear in the same opening.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-side governance gates where the constrained party is the operator and the action is blocked until a condition is met. One gates a high-stakes act on verified depth rather than a look-alike sign; the other gates whether the session runs at all and on whom. Naturally read together.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are positive-governance gates that constrain the operator's own license before anything is installed. One screens the subject's fitness and can decline outright; the other tests the want empirically and can return abort. Same family, different evidence standard.; `filter-shaping-pre-qualification` — a sharp opposed pair on the same object, the subject's retained veto. One narrows the operator's own license by declining to proceed when the subject is unfit or unauthorized; the other leaves the veto fully intact and instead shapes every input to pass through it. Same faculty, opposite postures toward it.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both discriminators already name each other as the contrast case: one gates the design, the other gates the person, and both are positive-governance moves that narrow the operator's license. The boundary is genuinely confusable at classification time, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.


<a id="entry-525"></a>

### target-selection

[#525](#entry-525) · [Back to operator-side-groundwork](#genus-128) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Design-time selection and operationalization of WHICH behavior/target the intervention will aim at, decided before anything is done to the subject; the payoff is the operator's target list, not any subject state. The variants are the selection criteria a writer chooses among: (a) FORWARD LEVERAGE — privilege behavioral cusps whose change unlocks disproportionate downstream contingency space, so one trained behavior cascades into untrained learning; (b) STANDING-CONTINGENCY MAINTAINABILITY — keep only targets the post-instruction environment will already catch and reinforce (and reject age-/community-atypical targets that suppress natural reinforcement), shifting the maintenance burden off the operator; (c) PRODUCING-BEHAVIOR VALIDITY — refuse to hang the contingency on an outcome or mere correlate; decompose the stated result into the definable behaviors that produce it and place the contingency there (named failure: contingency-on-the-product programs fail); (d) GOAL-PROXIMAL DIMENSION — operationalize the vague goal as one specific measurable dimension (rate, duration, latency, magnitude, topography) moved in a named direction, chosen by which dimension most directly advances the actual goal (calories, not bites); (e) TRAIT-TO-BEHAVIOR DECOMPOSITION — meet every intrinsic-trait label ('lazy','fearful') with 'what does X DO?' to dissolve the internal-cause attribution into a countable, environment-linked, targetable behavior; (f) STRENGTHS-FIRST BALANCE — force a fixed-count strengths inventory ahead of an equal-count deficit list at intake so the target pool tilts toward building, not only suppressing.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for target-selection when the writer's question is 'what should the intervention aim at?' — a design-time filter/operationalization on the operator's target list, nothing enacted on the subject. Pick the criterion by the sub-question: downstream leverage (a), will-it-last (b), causal validity (c), which measurable dimension (d), how to make a vague trait targetable (e), or is the pool strengths-balanced (f).


**Risk.** Plan-level selection and operationalization across six named criteria; this record does not itself execute the subsequent intervention.


**Why it works.** Behavior is maintained by its consequences, so an intervention aimed at an outcome or a trait label — neither of which the environment can reinforce — has nothing to act on; specifying a countable, environment-contactable response gives the contingency a surface. Targeting cusps works because responses that open access to new contingencies recruit further learning the operator never programmed, and choosing targets the natural setting already reinforces is what keeps them after the operator leaves. Falsifiable: contingencies placed on products rather than producing behaviors should show weaker and less durable change than matched behavior-level targets. [established; operant selection by consequences; behavioral cusps; response generalization and maintenance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Privilege the cusp that unlocks new contingencies*
  - "sets the occasion to access reinforcers that otherwise would not have been available" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Rank the eligible pool by leverage questions*
  - "Which behavior should be changed first?… modification is likely to provide access to more normalized settings… Will this new behavior produce reinforcement for significant others?" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (5): `goal-proximal-dimension-selection`, `producing-behavior-validity-gate`, `standing-contingency-target-filter`, `strengths-first-elicitation-frame`, `trait-to-behavior-decomposition`


**See also.** `beneficiary-target-filter` — both are design-time filters on the target list before anything is enacted, but one supplies selection criteria and the other an admissibility test keyed to whose benefit the change serves. Read together when deciding what an intervention should aim at.; `design-time-reconnaissance` — adjacent design-time operator moves that are easy to conflate, and each discriminator already names the other: one filters and operationalizes which target to aim at, the other exhaustively enumerates the space the plan must survive. They also interlock, since the enumeration supplies the environment map the selection criteria test against. Filtering is not enumerating, so no merge.; `influence-topology-node-selection` — a planner scoping an intervention faces both questions and they are genuinely different levers: one operationalizes WHICH behavior to aim at by leverage, maintainability, or measurable dimension, the other picks WHICH person in an influence graph to route the change through so the surrounding system sustains it. Neither substitutes for the other.; `operator-resource-generation` — two different operator-side design levers a writer uses in sequence and can be read together: one filters WHAT the intervention should aim at, producing a target list; the other disciplines HOW the tactical material to get there is generated, producing an option set. Neither enacts anything on the subject, and neither substitutes for the other.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both are planner-facing filters with nothing enacted on the subject, and they sit at consecutive design steps worth reading together: one chooses which behavior the intervention aims at, the other checks whether the chosen protocol's stated baselines determine the relations it should yield and blocks the run if not.; `peer-authored-target-selection` — both answer which targets the intervention should aim at, and the second is a direct authorship variant of the first: peers write the list with no self-veto instead of the operator applying design-time selection criteria. A reader on either should know about the other.; `preparatory-target-definition` — adjacent operator-side design moves that are easy to conflate. One decides which behavior the intervention should aim at, using selection criteria; the other is the hand-off that fixes the agreed operational definition and the watch-list before observation begins. Choosing a target and pinning down how it will be recorded are consecutive steps, and each entry's boundary is clearer next to the other.


<a id="genus-205"></a>

## operator-side-prep (3)

Disciplines that act on the operator, not the listener — pinning target definitions, drilling the operator's own precision, and stocking tactical material before any technique fires.

[operator-resource-generation](#entry-839) · [operator-training-via-monitor](#entry-758) · [preparatory-target-definition](#entry-510)


<a id="entry-839"></a>

### operator-resource-generation

[#839](#entry-839) · [Back to operator-side-prep](#genus-205) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Operator-side disciplines for SOURCING the content/tactics an intervention will use, before any technique fires — shaping the fix's material rather than pushing a subject state. Demonstrated forms: a fixed-order fallback cascade for producing a new behavior (recall a personal-history success in full sensory detail; if none, model someone who succeeds; if still none, fabricate/pretend; last, operator-coach the steps), then perform it immediately and check intended=received — justified by a congruence-preference rationale where each step down trades congruence for availability; a generate-N-before-committing count-gate where a monitor refuses commitment to the first tactic and repeats "how else could you get it?" until at least three distinct routes to a pre-named sub-outcome exist, building spare tactics so a failed move becomes a switch not a stall; and a recruit-existing-capacity redirect that blocks fresh construction and directs the subject to enlist an already-present part that demonstrably has the needed quality, treating internal resources as composable modules so the new function inherits proven competence. The shared lever is that the operator disciplines how the tactical/behavioral resource is produced (ordered fallback, count-gated redundancy, reuse-over-construction), building the operator's option set rather than moving a listener dimension.


**When to reach for this.** Not generic brainstorming/coaching — the tell in each is a hard discipline on sourcing: a strict ordered fallback justified by congruence and live-tested; a count-gate hard-bound to a pre-named outcome that blocks advancing on one option; or a reuse-over-construction redirect. None is a subject-state move — the payoff lands in the operator's tactical repertoire or the fix's content, not any x(t).


**Risk.** Operator-preparation/content-generation with (for the cascade) live verification; session-scoped, reversible, no consent surface or channel erosion — trainer/planning layer.


**Why it works.** The generate-three-options gate counters premature closure — people converge on the first adequate solution and stop searching, so an explicit count requirement forces the search past the first satisficing answer and reliably increases both the number and the quality of the best option in the set. The ordered fallback runs on congruence: self-generated content recruits the subject's own retrieval and motor memory, which is why recalling a real prior success outperforms adopting a modeled or operator-supplied one, with each step down the ladder trading fidelity for availability. Reuse-over-construction rests on the fact that an already-fluent response requires no acquisition trials, only re-cueing. Falsifiable: if first-generated tactics performed as well as best-of-three, or if operator-supplied behaviours transferred as well as recalled ones, the disciplines would be pointless. [plausible; premature closure in option generation; self-generation and retrieval fluency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Ordered fallback for sourcing a new behavior*
  - "If Rita says 'I've never succeeded…' I ask for a model… I can even say 'Well, make it up.'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Three routes before committing to one*
  - "If you've got only one choice, you are a robot. If you've got only two, you are in a dilemma. However, if you've got three, you begin to have behavioral flexibility." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Recruit an existing capacity, don't build one*
  - "I think it probably would be better if you found an ally that's already in there. You don't need to build a whole new ally." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `operator-delivery-craft` — both are operator-side disciplines whose object is the operator rather than the subject's state: one governs how the tactical material is sourced before anything fires, the other governs the transmitted signal itself. A reader working on operator craft rather than subject moves is served by the pair.; `parts-work-procedure-craft` — both are operator-side craft rather than subject-state moves, but one structures the running of a parts negotiation or reframe while the other disciplines how the intervention's content and tactics are sourced before anything fires.; `target-selection` — two different operator-side design levers a writer uses in sequence and can be read together: one filters WHAT the intervention should aim at, producing a target list; the other disciplines HOW the tactical material to get there is generated, producing an option set. Neither enacts anything on the subject, and neither substitutes for the other.


<a id="entry-758"></a>

### operator-training-via-monitor

[#758](#entry-758) · [Back to operator-side-prep](#genus-205) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

A monitor or acted stand-in exposes defects in an operator's own instructions or procedural choices, so the object of correction is the operator's craft. Two realizations are preserved. (a) FEIGNED-LITERALIST STAND-IN: a trainer role-plays a confused client and refuses to fill gaps in the trainee's instructions, requiring the trainee to specify the referent, internal action and sensory channel. This makes ambiguity visible during training. (b) ARTICULATION CHECKPOINT: a trainer or supervisor interrupts procedural drift and asks which protocol step the operator is on, what specific outcome is intended, and how the preceding action is expected to produce it. The operator supplies the answers rather than having the observer repair the move for them. Both use an external perspective to force explicit procedure and reasoning; neither requires reclassifying an actual client assessment as a rehearsal.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this when a training partner or observer makes the operator expose and correct their own procedural gaps. Use the acted-literalist form for ambiguous instructions and the articulation checkpoint for a mismatch between step, intended outcome and chosen action.
