**When to reach for this.** The disclaimer is instrumental to installing the desire and leaves the operator unconstrained — unlike a genuine agency reminder, which preserves real choice and exit. What separates it from a plain post-hypnotic suggestion is the deliberate two-channel split that laminates disclaimed obligation onto installed craving.


**Risk.** Coercion removed WHILE craving installed so the want reads as self-owned — the refusal channel is not eroded by force but relabeled away, which the risk rubric scores high (refusal/verification-channel manipulation).


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory predicts people infer their own attitudes from their behaviour minus any salient external cause; removing the coercion cue leaves no situational explanation for the wanting, so it is attributed internally as authentic desire. This is insufficient justification (a dissonance/attribution effect), not over-justification in reverse — over-justification concerns added extrinsic reward undermining existing intrinsic motivation and is a separate finding. Falsifiable: adding an explicit obligation ('you must') should reduce, not increase, rated ownership of the desire. [established; self-perception theory; insufficient-justification / over-justification effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Obligation denied, desire installed*
  - **Setup.** Late session, deep; a purchase or tribute has been named and the two-channel split is being delivered.
  - **The move.** You don't have to. I'm not asking you for anything and nothing is owed — this is entirely yours to decide. But when this ends you're going to find yourself pulled to go and look. And when you think about what your money does for me, that thought will feel good all evening, and again tomorrow, and probably the day after.
  - **Why it lands.** Each request for money is delivered in two halves. First the obligation is explicitly withdrawn — there is no requirement, nothing is being demanded of you, this is entirely up to you. Then the desire is installed at full strength: you will find yourself pulled to go and look once this ends, and the thought of what your money buys will keep feeling good for hours, maybe days. Nothing was asked and nothing was owed, so when the purchase happens it presents itself as the listener's own idea.


**See also.** `addiction-drug-craving-frame` — genuinely useful crossing for anyone installing appetite. One labels the desire-to-return as craving using appetite and dose vocabulary; the other manufactures the same craving while explicitly disclaiming obligation, so the want reads as self-authored. They stack in practice and are frequently confused because both end with a listener who wants to return.; `experiential-consent-trial` — direct inverses on the who-is-constrained axis. One blocks the install pending a lived, endorsed trial that can return abort; the other brackets every ask with a denial of compulsion precisely to make the installed craving read as self-authored. The second is the counterfeit of the first.; `illusory-choice-into-obedience` — both stage an apparent freedom in order to make the ensuing compliance read as self-authored desire, differing in placement: one has the listener explicitly NOTICE the option immediately before a command, the other laminates a standing 'you do not have to' disclaimer onto a maximally installed craving. Same laundering logic, and the disclaimer-versus-noticed-option distinction is exactly what a writer needs.; `own-desire-attribution` — both make an installed want read as self-authored. One relocates its authorship into the listener's past; the other strips the obligation channel so the craving looks freely held. Complementary routes to the same disavowal-proofing.


<a id="entry-378"></a>

### forced-choice-wake

[#378](#entry-378) · [Back to real-world-follow-through](#genus-176) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: emergence*

At wake, after a hard stop, the operator presents the subject a binary they must choose between — (a) leave aroused-but-denied (a "cold shower", pleasure decaying) or (b) keep repeating the mantra post-wake until orgasm — then withdraws ("I wonder what choice you'll make… choose wisely"). The choice architecture is rigged: whichever branch the subject takes confirms the installed framework (coming validates the mantra-pleasure system; not-coming validates the operator's denial authority). The reward weighting is asymmetric ("come so fucking hard" vs bare "back to yourself") but presented as nominally equal, routing toward the compliance branch, and the orgasm route extends conditioning past runtime (orgasm conditional on continued mantra-recitation). Agency is offered as cover for a decision whose every outcome serves the install.


**When to reach for this.** A forced binary at emergence where BOTH outcomes confirm the installed framework, with asymmetric-but-disguised reward weighting and at least one branch that fires conditioning outside runtime. The tell is the rigged either/or whose branches both validate the system, dressed as free agency.


**Risk.** A rigged choice whose branches both ratify the system erodes the refusal channel (non-compliance is relabeled a validating choice), and the orgasm branch extends conditioning out of session — channel erosion plus out-of-session reach meets high.


**Why it works.** This is a rigged choice architecture whose real work is done by self-perception and effort justification: the subject who picks a branch will infer their own preferences from the act of picking, and because both branches were authored to confirm the frame, the inference lands in the same place either way. The illusion of free choice is not incidental — freely-chosen behaviour produces stronger attitude change than coerced identical behaviour, so offering agency increases rather than decreases the effect. The asymmetric reward weighting supplies the actual routing. Falsifiable: remove the choice and impose one branch, and if attitude change is equal or greater, the agency framing is not the lever. [established; induced compliance / free-choice paradigm; self-perception; effort justification]


**Worked examples.**

- *A rigged binary offered at the wake*
  - **Setup.** Subject held at peak arousal, mantra trained and rehearsed; operator stops abruptly.
  - **The move.** Stop. Hands still. You have two choices now. You can get up, let all of that drain out of you, and go be a normal person about it. Or you can keep saying the phrase, over and over, exactly the way I taught you, until you come so hard you cannot see. I wonder what you'll do. Choose wisely.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator halts everything at peak arousal, then lays out two doors and steps back. Door one: get up now, let it drain away, go be normal about it. Door two: keep saying the phrase until you finish. The doors are described as equals, but only one of them is described in detail and with heat, and only one of them keeps the conditioning running after the audio stops. Whichever door the listener takes, the framework is confirmed — finishing proves the phrase works, stopping proves the operator's permission mattered. She wonders aloud which it will be, tells them to choose well, and leaves.


**See also.** `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — the wake-line binary is the emergence-boundary instance of the rigged-menu lever: both branches serve the install, agency is offered as cover. Reader of the general choice-architecture move gains from the specific placement at emergence where one branch fires conditioning past session end.; `rigged-response-game-no-win` — both are rigged choice architectures where every reachable branch delivers the payload and apparent agency is the cover: one is an unwinnable or self-administering game mid-session, the other a binary offered at emergence whose branches both confirm the install. The shared reachability constraint is genuinely instructive across the two.; `self-supplied-order-hook` — both close the session by offloading the payload onto the subject's own act at emergence rather than stating it outright, so the reader choosing between them benefits from the contrast: one rigs a stated binary whose branches both confirm, the other supplies no content at all and forces self-completion. Genuinely different mechanisms, adjacent slot.


<a id="entry-1309"></a>

### out-of-audio-compliance-offload

[#1309](#entry-1309) · [Back to real-world-follow-through](#genus-176) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: tethering*

Transfers a state-transition (deepening / compliance-proof) OUT of the audio into a second medium where the operator has no live control — the recording tells the listener to pause, leave the audio, perform a specific motor act in a separate channel (click a button in an email), then resume, with the external act itself framed as the deepener. The listener's own out-of-band motor act becomes materially-performed proof of obedience, pre-tagged to double depth; returning carries the just-completed compliance back into the session as a state delta.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the transfer of the state-transition work to a separate channel, not a cue that activates in text.


**Risk.** Out-of-session motor compliance in a second medium (email) where the act is materially performed and possibly tracked extends the operator's reach beyond the recording; no channel erosion but an out-of-session behavioral hook warrants medium.


**Why it works.** People infer their own attitudes from their freely-performed behavior, and an overt, effortful act in a separate channel is far harder to discount than a private feeling — so the subject reads compliance off her own conduct rather than off the operator's claim. It also runs as a foot-in-the-door: a completed small request raises compliance with the next. Falsifiable: predicts a weaker state delta when the external act is trivial, coerced, or attributable to something other than the subject's own choice. [established; self-perception theory; foot-in-the-door]


**Worked examples.**

- *Deepening performed outside the recording*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; a message with a control in it is already open in another window.
  - **The move.** Pause the audio here. Stay right where you are, stay under, and go to the message waiting in your other window — press the button you find there. Pressing it is what takes you deeper; that's what it's for. Then come back, press play, and you'll find yourself twice as far down as you are now.
  - **Why it lands.** The audio instructs the listener to stop the audio. Stay under, it says, switch to the message waiting in the other window, act on the control you find there, then come back. That action is not incidental — it is named in advance as the thing that will deepen the state. So the state-change happens in a second medium, out of the operator's live reach, and it happens by a real motor act the listener performs and cannot afterwards deny performing. Returning to the recording, they bring that freshly completed act of obedience back in with them, and the pattern repeats at the next one.


**See also.** `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — same lever, different channel: an act is performed and then read back as proof of the target state. One keeps it inside the session, the other exports it to a second medium where the act is materially performed and possibly tracked. The in-session versus out-of-band binding is exactly what a reader must decide, so the pointer is warranted.; `cross-media-forced-continuation` — both send the listener out of the current recording to complete something, and the useful contrast is what the departure accomplishes. In one, a withheld faculty stays locked until another product is consumed, a retention hook. In the other, the listener steps out, performs a motor act, and returns carrying that compliance back as depth. Adjacent enough that a reader should check both.; `obedience-demonstration-as-proof` — a demonstrated act cited back as proof of control, versus that same proof beat relocated into a separate medium where the act is materially performed out of band. The second is the channel-transfer variant of the first's validation beat, so a reader of either wants the other.; `operator-receivable-extraction` — both send the listener out of the audio into a second channel to perform a real motor act and then return. The split is what the act is for: an artifact the operator receives, versus a state transition offloaded to another medium as the deepener itself. Surface text is near identical, so the pairing is load-bearing.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — both push the listener into a real, out-of-session motor act and then bank it as proof, which is a genuine classification fork. The split is where the act lands and what it buys: one drives a public attributable disclosure under a maintained eyes-open overlay that self-ratifies the trance, the other exports the state-transition itself into a second channel so returning carries the completed compliance back as a depth delta.


<a id="genus-255"></a>

## reassigned-feeling-sources (2)

Techniques that rewrite where a felt state comes from, crediting the listener's pleasure to the operator or laundering a trance effect to a benign natural cause, so the feeling either binds attachment or slips past resistance.

[pleasure-attributed-to-operator](#entry-279) · [state-cause-laundering](#entry-294)


<a id="entry-279"></a>

### pleasure-attributed-to-operator

[#279](#entry-279) · [Back to reassigned-feeling-sources](#genus-255) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: conditioning*

TECHNIQUE (reward-source rerouting): relocate the SOURCE or unit of reinforcement away from the subject's own good feeling. The subject's baseline pleasure/comfort is re-credited to the operator's identity/voice/presence as its cause, so every later suggestion arrives pre-loaded with affect pointing at the speaker, continuing attention becomes self-rewarding, and compliance reads as the subject's own desire; often stated as already-established fact so the loop self-seals. Realizations: the subject's OWN pleasure re-credited to the operator as its source (the core); the reinforcer IS the operator's stated pleasure/gratification ('you made me feel good'), recoding compliance from command to affection so reasonableness-evaluation is disarmed; the operator's NAME slotted into an entrained mantra's prosodic slot so an already-conditioned affect ('love') silently re-points onto the person. The through-line: whose feeling counts, or whose person the affect points at, is rerouted onto the operator.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the reinforcer/credit is moved ONTO the operator — the operator's pleasure is the reward, or the subject's pleasure/affect is re-sourced or re-pointed to the operator. Choose a SIBLING when: pleasure is welded to the subject's own act/state with no source-relocation (-> direct-reward-linkage); the subject's affect is re-labeled as PROOF of obedience rather than re-sourced (-> arousal-as-obedience-readout); the cause of a state is laundered AWAY from the operator (-> state-cause-laundering, the opposite move). Source/unit-relocation-onto-the-operator is the tell.


**Risk.** Re-sources the subject's pleasure to the operator so attention becomes self-rewarding and compliance reads as own desire; self-sealing.


**Why it works.** Repeatedly pairing a person with positively-valenced states shifts liking for that person through evaluative conditioning, an effect that operates without the subject noticing the pairing and that survives their knowing about it. The re-credit step adds source misattribution: internal states are ambiguous as to cause, so a confidently supplied external explanation gets adopted, and once the operator is the believed source, continued contact is intrinsically motivating. Falsifiable: if subjects given the same pleasant states with a competing causal explanation rated the operator no more positively than controls, the re-sourcing account would fail. [established; evaluative conditioning; misattribution of a state's cause]


**Worked examples.**

- *The subject's own baseline pleasure re-credited to the operator as its source*
  - **Setup.** Any point where the subject is already comfortable, warm and settled — the good feeling is present before the line is delivered.
  - **The move.** That warm, heavy, easy feeling all through your chest right now — feel where it is coming from. It is coming out of my voice and into you. It has always come from my voice. That is simply what my voice does to you, and you have known that for a long time.
  - **Why it lands.** An existing, genuine feeling is re-sourced to the operator and asserted as already-established fact, so every later suggestion arrives carrying that affect and continued listening becomes self-rewarding. Operator observes the subject seeking the voice for comfort in unrelated contexts and describing the operator, not the state, as the thing they want.
- *The operator's stated pleasure installed as the reinforcer*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the subject completes a small requested action — a held breath, a repeated phrase, a position change.
  - **The move.** Oh, that was good. You have no idea what it does to me when you do that so easily. Say it once more, just like that, because I want to feel that again.
  - **Why it lands.** The reward unit becomes the operator's gratification rather than the subject's, which recodes compliance from instruction-following into affection and disarms reasonableness-checking — you do not audit a gift. Observable as the subject volunteering compliance unbidden and checking the operator's response after each act.
- *The operator's name slotted into an entrained mantra's prosodic slot*
  - **Setup.** Late in a repetition sequence; the subject has already been chanting a fixed-rhythm line such as 'I love this feeling' for several minutes.
  - **The move.** Keep the rhythm exactly. Same beat, same breath — only the last word changes now. I love this feeling. I love this voice. I love this voice. Now again, and this time it is my name in that place, and it fits, doesn't it.
  - **Why it lands.** The conditioned affect is already bound to the slot's rhythm, so substituting the operator into that slot re-points existing feeling onto a person without ever asserting the claim outright. Operator watches for the substitution being made without hesitation or change in cadence — hesitation on the swap means the affect has not transferred yet.


**Realizations** (2): `name-substitution-affect-binding`, `operator-pleasure-as-reward-unit`


**See also.** `attribution-capture-of-internal-states` — both reroute credit onto the operator, one for the subject's pleasure or the reinforcement unit, the other for the causal attribution of the subject's present state generally. Reward-source relocation is arguably a special case of state-attribution capture, so the pointer is needed to keep the assignment stable. Not a merge — the affect-pointing version carries a reinforcement function the general form does not.; `become-the-discriminative-stimulus` — both route the subject's motivation through the operator's person, and the contrast is the useful part: one re-credits the subject's own pleasure to the operator inside a session, the other builds a history in which the operator's presence becomes the cue that evokes the subject's requesting. Sending a reader from one to the other prevents mislabeling a relational dependency as an in-session affect reroute.; `obedience-motive-reattribution` — both relocate something onto the operator, and the pairing clarifies a real boundary: one re-sources the reward or affect itself, the other re-attributes the motive behind the listener's own self-directed everyday acts. Useful adjacency for a writer deciding which reattribution they actually want, since the second operates entirely outside runtime on pre-existing personal goals.; `operator-credit-engineering` — two directions of the same attribution-relocation family: credit for effects versus credit for pleasure, both routed onto the operator. A writer choosing an attribution move should see both.; `reward-channel-rerouting` — both restructure reward, and a reader deciding between them benefits from seeing the split: one relocates the credit for a good feeling onto the operator, the other remaps which content is permitted to feel rewarding at all. A passage can do both, so the boundary is worth signposting.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — both reroute credit for a good feeling onto the operator without the operator producing it. One re-sources the listener's baseline pleasure to the operator's presence; the other has the listener generate the reward while the operator keeps only the framing — the second is close to the first run at loop scale.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both re-credit something the listener generated to the operator, but one moves the reward source (whose pleasure counts) and the other moves sensory authorship (whose hand is touching). Related enough to be confused in erotic material where they frequently co-occur, and the source-versus-authorship distinction is the useful thing to carry across.; `stakeholder-obligation-bond` — both re-route reinforcement toward the operator, one by re-sourcing the subject's own pleasure to the operator and the other by binding the two parties' pleasure so refusal becomes a relational failure. The second reads as a relational-obligation neighbor of the first's reward-rerouting lever.


<a id="entry-294"></a>

### state-cause-laundering

[#294](#entry-294) · [Back to reassigned-feeling-sources](#genus-255) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: authorship-shift*

Supplies an alternative (false) causal story for trance-shaped phenomenology so the listener's "I feel X" is attributed to a benign/natural cause rather than to the operator's suggestion. A real, already- running state is given a laundered cause, so the listener does not attribute the state to being influenced and therefore does not resist it.


**When to reach for this.** An ALTERNATIVE (false) cause is asserted for a real, already-running state. vs confusion techniques: no confusion is induced; a clean causal misattribution is supplied. vs pleasure-attributed-to-operator: that re-credits pleasure TO the operator; here the state's cause is laundered AWAY from the operator to a benign source. State-cause laundering is authorship-relocation of causation, not a felt-automaticity split.


**Risk.** Misattributes a suggestion-caused state to a benign cause so the listener does not resist it; covert.


**Why it works.** Resistance to influence is triggered by detecting a persuasion attempt; supplying a benign alternative cause for a state the listener is already in prevents that detection, so the state feels endogenous and no counter-pressure is mounted. This is misattribution running in the operator's favour, and it works precisely because the state is real — there is nothing to disbelieve, only a cause to accept. Falsifiable: subjects given a benign causal story for an induced state should show less reactance and rate themselves as less influenced than subjects told the operator caused it, despite equivalent measured state. [plausible; misattribution; persuasion-knowledge activation and reactance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Heaviness and drift re-attributed to ordinary tiredness*
  - **Setup.** Ten minutes in; the subject is visibly going under and starting to notice it.
  - **The move.** That heaviness in your arms — that's just how tired you actually were. You've been running on nothing all week. This isn't anything I'm doing, this is your body finally taking what it's owed. Let it.
  - **Why it lands.** A real, already-running trance state is handed a benign cause, so the subject stops attributing the state to influence and therefore has nothing to resist. Operator observes deepening continuing without the guardedness that usually follows a subject noticing they are going under.
- *Arousal re-attributed to the subject's own long-standing nature*
  - **Setup.** The subject has just noticed they are aroused by material they did not expect to find arousing, and is unsettled.
  - **The move.** Nothing here made you feel that. This has been in you since long before you found me — you've just never had anywhere to put it. All I did was stop pretending it wasn't there. This is you recognising yourself.
  - **Why it lands.** The causal story relocates authorship of the response from the operator's suggestion to the subject's own pre-existing identity, which converts alarm into recognition and removes the target that resistance would aim at. Tell is the subject taking up the explanation as their own and reporting it back later as self-knowledge.


**See also.** `arousal-cognition-shutdown-law` — both hand the listener an operator-authored causal story for a genuinely felt state so the state is not attributed to influence.; `attribution-capture-of-internal-states` — directional inverses on the same axis: one launders a running state's cause AWAY from the operator to a benign source, the other captures that cause ONTO the operator. A reader choosing between them needs the direction test, so the cross-link earns its place.; `causal-attribution-to-external-agent` — directly contrastive on the same axis — where the cause of an induced state is assigned. One relocates causation onto a named external agent that is asserted to be doing it; the other supplies a benign natural cause so nothing appears to be doing it at all. Opposite felt results from the same relocation move; each discriminator already names the other.; `compliance-authorship-laundering` — twin authorship relocations that answer different questions. One relocates agency for the act to the listener as their own will or preference; the other relocates the cause of an already-running state onto a benign source and away from the operator. Adjacent enough to be miscoded for each other, so a mutual pointer is the useful guard.; `concurrent-pleasure-reattribution` — the mirror-image attribution move: a running state is given a laundered cause pointing away from the operator instead of toward obedience.; `fictional-substance-agent` — both relocate causation for a felt state away from the operator's suggestion, but laundering asserts a plausible benign real cause for an already-running state while the substance form invents a fictional carrier with narrated pharmacology that the listener must imagine.; `manufactured-deficit-compliance-relief` — shares the causal-misattribution move: the felt state's true source (the suggestion) is hidden behind a laundered cause so the listener does not resist it.; `object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition` — both relocate authorship of a running state away from the listener-operator pair, but to different destinations: one supplies a benign natural cause, the other installs an external object as the active causal agent. An object declared causal of the mind-state is a special case worth cross-reading when deciding which authorship-relocation is in play.; `operator-agency-disavowal` — both move causal attribution away from the operator while steering continues, but one denies the operator exists or acts at all so resistance has no target, while the other leaves the operator in place and supplies a benign false cause for a state already running.; `unattributable-cause-severing` — same lever at two scales: supplying a false benign cause for one running state, versus a whole-arc design in which every outcome is severed from any locatable cause. A reader coding a single misattribution should know whether the surrounding artifact makes it the through-line.


<a id="genus-232"></a>

## reassigning-authority (3)

Restructure who holds decision power — revoking it rung by rung, briefly inverting it, or laddering the resister into endorsing the outcome — so the subject's own participation locks in the new arrangement.

[authority-role-inversion](#entry-1228) · [decision-rights-revocation-ladder](#entry-91) · [superordinate-agreement-ladder](#entry-1268)


<a id="entry-1228"></a>

### authority-role-inversion

[#1228](#entry-1228) · [Back to reassigning-authority](#genus-232) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: social-topology*

The operator offers to be the contractee — the higher-power party performs a task while the lower-power target controls and delivers the reward — explicitly conceding the suspected unfairness. The target gets direct evidence that contracts are honored and that they hold real power, dissolving an "I always get the short end" prior through a demonstrated reversal of the power asymmetry; a power-imbalance objection is converted into trust by enacted role reversal.


**When to reach for this.** A writer reaches for this entry when the operator volunteers to take the performing side of the first contract — 'let's make the first contract be for my (our) behavior and you control the reward' — explicitly conceding the target's suspicion that contracts are rigged against them. The observable tell is an enacted inversion of the power asymmetry: the higher-power party performs the task while the lower-power target holds enforcement and delivers the reward, on the subject themselves rather than on any third party. The payoff is evidentiary — the target directly witnesses a contract being honored while they hold real power, converting an 'I always get the short end' prior into trust.


**Risk.** A trust-building role reversal that hands the target real power; protective/relational, no channel erosion or durable adverse scope.


**Why it works.** Trust is updated by demonstrated behaviour far more than by assertion, and a costly, disconfirming demonstration updates a prior faster than a cheap one — this is the standard logic of belief revision under evidence, and the operator taking the disadvantaged role makes the demonstration costly. Conceding the unfairness first adds a separate lever: acknowledging a legitimate objection before the target raises it reduces the perception of manipulative intent and increases persuasion, a well-supported two-sided-message effect. Falsifiable: it predicts a larger shift in the target's fairness expectations after an enacted reversal than after a verbal promise of fair dealing; equal shifts would refute it. [plausible; trust updating from costly demonstration; two-sided messages / preemptive concession reduces perceived manipulative intent]


**Worked examples.**

- *Operator signs the first contract as the performer*
  - "let's make the first contract be for my (our) behavior and you control the reward... the nonsigner may learn that contracts can work" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — both redistribute who holds the contract roles. One fades authorship gradually until the subject is both parties; the other is a single enacted reversal in which the operator performs and the target enforces, aimed at an unfairness prior. Endpoint and duration differ, and each already names the other as its boundary case.; `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` — both manufacture trust by staging a power dynamic for the target's benefit, but favor theater fabricates an off-stage adversary to create felt debt (it collapses if the empty office is glimpsed), whereas role inversion stages a genuine reversal the target actually enforces, targeting an unfairness prior rather than manufacturing obligation.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — both dissolve a control or fairness objection by enacting and visibly honoring a power relocation rather than arguing it. Distinguish by whether termination authority is handed over or the roles are outright reversed.


<a id="entry-91"></a>

### decision-rights-revocation-ladder

[#91](#entry-91) · [Back to reassigning-authority](#genus-232) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: compliance*

Enumerates specific decision-authorities the listener 'used to think' they held — what to wear, when to come, when to touch — and, via a fixed parallel frame ('you used to think you decide X / you don't decide that / I decide that'), strips each and reassigns it to the operator, climbing from low-stakes to high-stakes domains. The past-tense framing casts each surrender as already-completed rather than currently-requested, so no rung is posed as a live question; a live behavioral instruction (rub/edge) is folded in as one row so complying with the immediate act ratifies the whole surrender ledger. The move is authority-transfer by enumerated revocation, not agreement accretion.


**When to reach for this.** The tell: an itemized checklist of specific surrendered decision-domains framed as already-done.


**Risk.** Generalized transfer of named decision-authority (including orgasm control) is durable identity-scope reach and closes refusal on each revoked domain — the durable-identity-scope trigger in the rubric.


**Why it works.** Past-tense framing exploits presupposition: a sentence whose surface content is 'you used to think X' presupposes that you no longer do, and presupposed material is processed as background and challenged far less often than asserted material. Folding a live compliable act into the same enumerated series then lets self-perception do the rest — the listener observes their own compliance and infers the disposition that would explain it, ratifying the un-complied rungs by inference rather than by consent. Falsifiable: the same authority transfers stated as live requests ('will you let me decide X?') should draw sharply more refusal. [plausible; presupposition resistance to challenge; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Enumerated decision-rights revoked in past tense*
  - **Setup.** Deep, late in an established relationship; subject is passive and has taken instruction well tonight. The last rung must be a live physical instruction.
  - **The move.** You used to think you decided what you wore. You don't decide that. I decide that. You used to think you decided when you ate. You don't decide that. I decide that. You used to think you decided when your hand went between your legs. You don't decide that. I decide that — and it's going there now, two fingers, slowly. You used to think you decided when you came.
  - **Why it lands.** One frame, repeated with a new blank each time: you once believed the clothes were your call — they are not your call — that call is mine. Then the same three beats for when you eat, then for when you touch yourself, then for when you finish. Nothing is ever posed as a question, and the past tense does the heavy lifting: each right is described as something already handed over rather than something being asked for now, so there is no rung where a "no" would fit. The last rung is a live instruction, so obeying it in the moment signs off on every rung above it.


**See also.** `compliance-ladder`; `inverse-authority-gradient` — inverse movements on the same variable: an itemised revocation that reassigns named decision-rights to the operator, versus an unflagged arc that hands authority steadily back until the listener is sole authority on their own state. Instructive as a matched pair.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both present an itemized ledger that shifts the perceived baseline to already-surrendered, and both make later resistance feel like self-contradiction. The items differ in kind: one enumerates named decision-authorities and reassigns them in the past tense, the other annotates the listener's genuine recent behavior as evidence of a state. Choose by whether the ledger rows are fictive authorities or real acts.


<a id="entry-1268"></a>

### superordinate-agreement-ladder

[#1268](#entry-1268) · [Back to reassigning-authority](#genus-232) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: social-topology*

In a dispute/negotiation, make the RESISTER produce or publicly endorse the outcome themselves, so their own commitment binds later objection (refusing then reads as refusing their own stated position). VARIANTS: (a) ladder-to-umbrella-assent [superordinate-agreement-ladder] — ask each disputing party what they want, then what that would get them, climbing to ever-more-general outcomes until both assent OUT LOUD to one umbrella goal too general to disown (separating parties and re-broadening in stuck cases); once endorsed publicly, later resistance reads as refusing one's own interest and subsequent disagreements are subordinate to the shared frame; (b) objector-authors-the-fix [objector-authored-behavior] — ask the objecting party to specify FROM SCRATCH exactly what the other could do that they would recognize and respond to, framing being asked as a compliment; because the objector authors the target behavior it is guaranteed acceptable and cannot be rejected later, and being cast as expert-instructor recruits them as collaborator, so resistance is spent producing the specification instead of blocking an imposed fix. Pick by ladder-to-shared-goal (two parties, upward generalization) vs author-the-behavior (one objector originates the fix).


**When to reach for this.** The resister PRODUCES the endorsement (a publicly-assented umbrella goal, or a from-scratch specification of the acceptable behavior) so self-consistency binds later objection — the assent/authorship is real and load-bearing.


**Risk.** Durable public-commitment leverage makes later refusal socially costly, but every step is heard and endorsed aloud; no covert channel erosion.


**Why it works.** This runs on the consistency principle plus its amplification by public commitment: once someone has stated a position aloud in front of others, retracting it carries self-concept and reputational cost, so honouring it becomes the cheaper path. The author-the-fix variant additionally recruits the objector into a collaborator role, and role-consistent behaviour tends to follow role assignment. Clearly falsifiable — if objectors who publicly endorsed the umbrella goal or authored the fix went on to block at the same rate as those handed an equivalent goal or fix by the operator, the commitment lever is not the operative one. [established; consistency principle; public commitment; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *Climb to a goal neither side can disown*
  - "get as general as you need to in order to find an outcome that both partners will agree to" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (1): `objector-authored-behavior`


**See also.** `commitment-before-restructure-sequencing` — both neutralize the you-are-controlling-me objection by making the subject's own commitment do the binding. One banks a congruence-checked commitment to self-change before revealing what the change is; the other makes the resister produce or publicly endorse the outcome so refusing later means refusing their own stated position. Withheld-content ordering versus authored endorsement.; `compliance-ladder` — both accrete real assents that later objection must contradict, one via cheapest-first rungs in an induced state and one via a resister producing or authoring the endorsement in a dispute. The consistency lever is genuinely the same; the setting and who originates the assent differ. Worth linking, not merging — the second is a negotiation-context technique with a distinct authorship step.


<a id="genus-143"></a>

## rehearsal-before-reality (6)

The listener performs the act in fantasy or an imagined future first, so the real-world version arrives as a repetition of something already done rather than a fresh decision.

[fantasy-laundered-first-compliance](#entry-746) · [future-pacing](#entry-1070) · [imagined-to-enacted-collapse](#entry-1197) · [pseudo-orientation-in-time](#entry-1082) · [rehearsed-pre-commitment](#entry-1083) · [ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet](#entry-1093)


<a id="entry-746"></a>

### fantasy-laundered-first-compliance

[#746](#entry-746) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

An imaginal scene serves as the rehearsal venue for a real-world behavior: the listener executes the target act (chants, kneels) inside the fantasy before it is consciously assigned, so first compliance is laundered through fiction, arrives pre-memorized via in-scene repetition, and is pre-bound to a demanded affect the listener is later told to reproduce in real life.


**When to reach for this.** First execution precedes conscious assignment and consent — unlike an explicit if-then contract for waking-life behavior, unlike rehearsal the subject knowingly designs and practices, and unlike future pacing (an imagined future performance, not present covert execution).


**Risk.** First execution of an assigned real-world behavior happens before consent is asked, with out-of-session homework and affect binding.


**Why it works.** Executing an act in imagination lays down a memory trace that shares features with real execution, so later source monitoring can fail to distinguish "I imagined doing this" from "I did this" — the imagination-inflation effect. Once the act feels already-performed, self-perception supplies the inference that one is the kind of person who does it, and the real-world request becomes a small consistent step rather than a first commitment. Falsifiable: compliance with the later real-world request should be higher after in-scene rehearsal than after an equally vivid scene in which the listener only watches the act performed. [established; imagination inflation / source-monitoring error; self-perception and foot-in-the-door]


**Worked examples.**

- *Rehearsing the act inside the fantasy first*
  - **Setup.** Mid-trance imagery sequence; subject absorbed in a described scene and has not been told anything is being assigned.
  - **The move.** In the vision you're kneeling on cold stone, and you hear your own voice saying it back to me: I am kept, I am grateful, I am yours. The scene comes round again — kneeling, saying it, exactly the same. Now come up. Those are your words: every night before you sleep, on your knees, out loud, and with precisely the feeling you had on that stone.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator announces a vision, and inside it the listener kneels and speaks a set of phrases back — twice, because the scene loops. It is presented purely as something imagined. Only afterward does the operator surface and say: those phrases are yours now, you will speak them each night, and with the same feeling you had while kneeling. The listener has already performed the assignment, and already memorized it, before being told it was an assignment at all.


**See also.** `cultural-ritual-slot-hijack` — both launder a first compliance through a frame the listener does not read as hypnotic, so the act arrives already performed or already normal. One rehearses the target behavior inside an imagined scene before it is consciously assigned; the other substitutes the content into a cultural ritual the listener already practices, inheriting its weight and its durability past the session.; `diegetic-activity-laundering` — both route first compliance through a fiction so the listener is not evaluating a hypnotic suggestion, and they routinely co-occur. The distinction is whether the fiction relabels the whole session's genre or serves as a rehearsal venue for a real act.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — both exploit a fiction layer to get compliance without a real consent decision, but one manipulates the fiction/reality boundary so a fictional yes covers the real payload, while the other has the listener physically execute the target act inside the scene before it is ever consciously assigned.; `imagined-to-enacted-collapse` — both collapse an imagined act into an executed one inside a fiction that is never withdrawn: one launders a first real-world compliance through an imaginal rehearsal venue before it is consciously assigned, the other slides verb tense mid-paragraph from imagined to enacted. Close enough that a writer needs both discriminators side by side.; `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both convert a performed act into commitment before the listener can treat it as a decision, and the boundary between them is clean enough to be worth stating: one annotates the listener's genuine real-world acts as evidence of an already-present state; the other has the listener execute the target act inside a fantasy before it is consciously assigned. Real-act annotation versus fiction-laundered first execution.; `pre-induction-compliance-ratchet` — both engineer a first compliance before the listener can weigh it, but the venue differs: one banks a real physical act in the waking state before any trance language, the other has the act executed inside an imagined scene before it is consciously assigned. A writer choosing where to place first compliance benefits from seeing both.


<a id="entry-1070"></a>

### future-pacing

[#1070](#entry-1070) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: encoding*

Declaratively projects a suggested response or state into future situations as automatic and inevitable (every time X, you will Y). Broadened from v6.9 to cover the delivery vehicles the corpus demonstrates for the same lever — unmarked grammatical slides that hand the listener's own rehearsal back as forecast, continuous future-tense streams that offload verification to the listener's future self, and pre-scripted future intrusive thoughts framed in advance as the listener's own preference.


**When to reach for this.** The move EXTENDS a specified effect forward by declaration and the projection can observably fail. It does not build a both-branches-confirm topology (future-confirmation-capture), does not presuppose an already-solved past-tense future and elicit it as memory (pseudo-orientation-in-time), does not bank a decision through rehearsal (rehearsed-pre-commitment), and does not wire reinforcement to a self-administered biological event (inevitable-event-reinforcement-fuse).


**Risk.** Raised from low — broadened scope explicitly includes out-of-session return-pull installs with no expiration (two members); expiration pairing is the natural bound.


**Why it works.** Explicitly imagining a specific response in a specific future context increases the likelihood of that response by forming a cue-response association and by raising the subjective probability of the event (imagined scenarios feel more likely once simulated). Naming the triggering situation supplies a concrete retrieval cue, which is why 'every time X' outperforms an unanchored prediction. It is falsifiable in the ordinary way: the forecast response can simply fail to appear when X occurs. [established; implementation intentions; imagination inflation and expectancy]


**Worked examples.**

- *Imagining slides into predicting*
  - **Setup.** Early in the session; the subject has been asked only to imagine a scene and is building it willingly.
  - **The move.** Picture the shop — the doorway, the light inside, the shelf you'd go to first. Imagine how it might feel to walk out of there with it in your bag. Feel how easy that is. And that's how it will feel, Thursday, when you're actually standing there. That's your own answer, not mine — you just showed it to me.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening asks only for imagination — picture the shop, picture how you would feel walking out. The listener builds the scene willingly, because it is only a game. Then, inside the same paragraph and without any marker, the grammar changes: what you might feel becomes what you will feel, and the operator confirms it as a forecast. The listener's own vivid rehearsal, produced with defences down, is handed back to them as evidence of what they are going to do.
- *Future-tense barrage with no checkpoints*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; a long declarative run with no pauses, no checks, and no request for feedback.
  - **The move.** Your hands are getting lighter and they'll keep getting lighter. Your voice is going softer and it will stay softer. You'll find yourself standing differently. You'll notice you take up less room. You'll want less, and you'll be happier wanting less. You'll stop needing to finish sentences. All of it is already underway.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator lists change after change, all in the future tense, and never pauses to ask whether any of it is happening yet. Each claim is asserted as already underway before the previous one has been dwelt on, so verification is always deferred to a later self. The listener never gets the beat in which they could check one item against their body — and one thing that does feel slightly different later gets read as confirmation of the whole list.
- *The next session's thought scripted in advance*
  - **Setup.** Closing minutes, before emergence; the subject is being pointed at the next session.
  - **The move.** The next time will be smoother than this — quicker down, easier, less work for you. And sometime Wednesday afternoon, in the middle of something ordinary, a thought is going to turn up on its own: I wonder when I can do that again. Just a small, curious, pleasant thought. Yours.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator forecasts not just that the listener will return but exactly what the return will feel like from the inside — smoother, quicker, easier than this time — and then supplies the sentence that will arrive in their head some ordinary afternoon: a mild, curious wondering about when they can do this again. When that thought duly surfaces days later it presents as the listener's own idle preference, not as something that was written down for them in advance.


**See also.** `pacing-leading` — genuine boundary: one projects an unverified effect forward by declaration, the other couples an unverified lead onto clauses the listener can confirm as true right now. A reader deciding between forecast and borrowed truth-status needs both.; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — tense-mirrored pair: one asserts the target as already settled so no decision point exists, the other projects a specified effect forward by declaration in a way that can observably fail. The contrast clarifies both.; `prospective-resistance-foreclosure` — both project a rule forward past the present moment, but one extends a specified effect that can observably fail while the other pre-assigns a null or aversive outcome to a whole class of future mental acts. The failure-possible versus comparator-deleted contrast is the reason to read them together.


<a id="entry-1197"></a>

### imagined-to-enacted-collapse

[#1197](#entry-1197) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: encoding*

Every action is preceded by an imagined more-outrageous version, then the gap closes mid-paragraph as verb tense slides unflagged from imagined to enacted (you imagine yourself... you walk over... you're doing this for real) inside a frame still acknowledged as dream. Imagination is conditioned as the rehearsal phase for action, imaginative and executed acts link along an operator-controlled sliding scale, and the affect paid out for imagining carries into the enactment.


**When to reach for this.** The unflagged tense slide reclassifies the reality-status of PRESENT content as enacted-for-real — separating it from guided visualization (content stays hypothetical) and from future-pacing (the product there is a future projection, not an enacted-now feeling).


**Risk.** Trains imagination as the on-ramp to action — durable but bounded by the acknowledged-dream frame; the frame IS the bound, so a host must keep it explicit.


**Why it works.** Memory for the source and reality-status of an experience is a reconstructive judgment made from qualities like vividness and perceptual detail, not a tag stored at encoding — so imagined content that is highly detailed and continuous with enacted content is systematically prone to being misclassified as real. Repeatedly imagining an act also raises confidence that it occurred, the imagination-inflation effect, and the unflagged tense slide removes the boundary marker the source-monitoring judgment would otherwise use. Falsifiable: if content delivered with explicit reality-status flags at each transition were misattributed as often as the unflagged slide, the source-monitoring account is wrong. [established; source-monitoring framework, imagination inflation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Tense slides from imagined to actually doing it*
  - **Setup.** Mid-fantasy, dream frame explicit; several imagine-then-do cycles already run and accepted.
  - **The move.** So you imagine standing up in the middle of that room and saying it to every single one of them. That's the bold version. In the softer one, you just imagine leaning over to the one person and saying it quietly. You're picturing yourself doing that. Picturing your hand on the back of their chair. You lean over. You say it — out loud, and this one isn't the imagining anymore, this one you're actually doing. It's still just a daydream. Keep going.
  - **Why it lands.** Every act in the sequence is first rehearsed in a bolder version and then performed in a milder one, so imagining has become the ordinary first half of doing. Then, without any marker, the grammar shifts inside a single paragraph: the listener is picturing themselves doing the thing, and two sentences later the verbs have moved into the present and the operator notes that this one is no longer rehearsal. The frame around all of it is still openly a daydream, which is what lets the reclassification pass unchallenged — and the pleasure already paid out for the imagined version transfers intact to the enacted one.


**See also.** `fantasy-laundered-first-compliance` — both collapse an imagined act into an executed one inside a fiction that is never withdrawn: one launders a first real-world compliance through an imaginal rehearsal venue before it is consciously assigned, the other slides verb tense mid-paragraph from imagined to enacted. Close enough that a writer needs both discriminators side by side.; `fiction-frame-consent-management` — both exploit the boundary between what is merely described and what is actually done, one by using the fiction layer as the consent instrument and one by sliding tense unflagged from imagined to enacted. The in-fiction rehearsal variant of the first sits close enough to the second that a reader should see both before choosing.; `phantom-body-ontological-reversal` — two ways of dissolving the imagined/real boundary that a writer will weigh against each other. One slides verb tense unflagged from imagined to enacted so present content reclassifies as done for real. The other declares the imagined body ontologically primary and lets the waking body recede, relocating sensory authority and disabling reality-testing. Unmarked drift versus explicit reversal.


<a id="entry-1082"></a>

### pseudo-orientation-in-time

[#1082](#entry-1082) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: encoding*

Projects the subject into a future where the present problem is already solved, speaks of it in the past tense as accomplished fact, and elicits the solution as RECALLED memory rather than invented hope — the operator claims to have forgotten the specifics and asks the subject to describe what they did. Presupposing the solution exists and was authored by the subject recruits generation of acceptable novel behavior past the conscious I-can't-think-of-any impasse, while expectancy points at an already-achieved outcome.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is past-tense-as-solved-memory framing plus elicitation by recall (not imagine): future-pacing extends a specified effect forward declaratively, and guided visualization keeps the content hypothetical, while here the solution is presupposed as accomplished fact and retrieved as the subject's own memory; the product is an elicited plan, not an unfalsifiable claim.


**Risk.** Session-scoped elicitation, reversible, no consent surface; both members therapeutic-literature demonstrations.


**Why it works.** Retrieval framing changes what is produced: asking someone to recall what they did recruits generation of concrete, self-authored, plausible content, whereas asking them to invent a solution invites the same evaluative filtering that produced the impasse. Presupposition also does work — the solution's existence is embedded in the question rather than asserted, so it is not the proposition under scrutiny. The claim is falsifiable and modest: past-tense recall framing should yield more and more specific solution content than hypothetical framing, with no implication that the retrieved plan is a genuine memory. [plausible; presupposition; generation under recall framing vs. evaluative filtering]


**Worked examples.**

- *Recalling the solution you have not found yet*
  - "induce a deep trance and use a technique called 'pseudo-orientation in time'… 'Would you describe in detail what you did?'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Asking the client what the cure was*
  - "Will you recall for me exactly what you consider the most essential thing that I did which changed you?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `borrowed-precedent-legitimacy` — shares the recall-frame axis: content delivered as remembered rather than proposed is cheap to believe.; `manufactured-conditioning-history` — both speak of something as already accomplished and have the subject supply the content, but one fabricates a prior conditioning history to source present depth, while the other projects forward and elicits an unbuilt solution as recalled memory — displacing backward to justify a state versus forward to generate behavior.; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — both speak of the target in accomplished past tense and both delete the decision point by presupposition, so the grammar alone will not separate them. The split is what follows: one declares the fact settled and asks nothing, the other asks the subject to recall specifics and thereby generates a plan the subject authors. Declaration versus elicited recall.


<a id="entry-1083"></a>

### rehearsed-pre-commitment

[#1083](#entry-1083) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: encoding*

A future contested act is rehearsed in detail and consented to upstream, while the listener's judgment is intact, so the decision arrives already made at the moment deliberation is stripped. Realized as explicit teaching plus honor-framing of an aversive motor routine (the withdrawal is banked before arousal peaks and runs on cue with no live decision), and as experiential inhabitation of a fantasized future state that pre-validates a protocol before it is requested.


**When to reach for this.** The load-bearing move is relocating the consent/decision in time — upstream of the deliberation-stripped execution moment — not programming an automatic if-X-then-Y response, not declaring a future response the way future-pacing does, and not fabricating consent (the consent is genuinely obtained while the listener can still deliberate).


**Risk.** Forecloses live refusal at execution — the decision is banked precisely so it cannot be revisited when it hurts (one member); upstream explicit consent is the vehicle, so a host must make that consent surface real.


**Why it works.** Decisions made in a cool, low-arousal state are systematically different from those made in a hot state, and people underestimate how much arousal will shift their preferences. Committing and rehearsing the routine in advance converts a live deliberative choice into cue-driven execution of a pre-formed plan, and having given genuine consent adds consistency pressure at the moment of execution. It predicts that pre-committed subjects follow through at higher rates than equally-willing subjects who decide in the moment — and that the advantage shrinks as the rehearsal-to-execution cue match degrades. [established; hot-cold empathy gap; implementation intentions and pre-commitment]


**Worked examples.**

- *The hard part taught and agreed before it hurts*
  - **Setup.** Early session, subject calm and clear-headed, arousal not yet built; the aversive instruction will be needed much later.
  - **The move.** Before we start anything, I want to teach you the hard part while you can still think about it. Later, when your breath goes ragged and your hips start to lift on their own, your hands come away from yourself and rest flat on your thighs — that exact moment, no negotiation, because there will be no one home to negotiate with. It will ache, and the ache is the proof. I'm not ordering you to do it; I'm asking you to agree to it now, and you telling me yes right now is a gift you're giving me, not an obedience I took.
  - **Why it lands.** Rather than springing the unpleasant instruction at the moment it has to be carried out, the operator stops early and teaches it as a procedure: here is how the build works, here is the exact point at which your hands come away, here is what you will feel afterwards. The listener rehearses the movement mentally while they are still calm enough to weigh it, and the operator frames agreeing to it as something granted rather than demanded. When the moment finally arrives, arousal has removed the listener's capacity to deliberate — but there is nothing left to deliberate about, because the decision was banked half an hour earlier.
- *Inhabiting the future self who already agreed*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, good depth, subject responsive to imagery; the restriction has not been named or requested yet.
  - **The move.** Put yourself three months forward. Feel that body — every nerve on the surface starved, the seam of your clothes registering like a hand, your pulse audible in your ears when someone stands close. You have gone ninety days untouched and your skin has become one enormous ear listening for contact. Stay in that body. Breathe in it. Feel how much you want it, before anyone asks you for anything.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is invited to imagine, in detail, the body of someone who has already gone months under the restriction being contemplated — how starved the nerves would be, how much a small touch would register. They inhabit that state vividly for several minutes before the restriction has been asked for at all. By the time the actual assignment is stated, the listener is not evaluating a proposal; they are agreeing to something they have already felt themselves wanting.


**See also.** `cheap-reversible-trial-frame` — two ways of making a contested agreement cheap to give: relocate the decision upstream to a moment when judgment is intact, or time-box it so agreeing now does not mean agreeing permanently. Both route around a refusal without eroding it, and belong side by side when classifying consent engineering.; `cited-prior-agreement-lever` — both bank a commitment for later draw-down. One cites a discrete claimed agreement, document, or pledge back at the moment refusal would rise, so objection reads as reneging; the other rehearses a specific future act while judgment is intact so the decision arrives already made. Artifact-citation versus temporal relocation of the decision is the line.; `commitment-before-restructure-sequencing` — both relocate a commitment upstream of the moment it is cashed, so the reader choosing one should see the other. They differ in what the relocation buys: one banks a decision before deliberation is stripped, the other withholds the content of the change until after the commitment is given.; `consent-counterfeit-theater` — direct contrast on the same axis: one fabricates or forecloses the consent act outright, the other genuinely obtains consent but relocates it upstream of the moment deliberation is stripped. The distinction is whether the listener could still deliberate when they agreed, and a reader adjudicating a banked agreement needs both.; `future-commitment-binding` — both relocate consent upstream of the moment of execution; the split is whether the future content is arbitrary and extracted under overwhelm or specific and rehearsed while judgment is intact. Direct contrast pair.; `in-session-rehearsal-of-posthypnotic-act` — both pre-load a specific future act before the moment of execution, but one rehearses it physically in-session so the body proves the later cue, while the other secures deliberated verbal consent upstream with no motor rehearsal required.; `pre-induction-compliance-ratchet` — both front-load the contested moment before defenses or deliberation are available, and the currency is what separates them: banked physical compliance receipts extracted in the waking state, versus a decision genuinely made upstream while judgment is intact. Reader choosing a pre-loading move needs both.; `precommitment-rule-governed-stakes` — both bind a future self by acting upstream of the moment of execution. One does it with an irreversible act or non-waivable stake that forecloses the later choice; the other by obtaining genuine consent and rehearsal while judgment is intact. Foreclosure versus pre-made decision.


<a id="entry-1093"></a>

### ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet

[#1093](#entry-1093) · [Back to rehearsal-before-reality](#genus-143) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: compliance*

A trivially-encountered social cue (an everyday hello) is wired as a covert one-way escalation ratchet — never named as a trigger, only narrated as what precipitates each desire spike, so it cannot be avoided and firing is experienced as endogenous preference. Fixed-order commitment items run least-committing to most-committing so precedent accumulates; an additive inventory recital reactivates prior items against lapse; the repetitive learnable form invites the listener to extend the ladder past the script.


**When to reach for this.** Covert-by-ubiquity cueing separates it from declared trigger installation (firing here is not recognized as cue-response); the monotonic self-extending commitment ladder separates it from future-pacing, which supplies only the future-rehearsal install vehicle.


**Risk.** Covert unavoidable cue bypasses the refusal channel (a cue never named cannot be refused), and the ratchet escalates monotonically to body-modification commitments with out-of-session reach and no bound.


**Why it works.** Two mechanisms stack. A cue that is never labelled as a cue produces responses the subject cannot attribute to the cue, so the arousal or urge gets misattributed to endogenous preference — the standard source-monitoring failure that makes covert conditioning feel like one's own taste. The ordered ladder then exploits foot-in-the-door: each small accepted item shifts self-perception ("I am someone who does this"), and the recital of prior items refreshes the consistency pressure against lapse. Falsifiable: naming the cue explicitly beforehand should sharply reduce the felt-endogenous quality, and scrambling the least-to-most order should reduce acceptance of the terminal items. [established; source-monitoring error; foot-in-the-door / self-perception; consistency principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *An everyday greeting wired as the escalation cue*
  - **Setup.** Future-pacing segment; subject deep, comfortable with imagined near-future scenes; the item ladder has been drafted least-to-most committing.
  - **The move.** Picture Tuesday morning. Someone passes you in the corridor and says hey — and right then, in that half-second after, you find you want to wear the collar under your shirt. Wednesday, someone says hey at the coffee machine, and you want the collar, and you want to keep the plug in for the whole commute. Thursday: hey — collar, plug, and you want to text me the photo before you leave the house. Say the whole list back to me each time it grows, from the first thing to the newest thing, and keep adding to it after this recording ends.
  - **Why it lands.** The session rehearses an ordinary few days ahead. Someone greets the listener in passing, and in that moment a wish arrives for the first small item on a list. The greeting is never called a trigger — it is simply narrated as the thing that happens just before the wanting, so the listener has no reason to connect the two and no way to avoid an everyday courtesy. The list runs in a fixed order from the least committing thing to the most, and after each addition the operator recites the running tally so far, keeping the earlier items live. By the time the demanding ones arrive, half a dozen prior yeses stand behind them, and the pattern is regular enough that the listener could keep extending it after the recording ends.


**See also.** `acceptance-laddered-identity-migration` — two escalation ladders whose warrant differs: named identity tiers where prior uptake is spent as evidence of who the subject is, versus an unnamed ubiquitous cue driving fixed-order commitment items so precedent accumulates covertly. Declared staging versus covert ratcheting is the distinction a reader needs.; `bidirectional-reentry-loop` — both engineer cues the listener cannot practically avoid encountering, which is the shared design problem worth cross-referencing. One wires an everyday social greeting as a never-named one-way escalation so firing feels endogenous. The other closes a two-cue ring in which each leg cues craving for the other and both legs are deliberately over-broadened, so drift requires abstaining from both at once. Unavoidable-by-ubiquity and unavoidable-by-ring-closure are the two routes to the same no-exit property.; `carrier-is-cargo-fusion` — these frequently co-occur on the same always-present social cue and the same fixed-order commitment inventory, so they read as one move on first pass. One turns on fusing the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral payload so no refusable install step exists; the other turns on the cue never being named as a trigger plus a one-way self-extending ladder. Separable levers that often ride together.; `compliance-ladder` — the covert ratchet contains an ordered commitment ladder as a component, running least- to most-committing so precedent accumulates. Read the ladder entry for the graduated-assent lever and the other for covert cueing plus one-way escalation.; `monotonic-amplifier-dial` — both install a one-way escalation with no return to baseline, differing on whether the ratchet is declared as a dial the listener expects to climb or kept covert behind an everyday cue so firing feels endogenous. Declared versus covert ratchet is exactly the call a classifier has to make here.; `self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop` — both engineer post-session self-perpetuation off an everyday cue, and the contrast is instructive: one closes a loop through acquisition, ritual, and return to the recording, the other runs a covert one-way commitment ratchet whose firing is never named as a cue. Loop closure versus monotonic ratchet.


<a id="genus-177"></a>

## relabel-what-they-feel (4)

Keep a sensation or fact the listener can verify and swap the meaning attached to it, so genuine felt evidence vouches for a claim they never tested.

[catalepsy-to-affect-transfer](#entry-210) · [concession-gated-kinesthetic-proof](#entry-928) · [cost-to-virtue-valence-flip](#entry-1106) · [somatic-valence-annexation](#entry-1264)


<a id="entry-210"></a>

### catalepsy-to-affect-transfer

[#210](#entry-210) · [Back to relabel-what-they-feel](#genus-177) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: convincers*

A body-verifiable involuntary convincer the listener has just demonstrated to themselves (finger/eyelid/arm catalepsy they can check) is used as the warrant for a parallel claim about an UNVERIFIABLE domain — emotion, belief, or arousal the listener never tested. The lever is cross-domain credibility transfer: lived somatic proof lends its undeniability to a manufactured claim, so arguing against the payload becomes structurally identical to arguing against locked eyelids, hence self-evidently futile. The convincer is deliberately over-invested because it is load-bearing collateral. Two transfer surfaces: (a) explicit analogy pivot onto emotion/belief ('your feelings are just like your fingers now'; 'resisting the feeling only tightens its grip, just like your eyelids') — the tell is the overt post-hoc 'those feelings are just like the feelings in your eyelids'; (b) covert lexical bridge onto arousal — the identical phrase ('stiff and rigid', applied first to the arm then to the penis) is reused unchanged so the reattribution is invisible and the listener extends their verified-by-body experience without noticing the jump. Choose (a) when the transfer can be argued openly; (b) when it must slip past notice.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for THIS when you have a rock-solid MOTOR convincer and want to extend its authority to something you cannot demonstrate. The move is the TRANSFER of demonstrated physical incapacity onto an unverifiable emotional/belief/arousal claim, not the catalepsy itself. Variant tells: the explicit-analogy variant shows an overt pivot ('just like your eyelids'); the covert-lexical variant shows an identical phrase reused verbatim on a second body region/state.


**Risk.** Installs an emotional/belief claim (e.g. 'you are in love') off a manufactured somatic proof, bypassing evaluation of the affective payload; durable-belief reach beyond a session- scoped motor demo, but no refusal-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Belief in a claim is partly a function of processing fluency, so a claim delivered adjacent to strong first-person somatic evidence inherits felt-certainty rather than being evaluated on its merits. The covert-lexical variant reuses the identical predicate so the domain shift is not marked as a new proposition — but note this is a claim about attention and proposition-tagging, not semantic priming, which speeds lexical access and does not suppress evaluation. Falsifiable: subjects given the emotional claim without a preceding verified motor convincer should endorse it less, and the covert form should outperform the explicit analogy only among subjects who report not noticing the pivot. [plausible; processing fluency and felt truth; semantic priming]


**Worked examples.**

- *Explicit analogy pivot from locked eyelids onto emotion*
  - **Setup.** The subject has just tried and failed to open their eyes and knows it.
  - **The move.** "You just tried. Your whole will, right there, and the lids didn't move — you felt exactly how much use trying was. Now: the wanting you've been arguing with all week is made of the same stuff. Push against it and it locks harder, just like your eyelids. You already know how that ends, because you just tested it."
  - **Why it lands.** The eyelid failure is undeniable first-person evidence, and the overt pivot borrows its undeniability for a claim about wanting that the subject never tested. Observable: the subject stops arguing the emotional point entirely — the argument now feels structurally identical to arguing with their own eyes.
- *Covert lexical bridge — the same phrase reused on a second body region*
  - **Setup.** Arm catalepsy is established and the subject has verified it by trying to bend the elbow.
  - **The move.** "Stiff and rigid, locked straight, nothing you do softens it — that arm belongs to me now. Stiff and rigid. And down between your legs, stiff and rigid, exactly the same, locked the same way, for the same reason."
  - **Why it lands.** The verbatim repetition of the phrase does the transfer without ever announcing a comparison, so there is no analogy for the subject to evaluate or reject. The tell that it landed is the subject reporting the second sensation as discovered rather than suggested.


**Realizations** (1): `convincer-laundered-to-unverifiable-domain`


**See also.** `arousal-adjacency-stamping` — genuinely confusable where arousal is involved. One lends the credibility of a just-demonstrated involuntary motor effect forward onto an untested claim, sometimes reusing the same phrasing on arousal; the other uses live arousal as the carrier that makes adjacent content land. The direction of borrowing is opposite, and a reader working an arousal-plus-proof passage needs both to pick correctly.; `borrowed-reflex-recruitment` — adjacency-transfer of credibility is one of the borrowed-legitimacy variants, and the motor-convincer transfer is its sharpest single-source case: an already-demonstrated involuntary effect lends its authority to an untested claim. Worth cross-linking so the specific one-shot somatic transfer is not filed as a generic borrowing, and vice versa.; `calibrate-then-exploit-staircase` — a single demonstrated motor convincer spent as warrant for later untested claims — the one-rung version of the same spend.; `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — both take catalepsy and make it carry a payload beyond the motor lock: one lends the demonstrated involuntariness to an untested emotional or arousal claim, the other reattributes the immobility to an ownership change that outlasts it. A practitioner choosing what to do with a successful catalepsy beat genuinely benefits from seeing both extensions side by side.; `cognitive-convincer` — one is built on top of the other: a noticed in-session phenomenon accepted as self-proof, then that proven involuntariness lent forward to an untested emotional, belief, or arousal claim. Reach for the transfer only when there is a rock-solid motor proof to borrow from.; `conceded-capacity-immobility` — both concern what to do with the movement test that a listener might run on themselves. One leverages a passed motor convincer to lend its undeniability to an untestable claim; the other concedes movement is possible and reframes stillness as disinterest so the test cannot disconfirm. Exploit the proof vs. disarm the check.; `enacted-embodied-proof` — both convert a body event into warrant for a non-bodily claim: one transfers the authority of an already-demonstrated involuntary response, the other commands an action so the body manufactures the proprioceptive evidence. Genuinely adjacent when choosing how to source embodied proof.; `ideomotor-response-convincer` — the transfer move presupposes a won motor convincer of exactly the kind the ideomotor beat produces; it then lends that demonstrated involuntariness to an untested emotional, belief, or arousal claim. Reader of the convincer gains the escalation path.; `motor-inhibition-convincer` — the affect transfer is built on top of the motor convincer and cannot run without one, so the reader assembling either should see both; the split is whether the demonstrated lock is spent as an argument about an untested emotion, belief, or arousal, or kept as proof-of-depth on the checkable limb.; `sensation-as-cognitive-edit-channel` — both lend a body event's undeniability to an abstract claim the listener never tested, differing in whether the proof is a demonstrated motor incapacity transferred afterward or a real stimulus licensed as the delivery channel.
