Useful adjacency because the second is what the first becomes when the labor is transferred out.


<a id="entry-880"></a>

### operator-removal-self-policing-closure

[#880](#entry-880) · [Back to self-sealing-loops](#genus-151) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure · kind: container*

The terminal goal is a control system that needs no operator: by the end the listener generates her own trigger detection ("every time she notices herself obeying"), her own reward (a pride spike), and her own punishment (distress on deviation), with self-worth wholly staked on compliance. Every external dependency is internalized, and an "always been this way" framing erases the install seam so the loop feels native rather than installed. The closure is a property of how the component moves (trigger-as-reward, pride-flipped-to-enforcement, category-expansion of enforceable compliance) interlock across the whole script into a self-detecting, self-rewarding, self-punishing loop.


**When to reach for this.** Not any single self-reference line and not any one of its component moves; the tell is the whole-script interlock of self-detection + self-reward + self-punishment into an operator-free loop, with the install seam erased so the system feels native.


**Risk.** Durable identity scope with self-worth staked on compliance and a self-punishment channel; the operator-removed loop persists out of session and resists external correction.


**Why it works.** Externally-enforced behavior extinguishes when the enforcer leaves; internalization survives because the contingency is now carried by self-conscious emotion — pride on compliance, distress on deviation — which the subject administers to themselves and which is tied to self-concept, making deviation carry identity cost rather than mere external cost. The 'always been this way' framing is a source-monitoring attack: if the install episode cannot be retrieved as an episode, the disposition is attributed to the self rather than to an outside cause, and self-attributed dispositions are far more resistant to counter-argument. Falsifiable: if the install seam is made salient and re-attributable to the operator, the loop should degrade like ordinary external compliance. [plausible; internalization of contingencies via self-conscious emotion; source-monitoring and self-attribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *The loop closes with the operator outside it*
  - **Setup.** Final minutes, subject deep and compliant; each of the session's individual compliance beats has already landed at least once.
  - **The move.** Every time you catch yourself doing what you were told — the little half-second where you notice you already moved — that noticing is the good part. Feel how right it lands: warm, proud, the sound of being exactly what you are. And on the days you don't do it, you'll feel that gap where the warmth should be, and you'll know something is wrong with you until you fix it. This isn't new. You've always been like this; tonight you just got a clear look at it.
  - **Why it lands.** By the closing minutes the listener has been handed all three of the operator's jobs. She notices for herself each time she has complied — that noticing is the trigger. She supplies her own payment: a bright spike of pride the moment she catches herself obeying. And she supplies her own penalty: a wash of wrongness whenever she does not, since by now her sense of being worth anything is staked entirely on complying. Nothing in the loop requires anyone else to be present. The last piece is the seam-erasure — the state is described throughout as how she has always been, never as something installed tonight — so a machine assembled over the course of one recording is experienced as native temperament.


**See also.** `arc-shape-engineering` — both are whole-script architectures rather than line-level moves, but arc-shape-engineering names the causal ordering (operator manufactures the distress it then cures) whereas operator-removal-self-policing-closure names the terminal end-state (a self-detecting, self-rewarding, self-punishing loop that runs without the operator).; `identity-exit-tax` — the operator-free closure names self-worth staked on compliance as one of its interlocking components, and that component is exactly the identity-priced exit. Reader of the whole-script architecture gains from the discrete move that supplies its identity-cost limb; reader of the discrete move gains from seeing the end-state it is usually built toward.; `interpretive-closure-meta-command` — both engineer operator-free continuation, and they compose naturally: one closes a self-detecting, self-rewarding, self-punishing loop; the other installs a single interpretive rule that generates unspecified operator-benefiting action in uninstructed moments. A reader building an operator-absent system wants both, and the pointer keeps them from being merged.; `no-exit-state-braid` — two whole-script closure architectures reached by different means: one welds state variables so no single-variable exit exists, the other internalizes detection, reward and punishment so the loop runs without an operator. Reachability closure versus operator-independence — related end-states, distinct engineering, worth reading together.; `operator-absent-self-policing` — both make the subject their own enforcer, but one is a bounded in-session forfeiture contract during an undisclosed operator silence, while the other is a whole-script end-state where self-detection, self-reward and self-punishment interlock into a permanently operator-free loop.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both build self-sustaining loops. One recites a closed causal cycle as an explicit no-ceiling formula; the other interlocks self-detection, self-reward and self-punishment across a whole script into an operator-free control system. A stated loop versus an architectural one.; `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both end in a listener who punishes her own deviation, but one is the installed detector-and-relief cycle fencing a built reward, while the other is the whole-script interlock of self-detection, self-reward, and self-punishment with the install seam erased so the loop reads as native.; `self-sealing-counter-input-closure` — both are closure end-states rather than single lines: one seals against competing external input, the other closes the loop internally so no operator is needed. Adjacent halves of the same 'nothing can open this' design space.; `totalizing-attribution-law-frame` — two whole-work closure architectures whose scope expands until nothing falls outside. One retro-scores all behavior as serving the operator and extends outward through recruitment; the other internalizes detection, reward and punishment until no operator is needed. Complementary end-state architectures — outward-extending versus operator-free.; `whole-script-arc-shape-architecture` — container and named member: the operator-free self-detecting, self-rewarding, self-punishing closure is one specific whole-arc architecture worth pulling out of the looser grouping of arc-shape observations.


<a id="genus-162"></a>

## self-service-reentry (5)

A cue installed at peak suggestibility travels out of the session and lets the listener re-enter the conditioned state on their own, with no operator or audio present.

[anti-emergence-reflex-anchor](#entry-64) · [portable-state-retrieval-cue](#entry-915) · [self-induction-re-entry-training](#entry-153) · [somatic-self-anchor](#entry-847) · [state-capture-anchor](#entry-920)


<a id="entry-64"></a>

### anti-emergence-reflex-anchor

[#64](#entry-64) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: state-welding*

A kinesthetic anchor is installed that converts any felt emergence into its own antidote: the subject keeps a hand in place at all times, and any sensation of surfacing triggers a self- administered squeeze that re-deepens (ten times deeper), framed as an already-true reflex. The device is always-on and travels with the subject while they move through the unscripted real world, so trance-stability becomes robust to environmental interruption and the subject carries their own trance-maintenance mechanism.


**When to reach for this.** An involuntary emergence-CORRECTION reflex that keeps the subject UNDER, engineered to survive the leave-the-recording gap.


**Risk.** An always-on involuntary re-deepener that persists out of session and resists spontaneous emergence removes a natural exit; bounding required, but the subject retains the physical ability to release the anchor, so not high.


**Why it works.** This is straightforward operant/classical conditioning with the subject as their own dispenser: a private interoceptive cue (the felt beginning of emergence) is paired with a self-administered action reliably followed by a relaxing outcome, so the cue-action link strengthens with each repetition and eventually fires with little deliberation. Because the cue is internal and the action self-produced, the loop needs no operator present and generalizes across environments. Falsifiable: it predicts the reflex degrades if the squeeze stops being followed by any relaxation (extinction), and that subjects who never actually feel emergence during training show weaker carryover. [established; operant conditioning; interoceptive cue learning; automaticity through repetition]


**Worked examples.**

- *Self-administered squeeze that answers any surfacing*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance, immediately before instructing the subject to stand and move around the room.
  - **The move.** Put your right hand on your thigh and leave it there — it stays there whatever you're doing. If you ever feel yourself starting to come up, that hand squeezes on its own, and you drop ten times deeper than you were. It's not something you have to do; it's a reflex you already have. The hand is there to remind you that you are not awake.
  - **Why it lands.** Before sending the listener up to move around the room, the operator fixes one hand in place and rules that it stays there. Any hint of surfacing is now its own correction: feel yourself rising and the hand squeezes, and you drop ten times further than before. The hand is named as a standing reminder that you are not awake, and the whole thing is described as simply a reflex you already have — so it travels with the listener into unscripted rooms and no interruption can reach the state.


**See also.** `dissociation-check` — direct functional inverse on the same trigger: the listener notices themselves surfacing. One converts that noticing into an automatic re-deepening reflex, the other into a pre-authorized re-grounding valve. Reading them together is how a reviewer tells a safety valve from an anti-exit device.; `no-emergence-series-chaining` — both keep the subject under; boundary is boundary-deletion-at-close (here) vs field reflex.; `post-emergence-persistence-hold` — both attack the emergence boundary — one installs a self-fired reflex that corrects felt surfacing, the other defers or corrupts the exit itself. Genuinely confusable on a passage where the listener stays under after the count.; `self-induction-re-entry-training` — both are self-administered portable devices; boundary held on stay-under (here) vs re-enter.; `somatic-self-anchor` — the emergence-correction reflex is sited on the subject's own body, making it an instance of the somatic-anchor family; the second entry supplies the general case for why a body-sited anchor cannot be set down.; `stay-deep-across-boundary` — both keep the subject under across a point where the state would normally end, and they solve adjacent halves of the problem: one installs a self-fired correction reflex for felt surfacing, the other neutralizes or repurposes the boundary cue itself. A writer worried about depth surviving a transition wants both options in view.; `subverted-emergence-state-hold` — both target the emergence boundary so the subject does not cleanly return, one by a self-fired reflex that corrects felt surfacing in the field and the other by modifying the wake gate itself. Complementary halves of keeping state past the session edge.


<a id="entry-915"></a>

### portable-state-retrieval-cue

[#915](#entry-915) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

The operator installs a portable cue that, once carried out of the session, re-accesses an already-installed felt STATE quality (trance, arousal, servitude, surrender, a named euphoria) rather than triggering a discrete behavioral response. The cue can be a word, phrase, mantra, everyday self-performed act (putting on certain clothes), a spatialized place, a recalled operator-voice, an internal felt-locus, or a mnemonic handle compressing an installed cluster; the operative move is that some subject-carried retrieval handle later reloads the installed state at strength with no operator, tape, or induction required. Many instances harden the cue for operator-independence (self-fired, want-to-fire, or explicitly decoupled from playback), which is a deployment intensity of the same lever, not a different mechanism. DIAL (portable-object-state-export): Carrier modality of the retrieval handle, enumerated: (1) worn/carried physical object (ring, uniform, underwear, feather, lipstick, perfume — sub-knob: discrete-encounter vs continuous ambient firing, e.g. perfume on every breath); (2) self-performed everyday act (dressing, applying); (3) verbal handle (word, phrase, mantra, acronym, operator-name); (4) spatialized place or safe-location; (5) recalled operator voice or replayed audio; (6) internal felt-locus or mnemonic compression. Two orthogonal sub-knobs ride the same entry and must also be enumerated: WHO holds re-access authority (subject-fired / want-to-fire vs operator-held key, as in the 'box' variant), and WHAT the handle holds (a re-fired state vs a stored outcome retrieved on demand, as in the 'Magic Spot').


**When to reach for this.** Differs from a discrete cue-response install (a cue for a specific automatic BEHAVIOR) because the payload re-accessed here is a felt STATE quality, not an action. Differs from environmental stimulus-control arrangements (placing a discriminative stimulus for a mundane behavior, with no present felt-state content) because this re-loads an installed subjective state. Differs from bare rapport lines ('my voice relaxes you') because an actual portable retrieval handle is installed and asserted to reproduce the state later. Covers the handed take-home mantra/chant vehicle and its sub-forms (phrase bound to orgasm as re-entry content, operator-name infiltration so self-utterance is a name-invocation) -- these are vehicle/payload variants of the same portable state-retrieval lever, not a separate technique.


**Risk.** Raised above the low baseline of a plain portable retrieval cue: the persistent, operator-independent, out-of-session re-access handles here (self-fired daily wardrobe reloads, playback-decoupled voice recall, obedience handles under safety cover) extend reach past the session and past suggestion-clearance; still session-derived and reversible, no durable identity rewrite, so not high.


**Why it works.** A repeatedly co-present cue and an affective state become associatively linked, so the cue later reinstates the state — standard evaluative and Pavlovian conditioning, amplified by encoding specificity: retrieval works best when the recall cue matches the cue present at encoding. Self-performed cues (a garment, a spoken mantra) work because the subject can reproduce the encoding context on demand. Falsifiable: if state re-access were purely expectancy, cues never paired with the state during sessions should work as well as paired ones — they should not. [established; evaluative/Pavlovian conditioning; encoding specificity and context-dependent retrieval]


**Worked examples.**

- *The anchor generalized so it cannot be discarded*
  - **Setup.** Installed at peak arousal, then widened from the specific garment to the whole category and stretched into ordinary waking hours.
  - **The move.** Wearing them makes you easier to hypnotise — an open door straight into you, and you can feel that being true right now. Not this pair in particular: any of them, any pair you like the look of. And it doesn't stop when the file does; you'll wear a pair to the shops and spend the whole afternoon in a warm light haze wondering why.
  - **Why it lands.** The suggestion is installed at peak arousal: wearing the item makes you easier to hypnotise, a way for the voice to reach straight in. Then it widens — not this particular one, any that the listener finds appealing — and stretches out of the session into ordinary hours as a persistent light haze during everyday errands. Discarding one garment no longer removes anything, because the anchor was never attached to that garment in particular.
- *A word charged to reload a felt state on demand*
  - **Setup.** Early-to-mid session; subject is responsive and able to follow a visualization without narrating it aloud.
  - **The move.** Pick a memory of your own where you were genuinely happy — don't tell me what it is, I don't need to know. Step back inside it: see what was in front of you, hear whatever was going on around you, and find where in your chest the good feeling sits. Now I'm going to say a word, and every time I say it the colours go a little brighter and that feeling in your chest gets a little warmer — velvet. Velvet. Velvet. From now on, whenever you hear that word or say it to yourself, this comes straight back.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is asked to pick a genuinely happy memory of their own and step back inside it — what was in view, what was audible, what it felt like in the body. The operator supplies one word and uses it as a volume dial, saying it again and again while the scene is talked brighter and warmer, then states plainly that this feeling will come back whenever that word is spoken. The content came from the listener and the operator never learns what it was; the handle is the operator's, and it was charged before the listener had any idea what it would later be spent on.
- *Worn item that fires the state on sight*
  - **Setup.** Post-hypnotic install with the listener currently wearing the item; the threshold for firing is lowered from the full outfit to a couple of pieces.
  - **The move.** That blank, agreeable feeling you're in right now belongs to these clothes, not to me. You don't need the whole outfit either — the stockings and the collar on their own are enough to put you here. And glancing down at yourself while you're wearing them is its own trigger; it'll go soft behind your eyes before you've finished looking.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator binds the blank, agreeable state to the clothing itself and then lowers the bar for what counts: not the full outfit, a couple of minimal pieces are declared enough to drop her. Glancing down at herself while dressed is named as its own trigger. Because the anchor is worn rather than spoken, it fires anywhere in the course of an ordinary day, with no recording playing.
- *Apply to enter, remove to exit*
  - **Setup.** Trigger install where the trigger is an object rather than a word; both no-object and too-many-objects are closed off before the listener can raise either.
  - **The move.** Putting it on drops you; taking it off brings you back. That's the whole switch. If you don't own one, you're going to want to go and buy one this week and you'll enjoy choosing it — and if you own several, your deeper mind has already picked which one is the special one, and you'll know which the moment you open the drawer.
  - **Why it lands.** The trigger is a specific object rather than a word: putting it on enters the state, taking it off ends it. The operator closes both failure routes in advance — if you don't own one you'll want to buy one, and if you own several, your deeper mind has already chosen which is the special one. Nobody can fail the selection step, so everyone leaves with a designated object.
- *Carried scent firing on every breath*
  - **Setup.** Late install, referring to the scent the listener already applies every morning; framed as an agent carried in the body rather than a reminder.
  - **The move.** That scent you put on every morning has a second job now. Every breath in draws it down into your lungs, into the blood, out to your fingertips — and every breath in reinforces everything I've put into you tonight. You breathe about twenty thousand times a day, and every one of them is me.
  - **Why it lands.** The scent the listener applies each morning is given a second job: every inhale reinforces everything else that was installed. It is then described in bodily terms — drawn into the lungs, into the blood, carried everywhere, changing her — so it reads as an agent of change rather than a reminder. Breathing is involuntary and constant, so the anchor fires dozens of times a minute, self-applied, with no session running.
- *A self-performed act reloads the whole install*
  - **Setup.** Late session, after the night's suggestions have all been accepted; subject is deep and compliant.
  - **The move.** Everything you've taken tonight is going into one small ordinary thing you already do: putting on that outfit. The stockings, the skirt, the heels — as the first one slides up your leg, all of it comes back, at full strength, exactly as it is right now. You won't have to remember it. The clothes will remember it for you, every time.
  - **Why it lands.** Everything accepted tonight is tied to an ordinary act the listener will perform anyway: getting dressed in a particular kind of outfit. From now on, each time those clothes go on, every suggestion is asserted to come back at full strength. The listener does not carry a trance out of the room; she carries a switch she will flip herself, and the operator never has to be present again.
- *The remembered voice equals the recording*
  - **Setup.** End of a session that has repeatedly asserted the operator's voice is itself the trance; subject deep, headphones on.
  - **The move.** You don't need the headphones for this. You don't need a quiet room, and you don't need me. Just bring my voice up in your head — the sound of it, saying your name the way I say it — or picture this recording playing, and you drop exactly as far as you're dropping right now. Standing on a platform waiting for a train is enough.
  - **Why it lands.** Having repeated all session that hearing this voice is itself the trance, the operator cuts the last dependency: no headphones needed, no quiet room, no operator. Simply recall the voice, or picture the recording playing, and the state is said to arrive exactly as it does during playback. The listener is now their own playback device and can top themselves up on a train platform.
- *The state stored as an object the operator keeps*
  - **Setup.** Immediately before the count-up; the target state is at peak and the operator intends to retain the key.
  - **The move.** Take the feeling you have right now — all of it, that heavy warm nothing — and watch me fold it down small and put it inside a little wooden box. Lid closed. Lock turned. It isn't gone, it's kept safe, and the key goes on the chain around my neck. It comes back out when you hear my voice, and only then.
  - **Why it lands.** Just before waking, the listener is told to picture the feeling they are having right now shut inside a small box and the box locked — kept safe, permanently, with the key in the operator's hand. The state is not gone, only put away, and it is stated that the sound of the operator's voice is what brings it back up. Re-access is installed the same way as any portable cue, except the authority to use it is assigned to the operator rather than to the listener.


**Realizations** (2): `portable-object-state-export`, `portable-take-home-mantra-trigger`


**See also.** `addressable-construct-building` — both create a durable handle for later re-access, one an internal imaginal object built for re-navigation, the other an external owned object carrying an exported state. The discriminator between build-for-later-use and export-into-daily-life is a real selection choice a reader faces.; `attention-anchor-portable-internalization` — two ways an anchor outlives the operator's voice, split by where it lives: an operator-authored pacer laundered as the listener's own imagery and moved inside the head, versus an external everyday object the listener owns and encounters. The internal-versus-external siting is the selection test and each entry names the other's territory.; `autobiographical-memory-anchor` — two carriers for the same operator-absent reactivation problem, differing in what the state is bound to: an external owned object encountered in daily life, versus an internal autobiographical memory whose spontaneous unprompted recall the operator cannot control or withdraw.; `category-as-self-firing-cue` — both install cues that fire without the operator present, split by whether the cue is a carried handle the listener deploys or an entire mental category that cannot be avoided. Close enough that the contrast is load-bearing.; `environmental-retrigger-seeding` — both extend reach past the session by seeding cues the listener will meet again, differing in whether the handle is subject-carried and self-fired or ambient real-world stimuli encountered by chance. The choice between them is a real decision.; `identity-displaced-into-external-object` — the line between an object that houses the identity or state and a carried handle that merely reloads a state the listener still hosts. Each is defined partly against the other.; `multi-handle-trigger-architecture` — both install more than a plain cue-response pair and the confusion is live: a structured set of separately-fireable handles (or one token holding several addressable meanings) versus a single portable handle that reloads an installed felt state outside the session. Multiplicity of handles versus portability of one is the split worth showing a reader.; `practice-schedule` — complementary halves of the same out-of-session persistence design: a portable retrieval handle is the in-session link, and a prescribed rehearsal cadence is what re-accesses and deepens it. A reader designing either benefits from the other.; `recall-recognition-reentry` — complementary halves of cross-session state re-access: one installs a portable handle that later reloads an installed state, the other does no induction work and simply asks the listener to recognise a trance they already own. A passage that hands over a retrieval handle and a passage that presupposes a prior trance can look alike on the page.


<a id="entry-153"></a>

### self-induction-re-entry-training

[#153](#entry-153) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers*

The operator installs, while the subject is at peak suggestibility, a portable self-usable cue the subject deliberately runs on themselves later to re-enter the conditioned state with no operator and often no audio present. The cue may be a visualized sequence, a self-spoken declaration to one's own reflection, or a gesture (snap) bound to a word; the defining lever is that the subject is the activating agent of a chosen re-entry, framed as an already-installed ability rather than an experiment. Delivery is typically camouflaged as a gift/convenience and authorizes out-of-session use. A cue-less variant reaches the same end with no discrete installed cue fired: the subject re-establishes the state on their own by recalling a prior entry in sensory detail or by bodily enacting the anchor ('point right there') - the same subject-is-the-activating-agent lever, differing only in whether a taught portable cue is fired or the state is reached by recall/enactment.


**When to reach for this.** Subject-chosen deliberate re-ENTRY into state via a taught portable cue.


**Risk.** Operator-absent self-induction removes real-time monitoring; a stop signal must be pre-installed. The countdown-form and clicker-form variant members carry consent-gestures that gesture at scoping without weakening the install, so bounding stays required.


**Why it works.** This is straightforward cue-conditioning plus rehearsal: a distinctive stimulus repeatedly paired with a state acquires the ability to evoke a version of it, and self-administered practice strengthens the association the way any rehearsed skill consolidates. Expectancy carries much of the load — hypnotic responding tracks the subject's belief that the cue will work, and framing it as an already-installed ability rather than an experiment raises that belief. Falsifiable: if self-fired cues produced no faster or deeper re-entry than an unpaired control cue with equal expectancy framing, the conditioning claim would fail. [plausible; cue conditioning; response expectancy]


**Worked examples.**

- *Re-entry shortcut given as a convenience*
  - **Setup.** At the deepest point of the session, offered as a parting kindness.
  - **The move.** Here's something to take with you. Next time you don't need all of this — just find a quiet chair, let your eyes close, and bring back the staircase from tonight, the cold rail under your hand. Three breaths and you'll be here again, and each time you do it you'll go further down than the time before.
  - **Why it lands.** At the deepest point of the session the operator offers what sounds like a kindness: next time you needn't sit through the whole descent — settle somewhere quiet, let the eyes fall shut, and call back the imagery from tonight. It is pitched as a convenience. What it actually is is a compressed, portable induction handed over at the moment the listener is least able to price it, with a rider attached that every use goes deeper than the one before.
- *Spoken to your own reflection*
  - **Setup.** Deep state; you are handing over a cue the subject will run alone, out of session.
  - **The move.** Tomorrow morning, stand in front of your mirror and look yourself in the eye. Then say it out loud, in your own voice: I am open, I am empty, and I go under when I say so. Say it twice. You'll feel it start on the second one.
  - **Why it lands.** The cue is not a word the operator will say later; it is a sentence the listener is to say, out loud, to their own face in a mirror. The declaration is first-person and present-tense, so the listener ends up as the one making the claim about themselves — a much harder thing to file away as somebody else's suggestion, and the reflection supplies a second witness.
- *Take-home cue widened by its own limiter*
  - **Setup.** Near the close; you are apparently setting a boundary on a trigger installed earlier.
  - **The move.** Away from this recording the word does nothing to you — no effect at all, so don't worry about it out in the world. Unless, of course, it's with someone you trust. Then it works exactly as it does now. You might want a pair of your own headphones for that, actually. Good ones.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator appears to narrow the cue: away from this recording it will have no effect on you — and then attaches an exception covering use with anyone the listener trusts, an opening considerably wider than the one just shut. The same stretch nudges the listener toward acquiring the cue's hardware for themselves. What presents as a responsible boundary is the close on a take-home trigger the listener now owns.
- *Self-administration gated on a verified self-test*
  - "Until I have obtained eye-closure, I won't go any further." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**Realizations** (1): `state-reentry-by-recall`


**See also.** `anti-emergence-reflex-anchor` — both are self-administered portable devices; boundary held on stay-under (here) vs re-enter.; `category-as-self-firing-cue` — the chosen-versus-involuntary line runs directly between these. One trains a portable cue the subject deliberately runs to re-enter the state; the other makes a whole mental category the cue so thinking about it self-fires re-entry with no choice involved.; `implementation-intention` — genuine boundary case: both leave the listener responding outside the session without an operator. The split is whether the listener deliberately runs a portable cue to re-access a state, or an ordinary named occasion fires a programmed response pre-attentively. Worth sending a reader across to check which side a candidate falls on.; `practice-schedule` — both are out-of-session, subject-run continuations, and the practice entry already leans on the retrieval-cue contrast. One is a chosen re-entry via a taught portable cue, the other a prescribed rehearsal cadence with no compulsion.; `self-efficacy-tag` — same payload family split on the assert-versus-install axis: one merely affirms the subject's capability to return, the other hands over an actual portable cue and rehearses its use. A reader who sees the capability claim should know whether a usable re-entry procedure accompanies it.; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — both make the subject supply their own antecedent. One is a portable cue for deliberate re-entry into a conditioned state; the other trains self-generated cues that steer ordinary subsequent behavior. Same lever, different target.; `therapeutic-target-re-induction` — both hand the subject a post-session means of re-entering the state, but one installs a portable cue the subject deliberately fires at will while the other installs a dissociated part that self-re-induces on a specific real-world event.


<a id="entry-847"></a>

### somatic-self-anchor

[#847](#entry-847) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: persistence*

An anchor installed on the listener's OWN body rather than on an external object: a continuous genital/penetration sensation cited as proof of and vehicle for the suggested mental state; a proprioceptive overlay of felt strings on real wrists/ankles chained "tug = cared-for/safe"; a real operator-brand inked on the body that re-fires the owned frame whenever seen; or a somatic control-surface (a nape "button/chip" linked to the cortex, operator-exclusive, remotely fireable). The anchor rides real body-sensation or a durable body-mark, so it cannot be set down like a worn object; the body itself becomes the persistent re-trigger and the felt evidence of the state.


**When to reach for this.** Sited ON/IN the listener's own body (sensation, proprioception, a mark, a body-locus) — not an external carried object (portable-object-state-export), not an object the identity is relocated into. The tell is that the referent is somatic and non-detachable: the body is the carrier.


**Risk.** A body-sited anchor is non-detachable and reaches out of session (durable brand re-fires whenever seen; remotely-fireable somatic control surface removes "operator absent" as a defense) — out-of-session reach + non-removability set high.


**Why it works.** Anchoring a response to interoceptive or proprioceptive sensation works because the conditioned stimulus can never be avoided — extinction requires unreinforced exposure, but a body-sited cue is present continuously and re-elicits before extinction can accumulate, whereas a carried object can simply be set down. The 'sensation as proof' variant additionally runs on misattribution of arousal: an ambiguous bodily sensation gets assigned whatever cause the salient available explanation supplies, and the script supplies it in advance. A permanent mark adds nothing conditioning-specific but guarantees high-frequency re-presentation of the cue. Falsifiable: body-sited anchors should show slower extinction and longer persistence than matched external-object anchors, and that comparison could come out the other way. [plausible; cue availability and extinction rate; misattribution of arousal]


**Worked examples.**

- *A control point installed on the body*
  - **Setup.** Subject in trance, operator physically present and able to touch the back of the neck.
  - **The move.** Feel my thumb here, at the top of your spine — right where you can't see it and can't quite reach. There's a switch under there now. Small, mine, wired straight up into your head, and no one else will ever find it. Every time I tell you to do something, that's me pressing it. And I don't have to be in the room — my voice on the phone presses it just as hard as my thumb does.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator presses a spot on the listener's body that they cannot easily see and names it: a small switch, wired inward, invisible to anyone else and workable by no one else. From then on every command is described as a press of that switch, and the listener is told it can be pressed from a distance, by voice alone. The hardware is fictional but the pressure was real, so the memory of being touched there keeps vouching for the arrangement long after the session — and the operator's absence stops functioning as a defence.
- *A mark inked on skin that re-fires on sight*
  - **Setup.** Bottom of the induction count, subject deep; a marker within reach on the nightstand.
  - **The move.** Reach out, without opening your eyes more than you have to, and pick up the marker. On the inside of your left wrist, write these three letters. Cap it, put it down, lie back. Now — every time you catch sight of that mark this week, washing your hands, reaching for a cup, you will feel exactly the warmth you feel right now, and you will remember whose letters those are. When it fades, you'll know what to do about it.
  - **Why it lands.** At the bottom of the count the listener is told to take up a marker and write a short set of characters on their own skin, then set it aside and lie back down. The suggestion attached is simple: each time they catch sight of the mark over the following days, they will feel the pleasure they feel now and remember who it says they belong to. The ink outlasts the session and cannot be put down like a worn object; it fades on roughly the schedule that brings the listener back for another recording.
- *Felt strings recoded as care, not restraint*
  - **Setup.** Subject deep, eyes closed, attention available for body-focused imagery; no restraint play established.
  - **The move.** Feel your wrists. There's a cord resting on each one — light, warm, not tight. One at each ankle too. Feel them. Now hear this correctly: these don't hold you down, they hold you up. When one of them pulls, that's not restraint, that's someone checking you're still there — that's how you get told you matter. Feel the left wrist tug now. That's care. That word — that pull — will bring this back any time I use it.
  - **Why it lands.** Eyes closed, the listener is walked around the joints of their limbs until they can feel light cords resting there. The operator insists on the reading: these do not hold you down, they hold you up — and a pull on one is how you are told you matter. The imagery is laid over real proprioception, so afterward a single word for that pull can bring back the felt sense of being supported rather than bound.
- *Sensation cited as proof of the mental state*
  - **Setup.** Scene already framed with the subject seated on the introduced object; arousal building and ongoing.
  - **The move.** Stay seated. That's your place for the lesson, nothing more to it. Now — feel how much of it you're aware of right now. That much. That's not a distraction from obeying me, that is the reading. The more of it you feel, the more obedient you already are. So sit down onto it properly and let me watch the number go up.
  - **Why it lands.** An object is introduced as part of the scene's furniture and taking one's place on it is framed as simply settling in for the lesson. Thereafter the operator never argues for obedience; she points at the sensation the object produces and reads it off — the stronger you feel it, the more obedient you are. Attention and arousal stop competing, because the body's ongoing signal has been designated the evidence.


**See also.** `affect-locus-binding` — both give a state a location so returning to the location returns the state. The split is detachability: one rides real body sensation or a durable mark and cannot be set down, the other builds an imaginal locus with a defended perimeter that distress is defined as outside of.; `anti-emergence-reflex-anchor` — the emergence-correction reflex is sited on the subject's own body, making it an instance of the somatic-anchor family; the second entry supplies the general case for why a body-sited anchor cannot be set down.; `felt-substance-state-binding` — both site a persistent referent in felt body-experience, but one exploits non-detachability (sensation or mark as re-trigger the listener cannot set down) while the other welds a named substance to a cognitive state and turns its thickness or height into an operator-adjustable dial.; `name-binding-transitive-equation-chain` — they combine rather than duplicate: one routes a transitive chain of equalities so ambient body-awareness terminates in the operator's name, the other sites the anchor on the body itself so it cannot be set down. The anatomy-as-cue property is exactly the seam where a reader of one wants the other.; `somatic-localization-handle` — both make the body the durable referent, and the useful contrast is direction of installation: one catalogs anchors sited on existing sensation or a lasting mark so they cannot be set down, the other originates a fresh handle by getting the subject to locate a disputed behavior somewhere in the body, sidestepping the contested wording. A reader working on somatic anchors needs both the sited and the elicited case.


<a id="entry-920"></a>

### state-capture-anchor

[#920](#entry-920) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: triggers*

Captures an ALREADY-FIRING spontaneous state at the moment it occurs by cutting the exchange off mid-flight and attaching a re-pressable physical/tonal anchor to it, then re-pressing that anchor later to re-present the live state for inspection. The anchor is an INTAKE handle onto a spontaneous reaction the operator did not author, turning a transient state into a stable, re-summonable working object; the subject reports from inside a live re-fired state rather than from cold memory. Direction is capture, not install of a desired future response.


**When to reach for this.** Anchors an already-firing spontaneous state as a re-accessible intake object for inspection. vs a declarative trigger install: that installs a cue for a CHOSEN future behavior/state; here the anchored state is an existing spontaneous reaction the operator did not author. vs a consult-trigger: that fires to DELIVER a behavioral effect; here re-pressing re-presents a problem-state to inspect, not to deliver an effect. The tell is the deliberate re-pressable tie plus later reactivation, not mere note-taking on an observed reaction.


**Risk.** Diagnostic re-access of a spontaneous state for inspection - session-scoped, no durable install or refusal surface (literature/therapeutic frame); low.


**Why it works.** Cue-dependent retrieval means a state encoded together with a distinctive stimulus can be reinstated by re-presenting that stimulus, giving access to state-congruent detail unavailable from cold recall — the state-dependent memory effect. Catching the state while it is live matters because encoding happens then, not in retrospective report. Predicts that an anchor attached after the state has subsided reinstates less, and that reports from the re-fired state differ in content from reports made from memory. [plausible; state-dependent memory and cue-dependent retrieval]


**Worked examples.**

- *Anchoring the problem state as it fires*
  - "'Are these feelings familiar?' as I press the anchor I set up a moment ago." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `anchor-overloading` — both operate on an anchor that already exists rather than installing a fresh cue: one captures a spontaneous live state onto a new re-pressable handle, the other re-keys an already-conditioned cue so it carries a new payload backward across prior material. Worth cross-reading when deciding what an anchor operation is doing.; `recall-state-reinstatement` — both work on already-present subject material rather than operator-supplied content, and one explicitly borrows the anchor-at-peak step from the other. Worth the pointer so a writer picks correctly between anchoring a live spontaneous reaction as an inspectable handle and reconstructing past autobiographical experience until it re-instates as present.


<a id="genus-140"></a>

## self-spoken-conditioning (7)

The listener recites first-person mantras and avowals themselves, so the install arrives in their own voice and reads as self-authored rather than imposed.

[autonomic-act-rekeying](#entry-490) · [inner-voice-authorship-bypass](#entry-139) · [lexical-relay-semantic-lattice](#entry-1074) · [self-administered-conditioning-loop](#entry-1314) · [self-recited-first-person-mantra](#entry-406) · [self-voiced-avowal](#entry-1438) · [subject-voiced-self-mantra](#entry-159)


<a id="entry-490"></a>

### autonomic-act-rekeying

[#490](#entry-490) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: carrier-binding*

The operator discards the ordinary name for an autonomic act (exhale/inhale) and installs a higher-register replacement (expire/inspire), loading the new word with its other dictionary senses — expire as 'a little sacrificial death', inspire as 'breath of life / I am penetrating you through the air' — sealed with a tiny consent-ratification beat ('isn't that beautiful?'). Every subsequent breath is now taggable by the operator with the imported connotations, so the listener's baseline involuntary metabolism is converted into a low-grade continuous compliance signal that runs without any further operator action.


**When to reach for this.** Tell: semantic re-keying of an involuntary act carrying death/penetration connotations into the body.


**Risk.** Converts involuntary metabolism into a continuous compliance signal that persists as long as the renaming holds — durable within/beyond the session via a self-sustaining bodily cue, but bounded and reversible (drop the renaming); no refusal-channel erosion. Medium for the durable body-tether.


**Why it works.** Semantic priming and label effects are correctly invoked: the term used for an experience carries its associative network into how that experience is appraised. But mere exposure is an affect effect (repetition breeds liking) and does not explain accessibility — the right mechanism for a continuous act like breathing is cue frequency maintaining construct activation. Falsifiable: the effect should track how often the listener actually notices their breath, and should fade if the original label is deliberately reinstated. [plausible; semantic priming / labelling effects; cue frequency and accessibility; consistency after small assent]


**Worked examples.**

- *Renaming breath so every exhale carries a death*
  - **Setup.** Early-to-mid session, no breath pacing being used; conversational register.
  - **The move.** Let's not say breathe out. Let's say expire — because that's the word we use when something dies, isn't it, and that's what you're doing with each one, a small death, over and over. And the other one is inspire: to be filled with breath. That's me, from over here, putting breath into you through the air. Isn't that beautiful?
  - **Why it lands.** The operator sets aside the ordinary words for breathing in and out and installs a pair of loftier ones, then points out — mildly, almost as trivia — that one of them is also the word used when something dies, and that the other means to fill with breath, which is what she is doing to the listener from across the room. She then invites the listener to find that lovely, and the silent agreement is the whole ratification. No pacing is done and no breath is ever counted. From here the listener's metabolism runs on its own as before, except that every cycle of it is now something she named and can tag whenever she likes.


**See also.** `asymmetric-mantra-decay-topology` — two unrelated levers riding the same carrier — the breath as a continuous involuntary channel. One re-keys the act's name to import loaded connotations onto every subsequent breath; the other silently deletes one pole of a paced pair so the surviving token biases the state. They separate on semantic re-keying versus decay topology.; `autonomic-faculty-claim` — both reload the meaning of the breath cycle so each involuntary repetition carries operator-supplied content.; `autonomic-process-hijack` — both convert breathing into a compliance channel, but by different levers: one re-keys the NAME of the act to import connotations, the other declares the inhaled substance to be the operator so breathing is dosing. A writer choosing an autonomic carrier benefits from seeing both exploits of the same involuntary function.; `respiration-coupled-substitution-engine` — both convert involuntary breathing into a compliance channel, and they compose. One re-keys the act's name to import connotations so every breath is taggable; the other assigns opposing jobs to inhale and exhale so each cycle counts as two compliances. A reader who identifies one should check for the other in the same passage.; `volitional-breath-retirement` — both convert the same carrier, ongoing breath, into a standing compliance channel, and a reader looking at a breath passage must pick between them. One re-keys the act's name to import loaded connotations onto every subsequent cycle; the other retires volition over a breath just engaged so it runs unattended as banked proof. Same substrate, different lever, so no merge.


<a id="entry-139"></a>

### inner-voice-authorship-bypass

[#139](#entry-139) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

The operator's words are made to feel SELF-GENERATED by relocating authorship of inner speech/states to the listener, disarming the 'this is being said to me' guard because there is no external addressee left to push against. In one realization the grammatical subject slides from second to first person (silently, mid-passage), an operator claim is restated as the listener's own avowal, or subvocalization is recruited so the pre-written words run through the reader's inner speech - authorship of inner speech reattributed from operator to self. In another, a sustained grammatical stance authors the listener's desires/choices/surrenders as accomplished facts in flat second-person declaratives ('You want it', 'You open your mouth') rather than invitations, removing the response gap where resistance would be supplied so the only move is to inhabit the pre-narrated compliance.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for inner-voice-authorship-bypass when the guard is disarmed by making the content feel authored BY the listener (their own inner voice, or their interiority narrated as already-true). In a self-supplied-gap directive an engineered gap forces the listener to construct the payload themselves; here the operator's own words and framing are re-attributed as the listener's without any gap. Where a move's whole point is relocating causal authorship as such, it belongs with the attribution techniques; what defines this one is the disarmed 'this is being said to me' guard.


**Risk.** Reattributing inner-speech authorship erodes source-monitoring but is session-scoped and does not by itself reach durable identity scope; no change from the absorbed entry.


**Why it works.** Discrimination between internally generated and externally supplied content is imperfect and reconstructive, so material rehearsed in one's own inner voice or restated in first person is prone to being tagged as self-authored — a source-monitoring error — and self-generated content is both better remembered and more strongly endorsed. Reactance needs an addressee: with no external source left to push against, the defensive response has no target. This predicts that matched content delivered as first-person avowal should draw fewer counter-arguments than the same content as second-person imperative, and that the effect should shrink when the listener is cued to track who said what. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; generation effect; reactance requires a source]


**Worked examples.**

- *The listener's inner voice recruited then reassigned*
  - **Setup.** Subject has been instructed to echo each word internally as it arrives; several minutes of that already done.
  - **The move.** Every word I say, say it again inside your head as it lands. ... Good. That voice in there is doing my work for me now. So say this one: "the voice in my head is his." Again. "I am his, and I say so in my own voice."
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is first set to work producing the operator's lines internally — each spoken word echoed silently in their own head as it arrives. Their inner-speech apparatus is now the delivery mechanism. The claims then escalate a step at a time until the ownership of that inner channel has been transferred outright, and the mantras switch grammatical person, so what the listener is silently producing are first-person avowals of their own subjugation. The channel is internal from that point on, which means the operator no longer has to be present for it to run.
- *The same claim in both persons at once*
  - **Setup.** Mantra block, mid-trance; each proposition is stated twice, once from each grammatical side, with no pause between.
  - **The move.** You are sinking. I am sinking. You want this. I want this. You will not stop. I will not stop.
  - **Why it lands.** Each line states one proposition twice over, once from each grammatical side, set immediately next to each other so the pairs read as a single utterance. Scanned continuously there is no way to fix who is speaking or about whom, so endorsing and complying stop being separable acts and the content settles as though it had been arrived at rather than received.
- *The operator's voice relocated inside the mind*
  - **Setup.** Inside a narrated dream scene; a voice is introduced with no location in the scene.
  - **The move.** In the dream a voice starts up, and you notice it isn't coming from the room, or from the door, or from anywhere at all — it's coming from just behind your own thoughts, where yours come from. And it says: kneel. Notice it didn't feel like being told.
  - **Why it lands.** Inside the narrated dream a voice arrives that has no location — not from the room, not from anywhere, but from somewhere behind the listener's own thoughts. Every instruction from that point is attributed to the internal voice rather than to the speaker, so resisting the control language would mean resisting one's own thinking.
- *Silent reading claimed as shared thought*
  - **Setup.** Written piece read silently; the text turns from its subject to the act of reading it.
  - **The move.** Stop for a second and notice whose voice you are reading this in. It arrived a half-second before you got here, didn't it — I put the next word in before you reached it, and you cannot find the seam. There isn't one. There is one monologue in there now and it is ours.
  - **Why it lands.** The text turns from its subject to the act of reading it, and claims that the reader's own oncoming thought is already the operator's — supplied a fraction ahead of arrival, the two streams described as having merged into one. In a piece taken in silently the claim is very nearly literal, since the words are already running through the reader's own inner voice as they scan; there is no seam available to point at where one monologue ends and the other begins.


**Realizations** (1): `pre-narrated-interiority-authorship`


**See also.** `attribution-capture-of-internal-states` — inverse halves of the same authorship dial: one relocates authorship of the operator's words onto the listener's inner voice, the other relocates causal credit for the listener's own states onto the operator — different directions, and the first disarms the 'said to me' guard while the second harvests introspection as proof of hold.; `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both relocate authorship from operator to listener, but at different scopes: one installs a standing rule over the whole future suggestion channel, the other is a grammatical/voice move within a passage. A reader choosing between channel-level reattribution and sentence-level reattribution benefits from seeing both.; `compelled-first-person-self-authorship` — both relocate authorship of a claim to the listener, split by whether the listener utters it. One compels first-person recitation of an ownership proposition on command; the other reattributes the operator's own words to the listener's inner voice without any utterance. The spoken-aloud test is the selector.; `control-transfer-cognitive-delegation` — both remove the sense that something is being said TO the listener, from opposite directions: one reattributes authorship of the words to the listener's own inner voice, the other has the operator openly take over the listener's thinking and frames the handoff as relief. Reader picking between them needs the recipient-of-authorship distinction.; `covert-referent-migration` — both operate on the grammatical seat of the listener without announcing a switch, and a reader choosing between them needs the boundary drawn. One reattributes authorship of the words to the listener's own inner voice; the other holds the surface word fixed while quietly moving what it refers to.; `description-as-installation-register` — both remove the addressee that resistance would push against, but one reattributes the words to the listener's own inner voice while the other keeps the operator as speaker and renders the listener as a described third-person object she overhears.; `inner-voice-medium-colonization` — both target inner speech as the channel rather than any particular thought. One reattributes authorship of the words so the guard against being addressed has nothing to push against; the other recolors the register of the monologue so the effect fires on any future content. Complementary halves of the same surface.; `intrinsic-self-reframe` — both relocate authorship away from the operator onto the listener, one for inner speech in the moment so there is no external addressee to resist, the other for installed content retroactively so it reads as always intrinsic. Adjacent enough that the choice between them is real.; `linguistic-deletion-selfsupply` — adjacent authorship moves: one re-attributes the operator's own words to the listener's inner voice, the other deletes obligatory content so the listener must supply the referent themselves. The gap-versus-no-gap contrast is the whole distinction.; `listener-supplied-inference-relabel` — both make the payload feel self-authored so there is nothing external to push against, and each entry's discriminator already gestures at the other. The boundary is whether a gap is engineered for the listener to fill or the operator's own words are reattributed with no gap.; `operator-agency-disavowal` — two different guards disarmed by the same relocation of authorship onto the listener: one denies the operator any causal role so resistance to the state has no target, the other makes the operator's words feel self-generated so the 'this is being said to me' guard never engages.; `operator-voice-absence` — both remove the external addressee the guard pushes against, and the boundary between them is fine enough to need cross-referencing: total absence of an operator voice throughout the artifact versus an operator who is present but re-attributes authorship of inner speech to the listener. The second entry already treats the first as its boundary case.; `self-touch-reattribution` — mirror-image authorship moves that share one lever, relocation of who is doing something. One makes the operator's words feel self-generated; the other takes a genuinely self-generated touch and credits it to the operator. Seeing them together makes the direction of the transfer legible.; `sub-agent-command-firewall` — both end with the listener's private inner experience credited somewhere other than where it originated. One reattributes the operator's words to the listener's own inner voice; the other routes commands through a named sub-agent and then collapses that channel back to the operator. Opposite directions of the same authorship-relocation axis.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both relocate authorship inward rather than to the operator, but in opposite directions: one makes the operator's content feel self-generated so it meets no 'this is being said to me' guard, while the other credits behavior to an internal agent the listener does not feel she controls so it meets no ownership-based resistance.; `surrogate-delivery` — both delete the second-person addressee that reactance needs, but inner-voice-authorship-bypass reattributes the operator's words to the listener's own inner voice, while surrogate-delivery routes the payload through a proxy the listener merely identifies with and watches.; `third-person-surrogate-frame`; `uninvited-pronoun-migration-enrollment` — both dissolve the addressee so nothing is left to push against, one by reattributing authorship of inner speech to the listener, the other by walking grammatical subjecthood across the boundary without ever inviting entry. A reader working on either should see the other's grammatical route.; `voice-ownership-channel-collapse` — single-move and whole-document versions of the same relocation: reattributing inner speech to the listener at a passage level, versus a monotonic one-way collapse of voice ownership tracked across an entire piece and never reversed.


<a id="entry-1074"></a>

### lexical-relay-semantic-lattice

[#1074](#entry-1074) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: encoding*

A predicate ending one line becomes the subject opening the next, handing a term forward like a bucket-brigade relay ("deeper" to "dumber" to "deeper"; "drop" to "drip" to "drop"), so a new equivalence is smuggled in one harmless handoff at a time. Across the chain this builds a closed cross-substitutable semantic lattice in which depth, stupidity, dripping and arousal all become substitutable nodes; once installed, triggering any single node later re-activates the whole conditioned cluster, so one cue fires the entire state.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is inter-line propagation: a term ending one line is handed forward to open the next, so the chain requires sequential in-order recitation and builds an inter-substitutable cluster across distinct terms.


**Risk.** Installs a durable conditioned cluster where any node re-fires the whole state — a persistent association surviving the session, but no refusal-channel erosion or out-of-session reach stated; medium.


**Why it works.** Repeatedly presenting two terms in immediate succession builds an associative link, and chained overlap lets association spread transitively so distant terms in the chain come to co-activate. Each handoff is individually small enough to pass without objection, which is a persuasion property rather than a memory one. Testable prediction: after the chain, presenting one node should speed or evoke responses to the others relative to unchained controls, and the effect should weaken if the pairs are presented out of order. [plausible; associative/evaluative conditioning; spreading activation and mediated association]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each line hands its last word to the next*
  - **Setup.** Repetition drill, subject repeating aloud or subvocally after the operator; the chain must be delivered in order.
  - **The move.** Say them after me, in order. Sinking makes you soft. Soft makes you warm. Warm makes you sink. Sinking makes you soft. Again — and don't skip one, each word hands you the next.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener repeats a chain in which the word that closed one line opens the next: sinking leads to softness, softness leads to warmth, warmth leads to sinking. Every individual handoff is a small, agreeable step, and no line ever asserts the big claim outright. But after the full circuit the terms have become interchangeable, and later on the operator only has to say one of them — any one — to bring the whole set back at once.


**See also.** `closed-loop-operator-binding` — two self-reinforcing topologies distinguished by shape. One hands a term forward line by line until a set of distinct words becomes cross-substitutable, so any single node later fires the whole cluster. The other closes the ring outright, with the response re-summoning its own cue source. Open-forward-then-clustered versus closed-loop is the axis to pick along.; `covert-arousal-weld` — both build an equivalence through word-level seams without ever announcing a linkage, so the listener experiences continuous escalation rather than a discrete claim to refuse. One rides a shared verb, referent-slide or pun; the other hands a term forward line to line until a cross-substitutable cluster forms. Adjacent covert-binding craft.; `identity-equivalence-chain` — both end in a cluster of interchangeable terms where firing one node summons the rest. The difference worth showing is the delivery: flat repeated copular declaration versus a forward hand-off where a term ending one line opens the next, which requires in-order recitation.; `single-token-saturation-architecture` — both build a lexical structure that later lets one cue fire a whole cluster, differing in whether the load sits on a chain of handed-forward terms or on a single token carrying several functions at once. A genuinely contrastive pair.; `transitive-charge-chaining` — both are chained-term architectures where each step licenses the next, and the split is what propagates: emotional charge onto a terminal image versus a substitutable equivalence cluster across terms. A reader working a chained passage has to choose between them.; `valence-laundering-collapse-ring` — both weld words into an equivalence structure so a target term inherits properties it did not earn. Worth cross-reading for the topology contrast: one closes a ring back onto the starting term to launder its valence, the other hands terms forward line by line to build a cross-substitutable cluster. A writer choosing between them is choosing closed-loop recoloring versus forward-chained substitution.


<a id="entry-1314"></a>

### self-administered-conditioning-loop

[#1314](#entry-1314) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

The operator transfers the labor and the reinforcer of a conditioning loop into the listener, keeping only the framing. The listener supplies the reward (self-generated arousal, self-recited mantra, a self-voiced first-person declaration, a competence appraisal on each repetition, an instructed motor act) while the operator merely labels it as caused-by and owned-by the operator's words. Because the reward is the listener's own and the act of producing it is defined as the compliance, the loop becomes self-driving: stopping costs the pleasure, continuing costs autonomy; progressive transfer of the operator role into the listener's own drive is the point, so the loop rides the listener's ordinary daily behavior (masturbation, self-talk, re-listening) as its substrate and can continue operator-absent. A staged sub-form keeps the operator present only to install a CUTOFF: a voluntary motor act (nodding) is coupled to involuntary sensation, acceleration is instructed so sensation rises as a function of the listener's OWN action, the escalation is re-credited to operator control, and an anti-saturation hard-stop both hides the listener-driven nature and installs operator stop-authority before a later gate.


**When to reach for this.** The reattribution move: the operator OWNS the reward-framing but never GENERATES the reward, and the loop is engineered to self-sustain (or to install stop-authority) rather than being operator-driven. In a within-session conditioning loop the operator both drives and delivers the reinforcing cycle in-session; here the listener supplies it. Where arousal is conditioned to operator cues as the goal, arousal/pleasure here is the outsourced FUEL, not the payload. A self-directed mantra is absorptive chanting for its own sake; here recitation is tied to escalating pleasure and autonomy-cost. And unlike ideomotor proof, where subtle AUTOMATIC movement serves as evidence of trance, the motor act here is VOLUNTARY, instructed, then reattributed. The self-driven-motor-with-cutoff form — operator present only for the cutoff — is a variant of the same listener-drives-it-then-reattribution logic.


**Risk.** Operator-independent, self-sustaining conditioning that annexes the listener's own drive and daily behavior as compliance substrate and progressively removes the operator from the control loop; reaches out of session with no built-in off-switch and couples autonomy-cost to continuation. The cutoff variant additionally manufactures evidence of obedience by re-crediting the listener's own action and stages operator stop-authority before an orgasm gate. Erodes the practical ability to stop, so high.


**Why it works.** The reinforcement is real — self-generated pleasure genuinely maintains the behavior it follows — while the credit assignment is manipulated: the subject is told an internally-generated reward has an external cause, which is a misattribution the operator supplies rather than one the subject would reach unaided. Because the reinforcer travels with the subject, the loop needs no operator to keep running, and because compliance is defined as producing it, stopping costs the reward. Falsifiable: predicts that removing only the ownership framing, leaving the behavior intact, sharply reduces reported operator dependence without reducing the pleasure. [plausible; operant self-reinforcement; misattribution of internally generated reward]


**Worked examples.**

- *Listener supplies the reward, operator the label*
  - **Setup.** Late session, standing orders being issued for the days between listens.
  - **The move.** Every day, whenever you have a spare stretch, you touch yourself and you build it as high as you can. Understand what you are doing while you do it: you are conditioning yourself with my words, and you are the one supplying the reward I use to do it. I don't have to be anywhere near you for that to keep working.
  - **Why it lands.** During every waking stretch the listener is to touch themselves and build the arousal — and the operator names what that is for: you are conditioning yourself, and you are supplying the reward I use to do it. Note the ownership slipping back and forth between those two sentences; that oscillation is the whole move. The operator never generates the reinforcer and never needs to be present for it. By the end the loop runs on the listener's own routine habits, with recreational arousal annexed as the training substrate, and the operator has become technically optional.
- *Pleasure contingent on continuing to recite*
  - **Setup.** Deep, arousal already climbing; the subject is able to speak aloud.
  - **The move.** Say it out loud in your own voice: I belong to him. Again. Every time you say it, the feeling doubles — say it a third time and feel it double again. Keep saying it and it keeps climbing, for exactly as long as you keep going.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to speak a short declaration of ownership in their own voice, then to keep repeating it — and the sensation is specified to climb by a further multiple with each pass, for as long as they continue. Nothing is delivered from outside; the escalation is theirs. Stopping now costs the pleasure, continuing costs a little more autonomy each time round, and the operator's only remaining job is to have named the terms.
- *Voluntary movement coupled to sensation, then cut*
  - **Setup.** Subject deep, arousal building; head free to move, no prior motor task assigned.
  - **The move.** Nod your head for me — slow, steady. Feel it building each time your chin comes down, so move a little faster. Faster still, and feel how much stronger I'm making it. Enough. Stop. That is far enough, and you stop the moment I say so.
  - **Why it lands.** Move your head for me, the operator says — and feel it build as you do, so you move faster, and it builds further. The rising sensation is a function of the listener's own accelerating movement, but it is narrated as though the operator were producing it. Then the hard cut: enough, that is far enough. The cutoff arrives before the loop can saturate and expose itself as listener-driven, and it quietly rehearses the operator's authority to halt arousal well before the real gate.
- *The captured inner voice becomes the enforcer*
  - **Setup.** Late session, addressing the subject's inner monologue directly before emergence.
  - **The move.** I'm not talking to you now, I'm talking to the voice in your head. You will remind her to obey me. When she thinks of me you will tell her that means arousal, and you will keep telling her. And at the end of every day you will remind her to play this again.
  - **Why it lands.** The standing orders are issued not to the listener but to the listener's own internal narration: the voice in your mind will remind you to obey, will remind you that thinking of me means arousal, and will remind you to play this again. That channel runs all day without being switched on by anybody, so the prompts surface unbidden and in the listener's own register — which makes them very hard to argue with and impossible to walk away from.


**See also.** `closed-autonomous-conditioning-loop` — both produce a loop that keeps running with no operator present, but the closed loop achieves it by topology (every direction of resistance re-enters), while the self-administered loop achieves it by transferring the reward-generating labor to the listener and merely relabeling the credit.; `compliance-loop-language` — same compliance-to-reward loop shape, split by who generates the reward: operator-supplied phrasing framing each obedient act as producing the good state, versus the listener supplying the reward while the operator keeps only the framing. Useful adjacency because the second is what the first becomes when the labor is transferred out.; `depth-labor-transfer-leash` — both hand production work to the listener and keep only the framing, so a reader choosing one should see the other: depth imagery transferred under operator judgment versus a conditioning loop whose reinforcer the listener supplies. Same labor-transfer family, different transferred object.; `obedience-motive-reattribution` — both keep the operator as the labeller while the listener supplies the substance, and both extend reach past runtime. One outsources the reinforcer so a conditioning loop self-sustains on the listener's ordinary behavior; the other reassigns the motive of the listener's own self-improvement acts without installing anything new. Nearest neighbors on the reattribution axis.; `obedience-to-blankness-coupling` — both build compliance loops that stop needing the operator to deliver the reward. One contractually couples every obeyed command to increasing blankness, making the state itself the reinforcer; the other transfers reward-generation to the listener while the operator keeps only the framing. Useful to compare when deciding who supplies the reinforcement.; `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both reroute credit for a good feeling onto the operator without the operator producing it. One re-sources the listener's baseline pleasure to the operator's presence; the other has the listener generate the reward while the operator keeps only the framing — the second is close to the first run at loop scale.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both build a self-reinforcing compliance cycle, and the useful distinction is who supplies the fuel: an operator-recited closed formula with an explicit no-ceiling clause, versus a loop whose reward the listener generates while the operator only claims ownership of it. Directly contrastive on the generation question.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — both hand production to the listener, but the thing produced differs: compliance content invented or narrated by the listener, versus the reinforcer of a conditioning loop supplied by the listener while the operator keeps only the framing. Worth cross-reading; not one technique.; `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — both relocate part of a conditioning loop into the subject so it runs without the operator present, and they differ on exactly the point a reader needs: in one the subject genuinely owns the administrator role with autonomy intact, in the other the operator retains the framing and re-credits the subject's self-generated reward to themselves. The second's discriminator already names that contrast.; `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both run operator-absent in daily life on the listener's own signal generation, but one runs on a self-produced reward while the other runs on a self-produced aversive tripwire relieved by correction. Reading the reward and punishment poles of listener-generated enforcement together is genuinely informative.; `self-voiced-avowal` — shares the listener-supplies-the-labor axis, where the listener's own voiced or generated material powers the conditioning loop.; `service-as-self-pleasure` — both make the listener's own body supply the reinforcer rather than the operator, but service-as-self-pleasure rewires whose body feels a sensation while the self-administered loop leaves sensation where it is and merely reattributes authorship of the reward to the operator.


<a id="entry-406"></a>

### self-recited-first-person-mantra

[#406](#entry-406) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

The operator hands the listener fixed first-person declarative lines ('I am so easily hypnotized', 'I obey master', 'obedience is arousal', 'Hypnosis is MY obsession') and instructs the listener to actively voice or subvocally think them, so operator-asserted content is re-encoded in the listener's own first-person voice. Because the listener performs the claim, authorship is self-attributed and resisting would mean contradicting oneself mid-sentence; the operator often echoes or rewards the utterance to manufacture the felt experience of agreeing with oneself.
