Delivery surfaces vary (repeat-after-me hand-off, reward-gated recitation, paced-descent inner mantra echoed by the operator, escalating burn-in, interleaved you/me lines never explicitly told to repeat) but the lever is constant: recitation converts received suggestion into self-attested belief. REALIZATION: the payload is often a bare mantra, but the same enacted-self-voicing installs an IDENTITY predicate [<-593 self-voiced-identity-adoption: an asserted equation moved into first-person self-voicing (is-YOUR -> is-MY), doubled and drilled ('Again.'), so a transient state hardens into a self-owned identity via self-perception through enactment - the listener KNOWS they are repeating operator content; the adoption works through the act of self-attribution].


**When to reach for this.** The listener is the ACTIVE producer of operator-supplied content - voicing it aloud, sub-vocalizing it, or writing/inscribing it, on a loop - with an operator present who hands or mandates the payload; the self-production re-encodes the content in the listener's own voice and bypasses the defenses external commands trigger. DECODE absorbed: 593 = an enacted overt identity handoff (is-your -> is-my) drilled until the trait registers as descriptive. The load-bearing act is the LISTENER's own vocalization/inscription (remove the listener producing it and the move loses its anchor); the payload's grammatical person is incidental. A permanence payload a chant may carry is adjudicated in permanence-declaration, not here.


**Risk.** Session-scoped self-attributed belief install; reward-gated and escalating variants (two members) deepen commitment but do not on their own erode the refusal channel or reach out of session — parity with the medium carried by internal voice cultivation.


**Why it works.** Saying something in one's own voice, especially with the felt sense of having chosen to, produces attitude change toward the stated position — the induced-compliance and self-perception result that people infer their attitudes from their own observable behaviour, and the saying-is-believing finding that people come to believe messages they themselves produce. Repetition adds a second, independent route: repeated statements are rated as more true regardless of source (the illusory-truth effect), and over time the memory of where the claim came from degrades (source-monitoring error), so operator-supplied content is later recalled as one's own. Falsifiable: predicts weaker adoption when the recitation is obviously coerced (external attribution available) and when source memory is protected or reinstated. [established; self-perception / induced compliance; illusory truth; source-monitoring error]


**Worked examples.**

- *Self-chanted line credited with causing the depth*
  - **Setup.** Early deepening; subject can hold a silent phrase and the operator is narrating rather than asserting depth.
  - **The move.** One line, and you think it to yourself, over and over, silently: I drop so easily. Each time you think it, a wave of heaviness comes down through you — you're the one making it happen, I'm only watching. Keep saying it. There's another one. And another.
  - **Why it lands.** Instead of asserting that the listener is going under, the operator hands them one first-person line about how readily they drop and tells them to chant it silently, adding that each repetition itself produces the wave of heaviness. The listener's own inner voice is now doing the deepening and the operator is only narrating the result. Depth becomes a fact about the listener rather than a claim by the speaker, which means arguing with it would mean contradicting the sentence they are in the middle of saying.
- *Recitation gated behind the wanted reward*
  - **Setup.** At an escalation point where the subject is already straining toward a pleasure the operator controls.
  - **The move.** Before you get any closer, say it, and mean it: I am your obedient toy. Say it like you believe it — because if it comes out flat, nothing else comes at all. Again, properly, and then you can have it.
  - **Why it lands.** At each escalation the operator names a fixed self-labeling line and demands it be said, then attaches a condition: say it convincingly or the pleasure the listener is already straining toward does not arrive. Saying the sentence becomes the price of the thing they want, so agreement to the label is bought with arousal rather than argued for.
- *Inner-voice mantra echoed between count numbers*
  - **Setup.** Slow countdown deepener; subject instructed to think one fixed phrase in the gap after each number.
  - **The move.** Ten. In your own head, in your own voice: obeying is pleasure. [pause] Obeying is pleasure. Nine. Think it. [pause] Obeying is pleasure. Eight. Think it for me. [pause] Obeying is pleasure.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator counts down slowly, and in the gap after each number the listener is told to think one fixed equating phrase in their own mental voice — then the operator immediately speaks that same phrase before moving to the next number. The listener produces the sentence first and hears it confirmed a beat later, which manufactures the sensation of being agreed with by someone else about something they just thought themselves.
- *Repeat-after-me hand-off of first-person lines*
  - **Setup.** End of session, subject still under; content has been asserted in the second person throughout and is now handed back in the first.
  - **The move.** Repeat after me now. I am easily hypnotized. I like being hypnotized. I obey without thinking about it. I will listen again tomorrow. Good girl — those are yours now, in your voice.
  - **Why it lands.** At the end of the session the operator says to repeat after her, then feeds through a short string of first-person declaratives that restate, one by one, the claims she has spent the whole recording asserting in the second person. Nothing new is introduced; the same content simply changes speaker.


**Realizations** (2): `self-authored-repetition-install`, `self-voiced-identity-adoption`


**See also.** `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both end with the listener treating operator content as self-authored, by different routes: a standing rule over the whole future suggestion stream, versus the listener actively voicing supplied lines so authorship is self-attributed by the act. Easy to conflate in practice; the link marks the split.; `compliance-laundered-as-resistance` — both have the listener repeat a fixed first-person line whose voicing does the operative work.; `depth-labor-transfer-leash` — both hand production to the listener so the output cannot be disowned: one transfers the depth-generating labor under operator judgment, the other has the listener voice operator-supplied first-person claims.; `lesson-structure-encoding` — compelled first-person recitation is named as an amplifier of the enumerated lesson set, and the recitation entry treats that same act as the mechanism in its own right. A reader must decide whether the ordered propositions or the listener's own voicing is load-bearing, which requires both entries side by side.; `multivariable-state-yoke-forced-avowal` — both end with the listener voicing a first-person claim they were handed, and the forced avowal in one is a specific application of the recitation lever in the other. The difference is that the avowal seals a multi-variable yoke rather than standing as the payload itself — a reader of either should know the other.; `opaque-mantra-unauditable-dedication` — both have the listener utter operator-supplied lines, and the parameter is whether the payload is inspectable. Self-attested belief through first-person recitation versus commitment to a token whose meaning stays with the operator -- a chanted passage needs both entries to be placed.; `ownership-language` — same ownership-identity payload delivered from opposite ends: asserted by the operator as a fact about who the listener now is, versus voiced by the listener so authorship is self-attributed. The choice turns on who speaks the claim.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both hand the listener grammatical work to perform, and the second explicitly names the first-person-only case as its neighbor. Reader adjudicating a recited line needs to check whether the person is rotating through I/we/you (conscription) or held fixed at first person (self-recitation), so the cross-reference does real disambiguation work.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both put a compressed formula in play and can appear in the same passage. The distinguishing question is who produces it: one is an operator-stated closed causal cycle with an explicit no-ceiling clause, the other is the listener actively voicing supplied first-person lines so authorship is self-attributed. A recited loop can be both at once, so the pointer prevents a silent mis-assignment.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — both make the listener the producer, and the boundary is who supplies the words: novel content the listener invents or a control they operate, versus fixed lines handed over to be voiced back. Adjacent enough that the distinction needs to be visible from either entry.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — both relocate authorship of the payload onto the listener, but on opposite sides of a single axis: here the listener performs operator-supplied lines, there the listener genuinely supplies the content from a frame or menu. A reader deciding which to cite needs the other in view to answer 'who actually wrote the words?'; `self-voiced-avowal` — shares the operator-supplied first-person recitation axis, in its fixed identity-declarative mantra form.; `socratic-equivalence-assertion` — both install content through compelled listener recitation, and the divider is the payload shape: free-standing first-person lines versus a forced lexical equivalence between two concepts backed by a leading quiz. That is a real adjudication a reader will face.


<a id="entry-1438"></a>

### self-voiced-avowal

[#1438](#entry-1438) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

The operator hands the listener fixed first-person lines and has them voiced — aloud, subvocally, or even written as chalkboard lines — via repeat-after-me catechisms, chant instructions, mantra blocks paced between descent counts, reward-gated recitations, and first-person blocks simply narrated as if the listener were already speaking them. Because the listener performs the claim in their own voice, authorship is self-attributed: the proposition is encoded as a self-thought rather than a received instruction, and later resistance must argue against the listener's own recently-spoken voice. Operators reinforce the transfer by echoing the utterance back, pairing each repetition with a somatic reward, or gating a wanted pleasure behind saying the line — manufacturing the felt experience of agreeing with oneself. Some scripts state the performative logic outright: repeating the sentences is itself what "locks them into place as immutable psychological truths." Payload class ranges across identity labels ("I'm a helplessly hypnotized sissy"), depth attribution ("I am so easily hypnotized"), desert judgments ("It's what I deserve"), and equations ("obedience is arousal"); payload and repetition count are parameters, not fences.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the load-bearing move is transferring authorship of a claim into the listener's own voice. The tell is a scripted first-person utterance the listener produces under operator direction — spoken, subvocal, or written — typically flagged by "repeat after me," a chant or lines-writing instruction, or a first-person block delivered as the listener's own speech. The claim's content varies freely; what is constant is that the listener ends up the speaker of it.


**Worked examples.**

- *Arousal words asserted to cause arousal*
  - **Setup.** Arousal established and the subject is speaking aloud on cue; you are naming the mechanism as you install it.
  - **The move.** The word is hungry. Not the idea of it — the word itself, in your mouth. Say it: hungry. Feel that? That's the word doing it, and it gets worse the more you say it. Next time you listen you won't even decide to — it'll just fall out of you, and each one will pull the next one out after it.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator names a word, then states that the word itself — not the idea, the word — drives the arousal up, and demonstrates by saying it. Later the loop is exported: at the next session these words will start falling out of the listener's mouth on their own. Once the listener's own speech is a trigger for the state that produces more of that speech, the circuit runs with nobody at the controls, and the operator is no longer the bottleneck on how far it escalates.
- *Cross-seam — label spoken in a believed-waking state, then re-inducted*
  - **Setup.** Subject has been brought up to what they believe is full waking, mid-conversation, before a second induction.
  - **The move.** Before we go again — say it once, out loud, in your own voice, wide awake so you can hear yourself do it. 'I am an obedient thing.' Good. Now that you've heard yourself say it awake, sleep.
  - **Why it lands.** Speaking the claim in a state the subject believes is their ordinary waking self makes it un-attributable to trance, and re-inducting immediately denies any window to reconsider it. Observable in the drop in volume and the slight delay before speaking — the reluctance is the ownership handoff registering.
- *First-person recitation of the legitimizing judgment*
  - **Setup.** After a corrective or degrading beat that the subject accepted without protest.
  - **The move.** Say it back to me. 'It's what I deserve.' Again, slower. Once more, and mean it this time.
  - **Why it lands.** Routing the value-judgment rather than the label through the subject's voice supplies the legitimacy that makes the identity claim defensible from the inside; later resistance has to argue with the subject's own recent words. Observable in the third repetition losing its flatness and picking up affect.
- *Escalating avowal blocks that invalidate each other on retreat*
  - **Setup.** Late session; a sequence of first-person statements is being built, each a step past the last.
  - **The move.** Repeat after me, each one all the way through. 'I like being told what to do.' Now: 'I need to be told what to do.' Now: 'I'm no good at deciding anything for myself.' Good — and you meant the first two, so you meant that one.
  - **Why it lands.** Each block is a small step from the accepted one before it, and the closing line ties them together so backing out of the last requires disowning the first — a retreat cost the subject pays in their own voice. Observable in the hesitation appearing at block three and then resolving, which is the interlock closing.
- *repeat-after-me ownership transfer*
  - Now repeat after me. I am intensely sexually vulnerable to kashashakti.


**Realizations** (2): `self-authored-identity-claim`, `self-perpetuating-loop`


**See also.** `arousal-adjacency-stamping` — both wire arousal into the suggestion economy, but one uses a live arousal state as the carrier that makes separate content stick, while the other closes arousal onto itself so the listener's own utterances re-cause the state with no content payload at all.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — shares the performed-act-as-self-evidence axis, where doing or saying something in-session is read back as proof the state is already true.; `category-as-self-firing-cue` — both build an operator-free self-firing circuit, one where the listener's own utterances re-cause the state and one where an entire mental category becomes the cue. A reader choosing between token-level loop and category-level cue is served by both entries.; `closed-autonomous-conditioning-loop` — downgraded from merge. The second is the general closed self-running loop where every resistance vector feeds it; the first is one narrow vehicle in which the listener's own spoken arousal words are asserted to cause the state, plus a forward-installed automatic vocalization. The specific vehicle and the mindlessness move that suppresses the disbelief reflex are not implied by the general entry, so this is a species link rather than a duplicate.; `closed-loop-operator-binding` — both install self-sustaining circuits that need no further operator input, but the self-perpetuating loop closes on the listener's own vocalizations amplifying arousal (word to state to more words), while closed-loop operator binding routes the response back onto the operator-as-cue-source, so future contact or ordinary arousal re-summons the operator.; `compounding-dependency-loop` — both are closed self-amplifying circuits and the tell separating them is worth the link: one loops inside the session, where the listener's own utterances re-cause the state, while the other loops across sessions, where the only relief route for a raised waking baseline is more of the same material. Same topology, different span.; `deictic-self-rule-overextension` — both route the claim through the listener's own authorship; one seats an identity noun, the other re-scopes a true local fact into an always-everywhere rule. Readers choosing between self-authored payload types need both in view.; `identity-from-coerced-behavior` — both make an identity claim hard to repudiate by relocating its apparent source away from the operator: one sources it from already-compelled observable behavior, the other routes it through the listener's own voice. Adjacent design choices for the same problem.; `intrinsic-self-reframe` — two routes to making an identity claim unrejectable by removing the external author. One hands the listener the grammatical subject so they speak the claim; the other reframes the content as always having been intrinsic so there was never anything imposed. Adjacent enough that a reader choosing one benefits from seeing the other route.; `multi-modal-trigger` — pass B cited a low TRIG-14 pull but do_not_merge'd it; kept distinct as a self-feeding loop.; `operator-absent-self-renewal-loop` — both build loops that run without the operator, but one closes the circuit inside a single session (spoken arousal-words causing the arousal that produces more words) while the other closes it across sessions by making the urge to re-expose one of the reinforced installs.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both move an identity claim into the listener's own grammatical position, and the discriminators need each other to hold the line: one cycles a single predicate through multiple persons so no neutral stance exists, the other hands the claim to the listener as speaker so there is no external author to reject. Adjacent, not identical.; `pronoun-migration-identity-install` — both install identity while dodging a direct operator assertion, and their discriminators already reference each other. A reader deciding between them needs the axis: covert grammatical drift that moves the referent onto the listener versus an explicit ownership handoff where the listener speaks the claim.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both build a closed self-amplifying circuit with no ceiling, but the vehicles differ enough to keep them apart: one makes the listener's own vocalizations the loop's carrier and forward-installs automatic speech, the other recites the loop as a compressed verbal formula. A reader picking between them benefits from seeing the contrast in what closes the circuit.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — shares the listener-supplies-the-labor axis, where the listener's own voiced or generated material powers the conditioning loop.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — same ownership-handoff lever with different payload classes: novel compliance content the listener generates, versus an identity claim or its legitimizing judgment spoken in the listener's own voice. The payload class is the taxonomy's working boundary in this family, so they stay separate but must cross-reference.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — genus and species. The second is the general lever (authorship of the payload is relocated to the listener so there is no external author to reject); the first is the identity-claim species, where what the listener speaks is the label or its legitimizing judgment. A reader who reaches the general entry needs the identity-claim variant, and vice versa. Not a merge: the general entry also covers non-identity payloads.; `self-generated-failure-as-identity-proof` — both route an identity claim through the listener rather than the operator, but one requires an enacted failure as evidence and the other requires only spoken authorship of the claim. The boundary is worth showing: enacted proof versus ownership handoff.; `self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop` — both are closed self-sustaining loops whose payload is perpetuation rather than any single response, and the useful contrast is loop scope: one closes inside the session on the listener's own vocalizations, the other threads through daily life via an environmental cue, an acquisition step, and a return to the recording. The shared self-feeding topology is a real structural relationship, not just shared vocabulary.; `self-recited-first-person-mantra` — shares the operator-supplied first-person recitation axis, in its fixed identity-declarative mantra form.; `self-selected-category-slotting` — a tight, deliberate pair: the same identity content lands either because the listener speaks the claim aloud or because the listener privately assigns an unassigned category to themselves. Each discriminator already names the other, and the spoken-versus-silent split is exactly the choice a writer faces.; `socratic-equivalence-assertion` — both get their force from routing the claim through the listener's own voice so there is no external author to reject, and both are stickier than the same content asserted by the operator. One hands over an identity claim; the other forces an asserted equivalence between two concepts that diverge in ordinary usage. Same ownership handoff, different payload.; `third-person-proxy-normalization` — both are grammatical-person moves on identity content and each already names the other's neighbourhood: one hands authorship of the claim to the listener, the other launders a claim by shifting it into detached third person. A reader adjudicating a person-shift passage genuinely needs to see both options.


<a id="entry-159"></a>

### subject-voiced-self-mantra

[#159](#entry-159) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

The entire artifact is voiced in the first person from inside the desired endpoint, with no external operator addressing the listener — the text IS the self-talk the listener is to speak, mouth along with, or subvocalize. Because the voice already speaks from the already-altered self ("I'm an ecstasy slut", "I suck till I'm stupid"), identity-claims arrive pre-accepted rather than as suggestions to negotiate; the "is this me or them?" check is short-circuited because the listener is both speaker and target. The load-bearing event is the voicing, not the hearing; refusal collapses to "stop identifying / stop saying it," and there is no operator-says / listener-experiences loop to resist.


**When to reach for this.** First-person throughout with the LISTENER as the speaker and no operator surface at all.


**Risk.** Installs identity-claims as pre-accepted autobiography (e.g. "I used to be a feminist, but now I don't think") — a self-description rewrite; session-scoped and requires the listener to lend their voice, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Saying something yourself, in your own voice, is a stronger route to endorsing it than hearing it said — the generation effect and self-referential encoding both favour self-produced first-person content, and self-persuasion research finds that arguments one utters shift attitudes more than arguments one receives. It also removes the source cue that would let the listener attribute the claim to an outside party and discount it. Falsifiable: identity-claim endorsement should be measurably higher for spoken/subvocalised delivery than for merely listening to the same text. [established; generation effect; self-persuasion; self-referential encoding]


**Worked examples.**

- *Whole track spoken in the listener's I*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a text the subject reads or speaks aloud themselves; no operator voice appears anywhere.
  - **The move.** I am soft and slow and easy to move. I do what I am told and I like it. My head is quiet and warm and I am not going to fill it back up.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no operator anywhere in the text. Every line is first-person and present-tense, spoken from inside the finished state — not "you will feel" but "I feel," not "you are becoming" but "I am." Nothing is proposed, so there is nothing to accept or decline; the only two things a listener can do with the track are mouth along with it or stop it. The usual check — is this me talking or them? — has no seam to catch on, because the listener is simultaneously the speaker and the target.
- *First line licenses the before/after swap*
  - **Setup.** Very first line of a subject-voiced piece; establishes the before/after account.
  - **The move.** I used to be someone who argued. I'm not anymore. I'm the girl who says yes before she's finished hearing the question, and I have been for a while now.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening line is autobiography rather than instruction: I used to be one thing, and now I am not. Naming the discarded former self does the licensing work — everything stacked after it arrives as an account of a change that has already happened, not as a change being requested. Self-descriptions the listener would argue with as suggestions pass unchallenged as memories.
- *Narrated from inside an already-taken head*
  - **Setup.** First-person narration from inside an already-conditioned state; mid-passage.
  - **The move.** I can feel where the thoughts used to be. There's just warm space there now, and I like it better. When she tells me to kneel I'm already down before I've worked out why, and working it out afterward is more effort than it's worth, so I don't.
  - **Why it lands.** The story is told in the first person by someone already under, and the character does nearly all the work on themselves: the narration keeps explaining, from inside, why the mind has gone quiet, why complying feels good, why pushing back would be pointless. A listener lending their inner voice to a line about wanting to be told what to do has endorsed it in the act of reading it — there is no separate moment at which acceptance gets decided.


**See also.** `description-as-installation-register` — two poles of grammatical-person register as the install vehicle: the listener speaking the endpoint in first person with no operator surface, versus the operator describing the listener in third person and never issuing a second-person command. Both remove the command-evaluation interface by manipulating who is addressed.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both use first-person; braid rotates persons, mantra does not.; `scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier` — shares the first-person already-converted narrator voice as a delivery vehicle for pre-accepted identity content.; `self-reference-erasure` — both operate on the first-person position rather than on content, in opposite directions: one has the listener occupy it as the speaker of an already-altered self, the other removes or replaces the self-reference handle so there is no seat to assert from. A passage mandating self-directed speech can trip either, so the contrast is load-bearing.; `third-person-surrogate-frame` — grammatical-person opposites that already cite each other as contrast cases: one puts the listener in the speaker seat, the other makes the listener the described third party. Useful as a paired decision, since both remove the operator-addresses-you frame by opposite routes.


<a id="genus-235"></a>

## self-sustaining-contingencies (3)

Make the behavior keep itself running after the operator steps back, via precommitted stakes, self-administered rewards and records, or handoff to consequences the environment already pays.

[natural-contingency-handoff](#entry-530) · [precommitment-rule-governed-stakes](#entry-424) · [self-management-self-administered-contingency](#entry-433)


<a id="entry-530"></a>

### natural-contingency-handoff

[#530](#entry-530) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: transfer*

Retire the operator by handing maintenance to a natural contingency already operating in the target setting, via one of two levers. Contact lever: drive just enough emissions of the trained behavior in the generalization setting for it to contact the already-present reinforcer, then withdraw operator support once contact occurs. Fluency lever: do not stop at bare correctness — push measured performance (accuracy, rate, latency, duration, magnitude, topography) until the response is fluent enough to satisfy the natural setting's unforgiving timing/quality demands, because a correct-but-too-slow response never contacts reinforcement and extinguishes. Either way the response survives because the environment now selects and maintains it, collapsing operator effort from "sustain indefinitely" to "get the behavior over the natural contingency's threshold."


**When to reach for this.** The operator supplies no content and retires once natural reinforcement takes over — unlike moves that deliver operator content at the trance/waking threshold, schedule practice for state re-access, or sustain compliance for depth. Presupposes a target already screened by a standing-contingency maintainability filter; the deficit fixed is a CONTACT-frequency deficit (drive exposures) or a FLUENCY deficit (train measured dimensions to threshold), not broadened cues.


**Risk.** Durable out-of-session maintenance by the natural environment is the point; bounded, no channel erosion (two members).


**Why it works.** Responses persist only while something reinforces them, so operator-supplied reinforcement guarantees extinction on withdrawal unless the response has contacted a reinforcer that is already present in the setting. Fluency matters because natural contingencies impose timing and quality thresholds — a correct-but-slow response fails to produce the reinforcer and therefore extinguishes exactly like an incorrect one. Falsifiable: withdrawing support before the response has contacted natural reinforcement, or before it meets the setting's rate criterion, should produce reliable decay relative to matched cases where contact and fluency were achieved. [established; behavioral trapping / natural contingencies of reinforcement; extinction on schedule withdrawal; fluency thresholds]


**Worked examples.**

- *Bridge to first contact, then fade*
  - "consists of getting the learner to emit the behavior in the generalization setting just often enough to contact the contingency." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Train to fluency or it extinguishes*
  - "Behavior changes that seem to need generalization may only need better teaching. Try making the students fluent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `generative-substrate-training` — shares the fluency lever — pushing performance past bare accuracy so downstream behavior appears or maintains without further operator support.


<a id="entry-424"></a>

### precommitment-rule-governed-stakes

[#424](#entry-424) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Bind the FUTURE self in advance, during a low-temptation window, by restructuring the contingency so the later self cannot easily defect — pre-committing an irreversible act or a pre-set stake whose anticipated outcome (a rule-governed analog) controls present behavior across the delay a literal operant contingency could not bridge. FORMS: (future-self-precommitment) perform an IRREVERSIBLE or costly-to-reverse act while a tempting smaller-sooner reward is still temporally distant and discounted below the larger-later outcome (locking the cigarette case, early-month payroll savings, Odysseus at the mast), removing or penalizing the future impulsive choice before temptation peaks; soft pattern-over-days commitments are the same mechanism at a longer horizon; (self-imposed-penalty-commitment) pre-arrange a fixed penalty ( to a friend) on any day the target behavior fails a criterion, with a TRUSTWORTHY THIRD PARTY holding the stakes so it is non-self-waivable; (rule-governed-delayed-stakes) pre-commit a sizable, somewhat-delayed aversive tied to a behavioral limit (forfeit money to a despised cause for exceeding a cap; avoid a fine by exercising by midnight), a despised recipient sharpening the stake.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for PRECOMMITMENT / RULE-GOVERNED STAKES when you want to control a LATER behavior by binding the future self NOW — an irreversible act or a pre-set non-waivable stake set before temptation peaks, working across a delay. Choose it over: self-instruction/self-cueing (which supplies an antecedent that EVOKES the next response — precommitment FORECLOSES or penalizes the choice, foreclosure vs evocation being the structural line); self-administered contingency (which relocates the ongoing measurement-consequence ADMINISTRATOR role into the subject — precommitment arranges ONE future contingency, not an ongoing loop); an in-the-moment refusal / willpower act (precommitment is a separate act done in advance on the contingency structure). Facets differ by irreversible-act vs external-stakeholder-penalty vs delayed-aversive-stake.


**Risk.** Deliberately forecloses the future self's option to defect or withdraw, with out-of-session, costly-to-reverse reach — applied to another person this erodes the later refusal channel.


**Why it works.** People discount delayed outcomes steeply and, for many, hyperbolically, so the relative value of a smaller-sooner reward and a larger-later one reverses as the sooner one approaches — which is why a preference formed at distance predictably fails at close range. Acting on the contingency during the low-temptation window exploits that reversal: the choice is made while the larger-later outcome still dominates, and the act removes or prices the later defection. A third party holding the stake matters because self-imposed penalties are otherwise waivable by the same self that will want to waive them. Falsifiable: predicts commitment devices only help where preference reversal actually occurs, and that self-held, waivable stakes underperform externally held ones. [established; hyperbolic/delay discounting and preference reversal; commitment devices]


**Worked examples.**

- *Bind the future self while temptation is distant*
  - "Since the smoker is just about to have a cigarette, the value of a future cigarette is negligible, making it easy to shut the case" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (2): `rule-governed-delayed-stakes`, `self-imposed-penalty-commitment`


**See also.** `prospective-resistance-foreclosure` — both bind the later self during an earlier window, and the contrast is exactly the foreclosure-versus-evocation line one of them already draws. One pre-assigns a null or aversive outcome to a whole future class of mental acts so the later comparator is deleted; the other restructures a real contingency -- an irreversible act or a non-waivable stake -- so the later self cannot cheaply defect. Deleting the ability to evaluate versus removing the ability to choose.; `rehearsed-pre-commitment` — both bind a future self by acting upstream of the moment of execution. One does it with an irreversible act or non-waivable stake that forecloses the later choice; the other by obtaining genuine consent and rehearsal while judgment is intact. Foreclosure versus pre-made decision.; `rule-governed-behavior-install` — both put a contingency into words in advance rather than letting experience shape behavior, but precommitment sets a non-waivable stake or irreversible act that forecloses the later choice, whereas rule-governed install merely states the contingency so a rule-following repertoire produces the behavior from the description.


<a id="entry-433"></a>

### self-management-self-administered-contingency

[#433](#entry-433) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

Relocate the measurement-and-consequence machinery of a contingency INTO the subject, on the premise that the self is the one agent guaranteed present everywhere — extending contingency management into private events and settings no external agent can follow. Spans from bare self-observation (which changes behavior by reactivity alone) to a full self-run consequence loop. REALIZATIONS: (self-administered-contingency) the subject self-selects task and reward, self-monitors completion, and self-delivers the reward — a self-contract collapsing all four roles (integrity resting on honest self-monitoring), an accuracy-matching contingency (reinforcement for MATCHING an independent observer's record — reinforcing correct self-observation), or a self-scoring loop against an answer key with a self-delivered consequence; (two-response-self-management-split) the genus framing — emit a SEPARATE controlling response that manipulates a variable of the target function at a PRIOR time-point when the competing reinforcer is weak, converting an intractable in-the-moment impulse into a tractable earlier engineering problem; (self-monitoring-reactivity) bare observe-and-record with NO added consequence, where the act of measurement alone shifts the rate (and yields an ABC baseline); (self-recording) install a recording act contemporaneous with the target (tally, chart on the mirror) so the mark itself becomes an immediate discriminative/consequating event, with an accuracy-matched-to-observer training variant that thins the external check until the subject records accurately unsupervised.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for SELF-MANAGEMENT / SELF-ADMINISTERED CONTINGENCY when the CONTINGENCY-ADMINISTRATOR role (measure, and consequate or just observe) relocates into the subject, running as an ongoing loop the subject drives. Choose it over: precommitment / rule-governed stakes (which arranges ONE future contingency / binds the future self by a stake — this transfers the ongoing administrator role); self-instruction/self-cueing (which relocates the ANTECEDENT/cue, not the measurement-consequence loop); operator-outsourced conditioning loop (where the operator OWNS the framing and reattributes the subject's self-generated reward to themselves — here the subject genuinely self-administers, autonomy intact). Facets span reactivity-only (observe/record, no consequence) through full self-contract; the accuracy-matching variant trains correct self-observation rather than the behavior itself.


**Risk.** Durable out-of-session self-management capacity; the removed external delivery check is an integrity surface, not a consent surface. Builds independence, reversible.


**Why it works.** Two separable effects. First, self-monitoring alone changes behaviour by reactivity: measuring a behaviour makes it salient and evaluable against a standard, and rates shift even with no consequence attached — the effect is real but typically modest and decays as monitoring lapses. Second, self-delivered consequences work to the extent the self-report is accurate, which is why accuracy-matching against an independent observer is trained separately; the honest-self-monitoring premise is the weak joint, not an incidental caveat. Falsifiable: predicts self-management effects shrink as recording accuracy degrades, and that reactivity-only interventions fade faster than externally verified ones. [plausible; self-monitoring reactivity; self-regulation via standards; accuracy-matching contingencies]


**Worked examples.**

- *The subject holds all four contingency roles*
  - "A self-contract is a contingency contract that an individual makes with herself, incorporating a self-selected task and reward as well as self-monitoring of task completion and self-delivery of the reward." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *The self is the one agent present everywhere*
  - "What behavior change agent can go with the student to every necessary lesson, at all times…? The student's own 'self' can always meet these specifications" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Reinforce accurate self-recording, not the behavior*
  - "Brian was taught to monitor his own behavior and to match his self-recordings to the recordings of his teachers. Accurate self-recording resulted in teacher praise" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Score your own work and deliver your own consequence*
  - "students who have been taught to evaluate their own performance and provide their own feedback in the form of self-delivered rewards and error correction… are not dependent on the teacher's direction" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (4): `self-managed-contingency`, `self-monitoring-reactivity`, `self-recording`, `two-response-self-management-split`


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — process and end-state: the gradual handover of task, standard, monitoring and delivery from operator to subject terminates in exactly the self-run contingency loop the other entry describes. Not a merge - one names the fading schedule applied to authorship, the other the standing arrangement once the handover is complete.; `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — one is a deployable arrangement, the other the design constraints governing any such arrangement, including whether a self-delivered consequence has a sharp enough onset to function as one. The reference entry is explicitly the substrate the deployable moves sit on, so the link runs in a genuinely useful direction.; `operator-absent-self-policing` — both relocate the enforcement role into the subject so control persists with no external agent present, and the contrast is sharp and instructive: one is an autonomy-intact self-run loop the subject owns, the other a self-surveillance and forfeiture contract serving the operator. The pairing is the clearest way to teach that boundary.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — both relocate part of a conditioning loop into the subject so it runs without the operator present, and they differ on exactly the point a reader needs: in one the subject genuinely owns the administrator role with autonomy intact, in the other the operator retains the framing and re-credits the subject's self-generated reward to themselves. The second's discriminator already names that contrast.; `self-administered-contingency` — self-management genus for the same relocated-administrator arrangement, spanning reactivity-only observation through the full self-contract.; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — complementary halves of relocating behavioral control into the subject: one moves the measurement-and-consequence loop inside, the other moves the antecedent cue inside. Each is defined partly by not being the other, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.


<a id="genus-298"></a>

## session-environment-safeguards (2)

Rules about where the session may run and who may speak around a deep subject, so the setting can't inject hazards or counter-suggestions.

[context-gate](#entry-570) · [suggestion-field-hygiene](#entry-582)


<a id="entry-570"></a>

### context-gate

[#570](#entry-570) · [Back to session-environment-safeguards](#genus-298) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A firm, unambiguous pre-induction requirement that the session only be consumed in a safe, distraction-free context — not while driving, not while operating machinery, undisturbed and able to fully release attention. The constraint runs on whether the material may be used at all in the listener's current situation, stated before induction begins.


**When to reach for this.** Gates WHETHER the session may run given the listening context, constraining use — it does not select among live trained relations, does not police bystanders mid-state (suggestion-field-hygiene), and does not weaponize staging toward a payload (context-lock-staging, weaponized-safety-framing).


**Risk.** Purely protective constraint: gating effects to an agreed context limits scope rather than extending it; residual risk lives in the gated payload, not the gate.


**Why it works.** Hypnotic and deep-relaxation material deliberately narrows attention and reduces monitoring of the external environment, which directly degrades the vigilance and reaction-time demands of driving or machine operation — the risk is not exotic, it is ordinary divided-attention failure. Stating the constraint before induction matters because instructions given after attentional narrowing begins are less likely to be encoded and acted on; the pre-induction slot is when the listener still has full executive control to change context. Falsifiable: if listeners given the gate before induction comply at the same rate as those given it mid-session, or if attention-demanding secondary-task performance does not degrade during the session, the rationale fails. [established; attentional narrowing and divided-attention decrement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-induction use-gate stated before the first deepening line*
  - **Setup.** The opening seconds of a recording or session, before any induction language has been spoken.
  - **The move.** Before we begin: do not listen to this while driving, while operating machinery, or while doing anything that needs your attention. Find somewhere you can sit or lie down undisturbed for the next half hour, put your phone on silent, and only start this when you can let your attention go completely. If that is not now, stop here and come back later.
  - **Why it lands.** It constrains whether the material may run at all rather than steering anything inside the session, so a listener in an unsafe context is filtered out before absorption removes their ability to self-assess. The operator can observe compliance indirectly: subjects who honour the gate arrive settled, and reported mid-session interruptions drop.


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `suitability-screening` — complementary pre-induction gates that block the session on different axes. One rules on whether the listening situation is safe enough to proceed; the other rules on whether this person should be worked with at all. Both narrow the operator's license rather than pushing a state, and both commonly appear in the same opening.; `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — one is a plain pre-induction constraint on whether the session may run at all; the other bounds a trigger on a trust condition with a self-validating rider. The second explicitly defines itself against the first, so the link carries the distinction between a real safety rail and a loyalty hook wearing one.


<a id="entry-582"></a>

### suggestion-field-hygiene

[#582](#entry-582) · [Back to session-environment-safeguards](#genus-298) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Because a deep subject hears and registers everything said in the room as an active suggestion, the operator manages the whole acoustic/information field — issuing operational rules to surrounding staff, training them by having them serve as subjects, silencing untrained guests — so no stray fear or doubt voiced in earshot can act as a counter-suggestion and collapse the accumulated state. The room, not just the operator, sustains the state.


**When to reach for this.** An environmental-control directive aimed at BYSTANDERS to protect an achieved state — not reassurance addressed to the subject, not a pre-session listening-context requirement on the subject (context-gate), and a state-protection move, not a state-production one.


**Risk.** Protective maintenance of an existing consented state; constrains bystanders, not the subject.


**Why it works.** Expectancy is one of the better-supported determinants of hypnotic responding, and expectancy is set by whatever information reaches the subject — including remarks not addressed to them. A doubt or fear voiced in earshot is a credible negative expectancy cue, credible precisely because it appears unstaged and comes from a bystander with no apparent motive to influence, which is what makes overheard information persuasive. Managing the whole room rather than only the operator's own speech follows directly. Falsifiable: if overheard sceptical remarks produce no measurable drop in responsiveness relative to a silent-room control, the rationale is wrong. [plausible; expectancy effects on hypnotic response; persuasiveness of overheard information]


**Worked examples.**

- *Every utterance in earshot counts as suggestion*
  - "if fears are generated in any manner—by unfortunate remarks made by nurses, assistants or other doctors … the Esdaile state will be lost. Remember that your patients hear and understand everything" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**See also.** `disconfirmation-suppression` — both protect an already-running state by managing what the subject can hear rather than by producing the state. One is standing environmental hygiene aimed at bystanders; the other is a discrete instruction that blocks one present fact from reaching the subject. Read as the ambient and the acute form of the same guard.


<a id="genus-167"></a>

## sideline-the-waking-mind (4)

Split the mind in two and address only the deeper half, so the waking evaluator can't inspect, refuse, or disconfirm what lands.

[audience-split-bypass](#entry-255) · [forbidden-attention-authority-test](#entry-701) · [reality-test-insulation](#entry-244) · [split-self-unfalsifiability](#entry-1090)


<a id="entry-255"></a>

### audience-split-bypass

[#255](#entry-255) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: critical-faculty-softening*

The operator partitions the listener into conscious and subconscious minds, then RELOCATES the critical/evaluating faculty out of scope: the conscious mind is assigned an explicit ignore-task ('this is not for your waking mind', 'no need to pay attention', 'the subconscious hears it anyway'), or the resisting/skeptical surface is relabeled the 'conscious mind' and declared unrepresentative while the 'subconscious' / 'real self' is asserted to be already aligned and to have already decided — so any objection it raises is pre-classified as background noise it was told to ignore, or disowned as merely the unrepresentative layer. Resistance becomes a category error (raised by the wrong agent) rather than an impulse fed or a verdict captured; no live resistance impulse is required, the split is asserted pre-emptively so any future contradiction is pre-covered as 'just the conscious mind'. Some instances address material explicitly 'to your subconscious' and add a deniability hedge ('this file will NOT trance you now'). The frame does the work an induction normally would.


**When to reach for this.** vs resistance-fold: fold converts an exercised impulse; here the impulse is DISMISSED as out-of-scope. vs resistance-quarantine-partition: quarantine reifies and demotes a named faculty (standing structural demotion); here the split is an epistemic audience assignment — the conscious mind still functions, it is just told this content is not addressed to it. Tell: an explicit ignore-task / wrong-audience assignment presupposing folk dualism, delivered pre-emptively.


**Risk.** Session-scoped critical-faculty lowering via a framing move; reversible, no durable scope.


**Why it works.** Assigning the critical faculty an ignore-task works by licensing low elaboration: people scrutinise a message far less when they believe it is not addressed to them or not consequential for them, and low-elaboration processing leans on peripheral cues rather than argument quality. Pre-emptively labelling any future objection as the wrong speaker also inoculates against counterarguing by giving it a dismissive category before it arises. Falsifiable: if listeners told 'this is not for your conscious mind' generated as many spontaneous counterarguments, and shifted attitude no more, than listeners given the same content addressed directly to them, the mechanism would fail. [plausible; elaboration likelihood / personal relevance and counterarguing]


**Worked examples.**

- *The waking mind assigned an ignore-task*
  - **Setup.** The first sentence of the recording, before any induction; the addressee is named before the subject can settle.
  - **The move.** This isn't for you. This is addressed to the part of you underneath, and it will hear every word whether you attend or not. So — the thinking part, the one following this sentence: your job for the next twenty minutes is to pay no attention to any of it. You have no say in what's happening here. Ignore it. It isn't yours.
  - **Why it lands.** The first sentence states who the recording is addressed to, and it is not the listener as they usually experience themselves. The thinking part is not argued with or talked down; it is given a task — pay no attention to any of this — and told repeatedly that it has no say in the matter. Evaluation therefore stops not because the listener was persuaded but because evaluating has been reclassified as somebody else's job. Any objection it raises afterwards is background noise it was already instructed to disregard.
- *Resistance pre-attributed to the unrepresentative layer*
  - **Setup.** Early, before the subject has assembled any objection; the split is asserted pre-emptively.
  - **The move.** There's the front of you and there's the rest of you, and only one of them is in charge tonight. The front can grumble all it likes — file its objections, sure. Underneath, you already want this and you're already letting it through. So whatever comes up in the next hour, that's just the front talking, and the front doesn't get to answer for you.
  - **Why it lands.** The split is asserted early, well before the listener has assembled anything to push back with. The surface layer may object all it likes; the layer underneath is declared to want this already and to be letting it through regardless. There is consequently no move available that would register as successful resistance — objecting is simply the wrong agent speaking.
- *Drifting off reframed as the better channel*
  - **Setup.** Mid-induction, dropped in as a single sentence at the point where attention typically starts to wander.
  - **The move.** And if you drift off and stop following my voice — good. That's not you failing at this. The part that's actually taking this in doesn't need you listening, and it does its best work when you've wandered off. So let your attention go where it likes.
  - **Why it lands.** One sentence, dropped in mid-induction, closes the most ordinary escape route there is. If the listener's attention wanders — which it will — that is pre-declared to be fine, because the part that matters is still listening and still taking it in. Drifting stops being a failure of the session and becomes a deeper route into it.
- *Bypass named as the reason for the split*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a file with no induction at all; the bypass is named as architecture rather than tactic.
  - **The move.** There's no induction on this one. The conscious mind is dismissed — go and do something else, read your emails, get bored, I genuinely don't mind. It's going in regardless, because it isn't being said to you. The you that's listening isn't the one being addressed, so there's nothing here for you to agree to or turn down.
  - **Why it lands.** The conscious mind is explicitly released — no need to follow this, go do something else, get bored if you like — while the operator asserts the material is landing anyway. The bypass is stated as architecture rather than as a tactic, and because on this framing the listener as they experience themselves is not the one addressed, there is nothing for them to decline. There is no induction in the file at all; this frame does the work one would have done.


**Realizations** (1): `conscious-subconscious-audience-split`


**See also.** `antagonist-split-resistance-routing` — both partition the listener into two selves and use the split to disarm objection, and both already contrast against the same resistance-quarantine neighbor. One routes the listener's own felt resistance onto a losing self; the other declares the objecting layer the wrong audience. Close enough that a reader choosing between them benefits from the pointer.; `channel-partitioned-monitoring` — both partition the listener to place content beyond monitoring, but the audience split is an asserted conscious/subconscious addressing rule that dismisses objections as out-of-scope, while channel partitioning routes output across actual representational modalities so no level owns it.; `faculty-preserving-scope-restriction` — both leave the evaluating faculty running while removing its purchase, one by narrowing what it may range over and the other by declaring the content not addressed to it. Very easy to conflate, since both let the listener feel they are still thinking freely; the pointer helps make the call.; `faculty-removal-pass` — already cross-referenced in both discriminators and the pointer should stay: A relocates the evaluating faculty out of scope by assigning it an ignore-task, B claims the faculty removed outright. Same target, different disposal, and the pair is easy to confuse in text.; `observer-responder-split` — both partition the listener, but the payload differs: one assigns the evaluating faculty an ignore-task so objections are out of scope, the other preserves awareness precisely so the felt loss of volition is convincing. Useful contrast because the partition surface looks identical in text.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — both install a conscious/subconscious partition and then use it to move something off the listener: in one case the objecting faculty is declared the wrong audience, in the other the authorship of agreement is assigned to the not-self side. Same structural device, two different things relocated.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both run on the same folk two-minds premise and are separated by what is done with the split: one reassigns authorship of behavior to the listener's own internal layer so ownership resistance never engages, the other assigns the critical faculty an ignore-task so any objection is pre-classified as the wrong audience. A reader meeting a subconscious-addressing script needs the pair.


<a id="entry-701"></a>

### forbidden-attention-authority-test

[#701](#entry-701) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure*

The operator introduces a vivid catastrophe the conscious mind would reflexively orient toward (the room/body catching fire), then explicitly directs the subconscious to ignore it and keep listening. Continuing to listen despite the imagined threat is made proof that the subconscious has ceded safety-signaling authority to the operator. The threat is never resolved as a literal scene — it exists purely as a forbidden-attention test whose being-obeyed demonstrates authority over the listener's own safety orientation, after which senses 'turn off' as consequence.


**When to reach for this.** Not literal fear-play/content: the tell is the threat's function as an authority test over safety-signaling, not as a scene. This overrides the safety-orientation exit — a reachability/authority-topology move.


**Risk.** Trains the listener to override their own safety-signaling on operator instruction — directly erodes the safety/verification channel; must ship inside a host with entry/exit/aftercare. Extractor-disputed on the fire's exact function but all readings route through operator-authority-over-safety.


**Why it works.** Graduated compliance is the operative mechanism: a small directive followed makes a larger subsequent one more likely, via commitment and self-attributed cooperativeness. Note that the obedience literature supports incremental escalation, NOT the stronger claim that the magnitude of impulse overridden scales the authority granted — that dose-response is unevidenced and should not be asserted. Falsifiable: if compliance with an attention-competing instruction produced no increase in downstream acceptance relative to a neutral instruction, the escalating-compliance account fails. Whether this impairs genuine safety orientation, as opposed to being play-acted inside an accepted frame, is not established, and is the reason for the risk rating. [plausible; graduated compliance / obedience to authority; effortful suppression as costly signal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Ignoring the staged emergency as proof of authority*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance, subject fully absorbed and responsive; a vivid emergency is staged purely to be disregarded and is never resolved.
  - **The move.** Look at the room. The curtains have caught — it's up the wall behind you already, the heat is on the back of your neck, the smoke is coming across the ceiling toward you.

The part of you that's listening to me: ignore it. Don't turn, don't check, don't move. Stay with my voice. [pause] There. You didn't move. Something was burning and the part of you that decides what's dangerous waited to hear it from me instead. It doesn't answer to you any more. And now the hearing goes, and the touch goes, one at a time — there's nothing left in you that needs to be on watch.
  - **Why it lands.** Deep in, the operator has the listener picture the room going up in flames around them — close, real, unmistakably an emergency — and then instructs the part of them that is listening to pay it no attention and carry on. There is no task to perform and no response to produce; the whole point is what does not happen. Because the listener is still there, still following the voice while something that should have overridden everything is burning nearby, the conclusion is offered that the deeper mind has handed over its authority to decide what counts as danger. The fire is then dropped and never mentioned again — it was only ever a test, and the senses are described as switching off one by one now that nothing is left to guard them.


**See also.** `arousal-isolated-obedience-test` — two authority tests that differ in what the proof is made of: a staged threat whose being-ignored demonstrates ceded safety-signaling, versus a hard stop on a high-arousal action that isolates obedience from the arousal carrying it. Both are proof beats without a commanded ordinary response, so a reader picking a test benefits from the pair.; `manufactured-jeopardy-rescue` — both stage a threat that is never resolved, but the exits differ: in one, ignoring the threat is the proof of ceded safety-signaling authority; in the other, obeying is framed as the only escape from a danger the operator secretly authors. Ignore-as-proof versus obey-as-rescue is the cut a reader needs, and staging a fake danger to test authority is close enough that the pointer pays.


<a id="entry-244"></a>

### reality-test-insulation

[#244](#entry-244) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: concealment*

Splits a normal-functioning surface from a hidden deep 'ownership' so the conditioning becomes uncheckable against external feedback. The listener is told they are 'perfectly free to live your life normally' while also 'in my control 24 hours a day, 7 days a week,' with the contradiction left unaddressed and ownership placed 'deep in the recesses of your mind' beneath unchanged surface behavior — friends, partners, therapists see nothing, disabling resistance-by-comparison-to-baseline and preemptively removing the usual collapse trigger (conflict between trance-instructions and waking life).


**When to reach for this.** An explicit surface/depth partition installed specifically to insulate the conditioning from reality-testing. Tell is the partition, not comfort — separates from routine trance-safety reassurance.


**Risk.** Erodes the subject's own reality-testing / refusal channel by design (removes the baseline-comparison check that would prompt disengagement); high per the channel-erosion clause.


**Why it works.** Conditioning normally decays when it conflicts with everyday feedback; specifying that surface behaviour stays unchanged removes the comparison test that would generate that conflict, and also removes third parties (friends, partners, clinicians) as sources of corrective information. The unaddressed contradiction between 'free' and 'controlled' survives because the two claims are indexed to different levels and never brought into the same comparison. Falsifiable: subjects prompted to explicitly compare the two claims side by side should report the contradiction and show reduced acceptance. [plausible; removal of disconfirming feedback; social-comparison isolation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Normal surface, ownership underneath*
  - **Setup.** Once in the middle of the session and again in the wakener; delivered flatly, with no acknowledgement of the contradiction.
  - **The move.** You're perfectly free to carry on with your life exactly as before — work, friends, whoever you go home to, none of it changes and nobody sees a thing different about you. And you are mine, every hour of every day, all week, without a break. That part sits far below where anyone looks, underneath everything you show people, so there's nothing on the surface for anyone to notice and nothing for you to explain.
  - **Why it lands.** Twice — once in the middle, once on the way out — the listener is told they remain entirely free to go on living exactly as before, and in the same breath that they are owned around the clock. The contradiction is never addressed; the ownership is simply placed somewhere below the surface where behavior does not change. Nobody around the listener can see anything different, so there is no outside reading to test the claim against, and the ordinary thing that would break a session's spell — noticing a conflict with waking life — is removed before it can happen.


**See also.** `self-sealing-counter-input-closure` — two seals against different disconfirming channels — ordinary-life feedback versus competing hypnosis — already cross-named in each discriminator. The pointer is earned.; `split-self-unfalsifiability` — two halves of the same insulation strategy, differing in what feedback channel is disabled: an unchanged normal surface that defeats comparison against ordinary life and outside observers, versus a deep layer walled off from introspective self-report so noticing nothing reads as confirmation.


<a id="entry-1090"></a>

### split-self-unfalsifiability

[#1090](#entry-1090) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: self-partition*

Uses an installed conscious/subconscious (or surface/deep) partition not as a dissociative experience but as an epistemic shield around the install. The operator concedes the waking self may keep its personality, notice nothing, or forget, and pre-categorizes that surface report as harmless/expected/desired, while the "real" recipient is declared a deeper layer the conscious mind cannot access — so introspective self-report can never reach or falsify the deep claim ("I still feel like a person", "nothing changed", "I forgot" are all pre-absorbed as confirmation).


**When to reach for this.** Payload is unfalsifiability — noticing-nothing is pre-routed as confirmation and the deep claim is walled off from conscious disconfirmation. vs observer-responder-split (payload is in-session felt automaticity/spectatorship); vs evaluator-offline-channel (evaluator quieted so suggestions land now); vs resistance-quarantine-partition (a faculty's standing is demoted, not the epistemic reach of self-report).


**Risk.** Erodes the subject's own disconfirmation channel — introspective self-report is pre-neutralized as evidence, removing the refusal/verification channel (v1.1 high).


**Why it works.** Pre-committing every possible self-report to the same conclusion removes the disconfirmation channel a person would normally use to check a claim, and people rarely notice that an explanation covering all outcomes has no evidential content — this is the same structure that sustains belief in unfalsifiable systems generally. It is reinforced by the fact that introspective access to one's own cognitive processes is genuinely poor, so "you cannot check this from the inside" is locally true enough to feel credible. Prediction that could fail: subjects given an explicit falsification criterion beforehand ("if X, the install did not take") should report the claim as less credible than subjects given the all-outcomes-confirm framing. [plausible; unfalsifiability / lack of introspective access to cognitive processes]


**Worked examples.**

- *The surface self allowed to feel unchanged*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, install content about to be delivered; subject deep but not amnesic.
  - **The move.** Your everyday mind is going to stay exactly as it is — same opinions, same stubbornness, same taste in arguments — and that is correct. That is not the part I am talking to. What I am putting in goes underneath, where the thinking part has no window. So when you're back at your desk on Thursday and you notice you feel completely normal, completely yourself, nothing changed — that is precisely what the surface is supposed to report.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator concedes the obvious objection before the listener can raise it: the everyday mind will go on behaving like itself, with its own opinions and habits, and that is entirely fine. What has been changed sits underneath that, where the everyday mind cannot look. A listener who later notices that they feel entirely ordinary finds that observation already accounted for — it was named in advance as exactly what the surface was expected to report, so the report can never count as evidence against anything.
- *Forgetting pre-explained as the deep part remembering*
  - **Setup.** Late session, immediately before closing; subject deep, install already delivered.
  - **The move.** I'm not talking to you as one person anymore. The thinking part of you may lose every word of this by morning — it might keep nothing at all. The part further down keeps all of it. So if you wake and remember, that means it took hold. And if you wake with a blank where this hour was, that means it went past the part that would have interfered. There is no version where it didn't land.
  - **Why it lands.** Late in the session the operator stops addressing the listener as one person and starts addressing layers — telling them that the thinking part may well lose all of this, while a part further down keeps it. Every possible aftermath is now pre-assigned: remembering proves it took, forgetting proves it went deep enough to bypass the part that would have interfered.
- *Awake on the surface, owned underneath*
  - **Setup.** Emergence, subject just counted up, eyes open, alert.
  - **The move.** You're wide awake now. Fully alert, fully yourself, back in the room — and underneath that, something is still listening to me and still holding what I said. Anything you do freely today belongs to the awake one. Anything you do because I told you belongs to the other one. So when you tell yourself you feel completely ordinary, remember which of the two of you is talking.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator confirms out loud that the listener is fully awake now — and in the same breath states that underneath, something is still listening and still under instruction. Two selves are now on the table: anything the listener does freely belongs to the one that is awake, anything compliant belongs to the one that is owned. Reporting that one feels entirely ordinary stops being a defence, because it is a report from the self that was never the one in question.


**See also.** `evaluator-offline-channel` — both run off an installed conscious/subconscious partition and are already flagged against each other. A takes the evaluator offline so suggestions land unreviewed now; B uses the same partition as an epistemic shield so noticing nothing counts as confirmation. Delivery window versus unfalsifiability, and the pair needs the pointer to stay separable.; `fictional-anatomy-bypass-split` — both take a conscious-versus-deep partition and put it to structural work — one invents the anatomy to license bypass and pre-route objections, the other uses the partition as an epistemic shield so self-report cannot falsify the install. Adjacent uses of the same partition device, distinguished by whether the payload is bypass licensing or unfalsifiability.; `instrumental-dissociation-workspace` — both run on an installed or exploited part-self split, but one uses it as a workspace for handling charged material and the other as an epistemic shield that makes self-report unable to disconfirm the install. Same structural precondition, opposite purposes, so the pairing is a genuine disambiguation.; `named-alter-partition-install` — one builds a durable named second self that carries the conditioned behavior; the other exploits a conscious/deep partition to make the install unfalsifiable to introspection. Related because the first often supplies the partition the second exploits, but the payloads are distinct: a persistence vehicle versus an epistemic shield.; `reality-test-insulation` — two halves of the same insulation strategy, differing in what feedback channel is disabled: an unchanged normal surface that defeats comparison against ordinary life and outside observers, versus a deep layer walled off from introspective self-report so noticing nothing reads as confirmation.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — same installed partition, different payload extracted from it: one relocates authorship of consent onto the not-self locus, the other uses the partition as an epistemic shield so self-report cannot falsify the deep claim. Both discriminators already contrast against the same neighbors, so the link helps a reader place them.


<a id="genus-190"></a>

## single-focus-induction (4)

Induction moves built on one focal object — staring, eye fatigue, closure, a lone stable anchor — whose real felt effects the operator predicts and names as trance.

[attention-anchor-portable-internalization](#entry-17) · [eye-closure](#entry-107) · [fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer](#entry-26) · [single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer](#entry-157)


<a id="entry-17"></a>

### attention-anchor-portable-internalization

[#17](#entry-17) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: authorship-shift*

A focal object is authored entirely by the operator but attributed to the listener — built, it is claimed, from the listener's own closed-eye imagery or dream material ('I took all the pretty patterns and pulses from when you close your eyes') — then internalized (transferred inside the head) as the portable pacing object for everything after. The parasitic provenance means the listener cannot reject its contents without rejecting their own internal imagery, so it feels non-impositional; eye-closure removes the external check that it isn't actually pulsing; and once internalized the operator can cite 'the pulse' at will while the listener supplies the metronome, decoupling depth from operator narration.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from ordinary external-fixation induction by the parasitic-provenance attribution (the prop is claimed to be made of the listener's own mind) and the internalization into a portable self-supplied pacer. Separated from eye-fatigue-convincer's remembered-point member — there the internal anchor is a mere memory of a real external point ratified by fatigue; here the object is operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own so it cannot be disowned.


**Risk.** Session-scoped pacing object; the authorship-attribution laundering is manipulative but not out-of-session and does not erode the refusal channel.


**Why it works.** Attributing a suggestion's content to the listener's own mind removes the external source that criticality would normally target — a person can dispute a speaker's claim far more easily than they can dispute their own imagery. Internalising the pacer additionally means the listener generates the rhythm themselves, and self-generated pacing is not checkable against any external referent, so it cannot be observed to have stopped. Falsifiable: deliver the same anchor without the 'made from your own imagery' attribution; if reported resistance and rejection rates are identical, the provenance claim is doing nothing. [plausible; source discounting; self-generation effect; absence of an external disconfirming referent]


**Worked examples.**

- *A focal object claimed to be built from your own imagery*
  - **Setup.** Opening fixation; a glowing focal object has just been produced, before any demand is attached to it.
  - **The move.** Look at it. I made this out of the shapes that drift behind your eyelids when you close them at night — the little pulses, the colours in your own dreams. It's yours. Now close your eyes and let me put it inside your head, right behind your forehead.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator produces a glowing focal object and, before asking anything of it, tells the listener where it came from: she made it out of the shapes and colours that appear behind their own eyelids, out of their own dreams. Then she has them close their eyes and puts it inside their head. Whatever the listener now sees is content they cannot disown, because rejecting it means rejecting their own imagery — and with no eyes open there is nothing to check it against.
- *Internalized so the listener supplies the pulse*
  - **Setup.** Later in the same session or a subsequent one; the object has already been internalized and declared lovely.
  - **The move.** There it is — the pulse. You don't need your eyes shut for it and you don't need me to describe it. It's keeping time behind your forehead right now, and every beat of it takes you down one more.
