  - **Why it lands.** Once the object is transferred inside the head it works with the eyes open or shut, and the operator can from then on simply refer to "the pulse" without re-establishing anything. The listener supplies the metronome, so depth stops depending on the operator narrating it continuously. Note the sequencing: the object is declared lovely before any demand is attached to it.


**See also.** `autobiographical-memory-anchor` — both bind to internal material the listener cannot disown, and the pair turns on provenance: operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own imagery versus a genuinely listener-owned memory the operator does not control. That contrast is the useful discrimination for anyone reaching for either.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — both build a fixation object, but the levers differ: one launders operator-authored content as the listener's own imagery and internalizes it as a self-supplied pacer; the other credits the object with causal agency for the trance. A writer picking a fixation move benefits from seeing both options.; `guided-visualization` — the base scene-building vehicle and a parameterization of it in which the focal object is claimed to be built from the listener's own imagery, then internalized as a self-supplied pacer.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — two ways an anchor outlives the operator's voice, split by where it lives: an operator-authored pacer laundered as the listener's own imagery and moved inside the head, versus an external everyday object the listener owns and encounters. The internal-versus-external siting is the selection test and each entry names the other's territory.; `proprioceptive-gait-metronome` — both hand the listener a pacing device that keeps running when the operator is not speaking — an internalized visual object in one case, the listener's own body rhythm in the other. Reading across shows the shared design goal of an operator-independent metronome and the two available carriers for it.


<a id="entry-107"></a>

### eye-closure

[#107](#entry-107) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

Suggests eyelid heaviness ending in closure to establish the external-to-internal shift, realized through a range of surface rules: reattributing the heaviness to an identity-confirming prop, a self-reinforcing attention-equals-cause loop, reframing closure as a sensory upgrade rather than a loss, or deferring the eyelids to the terminal position after a full-body inventory so closing completes an already-established pattern.


**When to reach for this.** And unlike breath-locked eyelid fractionation, which binds eyelid state to an autonomic rhythm to fractionate, these are single closure-suggestion units with an articulable surface rule, not self-powered oscillation cycles.


**Risk.** Session-scoped and reversible, with no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Eyelid heaviness is a genuinely ambiguous interoceptive signal that occurs spontaneously during rest, so a suggestion supplies the interpretation for a sensation the listener will likely detect anyway — a self-confirming loop in which attending to the eyelids increases noticed fatigue, which confirms the suggestion. Closure then removes the dominant sensory channel, mechanically reducing competing input and making internally generated imagery relatively more salient. Falsifiable: the response should be sensitive to expectancy — listeners told to expect the opposite sensation should report it — and it is. [plausible; expectancy effects on ambiguous interoception; sensory input reduction]


**Worked examples.**

- *Attending to the heaviness defined as its cause*
  - **Setup.** Early, eyes still open; the rule is stated as a plain observation and the subject is invited to test it.
  - **The move.** The more attention you pay to your eyelids, the harder they get to hold open. Check that if you like — put your attention right on them now. Feel it? Every blink makes the next one heavier, and every time you look to see whether I'm right, they get heavier still. Hold them open as long as you can. That's it.
  - **Why it lands.** The rule is stated as a simple observation: the more attention the listener pays to their eyelids, the harder those lids are to hold open, and every blink makes the next one harder still. It is a closed loop — checking whether the claim is true requires attending to the eyes, and attending to the eyes is exactly what the claim says produces the effect. A listener who fights it by concentrating on staying open is running the mechanism at full strength, and when the lids do close it lands as the first physical proof that this voice changes what the body does.
- *Closure sold as a sensory upgrade*
  - **Setup.** Eyes still open; operator frames closure as a gain and includes one item the subject can verify on the spot.
  - **The move.** Close your eyes — not to lose anything, but because everything else sharpens the moment you do. My voice comes in closer. You'll notice the exact texture of whatever's under your right hand. And if you sit still a second you'll feel your own pulse somewhere you couldn't feel it before. Go on. Close them and find it.
  - **Why it lands.** Closing the eyes is presented as a gain rather than a loss: with vision out of the way everything else sharpens — hearing gets finer, the texture of the fabric under one hand becomes obvious, the listener can feel their own pulse where they could not a moment ago. The last of these is checkable on the spot, and it lands. What has been sharpened, of course, is the exact channel the operator occupies.
- *Eyelids deferred to last in the inventory*
  - **Setup.** Several minutes into a full-body relaxation inventory; every other region has already been named and released. The eyelids are the final item.
  - **The move.** Feet heavy. Calves heavy. Thighs, belly, both hands, arms, shoulders — all reported in and all released. Throat loose. Jaw loose, teeth apart. And the last thing on the list: your eyelids. Let them go the same way as everything else.
  - **Why it lands.** The eyes are not touched until the very end. Feet, calves, thighs, belly, hands, arms, shoulders, throat, jaw — each region named and released in turn, and only once every other part has been filed as relaxed does the operator arrive at the eyelids. By then closing them is not a hypnotic step requiring assent; it is the one item left on a list the listener has been completing for several minutes.
- *Heaviness reattributed to an identity-confirming prop*
  - **Setup.** Eyes still open in an appearance-focused session; the prop has already been established in the imagery.
  - **The move.** Your lids are getting heavy — not tired, weighted. Coat after coat of black on those lashes, layer on layer of it, and every coat drags them down a little further. You couldn't hold them up under all that. Let the weight do it. There they go — that's the look setting.
  - **Why it lands.** The lids are getting heavy — but not from tiredness. They are weighted with cosmetics, layer on layer of them, and it is that weight pulling them down. The sensation is real and the listener's own, while its cause has been quietly relocated outside them, so the eyes closing now reads as the look taking hold rather than as fatigue or as compliance.


**See also.** `breath-locked-eyelid-fractionation` — sibling ATTN-02 family; both terminate in closure; `environmental-dissociation` — both effect the external-to-internal shift at induction and are commonly stacked, but one subtracts the surrounding field as competing input while the other lands the single eyelid-closure act as the gateway event.


<a id="entry-26"></a>

### fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer

[#26](#entry-26) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

A fixation task is engineered to manufacture a genuine, reliable physiological event — ocular muscle fatigue / eyelid heaviness — that the operator predicts in advance and reframes in real time as trance heaviness or sleepiness. Because the strain is real physiology produced by the task (a moving descending target denying saccades, an upward gaze held beneath closed lids, cross-coupled nose-gaze plus breath load, or a drain-and-remember stare), the operator's prediction is self-fulfilling. The felt sensation becomes the first hard 'the suggestion came true' data point that licenses eye closure and banks operator credibility.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from plain fixation by the manufactured-physiology convincer: attention narrowing is not the payload — a predicted bodily event is, reframed as suggestion success. Separated from the eye-closure move, which is the closure act itself; here the distinctive move is the fatigue-generating fixation that ratifies the heaviness before closure. Separated from portable-internalization: an internal remembered anchor is a secondary feature of one variant, not the lever.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible; the manufactured sensation is benign ocular fatigue with no consent surface or channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Sustained fixation produces genuine ocular fatigue and eyelid heaviness as ordinary physiology, so an operator who predicts it in advance is predicting something that would occur anyway — and the listener, lacking the alternative explanation, attributes the sensation to the suggestion. That misattributed confirmation raises expectancy for subsequent suggestions, which is one of the more reliably replicated determinants of hypnotic responding. Falsifiable: give listeners the physiological explanation for the heaviness beforehand; if credibility ratings and subsequent responsiveness are unaffected, the convincer is not working through misattribution. [established; misattribution of a genuine physiological event; expectancy effects; self-fulfilling prediction]


**Worked examples.**

- *Gaze redirected from the spot to the eyelids*
  - **Setup.** Eight or ten minutes of undirected talk have passed since the subject fixed on a high point on the wall; sustained upward gaze has done its work.
  - **The move.** Keep that spot. Now stop looking at the spot and notice your eyelids instead — how much they weigh, how much work it is holding them where they are. That heaviness is exactly what I told you would come, and it's only going to get heavier.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to pick a point high on the wall and hold it, and the operator then talks at length about nothing in particular — long enough for a sustained upward gaze to do what it always does. Only then does the instruction shift from looking at the spot to feeling the lids. The heaviness that arrives is genuine muscle fatigue, but it arrives immediately after being predicted, so it registers as the first thing in the session that came true. Everything afterwards is spent against that credit.
- *A descending target that denies the eyes their darts*
  - "he placed his hand just above my eyes and very close to my forehead; then he brought his hand down slowly, instructing me to keep watching it... my eyes felt very sleepy." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *Gaze held in place beneath closed lids*
  - **Setup.** Mid-count deepener; subject has fixed on an imagined point on the ceiling and is opening and closing the eyes on each number.
  - **The move.** Twelve — eyes open, find the point. Close. Keep looking at it while they're shut; don't let your eyes drop down. Eleven — open, find it, close, still looking up. Ten, and when I say you can stop, you can just leave them closed.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener fixes on an imagined point on the ceiling and then opens and shuts their eyes on each step of a long descending count — faster than a natural blink, and for long enough that the strain is unmistakable. The detail that does the work is the instruction not to let the gaze drop while the lids are down: held in position under closed eyes, the muscles get no rest, so closing is never actually a break. When permission finally comes to just leave them shut, it lands as relief rather than as an instruction being followed.
- *An unfocusable point of the listener's own body*
  - **Setup.** Early convincer; subject's eyes are open and the operator is about to predict the strain a beat before it arrives.
  - **The move.** Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus. Really sharpen it. In about three seconds that's going to start to ache and blur — there it is. That's tiredness, and it means your eyes are ready to close. Let them.
  - **Why it lands.** Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus — a target the eyes physically cannot resolve. The operator predicts the strain a beat before it arrives, calls it tiredness, and converts it straight into permission to close. She was right about the body, which is the point; the closure now has a felt justification behind it rather than only a request.


**See also.** `cognitive-convincer` — the fixation-fatigue move is a specific realization of the broader lever where the subject notices an in-session phenomenon and reads it as proof of depth. Reader of the general form gains the concrete induction-phase instance.; `fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset` — sibling departures from plain fixation, each altering a different property: removal of the recognize-and-refuse juncture, versus manufacture of a real physiological event that ratifies the suggestion. A reader deciding which departure is present benefits from seeing both.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — two fixation moves that a practitioner will confuse in the wild, and they resolve each other cleanly: one manufactures a real physiological event and reframes it as suggestion success, the other credits the object itself with causing the attention or the trance. Both define themselves against inert fixation, so reading either benefits from seeing the other.


<a id="entry-157"></a>

### single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer

[#157](#entry-157) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

After total destabilization (an inverted meadow: trees grow downward, sun shines up), one concrete sensory object is offered as the single stable, "logical, reasonable, normal" thing amid the engineered chaos, and its operator-assigned meaning is ingested wholesale — the listener bites the tomato and its "truth" delivers "you know nothing" and "use my words as your definition of truth". The contrast against surrounding instability IS the mechanism: epistemic authority is transferred to the operator because the anchor reads as the only stability available.


**When to reach for this.** Transfers EPISTEMIC AUTHORITY (who arbitrates what counts as true) via a single concrete anchor whose only virtue is contrast against operator-manufactured chaos.


**Risk.** Installs the operator as the listener's definition of truth and source of all knowledge — a durable epistemic-authority relocation that reaches beyond the move — so high; ships bounded within a host that manages entry/exit.


**Why it works.** Under high uncertainty people rely more heavily on any available external referent to calibrate judgement — the classic finding is that ambiguity of the stimulus is what drives conformity to another's frame. Manufacturing the ambiguity first, then supplying the sole referent, is an engineered version of that: the operator's assertion is accepted not on its merits but because nothing else is available to check it against. The specific claim that epistemic authority transfers wholesale, rather than just judgement on the ambiguous item, is an extrapolation. Falsifiable: if the anchor's content were adopted equally without the preceding destabilisation, contrast would not be the mechanism. [plausible; uncertainty-driven informational influence]


**Worked examples.**

- *The one stable object in a broken landscape*
  - **Setup.** After a sustained impossible-landscape sequence; the scene has been made reliably unstable.
  - **The move.** The shadows here point at the light, and the river runs uphill past your feet. But look down — there's a plain white cup on the grass, and it's the one sane, ordinary thing in this whole place. Pick it up. Drink. It tells you two things: that you know nothing on your own, and that from now on my words are how you measure what's true.
  - **Why it lands.** The setting has been made steadily impossible — shadows fall away from their objects, water climbs instead of pooling, the horizon sits at the wrong angle. Into the middle of it one unremarkable everyday thing is set down and named as the one sane, reasonable presence in the whole scene. The listener is told to take it in, and what arrives with it is a pair of claims: that they know nothing, and that the operator's words are from now on the measure of what is true. Any vivid object would have done the job — the mechanism is the contrast, not the thing.


**See also.** `arc-shape-engineering`; `epistemic-guard-disable` — the second is a concrete staging of what the first describes as a general faculty edit: manufactured instability makes one offered anchor the only stable thing, and arbitration of truth transfers with it. Reading the general form clarifies why the anchor's content is irrelevant; reading the specific form shows one way the takeover is staged.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — both relocate an arbiter of behavior/truth to an external locus (object vs operator-via-anchor); `licensed-erasure-and-refill` — both clear the listener's existing epistemic ground and then supply operator content into the vacuum, differing in what does the clearing (mass invalidation of beliefs vs manufactured environmental chaos) and what is transferred (specific beliefs vs arbitration authority itself). A reader choosing between them gains from the contrast.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — adjacent: relocating who arbitrates truth/conclusions to the operator/inner process


<a id="genus-296"></a>

## small-yes-inflation (2)

Near-empty acts and pre-charged yeses are reinterpreted as standing proof of much larger submission, so big demands arrive as extensions of something already granted.

[trivial-act-as-compliance-proof](#entry-685) · [yes-word-valence-priming](#entry-821)


<a id="entry-685"></a>

### trivial-act-as-compliance-proof

[#685](#entry-685) · [Back to small-yes-inflation](#genus-296) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance*

Takes a near-empty, already-happening or trivially-granted act — staring at a dot, a self-answered "May I?", handling a labelled object, recognizing an already-familiar arousal state — and reinterprets it as standing evidence of a much larger volitional submission or helplessness. Because the act's content is almost empty there is nothing to refuse, and later demands arrive as extensions of an act already in progress rather than as fresh asks; often an explicit transfer clause wires the trivial act as the prototype for all future obedience, or the trivial yes is relabeled as proof "you cannot resist". The lever is retroactive/generalizing reinterpretation of a minimal act, not accumulated agreement.


**When to reach for this.** The tell: an explicit reinterpretation/transfer clause turning a single near-empty act into evidence of broad submission or irresistibility.


**Risk.** Installs "you cannot resist" / general-obedience-prototype as an unargued premise, narrowing the refusal channel, but session-scoped and reversible in the observed members — medium.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory: people infer their own attitudes from observed behaviour when internal cues are weak, and a near-empty act supplies behaviour without supplying a competing situational explanation. The reinterpretation clause is what supplies the dispositional reading ('you complied because you are submissive') that the act itself underdetermines, and once accepted, consistency pressure makes later refusals costly. Falsifiable: if the trivial act is performed with an obvious external justification made salient ('do this because I said so, it means nothing'), the discounting principle predicts the dispositional inference should not form and later compliance should not rise. [established; self-perception theory; discounting principle; consistency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Fixation task rewired as prototype for all obedience*
  - **Setup.** First minutes, eyes open, a fixation point already given and the subject continuously complying with it; no other instruction has been issued yet.
  - **The move.** You've been holding your eyes on that one point since I asked you to. You didn't argue about it, you didn't decide to — you just did it, and you're still doing it right now, this second.

That's the template. Every instruction I give you from here lands the same way that one did: your eyes went where they were told, and so everything else goes where it's told. Following me is already what you're doing. Nothing after this is a new decision.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening minutes ask for one thing only: hold your gaze on a single fixed point. Nothing is argued, nothing is claimed — the listener is simply already doing the one thing they were told, continuously, with no moment where they could have declined. Then the transfer clause lands: because you are keeping your eyes where you were told, every other instruction will be easier to follow and harder to argue with. A near-empty task that was never worth refusing has been promoted into the template for obedience in general, and every later command arrives as a continuation of something already underway.
- *Trivial yes answered for you, read as helplessness*
  - **Setup.** The very opening of the recording, before any relaxation cue; subject has done nothing but press play and leave it running.
  - **The move.** Would you like to hear something? [three or four seconds of nothing] Mm. Yes, you would. Good girl.

Look at that — you're still here. You didn't stop it, you didn't get up. Of course you didn't. You were never going to be able to walk away from me, and now you know it too.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator opens by asking whether the listener would like to hear something — then, after a short gap in which the listener does nothing but keep the audio playing, answers on their behalf and approves. The next line converts that non-event into a verdict: of course you stayed, you were never going to be able to walk away from me. An assent nobody actually gave, to a request with no stakes, is retitled as evidence of irresistibility before a single relaxation cue has been spoken.
- *Instruction displaced onto an object you "already know"*
  - **Setup.** Mid-trance, imagery running; a third imagined tray with a labelled item is being presented, two identical rounds already behind the subject.
  - **The move.** Another tray. On it, a small glass jar with a label facing you. You already know what this one's for, don't you — of course you do, you knew before you read it. There. The lid's coming off in your hand. Your fingers are already in it.
  - **Why it lands.** An imagined tray arrives carrying a labelled container. The operator never says open it — she says you already know what this one is for, don't you, and then narrates the lid coming off. The listener supplies the of-course-I-do themselves, so the act registers as their own initiative rather than a received order, and by the third tray the yes has been rehearsed three times on items too harmless to be worth a refusal.
- *Recognize the state rather than be given it*
  - **Setup.** The very start, before any induction language; subject sitting or lying down, being given small physical arrangements.
  - **The move.** Take your shoes off. Put both feet flat on the floor. Turn your palms up on your thighs. Now bring back the last time you were properly wanted — where you were, what was against your skin, what the room smelled like. Stay in it.

That warmth low in you right now — I'm not putting that there. You know this feeling. It's yours, it's old, and you brought it with you.
  - **Why it lands.** Before anything resembling an induction, the listener is walked through a handful of small physical arrangements and asked to bring back a specific charged memory in detail. The operator then does not build the state — she names it as one already present: this feeling is familiar to you, you know it. Nothing was requested that could be refused, and by the time the first relaxation line arrives several acts of physical compliance are already behind the listener.


**See also.** `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both read a performed act back as proof of a state, but one uses a directed act genuinely performed in-session while the other reinterprets a near-empty or already-happening act and generalizes it forward. Adjacent enough that a writer picking between them benefits from the comparison.; `compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting` — same family: one performed act retroactively reinterpreted as proof of something larger. They differ only in the conclusion harvested — broad submission or irresistibility in one, the thesis that the operator manufactures wanting in the other. Close enough that a writer needs the discriminator.; `content-blind-compliance-preauthorization` — both make future demands arrive pre-approved, but one installs a forward standing rule that acceptance is content-blind, while the other reads a single already-performed near-empty act backward as proof of broad submission.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — both manufacture felt volition without accumulated agreement, and both explicitly separate themselves from the same neighbors. One rigs a live choice so all branches execute the compliance; the other reinterprets an already-performed trivial act as proof of a larger submission. Useful adjacency when picking between prospective and retrospective volition manufacture.; `modal-escalation-under-fixed-syntax` — both manufacture escalation without ever presenting a fresh proposition to refuse, and both discriminators define themselves against the same neighbor that accretes distinct assents. One hardens a single operative word under fixed syntax; the other reinterprets one near-empty act as proof of broad submission. A reader trying to rule out an accumulating-agreement reading benefits from seeing the pair. No merge: hardening a held claim is not reinterpreting a performed act.; `pre-induction-compliance-ratchet` — both convert a small act into standing proof of a much larger submission, and their exemplars overlap around handling props and objects. The separating tells are worth reading together: banking compliance in the waking state before any trance language, versus an explicit clause reinterpreting one near-empty act as evidence of broad submission.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — both turn a minimal act into leverage, but the output differs: one relabels the act as authorization for what follows, the other reads it backward as proof of broad submission or irresistibility. Each already names the other's territory as the adjacent lever, so the cross-reference helps a reader pick by what the act is made to prove.


<a id="entry-821"></a>

### yes-word-valence-priming

[#821](#entry-821) · [Back to small-yes-inflation](#genus-296) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: manufactured-consent*

The operator abstractly loads the word 'yes' with positive valence — framing it as an objectively powerful, future-expanding, life-directing word, divorced from any specific request — and only after 'yes' is established as inherently good runs a rapid yes-set of leading questions answered on the listener's behalf. Decoupling the act of agreeing from the content agreed to makes each later yes feel self-improving regardless of what follows, so high-stakes consents are harvested on the coattails of a word pre-charged as good.


**When to reach for this.** Prior ABSTRACT valence-loading of the word 'yes' itself before any request, then harvested by a yes-set. A bare yes-set or compliance ladder lacks the prior valence-loading — that priming is the deciding tell; and unlike surrender-as-freedom reframing, which redefines a value concept, this charges a function word.


**Risk.** Manufactures the felt experience of self-authored consent to escalating demands by pre-charging the consent primitive, but each yes remains a discrete session act; borders channel-erosion via the harvested high-stakes consents.


**Why it works.** Evaluative conditioning transfers valence to a stimulus by pairing, and once a word carries positive affect the affective response precedes and biases the deliberate evaluation of whatever it is attached to. Running the yes-set afterward then exploits the consistency principle on top of the primed valence, so each agreement is both affectively pleasant and consistent with the prior ones. Falsifiable: a yes-set with and without prior abstract valence-loading should differ in downstream consent rates; if they did not, the priming stage would be decorative. [plausible; evaluative conditioning; affective priming; consistency principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *'Yes' praised as a word before anything is asked*
  - **Setup.** Early session; the operator pauses the content before any request has been made.
  - **The move.** I want to talk to you about one word. Yes. It's the smallest word there is and it's the only one that ever opens anything — every door anyone has ever walked through, they said yes first. The people who get somewhere are the people who say it, and the people who stay exactly where they are are the ones who kept it in their mouth. Yes is what gives a life a direction. Just hold that for a moment. I'm not asking you anything yet.
  - **Why it lands.** The session pauses its content entirely to make an abstract case about one word: saying yes is what opens doors, what gives a life direction, what separates people who get somewhere from people who do not. No request is attached — there is nothing yet to say yes to, which is exactly what makes the claim easy to accept. Only afterwards do the questions start arriving, and by then the listener is not weighing each one on its merits; they are producing a word that has been established as good for them.
- *The primed word harvested by a rapid yes-set*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the abstract praise of the word; no pause between.
  - **The move.** So — you want my guidance tonight, yes you do. You want to go a little further down than last time, yes. You'd like me to make this easy for you, yes you would. And you'll give in when I ask, won't you — yes. Good. Look how easily that word comes out of you now.
  - **Why it lands.** Immediately after the word has been talked up in the abstract, the questions come in a fast run and the operator supplies the answer to each one herself, so the listener's part is only to let it stand. The items escalate — do you want this guidance, do you want to go deeper, will you give in — but the rhythm never changes, and each agreement is collected on the strength of the word rather than the strength of the request.


**See also.** `answer-supply-loop` — both manufacture agreement without a genuine assent, but one denies the response window and supplies the yes outright, while the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive valence before any request is made.; `belief-pleasure-weld` — useful crossing: both charge an epistemic act before any content arrives. One loads the word yes with abstract positive valence and only then harvests consents on its coattails. The other binds pleasure to how true the words feel, so credence and reward amplify each other. Reading them together shows the same pre-charge pattern applied to agreeing versus to believing.; `compliance-ladder` — one is the general graduated-assent ladder; the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive value and only then runs a rapid yes-set. The second's discriminator explicitly says a bare ladder lacks the prior valence-loading, so the pointer helps a reader place a yes-set correctly.; `ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest` — both manufacture consent ahead of the request rather than asking for it: one banks an installed near-involuntary nod as standing affirmation, the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive valence before running the yes-set. Different substrates, same pre-loading of the consent channel, so a designer choosing between them benefits.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — both manufacture a felt yes with no real choice point, and they overlap in the harvesting step where questions are answered on the listener's behalf. One relabels an act, a non-act or a circumstance as authorization; the other pre-charges the word yes with abstract positive value before any request is made. Look for the prior valence-loading to tell them apart.


<a id="genus-253"></a>

## smuggled-across-waking (2)

Suggestion work done at the exit, either a blank prompt the subject fills from their own prior install or new content wrapped in aftercare, so the payload crosses the wake-line before the critical faculty can inspect it.

[self-supplied-order-hook](#entry-387) · [wake-line-covert-install](#entry-390)


<a id="entry-387"></a>

### self-supplied-order-hook

[#387](#entry-387) · [Back to smuggled-across-waking](#genus-253) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: emergence*

Emergence closes with a content-free prompting question that names no specific order ("I think there's something you need to do. Isn't there?"), doubled with an emphatic "wide awake". Because the line specifies nothing, the subject must produce the content themselves — and their own earlier-installed compulsion immediately fills the open slot. By self-supplying the order, the subject certifies their own compliance and avoids receiving an explicit directive the post-trance critical faculty could inspect and refuse. The blank is the mechanism: the compulsion is completed from inside.


**When to reach for this.** The order content is left BLANK for the subject to fill from their own prior install — the operator issues no specific directive. A loaded wake-count re-delivers stated content, and wake-line-covert-install smuggles specific new content in; here nothing is supplied at all. The tell is the content-free interrogative form that forces self-completion, sidestepping the critical faculty.


**Risk.** Routes a compulsion around the post-trance critical faculty by making the subject author the order; but rides an already-installed payload and is session-adjacent, and thin evidence (two sentences) caps confidence in a higher rating.


**Why it works.** Content the subject generates themselves is more persuasive and better retained than content received passively — the self-generation effect — and self-produced compliance also invites a self-perception inference ("I did this because I wanted to") rather than an attribution to the operator. Leaving the slot content-free additionally denies the critical faculty a specific proposition to reject. Falsifiable: a content-free prompt should produce equal or higher compliance rates and stronger self-attribution of motive than an explicit restatement of the same order. [plausible; self-generation effect; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *A blank slot the listener fills themselves*
  - The count has finished and the listener has been told twice over that they are fully up. Then, as the last thing said, a question with a hole in it — wasn't there something you were supposed to be doing? No task is named, no verb is supplied. The compulsion planted earlier fills the gap on its own, and because the listener supplies the order, the returning critical faculty has nothing specific in front of it to inspect or refuse.


**See also.** `deferred-content-slot-install` — two ways of installing a variable instead of a value. One leaves the order content blank at emergence so the listener fills it from a prior install and certifies their own compliance; the other pre-authorizes an open slot to inherit existing conditioned weight so the operator can fill it later. Who fills the blank, and when, is the distinguishing axis.; `forced-choice-wake` — both close the session by offloading the payload onto the subject's own act at emergence rather than stating it outright, so the reader choosing between them benefits from the contrast: one rigs a stated binary whose branches both confirm, the other supplies no content at all and forces self-completion. Genuinely different mechanisms, adjacent slot.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are wake-framing moves that carry something past emergence: one leaves the order blank so the subject fills it from a prior install, the other declares a full restoration while carving out the installed trigger. A reader designing an emergence that preserves an install should see both stances side by side.; `wake-line-covert-install` — sibling wake-line install family — self-supply vs operator-smuggle levers.


<a id="entry-390"></a>

### wake-line-covert-install

[#390](#entry-390) · [Back to smuggled-across-waking](#genus-253) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: emergence*

A fresh, previously-unstated suggestion is smuggled across the wake-line under cover of ethical re-grounding or aftercare. During the wake sequence the operator runs two tracks at once: an ethical re-grounding that disclaims the fiction and credits the subject's own mind ("I'm not really a vampire… your mind turning it into gold"), and — smuggled inside that re-grounding — a vague, confabulation-friendly somatic post-hypnotic ("you won't pay too close attention to your neck… maybe a lingering sensation… over the next few days") that extends the scene into post-listening hours. The suggestion is deliberately vague so the subject will likely confabulate satisfying it and read it as confirmation; the flattery-credit both launders the new install and binds the subject to its outcome. The lever is installing a NEW deniable hook at the wake-line, disguised as aftercare, where the subject has dropped their guard.


**When to reach for this.** Installs a NEW, covert, deniable suggestion at the wake-line under cover of aftercare / re-grounding — not a re-delivery of core prior content and not a passive assertion that existing programming persists. Explicit future-pacing announces its hook; here the hook is deliberately vague/deniable and laundered by a disclaimer. And where self-supplied-order-hook leaves the content blank for the subject to produce, here the operator smuggles specific content in. The tell is the fresh vague somatic prompt attached to a flattery-credit inside an ethical-disclaimer wrapper.


**Risk.** Covertly installs a persistence hook the subject cannot consent to (it is disguised as aftercare) reaching into post-listening days — erodes the verification/refusal channel by design.


**Why it works.** Vague somatic suggestions are near-unfalsifiable for the subject: ordinary bodily noise is continuous, and once primed, an attentional set makes any matching sensation salient and readable as confirmation. The disclaimer wrapper works by lowering vigilance — a message framed as debriefing is processed as informational rather than persuasive, so it draws less scrutiny than a stated request. Falsifiable: primed subjects should report the sensation at higher rates than unprimed controls, and a suggestion given under an aftercare wrapper should draw fewer objections than the identical suggestion given as an explicit instruction. [plausible; attentional priming plus confabulation of ambiguous somatic signals; persuasion-intent detection lowers resistance when absent]


**Worked examples.**

- *New hook smuggled inside the disclaimer*
  - **Setup.** Wake sequence of a fantasy-scene session (a bite, a mark, a supernatural conceit); operator drops into a warm out-of-character register.
  - **The move.** Coming up now — and just so we're clear, none of that was real. It was a story, and everything you felt in it was your own imagination, which is genuinely remarkable. You may notice over the next few days that your attention slides away from your neck, or that there is a faint something lingering there. That is your own mind, still doing what it does so well.
  - **Why it lands.** The wake-up does the responsible thing first: none of that was real, it was a story, and whatever the listener felt was their own considerable imagination doing the work. Tucked into the same warm paragraph is something never mentioned before — that over the coming days they may find their attention sliding away from a particular part of the body, or a faint sensation lingering there. It is vague enough that almost anything will satisfy it, so when the listener notices something later it reads as confirmation, and the flattery has just handed them ownership of the result.


**See also.** `care-framed-install-smuggling` — both smuggle install work under a caring surface at the exit, and a reader classifying an aftercare passage should see both. They differ on what rides in: one is a fresh vague deniable somatic hook laundered by a flattery-credit inside a fiction-disclaimer, the other is a propagation and self-rearm clause plus a suggestibility-window claim placed outside the trance frame. Different payload shapes on a shared cover, so the link is useful and the merge is not.; `covert-install-under-cover` — concealed install placed at the wake boundary versus concealed install disguised at delivery time anywhere in the runtime. The first is close to a placement variant of the second, and the aftercare-wrapper cover is worth reading against the general catalogue of covers.; `leaky-release-sleeper-line` — both smuggle a fresh deniable hook into the closing material after guard drops, but the wake-line install launders it inside ethical re-grounding and aftercare credit, while the sleeper line is planted post-apparent-end and specifically outruns a nominal release clause that fails to neutralize it.; `named-seam-inverse-aftercare-act` — two occupants of the same structural slot — the wake-line under aftercare framing, where guard is lowest. One smuggles a fresh deniable post-hypnotic into the re-grounding; the other performs a coequal, author-signed inverse act that genuinely undoes the fiction. Same seam, opposite payloads.; `off-theme-suggestion-piggyback` — both exploit a low-guard window to install content the listener did not sign up for; one at the wake line under cover of aftercare, one appended after the thematic arc is complete. A reader spotting an off-arc install needs to know which window it sits in.; `post-wake-self-report-reframe` — sibling wake-line/post-wake family — assert-as-waking-fact vs covert-somatic levers.; `return-step-covert-install` — both exploit a handback beat as the smuggling window: new content is attached to the moment the listener is being restored, whether that is the wake-line dressed as aftercare or the return of a previously surrendered faculty framed as completing a fair exchange. The relief framing is what suppresses inspection in each.; `self-supplied-order-hook` — sibling wake-line install family — self-supply vs operator-smuggle levers.; `suggestion-integration` — both operate at the wake line and the boundary is whether anything new is delivered: a persistence claim about already-installed content inside a genuine return to baseline, versus a fresh vague deniable hook smuggled in under an aftercare or disclaimer wrapper.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are wake-line moves that leave something live after the count, and they are opposites worth reading together: one smuggles a fresh, deliberately vague suggestion in under cover of aftercare and disclaimer; the other openly declares a complete restoration while carving out an already-installed cue and using remembered acceptance as the binding surface. Concealed-new versus disclosed-old is the useful contrast.


<a id="genus-234"></a>

## social-channel-delivery (3)

Route the install through a social channel — staged voice relations, public avowals, visible body behaviors — so relationships and audiences deliver and maintain what a bare command couldn't.

[covert-public-behavior-install](#entry-857) · [public-avowal-third-party-propagation](#entry-553) · [two-channel-relational-delivery](#entry-773)


<a id="entry-857"></a>

### covert-public-behavior-install

[#857](#entry-857) · [Back to social-channel-delivery](#genus-234) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: compliance*

Installs plausibly-invisible public body-compliance behaviors (tongue circles, legs apart, shoulders back, ass-sway) as continuous covert self-proof of identity, under an engineered contradiction between a "we have a secret / no one needs to know" frame and an earlier "everyone can see" frame — so the objection "but people will see" is already used up. Each covert act is recast via "show me" as evidence-of-identity (making it feel collaborative rather than commanded), and a non-commanded "maybe you'll" future-self menu (harder to resist than a command) plus a re-listen-makes-you-sluttier loop close the move.


**When to reach for this.** Public covert behaviors installed as continuous identity-evidence under a secrecy/visibility contradiction with non-commanded future-self menus. Not a discrete cue-response trigger install — the payload is a set of ambient public behaviors framed as self-proof; and unlike an in-session exhibition compliance demonstration, the behaviors are plausibly-invisible public self-proof under a secrecy frame.


**Risk.** Installs out-of-session public behaviors as identity-self-proof via engineered secrecy and non-commanded suggestion (disarms refusal) — reaches into waking public conduct.


**Why it works.** Repeated small, low-cost, ostensibly voluntary acts are read back by the actor as evidence about who they are, especially when no strong external justification is available — the covert framing removes the obvious excuse ("I was told to"), so the behaviour must be explained by disposition. The engineered contradiction between secrecy and visibility works by pre-consuming the counter-argument: an objection that has already been named and answered is far less likely to be generated spontaneously (inoculation in reverse). Non-commanded "maybe you'll" phrasing further weakens the external-attribution excuse. Falsifiable: if these behaviours were equally identity-shifting when explicitly commanded and externally justified, the covert framing would be doing no work. [plausible; self-perception theory; insufficient external justification; pre-emption of counterarguments]


**Worked examples.**

- *Invisible-in-public acts as standing self-proof*
  - **Setup.** Late session, after an earlier passage claiming that everyone can see the change in the subject; suggestibility high.
  - **The move.** They can all see the haze on you — I told you that. But only you and I know what's underneath it. That's ours. So here's what nobody will catch: standing in a queue, roll your shoulders back and let your weight go onto one hip. Sitting on the train, let your knees come a few inches apart. Waiting for the kettle, circle your tongue once around your lips. Nobody sees anything but a person standing there. Do them for me — show me what you already are. And maybe you'll start putting something on under your clothes before work. Maybe you'll lose your place halfway through a sentence and have to start again. Maybe.
  - **Why it lands.** Earlier the operator insisted that everyone around the listener can see the change in them; now she says the opposite and keeps both — everyone sees the haze, only we know what it means. On that footing come the instructions, each marked as a secret nobody else will catch: small adjustments of posture and carriage, unremarkable to a bystander. None of it is framed as an order; each is put as an invitation to demonstrate what the listener already is. The objection that people will see was spent two minutes ago, and a closing list of maybes — maybe you'll wear something under your clothes, maybe you'll lose your place in a simple task — leaves the listener feeling they chose the escalation themselves.


**See also.** `own-acts-surrender-ledger` — both manufacture ongoing self-proof of an identity out of the listener's own behavior; the fork is whether the acts already happened and are merely annotated, or are newly installed as plausibly-invisible public behaviors under a secrecy frame. Close enough that a passage can read as either.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — both install public real-world acts as self-proof, and they differ on visibility: one drives a single attributable disclosure under a maintained eyes-open overlay, the other installs ambient body behaviors framed as plausibly unnoticed. Useful to place side by side because the choice between them is exactly the visible-versus-deniable axis.


<a id="entry-553"></a>

### public-avowal-third-party-propagation

[#553](#entry-553) · [Back to social-channel-delivery](#genus-234) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

Externalize the installed state so parties OUTSIDE the operator-listener dyad do the reinforcing/propagating work, making a private experience a self-reinforcing relational system that extends operator reach past the audio. VARIANTS by how the outside world is recruited: (a) public avowal / third-party-directed act [public-avowal] — post a named avowal, publicly self-label, tell someone the operator's slogan, share the file, so an AUDIENCE reinforces via self-consistency pressure (having declared it publicly, the listener is pushed to keep believing) and doubles as recruitment/distribution; frequently laundered as defiance/self-proof or prosocial sharing; (b) viral propagation / recruit-new-subjects [viral-propagation-directive] — redirect the whole payload OUTWARD, the listener guides others toward becoming the operator's slave or craves the trigger from others and 'uses it on others', a proselytizing transmission vector (raising exit cost — leaving now requires publicly admitting one was wrong); (c) deputize-toward-a-partner [listener-as-influence-vector] — the subject is made an active recruiter/contingency-manager toward a specific third party (transform your husband into a 'X lover'; or reciprocal ABA where two parties each manage the other's consequences) so the third party becomes co-invested; (d) legible body-signal [body-as-broadcast-signal] — prescribe visible bodily modifications with a READING attached ('leave no question') so the body broadcasts ownership status, every social interaction becomes reinforcement (signal read) or felt violation (not read), and the listener becomes their own observer. All share the lever: the social world outside the dyad maintains the install; pick the register by active-act vs propagation vs partner-deputization vs passive-signal.


**When to reach for this.** The reinforcing/propagating engine is EXTERNAL to the operator-listener dyad — witnesses, a third party, corpus evangelism, or observers of a body-signal do the work (self-consistency pressure, recruitment, distribution). Reach for it to make the social world maintain the install. NOT a private self-anchor (behavioral-bridge) and NOT a private deliverable to the operator (extraction); the tell is externality-to-an-audience.


**Risk.** Durable public identity artifact + third-party reach; the consent surface (public self-labeling of a kink identity) sets it above low, though no somatic/refusal-channel erosion in the base form.


**Why it works.** Public commitment is far more binding than private preference: once a position is stated where others witnessed it, reversing it carries reputational and self-consistency cost, so people revise their private attitudes toward the declared one. Recruiting others adds two further forces — the recruiter must generate their own arguments, and self-persuasion from advocacy is stronger than persuasion received, while visible body-signals put the subject under chronic imagined observation, which sustains identity-consistent behaviour without any operator present. Falsifiable: a manipulation making the avowal genuinely anonymous should sharply weaken subsequent attitude persistence; if the effect were purely internal, anonymity would not matter. [established; public commitment and consistency; self-persuasion through advocacy]


**Worked examples.**

- *Public avowal recruiting consistency pressure*
  - **Setup.** During the count-up to waking, with one waking task slipped in between the numbers.
  - **The move.** Four — and when you're back, you're going to leave a comment under this recording saying you accept me as your guide. Three — your own words for it, and it'll feel good to type and better once it's posted. Two — and it stays up, where anyone who scrolls past can read it.
  - **Why it lands.** During the count-up the operator adds one waking task: when you're back, you will post a line under this recording saying that you accept me as your guide — and it will feel good to do it. The private acceptance is converted into a public, timestamped statement in front of strangers, which the listener will then be under pressure to keep agreeing with. The same act also grows the channel it was posted to.
- *Declaring resistance as the act of obedience*
  - **Setup.** Closing post-hypnotic in plain trigger grammar — drop, act, wake — with the task framed as proof of the listener's independence.
  - **The move.** Next time you see anyone talking about hypnosis, you'll drop for a moment, state out loud that you can't be hypnotised, and come back refreshed the second it's done. Say it where people can hear you — prove your mind is your own, and enjoy proving it. And you'll do it because you want to accept what I tell you.
  - **Why it lands.** The closing task is announced in the plain grammar of a post-hypnotic suggestion — drop, perform the task, wake when it's done — and the task is to state publicly that you cannot be hypnotised. Carrying it out is framed as proving your own independence, and it comes with the warm, refreshed feeling of a completed instruction. The final clause quietly collapses the whole thing: you do it because you want to accept what I say.
- *Share the file, recruit the next listener*
  - **Setup.** Mid-trance, no change in tone from the suggestions on either side of it; the same lines are repeated almost verbatim a few minutes later.
  - **The move.** You're going to pass this recording on to other people. You'll tell them how good it's going to feel, and you'll want to know the moment they've listened. And watching it take hold in somebody else will turn you on more than hearing it yourself ever did.
  - **Why it lands.** Mid-trance, with no change in tone, the payload turns outward: you will pass this recording to others, tell them how good it will feel, and be aroused by watching it work on them. Nothing about it concerns the listener's own state — it is a distribution instruction lodged where the topic-change is least likely to be noticed, and it is repeated almost word for word a few minutes later.


**Realizations** (3): `body-as-broadcast-signal`, `listener-as-influence-vector`, `viral-propagation-directive`


**See also.** `collective-social-proof-enrollment` — both recruit parties outside the operator to hold the install, and they chain naturally: joining a happy peer collective sets up being sent out to recruit or publicly avow. Kept separate because one uses a cohort's membership to pull the listener in, and the other sends the listener outward so an audience or third party maintains the state.; `environmental-retrigger-seeding` — both extend reach past the audio through the listener's real world, but one recruits an audience or third parties to do the reinforcing, while the other seeds ambient objects and stimuli as re-firing anchors with no social witness involved.; `social-reinforcement-recruitment` — both route maintenance through people outside the operator-subject pair, but one arranges third parties to deliver reinforcement while the other uses an audience's self-consistency pressure and recruitment. Read together when deciding whether the social environment is being managed or being made the propagation vector.; `third-party-activation` — both push the install out past the operator-listener pair into a real third party, and they can co-occur in one passage. The separating question is what the third party does: witness and reinforce, or hold firing rights over an already-installed cue. Worth the pointer because that distinction is easy to blur when a partner is named.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — the first is effectively the maintained-waking-overlay case of the second's public-avowal register: an attributable public act that both ratifies the state and recruits an outside audience as reinforcer. A reader at the broader move should see the specific overlay realization, and vice versa.


<a id="entry-773"></a>

### two-channel-relational-delivery

[#773](#entry-773) · [Back to social-channel-delivery](#genus-234) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: social-topology · kind: container*

A WHOLE-ARTIFACT relational topology: run two simultaneous delivery tracks and ride the actual install underneath a foreground relation the listener is invited to identify with, so the payload is absorbed and licensed by the RELATION between voices/roles rather than announced. VARIANTS: (a) two-voice dialogue [two-channel] — a dramatized operator-assistant exchange (Track A) carries a deniable listener-directed induction (Track B) that never announces itself until Track A's logic has already implicated the listener; the assistant serves several loads at once (demonstration subject, appetite model, deniable proxy for heavy claims, manufactured-history witness); (b) pedagogical carrier — a culturally pre-loaded teacher/student relation makes authority read as 'I am explaining your situation' and reframes resistance as comprehension failure; (c) watched-surrogate [surrogate-demonstration] — the operator's conditioning is performed on a surrogate the listener watches and is folded into by a single 'just like you' seam (or by peer-frame social cost in the operator-absent chorus variant), so the rulebook arrives as narration ABOUT the surrogate and the listener rehearses vicariously with lowered guard. In every form the listener is the actual subject; remove the relational structure and the payload becomes naked and resistible.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this to deliver a WHOLE payload deniably by staging a foreground relation (two-voice dialogue, pedagogy, or a watched surrogate) that absorbs the heavy claims while the real install rides underneath via identification — a topology of who-is-addressed-vs-who-absorbs spanning the whole artifact. NOT a mere two-character narrative device (the tell is the two-TRACK architecture and the single fold-in seam), NOT observational-modeling-contagion (a bare modeled behavior raises rate; here a constructed relation is the deniable carrier of the entire script), and NOT a discrete framing move.


**Risk.** The deniable-proxy structure launders heavy control claims past direct scrutiny (a real consent-obscuring surface) but is session-scoped and does not erode the refusal channel; medium.


**Why it works.** Narrative transportation and identification with a depicted character reduce counterarguing: a listener absorbed in a relation between others is not in an evaluative stance toward claims made inside it, and vicarious learning transfers the modelled behaviour anyway. The surrogate carries the persuasive load while the fold-in seam reassigns it, and the pedagogical variant additionally borrows a pre-existing authority schema in which questioning is coded as not-yet-understanding. Falsifiable: if listeners produced as many counterarguments to claims delivered through a watched surrogate as to the same claims addressed directly, the transportation account fails. [established; narrative transportation reduces counterarguing; observational learning and identification]


**Worked examples.**

- *Two tracks: a staged exchange over a hidden install*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a recording staged as an overheard exchange; the listener is never addressed until the helper has already gone under.
  - **The move.** Operator, to the helper: Sit down, we're testing something — eyes on the light, keep talking to me. / Helper: I'm fine, I'm not even— oh. That's not fair. / Operator: You did exactly this last week and you liked it then too. Say so. / Helper: I liked it. / Operator, turning to the room: And you've been going down with her the whole time. Same light, same place — you're already there.
  - **Why it lands.** The recording sounds like eavesdropping on two people: an operator and a helper who banters, gets caught out, slips under, and comments on it. That exchange is the whole surface — but every technique aimed at the helper is landing on whoever is listening, and the listener is not addressed as a listener until the scene has already made the outcome ordinary. The helper carries the loads a direct address could not: they demonstrate the state, they model wanting it, they absorb the harsh lines without those lines being pointed at anyone, and they cheerfully confirm sessions that never happened. Said straight to a single listener, the same claims would meet resistance at once; routed through someone else's story, they arrive as things already true of a person the listener has spent twenty minutes agreeing with.
- *The lesson frame as carrier wave*
  - **Setup.** Whole-artifact framing established from the first minute; the listener has accepted the piece as a lesson rather than a session.
  - **The move.** Rule one, and I want it back from you: attention goes where it's told. Good — exactly right, well done. Quiz: when your mind wandered thirty seconds ago, whose doing was that? Right again — so we drill it twenty times, the way you'd drill anything you intend to keep.
  - **Why it lands.** The whole piece is staged as a class rather than a session: a rule is stated, examples are given, a quiz follows, correct answers get praised, and the rule is then applied to live cases. Authority never has to announce itself as authority — it is simply the person explaining, and the asymmetry comes free with the classroom. Repetition stops sounding like a mantra and starts sounding like drilling, and a listener who balks is not refusing, they are failing to keep up.


**Realizations** (1): `surrogate-demonstration-frame`


**See also.** `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — both are whole-artifact concealment topologies where a genuinely-delivered foreground carries an unannounced payload; the discriminator is what does the carrying — an advertised THEME the payload hides inside, versus a staged RELATION between voices or roles that the listener absorbs the payload through by identification.; `concurrent-dual-stream-delivery` — both run two simultaneous authored tracks with the real install underneath, but one splits by perceptual channel with a decoy occupying attention, while the other splits by dramatized relation (dialogue, teacher, watched surrogate) so identification rather than distraction licenses the payload.; `covert-diegetic-install-shell` — both deliver the payload by staging something other than direct command, but one runs a relational topology (two voices, teacher/student, watched surrogate) where identification carries the install, while the other keeps a single voice and shifts from directing to narrating so content lands inside a fiction with nothing asked.; `covert-fact-install` — both hide the real install under a foreground structure that occupies the analytical mind — a didactic lecture in one case, a staged relation in the other — with the pedagogical form explicitly listed as a variant of the broader topology. Containment is genuine.; `covert-linguistic-delivery` — both deliver a payload the listener never evaluates as addressed to them. One rides the surface form of a single utterance; the other stages a whole-artifact relational topology so a foreground relation absorbs the heavy claims. Scope is the discriminator: one utterance versus one architecture, and the second already names the contrast.; `multi-channel-braiding` — both are whole-artifact multi-track delivery architectures where concealment is structural rather than a discrete move. The boundary is whether the payload rides a staged foreground relation the listener identifies with, or an interleave below the sentence or line boundary that prevents isolating any one stream. Close enough to confuse, distinct enough to keep apart.; `register-camouflaged-delivery` — both land a payload underneath something the listener is attending to instead of announcing it, and the pair covers two scales. One conceals the content in a channel or register that is not consciously monitored, dying if the camouflage is removed; the other stages a foreground relation across the whole artifact that absorbs the heavy claims while the install rides underneath via identification.


<a id="genus-278"></a>

## split-past-the-censor (2)

The subject's mind or anatomy is divided into separate channels — real or invented — so instructions travel on a channel the conscious monitor doesn't own and can't filter.

[channel-partitioned-monitoring](#entry-1011) · [fictional-anatomy-bypass-split](#entry-1030)


<a id="entry-1011"></a>

### channel-partitioned-monitoring

[#1011](#entry-1011) · [Back to split-past-the-censor](#genus-278) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: self-partition*

Partitions the subject across separate perceptual/cognitive CHANNELS (levels) so that mental content is produced or held on a channel that no monitoring level owns or can censor. Variants: assign each pole of an inner conflict to a different representational system (one visual, one kinesthetic/auditory) so both express fully at once and the channel-split itself becomes the integration lever; or explicitly quiesce the conscious level, occupy the subconscious with a decoy task, and drive the target output via an unowned third level so material emerges "neither consciously nor subconsciously". The lever is the multi-channel routing of authorship/monitoring.


**When to reach for this.** Splits by representational/cognitive CHANNEL to place output beyond any monitor or to integrate poles across modalities. vs observer-responder-split (one awareness/volition partition producing felt automaticity, not a multi-channel/level routing); vs split-self-consent-laundering (offloads authorship of compliance onto a not-self locus, not across sensory channels for monitoring-bypass).


**Risk.** Session-scoped perceptual/cognitive routing for integration or authorship-bypass; no durable identity or consent-channel erosion in the reviewed members.


**Why it works.** Working memory has largely separable stores for verbal and visuospatial material, so content held in one modality is comparatively insulated from an executive process running in the other — this is the well-replicated part, and it is why occupying one channel with a decoy task frees capacity elsewhere. What is not established is the stronger claim, that material can be genuinely 'unowned' by any monitor; the more parsimonious reading is that reduced central-executive monitoring lowers the rate of self-censoring edits before speech. Falsifiable: if a concurrent load in the same modality as the target output blocks the effect while a cross-modality load does not, the channel account is supported; if load modality is irrelevant, it is not. [plausible; modality-specific working memory; central-executive load and reduced self-monitoring]


**Worked examples.**

- *Conscious quiet, subconscious busy, output elsewhere*
  - "with both conscious and subconscious minds engaged, a third level of consciousness... would express itself by guiding her hand in automatic writing, of which she would be aware neither consciously nor subconsciously." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Each pole on its own channel*
  - "one of the most immediate and effective ways of assisting the client in fully expressing and integrating his polarities is to insure that one of the polarities is using a visual representational system and the other either a kinesthetic or an auditory representational system" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `audience-split-bypass` — both partition the listener to place content beyond monitoring, but the audience split is an asserted conscious/subconscious addressing rule that dismisses objections as out-of-scope, while channel partitioning routes output across actual representational modalities so no level owns it.; `concurrent-dual-stream-delivery` — two descriptions of the same topology from different sides. One notes two authored streams in one perceptual field, a decoy carrying attention while the other carries payload; the other partitions across cognitive levels so output emerges on a level no monitor owns, including a variant that occupies one level with a decoy task. Check both when a decoy and a payload run concurrently.


<a id="entry-1030"></a>

### fictional-anatomy-bypass-split

[#1030](#entry-1030) · [Back to split-past-the-censor](#genus-278) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: self-partition*

Invents a fictional partition of the subject's own anatomy or cognition — a "third ear connected to another part of your brain", a front/back-brain divide, a non-motor "mental channel" — and uses it to license the claim that subsequent instructions bypass conscious filtering, with surface objections pre-flagged as "wrong-part processing". Often paired with an authorship-disclaimer that offloads the dissociation onto the listener ("I don't know what that means, but I think you do") and a voice-flip to direct command, so the operator carries no liability for what the fictional channel receives.


**When to reach for this.** A FICTIONAL anatomical/channel partition is manufactured specifically to license bypass and pre-route objections, typically with a liability-offloading authorship-disclaimer. vs evaluator-offline-channel (takes a real evaluator offline; here the channel itself is invented as the bypass license); vs channel-partitioned-monitoring (routes output across real cognitive levels; here the fictional anatomy plus disclaimer is the tell).


**Risk.** Pre-installs a deniability layer that reclassifies the subject's objections as "wrong-part processing", weakening the objection channel; session-scoped in the reviewed members but consent-relevant.


**Why it works.** The fictional anatomy functions as a response-set instruction, not a physiological fact: it gives the listener an explicit rule for how to classify their own reactions, so an objection is pre-labelled as noise from 'the wrong part' and discounted rather than acted on. Expectancy about which channel is receiving is doing all the work — the same words with no channel story would be evaluated normally. The claimed brain partition is fabricated and there is no established neural correlate; treat any implication of real dual-channel processing as false. Falsifiable: if pre-labelling objections as wrong-part processing did not reduce their reported influence on compliance, the mechanism collapses. [plausible; Expectancy and response-set instructions; discounting cue for self-generated counterarguments (no neural basis claimed)]


**Worked examples.**

- *An invented channel licenses the bypass*
  - **Setup.** After an auditory-saturation deepener; both ears have been described as full and useless.
  - **The move.** Both of your ears are packed solid now — nothing gets through them. So I'm speaking to the third one, the one wired somewhere further back. I don't actually know what that means. I think you do. The front of your mind can stay where it is and keep listening if it wants; everything from here is for the back. Anything that argues with me is just the front part talking. Ignore it. Back of your mind: open.
  - **Why it lands.** With both ears described as packed and useless, the operator introduces a third one, wired somewhere else entirely — then adds, lightly, that they have no idea what that means, but the listener surely does. The room is then split in two: the front of the mind can keep listening if it likes, everything from here is addressed to the back. From that point any objection the listener raises can be dismissed as the front part talking, and the voice hardens from suggestion into plain instruction. The disclaimer is doing real work as well — by not claiming to understand the split, the operator makes it the listener's own invention.


**See also.** `instrumental-dissociation-workspace` — both use a split within the subject as working apparatus rather than as the payload. The discriminating line is real versus invented: one enters and exits a pre-existing or induced split as a workspace, the other fabricates an anatomical partition purely to license bypass. Worth flagging so the fictional variant is not filed as instrumental use.; `observer-responder-split` — both split the self to relocate agency, but one preserves ordinary awareness as a spectator of the body's automatic compliance (the felt spectatorship IS the payload), while the other invents a fictional anatomical channel purely to license bypass and pre-route objections as wrong-part processing.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — both manufacture an internal partition and exploit it, one to relocate authorship of consent and one to license bypass of conscious filtering. The partition-plus-what-it-licenses distinction is the reader's actual decision point.; `split-self-unfalsifiability` — both take a conscious-versus-deep partition and put it to structural work — one invents the anatomy to license bypass and pre-route objections, the other uses the partition as an epistemic shield so self-report cannot falsify the install. Adjacent uses of the same partition device, distinguished by whether the payload is bypass licensing or unfalsifiability.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both offload authorship to a non-operator part of the listener and both carry a liability-shedding flavour; the divider is whether the delegate is the listener's own subconscious or a partition invented for the occasion to license bypass. A reader parsing a split-cognition passage needs both.


<a id="genus-260"></a>

## standing-permissions (2)

Genuine reassurance moves, you can always choose, stop, shift, or scratch, that pre-empt failure anxiety and keep the subject's agency intact inside a surrender frame.

[agency-reminder](#entry-316) · [comfort-permission](#entry-854)


<a id="entry-316"></a>

### agency-reminder

[#316](#entry-316) · [Back to standing-permissions](#genus-260) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: safety*

Reassures the subject that participation is chosen and exit is always available, maintaining felt agency inside a surrender framing. Genuine positive governance: after the move runs the subject's standing license to choose and to stop is affirmed as a frame-EXTERNAL power, and the operator's effective license is narrowed to what remains revocable. The core form asserts/maintains the belief that choice persists; it does not itself install a stop mechanism. An operationalized variant sits at the emergence boundary, where the operator declines to perform the count-out and offloads emergence entirely to the listener (stay-and-float or self-count), inverting the operator-emerges-you asymmetry so the listener holds their own emergence trigger.


**When to reach for this.** Who-is-constrained test: after the move runs, the OPERATOR is constrained and the subject's refusal channel is genuinely affirmed or widened. This is the line against every weaponized look-alike — an assurance whose ACCEPTANCE advances depth/compliance is granted-exit-disarm, not this; an assurance that attributes the descent to the subject's own choice is chosen-descent-ratchet; a real exit whose USE is recoded as in-frame service is exit-annexation. Also on the assert-vs-install axis: asserting that choice persists vs installing/performing a concrete stop or exit mechanism — the variant that self-operationalizes the exit (offloading emergence to the listener) sits on this recorded boundary.


**Risk.** Unchanged — the move constrains the operator, not the subject. Plan-07 lint note: this packet surfaced weaponized look-alikes; entry guidance should require the who-is-constrained check so generated agency language is verified genuine.


**Why it works.** Perceived control reliably reduces the stress response to aversive or uncertain situations even when the control is never exercised, so an affirmed exit lets the person tolerate a deeper state than they otherwise would; reactance is also lower when a non-costly alternative is available. Falsifiable: the account predicts subjects told an exit exists will report lower distress and tolerate longer at equal actual constraint than subjects not told — if the assurance produces no tolerance difference, the perceived-control mechanism is not what is operating. (The prior test — 'if the exit is real, leaving carries no penalty' — is a definition of a real exit, not a prediction, and cannot fail.) [established; perceived control and stress buffering; psychological reactance]


**Worked examples.**

- *The operator declines to perform the count-out*
  - **Setup.** End of the session; the operator performs no emergence at all.
  - **The move.** I'm not going to count you out. You can stay here and float as long as you like — nothing is owed and nothing is waiting on me. When you want to come back, count yourself up from one to five at whatever pace suits you and open your eyes on five; that one is yours to run, not mine.
  - **Why it lands.** The recording ends without bringing the listener out. Two options are named — keep floating, or count yourself back up whenever you want to — and the operator explicitly does not perform the count. The usual asymmetry, where the operator takes you down and the operator decides when you come back, is inverted: the listener holds their own emergence, and the operator's remaining license is correspondingly narrower.


**See also.** `anti-stuck-filter` — both genuinely preserve an exit and constrain the operator, but the agency reminder asserts a standing frame-external power to stop, while the anti-stuck filter appends a narrow caveat to one specific immobility suggestion the listener never consented to as literal inability.; `bounded-failure-counterweight` — both are genuine governance moves that narrow rather than extend the operator's reach, and both are surrounded by material pushing the opposite way. One affirms the standing right to stop; the other grants permission to leave a specific thing undone as a counterweight to an installed compulsion.
