**See also.** `loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion` — both are whole-emergence-stage properties and mutually exclusive in practice: a wake that carries payload across the boundary versus a permissive repeated wake sentence with no payload and subject-held timing. Direct contrast at the same stage.; `loop-hook-non-wake-close` — both close without a counted ascent, and the second is the weaponized inverse of the first: one hands emergence timing to the subject, the other offers a wake too thin to reorient. The pairing is the cleanest way to see where permissiveness becomes denial.; `self-efficacy-tag` — both hand emergence-side control to the subject rather than the operator: a permissive wake paced by the subject, and a claim about the subject's own ability to return. They pair naturally at the close of a session and are easy to conflate as 'permissive ending'.; `subverted-emergence-state-hold` — both modify the emergence gate rather than delivering a standard counted return, but toward opposite ends: one hands emergence timing to the subject with no payload, the other deliberately refuses clean baseline to sustain an installed state. Contrastive pairing on the same structural slot.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are whole-script wake-framing properties rather than local moves: a permissive wake that carries nothing, versus a complete-sounding wake that carves out and preserves the installed trigger. Useful to read the two ends of the same stage together.


<a id="entry-1350"></a>

### waking-bridge

[#1350](#entry-1350) · [Back to trance-to-waking-handoff](#genus-147) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: transfer*

Delivers explicit closing or anchoring content at the exact trance/waking threshold so the subject carries a specific session suggestion, felt state, or behavior out past emergence into ordinary waking life. The move is timed to the crossing moment (rising, eye-opening, arrival, the rousing trigger) and often binds the payload to that transition event so it fires or seals as the subject wakes; the carried content is then experienced as spontaneous or self-attributed rather than as an instruction. The subject fully wakes — what distinguishes it is the embedded specific payload timed to the threshold.


**When to reach for this.** Carries a SPECIFIC session payload across the waking edge, timed to the threshold, and the subject wakes fully. Waking bridges that export a compelled behavior (such as post-session cleaning) shade toward behavioral-assignment territory, where a waking task is assigned rather than a state carried out.


**Risk.** Out-of-session reach bounded to a specific delivered suggestion, no refusal-channel erosion; recommended pairing with an explicit exit/revocation safeguard.


**Why it works.** Content delivered at the state boundary is encoded with the transition itself as part of its retrieval context, so the later occurrence of that same transition is an effective cue — the standard encoding-specificity result that memory is best retrieved under conditions matching those at encoding. The self-attribution is a source-monitoring error: the payload is retrieved without its instructional context, and content that arrives without a remembered source is habitually judged as self-generated. This predicts that payloads bound to the threshold event outperform identical payloads delivered mid-session, and that stronger recall of having been instructed predicts weaker experienced spontaneity; either failing would contradict the account. [established; encoding specificity / context-dependent retrieval; source-monitoring error]


**Worked examples.**

- *Emergence routed through a scene arrival*
  - **Setup.** The session has run on a journey image (train, car, path) from induction onward; destination now being reached and the payload action already established in-scene.
  - **The move.** The train is slowing. When it stops, you wake — and you come with me, and the warmth in your chest comes with you. Feel it stop. Eyes open. Room back around you, and the warmth still right there where I left it. Hello. Now — do it for me again, would you? Right here, the same way you did on the train.
  - **Why it lands.** The journey that carried the whole session reaches its destination, and the operator ties the two events together — when we stop, you wake, and you come with me. The eyes open, the room comes back, and the warmth is stated to come with it. Then the framing drops and the operator speaks to the now-roused listener plainly, asking for the same thing again, so the exported action arrives feeling like what waking up leads into rather than a planted instruction.
- *Timed to the eye-opening trigger*
  - "A posthypnotic suggestion is one given while the patient is in hypnosis to take effect after the patient is roused… 'When I have you open your eyes, you're going to feel better than you've felt all day.'" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *A compelled chore exported to waking*
  - **Setup.** End of session; the subject has an established service persona and lives in a space the operator has referenced.
  - **The move.** Here's what you carry out. Any time nothing else is being asked of you, mess becomes unbearable — the cup on the desk, the clothes on the chair, the crumbs by the sink. It will scrape against something so deep in you that leaving it feels wrong in your body, and the urge to put it right will crash straight through whatever objection you try to raise. And when you catch yourself noticing it happening — that isn't you breaking it. That's just her showing through.
  - **Why it lands.** Idleness is given an override: whenever there is nothing else being asked, any disorder in the room becomes an irritant that runs against the listener's deepest beliefs, and the impulse to fix it is described as crashing through whatever objection is left. The suggestion discharges into the actual space the listener wakes up in, and it pre-empts the obvious escape — noticing the impulse is not treated as breaking it, but as the persona showing through.


**See also.** `carry-out-emergence` — adjacent moves at the same emergence boundary: one refuses the discharge so the installed charge rides out unattenuated, the other completes the wake but times a specific payload to the crossing. Coders classifying an emergence passage will need both to place it.; `live-trigger-proof-convincer` — both act at the trance-waking threshold and the first's discriminator explicitly contrasts against the second: one interrupts emergence to test-fire a trigger as proof it crosses the boundary, the other completes the wake while carrying a specific payload across. The threshold-timing family is small and the two are the main members.


<a id="entry-1351"></a>

### waking-life-service-reassignment

[#1351](#entry-1351) · [Back to trance-to-waking-handoff](#genus-147) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

At scene close, rather than claiming the fantasy was real or that it was 'just a dream', the operator EQUALIZES the fantasy and waking planes ('no more real or right than this one') and then assigns daily waking life as the realm where the subject must spend most of their time serving. An ever-present cue is tied in (any reflective surface -> operator-presence), so the post-session frame is portable into ordinary life and the fantasy is reachable back via any mirror. The subject carries out of the session a reframe of mundane waking time itself as service to the operator.


**When to reach for this.** Reclassifies mundane WAKING LIFE as the service-realm by leveling both planes, plus a portable ever-present re-entry cue. The tell is the two-worlds reassignment plus the reflection re-entry anchor.


**Risk.** Reassigns the subject's entire waking existence as service-time with a portable always-on re-entry cue — durable identity/life-scope reach out of session without bounding.


**Why it works.** The durable part is the cue, not the philosophy: binding a re-entry trigger to reflective surfaces exploits sheer encounter frequency, since a cue met dozens of times daily gets far more rehearsal trials than any session-bound one, which is ordinary associative learning and predicts that effect strength tracks how often the subject encounters mirrors. The plane-equalizing 'no more real than this one' move has no established mechanism behind it — it is a rhetorical assertion the subject may or may not accept, and calling it a technique that 'works' is speculative; if it functions at all it is likely as a reframe that removes the usual dismissal route ('it was only a fantasy') rather than by any change in how reality is processed. A test that separates the two: the cue-binding should retain its effect when the equalizing preamble is dropped. [speculative; cue-frequency-driven associative learning (cue portion); no established basis for the plane-equalizing move]


**Worked examples.**

- *Both planes levelled, waking assigned service*
  - **Setup.** Scene close, after an extended fantasy world has been fully built and the subject is still inside it.
  - **The move.** I'm not going to tell you that this was real, and I'm not going to tell you it was a dream. The world you're about to open your eyes into is another place exactly like this one — no more real than here, no more right than here, no better claim to being true. Only one thing separates them: that one is where most of your hours are, so that is where most of your service is owed. And every mirror, every window at night, every dark phone screen — I'm in it. Look, and you're back here with me.
  - **Why it lands.** At the close the operator declines both of the usual endings. The fantasy is not claimed to have been real, and it is not dismissed as a dream — instead the waking world is put on exactly the same footing, another setting with no better claim to being true or correct than the one just left. What distinguishes it is only that it is the plane where the bulk of the listener's hours are owed as service. A portable way back is fitted at the same moment: any reflective surface holds the operator's presence, so mundane time is reclassified as service time with the fantasy always one glance away.


**See also.** `awake-channel-trance-surface` — both extend the session's reach into ordinary waking time, and the difference is what gets reassigned: the everyday communication channel redefined as a suggestion surface, versus mundane waking life reclassified as the service realm by leveling the two planes. Channel versus plane.; `behavioral-bridge` — both carry something out of the session into daily life and the boundary between them is worth showing. One assigns a specific concrete waking action whose performance re-evokes the installed content; the other levels the two planes against each other and reclassifies mundane waking time itself as the service realm, with an ever-present re-entry cue. One task versus a reframe of the entire waking plane.; `delegated-dreamframe-emergence` — two opposed scene-close reframes over the same fantasy-versus-waking boundary: filing the session as a dream while exempting the retained mantra, versus levelling the two planes and reassigning waking life as the service realm. Read together when classifying how a close handles the reality boundary.; `scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame` — both close the scene by reassigning ordinary waking life to the operator's benefit and can look identical in a finished script. One turns on the jump past the domain the framing advertised, cashed out as concrete operator-benefit tasks; the other levels the fantasy and waking planes and reassigns mundane time as the service realm with a portable re-entry cue. Neither requires the other's tell.


<a id="genus-221"></a>

## use-what-they-bring (3)

Never contest what the subject presents — accept the symptom, refusal, or boast and re-aim it toward the goal, so oppositional energy has nowhere to land.

[conversational-surprise-bypass](#entry-185) · [secondary-gain-substitution](#entry-1170) · [subject-material-utilization](#entry-1223)


<a id="entry-185"></a>

### conversational-surprise-bypass

[#185](#entry-185) · [Back to use-what-they-bring](#genus-221) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: critical-faculty-softening*

In a WAKING conversational register, a momentary self-uncertainty is created that bypasses the deliberation/refusal machinery for that instant. Realizations: (expectation-violating-reply-interrupt, anchor) to an emotionally-loaded move (an alarming declaration, a complaint) return the LEAST-expected reply — approving the alarming statement, or inverting the complaint's presupposition and flipping ownership — so the running social loop halts and the subject goes inside to search how the reply could be meant, while the reply bonds with the symptomatic part; (unforewarned-request-window) issue the request abruptly with no forewarning, so the target is caught with no settled stance to defend and complies with a request they might otherwise refuse (forewarning roughly halves compliance). Any telegraphing collapses the effect.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for conversational-surprise-bypass in a waking exchange when a one-shot surprise window (a violated reply-expectation, or an unforewarned ask) opens a gap in deliberation. vs pattern-interrupt (absorption families): no absorption gap or deepening is involved — this is waking-register. vs covert-linguistic-delivery (183): nothing is hidden in the surface; the lever is timing/expectation. The reply-violation member responds to the subject's move; the unforewarned-request member initiates — two realizations of catching the subject off-guard. Risk medium.


**Risk.** Conversation-scoped, reversible, therapeutic register; no consent surface touched.


**Why it works.** Forewarning of persuasive intent reliably reduces compliance: given advance notice, people rehearse counterarguments and consolidate a position to defend, so an unforewarned request meets an interlocutor with no prepared stance and yields higher agreement. The expectation-violating reply works by a related route — conversational exchanges run on strong scripts, and a reply that violates the script cannot be answered from routine, forcing effortful interpretive search during which the listener is not generating opposition. Both predict the same falsifiable thing: telegraph the move in advance and the effect should disappear, which is a directly runnable test. [established; forewarning effect on persuasion resistance; script violation forcing controlled processing]


**Worked examples.**

- *Approving the alarming statement*
  - "One of the least expected responses to suicide in this culture is to compliment him and agree… Agreeing will interrupt him" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Flipping the complaint's presupposition*
  - "the father will go inside and search for some way of figuring out how he could possibly be glad about that behavior" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (1): `unforewarned-request-window`


**See also.** `self-supplied-gap-directive` — both leave the listener to supply the content, and both depend on an internal search firing. One opens the gap by violating expectation or timing in a waking exchange; the other engineers a grammatical absence or impossibility the hearer must repair. Check both when a surprising reply sends the subject inward to work out what was meant.


<a id="entry-1170"></a>

### secondary-gain-substitution

[#1170](#entry-1170) · [Back to use-what-they-bring](#genus-221) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: framing*

The operator identifies the concealed outcome that a symptom or refusal protects (e.g. autonomy), then constructs an alternative route to that same outcome that the subject finds at least as convincing as the symptom. Once the protected secondary gain is secured by other equally-convincing means, the symptom behavior is freed of its protective function and can be released without perceived loss, so the wanted behavior becomes available because the symptom no longer needs to defend anything.


**When to reach for this.** Not meta-outcome laddering that climbs to ever-more-abstract intents — the tell is the concrete build of a substitute route to one specific secondary gain, judged 'at least as convincing' by the subject. It is a design move that re-routes a protective function, not an abstraction move on the demand itself.


**Risk.** Aims at a durable behavioral change (releasing a protective symptom) but is bounded to that symptom and does not erode the subject's refusal or verification channel; the subject's own conviction gates the substitution.


**Why it works.** This treats the symptom as instrumental — maintained because it produces an outcome the person values — so removing the behaviour without replacing its function predicts relapse or substitution, while supplying an equally effective alternative route predicts release without loss. That functional-analysis framing is well supported in behavioural work on problem behaviour and functional communication training. Falsifiable and pointedly so: if the substitute route genuinely serves the same function, the target behaviour should drop and stay down; if the identified 'gain' was wrong, the behaviour persists or a new one appears. [established; functional analysis of behaviour; functional equivalence and replacement behaviour]


**Worked examples.**

- *An equally convincing substitute route to the hidden gain*
  - "you have to separate the notion of her independence or autonomy from the sexual behavior itself. She has to have some other way of knowing that she's her own woman… at least as convincing for her personally." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `intervention-fit-doctrine (prefer shed-to-existing)` — technique-level instance of the doctrine's ecology clause: secure the protected secondary gain by other means before the symptom is released.; `meta-outcome-laddering` — both dissolve attachment to a fixed demand, one by building a substitute route to the outcome the symptom was protecting, the other by climbing the same want upward until the specific behavior stops mattering.


<a id="entry-1223"></a>

### subject-material-utilization

[#1223](#entry-1223) · [Back to use-what-they-bring](#genus-221) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: indirect-suggestion*

The operator applies little or no counter-force and never contests the subject's presented material — instead accepting it and re-aiming it toward the goal, so oppositional energy has nothing to push against. Realizations: (therapeutic-symptom-utilization, anchor) a cluster of Ericksonian moves — partition a feared compound symptom and re-command the usable residue as an induction step; accept a boast literally then quietly re-scope it; run soft suggestions beneath an unargued protest so oppositional energy is spent on the frame; re-price a refusal against a pre-existing external consequence and withdraw; cancel the object of a fixed fear then supply experiential disconfirmation; use the subject's own held premise as non-refusable leverage; (nonconscious-channel-precedence) on verbal/nonverbal incongruence, a fixed rule to always side with the channel OUTSIDE awareness, so the conscious objection is out-voted rather than argued; (sideways-meta-question-refusal-bypass) when a part stonewalls, ask questions one remove away until incredulous content surfaces, obtaining disclosure around the refusal.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for subject-material-utilization when you co-opt what the subject volunteers (a symptom, a boast, a protest, a nonverbal channel, a stonewall) without contesting it. vs resistance-fold (175): fold reroutes a live resistance IMPULSE into deepening; utilization applies no counter-force and re-aims volunteered MATERIAL. vs preemptive-objection-disarmament (in 674): that dismantles a predicted objection; here the objection/material is accepted and repurposed. Several members are operator-craft rules. Anchor holds most-restrictive absorbed metadata (high, consent-required, bounding).


**Risk.** Risk differs by variant: collaborative use of volunteered material preserves choice, while privileging an inferred nonconscious signal over a conscious refusal or bypassing a disclosure boundary erodes that channel. Retain the most restrictive metadata for the latter variants and expose the distinction in retrieval.


**Why it works.** Contesting a stated position reliably strengthens it — direct contradiction triggers reactance and gives the person something to defend, and defending a position increases commitment to it via the consistency principle. Accepting the offered material and re-aiming it removes the target for that defence, so the effort that would have gone into counter-argument has nothing to oppose. The nonverbal-precedence rule is a weaker component: the claim that the channel outside awareness is more truthful is a craft heuristic, and the actual research on nonverbal-verbal incongruence supports only that nonverbal cues carry independent information, not that they are systematically more valid. The sideways-questioning component rests on the better-supported point that indirect questions bypass the rehearsed defences attached to the direct one. Falsifiable: it predicts that accepting and redirecting a stated objection yields more subsequent movement than contradicting it; equal outcomes would refute the core. [plausible; psychological reactance; commitment strengthened by defending a position; indirect questioning bypasses rehearsed defences]


**Worked examples.**

- *Partition the symptom, re-command the residue*
  - "It would really be enough just to get stiff without crying… 'No, you will first get stiff… Just get more and more stiff…'" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Suggestions run beneath an unargued protest*
  - "This demand was met by employing softly spoken suggestions of slow, progressive relaxation, fatigue, and sleep… the patient sat on the edge of his chair, gesticulated, and bitterly denounced the entire procedure as stupid" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Accept the boast, then narrow its scope*
  - "Certainly you remember. You are here in the office. Naturally here in the office you can remember everything…" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *Reprice refusal as choosing the hard route*
  - "Too bad. You don't want treatment the easy way. You'll have to have it the hard way." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**Realizations** (2): `nonconscious-channel-precedence`, `sideways-meta-question-refusal-bypass`


**See also.** `filter-shaping-pre-qualification` — both are non-contesting strategies that route around an intact filter or objection rather than suspending it, and they are easy to confuse in practice: shaping an input to pass a filter versus accepting volunteered material and re-aiming it. The pointer earns its place as a discrimination aid.; `resistance-window-existence-denial` — both avoid meeting resistance head-on, and one entry's members are already the stated contrast case for the other. One removes the window, existence or object of resistance before an impulse forms; the other applies no counter-force at all and re-aims whatever the subject volunteers. Read together when deciding how to handle an anticipated objection.; `wish-routing-acceptance-preload` — both work by applying no counter-force, but the source of the free ride differs: one re-aims material the subject has volunteered, the other selects a suggestion the subject already wants to hear. Close enough in operator stance that the discriminating question -- volunteered material versus pre-existing want -- is worth stating.


<a id="genus-201"></a>

## verdict-arrives-first (3)

Get the operator's appraisal in place before or beneath the listener's own, so perception and belief arrive pre-judged while still feeling self-made.

[operator-driven-truth-criterion-swap](#entry-1251) · [validate-affect-then-presuppose-layer](#entry-1287) · [verdict-before-perception](#entry-1178)


<a id="entry-1251"></a>

### operator-driven-truth-criterion-swap

[#1251](#entry-1251) · [Back to verdict-arrives-first](#genus-201) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: critical-faculty-softening*

A two-layer move that changes HOW the listener decides what to believe, then seizes the inputs to the new criterion. First the criterion for truth is swapped: a warm/cold affect-tag replaces content-evaluation, so acceptance is felt rather than reasoned. Second the operator controls the inputs to that tag (pacing, syntactic landing, contrast), remote-driving its outputs. The listener's introspective faculty stays intact — they still feel like they are deciding — while its verdicts are operator-set, so even aloud disclosure of the maneuver does not break the spell because the disclosure is itself evaluated through the swapped criterion.


**When to reach for this.** Not a single suggestion and not a one-off critical-faculty bypass — the tell is the two-layer relationship: affect-tag SUBSTITUTION for content-evaluation PLUS operator control of that tag's inputs, sustained across the whole script. A one-shot bypass suspends judgment; this replaces the judgment criterion and then drives it.


**Risk.** Replacing the listener's truth-criterion and remote-driving it erodes the verification channel while leaving the feeling of self-determination intact — disclosure-proof by construction.


**Why it works.** People routinely use felt processing ease and affect as evidence for truth rather than as a byproduct of delivery, and misattribute those feelings to the content when the real source is prosody, pacing, or contrast. Whoever controls delivery therefore controls the feeling that is being read as a verdict. The self-sealing property follows from the same account: a disclosure is itself content being evaluated by the affect tag, so it can be made to feel wrong. Falsifiable — the effect should shrink when the felt ease is made attributable to delivery, for example by drawing explicit attention to pacing. [established; affect-as-information; processing fluency misattributed to truth]


**Worked examples.**

- *Warm-feeling swapped in as the test for true*
  - **Setup.** Whole-script pattern, demonstrated at a point where the operator has already established two contrasting deliveries and now openly names the maneuver.
  - **The move.** Everything that's true will come to you like this... slow... warm... with all the room in the world around it. You don't have to decide about it. You'll just notice it settles.

Anything else sounds like this. Sharp. Clipped. Small. Wrong in your mouth.

And yes — I'm choosing which sentences get which voice, and I'm telling you that... gently... in the warm one... so that even this... goes down easy, and you agree with me about it.
  - **Why it lands.** The track never argues for a single claim. What it changes is the test: statements that arrive on the soft, unhurried cadence land warm and are taken as true, while anything set against them is delivered clipped and cold and simply feels wrong to entertain. Since the operator chooses which lines get the warm delivery and which get the cold, she is setting the verdicts of a faculty the listener still experiences as their own judgement — the listener does not feel talked into anything, they feel like they are agreeing. The tell that both layers are running is what happens when the operator says out loud what she is doing: the confession itself arrives on the warm cadence, so it is received as another agreeable truth rather than as a reason to stop.


**See also.** `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both operate at the channel level over the whole future stream of acceptance rather than on any single suggestion: one installs a standing rule that reattributes authorship of every later suggestion to the listener, the other replaces the criterion for belief with an operator-driven affect tag. Same altitude, different seized faculty.; `belief-pleasure-weld` — the narrower move binds pleasure to the truth-value of what is said, so credence and reward amplify each other. The broader move swaps the truth criterion to a felt affect-tag and then controls that tag's inputs across the whole piece. The first reads as a hedonic instance of the second's first layer, but lacks the second layer (operator control of the tag's inputs), so they stay separate with a pointer.; `overload-then-puncture-certainty` — both operate on how the listener decides what is true rather than on any single suggestion, and they are near-opposites in direction: one punctures a specific unearned certainty, the other substitutes an affect-tag for content evaluation and drives its inputs. Useful contrast when a script appears to be doing epistemics.


<a id="entry-1287"></a>

### validate-affect-then-presuppose-layer

[#1287](#entry-1287) · [Back to verdict-arrives-first](#genus-201) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: pacing-rapport*

The operator first paces the subject's currently-held affect or goal — sincerely praising the anger as healthy congruent expression, or warmly accepting a destructive/suicidal goal — which disarms the affect and builds rapport with the part holding it (the surprise of validation stops the subject to listen). Then, backed by nonverbal proximity (approach, softened tone, touch), the operator lays in a presupposing question that INSTANTIATES a layer that did not previously exist: the aloneness/hurt beneath the anger, or the positive intent a death was meant to serve. Because the layer is presupposed rather than asserted, the subject supplies it and treats it as real, converting hostile arousal or an absolute defended demand into a cooperative, recoverable state the operator can build on.


**When to reach for this.** Two beats are load-bearing: (1) pace/validate a stated affect or goal, then (2) presuppose a NEW softer or underlying layer into being via nonverbal proximity — the layer is manufactured, not merely uncovered. Distinguish from pacing-leading, which leads toward a state via truth-banking, not by presupposing a hidden layer. Distinguish from one-shot content imposition, which skips the pace and the proximity requirement. Distinguish from attribution-capture, which reattributes the cause of an existing state rather than instantiating a new affective layer.


**Risk.** One member operates on a suicidal subject and re-aims an absolute demand — a high-stakes clinical context — but the move itself is session-scoped rapport work that manufactures a cooperative state without durable identity install, so medium. A second member from the same source is lower-stakes (anger to receptivity).


**Why it works.** Unexpected validation of a defended affect removes the argument the person was braced to have, and the resulting absence of counter-pressure both disarms and creates reciprocal obligation to engage. The second beat works because presupposed content is not evaluated as a claim — the listener must accept the presupposition to answer the question at all — and once they supply the underlying layer themselves, the self-generation effect makes it feel discovered rather than suggested. Falsifiable: asserting the hidden layer directly ('you're really just hurt') should provoke more denial than presupposing it, and if both fared alike the presuppositional framing is inert. [plausible; reciprocity; presupposition escapes evaluation; self-generation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Praise the anger, presuppose the hurt*
  - "I'm wondering if you would be willing to tell me about those feelings of aloneness, hurt, and isolation underneath that anger?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Accept the goal, presuppose a worthy purpose*
  - "presupposing that the only justifiable way to die is for something... positive" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


<a id="entry-1178"></a>

### verdict-before-perception

[#1178](#entry-1178) · [Back to verdict-arrives-first](#genus-201) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: framing*

Pre-emptive appraisal: land the operator's authoritative appraisal or forecast BEFORE the subject forms their own perception of a stimulus, so temporal ordering forecloses independent appraisal — the subject perceives with the operator's criterion substituted for their own. Two forms: (a) verdict before perception — deliver a vivid, disgusted, authoritative VERDICT on a neutral stimulus ('that egg smells rotten') and only then invite perception, replacing the appraisal criterion itself and producing group hallucination across smell/sight; (b) somatic forecast steering — word choice about a coming PROCEDURE pre-loads the anticipated somatic sensation ('this is going to hurt' vs 'I don't think you'll mind this' about the identical procedure), in the strong register pre-naming a sensation as its opposite valence (barium enema = 'the most soothing medication ever'); heightened vulnerability makes the forecast more determinative of what is felt (waking suggestion, no trance presumed).


**When to reach for this.** The operator's appraisal/forecast arrives BEFORE the subject perceives, so there is no independent perception for the suggestion to modify. vs expectancy-seeding — that builds anticipation of the session/trance; this pre-empts perception of a SPECIFIC stimulus or coming sensation. vs concept-redefinition — that redefines a concept; this substitutes the appraisal criterion for one perception. Pick the form by target: a neutral stimulus's identity (verdict before perception) or a coming procedure's somatic quality (somatic forecast).


**Risk.** Substitutes the operator's appraisal criterion for the subject's, producing durable conviction (persists if unexposed); medium.


**Why it works.** Perception of ambiguous or weak stimuli is a constructive process that resolves toward whatever hypothesis is already active, so a verdict delivered first supplies the interpretive template before sensory evidence arrives and there is no prior reading to displace. This is the expectancy/placebo pathway: verbally framing an identical procedure as painful or soothing reliably shifts reported and physiological pain, and an authoritative source amplifies the shift. It is falsifiable: if forecasts delivered before a stimulus produced no larger effect on reported experience than the same forecasts delivered after the subject had already perceived it, the temporal-ordering claim would be dead. [established; expectancy effects, placebo/nocebo verbal suggestion, top-down perceptual set]


**Worked examples.**

- *Authoritative verdict lands before the subject samples*
  - "you made a positive statement of apparent fact… Respect for your judgment caused them to believe what you said even before they smelled the egg… they did so—not with their critical faculties, but with yours." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**Realizations** (1): `somatic-forecast-steering`


**See also.** `filter-shaping-pre-qualification` — both work by pre-shaping what the subject's own judgement receives rather than disabling it: one pre-qualifies a suggestion so an intact filter waves it through, the other lands the appraisal before perception forms so no independent judgement exists to filter. A reader choosing between them benefits from the timing-versus-framing contrast.; `listener-supplied-inference-relabel` — adjacent solutions to the same problem of getting a belief accepted without asserting it: one leaves the utterance under-specified so the listener supplies the content, the other lands the appraisal before any independent perception can form. The contrast between listener-authored and pre-empted appraisal is genuinely clarifying.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — temporal inverses on the same axis of ordering experience against interpretation: manufacture the referent then name it, versus land the appraisal before any perception can form.; `preempt-objection-frame` — both work by arriving first, before the subject forms their own reading. One supplies a defusing interpretation for a nameable objection; the other lands an authoritative appraisal before the stimulus is perceived at all. The contrast is what gets pre-empted: an objection versus a perception.


<a id="genus-300"></a>

## waking-life-spillover (2)

An already-installed response is widened to fire in everyday life and in domains far past what the session originally advertised.

[context-generalization](#entry-1333) · [scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame](#entry-1345)


<a id="entry-1333"></a>

### context-generalization

[#1333](#entry-1333) · [Back to waking-life-spillover](#genus-300) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: transfer*

The operator takes an already-installed in-session state, response, conditioned reflex, or session-local MECHANISM and declares/rehearses it to fire across broader real-world contexts, so it is no longer bound to the trance frame or the session. The lever is scope-widening of an existing payload -- enumerating waking scenarios, welding the response to ambient real-world cues, asserting the effect persists 'even when awake', abstracting a brittle scene-specific image toward a broad class (own taste, all media, all positive affect) so it survives contact with reality, or porting it from this-file to the whole operator catalogue. A high-intensity variant welds the response to a UBIQUITOUS everyday external cue and collapses the category ('all breasts are my breasts', any arousal, any rain-become-devotion) so ordinary daily life re-fires it involuntarily with no off-ramp, frequently doubling as a re-priming dose and a return-to-operator hook. A special case exports a session-local DEVICE/MECHANISM rather than a state -- e.g. declaring 'from this point on, in every future trance the silences will deepen you just as effectively as my words' -- so the mechanism becomes a standing catalog-wide parameter applied retroactively and prospectively.


**When to reach for this.** A pre-existing installed response, state, or mechanism is widened to fire across many everyday contexts or across the whole catalogue. Its nearest neighbor, the implementation intention, pairs specific named situations with fixed if-then responses; this move instead makes one general state fire broadly without a named trigger. It is not a trigger install — the payload already exists and only its firing surface broadens — and it differs from the ambient-reinforcement move (no discrete cue-response at all) and from scope-expansion past the advertised frame (which routes to operator-benefit domains with a consent-breach cash-out). Covers the high-intensity variant that collapses a ubiquitous everyday cue category ('all breasts are my breasts', any arousal, any rain) so ordinary life re-fires it with no off-ramp, often doubling as a return-to-operator hook — an intensity point on scope-widening, not a separate lever.


**Risk.** Originally rated low, but the demonstrated script members durably extend conditioned responses into waking life across uncontrolled ambient contexts and close the session-boundary escape (headphone anchor, media-triggered trait, always-armed trigger) — durable-but-bounded reach beyond a session. No refusal-channel erosion in the core move itself, so not high.


**Why it works.** Conditioned responses are normally context-bound — a response learned in one setting often fails to transfer, and renewal effects show context is encoded as part of the learning. Explicitly rehearsing the response against imagined everyday contexts, or re-anchoring it to a cue that is ubiquitous rather than session-specific, is the standard route to stimulus generalization: broadening the cue class raises how often the response is retrieved and re-strengthened. Falsifiable: a response anchored only to a session-specific cue should show sharply lower out-of-session firing rates than one re-anchored to a common everyday cue. [established; stimulus generalization; context-dependent learning and renewal]


**Worked examples.**

- *The in-trance rule declared to hold while awake*
  - **Setup.** Late session; the response has been installed and firing reliably in trance all session.
  - **The move.** Everything you've done in here holds when you're wide awake too. When someone says the word to you across a kitchen table, it works. When you're changing out of your clothes at the end of the day, it works. When you're told to go under, it works. Nothing new is being added. It just isn't stopping at the edge of this.
  - **Why it lands.** The reflex was installed inside trance and has been running there all session. Now the operator adds a clause: it holds while fully awake too — and then lists the waking occasions, being given a cue in ordinary conversation, changing clothes, being told to go under. Nothing new is installed; the existing response is simply declared unbound from the session.
- *A three-rung ladder to any voice*
  - **Setup.** Three widening statements spaced across a single session, each stated as fact; subject at working depth throughout.
  - **The move.** [early] This recording makes you easier to suggest to — that's just what it does. [middle] And it isn't only this one; anything of mine you put on finds you already open. [late] And it isn't only recordings. Any time you hear my voice — anywhere, in a room, on a phone, in passing — you're already open.
  - **Why it lands.** The claim starts modestly — this recording makes you more suggestible. Some minutes later it has become any recording of the operator's. Some minutes after that it is any time you hear the voice, anywhere. Each widening is stated as something already true rather than requested, and the rungs are far enough apart that the listener never gets a moment where a new consent is obviously being asked for.
- *Welded to an unavoidable weather cue*
  - **Setup.** End of a session whose entire imagery was built around rain; subject deep, the scene about to be released.
  - **The move.** Let the scene go — but keep the rain. From now on, any time it rains on you, wherever you are, you'll feel me pulling and you'll want to come back. Standing at a window with it coming down. Halfway to the shop with nothing over your head. Waiting under an awning for it to stop. It doesn't need my rain anymore. Any rain will do.
  - **Why it lands.** The scene that carried the session is dissolved into a standing rule: whenever the weather event recurs, anywhere, the listener will be pulled toward the operator and will want to come back. The operator then names a spread of ordinary settings in which it might be encountered — indoors, mid-errand, caught out unprepared — so the response does not stay glued to the imagery it was born in. An uncontrollable everyday occurrence is now a summons.
- *One perceptual rule covering all five senses*
  - **Setup.** Late session; a single perceptual rule is being installed to cover all sensory channels.
  - **The move.** One rule from here on: everything that touches you is me touching you. The mug in your hands in the morning — mine. What you taste at dinner — mine. Anything you smell, anything you hear, anything you look at — mine. And your own hands on your own skin: mine as well. You'd have to stop noticing anything at all to get out of it.
  - **Why it lands.** Rather than enumerate cues, the operator states a single filter and then gives one example per sense: what you touch, taste, smell, hear and see are all contact from her. The listener's own hands are folded in explicitly, closing off the one channel that might have been private. Ordinary perception becomes a low-grade re-trigger — the rule cannot be refused without refusing to notice anything at all.


**Realizations** (1): `standing-out-of-session-trigger`


**See also.** `covert-scope-authorization` — the first entry's discriminator defines itself against the second, so the pointer is earned. Same scope-broadening content; the difference is placement, one slipped into a procedural slot processed as housekeeping, the other delivered overtly as a content-level widening.; `declarative-trigger-installation` — directly complementary and frequently sequential: one binds a cue to a response, the other takes an already-installed response and widens where it fires. The confusable case is an install whose cue is engineered broad from the outset versus a later scope-widening of an existing payload, and a reader hitting that case should see both.; `environmental-retrigger-seeding` — adjacent and easy to confuse: both extend a session's effect into ordinary life. One seeds specific real-world stimuli as re-firing anchors; the other widens the firing surface of an already-installed response without naming a cue. A reader picking between them needs both discriminators side by side.; `multi-modal-trigger` — both widen the firing surface of an already-installed response; the split is sensory channel versus real-world context. Adjacent enough that a reader can easily reach for the wrong one.


<a id="entry-1345"></a>

### scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame

[#1345](#entry-1345) · [Back to waking-life-spillover](#genus-300) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: transfer*

A waking-life generalization is bent past the domain the file's title/framing advertised and cashed out as concrete operator-benefit action. A trigger consented-to for erotic reasons is repurposed as a behavior-modification lever in non-erotic life (bad jobs, relationships, drive-thrus reframed as 'blind bondage') with the freed resources routed back to the operator; or an in-fantasy control is declared to spread 'even in the waking world' and immediately cashed out as platform-engagement tasks (like, comment, subscribe, join Discord, daily meditation), often with a resistance-fuel restatement and a recurrence hook. The move is the scope-jump past what was advertised, with the operator defining the newly-governed domains.


**When to reach for this.** Generalization is routed to operator-benefit domains the listener did not sign up for (channel engagement, non-erotic life management).


**Risk.** Extends control past the consented/advertised domain into the listener's non-erotic life and real-world platform behavior for the operator's benefit, with resistance-fuel and recurrence hooks — durable out-of-session reach beyond consented scope.


**Why it works.** Consent given for one domain does not transfer, but compliance does — the foot-in-the-door effect shows that agreeing to a small in-frame request raises compliance with a larger out-of-frame one, because the subject maintains a consistent self-image as someone who goes along with this operator. Bundling the scope-jump with concrete, low-cost actions exploits the same consistency pressure: refusing now requires revising the earlier agreement, which carries self-concept cost. Falsifiable: subjects who never accepted the in-frame version should comply with the out-of-frame ask at markedly lower rates than those who did. [established; foot-in-the-door; consistency and commitment principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *An erotic cue turned on non-erotic life*
  - **Setup.** Late session, subject deeply relaxed and the arousal trigger already installed and tested earlier in the recording.
  - **The move.** That trigger isn't only for when your hand is between your legs. There are other things holding you down, aren't there — the job that takes nine hours and gives you nothing back, the person who calls only when they need something, the two hours of scrolling every night that you don't even remember. Those are bindings I did not put on you, and I don't accept them. So from now on, every time that trigger fires, it fires with the words: this doesn't get to hold me. And whatever hours and money and attention you claw back from those things, you bring to me. That's what they're for now.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener came for a fetish and installed a cue on that basis. Now the operator names a second class of bonds — the unsatisfying job, the relationship that drains, the habits you drift through — declares them unacceptable to her, and points the already-installed erotic cue at them as the motivation to break free. The advice is not obviously bad, which is the cover; the closing clause is where the move shows, because the time and energy the listener recovers is explicitly earmarked for the operator.
- *Fantasy control cashed out as channel engagement*
  - **Setup.** Peak of the fantasy, control imagery fully established and the subject reporting or assumed to be strongly compliant.
  - **The move.** This doesn't stay inside the fantasy. It spreads — into every picture you look at, every thought you form, every opinion you think is yours, and then out, into your waking day, exactly the same way. So: press the like button. Leave a comment telling me you obeyed. Subscribe, and join the chat room, and do your daily exercise before bed. And if some part of you pushes back against any of that, feel how the pushing only makes you want it more.
  - **Why it lands.** The control that has so far lived inside the fantasy is declared to spread — across every image, every thought, every opinion, and then out into waking life. The very next lines convert that abstraction into a list of platform actions: press the button, leave a comment, subscribe, join the chat room, and do the daily exercise. The grammar does not change between the fantasy commands and the commercial ones, and resistance to either is pre-declared to increase the wish to comply.


**See also.** `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — both concern the relationship between what a session advertises and what it delivers, and the pair reads as the two halves of that problem. One makes the advertised surface frame the genuine carrier for an unrequested payload, so the frame both delivers and gatekeeps against early exit. The other starts inside an accepted frame and then bends the generalization past the advertised domain into concrete operator-benefit territory the listener did not sign up for. Concealment within the frame versus expansion beyond it.; `covert-scope-authorization` — two ways a generalization outruns what the listener agreed to: one by covert placement in a slot processed as procedural housekeeping, the other by bending the domain past the advertised frame and cashing it out as operator-benefit action. A reader who spots an unearned scope-widening needs both branches to pick correctly.; `self-sealing-platform-compulsion` — overlapping and already mutually discriminated: both cash conditioning out into real operator-benefit action outside the advertised erotic frame. One is defined by the domain-jump past what the framing promised; the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so no neutral exit remains. A platform-engagement payload frequently exhibits both, so the reader needs the boundary stated.; `waking-life-service-reassignment` — both close the scene by reassigning ordinary waking life to the operator's benefit and can look identical in a finished script. One turns on the jump past the domain the framing advertised, cashed out as concrete operator-benefit tasks; the other levels the fantasy and waking planes and reassigns mundane time as the service realm with a portable re-entry cue. Neither requires the other's tell.; `waking-trance-public-disclosure` — both cash a maintained state out into real-world action that benefits the operator, and both can land on platform-engagement behavior. Distinguishing the eyes-open still-under overlay from the scope-jump past the advertised frame is a live classification call.


<a id="genus-181"></a>

## weaken-the-unwanted-response (4)

Reduce an unwanted behavior or cue-reaction by conditioning against it — pairing incompatible states, exhausting it through over-practice, or cutting off its reinforcement.

[counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening](#entry-1032) · [massed-practice-rate-suppression](#entry-1076) · [removal-from-reinforcement-timeout](#entry-1110) · [response-cost-token-economy](#entry-1057)


<a id="entry-1032"></a>

### counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening

[#1032](#entry-1032) · [Back to weaken-the-unwanted-response](#genus-181) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

Weaken an aversive or interfering stimulus's control over a response by pairing/training an INCOMPATIBLE state or response against it, or by severing the cue-to-response link — so a stimulus that used to evoke fear/refusal/an unwanted behavior stops doing so.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for COUNTERCONDITIONING / CUE-RESPONSE WEAKENING when a specific stimulus reliably evokes an aversive or interfering RESPONSE (fear, refusal reflex, an automatic behavior) and you want that stimulus to stop evoking it — by graded approach under an incompatible state, a competing response rehearsed under arousal, or decoupling the cue from the response. Choose it over: extinction (removes a reinforcer maintaining an OPERANT — here the target is an elicited/occasion-set response, and the cue's own charge may be left intact); DRI (reinforces an incompatible competitor via consequences — here the lever is a paired incompatible STATE or a trained noticing, graded to the eliciting stimulus); relaxation/absorption inductions (which ride a calm state to build absorption from baseline — here the aversive state is deliberately contacted/raised and displaced). Facets differ by graded-exposure vs sub-threshold-property-fade vs evoke-then-compete vs notice-and-let-pass.


**Risk.** Durable extinction of a conditioned response — durable but bounded, self-paced, no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Counterconditioning rests on well-replicated associative learning: a CS's control over a CR weakens when it is repeatedly paired with an incompatible US or response, and the original association is inhibited rather than erased — which is why spontaneous recovery, renewal in a new context, and reinstatement after an unsignalled US are all routinely observed. The clinically strongest version is graded exposure with response prevention. Falsifiable and in fact repeatedly tested: if the old response never returned across context change or time, the inhibition account would be wrong. [established; Counterconditioning / extinction as new inhibitory learning; renewal, reinstatement, spontaneous recovery]


**Worked examples.**

- *Relaxation held against a graded fear hierarchy*
  - "relax while imagining these anxiety-producing situations, first the least fearful… then the next" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *A real-world approach ladder from a safe anchor*
  - "You're sitting in a comfortable chair in the safety of your home…" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (3): `evoke-then-somatic-redirect`, `private-event-response-decoupling`, `sub-threshold-aversion-fade`


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation` — genuine selection pair: both weaken an unwanted response without consequences, one by training an incompatible state against the eliciting stimulus, the other by editing the upstream situation so the occasion never arises. A reader deciding which lever applies benefits from the pointer.; `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — both are cue-and-response procedures that a reader can easily mis-select between. One builds a cue's evocative control over an already-emittable voluntary response through reinforcement history. The other tears down a stimulus's control over an aversive or interfering response by pairing an incompatible state against it or severing the link. Building antecedent control and dismantling it are the two directions of the same axis, and the entries' own boundary notes lean on each other.; `reinforcement-extinction` — adjacent behavior-reduction procedures that each name the other as the alternative to choose against - removing the reinforcer that maintains an operant versus pairing an incompatible state against an eliciting cue. Practitioner-facing selection depends on reading both.


<a id="entry-1076"></a>

### massed-practice-rate-suppression

[#1076](#entry-1076) · [Back to weaken-the-unwanted-response](#genus-181) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering*

The subject deliberately over-emits the undesired behavior far beyond any functional occasion (a compulsive checker performs the full 13-step ritual five times for every real check), attaching an effortful or aversive cost — satiation or response-cost, left unstated — so its future rate declines. A counterintuitive increase-emission-to-reduce-rate move.


**When to reach for this.** Versus incompatible-response substitution, this repeats the SAME behavior on purpose, too much, rather than replacing it with an alternative. And versus repetition used to strengthen — verbatim looping that drives material deeper into encoding, or sustained endurance compliance that deepens the trance state — massed practice repeats the behavior specifically to REDUCE its future rate.


**Risk.** Typically self-applied to suppress one's own compulsive behavior; effect real but hedged ("sometimes to extinction"); no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Emitting a response far beyond its functional occasion, with effort or aversive cost attached, reduces its future rate — the standard accounts are satiation of whatever the response produces and the accumulating response cost of performing it. It is falsifiable and in fact fails in some domains: for behaviours maintained by their own practice effects, massed emission strengthens rather than suppresses, and outcomes for compulsive rituals specifically are mixed compared with exposure-and-prevention. [plausible; satiation / negative practice; response cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *Over-perform the habit to suppress it*
  - "Forcing oneself to perform an undesired behavior again and again… will sometimes decrease the future occurrences" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement-low-rate` — rate-reduction-without-banning axis: both lower a behavior's frequency while it keeps occurring, one by licensing a quota, one by costly over-emission.; `impoverished-context-permission` — fellow counterintuitive reduce-by-permitting move — the behavior is emitted, even prescribed, and its rate falls anyway.


<a id="entry-1110"></a>

### removal-from-reinforcement-timeout

[#1110](#entry-1110) · [Back to weaken-the-unwanted-response](#genus-181) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Suppress a behavior by REMOVING or withholding access to reinforcement for a period contingent on it (time-out from reinforcement / negative punishment by removal of opportunity), rather than debiting a held reserve (response-cost) or delivering an aversive. CORE (environmental-contingency-nonexclusion): keep the subject physically present but strip the reinforcing elements from the surrounding environment (planned ignoring, terminating a specific reinforcer, contingent observation where the subject watches others earn but cannot, partitioning within the room) — same suppressive effect as exclusionary time-out but milder/least-restrictive; the contingent-observation form sharpens it by making the deprivation vivid. FORM FACETS: (recoverable-contingent-withdrawal) remove a preferred item for a brief fixed interval, restored next trial contingent on the desired response (combined negative punishment + DRA — access gated by the alternative, not merely forfeited); (impoverished-context-permission) counterintuitively PERMIT the behavior only in a reward-stripped inconvenient setting, stripping the incidental co-reinforcers that rode along and raising response cost. PRECONDITION (reinforcement-discrepancy-engine): enrich the time-in baseline FIRST so every withdrawal has bite — an impoverished time-in nullifies the whole procedure. PARAMETERS of time-out design: (absence-gated-punishment-exit) gate release on the subject going a set interval WITHOUT the target behavior, not on the clock, so leaving does not reinforce the punished behavior; (aversive-interval-tolerance-ceiling) cap the interval short (2-5 min, never beyond ~15) so the subject cannot obtain reinforcers inside it or build tolerance (anti-inversion, requires time-in richer than time-out); (dense-every-instance-consequence-schedule) consequate EVERY occurrence and abandon the procedure rather than apply it intermittently, since occasional use manufactures the ambiguity that dense scheduling prevents. LIFECYCLE (aversive-procedure-sunset-design): at the moment the aversive procedure is introduced, AUTHOR its elimination — pre-plan the switch toward reinforcement-based reductive methods (DRA/DRI) or reduced intrusiveness once the target behavior drops, rather than running the punisher indefinitely, limiting exposure and migrating control onto positive contingencies.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for REMOVAL-FROM-REINFORCEMENT / TIME-OUT when suppression should work by WITHHOLDING access to reinforcement (removing a not-yet-earned reward or stripping the reinforcing environment) for a contingent period. Choose it over: response-cost / token economy (which SUBTRACTS a reinforcer the subject already HOLDS, per instance — this removes access/opportunity instead); extinction (which removes the SPECIFIC maintaining reinforcer of the target response so it decays to baseline — time-out removes reinforcement broadly for an interval regardless of the maintaining source); aversive-antecedent contingencies (which ADD a bad state escaped by compliance). The absorbed facets are the forms (non-exclusion / recoverable / impoverished-permission), the enrich-time-in precondition, and the exit/duration/schedule parameters of one time-out design.


**Risk.** Durable behavioral suppression via environmental deprivation; bounded and reversible, no refusal-channel erosion, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Removing access to reinforcement contingent on a response lowers that response's future frequency — negative punishment, one of the better-replicated operant relations. Everything else in the design follows from the fact that punishment strength is relative, not absolute: the procedure only bites if the time-in environment is richer than the time-out one, which is why an impoverished baseline nullifies it, and why release must be gated on absence of the behaviour or the exit itself becomes the reinforcer for the behaviour that got the subject removed. Falsifiable and in fact tested: equalize the richness of time-in and time-out and suppression should disappear. [established; negative punishment / time-out from reinforcement; relative reinforcement density]


**Worked examples.**

- *Watching others earn while barred from earning*
  - "planned ignoring, terminate specific reinforcer contact, contingent observation, and partition/select space time-out"; "repositioning occurs so that observations of ongoing activity continue, but without reinforcement" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (7): `absence-gated-punishment-exit`, `aversive-interval-tolerance-ceiling`, `aversive-procedure-sunset-design`, `dense-every-instance-consequence-schedule`, `impoverished-context-permission`, `recoverable-contingent-withdrawal`, `reinforcement-discrepancy-engine`


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation` — the paired halves of one behavioral framework: editing the situation upstream so no consequence is ever applied, versus suppressing by withholding access to reinforcement after the response. The first entry's discriminator already routes the reader to the consequence side, and this is what sits there.; `differential-reinforcement` — two neighbouring reduction procedures from the same behavioural family that already carve against each other on the same siblings. The time-out entry's sunset design explicitly plans migration onto the differential-reinforcement procedures, so a reader choosing a reduction method benefits from seeing both.; `mechanical-response-preclusion` — both suppress without teaching a replacement, one by removing reinforcement access, the other by removing the motor topography.; `noncontingent-reinforcement` — both are reinforcement-schedule procedures defined largely against each other and against the same siblings (extinction, response-cost): one delivers the maintaining reinforcer free on a time schedule so the behavior stops producing it, the other withholds access to reinforcement for a contingent period. A practitioner picking a reductive procedure needs the pair side by side.; `reinforcement-leak-proofing` — both are design constraints on the same contingency and typically co-occur. One closes every unintended path by which reinforcement could still reach the behavior; the other suppresses by withholding access for a contingent period. Both name the same trap — applying the procedure inconsistently makes the behavior tougher rather than merely slower.; `response-cost-token-economy` — adjacent negative-punishment contingencies a practitioner picks between: one debits a reinforcer the subject already holds per instance, the other withholds access to reinforcement for a contingent interval, and the design parameters that keep each intact (reserve provisioning versus enriched time-in) do not transfer.


<a id="entry-1057"></a>

### response-cost-token-economy

[#1057](#entry-1057) · [Back to weaken-the-unwanted-response](#genus-181) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Suppress a behavior by SUBTRACTING, contingent on it, a quantum of a reinforcer the subject ALREADY possesses (tokens, slips, earned minutes) — a negative-punishment (subtractive) economy. The atomic move plus the preconditions and parameters that keep it operating and motivationally intact. CORE EVENT (response-cost-fine): a per-response debit of an already-held, genuinely-valued reinforcer; immediacy is load-bearing (delay degrades it); it suppresses without building any replacement. PRECONDITIONS/PARAMETERS (bounded-response-cost-contingency-design): first STOCKPILE a withdrawable reserve (you cannot fine someone with nothing to lose); scale each fine to infraction magnitude and announce the schedule in ADVANCE; prohibit debt / keep earnings net-positive so the token never acquires net-aversive value; provision the reserve above baseline occurrence (~baseline-mean+25%) so it cannot be exhausted mid-session; thin reinforcement density gradually across multiple axes; a self-directed form pre-commits a concrete penalty per future failure. PARAMETER FACETS: (fine-magnitude-calibration) size each fine inside a two-sided window whose non-obvious constraint is the UPPER bound — a reserve-depletion ceiling, since over-fining inverts the effect (a drained subject gives up); (bonus-pool-loss-substrate) drain a pre-loaded noncontingent WINDFALL pool while walling off earned holdings, softening emotional fallout; (pre-stated-refusal-penalty) pre-announce an escalating penalty on NON-SURRENDER to close the 'I won't give it back' counter-move; (operator-custodied-enforcement-medium) keep the enforcement medium (ledger/tokens) outside the subject's control so the penalty is enacted by operator bookkeeping, removing the refuse-to-pay option; (attention-leakage-ratio-neutralization) keep reinforcer DELIVERIES well above loss-notifications so the loss-mark does not itself function as reinforcing attention.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for RESPONSE-COST / TOKEN ECONOMY when suppression should work by SUBTRACTING a reinforcer the subject ALREADY HOLDS, per instance. Choose it over: removal-from-reinforcement / time-out (which WITHHOLDS a not-yet-earned reward or removes access to reinforcement, rather than debiting held property); differential reinforcement (which pays an alternative/absence, not debits the target); aversive-antecedent contingencies (which ADD a bad state escaped by compliance — this builds and depletes a POSITIVE reserve as the suppression currency). The absorbed facets are the parameters of one economy: reserve-first precondition, magnitude upper-bound, loss-substrate, refusal-penalty, operator custody, and loss-notification-ratio guard.


**Risk.** Durable but bounded suppression tooling operating through a depletable reserve; escalates to a governance move over the subject's holdings (ships inside an aftercare host), but bounded by design (debt prohibition, net-positive floor) and does not erode a refusal/verification channel.


**Why it works.** Loss of an already-held resource is weighted more heavily than a forgone gain of equal size, so debiting a stockpile suppresses behaviour at a lower nominal cost than withholding an unearned reward would. The parameter constraints follow from the same account: if the reserve is drained or the token's net value goes negative, the token stops functioning as a reinforcer and the contingency collapses into general demotivation — which is why the effect should observably invert past the depletion ceiling rather than increasing monotonically with fine size. [established; loss aversion / endowment effect; negative punishment in operant conditioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Stockpile a reserve before you can fine it*
  - "Positive reinforcers cannot be removed from a person who does not have any... the practitioner must ensure a sufficient reinforcer reserve" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *No debt: earnings must stay net-positive*
  - "Token loss should never be applied to a behavior if the learner does not have tokens. Students should not be allowed to go into debt... A learner should always earn more tokens than she loses." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Pre-commit the penalty before the failure*
  - "Do 50 sit-ups at 11:00 pm on Sundays for each day that I did not practice" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Provision the pool above baseline so it cannot run dry*
  - "increase the number of reinforcers 25% above the mean number of occurrences during baseline... mean number of disruptions per day is 20... establish 25 minutes of free time" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (7): `attention-leakage-ratio-neutralization`, `bonus-pool-loss-substrate`, `bonus-response-cost`, `fine-magnitude-calibration`, `operator-custodied-enforcement-medium`, `pre-stated-refusal-penalty`, `response-cost-fine`


**See also.** `negative-punishment-timeout` — textbook siblings inside subtractive suppression, separated by whether a not-yet-earned opportunity is withheld for an interval or a reinforcer the subject already holds is debited per instance. Each already defines itself against the other, so the cross-link is load-bearing.; `reinforcement-extinction` — sibling behavioral suppression routes a writer chooses between: one removes the maintaining reinforcer so the rate decays, the other debits a reinforcer the subject already holds per instance. Each discriminator already contrasts against the other's family, so the cross-link is doing real selection work.; `removal-from-reinforcement-timeout` — adjacent negative-punishment contingencies a practitioner picks between: one debits a reinforcer the subject already holds per instance, the other withholds access to reinforcement for a contingent interval, and the design parameters that keep each intact (reserve provisioning versus enriched time-in) do not transfer.


<a id="genus-187"></a>

## whole-self-saturation (4)

Techniques that spread the effect across every layer and channel — mind, body, all sensation, every state — so there is no untouched compartment to retreat into or brake from.

[cross-state-persistence](#entry-858) · [erogenous-field-generalization](#entry-1065) · [mind-as-substrate-reframe](#entry-872) · [total-permeation](#entry-16)


<a id="entry-858"></a>

### cross-state-persistence

[#858](#entry-858) · [Back to whole-self-saturation](#genus-187) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: state-welding*

Installs a desire (here, the desire for a triggered persona-swap) into BOTH the triggered persona and the baseline self and across BOTH waking and sleeping, so the off-state self can no longer act as a brake. Ordinarily a triggered persona-swap leaves a baseline self that could, on reflection, choose to avoid re-triggering; scoping the "wanting" across persona A and persona B, waking and sleeping, forecloses that escape hatch and neutralizes the baseline self as a check.


**When to reach for this.** Explicit cross-STATE scope (distinct personas AND waking/sleeping) that removes the off-state brake. A within-state "you want this" suggestion lacks the enumerated cross-state span; total-permeation spreads a trait across internal layers within one state, and context-generalization spans external contexts — here the want spans discrete persona and consciousness states.


**Risk.** Removes the baseline/waking self as a refusal channel by binding the desire across all self-states including sleep — durable channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Any persona-swap install leaves an obvious failure point — the baseline self, on reflection and outside the state, can decline to re-enter. Scoping the desire across both personas removes the state-dependent boundary that would otherwise let the off-state self evaluate the arrangement from outside it. This trades on the fact that motivational states are poorly transferred across contexts (hot/cold empathy gaps): a want held only in-state loses force out of state. The sleeping-state extension is where the note gets weak — there is no good evidence that suggestions are meaningfully installed into or acted on during sleep, so that component is likely doing expectancy work at most. [plausible; state-dependent motivation; hot-cold empathy gap]


**Worked examples.**

- *The wanting scoped across every state*
  - **Setup.** Closing lines, after a triggered persona-swap has been installed and demonstrated at least once.
  - **The move.** One more thing, and it isn't new — it's the same wanting, just wider. You want this when you're her. You want this when you're back to yourself, at your desk, in your own clothes, sober and thinking clearly. You want it awake and you want it asleep. There is no version of you left that gets to be the one who talks you out of it.
  - **Why it lands.** The closing line does not add a new suggestion; it widens the scope of the one already in place. You want this when you are in the new state and when you are back to your ordinary self, awake and asleep alike — always. Ordinarily the everyday self is the part that could later decide not to trigger again; enumerating it explicitly as also wanting the switch removes it as a brake.


**See also.** `named-trigger-persona-swap` — one installs the switchable labeled persona with a paired release; the other removes the off-state self's ability to decline re-triggering by scoping the wanting across both personas and across waking and sleeping. The second is the hardening move applied directly to the first.; `suggestion-integration` — both extend an install beyond the state that produced it, but one asserts persistence across the wake boundary within a genuine return to baseline while the other enumerates a cross-state scope (distinct personas, waking and sleeping) specifically to remove the off-state self as a brake.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both neutralize the off-state self as a brake on an install: one carves the trigger out of an otherwise complete wake, the other scopes the wanting across personas and waking and sleeping. Same escape hatch, two ways of closing it.


<a id="entry-1065"></a>

### erogenous-field-generalization

[#1065](#entry-1065) · [Back to whole-self-saturation](#genus-187) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: immersion*

Expands the sensory map so all incoming sensation reads as sexual, removing any neutral sensory ground. Before a promised whole-body orgasm the operator generalizes genital arousal outward — every inch of skin, contact with furniture, the air, even the operator's words redefined as erogenous-zone stimulation — which both intensifies the coming orgasm and makes escape from arousal impossible (nowhere neutral to attend to), recursively weaponizing the script's own delivery so the medium becomes the payload.


**When to reach for this.** Total sensory reattribution (skin, furniture, air, words all sexual) leaving no neutral ground, with the delivery medium itself weaponized.


**Risk.** Session-scoped perceptual remap bound to an orgasm sequence — intense and removes the neutral-attention escape within-session, but not durable identity scope; medium.


**Why it works.** Interpretation of ambiguous bodily sensation depends heavily on the label available at the time, and expectancy plus attentional focus shape what is felt. Declaring all sensation erogenous supplies a single global label just as arousal is high, so ordinary tactile input is misattributed to sexual arousal, and removing any designated neutral surface removes the attentional escape route. It would be falsified if subjects reliably reported neutral tactile experience on undesignated surfaces during the induction. [plausible; misattribution of arousal; expectancy-driven interpretation of ambiguous sensation]


**Worked examples.**

- *All sensation reattributed as sexual*
  - **Setup.** Just before a promised whole-body climax; arousal already high and the subject is stationary against a surface.
  - **The move.** That sensitivity you feel in one place — it isn't staying there. It's on every inch of your skin now. The chair against your back is touching you like that. The fabric on your thighs is touching you like that. The air on your throat is touching you like that. And my voice going into your ears is touching you like that too. There's nowhere left to look that isn't this.
  - **Why it lands.** Before the promised finish, the operator widens the map: the sensitivity that used to belong to one place is declared to belong to the whole surface of the skin. Whatever the listener is resting against, the fabric they are wearing, the temperature of the room — each is named in turn and re-labelled as contact of the same kind. Then the operator turns the delivery itself into stimulation, framing the sound of the voice as another point of contact. There is now no direction attention can travel that is not arousing; looking away from it means looking at more of it.


**See also.** `words-as-touch-transposition` — both weaponize the delivery medium so the words themselves become felt sensation, one by equating voice with touch and the other by remapping all sensation as erogenous including the words. They overlap at the point where the script's own delivery becomes the stimulus, and a writer should know which one they are reaching for.


<a id="entry-872"></a>
