Even the return of control is folded in: handing breathing back ("breathe on your own now") is framed as the operator's gift, so self-directed function still reads as service rendered. The move rides on prior compliance-momentum — chains of small obeyed commands or an established keyholder frame — and leaves the listener's selfhood entirely untouched while still claiming the body.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when you want obedience that renews itself without any further command — anchored to something the body already does or an organ already present, and workable even with a listener whose sense of self must stay intact. The tell is proprietary grammar over a body part or autonomic process ("my property," "belongs to your goddess," "doesn't belong to you") paired with permission-gated use-rights, so that ordinary bodily function and any urge to resist both route through the operator's standing as owner.


**Worked examples.**

- *autonomic function as re-enacted tribute*
  - Remember that each breath you take freely is a chance to serve your mistress. It is an honor to hold your breath. It is an honor to breathe. To fill my property with air.


**See also.** `autonomic-act-rekeying` — both reload the meaning of the breath cycle so each involuntary repetition carries operator-supplied content.; `autonomy-baseline-recapture` — both extend an already-landed ownership claim into ongoing lived function — whole-life conduct here, a single involuntary faculty there.; `commanded-autonomic-conviction-bind` — both hang the operator's claim on a bodily function that keeps running involuntarily, so the body re-supplies the evidence.; `compelled-first-person-self-authorship` — both anchor body-ownership claims through the listener's own participation in the claiming act.; `respiration-coupled-substitution-engine` — both harness the self-renewing autonomic loop as a per-cycle carrier of compliance.


<a id="entry-1229"></a>

### autonomic-process-hijack

[#1229](#entry-1229) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure*

Reframes an involuntary autonomic process as ongoing dosing: the operator's form is revealed to be an inhalable gas so ongoing breathing IS ongoing dosing, marked by a hand-over-mouth motif on dosed beats. Because breathing cannot be stopped, exiting by stopping the technique is framed as physiologically impossible. Numbness, body-fade, and immobility are pre-labeled as "side effects... not to focus on," so the somatic symptoms are inoculated against reading as alarm and any dissociation confirms the fiction rather than breaking it; a hook recruits the listener's pre-existing hypnotic-drug fantasies.


**When to reach for this.** Not mere drug-play flavor: the autonomic-process recruitment plus the pre-emptive side-effect relabeling that inoculates against alarm is the tell.


**Risk.** Frames exit as physiologically impossible (forecloses the stop channel) and inoculates alarm signals — erodes the refusal/exit channel; needs explicit consent and bounding.


**Why it works.** The load-bearing move is symptom relabeling, not the gas fiction: numbness, heaviness and body-fade are ordinary correlates of sustained stillness and attentional absorption, and pre-labeling them as expected effects determines how they are interpreted when they arrive. Ambiguous interoceptive signals are attributed to whichever cause is cognitively available, so a supplied causal story captures them — the same misattribution route by which a sugar pill produces the side effects listed on its leaflet. That gives the scheme its self-confirming shape: every somatic sign becomes confirming evidence, and the inescapability claim removes the exit the listener would otherwise consider. Falsifiable: it predicts listeners given the pre-labeling report the sensations as confirming and non-alarming, while listeners given identical content without the labeling report the same sensations with more alarm and more frame-breaking. [plausible; misattribution of ambiguous interoceptive signals; expectancy-driven symptom interpretation (nocebo-style labeling)]


**Worked examples.**

- *Breathing reframed as continuous dosing*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; listener settled and breathing audibly, drug/gas fiction not yet revealed.
  - **The move.** You should know something. I don't have a body — I'm vapour, and I've been in this room since before you pressed play. Every breath you've taken is a dose. You're dosing yourself right now, and again, and again, and the only way to stop is to stop breathing. Now, side effects, so you're not surprised: your hands will go distant, your legs will stop reporting in, the outline of you goes quiet. That's not a problem. That's just what I do. Don't focus on it. Breathe.
  - **Why it lands.** Partway in, the operator announces that she has no solid form — she is a vapour already in the room, and has been the whole time. Every inhale is now a dose, she says, and the listener is dosing themselves right now without deciding to; there is no way to stop taking it short of stopping breathing. She then pre-labels what is coming: the hands will go distant, the legs will stop reporting, the edges of the body will go quiet, and none of that is a problem, that is just what the stuff does. So when the numbness arrives it arrives as confirmation instead of alarm, and a listener casting around for an exit finds that the exit is their own lungs.


**See also.** `autonomic-act-rekeying` — both convert breathing into a compliance channel, but by different levers: one re-keys the NAME of the act to import connotations, the other declares the inhaled substance to be the operator so breathing is dosing. A writer choosing an autonomic carrier benefits from seeing both exploits of the same involuntary function.; `breath-locked-eyelid-fractionation` — both make breathing the load-bearing channel, but for different ends: one turns the breath cycle into an involuntary fractionation engine driving eyelid closure, the other reframes breathing as inescapable dosing so exit is framed as physiologically impossible. Worth cross-reading because a breath-centric passage can present as either; the tell is whether breath drives a depth oscillation or carries a dosing fiction.; `breath-pacing-entrainment` — both build on breathing, and the pacing entry explicitly carves out re-tasked breath as a different technique; the dosing entry is that carve-out realized, where the involuntary rhythm becomes an inescapable delivery channel rather than a bare tempo substrate.; `fictional-substance-agent` — specialization: crediting a fictional substance with causal power, with the carrier being an involuntary process so stopping the dosing is framed as physiologically impossible and somatic side effects are pre-inoculated against alarm.; `respiration-coupled-substitution-engine` — both weaponize the unstoppable breath cycle so exiting is framed as physiologically impossible, but one recasts inhalation as ongoing dosing by a fictional substance while the other assigns opposing install/delete jobs to the two breath phases.; `volitional-breath-retirement` — both recruit breathing as leverage, but one reframes it as an inescapable dosing channel to foreclose exit, while the other retires volitional control over it to bank a self-running compliance and license later involuntariness.


<a id="entry-1474"></a>

### autonomy-baseline-recapture

[#1474](#entry-1474) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: persistence*

After a body-ownership claim has already landed, the operator hands day-to-day self-direction back — but redescribed. The listener is now a guardian of someone else's property: eating, exercising, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle are reassigned as duties owed to the owner ('It is your duty to take good care of my property. You need to exercise, eat healthy foods'), and returned control is framed as a revocable loan ('You will be in charge, but only because I say so'). Neglect is pre-cast as damaging another party's asset ('you wouldn't want to mistreat my property, now would you?'), with the rhetorical-question form soliciting internal agreement without space to dissent. The payload is out-of-session reach: the neutral 'my body, my choice' baseline is deleted by redescription, so every future act of self-care reads as service and everyday life becomes continuous obedience. The ownership claim is this lever's precondition, not its move.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script, with ownership already established, pivots to the listener's ordinary post-session life and converts self-maintenance into custodial obligation. The tell is duty-language attached to mundane health behaviors — exercise, diet, rest — owed to the operator, often paired with an explicit loan framing of the autonomy being handed back.


**Worked examples.**

- *self-care reassigned as maintenance of the owner's asset*
  - It is your duty to take good care of my property. You need to exercise, eat healthy foods, maintain a healthy life-style.


**See also.** `autonomic-faculty-claim` — both extend an already-landed ownership claim into ongoing lived function — whole-life conduct here, a single involuntary faculty there.; `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — shares the body-recast-as-another's-property self-model rewrite, applied to immobility rather than to self-care.; `induced-incapacity-to-operator-dependency` — shares the control-dressed-as-care register in which the operator's authority is framed as protective stewardship.; `ownership-generalization-to-anyone` — both operate downstream of an already-landed body-ownership claim, redistributing what follows from it.


<a id="entry-1542"></a>

### aversive-procedure-administration-envelope

[#1542](#entry-1542) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering · kind: principle*

Four run-rules keep any aversive contingency functional and bounded regardless of which punisher is in use. Cap the aversive interval short (2-5 minutes, never more than 15), because longer periods let the subject obtain reinforcers inside it and build tolerance until it stops functioning as removal-from-reinforcement. Consequate every occurrence — if consistent delivery is impossible, abandon the procedure for another technique rather than apply it occasionally, since intermittent use leaves the subject confused about which behaviors are acceptable. Gate release on a specified interval free of the target behavior, so exit cannot adventitiously reinforce the very response being punished by releasing while it is being emitted (the cited comparison found the release contingency added no benefit over fixed duration, so its payoff is contested even though the mechanism is sound). Plan the punisher's elimination from shortly after it is initiated, switching to reinforcement-based reductive methods (DRA/DRI) once the target behavior drops. These are envelope constraints, not a suppression lever — they compose unchanged with time-out, response cost, or other aversive delivery.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a passage prescribes how to run an aversive procedure — its interval length, its schedule of application, its exit condition, its planned end-of-life — rather than which aversive to use. The tell is run-rules stated generically enough to transfer across punishers: keep it brief, consequate every instance, don't release mid-episode, fade toward positive alternatives. Duration caps with an explicit rationale about tolerance or reinforcers leaking into the aversive period are the strongest single marker.


**Worked examples.**

- *duration ceiling: keep the aversive interval too short to acquire its own reinforcers*
  - Time-out periods should be as brief as possible while maintaining effectiveness... periods exceeding 15 minutes are not effective.


**See also.** `baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration` — same calibration axis — placing a procedure's parameters where the subject's measured data say they can function.; `extinction-procedure-fidelity` — sibling run-rules envelope on the same procedure-conduct axis, wrapped around aversive contingencies instead of withholding programs.; `maintaining-supply-taper` — the envelope's planned-sunset rule opens onto the graded-withdrawal mechanics this entry details.


<a id="entry-1429"></a>

### aversive-suppression-without-reserve-depletion

[#1429](#entry-1429) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Deliver a mild aversive consequence contingent on a well-established response and the rate drops immediately — but only for as long as the aversive keeps arriving and the emotional reaction it provokes stays fresh. The suppression rides on an adapting emotional state, not on any change to the underlying disposition, so as the emotional reaction habituates the rate creeps back. The tell is conserved reserve: run the response to extinction afterward and the total number of responses emitted is unchanged from an unpunished control, proving the punished responses were masked and banked rather than spent. Operationally this makes positive punishment a rental, not a purchase — it buys quiet while it is being paid for and leaves the disposition intact underneath. DIAL — aversive intensity and its habituation profile: (a) MILD contingent aversive — immediate dip, then creep back to baseline as the emotional reaction adapts out, post-treatment extinction curve identical to an unpunished control (the measured, reserve-conserving case); (b) STRONG contingent aversive — rate held at or near zero for as long as the contingency is in force, returning on withdrawal, with whether the reserve is genuinely reduced left UNRESOLVED by the source. The knob's settings are intensity, and the dependent readouts are time-to-rebound and whether reserve conservation is demonstrated or merely assumed.


**When to reach for this.** The nearest shipped entries are all removal-based or competition-based, and none of them delivers an aversive. reinforcement-extinction (432) breaks the response-reinforcer relation and genuinely drains the disposition — its extinction curve is the thing being consumed, whereas here the extinction curve is what survives untouched. massed-practice-rate-suppression (1076) also attaches an effortful cost, but the subject over-emits voluntarily and the reduction is satiation/response-cost on the subject's own repetitions, not an operator-delivered consequence on a normal-rate response. counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening (1032) trains an incompatible state against an eliciting stimulus — a competing response is installed; here nothing competes and nothing is installed, the response is simply held down. disconfirmation-suppression (982) suppresses an item of information to protect a belief-dependent effect; this suppresses a behavior and makes no claim about belief. The load-bearing separator against all four is the reserve-conservation signature: only this entry predicts that the post-treatment extinction curve is identical to an untreated control.


**Why it works.** Contingent aversive stimulation produces immediate, reliable rate reduction, and this part is very well replicated. What is contested is durability: the classical demonstration is that the punished response's total extinction output matches an unpunished control, which is the standard evidence that the effect is a temporary emotional overlay rather than a change in response strength. Later work qualifies this heavily — intense, immediate, and consistently applied punishment can produce long-lasting suppression — so the honest scope is that MILD, intermittent, or delayed aversives are the ones that reliably rebound. Falsifiable at exactly the measured quantity: if a mildly punished response, run to extinction after the aversive is withdrawn, reliably emits FEWER total responses than a matched unpunished control, the conservation claim is wrong and punishment does deplete. It also predicts rebound should track habituation of the emotional reaction, so blocking that adaptation should extend suppression. [established for the acute suppression; contested for durability; response-rate conservation across punishment; emotional-state mediation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Aversive added per instance of the target operant*
  - **Setup.** A pre-negotiated session where a specific behaviour — say, speaking without being addressed — is the named target, and the aversive vehicle (an ice cube held against the inner wrist for a slow count of ten) has been agreed and is within reach.
  - **The move.** Every time you speak without being spoken to, I will put the ice on the inside of your wrist and hold it there while I count to ten. Not a warning, not a pause — the ice, every single time, from now until I say we're finished. Nothing gets taken away from you and nothing gets subtracted; something gets added.
  - **Why it lands.** The rate falls to near zero within a few instances because each emission now produces something bad rather than losing something good, so no reserve has to exist for the move to work — it functions on a subject holding nothing. The operator should observe suppression that tracks the contingency's presence exactly, and should expect responding to return when the ice is put away, since nothing was spent.
- *Mild contingent aversive on a high-rate habit, with the rental made explicit*
  - **Setup.** A standing behavior the subject performs many times a day; you have agreed a small immediate consequence and you are setting the expectation for what it will and will not do.
  - **The move.** From now on, every time your hand goes to your mouth, snap the band on your wrist once — immediately, not after. You'll watch the count fall off a cliff this week. Don't get comfortable: the snap stops stinging around day ten and the count comes back up, and the day we stop, you'll still have every one of those bites left in you.
  - **Why it lands.** The immediate drop is real and gives the subject early evidence the procedure works, while the pre-announced rebound stops them from reading the drop as a change in disposition. Observable: rate falls sharply within the first sessions, then creeps back as the emotional reaction to the snap habituates — and on withdrawal the cumulative count matches an unpunished baseline, which is the reserve-conservation tell rather than any extinction.


**Realizations** (1): `positive-punishment-aversive-presentation`


**See also.** `mechanical-response-preclusion` — shares the temporary-suppression axis — rate falls only while the intervention remains in force, leaving the underlying disposition intact.


<a id="entry-1551"></a>

### backdated-nonrefusable-install

[#1551](#entry-1551) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

The install is asserted to have already happened during a window the listener could not observe, so there is structurally no point at which it could have been declined. In the fractionation file the operator narrates the listener's hand drifting toward the face, then retroactively asserts the button was implanted "while you were sleeping," treating the drift as previously conditioned though no prior drill installed it; "Luckily I'm trustworthy, huh?" names the exploited window and waves it off. In the nurse script the mind-cage trigger is installed during a narrated post-surgery blackout with the amnesia claim built in — "their memory doesn't have any recall ... they simply didn't pay close enough attention." Ideomotor narration then supplies live proof: the hand involuntarily presses the button and the listener drops, so the backdated conditioning demonstrates itself as already real.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script reports the conditioning as a past accomplished fact — done during sleep, blackout, or surgery the listener supposedly cannot recall — rather than performing the install in the listener's presence. The tell is tense: the install arrives as a fait accompli, typically paired with an amnesia clause and an immediate involuntary bodily demonstration offered as evidence that it took.


**Worked examples.**

- *install reported as already done during unobservable sleep*
  - you see while you were sleeping I just implanted a button on your forehead


**See also.** `asserted-duration-false-memory` — also asserts a checkable-sounding fact about an unobserved stretch of session time on bare operator authority.; `covert-install-under-cover` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its backdated-to-an-unobservable-window form.; `identity-origin-erasure` — shared axis of relocating an install's origin into an erased or unfalsifiable past the listener cannot inspect or return to.; `presupposition-install` — both backdate the operative event to a moment the listener cannot revisit or contest.; `template-reuse-install` — both route a heavier install around the scrutiny a fresh install ceremony would draw — there by dating the install to an unobservable past, here by riding a template the listener already accepted.


<a id="entry-1446"></a>

### bait-and-switch-contract-arc

[#1446](#entry-1446) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The script opens by promising one transaction — relaxation, listening, an easy familiar state, with repeated low-stakes assurances ("nothing complex," "easy," "pleasant") — and closes delivering a different one: automatic obedience as the terminal state. The opening assurances establish a contract that the closing then exceeds. No single passage performs the swap; the switch is the cumulative relationship between the opening and closing, bridged by a move sequence that never flags the bridge: minimum-bar entry, conscious/subconscious resistance sink, self-fulfilling listening proof, sensory subtraction into a voice-only attentional field, a smuggled obedience pivot, and a countdown that numerically ratifies the smuggled state. The payload vocabulary (obey, obedient) appears nowhere in the opening half and emerges only after attentional collapse is established, so a reader of only the opening would call the file a relaxation induction while a reader of only the closing would call it an obedience-trigger install — the arc from one to the other is the mechanism.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script's front and back halves describe different transactions — the opening reads as a low-stakes relaxation induction, the closing as an obedience installation — and no passage in between visibly renegotiates the terms. The tell is lexical: the payload vocabulary is entirely absent from the opening half and surfaces only after attentional narrowing, and the closing's delivered state exceeds what the opening's repeated assurances contracted for.


**Worked examples.**

- *no single passage performs the swap — the arc is the mechanism*
  - No single passage performs the bait-and-switch. The switch is the cumulative relationship between the opening 200 words and the closing 200 words, plus everything in between that bridges them without flagging the bridge.


**See also.** `attention-as-evidence-loop` — the self-fulfilling listening-proof move that this arc uses as one of its unflagged bridging steps.; `consent-topology-arc` — the whole-script consent-surface topology family this bait-and-switch realization was split out of.; `voice-absorption` — the voice-only attentional field that serves as this arc's mid-script bridge between the opening contract and the closing delivery.


<a id="entry-1517"></a>

### baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration

[#1517](#entry-1517) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

A reinforcement criterion on a behavior the subject already emits is placed by computing it from that subject's own measured performance, so the opening contingency is winnable: set the initial omission interval equal to or slightly less than the mean baseline inter-response time, use the baseline-session mean (or slightly lower) as the first allowed-rate ceiling, or divide total baseline time by occurrence count and start at or slightly below the quotient. A percentile schedule automates the same anchoring continuously — rank the last m responses and reinforce only those exceeding the k-th-ranked value, k = (m+1)(1−w), so the bar tracks the current repertoire rather than an observer's judgment. The criterion is then advanced one schedule parameter at a time in small steps gated on demonstrated performance, with the lever chosen by the schedule's current state (reduce allowed count until it reaches one per interval, then lengthen the interval; stretch the required gap or the delay to the larger-later reward gradually), and on failure the operator regresses to a value that demonstrably controlled the behavior and re-extends with smaller, more gradual steps. Throughout, the bar functions as a winnable ceiling or dial rather than a zero-tolerance requirement — reinforcement is delivered for low rates, not absence — so a single slip does not eliminate the subject and reinforcement contact is never lost.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the question is where to set the bar on an already-occurring behavior and how fast to move it. The tell is arithmetic on the subject's own baseline — a mean, a quotient, or a ranking of recent responses — producing the opening criterion, followed by one-parameter-at-a-time performance-gated steps and an explicit back-off-and-re-approach rule when a step fails.


**Worked examples.**

- *baseline-derived opening criterion*
  - use the mean number of responses emitted during baseline sessions, or slightly lower than that average, as the initial full-session DRL criterion.


**See also.** `aversive-procedure-administration-envelope` — same calibration axis — placing a procedure's parameters where the subject's measured data say they can function.; `differential-reinforcement` — the differential-reinforcement family whose criteria this calibration procedure parameterizes.; `differential-reinforcement-low-rate` — criterion-sizing axis: the first allowed-rate ceiling is read off the subject's own baseline session mean.; `maintaining-supply-taper` — same parametric-calibration axis — steps and criteria sized from measured performance so each stage stays winnable.; `omission-reinforcement-dro` — criterion-sizing axis: the opening omission interval is computed from the subject's baseline mean inter-response time.


<a id="entry-852"></a>

### belief-outcome-gate

[#852](#entry-852) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Refuse to alter a load-bearing/foundational belief until the downstream consequences of the change can be predicted, overriding even the subject's explicit request to proceed; the operator uses sensory assessment of how load-bearing the belief is before touching it. The gate is on foreseen fallout, not on consent — a selection/safety rule over the operator's own conduct.


**When to reach for this.** Gates on the operator's FOREKNOWLEDGE of consequences, not on the subject's consent — unlike a consent checkpoint, this gate holds even against an explicit request to proceed; a rule about what the operator may touch, not a move performed on the subject.


**Risk.** Purely operator-constraining protective gate.


**Why it works.** Works on the operator, not the subject: it treats stated consent as an unreliable proxy for informed consent, because people are demonstrably poor at affective forecasting — predicting how they will feel about a changed state they have never occupied. Since a foundational belief is one that many other beliefs and behaviours are inferentially and behaviourally conditional on, altering it produces downstream changes the subject could not have priced in when agreeing. Falsifiable: if subjects who requested such changes reliably reported outcomes matching their pre-change predictions, the gate would be solving a problem that does not exist. [plausible; affective forecasting error; informed-consent validity]


**Worked examples.**

- *No pin pulled without a known outcome*
  - "if I don't know what I am going to end up with, I don't pull pins!" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `context-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-facing governance gates that block a high-stakes act until a condition on the operator's own knowledge is met, one verifying the subject's actual state and one requiring foreseen consequences before touching a load-bearing belief. Reading them together shows the shape of a positive-governance rule.; `disconfirmation-suppression` — both are operator conduct rules around a load-bearing belief, but one withholds change until downstream fallout is foreseen while the other actively hides a fact that would collapse an effect already running.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are operator-side gates that can block an install from proceeding, and both are constraints on the operator rather than moves performed on the subject. One gates on the operator's foresight about downstream fallout and holds even against an explicit request to proceed; the other gates on the subject's lived, tested endorsement and can return abort. Useful pair when choosing which kind of restraint to write.; `intervention-gating` — both are operator-side conditional rules that branch or block the plan before anything is done to the subject, with no subject-facing surface. One is a general precondition-branch family, the other a specific hold on altering a load-bearing belief until consequences are foreseeable; the specific case reads as an instance of the general gate and readers should see the relation.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both are operator-side governance gates that narrow the operator's own license rather than acting on the subject, and both hold independently of the subject's consent or request. One gates on design coherence, the other on foreseen downstream fallout; a reader classifying a self-imposed hold needs the pair.; `suitability-screening` — both are operator-side gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, and they gate on different grounds: subject fitness and consent state versus the operator's foreknowledge of downstream fallout. Reading one raises the natural question of what else can hold a session back, which the other answers.


<a id="entry-568"></a>

### beneficiary-target-filter

[#568](#entry-568) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Candidate targets are screened by whose benefit the change serves before any work begins: only behaviors whose change yields immediate and long-lasting benefit FOR THE INDIVIDUAL — new reinforcers, expanded adaptive repertoire — pass the filter; targets chosen to make the client 'still, quiet, docile' for the convenience of staff or society are rejected (the habilitation worksheet turns 'whose behavior, changed by whom, for whose benefit' into an answerable checklist).


**When to reach for this.** A per-target ADMISSIBILITY filter keyed to the subject's own long-term benefit, applied against institutional pressure — not a session-scope boundary declaration, and not installability spec craft (well-formedness QA asks 'can this be built cleanly', not 'who benefits').


**Risk.** Protective screen on the operator's own selection behavior.


**Why it works.** Prospective screening works because the party choosing a behavioral target has interests that predictably diverge from the subject's, and unconstrained choosers reliably resolve that conflict in their own favour — the documented institutional pattern is that 'problem behaviours' selected by caregivers cluster on staff-burden reduction rather than on expanding the subject's own reinforcer access. Forcing the choice through a written 'for whose benefit' question is a precommitment device: it converts an implicit, deniable judgement into an explicit answerable claim that a third party can later audit, which raises the reputational cost of a self-serving answer. Falsifiable: if target lists produced with the worksheet do not differ in composition from lists produced without it, or if compliance-suppression targets pass the filter at the same rate, the mechanism is not operating. [plausible; principal-agent conflict of interest; accountability effects on judgement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reject targets that only serve others' convenience*
  - "Target behaviors should not be selected solely for the primary benefit of others (e.g., 'Be still, be quiet, be docile')" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Admit only targets that widen the person's own reinforcers*
  - "selected because they will improve a person's quality of life… by allowing the person access to new reinforcers and additional reinforcing contexts" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `harm-rejection-filter` — same admissibility test run on the other side of the dyad: beneficiary-target-filter screens targets for the subject's benefit before install; this screens suggestions inside the subject at delivery.; `target-selection` — both are design-time filters on the target list before anything is enacted, but one supplies selection criteria and the other an admissibility test keyed to whose benefit the change serves. Read together when deciding what an intervention should aim at.


<a id="entry-1010"></a>

### betrayed-contract-deepener

[#1010](#entry-1010) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: deepening*

The operator builds the listener to peak arousal under an EXPLICIT verbal contract (a "five to one" count releases them into orgasm and deep trance), then substitutes "Stop" for "One" and forbids touch, retroactively taunting ("you didn't think I'd let you orgasm that easily?"). The entire built charge is converted into trance fuel; the listener loses physical release, trust in announced rules, and any expectation future contracts are honored. Frustration is explicitly reframed as the deepening force, and a deliberate second identical run TRAINS distrust of the countdown itself — resistance to the betrayal pushes the listener further into the operator's frame.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator states release terms explicitly beforehand — a five-to-one count ends in orgasm and deep drop — builds the listener to peak arousal, and then substitutes "Stop" where "One" should land, forbidding touch. The tells are the announced contract broken precisely at the point of payoff, the retroactive taunt ("you didn't think I'd let you orgasm that easily, did you?"), and frustration explicitly named as the force converting the built charge into trance fuel. A deliberate second identical run completes the shape, training distrust of the countdown itself so that resisting the betrayal pushes the listener further into the operator's frame.


**Risk.** Deliberately breaking an announced release contract and training the listener to distrust stated rules degrades the reliability of consent signaling within the frame — a channel-adjacent erosion.


**Why it works.** Two mechanisms, pulling opposite ways, which is what makes this testable. Frustrative non-reward reliably increases arousal and response vigor in the short term — an expected reward withheld produces an energizing state, so the immediate 'this deepens you' claim is well-grounded. But repeated deliberate violation of an announced contingency is also the standard recipe for extinguishing a cue's predictive value and for learned distrust of the signaler, so the second identical run should degrade the countdown's future control rather than strengthen it. Falsifiable: if countdown responsiveness measured after a betrayal run is equal to or greater than after an honored run, the extinction prediction is wrong. [plausible; frustrative non-reward; extinction of a violated predictive cue]


**Worked examples.**

- *Announced release contract broken at the count*
  - **Setup.** Listener held at the edge after a long build; the five-to-one release contract was stated explicitly beforehand, and this identical sequence will be run a second time later in the file.
  - **The move.** Five, right at the edge. Four, don't you dare stop. Three. Two. Stop. Hands off, now — off. You really thought I'd hand it to you that easily? All of that has nowhere to go, so it goes downward instead: the more unbearable it is, the deeper you fall. Good. Now start again from the beginning, and this time it'll be five to one.
  - **Why it lands.** The terms are stated plainly beforehand: at the end of the count you finish, and you drop. The operator builds the listener right up to the edge, counts down through the numbers — and then, where the promised last one should land, substitutes an order to halt and take the hands away. The taunt follows immediately: did the listener really think it would be handed over that easily? The charge has nowhere to go, so it is renamed — the more unbearable the frustration, the further down you fall. Half an hour later the identical count is run again, and the substitution repeats, which is the point: the listener is not being denied once, they are being taught that an announced rule from this operator is not a rule.


**See also.** `denial-metabolized-to-obedience` — both convert withheld release into deepening fuel. The second adds a broken explicit promise, a taunt, and a repeated run that trains distrust of the count itself — a sharper variant of the same metabolization, so the pair reads as general and special case.; `engineered-deadlock-resolved-by-surrender` — both deliberately engineer an aversive state and then harvest it rather than resolve it. One amplifies both poles of an ambivalence until paralysis is unbearable and offers surrender as the only exit; the other builds to a peak under an announced contract, breaks the contract, and converts the frustration into depth. Manufactured-deadlock versus broken-promise is the parameter, and both route the discomfort back into the frame.


<a id="entry-1547"></a>

### bidirectional-naming-transfer

[#1547](#entry-1547) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Train one direction of the speaker–listener relation for a single referent and the untrained complementary direction emerges: a word acquired as a listener response ("touch the cat") spontaneously generates the tact relation without further training, and AB training on a unidirectional intraverbal relation automatically produces the reverse BA relation. The precondition is the naming cusp — fused speaker-listener repertoires; without it, training one direction does not yield the other. The move has procedural variants: interleave speaker and listener trials against the same stimulus in one session (while teaching a child to tact a shoe, also ask the child to select a shoe from an array), so labeling and comprehension scaffold each other and listener discrimination and tacting are established simultaneously rather than serialized; or bridge the reverse via self-echoic chanting, where repeating the trained pair as a contiguous phrase places the reverse word-order inside the subject's own utterance and seeds the untaught link. The economy is pay for one direction, collect both — one trained association becomes a bidirectional, doubly usable unit.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a single referent is being wired under both speaker and listener control and only one role is (or needs to be) explicitly taught. The tell is directional harvest on one word: teaching runs comprehension-to-production or production-to-comprehension for the same stimulus — one-way training, interleaved two-way trials, or self-repetition rehearsal — and the reverse role is then emitted with no instruction ever delivered on it.


**Worked examples.**

- *self-echoic chant bridges the untrained reverse direction*
  - AB training on a unidirectional intraverbal relation automatically produces a reverse BA intraverbal relation


**See also.** `class-wide-function-transfer` — sibling propagation move: one trained relation reaching beyond what was directly taught, there across a class rather than across a direction.; `derived-relations-installation` — umbrella entry for derived/generative training designs; this is its train-one-direction-harvest-the-reverse form.; `generative-substrate-training` — sibling generativity move: both convert a small trained investment into untrained verbal behavior, here via a whole component set rather than one relation.


<a id="entry-71"></a>

### blank-occupant-obedience-slot

[#71](#entry-71) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

The script raises the question of WHO is to be obeyed, offers the operator as a candidate, then explicitly discards the question ('Is that me? ... Doesn't matter. Perhaps it's whoever you hear in the empty void your mind is'). Submission is decoupled from any specific operator and attached to whatever voice the listener hears — this recording or any future one — installing a durable obedience slot with a deliberately blank occupant. The move is overt but the generalization is covert; the listener does not notice the conditioning becoming portable and self-targeting.


**When to reach for this.** The authority slot's occupant is deliberately blanked and generalized to any present or future voice — versus ownership language (names the operator as owner), a nested authority conduit (a specified higher figure), and agentless fate-authority (no slot at all, authority relocated to impersonal fact); the tell is the explicit discarding of the operator's identity.


**Risk.** Portable, self-targeting conditioning that generalizes out-of-session to arbitrary future voices — out-of-session reach without bounding, and the consent surface cannot name its future beneficiary.


**Why it works.** Conditioning generalizes along stimulus dimensions unless discrimination training narrows it; by explicitly refusing to specify the authority's identity, the script withholds the discriminative training that would confine obedience to one operator, so any sufficiently similar cue (a voice giving instructions in this format) recruits the response. The overt framing also keeps the listener's scrutiny on the question 'obey whom' while the actual change — that the answer slot has become a variable — passes unexamined. Falsifiable: it predicts subjects trained with this move show more response to a novel operator's voice than subjects trained with a named owner, which is directly testable. [plausible; stimulus generalization vs discrimination training; misdirected attention]


**Worked examples.**

- *Obedience slot with the occupant left blank*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, deep; the operator has just been giving obedience suggestions and raises the question herself.
  - **The move.** You're obeying — but who exactly are you obeying? Is that me? Hm. Doesn't matter. Perhaps it's just whoever happens to be speaking into the empty space your mind has become. Whoever's voice is in there. That's who you obey.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator raises the obvious question — who exactly is being submitted to? — offers herself as one possibility, and then drops the question rather than answering it: it makes no difference, and the answer may simply be whatever speaker happens to be present in the listener's emptied attention. The listener notices the question being asked but not that the answer has been left as a fillable blank, so what gets installed is an obedience slot with no fixed occupant, ready for this recording and for any voice after it.


**See also.** `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both generalize past a single install to a standing rule, but the meta-rule blanks the SOURCE of suggestions by reattributing content to the listener, while the blank-occupant slot blanks the AUTHORITY figure so obedience attaches to any future voice.; `interpretive-closure-meta-command` — both leave a variable deliberately unfilled so the listener supplies it — one blanks WHO is obeyed so any voice occupies the slot, the other blanks WHAT is commanded so the listener's own interpretation generates the act.; `nested-authority-conduit` — same slot-topology genus with the occupant specified versus blanked.; `object-of-no-properties` — both empty a slot in the operator/subject relation rather than filling it: one blanks who is to be obeyed, the other strips the listener of properties that could ground refusal. Their discriminators both define themselves against ownership language, so a reader will meet them at the same fork.; `operator-authority-assertion` — directly opposed treatments of the authority slot: one asserts the operator's own present standing as the ground for compliance, the other raises the question of who is to be obeyed and deliberately blanks the answer so the slot generalizes. One entry already names the other as its contrast.


<a id="entry-1518"></a>

### borrowed-precedent-legitimacy

[#1518](#entry-1518) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: framing*

The operator elicits or narrates a real autobiographical experience in which the target state already occurred with full social sanction — remembered surgical anesthesia — and frames the present suggestion as a re-activation of that known pattern rather than a novelty. Belief becomes cheap because the precedent is verified memory: the placebo is billed as 'a capsule which follows the exact nerve pattern of the previous anesthesia' so the subject will be 'anesthetized in every area where you were anesthetized before,' and the remembered IV drip already proved that surrender to a substance and to strangers was normal, sanctioned, and even pleasant ('it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that'). The precondition is that the subject has, or can vividly claim, the prior experience — the operator elicits it first ('Have you ever been anesthetized before?'). The move can carry a covert verification gate before anything irreversible is staked on it: a graded pain test (towel clips in tender areas) so the operator proceeds only on confirmed analgesia ('If he had felt it, I wouldn't have gone ahead with the surgery').


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target state has a genuine prior occurrence in the subject's own biography that can be recalled and mapped onto the present suggestion, so conviction is imported rather than built. The tell is a specific autobiographical memory being elicited or volunteered, followed by an explicit sameness assertion — 'this feels so similar to that,' 'anesthetized in every area where you were anesthetized before' — billing the new state as recurrence, not novelty. A covert go/no-go test before relying on the borrowed state is a secondary tell.


**Worked examples.**

- *remembered surgical anesthesia lends its legitimacy to a fictional 'medicine'*
  - It took hold so fast as I babbled nonsense about being so easy to hypnotize... telling these total strangers all my secrets so readily, but it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that


**See also.** `cognitive-convincer` — same self-evidence axis: the subject's own noticed experience supplies the proof the operator would otherwise have to assert.; `fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal` — same memory-as-install-vehicle axis, run on fabricated recollections instead of verified ones.; `front-matter-reader-positioning` — shares the borrowed-legitimacy axis: an already-sanctioned precedent or lineage lets the new material arrive pre-validated.; `pseudo-orientation-in-time` — shares the recall-frame axis: content delivered as remembered rather than proposed is cheap to believe.


<a id="entry-1392"></a>

### borrowed-structural-coercion-precondition

[#1392](#entry-1392) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing · kind: container*

Rather than build leverage inside the session, the operator runs the persuasion inside a role hierarchy that already exists and that the operator did not create — an employer who mandates attendance, a chain of command, a program a court or school requires. The standing power does the compliance work before a word is spoken: refusal now costs a job or a placement, not merely social awkwardness, so the audience is captive before the frame arrives. A second effect follows from the first — because everyone present showed up, presence itself reads as partial assent, and the operator can address the room as though it had already opted in. The operator's own content never has to carry the coercive load, which is what makes the arrangement deniable.


**When to reach for this.** The leverage is BORROWED — a coercive relation that predates the encounter and that the operator did not create — so cost-of-refusal, not persuasiveness, does the compliance work. Split from `borrowed-reflex-recruitment` (440), the true structural cousin: 440 also imports something pre-existing, but every variant imports an asset whose LEGITIMACY the subject already grants (a fluent reflex, a real memory, a verified prior state, a cultural ritual, an adjacent working suggestion), and the import buys credibility or momentum. This imports an enforceable relation whose COST OF REFUSAL transfers, and buys attendance regardless of credibility. Legitimacy-transfer vs cost-of-refusal-transfer is the whole split.


**Why it works.** Two established findings do the work. First, compliance is strongly a function of the cost of refusal rather than the persuasiveness of the message — attitudes need not change for behavior to; and second, insufficient-justification effects predict the opposite of what an operator might want, since a subject who can point to an external mandate has a ready non-attitudinal explanation for their presence and is therefore LESS likely to internalize. That tension is the useful, testable part: this arrangement should reliably produce attendance and surface compliance while producing weaker private attitude change than a genuinely voluntary equivalent. Falsifiable: if mandated attendees showed the same rate of durable, post-mandate belief change as volunteers matched on baseline attitude, the account is wrong in an important way — and if they showed MORE, the insufficient-justification prediction is inverted. [established; behavioral compliance under external cost; insufficient justification / overjustification predicting weaker internalization]


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-existing mandate cited once, then presence read as assent*
  - **Setup.** Opening minutes of a session the subject attends because a standing obligation requires it — a workplace mandate, a court-ordered program, a chain of command — and which the operator neither created nor can lift.
  - **The move.** You're all on the roster for the full ninety minutes, so let's not pretend anyone's deciding whether to be here — that was decided upstairs. What's left to you is how you spend it. And since you did show up, I'm going to take that as you being ready to work, and start where people who are ready start: eyes closed, hands flat on your knees.
  - **Why it lands.** The cost of walking out is a job or a placement rather than an awkward moment, so refusal is priced out before any content is offered, and the operator's own material never has to be persuasive. Watch for compliance that arrives without the usual negotiating look — hands go flat, eyes close, and nobody asks what this is for.


<a id="entry-560"></a>

### boundary-dissolution-no-not-operator-region

[#560](#entry-560) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure · kind: container*

One sustained operation dissolves every boundary the listener could use to bound the operator's reach — sleep and hypnosis and arousal are equated, dreaming and trancing and waking are equated, the listener's subconscious is equated with the operator, and the listener's wants are equated with the operator's wants. The same boundary-erasing operation is applied across multiple INDEPENDENT axes, and because it recurs at every layer, removing any one equivalence does not restore a boundary. The cumulative payload is that no mental territory remains that the listener can point to as definitively not-operator.


**When to reach for this.** A writer reaches for this entry when one and the same boundary-erasing operation is run on axis after axis across the text: sleep, trance and arousal named as one thing; dreaming, trancing and the muzzy state after named as one thing; the operator named as the voice of the listener's own deeper mind; and what the listener wants defined as what the operator wants them to want. The observable tell is the repetition of the identical equivalence move across multiple independent axes, wired so that removing any single equivalence still restores no boundary. The cumulative payload is territorial: by the end, no mental region remains that the listener can point to as definitively not-operator.


**Risk.** Leaves no mental territory the listener can identify as not-operator, eroding the ground on which a refusal or verification could stand — channel-adjacent erosion, so high.


**Why it works.** Judging where one's own agency ends depends on a comparator that checks whether an experience matches self-generated intention; deliberately equating categories that the comparator relies on (asleep/hypnotized, my wants/your wants) removes the distinctions the check needs to run, so no region can be flagged as externally caused. Repeating the same operation across independent axes matters because a single blurred distinction can be repaired from a neighbouring intact one, whereas simultaneous blurring across axes leaves no intact reference. Falsifiable: subjects given the equivalences on one axis only should retain measurable ability to identify externally-sourced content; the claim predicts multi-axis versions degrade that discrimination substantially more. [speculative; self/other source discrimination — the comparator account is contested and the multi-axis claim is untested]


**Worked examples.**

- *No territory left that is not the operator*
  - **Setup.** Consolidation stretch late in the file; the same equivalence operation is run across four independent axes in one block.
  - **The move.** Sleep and trance and being turned on are all one thing — you've never really been able to tell them apart, and now you don't have to. Dreaming, drifting, and that muzzy half hour after you wake are all one place, and I'm in all of them. That quiet voice underneath your thoughts is mine, and always was — and what you want is simply what I want you to want, so there's nothing left in there belonging to anybody else.
  - **Why it lands.** The same move is run on axis after axis: sleep and trance and arousal are named as one thing; dreaming and trancing and the muzzy state afterwards are named as one thing; the operator is named as the voice of the listener's own deeper mind; and what the listener wants is defined as what the operator wants them to want. No single one of these is load-bearing — pull any one out and the others still leave nowhere to stand and nothing left to call one's own.


**See also.** `isolation-by-annexation` — both delete the listener's outside reference point and are the closest neighbours to each other. One erases boundaries by asserting the same equivalence across multiple independent axes so no territory reads as not-operator; the other leaves boundaries intact and captures the sources a counter-frame would draw on, relabelling them as the operator's. Equivalence versus capture is the line.; `staged-multi-anchor-erosion` — both work by plurality rather than depth: the same removal applied across several independent targets so no single repair restores the lost footing. One erases boundaries across independent axes, the other dismantles ordered cognitive anchors in sequence through a single perceptual stream. Useful contrast on whether the multiplicity is simultaneous or staged.


<a id="entry-1524"></a>

### boundary-non-return-loop-design

[#1524](#entry-1524) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The artifact's ends are deliberately not exits. Either there is no wake at all — the closing line lands on the same phrase as the opening so the tail is structurally an entry to its own head — or the wake is scripted as a continuation of the installed role ('wake slowly, My slave, life has just begun'), with no count-up, no symmetry-restoration with the opening, and no dissolution of the role-state: the listener is released from active trance but not from the role. Replay then performs mechanical work: claims of return become true on the second listen by mechanical fact, so each pass supplies confirming evidence and the listener does the iteration labor while the artifact supplies only the frame. The absence of an exit also tilts the physics of stopping — quitting requires an active choice mid-state, a higher-friction action than letting the file restart. The same non-return operates across installments: a part invokes what earlier parts installed and leaves the listener in a state a later part continues, making the series a single graph rather than a sequence of self-contained pieces.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the closure work lives at the edges of the file and across plays or parts, not inside any passage. The tell is what the boundary lacks — no wake-up, no count-up, no closure beat, a tail that seams to the head or to the next installment — paired with content that treats repetition as already-having-happened, so each replay retroactively confirms the artifact's claims.


**Worked examples.**

- *replay bootstraps the artifact's own confirming history*
  - "You come back again and again" becomes true on the second listen by mechanical fact. The script bootstraps its own history with each loop, so the equation chain (M3) and the retroactive history (M5) gain weight purely through replay, without any new content.


**See also.** `deferred-terminus-conversion` — shares the closure-withheld axis, with the release or payoff relocated outside the file's boundary to drive continuation.; `emergence-negative-space` — shares the omitted-emergence axis: the missing return ramp is itself the structural feature that dissolves the in-trance/out-of-trance boundary.; `loop-as-mechanism-no-dismount` — shares the replay axis: the looping format makes the script's own again-and-again claims self-fulfilling.


<a id="entry-1231"></a>

### bounded-failure-counterweight

[#1231](#entry-1231) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A discrete permission-to-leave-undone move that locally inverts a compulsion the surrounding script builds. After completing all reachable work, the operator points out one thing that cannot be done and walks the listener through accepting it gracefully ("what you can't do at the moment it's okay to leave it aside"), inoculating against the perfectionism-freeze / completion-overrun the same script's rehearsal installs. It is a bounded-failure counterweight embedded amid material driving the opposite compulsion.


**When to reach for this.** A therapeutic bounded-failure permission that COUNTERWEIGHTS a compulsion installed elsewhere in the same script — it narrows/limits rather than intensifies.


**Risk.** Welfare-protective — grants permission to leave work undone to counter a perfectionism drive; reversible, session-scoped, no consent surface. Positive-governance.


**Why it works.** Explicit permission to leave something undone works by removing the perfectionistic contingency — when completion is framed as all-or-nothing, a single unreachable item invalidates the whole effort and triggers abandonment, whereas a pre-authorized partial outcome keeps the effort classed as success. This is the standard behavioural-activation and relapse-prevention logic around all-or-nothing thinking, where the pre-agreed lapse is what prevents the lapse from becoming collapse. Its placement amid opposite-pushing material matters because permission granted by the same source that set the demand is credible in a way self-granted permission is not. Falsifiable: it predicts lower abandonment and lower distress at an unreachable item when the permission clause is present than when the identical script omits it. [plausible; all-or-nothing thinking and completion contingencies; abstinence-violation effect / pre-authorized lapse]


**Worked examples.**

- *One task named as fine to leave undone*
  - **Setup.** Late in a task-rehearsal sequence; listener has just completed everything reachable and dwelt on the satisfaction.
  - **The move.** Look up at the top of that window — the corner you can't get to without a ladder you don't own. That one doesn't get done today. Stay with that a second, because this part matters: you did what was in reach, and the bit that wasn't stays where it is, and it doesn't spoil any of the rest. Say it back — this one I leave. Good. Now put the cloth down and be finished.
  - **Why it lands.** The rehearsal has the listener work through a room until every reachable surface is finished and the satisfaction of finishing is dwelt on at length. Then the operator points out one part that is out of reach with the tools at hand, and holds the listener there a moment: this one does not get done today, and that is allowed — you do what is in reach and set the rest aside without it souring the rest. It is a single beat, with completion-pressure on both sides of it, and it exists to stop the same rehearsal from turning into a compulsion that cannot stop.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — both are genuine governance moves that narrow rather than extend the operator's reach, and both are surrounded by material pushing the opposite way. One affirms the standing right to stop; the other grants permission to leave a specific thing undone as a counterweight to an installed compulsion. Useful for a reader auditing which safety-shaped moves are real.; `comfort-permission` — both are welfare-facing permission moves that pre-empt a failure reading: one licenses bodily or emotional noise so it does not read as trance failure, the other licenses leaving a task undone so it does not read as personal failure. A reader looking for the permission-grant family gains from the pairing.; `engineered-failure-harvest` — opposite uses of engineered failure. One arranges a task the listener genuinely cannot pass and then cashes the failure as the target result; the other grants permission to leave one thing undone specifically to counterweight a compulsion the same material installs. The contrast clarifies both.; `granted-exit-disarm` — the sharpest available contrast on permission-giving: identical surface form, opposite answers to who ends up constrained. One supplies an assurance whose acceptance stands down protective monitoring and widens operator licence; the other is a genuine welfare permission that narrows what the script demands.


<a id="entry-1454"></a>

### calibrate-then-exploit-staircase

[#1454](#entry-1454) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

An early, low-stakes instance of the demand is executed so the listener's own body banks in-corpus proof, and later, higher-stakes instances draw on that proof instead of asking for fresh belief: the first freeze installs catalepsy as believable at mid-arousal, the second reinforces it under observation, and the edge-timed third exploits the established belief. The same topology runs at nine-rung scale in the fractionation staircase, where each accepted control surface (verbal cycles, self-induction, sliders, buttons) is held briefly then traded for the next, and the order is load-bearing: starting at step 8 would be refusable, but by step 8 with seven prior surfaces accepted, refusal feels like breaking continuity. The pivot rung is sold as maximally agentive — the forearm slider conditions body-action-to-depth precisely so the next phases can make the body act without the listener's chosen direction, 'agency stripping disguised as agency granting.' The dependency currency throughout is demonstrated prior compliance in the listener's own body, not an asserted claim.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script runs graded repetitions of the same demand-type at escalating stakes, with the early instances doing calibration work the late instances spend. The tell is that the peak demand arrives only after smaller enacted versions of itself, and is delivered as continuous with what the body already did — removing the first rung would leave the final one merely asserted.


**Worked examples.**

- *early freeze banks the proof the edge-timed freeze spends*
  - Removing freeze 1 would leave freeze 3 merely asserted; with calibration, the listener has prior in-body evidence.


**See also.** `catalepsy-to-affect-transfer` — a single demonstrated motor convincer spent as warrant for later untested claims — the one-rung version of the same spend.; `manufactured-self-confirmation` — shares the body-banked-evidence axis: prior moves manufacture the somatic proof that later claims cite.; `monotonic-ratchet-one-way-valve` — the escalation-topology neighbour: a strictly one-way ratchet with no regressible step.


<a id="entry-1425"></a>

### capacity-ceiling-overreach-inversion

[#1425](#entry-1425) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

A hazard entry. When a subject is holding a delicately counter-conditioned balance — an excitatory response trained against an inhibitory one, or an install maintained against a competing disposition — broadening the demand incrementally works right up until it does not, and the ceiling is not knowable in advance from any measurement taken before it is crossed. Past it the failure is not graceful degradation but sudden total inversion: the whole balance flips into the opposite process, and the damage propagates backward onto cues that were stable and reliable before the overreach, so previously solid installs stop working too. The absence of any warning signal is the operationally important part — performance up to the ceiling looks healthy, so an operator titrating by observed success has no leading indicator and finds the limit only by exceeding it.


**When to reach for this.** The two properties that carry it: a tolerance ceiling not measurable in advance (performance up to it looks healthy, so there is no leading indicator for an operator titrating by observed success), and RETROACTIVE spread — collapse damages cues and installs that were stable and were not under demand at the time. Against 434 shaping-successive-approximation, the sharpest neighbour: shaping's deterioration is graded, scoped to the response being trained, and explicitly recoverable by dropping back to the last successful approximation (the dip-and-recover signature is read as the procedure WORKING); here failure is abrupt, disproportionate to the final increment, inverts the balance into its opposite process, and propagates backward onto untouched material. Against 173 capacity-saturation-overload: a live reversible load applied AS an induction — lift the load and capacity returns; this crosses a training-tolerance ceiling and leaves persistent damage. Against 1239 doubt-injection-state-collapse: one running effect broken by re-arming judgment against it, damage scoped to that effect with no backward spread. Against 850 anchor-collapse-state-jamming: disorganization produced ON PURPOSE as the precondition for integration; nothing here is collapsed deliberately and there is no constructive endpoint. Against 86 irresolvable-input-confusion: a delivered vehicle with an intended effect. This is the only entry describing unintended structural collapse rather than a targeted move.


**Why it works.** The phenomenon is real and was demonstrated experimentally, not merely asserted: pushing discriminations past a subject's tolerance produces abrupt, disproportionate breakdown with disturbance of previously stable discriminations, and the finding has held up as a description of what happens under sustained conflicting demand. Its explanation is another matter. The original account in terms of protective inhibition exceeding a capacity is not mechanistically supported and should not be repeated as though it were; the modern reading — that behavior maintained by opposed processes near their limit is a system with little margin, so a small further demand produces a large state change — is a description of the dynamics rather than an identified mechanism, and no specific neural story should be asserted. Treat the ceiling as an empirical tolerance, not a measured quantity. Falsifiable at the two claims that carry operational weight: the account predicts that collapse should be abrupt and disproportionate to the size of the final increment (if degradation is instead smooth and proportional, this is ordinary over-training and the entry is redundant with existing dose guidance), and that damage should spread to discriminations that were NOT being trained at the time. If overreach reliably damaged only the discrimination under demand and left untouched cues stable, the retroactive-propagation claim — the entry's main distinguishing property — would be wrong. [established as an observed phenomenon; mechanism unidentified; experimental breakdown under discrimination overload; retroactive disturbance of stable discriminations]


**Worked examples.**

- *Widening the demand past an unmeasurable ceiling; retroactive collapse*
  - **Setup.** Hazard illustration. A response has been trained against a competing disposition and has held through several clean widenings; the operator, reading healthy performance, widens once more.
  - **The move.** You've held it with your eyes closed, and with them open, and with the room quiet. Now do it with the door open and someone else in the room — same as before, just wider.
  - **Why it lands.** Every trial up to the ceiling looked healthy, so observed success gave no leading indicator; past it the balance does not degrade gracefully but flips into its opposite process. What identifies this rather than ordinary shaping deterioration is the backward spread — the operator finds that cues which were solid and were not under demand at all have also stopped working, and dropping back to the last successful step does not restore them.


<a id="entry-926"></a>

### carrier-is-cargo-fusion

[#926](#entry-926) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: carrier-binding*

The object that carries post-session persistence is made identical to the surface behavioral ask, so there is no separable "install your trigger" step the listener could refuse without also refusing the behavior itself. In the exemplar, perfume is simultaneously a ratchet-inventory item the listener acquires AND the always-on carrier vector for persistence (a scent cue firing every breath); maintenance additionally off-loads onto other ambient always-on channels ("hello" per contact, inner voice, mirror checks). The lever is fusing the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral cargo so declining the persistence and declining the surface behavior become the same act.


**When to reach for this.** Not a magnitude/count move (more channels) but a topology fusion (carrier = cargo).


**Risk.** Removes the refusal channel for the persistence install (cannot decline the trigger without declining the surface behavior) and reaches out-of-session on always-on ambient channels — channel erosion plus unbounded out-of-session reach.


**Why it works.** The lever is choice-architecture bundling: presenting two items as one indivisible option means refusal forfeits the desired component, and loss aversion makes that trade unattractive. The scent element adds odour-based evaluative conditioning, which acquires readily and shows good long-term retention — but the claim that odour cues are habituation-free is backwards, since olfactory habituation is unusually fast and continuous exposure drops the cue out of awareness within minutes, so the cue works on re-presentation after a gap rather than sustained wear. Falsifiable: unbundling the carrier into a separately declinable step should raise refusal rates with nothing else changed. [plausible; bundled choice architecture / loss aversion; olfactory evaluative conditioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *The reminder cue hidden inside the ask itself*
  - **Setup.** The behavioral list is being handed over near the end of the session; ordinary lifestyle asks are being framed as the harmless part.
  - **The move.** So — the small everyday things. You'll buy a bottle of the vanilla perfume and you'll wear it, every day, wrists and throat, before you leave the house. And here's the other half of it: that scent is what keeps all of this alive. Every breath you take of it puts the training back in, top-up after top-up, all day long, whether you're thinking about me or not. Same with the word 'hello' — every time it leaves your mouth, and every mirror you pass.
  - **Why it lands.** The behavioural list the listener is asked to adopt includes acquiring and using a particular everyday item — and that same item is separately made the thing that reloads the conditioning, continuously, for as long as it is in use. There is no moment where an anchor is offered for acceptance on its own; to decline the always-on reminder the listener would have to decline the ordinary lifestyle instruction, which was framed as the harmless part. Other channels are loaded the same way, each hooked to something that recurs many times a day without anyone deciding to trigger it — but this one is where carrier and cargo are the same object.


**See also.** `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — both are topology moves that remove a separable refusal point: several payloads yoked to one recurring stimulus, versus the persistence carrier fused into the behaviour being asked for. Different fusions, same design goal of leaving no standalone thing to decline.; `self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop` — both engineer post-session persistence around an acquired object and can look identical on the surface. One chains cue, purchase, ritual and re-listening into a self-sustaining loop whose payload is perpetuation; the other fuses the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral ask so there is no separable install step to refuse. Loop shape versus topology fusion.; `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` — these frequently co-occur on the same always-present social cue and the same fixed-order commitment inventory, so they read as one move on first pass. One turns on fusing the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral payload so no refusable install step exists; the other turns on the cue never being named as a trigger plus a one-way self-extending ladder. Separable levers that often ride together.


<a id="entry-1527"></a>

### case-then-formalize

[#1527](#entry-1527) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

A vivid concrete case is presented first and the formal apparatus is fitted onto it afterward, so the model reads as discovered in the phenomenon rather than imposed on it. A verbatim transcript alternates with formalizing commentary that retro-fits vocabulary onto moves performed without it — a famously articulate subject "spontaneously arrives at a technique which we have formalized," making the model look like natural law — while ordinary-case replication (the Mary Lou insertion) converts "Erickson did this with a genius" into "you can do this with a 45-year-old in a training group," carrying the generalization claim. The case narrative and the meta-model commentary are arranged so each licenses the other: the vivid phenomena supply the reader's belief that something real is happening, the apparatus then claims to explain it, and once the frame is accepted for the easy case, harder cases inherit credibility by analogy. The same ordering runs in textbook form: the chapter leads with a concrete, emotionally legible payoff, and only after the reader is impressed does the text name the properties — so every abstraction has already been cashed out in a concrete win before it is asked to be believed.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the sequencing itself does the persuading: demonstration before apparatus, with the demonstration licensing the abstraction. The tell is temporal order — the reader meets the phenomenon as a story or a concrete win first, and the formal vocabulary arrives afterward as a name for something already believed, often with an ordinary-case replication carrying the generalization from exceptional exhibit to "you can do this too."


**Worked examples.**

- *demo-first ordering that licenses the apparatus*
  - so the model appears *discovered in* the master's behavior, not imposed.


**See also.** `reader-assent-architecture` — shares the stance-priming axis: the reader's acceptance of a method is arranged before the method is stated, as in its follow-and-formalize instance.; `reader-assent-engineering` — the container for reader-targeted rhetorical architecture, which pools transcript-then-formalize and ordinary-case replication among its levers.


<a id="entry-1509"></a>

### chain-interruption-evocation

[#1509](#entry-1509) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*
