A forbidden or unavowable wish is carried out by a motor act that is competently executed but aimed wrong — the object slips, the name comes out as the other name, the message goes to the wrong recipient — so the wish is fully discharged while the act arrives labelled as a failure of execution rather than a choice. Because errors are a category everyone already grants, the act needs no defence and admits no interrogation; the agent produces both the deed and the alibi in one motion, with no second party required to supply either. Scripted toward a listener, it works as a deniability primitive: an outcome is specified together with a manner of arriving at it that the listener can disown, so the compliance is real and the authorship is not claimable.


**When to reach for this.** Against subconscious-agent-authorship-offload: there authorship of a real act is reassigned to the subject's own inner agent as a NARRATED frame the operator supplies; here no narration and no second party are involved — the error itself is the concealment vehicle, and it is generated by the same agent who wanted the outcome. Against object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition: that relocates causation onto an external object declared to be doing the work; the alibi here is a category of event (a slip) rather than an agent. Against self-perpetuating-loop: that is a closed amplifying circuit; this is a single discharge with a built-in cover and no feedback. Against referent-voiding-portable-obedience: that strips an impulse's object while preserving the impulse; here the object is hit precisely and it is the AIM that is disavowed. The load-bearing tell across all four: the cover story is the malfunction, so the more competent the surrounding performance looks, the better the error reads.


**Why it works.** Responsibility attribution keys on perceived intent, and errors are the standard socially-granted exemption from intent, so routing an outcome through an error form buys the outcome at no responsibility cost to either the actor's self-concept or their standing with observers. The distinctive prediction is a rate asymmetry: errors should not be uniformly distributed across possible wrong outcomes but should over-produce outcomes the agent had reason to want, which is directly measurable. Falsifiable: tally slips against the space of available wrong outcomes and check whether wish-congruent ones are over-represented relative to phonological, motor, or proximity-based accounts of the same error. If error direction is fully explained by those mundane factors with no residual wish-congruence, the laundering account has nothing left. [plausible; intent-based responsibility attribution and the excuse value of accidents; wish-congruent error direction is contested and rarely tested against phonological baselines]


**Worked examples.**

- *Outcome specified together with a misfire that carries it*
  - **Setup.** Late in a session with a subject who has said outright that they will not ask for a particular thing directly; the task frame is already established.
  - **The move.** Tonight, when you're typing to them, you're going to reach for the delete key and your finger is going to land one over. The message goes as written, and you look at the screen afterward and see it gone. You didn't send it. Your hand did.
  - **Why it lands.** The wanted outcome is delivered in full while the act arrives pre-labelled as a slip, so the subject never has to occupy the position of having chosen it and nobody else has to grant them cover. The operator sees compliance without the usual negotiation, and hears the subject afterward report the event in the passive — the deed described, the decision absent.


<a id="entry-1526"></a>

### evidence-apparatus-credibility

[#1526](#entry-1526) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft*

The text sets the reader's trust level through its visible evidentiary and authority apparatus, before and independently of any single claim's merits. Dense per-claim citation converts persuasion claims from author's opinion into documented empirical finding, with the reader treating citation density as a proxy for truth. The notes work directly on the reading skeptic: replication is foregrounded ("done twice, with the same results"), and the accumulation of independently-cited instances functions as the argument itself — the weight of many converging sources standing in for demonstration. Dissent is staged and then settled in-house: an internal critique (Furman & Lepper) is surfaced and answered in-text, modeling a mature, self-correcting scholarly community that metabolizes objections rather than suppressing them. New principles borrow doctrinal grandeur by being routed through already-accepted ones — operant selection yoked to Darwinian natural selection and elevated as "the bedrock on which other behavioral principles rest" — so acceptance is engineered by association and authority before any specific claim is defended.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the persuasive work lives in the citation and authority layer — endnotes, bibliographies, stacked scholar names, foregrounded replications, staged-and-settled objections — rather than in demonstrations, drills, or the body argument itself. The tell is that trust is built wholesale: the apparatus underwrites every claim at once, and the reader's acceptance tracks the visible breadth and convergence of sourcing rather than the merits of any individual passage.


**Worked examples.**

- *citation density read as truth-proxy*
  - the reader treats citation density as a proxy for truth.


**See also.** `concede-then-rescue-forebear` — shares the staged-and-settled-objection axis: trust raised by conceding and disarming the reader's likely objection in-house before they can raise it.; `front-matter-reader-positioning` — both set the reader's stance toward the material before and independently of any individual claim being argued.; `reader-assent-engineering` — the container for reader-targeted whole-chapter architecture, which pools citation-density-as-truth-proxy among its credibility-regime levers.; `unifying-frame-overlay` — shares the accumulation-as-argument axis, there with converging instances accruing acceptance to an overlaid frame rather than to a cited claim.


<a id="entry-1366"></a>

### external-role-power-entry-lock

[#1366](#entry-1366) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

Two locks are set before the subject ever hears the payload, and both sit outside the influence frame itself. First, the program's actual content is withheld at the point of invitation — what is disclosed is a benign cover (training, a workshop, a seminar) that would not be refused. Second, attendance is made a condition of something the subject materially depends on, by routing the invitation through a party with real-world role power over them: an employer, a supervisor, a licensing body, a landlord. By the time the true content appears, leaving no longer costs an awkward exit; it costs the job. Departure requests are then refused or deferred against that structural cost, so the subject's continued presence — which any later consent record will cite — was never a live choice.


**When to reach for this.** Two locks, BOTH outside the influence frame, both set before the payload is heard: content withheld at invitation, and attendance made a condition of something the subject materially depends on via a third party with real-world role power (employer, supervisor, licensing body, landlord). The nondisclosure half alone is NOT this - that is `withheld-frame-reveal` (454), whose cover is cashed rhetorically inside the session with no cost attached to walking out, or the bait-and-switch member of `consent-topology-arc` (4), which is a whole-artifact consent topology inside a voluntarily consumed file. `scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame` (1345) likewise bends past what was advertised but the subject can close the tab for free. The deciding tell is that the exit cost is MATERIAL and EXTERNAL and is held by someone who is not the operator: `asymmetric-state-lock` (1292) monopolizes exit from an already-installed state via an operator release condition inside the frame; `exit-annexation` (1027) leaves the exit materially real and captures only what using it MEANS; `cross-media-forced-continuation` (697) raises continuation cost through content topology; `named-person-release-gate` (909) terminates a permission chain on an installed belief. Here nothing is installed yet, the exit's meaning is untouched, and what changed is that leaving now costs the job.


**Why it works.** Two separate effects compound. Sunk-cost and effort-justification research shows that people who cannot leave a situation without material loss tend to resolve the dissonance by revising their evaluation of the situation upward rather than by absorbing the loss — attitude follows the constrained behaviour. Separately, the compliance literature on legitimate authority shows that requests routed through an established role relationship draw far higher compliance than identical requests from a stranger, because the role, not the request's content, is what is being evaluated. Falsifiable: run the identical program with identical nondisclosure but voluntary attendance and no employment link. If uptake, stated endorsement, and refusal-to-leave rates are the same, then the structural cost is decorative and the nondisclosure alone is carrying the effect. It would also be contradicted if subjects with genuinely portable skills and easy re-employment showed the same retention as those with high exit cost — the mechanism predicts retention should track the actual cost of leaving, not merely its assertion. [established; effort justification / induced compliance; legitimate-authority compliance effects]


**Worked examples.**

- *Benign cover at invitation plus third-party role power holding the exit cost*
  - **Setup.** The invitation stage, out of session and before any payload exists — the subject's supervisor, not the operator, is the one who makes the approach.
  - **The move.** Attendance is expected for everyone on your team — it's a two-day communication workshop, and I've already put you on the list. HR is tracking who completes it, so let me know if there's a genuine conflict and we'll find you another date.
  - **Why it lands.** Both locks are set before a word of the actual content is heard and both sit outside the influence frame: the disclosed cover would not be refused, and the cost of leaving is held by an employer rather than by the operator. The operator observes departure requests deferred against a material cost rather than an awkward one, which means the continued presence any later consent record cites was never a live choice.


<a id="entry-1364"></a>

### external-tie-severance

[#1364](#entry-1364) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

Family, employment, and friendships outside the group are dismantled under sustained pressure — moves, schedule capture, prescribed cutoffs, relabeling outsiders as hostile — until the group is the only source of belonging, income, and information. Two things go at once: the triangulation channel, since no one remains who could compare the group's claims against an outside account, and the exit route, since leaving now costs everything rather than costing membership. Neither is a claim made to the subject; both are structural facts about their life, which is why the effect does not depend on the subject believing anything in particular.


**When to reach for this.** Against `isolation-by-annexation` (0.569): that leaves the relationships standing and relabels them as secretly the operator's, pre-empting the counter-frame from inside; this removes the relationships in fact — after annexation the mother still exists and could still be called, after severance she cannot. Against `environmental-dissociation` (0.553): that fades competing perceptual input inside a session and reverses on waking; this is an out-of-session structural change to the subject's life with no in-session component. Against `closed-epistemic-self-validation-loop` (0.560): that closes the evidence channel by wiring claims to self-induced states; this closes it by deleting the people who would have supplied contrary evidence. Against `no-exit-state-braid` (0.547): that welds internal state variables so no single-variable exit exists; the variables here are external and material — job, housing, kin.


**Why it works.** Belief correction depends on access to independent sources, and the cost of leaving a group is set by what one has outside it — so cutting external ties raises exit cost and removes correction at the same time without any persuasion being attempted. Falsifiable: the account predicts that restoring a single outside contact should produce measurable belief revision and raise departure rates even with all in-group content unchanged. If reconnecting former members to outside ties reliably produces no revision, the correction-access half is wrong. It further predicts that members with intact outside employment or kin leave at higher rates than matched severed members; equal rates would show that severance is a correlate of commitment rather than a cause of retention.


**Worked examples.**

- *Removing the material means of consulting an outside reference*
  - **Setup.** Months into a live arrangement, out of session, where the subject has already moved into shared housing and the operator now closes the remaining independent channels; no claim is being made about anyone's trustworthiness.
  - **The move.** Give notice at work on Monday — we'll cover you, so you won't need the income. The car goes back this week; I'll drive you where you need to go. And the phone plan comes off your name onto the house account, so you don't have to think about the bill again.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing has been asserted about the outside world and nothing relabeled — the subject can go on believing their family is entirely reasonable and still have no income, no transport, and no independently held line with which to reach them. The operator observes the erosion downstream: perception-checking stops not because it was defeated but because there is no longer a position from which to attempt it, and the group's account becomes the only reachable one.
- *Schedule capture and relocation, with no cutoff ever announced*
  - **Setup.** Out of session; a debrief or orientation frame where a recruiter describes how membership works, with the subject already attending regularly.
  - **The move.** Nobody here is going to ask you to give anyone up — that's not how we do things. What I'd suggest is you come to the Tuesday study as well as Sunday, and Thursday service prep, and we do Saturday work parties most weeks. And there's a room opening up in the house on the north side, forty minutes closer, cheaper than what you're paying. Take it and you'd have your evenings back. See how it looks in six months.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is ever framed as a demand to drop anyone: the group's calendar simply expands until no unclaimed evening remains, and a relocation puts distance in the way of the rest. The ties end by attrition, so there is no moment the subject can point to as the one they should have refused, and no instruction to disobey. The structural tells are the ones to read — whether an outside account could still be reached to check a claim, and what leaving would now cost. Both answers change long before anyone notices a decision was made.


**Realizations** (1): `material-verification-base-severance`


<a id="entry-1513"></a>

### extinction-procedure-fidelity

[#1513](#entry-1513) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering · kind: principle*

The conduct doctrine that lets a withholding program survive its own side effects. Anticipate the predictable cascade — extinction burst, response variation, increased magnitude, spontaneous recovery, resurgence, emotional and aggressive outbursts — and hold the contingency steady through it, because relenting mid-burst reinforces a now-intensified response and it is critical that extinction-produced aggression not produce reinforcement, or a worse behavior is trained to do the old job. When full withholding is unbearable for the operator, titrate tolerance stepwise: baseline the comfortable ignoring duration, then wait an additional five minutes every two days until the target is reached. Re-apply after any relapse rather than treating it as failure — decreases become increasingly rapid with each successive application, and the effect is additive when the subject can discriminate the onset of extinction; where tolerable, contrive extra evoking situations so trials accumulate faster. Maintenance then splits by intrusiveness: leave the extinction procedure in effect permanently, or fade an intrusive apparatus in small increments; and guard adjacent schedules by withholding any free, noncontingent delivery for roughly ten seconds past a just-emitted problem behavior so the reinforcer never lands on it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the material is the operating discipline around a withholding program rather than the withholding itself — how to weather the spike, when to re-run, how to pace an operator who cannot hold the line, how to keep the gain afterward. The tell is second-order instruction: the contingency is already chosen and set, and the text governs the operator's steadiness, timing, and maintenance choices across the run's predictable turbulence — anticipation of a named side-effect cascade, stepwise tolerance schedules, relapse re-runs, delivery-boundary timing guards.


**Worked examples.**

- *hold the line through the burst*
  - Applied behavior analysts need to anticipate extinction bursts and be prepared to consistently withhold the reinforcing consequence.


**See also.** `aversive-procedure-administration-envelope` — sibling run-rules envelope on the same procedure-conduct axis, wrapped around aversive contingencies instead of withholding programs.; `function-based-extinction` — the conduct doctrine for running this withholding program through its predictable side-effect cascade.


<a id="entry-1521"></a>

### faculty-reified-as-depletable-substance

[#1521](#entry-1521) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: authorship-shift*

An internal faculty — conscious control, resistance, the mind itself — is asserted, never hypothesized and with no simile, to be a finite physical substance subject to mechanics: a fluid draining out through openings at the feet, hands, and neck, or sand falling through an hourglass bound to a countdown. The grammar makes the depletion inevitable ('because if there's an opening, it just has to start draining'), so letting go is demoted from a volitional act that could fail to passive observation of physics already underway — the listener's only role is to notice. Continued resistance is framed so that exercising it spends the very quantity needed to keep resisting: a listener fighting the countdown still 'spends' sand. The reification itself removes volition — no external agent performs the change — and it often carries an operator-held reversibility gate that latches the emptied state ('There's no way to return your mind. / Until I flip the hourglass back upright.').


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when letting go must be made to feel inevitable rather than chosen — when a volitional surrender could fail or be withheld, convert it into physics the listener merely watches. The tell is a faculty named as a measurable quantity undergoing mechanical depletion (draining, falling, emptying) on the operator's schedule, stated as plain fact with no 'as if' or 'imagine,' frequently with restoration gated behind an operator action.


**Worked examples.**

- *conscious control as fluid that must drain through body openings*
  - because if there's an opening, it just has to start draining


**See also.** `dissolution-then-installation` — the whole-artifact emptying-then-writing architecture that a drain of this kind typically serves as first movement.


<a id="entry-1153"></a>

### failure-state-inversion

[#1153](#entry-1153) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

An outcome culturally coded as shameful loss of control (nocturnal emission) is explicitly named, invoking the latent shame, and re-tagged as radical, extreme success and a spiritual and sexual experience, with uncontrolled release tied to devotion. Converting the one uncontrollable release route into evidence of successful training removes the listener's escape hatch: loss of control can no longer be read as failure, and the reframe routes toward chastity and pleasure-control programs (fewer waking orgasms means more wet dreams means more success).


**When to reach for this.** Shame-invocation-then-overwrite of an uncontrollable event class, requiring latent shame for leverage; not a plain chastity rule and not generic positive reframing, the tell is that the OLD meaning is named precisely to be overwritten and the event is one the subject cannot prevent. vs response-foreclosure — that closes the subject's response space generally; this overwrites the interpretation of one involuntary event class.


**Risk.** Forecloses the failure/disconfirmation reading of an out-of-session involuntary event and ties it to devotion plus cross-sell routing toward pleasure-control programs.


**Why it works.** The reframe works through cognitive dissonance reduction: an event the person cannot prevent but has been taught to feel ashamed of creates standing discomfort, and an offered reinterpretation that removes the shame is accepted because it is cheaper than continued self-blame. It also closes the failure attribution route — once loss of control is coded as success, no outcome disconfirms the training, which is a self-sealing structure. Testable prediction: the reframe should take hold only in subjects who actually carry the prior shame, and should be inert in those who never coded the event negatively. [plausible; cognitive dissonance reduction; shame relief as reinforcement]


**Worked examples.**

- *An uncontrollable failure re-tagged as success*
  - **Setup.** Rules/reframe segment of a chastity-adjacent session; subject has an existing chastity or denial protocol and latent embarrassment about nocturnal emission.
  - **The move.** Let's name the thing you've never told anyone. You wake up in the night, sticky, and you strip the sheet before anyone sees, and you file it under something gone wrong with you. That isn't a lapse. That is the strongest result this work produces — your body finishing the devotion while you're too asleep to interfere with it. So it's simple arithmetic from here: the fewer times you touch yourself awake, the more nights you wake up like that, and every one of those mornings is a mark in your favour.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator raises the one outcome the listener cannot prevent and has always quietly filed under embarrassment — naming the old shame out loud, including the fact that it was kept private. Then she overwrites it: that is not a lapse, it is the strongest possible sign the training is taking hold, and it is bound to devotion rather than to loss of control. The listener's remaining escape hatch closes, because the event they would have read as proof of failure has been pre-assigned the opposite meaning — and the arithmetic runs the same way, since the fewer occasions there are for a waking release, the more often the re-tagged outcome occurs.


**See also.** `arousal-as-obedience-readout` — same lever on different events: an involuntary bodily signal the subject cannot switch off is re-tagged so it reads back as evidence for the operator's frame. One relabels ongoing arousal as an obedience readout; the other names a shame-coded uncontrollable release and overwrites it as success. The second additionally requires latent shame, which is the discriminating precondition.; `denial-as-will-defeat-reframe` — both convert an aversive sexual outcome into evidence the conditioning is working, and a writer building one will often want the other: one operates on sustained unrelieved arousal, the other on a single involuntary release event whose cultural shame is named in order to be overwritten. Reading the pair clarifies that the reframe target is a felt state in one case and an event class in the other.; `orgasm-gated-amnesia` — both re-tag an uncontrolled sexual release as evidence of successful conditioning. One makes the triggered climax the operator that purges prior self-content and locks the install; the other names a culturally shameful involuntary release and overwrites it as extreme success. Voluntary-triggered lock versus shame-overwrite of an unpreventable event is the discriminating axis.; `value-hierarchy-inversion` — both convert something coded as loss into something coded as gain. One reranks a worth or motivational ordering so subordination reads as an upgrade; the other names a shame-coded involuntary event precisely in order to overwrite its meaning as success. The contrast is ordering versus single-event interpretation.


<a id="entry-1443"></a>

### felt-rate-time-dilation

[#1443](#entry-1443) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: immersion*

Warps the subjective RATE of time inside the state, and the warp itself is the immersive payload — the stretched moment is the experience being sold. It can be run live as a direct expectation installed just before an edge cycle — "Every second. Passing so. So. Slowly... Is going to feel. Like hours" — so the dilation is experienced rather than merely described, amplifying the perceived intensity of the most acute moment without changing the physical act. Or it is argued into being from attentional scarcity: the mind maintains its sense of the present only by spending attention on it, arousal consumes that attention, so time slows because the mind is "too drawn to pleasure to deal with anything so boring as time" — a causal story that makes the distortion feel inevitable and self-generated rather than suggested, and from which stacked, simultaneous climaxes are then derived. Either way the subject still has a clock; it simply runs at an operator-set rate, in the lineage of time distortion installed for immersion by manipulating the felt rate of passage.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script stretches or compresses how fast time feels while keeping the listener inside the moment — seconds asserted to feel like hours, climaxes lingering or stacking on top of each other because time has slowed. The tell is rate language: time is still passing and still being felt, but at a speed the operator sets, and the warped speed itself is what the listener is there to experience.


**Worked examples.**

- *rate-warp expectation installed live at the edge*
  - Every second. Passing so. So. Slowly... Is going to feel. Like hours. Just hours. Hours and hours of deep. Agonizing. Sexual pleasure.


**See also.** `arousal-cognition-shutdown-law` — shares the attentional-scarcity premise, where arousal consuming the mind's limited attention is argued to alter cognition.; `time-as-malleable-construct-induction` — shares the time-as-plastic axis, where felt duration is first moved from background given to operator-modifiable variable.; `time-dilation-immersion` — shares the felt-time-manipulation axis, covering the broader family where time's passage or measurability is bent for immersion.


<a id="entry-1428"></a>

### fiduciary-role-capture

[#1428](#entry-1428) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

A genuinely credentialed professional — someone whose training carries a duty owed to the people in front of them — is brought inside the frame as a member, so that their loyalty to the group outranks the duty their role encodes. Their real skill is then applied to the leadership's ends against the very members the role exists to protect: procedures performed, sedation administered, professional rulings issued to serve the group's account rather than the member's interest. The capture is doubly effective because the role's own legitimacy travels with it — members read the professional's participation as evidence that what is happening is within bounds, which is exactly the inference the credential is designed to license.


**When to reach for this.** vs protective-role-conscription (1123): that assigns the LISTENER a fictional protective bystander costume inside a scene so hypnotic content lands past their self-relevance monitoring — the role is fictive, the target is the listener, and the whole thing is in-frame. Here the role is real, externally credentialed, and worn by a third party, and the inversion is of an actual duty rather than a story position. vs third-party-activation and interposed-proxy-agent (545): those delegate firing rights over an installed cue or install a fictive agent that issues commands; nothing is delegated here — a person with independent standing and independent obligations is annexed. vs peer-mediated-contingency (534): that recruits ordinary peers as reinforcers, which requires no credential and inverts no duty; the tell here is specifically that the captured party's role is the one members would appeal TO for protection. vs authority-diffusion-plurality (439): that dissolves the authority surface so there is no one to resist; this ADDS a sharply-defined authority whose legitimacy is borrowed intact. vs impersonal-mechanism-alibi (1157): the authority here is personal, named and in principle checkable against the professional's own governing body — which is also the practical countermeasure.


**Why it works.** Professional legitimacy functions as a heuristic cue: the presence of a credentialed party licenses compliance with acts that would otherwise be refused, and obedience studies show the effect survives the act being visibly harmful. Loyalty conflicts resolve toward the in-group when membership is the professional's primary social identity, which is why capture works through membership rather than through payment or coercion. Falsifiable and checkable against real cases: if members' compliance with a harmful procedure were unchanged by whether a credentialed insider was present and endorsing, the borrowed-legitimacy component is not operating; and if captured professionals' deviations from standard practice were no greater inside the group than in their outside practice, then the in-group loyalty account is wrong and the entry describes ordinary malpractice rather than a topology lever. [plausible; authority cues licensing compliance; in-group loyalty overriding role obligations]


**Worked examples.**

- *In-group physician introduced as member first, credential second*
  - **Setup.** A group session; the professional is already a committed member, and the leadership is about to ask something of members that their role would normally caution against.
  - **The move.** Before we go further — you all know her, she sits in the third row every week, she's one of us. She's also fifteen years a licensed physician. She's looked at what we're doing here and she's the one who suggested we go ahead. So if anyone's carrying a worry about whether this is safe, take it to her afterward and she'll tell you exactly what she told me.
  - **Why it lands.** Members read the credential as an independent check while the loyalty ordering — member first, professional second — has already been announced, so the check has been quietly disabled at the moment it is invoked. Observable: worries stop being raised to the leadership at all and get routed to the captured professional, and the room's objection rate drops without any objection having been answered.
- *Professional's ruling issued about a member, to the group's benefit*
  - **Setup.** A member has begun questioning the group publicly; the captured professional holds a role whose assessments members treat as neutral.
  - **The move.** I've had a look at him and I'll say this plainly, with my professional hat on: what you're seeing isn't disagreement, it's exhaustion presenting as agitation. He needs rest and quiet, not a platform. I'd ask everyone to give him some space this week.
  - **Why it lands.** The dissent is reclassified as a symptom by exactly the person members would have appealed to for protection, so the appeal route and the suppression route are the same channel. Observable: peers stop engaging the dissenter's content and start managing his wellbeing, and the substantive question never gets restated.


<a id="entry-1459"></a>

### fixation-object-role-inversion

[#1459](#entry-1459) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: attention*

After sustained fixation has banked attention on an object, the object's function is flipped mid-script while the object itself persists. A spiral established as the fixation destination is inverted into a window — 'beyond the spiral, you can see something beautiful' — becoming the frame rather than the picture, pulling attention through it into an expansive constructed space the operator can populate at will. A sparkle of light that has pinned the listener's awareness in place through a long body scan is released to float back and fall, carrying the listener down with it: the anchor that held attention horizontally becomes the vehicle of vertical descent. In both forms the fixation work is preserved as the cost of entry — accumulated focus-tension converts directly into deepening or absorption — and the listener does not notice the role-change because the same object remains present across the transition (the spiral keeps spinning while becoming a window). Requires that fixation on the object has already succeeded; the flip is the payload.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a long-held fixation object is suddenly given a new job partway through the script. The tell is the same object standing on both sides of a state transition — the spinning spiral now looked through rather than at, the held point of light now falling and taking the listener with it — with the shift carried by the object's changed role rather than by any instruction to attend to something new.


**Worked examples.**

- *fixation object repurposed as aperture into constructed space*
  - As the spiral spins, you might notice that beyond the spiral, you can see something beautiful. You could see the vast emptiness of space, but it's not truly empty. Look deeper, imagine deeper beyond the spiral.


**See also.** `fixation` — the fixation primitive is the substrate this move banks before flipping the object's function.; `scaffold-then-spend-sequencing` — shares the bank-early-spend-late shape: work invested up front is cashed by a later move that depends on it.; `staged-multi-anchor-erosion` — shares the staged-mutation axis: an established attention structure is transformed mid-stream rather than merely deepened.


<a id="entry-5"></a>

### frame-lamination-non-return

[#5](#entry-5) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The script stacks two or more narrative/procedural frames and then structurally fails to reopen the outer one(s), leaving the listener stranded in the innermost layer at exit, with a dependency-relation between layers that launders each into the next. Realized forms: a story-in-a-story where three nested layers fuse and the outer frames are abandoned so emergence wakes the listener from trance but not from the dream; a domestic-narrative envelope wrapping every hypnotic operation with no metalanguage break naming a procedure, never closing the outer frame so memory residue is narrative-not-procedural (which eases amnesia); and a three-layer ritual nesting where each layer launders the next (fantasy makes the prescription feel sacred, the prescription makes the fantasy feel like preparation, the chant acquires retroactive provenance). The lever is the topology of frames — laminating them so no line ever restores the outer reality — not any single utterance.


**When to reach for this.** The mechanism is the FAILURE-to-return / the dependency-relation between layers across the whole back half, cited only to the absence of a closing beat, never to one line.


**Risk.** Leaving the listener at exit inside an unclosed inner frame is an incomplete-emergence property; bounded delivery (host supplying a real exit/aftercare) is the mitigation, so requires_bounding is set even though no refusal channel is directly eroded.


**Why it works.** Reality monitoring depends on explicit boundary markers — entering and exiting a frame is what tags material as 'imagined' versus 'actual' — so omitting the exit marker leaves content encoded without the source tag that would quarantine it. Narrative encoding without a procedural label also means the memory retrieved later is a story that happened rather than a technique that was applied, which offers no handle for critical review. Falsifiable: compare scripts identical except for a closing frame-return; if post-session source-attribution accuracy and reported carryover are the same either way, frame closure is not doing the work. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; reality monitoring and boundary cues in narrative transportation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Nested frames that never reopen*
  - **Setup.** The emergence, at the very end; the storyteller frame and the dream frame were both dropped a third of the way in and never resumed.
  - **The move.** One, two, three — eyes open, wide awake, feeling wonderful. The voice is still there in the corner of the room, and the room is still the one from the dream, and that's all fine. Go on with your evening.
  - **Why it lands.** Layer one: the operator asks permission to tell a story. Layer two: inside the story, a dream. Layer three: inside the dream, a voice speaking. Roughly a third of the way in the three fuse and the outer two are simply dropped — no return to the storyteller, no line resetting the scene, nothing. The emergence at the end wakes the listener out of trance but never out of the dream, so the fiction is still load-bearing when the file stops. You cannot point at the line that does this; the mechanism is the closing beat that never comes.
- *Every procedure disguised as a household errand*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the arrival, the washing, and the walk downstairs have all already been narrated as ordinary household events.
  - **The move.** You sit down in the chair in the back room, and she tips your head back against the rest, and she starts to wipe. Left side first, then the right, then across. When she's done there's simply nothing on that side of the cloth anymore.
  - **Why it lands.** Arriving and washing is the induction; walking down the stairs is the deepener; the treatment in the chair is the erasure. At no point does the operator step outside the errand to announce that a deepening is about to happen — there is no line of procedural metalanguage anywhere. The outer visit never closes either: the wake-up returns the listener to their own room without ever bringing them back from the imagined house. What they remember afterwards is a place they went, not a procedure that was done to them, and you cannot recall a technique you never perceived as one.
- *Each layer lends the next its provenance*
  - **Setup.** Final section, plain real-world instruction; the middle section already had the subject speak these exact words inside an imagined ceremony.
  - **The move.** On the first night of each month, kneel where you keep the bowl, light the one candle, and say the words you already said tonight. Say them out loud. You know them — they came out of your own mouth an hour ago.
  - **Why it lands.** The middle section has the listener perform a set of spoken words inside an imagined ceremony. The final section is a plain real-world instruction: say these words, on these dates, with these objects. On its own the instruction is bureaucratic and the ceremony is a one-off scene, but stacked they launder each other — the ceremony makes the schedule feel sacred, the schedule makes the ceremony feel like preparation. The words are taught in the imagined scene precisely so that, by the time they are prescribed, they are not a text the operator wrote but something the listener already said.


**See also.** `covert-frame-entry` — complementary ends of the same frame apparatus: one crosses the entry seam invisibly under a false benign frame, the other fails to reopen the outer frame at exit so the listener is left inside. Reading both gives the entry and exit halves of frame handling.; `declarative-nested-trance-recursion` — both present as stacked layers, so the surface reads identically and the discrimination is not obvious from the text. One is a topology property of the whole arc, where outer frames are never reopened and the listener exits stranded in the innermost layer; the other stacks declared trance-within-trance layers to remove any foothold for verifying depth. Worth the cross-link because a reader looking at nested layers has to decide whether the point is depth or non-return.; `emergence-negative-space` — both are whole-arc negative-space properties about frames that never reopen; one is about nested narrative layers left unclosed, the other about the missing emergence ramp. Close enough that a reader must be told which evidence assigns to which.; `foreclosed-emergence` — both leave no route back to ordinary baseline; one by never reopening an outer narrative frame, the other by deleting the clean waking end-state from what the close makes reachable. Structurally different but constantly confusable at the exit.; `loop-hook-non-wake-close` — both weaponize the absence of a proper return at the end of a session, one by never reopening the outer narrative layers, the other by offering a wake too thin to reorient. A reader analysing a session that ends wrong needs both readings on the table, since the tell is whether the missing return is a frame or the emergence itself.; `no-emergence-series-chaining` — both leave the listener without a clean return, and a reader who has one will misfile the other. The distinction is what fails to close: an outer narrative frame that is never reopened within a single piece, versus the emergence event itself being deleted so the state is forwarded across a boundary into the next.; `operator-voice-absence`


<a id="entry-1373"></a>

### friction-as-artifact-filter

[#1373](#entry-1373) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

The operator deliberately arouses resistance around a piece of material before accepting it, on the reasoning that material which survives active friction is less likely to be an artifact of the operator's own influence. Rather than smoothing the path so the subject agrees easily, the operator pushes back, invites contradiction, states the opposing case, or withholds the confirmation the subject is angling for, and only credits what still stands afterward. The move constrains the operator rather than the subject: it deliberately raises the cost of getting a yes, and it makes an easy yes a warning sign rather than a success. Its practical form is a rule about what counts as evidence in the operator's own notes — agreement obtained without friction is provisionally discounted, and material the subject maintained against pressure is weighted up.


**When to reach for this.** The operator deliberately RAISES the cost of obtaining a yes and treats an easy yes as a warning sign, crediting only material that survived the friction. This is the inverse of rigged-verification-capture, where every branch of the check is pre-mapped to confirmation. The tell is direction of operator interest: every neighbour makes agreement cheaper to obtain, this one makes it dearer in order to learn what cheap agreement conceals.


**Why it works.** Compliance and genuine endorsement produce the same surface response under low-friction conditions, so an easy yes carries almost no information about which one occurred; adding a cost to agreeing separates them, because a subject merely going along has little reason to pay it. The filter works by raising the response threshold until demand characteristics stop being sufficient to clear it. Falsifiable and directly checkable: compare material accepted under friction with material accepted smoothly on any independent criterion — later stability, corroboration from outside the session, whether it survives a change of operator. If the friction-filtered material fares no better, the filter is costing sessions and buying nothing. There is also a real failure mode worth stating: friction selects for stubbornness as well as for accuracy, so a subject who simply digs in under pressure will pass this filter while a compliant but correct subject fails it, which means the filter reduces one artifact class at the price of introducing another. [established; demand characteristics and acquiescence in low-cost agreement; costly signalling as a separator of genuine from compliant response]


**Worked examples.**

- *Counter-case stated before the yes is accepted*
  - **Setup.** The subject has just produced a piece of material the operator would like to credit — a memory, a preference, a stated want — and is visibly angling for confirmation.
  - **The move.** Before I take that: I think you might be handing it to me because I've been leaning on it for twenty minutes and you can hear which answer I want. So here's the opposite case — that it never mattered to you and you've assembled it just now out of what I've been implying. Argue me out of it. If you can't be bothered to argue, I'm writing it down as mine, not yours.
  - **Why it lands.** Raising the cost of a yes means only material that survives friction gets credited, and an easy yes becomes a warning sign rather than a result. The operator observes the difference between a subject who holds the claim under pressure and adds detail, versus one who folds or softens — the latter marks probable operator artifact and is discounted in the notes.


<a id="entry-702"></a>

### front-end-gift-directed-obligation

[#702](#entry-702) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: compliance*

The operator renders an initial no-cost service (a free home inspection); when paid work is then offered while the obligation is live, reciprocity directs the discharge of the debt to the specific benefactor. The target both awards the business to that firm and stops comparison-shopping, so the consideration set collapses to one vendor and price scrutiny is suppressed, the actual profit mechanism.


**When to reach for this.** A front-end free service attributable to a specific firm followed by a paid offer while the debt is live; not a genuinely disinterested favor. The paired boundary condition separates it from generic gift-giving: the gift must leave a viable repayment channel, since blocking repayment reverses the effect into resentment.


**Risk.** Transaction-scoped and escapable, a target who reframes the free service as a sales tactic exits; no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** The reciprocity norm is a well-replicated obligation-generator: an unrequested gift creates a felt debt, and crucially the debt is directed at the specific giver rather than dischargeable generally. That directedness is what collapses the consideration set — comparison shopping would leave the debt outstanding. Falsifiable and already tested in the literature: if the recipient is given an alternative way to repay, or the gift is framed as an unattributable industry standard, the effect on vendor choice should vanish. [established; reciprocity norm; directed obligation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Free service directs the debt and kills comparison-shopping*
  - "most people who agree to a free home examination give the extermination job to the examining company… They apparently feel an obligation to give their business to the firm that rendered the initial, complimentary service." — Cialdini (1984), Influence


**See also.** `perpetual-obligation-ledger` — both run the reciprocity norm, but one over-repays by a labeled surplus so the ledger never reaches zero and the relationship stays open, while the other places a single front-end free service so the one live debt is discharged to a specific benefactor and comparison-shopping stops.; `reciprocity-ledger-seeding` — same reciprocity lever run at two ranges: one seeds an obligation ledger far in advance as a desirable identity, the other renders an immediate free service and collects while the debt is live. A reader identifying an obligation play benefits from seeing both the pre-seeded and the front-loaded form, and from the repayment-channel boundary condition.; `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` — two ways to manufacture a live debt that then directs its own discharge: theatrical costly effort on a predetermined outcome, versus a real no-cost service rendered before the paid offer. Real-versus-staged cost is the selection question, and both collapse the target's consideration or refusal channel the same way.


<a id="entry-1530"></a>

### front-matter-reader-positioning

[#1530](#entry-1530) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

Before any content is argued, the opening/front matter positions the reader as already inside the method's success, working on the reader's state rather than on evidence. One route names the reader's desire as already-felt: a first-person testimonial frames understanding-how-people-work as "my biggest reinforcer" and closes with the rhetorical question "How could you resist that?", so the reader's assumed enthusiasm becomes the platform on which the dry material is then laid and skeptical reading is pre-empted by consensus framing. The other route presupposes competence: the text legitimizes itself by embedding the method in a prestige lineage (Watzlawick/MRI, Haley, Minuchin, Satir) so it arrives pre-validated, and presupposes the reader already knows the basic six-step model, converting "you should learn this" into "you already have the basics, here is the advanced layer." Combined with a hit-and-miss-art-to-systematic-interventions promise, the front matter manufactures both credibility and a forward-leaning yes-disposition before a single technique or definition appears.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when an opening or front-matter posture operates by presupposing something about the reader's own state — their desire already felt, their competence already in hand — before the first claim is argued or demonstrated. The tell is posture preceding content: desire-naming testimony ("how could you resist?"), lineage-backed prestige, or presupposed familiarity doing the recruiting, with no evidence apparatus yet on the table. It is a whole-opening rhetorical strategy on the reader, not a single citable move in the body text.


**Worked examples.**

- *competence presupposed before any technique is taught*
  - pre-positions the reader as already-competent-but-incomplete


**See also.** `borrowed-precedent-legitimacy` — shares the borrowed-legitimacy axis: an already-sanctioned precedent or lineage lets the new material arrive pre-validated.; `evidence-apparatus-credibility` — both set the reader's stance toward the material before and independently of any individual claim being argued.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both lay groundwork before the payload so the later material lands on a prepared disposition rather than being evaluated cold.; `participation-drill-pedagogy` — sibling whole-text move on the audience: that one positions the reader before content arrives, this one drills the reader through it.


<a id="entry-1511"></a>

### function-based-extinction

[#1511](#entry-1511) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Identify the maintaining reinforcer via functional assessment, then arrange that the behavior no longer produces it, so the response rate declines toward its pre-reinforcement baseline. The functional read replaces the lay move of just ignoring it — the payoff may not be attention at all, and mis-targeted ignoring is the named anti-pattern. The withholding must cover every maintaining source at once, since withholding one source of reinforcement while another stays live may have minimal or no effect. Realization then follows the identified channel: for escape-maintained behavior, block the exit so the behavior cannot purchase escape — physically guiding the subject through the demand or re-presenting refused food until the aversive situation no longer terminates contingent on the response; for attention- or conflict-maintained behavior, deny the payoff by flat restatement of the contingency and disengagement, including reading resistance talk as escape behavior whose complaints are ignored while reinforcement is delivered contingent only on actual task performance. The lever throughout is removal of the maintaining contingency, not delivery of any aversive event.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a writer takes down an established behavior by first diagnosing what it earns and then making that exact payoff stop arriving. The tell is the diagnose-then-cut sequence: the text names the maintaining consequence (escape, attention, whatever the assessment reveals), then shows the behavior still occurring but no longer purchasing anything — the demand stays in place, the operator walks away, the complaint goes unanswered — with the decline attributed to the broken contingency rather than to anything delivered. The behavior is starved at its identified feeding point, not suppressed.


**Worked examples.**

- *escape payoff cut after functional identification*
  - Flo's tantrums can be placed on extinction by ensuring that the reinforcer (e.g., avoidance of the activities ...) no longer follows problem behavior (tantrums).


**See also.** `extinction-procedure-fidelity` — the conduct doctrine for running this withholding program through its predictable side-effect cascade.; `function-first-targeting` — an intervention that consumes the functional read — withholding the identified maintaining reinforcer rather than the visible form.; `noncontingent-reinforcement` — same maintaining-reinforcer axis run the other way: the reinforcer is delivered free on a clock schedule so the behavior stops purchasing it.; `reinforcement-extinction` — genus entry for the same withhold-the-maintaining-reinforcer move, spanning every reinforcer channel plus integrity and chain-structured facets.


<a id="entry-1536"></a>

### function-first-targeting

[#1536](#entry-1536) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: operator-craft · kind: principle*

Refuse the topographical read: a behavior is classified by its controlling variable and maintaining contingency, not its visible form, and the intervention is aimed there. "Two responses of the same topography can be completely different behaviors depending on the controlling variables" — saying "fire" while reading and yelling "Fire!" at smoke are different behaviors — and "the topography, or form, of a behavior often reveals little useful information about the conditions that account for it," so assessment discovers what reinforcer the behavior reliably produces (get something / escape something) and the chosen intervention has a mechanistic reason to work rather than being a guess against the symptom. The same logic extends to profiling: measure the relative strength of each component operant class and identify the functional source of control, so intervention targets the specific eroded class rather than the repertoire generically. It also runs as a fast form-based selector, where a recurring paradoxical pattern — "Anything with the form of 'The more you try to do one thing, the more you get the opposite'" — routes the case to the matching treatment model. The output in every case is a routing decision about where to aim, made before any technique is applied.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when choosing where to aim an intervention on an already-observed behavior — the practitioner is deciding what to change, not yet changing anything. The tell is a classification step that asks what maintains or controls the act (what payoff it produces, which functional class carries it, which recurring pattern-form it instantiates) while treating the act's visible shape as uninformative, followed by an intervention pointed at that controlling relation.


**Worked examples.**

- *Identical surface acts sorted into different behaviors by controlling variable*
  - two responses of the same topography can be completely different behaviors depending on the controlling variables


**See also.** `descriptive-functional-assessment` — the observational assessment procedure that discovers the maintaining function this rule says to aim at.; `function-based-extinction` — an intervention that consumes the functional read — withholding the identified maintaining reinforcer rather than the visible form.; `functional-reinforcer-rerouting` — function-over-topography axis: classifying the behavior by its maintaining contingency is the assessment step this rerouting builds on.; `preparatory-diagnostic-read` — the umbrella operator-side diagnostic-read surface whose read-discipline face this classification rule governs.


<a id="entry-1506"></a>

### functional-reinforcer-rerouting

[#1506](#entry-1506) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Start from a functional assessment that names the exact reinforcer currently maintaining the unwanted behavior; the intervention then re-plumbs that reinforcer rather than replacing it. The old channel is closed — the problem behavior goes on extinction for its own payoff, as when an escape-maintained tantrum stops earning escape — while the identical reinforcer is delivered contingent on a trained alternative, such as brief escape for handing over a BREAK card, or a communicative response that produces that same reinforcer and so supplants the problem behavior under the same motivating operation. The replacement can also be chosen topographically incompatible with the target (click for silence instead of scolding noise), so the competitor physically displaces it. Because the replacement is functionally equivalent — it 'should produce the same reinforcers that previously maintained the problem behavior' — the existing motivation is preserved and redirected, not starved. The same function map generates hard contraindications: escape-maintained behavior must never be treated with time-out or planned ignoring, because those deliver the very escape that maintains it, and attention-maintained behavior must not be met with reprimands or counseling, which deliver attention.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a functional assessment has already identified which specific payoff sustains an unwanted behavior, and the plan's whole leverage is routing that identified payoff through a sanctioned response while the old response stops earning it. The tell is the same reinforcer appearing on both sides of the design — extinction on the problem channel, contingent delivery on the trained alternative — often accompanied by function-derived contraindications ruling out interventions that would accidentally deliver the maintaining reinforcer.


**Worked examples.**

- *functionally-equivalent replacement channel for the same reinforcer*
  - The operator identifies the reinforcer maintaining the problem behavior (via functional assessment), then teaches an adaptive communicative response (sign, vocalization, device, card) that produces that *same* reinforcer.


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement` — schedule-family axis: rerouting realizes the DRA arm of differential reinforcement with the maintaining reinforcer as the payoff.; `function-first-targeting` — function-over-topography axis: classifying the behavior by its maintaining contingency is the assessment step this rerouting builds on.


<a id="entry-1405"></a>

### generalization-gradient-coupling

[#1405](#entry-1405) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

An installed cue is not an isolated point but a centre with a halo of near-miss variants that fire it. Withholding reinforcement from ONLY the halo — deliberately extinguishing the near-misses while leaving the trained centre alone — drags the centre down with them, sometimes all the way to zero. Halo and centre behave as one coupled system rather than as independent responses, so there is no clean way to narrow a cue by starving its periphery. Operationally this is a hard constraint on selective decommissioning: any attempt to trim an over-broad trigger by unreinforcing its edges risks taking out the trigger itself.


**When to reach for this.** An unengineered coupling between one cue's trained centre and its near-miss halo: extinguishing only the halo drags the centre down with it, so an over-broad trigger cannot be narrowed by starving its periphery. Against trigger-network-mutual-binding (1323) — the tell is that nothing was wired: 1323's inextinguishability is a designed topology over MULTIPLE separately-installed triggers cross-firing laterally, whereas this is a gradient property of a SINGLE cue and appears in installs that never touched a second trigger. Against discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement (306) — 306 is the procedure that DEFEATS this coupling by reinforcing the centre CONCURRENTLY while withholding at the periphery; the coupling described here holds only in the unreinforced-centre case, which is exactly the scope line between the two. Against reinforcement-extinction (432) — 432's collateral warnings concern topography substitution and un-enumerated reinforcer sources, i.e. spread across RESPONSES and reinforcer channels; this is spread across the STIMULUS dimension of one cue. Not context-generalization (1333): that widens an intact payload's firing surface deliberately; here the spread is in the extinction direction and unwanted.


**Why it works.** Presupposes that the trained response is indexed to a stimulus DIMENSION with graded strength, not to a discrete token — which is why unreinforcing points on the dimension moves the whole gradient. Falsifiable: if the centre can be held at full strength while the periphery is extinguished, given enough differential trials, then centre and halo are separable and the coupling claim fails. Directly testable against discrimination training, where exactly that separation IS achieved — so the honest scope of this entry is narrow: it holds where the periphery is unreinforced without the centre being concurrently reinforced, and predicts that adding concurrent centre reinforcement rescues it.


**Worked examples.**

- *Halo starved, centre goes with it*
  - **Setup.** A snap-cue has been installed on a specific two-finger snap and has generalized: the subject is dropping on any sharp click, including a pen and a light switch. The operator wants to narrow it.
  - **The move.** For the next two weeks, when you hear a click that isn't my snap — a pen, a switch, a door — nothing follows it. No response from me, no acknowledgement, no drop. You'll notice the near-misses stop meaning anything. [Two weeks on, with no reinforcement given to the trained snap either:] Ready? [snap]
  - **Why it lands.** Starving the near-miss halo without concurrently reinforcing the trained centre pulls the centre down with it: the two-finger snap that was reliable now produces a flicker or nothing at all. The operator observes the trigger they intended to keep, failing on its own token, and reads this as the coupling rather than as a decayed install.


<a id="entry-1546"></a>

### generative-substrate-training

[#1546](#entry-1546) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Instead of training every target response item by item, the operator installs a set of prerequisite component repertoires — echoic, tact, listener, and self-listener behaviors, or simple component skills taught to fluency rather than mere accuracy. Once the components are jointly present, new composite performances appear without further training or reinforcement: novel tacts and mands emerge incidentally, and fluent components combine without apparent instruction into complex patterns the operator never taught (factoring emerging from fluent arithmetic). The repertoire becomes generative, converting a per-item training cost into a one-time substrate cost. Two load-bearing conditions: the full prerequisite set must be jointly operative — partial substrates do not yield the incidental gain — and in the fluency variant, accuracy alone reportedly does not produce adduction. The new items must lie within the relational space the substrate spans; lessons can be designed so that teaching select concepts results in acquiring concepts that were not taught directly.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the goal is untrained capability appearing for free after an up-front investment in a component base — paying once for the substrate instead of per target. The tell is that no instruction ever touches the composite performance itself: the writer builds echoic/tact/listener components or drills simple skills to fluency, then tests for novel outputs that were never reinforced. The lever is the substrate as a whole, not any trained relation between the target stimuli.


**Worked examples.**

- *component repertoires installed, novel outputs emerge free*
  - once a child can emit echoic, tact, listener, and self-listener behaviors, new mands and tacts can be acquired incidentally with no formal training or reinforcement history


**See also.** `bidirectional-naming-transfer` — sibling generativity move: both convert a small trained investment into untrained verbal behavior, here via a whole component set rather than one relation.; `derived-relations-installation` — umbrella entry for the whole family of designs where training a subset makes an untaught repertoire emerge; this entry is its component-substrate form.; `matrix-recombinative-training` — neighboring generativity route — composite performance emerges from fluent component repertoires rather than from recombining taught combinations.; `natural-contingency-handoff` — shares the fluency lever — pushing performance past bare accuracy so downstream behavior appears or maintains without further operator support.


<a id="entry-1507"></a>

### graded-concurrent-choice-architecture

[#1507](#entry-1507) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Every option stays simultaneously live — including the problem behavior — and the operator instead rigs the relative terms of the concurrent contingencies so response allocation drifts on its own. The alternative is made to pay richer, faster, and more reliably ('maximizing the difference between rates of reinforcement obtained by the two response classes'), or engineered to cost less response effort than the target, or laid out as a signaled graded menu: completing the task earns a long high-quality break with preferred toys, appropriately asking earns a short low-quality break, and eloping still 'works' but yields a minimal degraded outcome — ten seconds, no toys, neutral blocking — each option tagged by color. Nothing is prohibited or withheld; the matching law does the suppression, since the subject allocates responding in proportion to obtained reinforcement and experiences only that the good option works better. This is the design of choice precisely when the maintaining reinforcer cannot be safely withheld, so unsafe extinction is avoided while demand requirements for the best-paying option are ramped up over time.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the unwanted behavior's payoff cannot safely or practically be cut off, or when you want suppression to arrive as free choice rather than prohibition. The tell is a set of concurrently available, deliberately tiered contingencies — differences in rate, quality, immediacy, or effort, sometimes explicitly signaled — where the unwanted response is still permitted and still pays, just worst.


**Worked examples.**

- *concurrent-schedule payoff tilting with all options left live*
  - the client allocates more responding to the alternative behavior and less responding to the problem behavior, as described by the matching law


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement` — schedule-family axis: the graded menu is the concurrent-choice arm of differential reinforcement, tuned by the matching law.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — choice-architecture axis: both steer through a menu of live options, one by tilting relative payoffs, one by binding every branch to the same outcome.


<a id="entry-1358"></a>

### graded-induction-suppression-spread

[#1358](#entry-1358) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: conditioning*

Where a set of anchors has been conditioned across an ordered dimension — positions in a row, points on a scale, a sequence of tones — suppressing ONE member does not act alone: neighbours lose strength in proportion to their distance from the suppressed locus. The nearest neighbour falls to near zero, the next to roughly half, the far end is untouched, tracing a gradient rather than a boundary. The operator move is therefore anchor selection: pick the locus whose surrounding band you want flattened, suppress only that one, and let induction do the rest of the work. Suppressing an end-of-series anchor flattens a one-sided tail; suppressing a mid-series anchor scoops a symmetric well out of the middle.


**When to reach for this.** vs trigger-network-mutual-binding: that gives an all-or-nothing web — any node recruits every other, with no metric and no falloff — whereas the payload here is precisely the distance weighting, so suppression is graded and the far members genuinely survive. vs reinforcement-extinction: extinction has no spread-to-neighbours face at all; it targets one response class and its own chain-structured facets propagate along a CHAIN (link order), not along a perceptual/spatial similarity dimension. vs staged-multi-anchor-erosion: that removes several distinct cognitive anchors one at a time in a deliberate sequence, each addressed on its own — here exactly one anchor is acted on and the others move without being touched. vs lexical-relay-semantic-lattice: that relays meaning across a semantic net; this is a strength gradient over an ordered stimulus dimension, and it suppresses rather than propagates content. Requires a pre-conditioned ordered series with real perceptual proximity between members; on an unordered anchor set there is no gradient to exploit and the move degrades to ordinary single-anchor extinction.


**Why it works.** Conditioning attaches not to a point stimulus but to a region of a stimulus dimension, so changes made at one value transfer to nearby values in proportion to their similarity — the same generalization that spreads acquisition also spreads suppression, giving a falloff curve rather than a clean edge. This predicts an ordering constraint the operator can exploit: the shape of the resulting profile depends on where in the series the suppressed anchor sits. Falsifiable: suppress a mid-series anchor and measure the immediate neighbours; if they hold their pre-suppression strength, or if all members drop equally regardless of distance, the gradient claim is wrong and the effect is either absent or an undifferentiated web. Note the specific ratios (nearest to near-zero, second to about half) are a reported profile from one ordered series, not a constant to be assumed across dimensions. [established; stimulus generalization and generalization gradients; induction across a stimulus dimension]


**Worked examples.**

- *Mid-series anchor suppressed to scoop a symmetric well*
  - **Setup.** Five touch anchors have been conditioned in order along the subject's forearm, wrist to elbow, and each reliably produces its own response; the operator wants the middle band flat and both ends intact.
  - **The move.** The third spot — the one halfway up — I'm pressing now, and it does nothing. Nothing at all, no matter how long I hold it. Feel it go flat under my thumb. Just that one.
  - **Why it lands.** Suppression at the mid-series locus spreads outward by perceptual distance rather than by any stated rule, so anchors two and four come back weak and anchors one and five test near full strength — a gradient, not a boundary. The operator confirms by walking the row afterward and observing a symmetric dip centred on the treated spot, with no instruction ever given about the neighbours.
- *End-of-series anchor suppressed to flatten a one-sided tail*
  - **Setup.** Same conditioned row of five, but the operator wants the top of the series dulled while the lower positions keep working at full strength.
  - **The move.** The last one, up at the elbow — press it yourself. It's dead. Empty. Press it again and feel how there's nothing there to find.
  - **Why it lands.** Because the suppressed locus sits at the end of the dimension, the falloff runs in only one direction: position four drops substantially, three a little, and one and two are untouched. The operator observes an asymmetric tail rather than the symmetric well produced by a mid-series choice, which is the whole reason anchor selection is the move.


<a id="entry-1436"></a>

### harm-rejection-filter

[#1436](#entry-1436) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Installs a standing, automatic protective filter: the subject's deeper mind screens incoming suggestions and silently declines any that conflicts with the subject's genuine well-being or safety — without waking, without effort, and without the subject adjudicating in the moment. Framed as pre-existing and automatic ('your deeper mind only accepts what is good for you; everything else passes through and fades') rather than as a deliberate in-the-moment choice, which is what resolves the safety/depth trade: the conscious subject is never recruited as a vigilant gatekeeper, rejection happens below awareness as silent non-uptake, and compliance with everything inside the boundary is undisturbed. The filter is general and content-blind — it names no specific forbidden items; it keys on conflict with well-being, so it covers suggestions nobody thought to negotiate.


**When to reach for this.** The genuine article that a whole neighborhood of subversions counterfeits — reach for it when a REAL standing rejection faculty is installed or affirmed with the subject as the protected party. named-safety-belief-purge is its direct inverse, locating the internal safety faculty and deleting, rerouting, or co-opting it; weaponized-transparency-inoculation inverts it into a single-channel filter admitting only the operator; weaponized-safety-framing wears the safety surface while the safety element itself carries the payload; pre-armored-safety-ratchet locks the safety VERDICT against downward revision, where a real filter keeps revising; anti-stuck-filter is the local per-suggestion caveat where this is the general standing screen; and beneficiary-target-filter runs the same admissibility test on the operator's side before installation. The tell: rejection authority stays with the subject's own deeper mind, and the filter's output is silent non-uptake, not distress, debate, or emergence.


**Risk.** Protective by construction; the field-level hazard is false assurance — a stated filter is a suggestion, not a guarantee, the corpus's attested safety-net language is overwhelmingly subversion, and a filter's claimed presence must never license payloads that would not be run without it.


**Why it works.** Delegating rejection to the deeper mind resolves the safety/depth trade: vigilant conscious monitoring is incompatible with absorption and raises anxiety, while a rejection process framed as automatic and already-existing costs no attention and generates no reactance — it asks the subject to do nothing, only confirms something presented as already true. There is a real substrate underneath: hypnotic subjects reliably fail to take suggestions that conflict with strong values, so the install is partly a truthful description that raises the salience and felt permission of an existing capacity rather than building one from nothing. Falsifiable: subjects with an installed filter should show unchanged uptake of benign suggestions but increased silent non-uptake (without emergence or distress) of value-conflicting test suggestions, relative to no-filter controls. [plausible; suggestion non-uptake under value conflict; monitoring disrupts absorption; describing a capacity raises its availability]


**Worked examples.**

- *Installing the filter before deepening*
  - **Setup.** Early in the session, before any payload; delivered as descriptive fact rather than a rule being made.
  - **The move.** And here's something you don't have to think about, because it's already true: your deeper mind is careful. It takes what's good for you and lets everything else drift past like noise. You never have to check, you never have to guard — anything that doesn't serve you simply doesn't land, and you can go as deep as you like knowing that.
  - **Why it lands.** The is-already-true framing asks nothing of the subject, so the line deepens rather than interrupts; 'you never have to guard' retires conscious vigilance, which is what actually buys the extra depth.
- *The filter as answer to a voiced worry*
  - **Setup.** Pre-talk; the subject has asked what happens if a suggestion is wrong for them.
  - **The move.** Then it won't take, and it won't be a struggle either. If anything I say doesn't fit you, your deeper mind just declines it — quietly, on its own, even while the rest of you stays exactly this relaxed. It's not a door you hold shut; it's a filter that was always there.
