**Why it works.** The barrier at a stall is usually the act of saying rather than the content itself, since uttering a thing makes one its author in a way that assenting to another's utterance does not — so relocating the utterance to the operator removes the specific cost that was blocking while leaving the information transfer intact. Assent is cheaper than production for the same proposition, and that gap is the whole lever. Falsifiable: compare stalls closed by operator completion against stalls met with silent waiting. If disclosure rates are equal, the completion is buying nothing over patience. The contamination claim needs its own and harder test, because it determines whether this move is usable at all: seed deliberately incorrect completions at stall points and measure the acceptance rate. If subjects reliably reject wrong completions, the risk is manageable; if wrong completions are accepted at a substantial rate — which is what the suggestibility of the stall moment predicts — then anything obtained this way is a joint construction and must not be treated as the subject's own report. Until that rate is known, output from this move should be labelled operator-contaminated by default. [plausible; the asymmetry between producing and assenting to a statement; suggestibility of leading and completed prompts, where the contaminating effect of supplied content on subsequent report is well documented.]


**Worked examples.**

- *Operator speaks the stalled remainder; subject left only to assent or correct*
  - **Setup.** The subject is mid-sentence on loaded material of their own, has stopped dead, and is not going to finish it.
  - **The move.** You wanted him to notice you were gone. That's the end of the sentence — I'll say it so you don't have to. Nod if that's it, or tell me which word I got wrong.
  - **Why it lands.** The threshold drops from producing the words to not objecting to them, which is materially cheaper, and the disclosure enters the record jointly authored. The intrinsic cost is contamination: an accepted true completion and an accepted false one look identical in the moment, so the operator marks it as operator-supplied and re-tests it later from a different angle.


<a id="entry-1416"></a>

### operator-receptive-suspension

[#1416](#entry-1416) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

A design-time discipline on the operator's own attention rather than on anything transmitted: while the subject produces material, the operator deliberately suspends judgement, forms no expectation about what should come next, and makes no effort to fix anything in memory — holding an even, unselective attentional posture across everything heard. Suppressing selection is the point: any expectation about what matters causes the operator to attend to confirming material and skip the rest, so the material that would have contradicted the working hypothesis never reaches them. Refusing to consolidate deliberately keeps the operator's read revisable, because a note taken now is a commitment that shapes what is heard for the rest of the session.


**When to reach for this.** The manipulated variable is the operator's own RECEPTIVE state in the moment — suspend judgement, form no expectation, fix nothing in memory, hold even unselective attention — so the material that would contradict the working hypothesis still reaches the operator. vs operator-delivery-craft (1280), the only other in-session operator-side entry: its object is what the operator TRANSMITS (tone, manner, gesture, intonation, texture); here output is unchanged and intake is the disciplined thing. vs measurement-confound-mitigation (500), the nearest data-validity move: that protects validity by ARRANGING observation (spread across times, settings, caretakers; repeat until reactivity decays) — a sampling design; this protects it by refusing to filter within a single live sample. vs preparatory-diagnostic-read (840): that runs a probe to extract a datum; here nothing is probed and no datum is targeted. vs operator-training-via-monitor (758): offline craft correction against a stand-in, not a live posture. vs defusion-observer-stance (1191): same surface posture but performed ON the subject as a technique; here the subject is not instructed at all.


**Why it works.** An observer who holds a hypothesis preferentially notices and encodes hypothesis-consistent material, so the record they end the session with is biased toward what they expected before it started; withholding selection and premature encoding is a countermeasure against that, at the cost of recall volume. Falsifiable: have operators run the same session material under an expectation-forming instruction and under a suspend-and-do-not-fix instruction, then score what each reports afterward against a full transcript. If the two groups' reports omit the same proportion of hypothesis-contradicting material, the discipline is buying nothing; if the suspension group's recall is simply worse across the board with no shift in what is preferentially lost, the account fails. [established; confirmation bias in hypothesis-driven observation; expectancy effects on encoding and recall]


**Worked examples.**

- *Even unselective intake while the subject free-reports*
  - **Setup.** Subject is in a settled trance and has been asked to say whatever arrives; operator has a working hypothesis about what the material is about and is about to reach for a notepad.
  - **The move.** Take as long as you like between things. You don't have to make them connect, and you don't have to finish one before the next arrives — just say them in the order they come.
  - **Why it lands.** The instruction to the subject is minimal; the actual work is that the operator sets the pen down, forms no prediction about the next item, and lets each one land at equal weight. What the operator observes is their own pull toward the third or fourth item that fits the hypothesis — noticing that pull is the signal that selection has resumed, and the corrective is to return to unweighted listening rather than to note anything.


<a id="entry-1393"></a>

### operator-side-affect-depersonalization

[#1393](#entry-1393) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft · kind: principle*

A discipline the operator runs on themselves, not on the subject. When the subject's intense affect lands on the operator — devotion, fury, erotic fixation, dependency — the operator deliberately recodes it from a personal event addressed to them as a person into an impersonal and largely predictable product of the situation, something the role would have generated in whoever occupied it. Removing the personal stake removes both failure modes: the operator neither ruptures the frame by defending themselves nor reciprocates and collapses the asymmetry the work depends on. The re-attribution is held privately and changes nothing the subject hears; its whole output is the operator's own stability under pressure. It is a stance, so it must be rehearsed before it is needed — it does not arrive on demand mid-scene.


**When to reach for this.** Every nearest neighbour relocates causation in the SUBJECT'S model in order to act on the subject; this relocates causation in the OPERATOR'S model in order to act on the operator. `impersonal-mechanism-alibi` tells the subject their change was caused by an unfalsifiable impersonal source so doubt becomes a category error — subject-facing, and its purpose is disarming the subject. `causal-attribution-to-external-agent` names an external non-consumed cause so the subject's volition has nothing to push against — again the payload lands in the subject. `object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition` and `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` both offload authorship to somewhere other than the operator, but the erosion of ownership is the subject's. Direction of application is the whole discriminator: nothing the subject perceives changes here. Its true siblings are the operator-side governance entries — it sits alongside operator-craft's delivery and diagnostic faces, differing from those in that it regulates the operator's AFFECT rather than their knowledge, materials, or delivery.


**Why it works.** Cognitive reappraisal — reinterpreting the meaning of an emotional stimulus before the response fully deploys — is one of the best-supported emotion-regulation strategies, and it reliably outperforms expressive suppression on both physiological cost and downstream performance, because suppression leaves the appraisal intact and merely hides the output. Recoding a subject's pull as role-generated rather than person-directed is an antecedent-focused reappraisal of exactly this type, which is why it predicts lower operator strain than gritted-teeth composure. Falsifiable: if operators trained in this reappraisal showed the same rate of frame-breaks and the same physiological load as operators told simply to suppress their reaction, the reappraisal account collapses into ordinary self-control; and if the effect held equally when the operator privately believed the affect WAS personally addressed, the depersonalizing content is inert. [established; cognitive reappraisal vs expressive suppression in emotion regulation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Silent role-attribution rehearsed before the session, run when devotion lands*
  - **Setup.** The operator practises this alone, ahead of time; it fires mid-scene the moment a subject's declaration of love, fury, or fixation lands on them personally. Nothing in the delivery changes.
  - **The move.** (held silently, while the outward line continues unchanged) This is the chair talking, not me. Anyone sitting where I am sitting, saying what I just said, would be getting this exact sentence right now. It is a product of the position, it is on schedule, and it is not addressed to me.
  - **Why it lands.** Stripping the personal stake removes both the defensive flinch that would rupture the frame and the pull to reciprocate that would flatten the asymmetry the work runs on. The subject perceives nothing new; the operator observes their own voice staying level, no pause before the next line, and no urge to answer the declaration.


<a id="entry-578"></a>

### operator-side-design-gating

[#578](#entry-578) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

A planner-facing go/no-go coherence check performed on the intervention DESIGN before deployment: the operator maps in advance which baseline relations will be taught and which derived relations must logically emerge, and detects arrangements where the baselines underdetermine the derived relations. If the planner cannot specify the derived relations the training should yield, transformation of function is unpredictable and the protocol is unsound — so the enumeration itself becomes a diagnostic that gates whether the protocol runs.


**When to reach for this.** Positive governance nonetheless: the operator's license is narrowed and the action blocked.


**Risk.** A design-soundness gate that blocks shipping an incoherent protocol; operator-constraining, no subject-facing risk.


**Why it works.** Derived relations only emerge when the trained baselines logically entail them; if the planner cannot enumerate what should emerge, that is usually because the baseline set does not in fact determine it, and any function transfer observed would be unattributable to the training. The enumeration is therefore a cheap proxy for design underdetermination — an author who cannot state the predicted outcome has not specified a testable protocol at all. Falsifiable: if protocols whose derived relations cannot be pre-specified nevertheless produce the intended transfer at the same rate as fully specified ones, the diagnostic is worthless. [plausible; derived relational responding; predictive specification as a design test]


**Worked examples.**

- *If you cannot name what should emerge, do not run it*
  - "applied relational interventions are pointless if one cannot specify the derived relations that training is expected to yield" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side governance gates that narrow the operator's own license rather than acting on the subject, and both hold independently of the subject's consent or request. One gates on design coherence, the other on foreseen downstream fallout; a reader classifying a self-imposed hold needs the pair.; `depth-verification-gate` — two positive-governance gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, differing in gated object: one refuses to act until the subject's state is independently verified, the other refuses to deploy until the design's derived relations can be specified in advance. A writer selecting a pre-action gate benefits from seeing both.; `design-time-reconnaissance` — both are planner-facing pre-deployment checks on the design with nothing delivered to the subject: one exhaustively enumerates the space the plan must survive, the other tests whether the planned baselines actually determine the intended emergent relations and blocks the protocol if not. Enumeration and the go/no-go gate it feeds are naturally read together.; `suitability-screening` — both discriminators already name each other as the contrast case: one gates the design, the other gates the person, and both are positive-governance moves that narrow the operator's license. The boundary is genuinely confusable at classification time, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.; `target-selection` — both are planner-facing filters with nothing enacted on the subject, and they sit at consecutive design steps worth reading together: one chooses which behavior the intervention aims at, the other checks whether the chosen protocol's stated baselines determine the relations it should yield and blocks the run if not.


<a id="entry-1374"></a>

### out-of-band-corroboration-confrontation

[#1374](#entry-1374) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: operator-craft*

The operator leaves the dyad, obtains an account of the disputed matter from an independent third party who has no stake in the subject's self-presentation, then returns and confronts the subject with the discrepancy between the two records. Because the operator now holds a version of the facts the subject did not author and cannot revise, the subject's editorial control over the factual record is broken and the usual repair moves — vagueness, qualification, gradual restatement — stop working. The confrontation typically forces an explicit retraction, and the retraction is itself the diagnostic payload: the point at which the account was defended hardest marks where concealment was operating. The lever is the out-of-band evidence channel, not the confrontation manner, which can be gentle.


**When to reach for this.** The evidence is gathered OUTSIDE the session from a party the subject does not control, and is used adversarially against the subject's own account. staged-external-reality-corroboration also reaches outside the session but manufactures perceptible events to convince the SUBJECT of a fiction — here real testimony is collected to disconfirm the subject, and nothing is staged. rigged-verification-capture pre-loads the subject's own introspective check so every outcome confirms; this runs no check inside the subject at all — the check happens elsewhere, with a party the rigging cannot reach. disconfirmation-suppression is the exact inverse operation on the same information environment: it blocks a disconfirming fact from reaching the subject to protect a running belief, where this imports one deliberately to collapse an account. withdrawn-doubt-open-loop implies an unnamed defect and withdraws so the subject elaborates the doubt themselves; here the defect is named, specified, and backed by an external record, so there is nothing left to elaborate — the loop closes rather than compounds.


**Why it works.** An account defended in private is cheap to maintain because the only auditor is the person maintaining it; introducing a record the subject neither produced nor can revise removes that monopoly, and the cost of continuing to defend rises sharply once a second source is in the room. The retraction is informative for a separate reason: effortful defense is not distributed randomly across a narrative, so the locations where it concentrates carry information about what the subject is protecting. Falsifiable: if subjects retracted at the same rate and at the same points when confronted with a discrepancy the operator merely asserted (no actual third party consulted) as when a real independent account was produced, then the out-of-band sourcing is decorative and the effect is ordinary confrontation pressure. Equally, if the retraction points were uncorrelated with independently established concealment, the diagnostic claim fails. Note this move also generates false retractions under pressure, so a retraction is evidence about defense intensity, not about truth. [plausible; third-party corroboration and its effect on account revision; social pressure to retract under evidence; known false-confession risk under confrontational questioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Independent account collected outside the session, then the discrepancy laid down*
  - **Setup.** The subject has given a shifting account of a disputed episode; between sessions the operator has spoken with a third party who was present and has no stake in the subject's self-presentation.
  - **The move.** I spoke to the person who drove you home that night. Her account and yours don't match on one point: she says you'd already made the call before you got in the car, and you've told me twice it was after. I'm not angry and I'm not building a case — I just can't work from a version I know isn't the one that happened. Which of those is true?
  - **Why it lands.** Because the operator holds a record the subject did not author and cannot revise, vagueness and gradual restatement stop working and an explicit retraction is usually forced. The retraction is the diagnostic payload — the point defended hardest marks where concealment was operating — and the manner can stay gentle, since the lever is the out-of-band channel rather than pressure.


<a id="entry-1419"></a>

### outcome-step-unblocking

[#1419](#entry-1419) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

When a payoff is already fully predicted by an existing cue, a newly-introduced second cue learns nothing — the existing cue leaves no unexplained outcome for the new one to attach to. The repair is to raise the payoff magnitude at exactly the moment the new cue is introduced, so the outcome now exceeds what the established cue predicts and the surplus is available for the newcomer. What matters is the STEP between the old level and the new one, not the absolute size of the payoff: a uniformly large reward that was always this large blocks just as completely, and a modest reward that has just been increased unblocks. Once the new cue has absorbed the surplus, the payoff can be returned to its prior level.


**When to reach for this.** None of the neighbours model the headroom this depends on, and none is a repair procedure for a stacking failure. vs disconfirmation-suppression: an operator guard that hides a contradicting fact to protect a running belief — here nothing is hidden and the operator deliberately changes a real quantity. vs replay-until-ready-failure-absorber: absorbs failure by redefining success so repetition is licensed; that is precisely the wrong response to blocking, since repeating a blocked pairing at constant payoff teaches nothing no matter how many times it runs. vs ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet: a monotonic commitment ladder that escalates without a payoff step and is never named as a cue; here the escalation is in outcome magnitude and its timing relative to a cue's introduction is the entire lever. vs pattern-interrupt: a one-shot disruption of a running pattern with immediate gap-filling — surface similarity in that both exploit a violated prediction, but that violates a sequence expectation to open a receptive moment, while this violates a magnitude expectation to create learnable surplus for a specific cue. Pairs with over-expectation-cue-drain as its opposite failure: too much summed expectation drains cues, too little surplus blocks them.


**Why it works.** If cues compete for a finite amount of unexplained outcome, a fully-predicted outcome leaves nothing to compete for and a new cue stays inert — so the way to make a redundant cue learnable is to manufacture unexplained outcome by moving the outcome, not by repeating the pairing. Falsifiable: run three conditions — new cue added at constant payoff, new cue added with a payoff step up, and new cue added at a payoff that was always at the higher level. If the always-large condition unblocks as well as the stepped one, the critical variable is absolute magnitude rather than the change, and the entry's central claim is wrong; if the constant-payoff condition learns as well as the stepped one, blocking is not occurring here at all. [established; blocking and unblocking-by-outcome-change in the Rescorla-Wagner framework]


**Worked examples.**

- *Payoff stepped up at the moment the new cue is introduced*
  - **Setup.** A hand-on-shoulder cue already fully predicts the reward; a new spoken word has been paired with the same reward several times and has learned nothing.
  - **The move.** New word today — 'settle'. Settle. [pause] And this time it isn't the usual praise, it's the long one you get at the end of a whole session, right now, for one word.
  - **Why it lands.** Raising the reward magnitude at the exact moment the new cue appears creates surplus the established cue does not predict, and the newcomer absorbs it. The step is the lever, not the size — a reward that was always this large would block identically. Test by firing 'settle' alone a session later; once it carries, the reward can be returned to its ordinary level.


<a id="entry-1362"></a>

### outward-reproach-inversion-rule

[#1362](#entry-1362) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

The operator installs a standing interpretive rule rather than a one-off reading: every complaint the subject makes about someone else is returned as a statement about the subject. The direction of the accusation is inverted mechanically, without regard to whether the outward charge was accurate, on the stipulated premise that a reproach aimed outward is the audible half of one aimed inward. Because the rule is general, it applies before any particular grievance is examined, so the subject's whole channel for external criticism becomes a channel for producing self-directed material — and complaining about the rule is itself a complaint, and gets the same treatment.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is a STANDING, content-neutral directional inversion: every outward-aimed reproach is returned as inward-aimed, applied before the outward charge is examined and regardless of its accuracy, with objections to the rule receiving the same treatment. Against 245 self-sealing-counter-input-closure — the nearest neighbour and the one to check first — that is also a self-applying standing meta-rule, but it VOIDS competing input (pre-classified wrong-by-definition, routed into the existing erasure, never evaluated); this one EVALUATES nothing either but PRODUCES from the input, converting the subject's channel for external criticism into a generator of self-directed material. 245 closes a channel; this repurposes one, which is why it yields content rather than silence. Against 125 old-self-discreditation: that names and disavows a specific prior self so the return path closes; this names no self and is forward-standing over whatever arrives. Against 104 evaluative-reframe-content-relabel: that holds the referent fixed and moves its valence; this holds the valence and reverses the referent's direction (them -> you). Against 1339 obedience-motive-reattribution: that reassigns the motive of acts to the operator; this reassigns the target of an accusation back onto the speaker.


**Why it works.** A standing rule applied before inspection removes the case-by-case test that would otherwise let some complaints stand, so its reach comes from being general rather than from being right in any instance — and its self-application to objections is what makes it hard to exit rather than any evidence for it. Falsifiable: apply the rule to a set of complaints where the outward charge is independently verifiable and some are true; if the subject accepts the inversion at the same rate for verified-true complaints as for unverifiable ones, the uptake is driven by the rule's form and not its accuracy, as claimed. Conversely, if subjects reliably reject the inversion on verifiable complaints while accepting it elsewhere, the rule is not standing but case-sensitive and the entry overstates its reach.


**Worked examples.**

- *Standing content-neutral inversion, self-applying to objections*
  - **Setup.** Early in an arrangement, installed as a rule before any particular grievance has been raised, so it is in force whenever the subject next complains about anyone.
  - **The move.** Here is how we handle complaints from now on. Anything you say about someone else, you are saying about yourself — I will hear it that way every time, before I've even considered whether they did it. If she's cold, you're cold. And if you tell me this rule is unfair, then what you've just told me is that you are unfair.
  - **Why it lands.** Because the inversion is applied before the outward charge is examined and without regard to its accuracy, the subject's entire channel for external criticism is repurposed into a generator of self-directed material rather than closed off. The operator observes complaints continuing to arrive — that is the point, the rule yields content rather than silence — and observes objections to the rule feeding themselves back into it.


<a id="entry-1418"></a>

### over-expectation-cue-drain

[#1418](#entry-1418) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

Two cues that have each been separately trained to a strong response are presented together on the same payoff. Because their expectations sum, the combined prediction now overshoots what the payoff can actually deliver, and the trial — despite being fully reinforced — registers as a shortfall. Both cues are decremented, so a compounding intended to make the pairing stronger instead weakens each cue, and the loss distributes across them so that reinforcing the pair drains one onto the other. The operator sees a trigger that used to fire cleanly degrade after being stacked with another strong trigger onto the same reward.


**When to reach for this.** This contradicts, rather than extends, the accumulation assumption in its nearest neighbour. vs progressive-conditioning: that installs a belief that effect compounds monotonically with every return and firing, no ceiling and no decay — this names the exact regime where a reinforced trial DECREASES response strength, and predicts that stacking two saturated cues onto one payload is the reliable way to hit it. vs within-session-conditioning-loop: massed fire-and-reward inside a session, which assumes each cycle adds; here the failure appears only when summed expectation crosses the payoff ceiling, so the same massed drilling produces loss instead of gain. vs bidirectional-reentry-loop: a two-cue topology, but the two cues there cue each other and the point is inextinguishability; here the two cues meet on a shared payoff and the point is mutual degradation. vs replay-until-ready-failure-absorber: rewrites what counts as success to license repetition; that frame would actively mask this failure, since the degradation would be read as on-track. The entry's value is as a named failure mode with a stacking precondition, not as a move an operator would want to perform.


**Why it works.** When learning is driven by the gap between predicted and actual outcome rather than by mere co-occurrence, a summed prediction exceeding the actual outcome yields a negative gap, and a negative gap subtracts from every cue present regardless of whether the outcome was delivered — so 'reinforced' and 'strengthening' come apart. Falsifiable and directly testable: train two cues separately to asymptote, then compound them on the unchanged outcome for several trials, then test each alone. If neither cue's individual response strength has dropped, the summation account is wrong for this material; if the drop appears even when the compound's summed expectation is well below the outcome ceiling, then something other than over-expectation is causing it. [established; Rescorla-Wagner prediction-error learning and the over-expectation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Two saturated triggers stacked onto one payoff*
  - **Setup.** A snap and a spoken keyword have each been separately conditioned to a strong drop response; the operator, wanting a bigger drop, fires both together onto the usual single reward.
  - **The move.** Both at once this time. [snap] Sink. — Good. That's exactly right, that's the same good as always.
  - **Why it lands.** The two summed expectations overshoot what the single reward can deliver, so a fully reinforced trial registers as a shortfall and both cues are decremented. The operator's observable is the next solo trial: the snap that used to drop the subject cleanly now produces a slower, shallower response, and so does the keyword. Recognising this is the value — the correct read is stop stacking, not drill harder.


<a id="entry-1475"></a>

### ownership-generalization-to-anyone

[#1475](#entry-1475) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: persistence*

Body-ownership is de-individuated by bare chant repetition: a short sequence flips 'my body' to 'his body' to 'everyone's body', repeated in close succession with no argument or justification — assertion by chant. The pronoun 'his' appears without an antecedent, so no specific proprietor is installed; the body becomes a public/shared object before any particular person is named, and the unfilled slot broadens to whoever the listener is thinking about. The payload is removal of the 'this body is mine to consent for' frame itself: future body-directed commands need no addressee and no belonging relation, because the body is pre-assigned to anyone. The move is parasitic on already-active sensory attention to the body — it lands inside a touching-myself state set up two lines earlier — and does heavy structural lifting in only a few lines of script.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the belonging relation over the body is being deleted rather than assigned — the standing to consent is removed with nothing installed in its place. The tell is a proprietor slot left deliberately generic or unfilled ('his', 'everyone's') and bare repetition standing in for any argument.


**Worked examples.**

- *antecedent-free chant deletes the consent-owner slot*
  - My body is his body. My body is everyone's body. My body is everyone's body. My body is everyone's body.


**See also.** `autonomy-baseline-recapture` — both operate downstream of an already-landed body-ownership claim, redistributing what follows from it.; `refusal-satiation-redirect` — both flip a chanted phrase's meaning through a small in-cadence textual mutation rather than by argument.; `third-party-activation` — shares the axis of control or access rights extended beyond the original operator to other parties.


<a id="entry-1427"></a>

### parallel-isomorph-bind-defusion

[#1427](#entry-1427) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

Against a forced either/or, the operator does not argue either branch. Instead they present a structurally identical binary drawn from a domain where the listener already accepts that both terms hold at once and neither excludes the other, and let the mapping stand without asserting the conclusion. The listener carries the co-necessity across themselves, and the exclusive 'or' in the original dilemma reads as a mistake in the framing rather than a fact about the world. Because the parallel case is one the listener will not dispute and the operator never states the target conclusion, there is no proposition to reject — the dilemma dissolves as the listener's own inference.


**When to reach for this.** The taxonomy is heavily stocked with bind CONSTRUCTION and carries no bind DISSOLUTION move; this is the inverse operation on the same object. vs no-lose-double-bind (269): that builds a choice whose every branch confirms the operator's frame; here an existing exclusive choice is shown not to be a choice at all, and no branch is loaded. vs engineered-deadlock-resolved-by-surrender (744): that amplifies both poles until paralysis and sells surrender as the only exit; this collapses the opposition so there is no deadlock to escape, and no agency is handed over. vs exhaustive-either-or-compliance-probe (659): that inserts resolvable binaries to harvest low-stakes compliance and habituate an accept-any-answer frame; here exactly one binary is in play and the output is its dissolution, not compliance. vs antagonist-split-resistance-routing (249): that routes the listener's affect onto a losing self; nothing is routed here and no self is split. vs pacing-leading (1282): pacing borrows the truth of accepted statements to carry a LEAD somewhere new; this borrows the STRUCTURE of an accepted case to defuse a dilemma in place, and there is no destination.


**Why it works.** Whether two properties read as mutually exclusive is a feature of how a case is represented, not of the properties, and analogical transfer moves relational structure between domains more readily than it moves content — a source case the listener already accepts supplies the relation 'both, and neither excludes the other' and the target inherits it. Self-generated conclusions also resist counter-argument better than supplied ones, which is why the operator's silence at the end is load-bearing rather than coy. Falsifiable: the defusion should depend on structural correspondence, not on the parallel case being merely agreeable — an equally acceptable but structurally NON-parallel case should fail to shift the listener's reading of the dilemma. If any pleasant undisputed example worked as well as a genuine isomorph, this is rapport or mood, not analogical mapping. [plausible; structure-mapping in analogical transfer; self-generated conclusions resist counter-argument]


**Worked examples.**

- *Everyday co-necessity case offered flat, conclusion left unspoken*
  - **Setup.** Mid-conversation, subject has stated the dilemma out loud — "either I'm actually into this or I'm just being agreeable" — and is waiting for you to pick a side.
  - **The move.** Okay. Tell me something first — when you're driving somewhere you chose to go, are you steering the car or is the car carrying you? Both, obviously; the steering only does anything because the engine's already running, and the engine only goes somewhere because you're steering. That's all I wanted. Say the rest of yours out loud again if you still want to.
  - **Why it lands.** The parallel is one nobody argues with, and the operator never says "so you can be both into it and agreeable" — the subject completes the mapping unprompted, which means there is no claim on the table to push back against. Watch for the pause before they re-state the dilemma: they typically restate it with the "or" softened to "and", or drop it entirely and change subject, which is the dissolution rather than a concession.


**See also.** `pseudo-syllogistic-necessity` — both let a borrowed logical structure carry the conclusion so the listener experiences it as reasoned-to rather than told.


<a id="entry-1529"></a>

### participation-drill-pedagogy

[#1529](#entry-1529) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

The reader or student is made to produce answers and be corrected against a fixed key, so vocabulary and screening rules install through rehearsal rather than through evaluation of the claims. One form is Socratic build-out: the author poses a step, lets participants give a plausible-but-wrong answer, then exposes why it fails — reinforced by live inductions on resisting students, so the audience watches the move land on someone who didn't intend to be a subject. Extended into a drill, roughly ten near-identical public failure-correction cycles hold difficulty constant while content varies wildly, so the discrimination generalizes across contexts — and by the third or fourth correction the reader predicts the rejection before it lands, which is the actual installation of the skill. In textbook form the same shift runs through recognition-grid multiple-choice items with section back-pointers, re-presenting every key term as a fact-to-be-matched rather than a claim-to-be-evaluated, and through novel-vignette items that test whether stimulus control of the reader's own verbal behavior has transferred beyond the taught examples. Across all of it the right answer is fixed and locatable, moving the reader's relationship to the material from evaluation to retrieval.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the text makes its audience perform — volunteering candidate answers, classifying vignettes, taking recognition quizzes — and scores that performance against a fixed, locatable key. The tell is participation plus correction: the reader is producing and being graded rather than weighing claims, and mastery surfaces as predicting the correct answer before it is given.


**Worked examples.**

- *serial public failure-correction drill*
  - You may not learn to build parts, but you're going to learn what a function is by the time you leave here!


**See also.** `conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating` — both sharpen a discrimination through reinforced correction trials where the right answer is fixed by the arrangement.; `front-matter-reader-positioning` — sibling whole-text move on the audience: that one positions the reader before content arrives, this one drills the reader through it.; `rule-governed-behavior-install` — shares the axis of how a repertoire installs — stated verbal rule versus contingency-shaped rehearsal.; `unifying-frame-overlay` — sibling book-scale pedagogy strategy: where this entry retrains the reader's classifying lens, that one installs vocabulary through drilled participation.


<a id="entry-1441"></a>

### partitioned-trigger-control-surface

[#1441](#entry-1441) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

Several triggers are installed in one campaign, each bound to a distinct, non-interchangeable function: a re-entry cue that recalls the trance-plus-transformed state, a state-arrest cue that drops and freezes the listener motionless, an identity-tag the listener calls themselves, and a scoped command-mode that strips refusal on subsequent commands until an explicit terminator cue ("Do what you want Barbie") closes it. The partition is the technique — the listener emerges with several handles attached to different facets of the installed state, addressable independently, so the operator holds a structured remote-control vocabulary rather than a single cue-response pair. The surface can extend beyond the live session: some cues are declared invocable by unspecified third parties, by voice or by email. Each trigger may also be installed at the peak of its own phenomenological rehearsal, so the cue fires an already-demonstrated experience rather than summoning a cold one, and side-effects like a post-freeze pronoun ban give the operator a verifiable tell that the install landed.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when one campaign deliberately installs multiple non-interchangeable triggers as a control vocabulary. The tell is a trigger inventory where each cue maps to a different function — re-entry, freeze, identity-tag, scoped command-mode — with explicit terminators or scope limits on at least some cues, and possibly channels (third parties, writing) that extend invocation beyond the operator's live voice.


**Worked examples.**

- *one trigger per function*
  - The triggers do separable jobs: one is for state-recall (drop + transform), one is for state-arrest (drop + freeze), one is for identity-tagging (the name to call yourself).


**See also.** `command-token-substate-toggle` — shares the substate-toggle axis, where paired tokens move the listener between distinct in-trance configurations.; `multi-handle-trigger-architecture` — shares the multi-handle control-surface axis, whose partitioned sub-form this entry realizes as a full campaign.; `volition-override-failsafe` — shares the second-order scoped-command axis, where one cue strips the refusal gate on subsequent commands until a terminator closes it.


<a id="entry-836"></a>

### parts-work-procedure-craft

[#836](#entry-836) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Operator-side craft for RUNNING an internal-parts negotiation or reframing procedure -- shaping the procedure's structure, tractability, and completeness, orthogonal to whatever content the parts are led toward. Realizations: (a) SLACK MANUFACTURE — in a stuck two-party (parts) conflict, manufacture tradeable currency so bargaining becomes structurally possible: confirm that interference runs both ways (each party blocks something the other wants, so a mutual non-interference swap becomes purchasable, doubling as a model-selection gate), or pre-load count-balanced non-essential throwaway items so concessions cost nothing real -- either way a slack-free deadlock gains give-and-take room; (b) SPOKESPART SERIALIZATION — convene all present parts, have them elect a single spokespart, instruct the rest to hold, then poll one at a time (naming/tracking each by voice, pausing/reconvening) so a many-party negotiation is serialized into single turns bounded by the operator's working memory instead of collapsing into simultaneous noise; (c) SUBSTITUTE EXISTING BEHAVIOR — a procedural compression of the six-step reframing model: rather than generating three new behaviors, treat the parts' existing behaviors as already-adequate and slot in a substitute existing behavior/anchor, making the only new element the renegotiation of mutual non-interference (nothing removed, so resistance drops); (d) BOTH-POLES REFRAME — for a sequential polarity (crash-diet and binge; up and down) whose halves are opposite in content but identical in form (both obsessions, both loss-of-control), reframe BOTH poles rather than only the presenting one, so the other cannot rebound ('Now is my chance!') -- a completeness/relapse guard. The shared lever is engineering the parts/reframing PROCEDURE itself.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for parts-work-procedure-craft when the writer is RUNNING an internal-parts negotiation or reframe and needs to make the procedure workable/complete -- operates on the negotiation/reframe STRUCTURE, not on any party's state or the substantive reframing content. Tells: costless/symmetric tradeable currency created for a deadlock (a); turn-taking discipline elect/hold/poll/name-by-voice (b); reuse an existing behavior to compress the six-step model (c); reframe both poles of a same-form polarity as a relapse guard (d).


**Risk.** Session-scoped negotiation-frame design between parts; no consent surface touched.


**Why it works.** Working-memory limits are the binding constraint on multi-party negotiation, which is why serializing turns and naming each voice works — an operator tracking four simultaneous streams exceeds capacity and loses the thread, while polled single turns stay within it. The slack-manufacture and substitute-existing-behavior moves exploit loss aversion and the endowment effect: a proposal framed as removing something a party currently has is resisted disproportionately to its objective value, so restructuring the deal so nothing is surrendered removes the resistance without changing the substance. Both-poles reframing follows from the observation that oppositely-valenced behaviours sharing a functional class are maintained by the same contingency, so treating one leaves the reinforcer available to the other. Falsifiable: if serialized and unserialized sessions completed equally often, or if removal-framed and substitution-framed identical deals were accepted at equal rates, the craft would be inert. [plausible; working-memory capacity limits; loss aversion / endowment effect; functional response class]


**Worked examples.**

- *Balanced throwaways loaded in to create room*
  - "items which are not essential, which are 'throwaways' for the purpose of barter. I've got to have an equal amount of those on both sides… I've got to create room to move first." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Confirm interference runs both ways, then trade*
  - "both parts want something from the other, and all you've got to do is make a trade." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (3): `both-poles-reframe`, `spokespart-serialization`, `substitute-existing-behavior`


**See also.** `cheap-reversible-trial-frame` — both unstick a blocked negotiation without conceding the substantive content, so a practitioner facing a deadlock benefits from both; the difference is where the give comes from — one manufactures tradeable currency and turn discipline between internal parties, the other lowers the price of a single assent by making the commitment explicitly temporary and reversible.; `operator-resource-generation` — both are operator-side craft rather than subject-state moves, but one structures the running of a parts negotiation or reframe while the other disciplines how the intervention's content and tactics are sourced before anything fires.; `parts-work-positive-intent-elicitation` — both are operator-side craft for running an internal-parts procedure, and the second explicitly excludes elicitation content while the first supplies it. A practitioner running a parts negotiation needs both: what to ask a part, and how to keep the negotiation tractable and complete. Genuinely complementary rather than overlapping.


<a id="entry-1449"></a>

### payload-loaded-wake

[#1449](#entry-1449) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: emergence*

The emergence ramp executes — a real count-up or wake exchange runs and the listener genuinely surfaces — but the ramp is subverted into a delivery vehicle for the install rather than its discharge. Attested forms: install lines interleaved inside the ascending count itself ("Still, deeply poison. / Deeply addicted." between counts 2 and 3, with "Do something to please me now, treasure" issued as the terminal line, making the installation the last loud signal and a fresh waking-state command the session's end); the trigger fired as the final words at the wake-cue ("One. Two. Three. Up. Safeties off.") with no reorientation or aftercare, leaving a residual trigger-active state to bleed into post-session life; and a wake that names itself porous (a content warning stating it is light enough that reloop and fractionation are possible), sealing the identity tag "pulse addicts" as the last word heard, pre-loading dreams as a continuation surface, and framing the return to ordinary life as the operator's between-session interval rather than termination. In every form, what crosses the trance boundary with the waking listener is payload.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a wake genuinely runs — the count-up completes, the listener surfaces or confirms being awake — yet the loudest final signals are install content. The tells: suggestion lines nested between the ascending numbers, a trigger phrase or identity tag as the file's literal last words, and continuation surfaces (dreams, the next session, a fresh waking-state command) loaded during or immediately after the ascent, so reorientation happens carrying the payload with it.


**Worked examples.**

- *the wake seals the install instead of discharging it*
  - The wake doesn't extract the install. It seals the install as persistent into post-listen state and pre-loads dream-state as continuation surface.


**See also.** `emergence-negative-space` — the far end of the emergence-design axis, where the ramp is omitted entirely instead of executed and subverted.; `emergence-reinduction-seed` — the forward-pointing use of the same window: the count laced to seed the next session's re-entry rather than to seal this session's install.; `subverted-emergence-state-hold` — the neighboring subverted-exit design where the wake state itself is altered — foggy or awake-but-tranced — rather than a real surfacing whose content is install.


<a id="entry-1376"></a>

### peripheral-first-inhibition-spread

[#1376](#entry-1376) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

An unwanted response is removed by never working on it directly. The operator trains non-reinforced discrimination at cues maximally distant from the target along a similarity or spatial dimension, then moves stepwise inward — nearer neighbours, then nearer still — and lets the accumulated inhibition spread to the target, which is treated last or not at all. The ordering is the whole technique: because the defended cue is never contacted while it is still defended, the subject has no occasion to mount the protection that direct extinction work would trigger, and by the time the sequence arrives the target sits inside a field of neighbours that already fail to produce the response.


**When to reach for this.** The operator's activity is concentrated on the target cue's NEIGHBOURS and the target is worked last or never, with suppression arriving by generalization along the similarity dimension. Against counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening (1032), which is the same dimension traversed the other way: its graded-exposure facet APPROACHES the eliciting stimulus under an incompatible state and its sub-threshold-property-fade works a property of the target cue itself — both contact the target, this retreats from it. Against reinforcement-extinction (432), which requires every maintaining source to be enumerated and cut AT the target: here the target's contingency is never touched. Against antecedent-manipulation (1052), which removes the cue so the occasion stops arising: here the target cue remains fully available throughout. The falsifying test is the tell — stop the sequence before reaching the target and probe it; if responding is unchanged, no spread occurred and there is no technique.


**Why it works.** Non-reinforced training at one point on a stimulus dimension does not stay local — inhibition generalizes along that dimension with a gradient, so treating neighbours deposits suppression that reaches the untreated target in proportion to its similarity to what was treated. Ordering from remote to near matters because it lets the gradient accumulate before the defended point is approached, rather than provoking whatever protection direct contact would. Falsifiable, and the test is sharp: run the sequence but stop before reaching the target, then probe the target. If target responding is unchanged, no spread occurred and every gain was local to the treated cues — the entry's central claim is dead. Conversely, if remote-first and near-first orderings produce identical target outcomes, the spatial ORDERING is not load-bearing and this collapses into ordinary generalized extinction. Both results are informative and both are cheap to obtain. [established; generalization gradients of conditioned inhibition in classical conditioning. Pavlov's own irradiation account of WHY it spreads is a superseded physiological theory and should not be cited as the mechanism — the gradient phenomenon survives the theory that explained it.]


**Worked examples.**

- *Outward-in ladder: distant neighbours worked, the defended cue untouched*
  - **Setup.** The subject flinches hard at one specific cue — a hand at the back of the neck — and has defended it every time it was approached directly. The operator opens at the far end of the same dimension.
  - **The move.** Today I'm not going anywhere near your neck. Give me your left forearm — two fingers resting there, and nothing happens, and you notice nothing happens. Now the inside of the elbow: same thing, nothing. Now the top of the shoulder. Nothing there either. That's where we stop for today.
  - **Why it lands.** The defended cue is never contacted while still defended, so the subject has no occasion to mount the protection direct work would trigger; inhibition accumulates at the neighbours and generalises inward along the similarity dimension. The falsifying probe is the tell — halt the sequence short of the target and test it; if responding is unchanged, no spread occurred and there is no technique.


<a id="entry-1386"></a>

### phase-gated-suppressor-timing

[#1386](#entry-1386) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

The after-effect of a delayed conditioned reflex can alter the response to a succeeding positive stimulus according to whether inhibition remains isolated or excitation has emerged. In Pavlov's animal experiments, a metronome associated with a three-minute delayed reflex was presented for only its early inhibitory portion, then a previously measured positive tactile or visual stimulus was tested. In one dog the ensuing reflexes were diminished; the excitatory phase did not emerge during a two-minute interval after the metronome's isolated action. In another dog, with the same interval, excitation did emerge and the succeeding positive reflex was augmented, which Pavlov attributed to summation. The measured change is in the later positive test response under the host reflex's after-effect. Preserve phase isolation, individual differences, and the direction of that influence; the probe is not an inhibitory command acting on the host.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting principle when distinguishing inhibitory after-effects from excitatory summation in the response to a later positive stimulus, with the preceding delayed reflex's phase isolation explicitly considered. Forward pairing or cue-order rules concern acquisition or predecessor selection; this account concerns an already established delayed reflex and its effect on a later test response. Opposed-state fusion binds opposed effects in a script and is not the reported procedure. Timing is relevant to the phase account, but the cited contrast is between two dogs under the same interval, not an interval sweep proving sign reversal in one fixed cue-and-animal pair. A breathing rhythm is not evidence of these conditioned phases, and a stop request is not the positive probe used here.


**Why it works.** The report gives a 60–70% reduction of positive tactile and visual reflexes in the first dog after the metronome's inhibitory phase, and an increased positive effect in a second dog. Pavlov relates this difference to effective separation of the inhibitory and excitatory phases in the first dog versus earlier, stronger excitation and incomplete separation in the second. Under the same two-minute interval, the first dog showed no emergence of the excitatory phase while the second did. The source also emphasizes variability across dogs. This supports a historical account of phase-dependent after-effects and summation, not a universal timing-only sign law, a guaranteed crossing point in an interval sweep, or the claim that a mistimed human interrupt strengthens what it is intended to stop. It provides no breath-timed stop procedure.


**Worked examples.**

- *A later positive test response under different delayed-reflex after-effects*
  - **Setup.** A reader is comparing two dogs in Pavlov's delayed-reflex report. After the early portion of a delayed metronome reflex, a positive stimulus from another sensory modality is used to test the after-effect.
  - **The move.** Draw two timelines with the same two-minute interval. For the first dog, mark that excitation did not emerge during the interval and that the later positive reflex was diminished. For the second, mark the emergence of excitation and the increased later positive effect attributed to summation.
  - **Why it lands.** This authored diagram instruction illustrates the reported comparison without inventing a human intervention. It holds the interval constant across the two dogs and makes the phase difference explicit. The dependent observation is the positive test response; the example does not reverse the causal direction into a suppressing probe controlling its host, infer the phases from breathing, or prescribe when to deliver a stop cue.


<a id="entry-1476"></a>

### pluralistic-ignorance-freeze

[#1476](#entry-1476) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: social-topology · kind: principle*

In an ambiguous emergency among co-present strangers, each bystander reads the calm non-response of the others as evidence that nothing is wrong, and so stays calm too — every onlooker mutually pacifying every other, each person's inaction becoming proof to the next, recursively. No operator is required and no model performs any act; the crowd's mutual monitoring alone generates the suppression, so a crowd produces less help than a lone witness would. The freeze is experienced as a calibrated read of the situation, not as paralysis: a witness explains he 'did not investigate because no one else seemed to be paying attention.' It requires genuine ambiguity, multiple co-present observers who are strangers, and visibility of one another's (non)response. As a lever it is exploited by suppressing cues that anyone is responding; as a defense it is broken by singling out one person.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when passivity emerges from a crowd mutually reading its own non-response in an ambiguous situation — nobody demonstrates anything, and the suppression is self-generating among peers. The tell is the inversion: more witnesses yielding less action, with each witness reporting their inaction as a reasonable inference from everyone else's calm.


**Worked examples.**

- *crowd non-response read as proof of no-emergency*
  - not investigate because no one else seemed to be paying attention.


**See also.** `self-sealing-feedback-loop` — shares the closed evidence-loop structure in which each participant's state is read as proof of the others'.; `self-validating-language` — shares the axis of present-moment behavior being recycled as evidence about what is really happening.


<a id="entry-1480"></a>

### polarity-response-utilization

[#1480](#entry-1480) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

With a subject whose reflex is to contradict whatever is offered, the operator states the negation of the desired action as doubt — 'I don't think it would be possible for you… to come up here and work in front of this entire group' — and the contradicting reflex fires the wanted behavior in rebellion. The same move runs in reverse on the subject's own negative position: instead of reassuring, the operator agrees emphatically and amplifies past the subject's own claim ('you must be beyond help… lock yourself in the closet'), and the subject flips to argue the opposite — her own competence — which was the goal. Resistance is not defeated or converted; it succeeds, and is merely aimed by the operator's choice of what to oppose. Because the subject experiences self-driven defiance ('I'm not that bad; come on… let's just get on with it'), the resulting motivation is self-authored rather than imposed. It requires a reliably polarity-responding subject read correctly in advance — on a compliant subject the stated negation is simply obeyed, and an amplified agreement taken at face value can do harm.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the subject reliably takes the other side of anything offered and you want that reflex to do the work — the outcome should arrive as the subject's own defiance. The tell is an operator voicing the opposite of the actual goal, as doubt in the subject's ability or as emphatic over-agreement with the subject's negative self-assessment, and then letting the flip supply the behavior.


**Worked examples.**

- *stated doubt fires the contradiction reflex*
  - I don't think it would be possible for you… to come up here and work in front of this entire group.


**See also.** `commanded-autonomic-conviction-bind` — both are Erickson demonstrations that explicitly invite the subject's resistance and put it to work for the operator's outcome.; `response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure` — both arrange in advance that the listener's oppositional responses route into the target behavior.; `trojan-goal-contract` — both state an ask that is the opposite of the intended outcome so that pursuing it delivers the operator's goal.


<a id="entry-1401"></a>

### post-episode-cue-mapping

[#1401](#entry-1401) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

After an automatic reaction has fired and passed, the subject writes down what immediately preceded it — the word, the tone, the setting, the body state — building over several episodes a log from which the actual firing cue can be read off. An opaque 'it just happens to me' converts into a named antecedent, and a named antecedent is something the subject can see coming, prepare for, or arrange not to encounter. Nothing is installed and the response itself is untouched; what changes is that the subject now holds the cue-response map that the installing party held. This is the audit step that install-concealment moves exist specifically to prevent, and it works retroactively on triggers whose install the subject cannot remember, because it reads the cue off the behavior rather than off the memory of being given it.


**When to reach for this.** Against internal-event-keyed-trigger, declarative-trigger-installation and implementation-intention: all three INSTALL a cue-response pair; this one discovers an existing pair the subject did not author, and installs nothing. The direction is the tell — those write the map, this reads it. Against fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal: that manufactures a rehearsal history to make a response feel native; this recovers a real antecedent to make a response feel foreign. Against self-observation-instrumentation: that engineers the contingency so a subject's self-COUNT of a behavior's score is truthful, and its object is the behavior's rate; here nothing is reinforced, no count is verified, and the object is the antecedent rather than the score. Within safety it is the family's first discovery move — the existing entries supply exits, bounds, checkpoints and screening, all of which presuppose you already know what you are bounding.


**Why it works.** A conditioned response fires faster than introspection can catch its antecedent, so real-time self-report of 'what set that off' is unreliable — but the antecedent is recoverable across episodes because it is the element that recurs while everything else varies, which is why the log needs several entries and a single one proves nothing. Written-at-the-time recording also sidesteps the reconstructive drift that retrospective recall introduces. Falsifiable: compare cue identification from contemporaneous multi-episode logs against a subject's confident from-memory nomination of their own trigger. If the two agreed at the same rate, the logging discipline adds nothing over just asking. It further predicts logs converge on a cue faster the more the surrounding context varies between episodes — if a subject logging in one fixed setting identified the cue as readily, the recurrence mechanism is not what is doing the work. [established; ecological momentary assessment vs retrospective recall; functional antecedent analysis]


**Worked examples.**

- *Antecedent log kept across episodes, cue read off the behavior*
  - **Setup.** The subject has an automatic reaction they describe as arriving out of nowhere; this is given after one has fired and fully passed, not during.
  - **The move.** Next time it happens, once it has passed, write down four things and only four: the last words you heard, whose voice, where you were standing, and what your hands were doing. Don't interpret any of it. Do that for the next five times it fires, then bring me the five and we'll read them side by side for what repeats.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is installed and the response is untouched; the subject simply acquires the cue-response map the installing party held, which works retroactively even where the install itself is unremembered because the cue is read off behavior rather than off memory. Observable: by the fourth or fifth entry the subject names the antecedent themselves, and "it just happens to me" is replaced by a specific word, tone, or setting they can now see coming.


<a id="entry-1365"></a>

### pre-pairing-exposure-immunization

[#1365](#entry-1365) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

Repeated unpaired exposure to a cue before it is paired with an outcome can reduce subsequent evaluative conditioning relative to a cue without that exposure history. The relevant operation is pre-exposure before acquisition, not weakening an already established cue association. The cited meta-analysis distinguishes cue-only trials before, during, and after pairing: before and after trials were associated with reduced evaluative-conditioning magnitude, while intermixed trials during acquisition showed a different pattern. Two possible writing applications remain hypotheses: participant-side familiarization with a prospective cue, and author-side reserving a cue until its meaningful introduction. Neither application establishes durable immunity, a fixed maximum installable response, or a prescribed exposure count.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting principle for unpaired cue exposure BEFORE the relevant acquisition phase. Cue-only presentations AFTER an association has been established concern extinction or weakening and are not inherently inert. A semantically neutral carrier that is already paired with a response and reward, as in 1325's practice variant, is not the same procedure: neutral meaning does not imply consequence-free exposure. Habituation concerns change in an elicited response with repetition, while this entry concerns how prior unpaired exposure relates to later acquisition. Prior ordinary responses to a cue do not by themselves determine whether the specific association under discussion has been acquired.


**Why it works.** The cited evaluative-conditioning meta-analysis reports reduced EC magnitude when CS-only trials occur before acquisition (latent inhibition) or after CS–US pairing (extinction), and distinguishes these from CS-only trials intermixed during acquisition. This supports keeping exposure timing explicit. It does not establish the entry's former claim that post-pairing exposure is inert, a guaranteed lower ultimate ceiling, or a hundred-times-daily protection method for human script cues. Attentional or learned-irrelevance accounts may explain pre-exposure effects, but they remain explanatory accounts rather than direct evidence for those proposed writing applications. Any claim about persistence across delays or contexts requires evidence specific to that arrangement.


**Worked examples.**

- *Subject-side immunization: pre-spending a cue's conditionability*
  - **Setup.** A hypothetical familiarization example before a particular cue-outcome association has been introduced; no protection or conditioning ceiling is assumed.
  - **The move.** The character repeatedly encounters the same word in ordinary, unpaired contexts before it acquires a special role in the story. Treat the possible effect of that history as a question, not as an instruction promising immunity.
  - **Why it lands.** This illustrates the temporal difference between prior unpaired exposure and later pairing. The cited review supports a pre-exposure effect on evaluative-conditioning magnitude in its evidence base, but does not supply this human script scenario, a fixed daily dose, or proof that the word can never acquire a strong response. A source-grounded comparison would retain the exposure history and avoid inventing a measured flattened asymptote.
- *Operator-side sequencing constraint: never spend a cue on ambient use*
  - **Setup.** At the writing stage, an author compares a cue used incidentally in the opening with a cue first introduced at its meaningful moment.
  - **The move.** Mark the cue's first appearance and any earlier unpaired uses. If reserving it for the meaningful passage, record that as a design choice and a hypothesis about exposure history, not as a guarantee of a stronger install.
  - **Why it lands.** The author-side variant preserves the useful sequencing question: has this cue already appeared without its intended association? It does not claim that all earlier ordinary usage spends a fixed store of conditionability or that later cue-only exposure is inert. The cited review explicitly treats post-pairing CS-only trials as capable of reducing evaluative conditioning.


<a id="entry-1554"></a>

### presupposed-conditioning-fire

[#1554](#entry-1554) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

No binding act occurs: the operator names a specific word — "automatically" — and declares it already burned into the subconscious, so the assertion itself functions as the install and installation reads as discovery. The evidence offered is the listener's own just-trained reflex: "doesn't it feel like it's burned into your subconscious already? ... Because it is," a bootstrap in which the proof of the trigger is the response the proof itself elicits. Because the alleged conditioning is dated to the past, the claim is unfalsifiable — the listener's recent felt compliance is retroactively presented as confirmation that the trigger already existed, and any current sensation counts as further proof. The result is a discrete conditioned response keyed to one word ("a trigger for you to say yes and automatically obey when you hear that word from your dominant"), converted from a generic compliance gradient without any visible act of creation.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator asserts a trigger ALREADY exists rather than performing any installation in view, and invites the listener to discover it as a pre-existing fact. The tell is a rhetorical question pointing at the listener's own present sensation as evidence, immediately ratified by flat operator confirmation ("Because it is") — the felt response the session just manufactured is recycled as proof of prior conditioning, leaving nothing the listener could check or refuse.


**Worked examples.**

- *self-confirming assertion-as-install bootstrap*
  - that word, automatically, doesn't it feel like it's burned into your subconscious already? / Mm-hmm. / Because it is.


**See also.** `arousal-cognition-shutdown-law` — shares the install-as-discovery grammar: the assertion is delivered as a report of wiring that already exists rather than as a suggestion.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both let a just-manufactured experience stand as the evidence for a claim delivered afterward, so the claim reads as description rather than assertion.; `self-validating-trigger-hype` — both close the disconfirmation exit so that whatever the listener feels reads back as proof the claim is true.


<a id="entry-1485"></a>

### presupposition-install

[#1485](#entry-1485) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

The target proposition is placed in a grammatically presupposed position, so that parsing the sentence for meaning forces its acceptance: a relative clause ("the chair that you will soon find yourself comfortably sitting in"), a factive complement — predicates like realize, aware, recognize presuppose their complements true ("aware that you are deeply in trance"; "Are you aware that you are sitting on my hat?") — an adverb ("Are you deeply in trance?" presupposes in trance), or a predicate that lexically entails prior occurrence ("keep on listening" presupposes the listening has been happening; keep, continue, still all backdate compliance so there is no decision point at which to refuse). Because the claim is never asserted on the surface, there is no assertion to refuse: even answering "no" to the foreground question concedes the embedded content, and challenging the surface leaves the presupposition untouched. Stacking several presuppositions compounds the difficulty of challenge. The move needs a subject who is processing the sentence for meaning rather than auditing each clause's truth, and an embedded claim they are not already actively contesting.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a claim would draw refusal if stated outright and you want it accepted as settled background instead — including framing compliance as already underway so refusal has no decision point. The tell is that the contested content never occupies the main clause: it hides inside relative clauses, factive complements, adverbs, or keep/continue/still predicates, while the foreground offers something else — a question, a timing or sub-choice — to engage with. It works identically in print and speech, needing no prosody and no second reading.


**Worked examples.**

- *compounded presuppositions leaving no surface assertion to refuse*
  - Erickson compounds the presuppositions, making it very difficult for the client to challenge the truth of the statement you are in trance


**See also.** `backdated-nonrefusable-install` — both backdate the operative event to a moment the listener cannot revisit or contest.; `indirect-command-smuggling` — both are Erickson covert-delivery grammar in which the surface form differs from the recoverable payload.; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — both deliver the target as already-settled fact so no live decision point exists at which to refuse.


<a id="entry-1470"></a>

### pretend-frame-belief-decoupling

[#1470](#entry-1470) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

Performance is licensed without belief or commitment: the operator explicitly grants that imagining, considering, or pretending a behavior is not the same as doing or believing it, so the blocking assumption "consider = must do" or "respond = must believe" dissolves and the listener can simulate freely. The skeptical listener who would otherwise bail at "I'm not actually feeling hypnotized" keeps producing the observable behavior — eye-close, eye-open, playing along with the game — which is the only input the loop needs. The frame is one-directional: the operator narrates pretense becoming real ("eventually I'm wondering how the feelings will shift and change in your body"), never real becoming pretense, so the exit ramp quietly disappears while the license stands. The same valve can run with polarity flipped — "Pretend to be awake / At least pretend for me" — reusing pretense as the compliance channel in the opposite direction. The move works overtly as a stated contract or as an explicitly drawn distinction between considering a behavior and doing it; either way the prohibition it removes is self-imposed, living at the consideration gate.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the listener's resistance sits at the threshold — a skeptic or self-monitor who won't respond because responding would mean admitting it's real, or won't even consider because considering feels like commitment. The tell is an explicit permission to "just pretend" or "just consider" with no stake attached, followed by narration that steers the pretense toward the genuine state. It suits openings and re-inductions where behavioral throughput matters more than professed belief.


**Worked examples.**

- *one-way pretend license*
  - maybe at first you're just pretending and playing along with the game of being hypnotized and fractionated. But eventually I'm wondering how the feelings will shift and change in your body.


**See also.** `belief-gate-contingent-yoking` — both let sustained pretense do real operative work while belief is bracketed out of the loop.; `post-wake-self-report-reframe` — both work the 'was I really hypnotized or just playing along' interpretation of the listener's own performance.


<a id="entry-575"></a>

### procedure-well-formedness-QA

[#575](#entry-575) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

The operator validates the authored install/procedure against a hard external test before it runs on a subject, refusing 'the author is satisfied' as the standard. Realizations: (a) INSTALL SPEC WELL-FORMEDNESS — withhold or reshape an install until its specification passes tests: the outcome must be single and tightly bounded ('will this give us ONLY what we want?') so it cannot overshoot and rival parts have nothing to veto; installation is gated on no internal part objecting, each objector's positive function folded into the rebuilt design to prevent relapse-by-sabotage; and the target must be an active, emittable behavior at all (the dead-man test) before measurement begins; (b) PROCEDURE-FIDELITY ENACTMENT-TEST — a trained third party reads the description and physically enacts it, and ANY mistake, added step, omission, or clarifying question counts as proof the description is defective, paired with exhaustive-branch scripting (pre-specify a response to every alternative response) so the procedure transfers without the author present. Both change the operator's design and the document's completeness, not a listener state.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for procedure-well-formedness-QA when the writer's question is 'is the thing I authored correct and transferable before I run it?' — a validity test on the OPERATOR'S artifact (the install spec or the written procedure), enacting nothing on the subject.
