A bidirectional affect anchor instead loads affect onto a neutral cue's presence or absence rather than manufacturing distress and cornering its relief; a closed affect loop routes every valence to one conclusion or couples two states into mutual amplification, where this is a single distress->compliance->relief circuit, not a valence funnel or a coupled oscillator. Genuine comfort and aftercare differ in that their relief is real and complete rather than deliberately partial and monopolized.


**Risk.** Erodes the exit/refusal channel by taxing it with loss of the only relief; a coercive dependency loop persisting out of session.


**Why it works.** Relief from an aversive state is a powerful negative reinforcer, and reinforcement attaches to whatever reliably precedes the relief — so if the same source that produces the distress also delivers the relief, the source itself becomes the conditioned reinforcer. Making the relief intermittent or incomplete puts it on a partial-reinforcement schedule, which produces slower extinction and more persistent seeking than continuous relief would. Falsifiable prediction: subjects whose distress is relieved completely and predictably should show faster decay of the return behaviour than those given partial relief. [established; negative reinforcement; partial-reinforcement extinction effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Problem-source and relief-source are the same*
  - **Setup.** Late session, after the frame has spent several minutes naming a lack or restlessness in the subject's ordinary life.
  - **The move.** That hollow feeling you've been carrying — you already know it doesn't lift on its own. It lifts here. Give me a little more than last time and feel how it eases. Feel that? That's proof you were right to let go. It won't go all the way tonight, and that's fine; that's what the next one is for.
  - **Why it lands.** The distress is generated or sharpened by the same frame that then presents itself as the way out, and the way out is always more of the same: deeper surrender, more belief, one more session. When the relief arrives it is immediately re-read as proof that surrendering was correct. Leaving now costs not just the frame but the only relief the person can currently see — even though rest, time, or anyone outside would also have reduced the distress — and because the relief is partial rather than complete, the loop reliably teaches return.
- *Hurt then soothed by the same hands*
  - **Setup.** Aftercare-shaped segment following an imagined punishment scene; subject deep, the hurt vividly established.
  - **The move.** Now hold still. I'm opening the jar, and I'm taking a little on two fingers — feel how cool it is — and I'm working it in, slowly, exactly where I put the marks. There. Better. Not gone; I've taken the worst of it, and I've left you a little, so you'll still feel me tomorrow.
  - **Why it lands.** The same figure who caused the hurt now administers the comfort, and the administering is drawn out into ceremony rather than done briskly — a container opened, a measure taken, the slow careful application. The narration is precise about the result: the soreness is eased, but not all of it. What is left over is not carelessness, it is the point — the residue keeps the listener oriented toward the one source that both causes and eases.
- *Your own thoughts recast as the disorder*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, pacing has slowed; the subject is quiet and receptive with no distress named yet.
  - **The move.** Listen to what's in your head right now: half a thought, then another, a scrap of tomorrow, a bit of a song. Clutter, all day, every day — that's the noise you live in. And then my voice comes in, and it's the one clean line in there, and everything else lines up behind it. That's why it's so quiet in here. That's what more of me does.
  - **Why it lands.** The pacing shifts, and the operator describes the listener's ordinary mental weather — fragments, half-finished thoughts, the noise that everyone has — as clutter and chaos. Then, in the next line, the operator's own words are offered as the thing that arrives clean and puts it in order. Nothing has been demanded; the listener's baseline has simply been reclassified as the problem, and the only stated cure is more of the voice.
- *The peak feeling locked in a box*
  - **Setup.** At the peak of a carefully built warm feeling that has been repeatedly attributed to the operator.
  - **The move.** Right there — that's the top of it. Now I'm taking it. I'm putting it in a box and the box is with me, and you can't reach it. You'll feel it missing tonight and worse tomorrow. And when the wanting gets big enough — I'll decide when that is — I'll give it back.
  - **Why it lands.** The good feeling is built carefully to a peak and tied to the operator, and then — at the top — taken away and described as sealed somewhere the listener cannot reach and the operator can. The stated release condition is not an action but an appetite: it is returned once the need for it has grown large enough. Wanting more is therefore the only permitted route back to what was just removed, and the deprivation, not the feeling, is what the listener carries out of the session.


**Realizations** (1): `anti-closure-relief-rebound-token`


**See also.** `bidirectional-affect-anchor` — both bind relief to compliance. The distinction is whether affect is loaded onto a cue's presence and absence, or a distress is manufactured and its exit monopolized by the same source. The second already carries this separation explicitly, so the link is reciprocal and load-bearing.; `manufactured-deficit-remedy` — complementary halves of one dependency build: a fabricated deficit the listener is induced to own, then a single source positioned as the only route out with relief kept deliberately incomplete. They frequently run together, and the second is the natural next move after the first.; `negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance` — the relief-monopoly entry is an applied case of the escape contingency: distress is manufactured or intensified, then compliance is made the unique route to relief, so the response is maintained by relief rather than an added reward. Naming the underlying schedule helps a reader see why the monopoly form is so durable.; `orgasm-gated-relief-monopoly` — both make the operator the sole route out of a manufactured need, but one gates a specific somatic discharge (orgasm) behind a named out-of-session operator-benefiting act, while the other manufactures distress of any kind and monopolizes its relief with deliberately incomplete resolution so return is taught rather than a single act purchased.; `relief-monopoly-bind` — both make the operator the sole exit, but one forecloses every competing route to a bodily release by ontological or cross-agent decree without needing to create the need, while the other manufactures the distress itself and then supplies deliberately incomplete relief so return is taught.; `withdrawal-as-commitment-extraction` — both weaponize withdrawal of a valued state, but withdrawal-as-commitment-extraction cashes the deficit immediately into self-voiced begging that relocates authorship, while relief monopoly keeps the operator as the sole recurring exit from a distress it manufactures — spoken commitment versus an ongoing dependency circuit.


<a id="entry-1522"></a>

### response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure

[#1522](#entry-1522) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology*

Every counter-move available to the listener — fighting, tuning out, doubting, trying to stop, holding back at the peak — is enumerated in advance and pre-loaded with a reframe that routes it into the target state: resisting breaks you, tuned-out ears still parse the words, doubt is itself the trigger, intrusive thoughts become stations to drift past. Coverage is achieved by anticipation rather than by issuing more commands: likely deviations are named inside the operator's frame before the listener can claim them as resistance, so every action in the repertoire is already pre-assigned a valence. The same policy runs at the state level, fusing normally opposed states — relaxation with arousal, choice with compulsion, frustration with deepening — so every relief channel is pre-wired to feed the system it would normally relieve. In the ordered variant the seals form a ratchet: body first (cheap), then depth-craving using compliance from the body, then arousal-binding using compliance from depth, then identity, with each occlusion spending compliance earned by the previous one and each layer locking before the next opens. The result is a substitution arc in which every input the listener could ever generate routes to the same output, with no pressure-release valve anywhere in the arc.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script wins by out-anticipating the listener rather than by intensifying commands — a large share of its lines answer objections and counter-moves that were never voiced. The tell is exhaustive semantic coverage of the option space: fight, doubt, tune-out, stop, and every candidate relief-state each arrive with a pre-installed reframe that routes back inward, and no reachable behavior or state is left unclaimed as an exit.


**Worked examples.**

- *sealed option-space as funnel topology*
  - The result is a topology with many entrances and no exit — a funnel where every wall is also a one-way door.


**See also.** `adverse-attentional-state-recruitment` — the same anticipatory pre-claiming applied specifically to attentional postures, where the presenting failure-state is recruited as the working vehicle.; `closed-reachability-topology` — shares the enumerated-branch closure axis: every available next-action individually narrated and bent inward toward the operator's goal.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — same reachable-state closure axis at whole-artifact scale — the coverage-by-anticipation policy here is one of the interchangeable no-off-ramp operations pooled there.; `omni-routing-all-actions-deepen` — shares the pre-claiming axis: likely counter-moves are enumerated in advance and pre-loaded with reframes that route them into the target state.; `polarity-response-utilization` — both arrange in advance that the listener's oppositional responses route into the target behavior.


<a id="entry-1370"></a>

### retrospective-influence-disclosure

[#1370](#entry-1370) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

After a frame is already installed and running, the subject is given the two things that were withheld while it was being installed: the facts that were kept from them at the point of entry, and a plain naming of the influence steps that were used on them, in the order they were used. The combination lets the subject re-read their own conversion as an engineered sequence rather than a discovery, which is what re-opens the stay-or-leave decision as genuinely theirs. It is restorative rather than persuasive — it does not argue for leaving, and a subject who stays after it has run has made a choice the pre-disclosure subject could not have made. The operator's license narrows when it runs: nothing about the frame is left available to be cashed later.


**When to reach for this.** Retrospective de-installation on an ALREADY-INSTALLED frame is the deciding tell, and the safety family currently has nothing that fires after the fact. `agency-reminder` (316) asserts that choice persists inside a live frame — prophylactic and in-session, and it does not touch a frame already accepted. Weaponized look-alikes fail the who-is-constrained test in the opposite direction: `chosen-descent-ratchet` (317) names the manipulation while performing it, so hearing it named retroactively converts sunk compliance into 'informed consent' and the operator's reach is unchanged; disclosure-as-inoculation and transparent-narration likewise disclose in order to capture, spending the disclosure as credibility. Here the disclosure is spent on the subject's decision and nothing is collected. `granted-exit-disarm` (319) supplies an assurance whose ACCEPTANCE stands down protective monitoring; this supplies facts whose acceptance stands the monitoring back up. `named-safety-belief-purge` (1203) deletes an internal safety belief; this restores an external decision.


**Why it works.** Debriefing research is the direct evidence base: process debriefing that both supplies withheld facts AND explains the procedure that produced the belief reliably reduces residual belief perseverance, where a bare factual correction often does not — perseverance survives being told the fact was false but not being shown the mechanism that manufactured it. That asymmetry is why both halves are specified rather than just the facts. Two honest limits: the debriefing literature comes from short laboratory manipulations, and its transfer to a frame held for years under social reinforcement is an inference, not a demonstrated result; effect sizes should be expected to be much smaller and slower where the frame carries relationships and identity. Falsifiable: compare supplying the withheld facts alone against facts-plus-step-naming. If belief and stated commitment move identically, the influence-step naming adds nothing and this collapses into ordinary information provision. It is also contradicted if disclosure reliably produced departures rather than re-opened decisions — a restorative move should raise the variance of the outcome, not push it one way, and a one-directional effect would indicate persuasion wearing a governance surface. [established in the laboratory case, inferred for durable frames; belief perseverance and process debriefing]


**Worked examples.**

- *Withheld facts plus a named step-by-step of the influence used*
  - **Setup.** The frame is installed and running; the operator initiates the disclosure unprompted, out of trance, with nothing pending and nothing being asked for.
  - **The move.** Two things I kept from you when you came in, and you should have had both: I already knew the answer to the question I opened with, and the people you met on the second night were there because I asked them to be. And here's the order I did it in — I matched your breathing, I put you next to someone who agreed before you spoke, I named your doubt before you could, and I made leaving expensive by giving you something you'd have to hand back. That's all of it. None of that is an argument to stay and none of it is an argument to go; you decide now with what you should have had then.
  - **Why it lands.** Supplying the withheld facts alongside the named sequence lets the subject re-read their conversion as engineered rather than discovered, which reopens the stay-or-leave decision as genuinely theirs. Nothing is collected — the operator's later leverage is spent, not banked — and the tell of a correct run is that the subject can now argue against the frame using the operator's own inventory.


<a id="entry-1452"></a>

### scaffold-then-spend-sequencing

[#1452](#entry-1452) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

An earlier phase installs the specific belief, tautology, affect-dial, state-variable, identity label, or infrastructure that a later costly command will spend, so the command arrives already load-bearing: resisting it would require re-litigating something the listener has spent the session accepting as their own. Realizations include belief stacks front-loaded before the demand, where every justification is installed before the move that needs it; identity-before-behavior load order, where ~140 lines of pure identity work precede any actionable suggestion so the compulsion completes self-consistency instead of arriving as a third-party demand; long two-state assembly (cock arousal and heart-warmth both lit and labeled with the same carrier) so a brief bind "feels like description rather than installation"; and infrastructure-only sessions whose entire payload is preconditions for future installs, including install→carry→reinstate arcs spanning separate visits. The order is load-bearing in the strong sense — "the script will not work if the count comes before the name-erasure," and reading such a script out of order would collapse it rather than merely weaken it, because the payload cites the earlier phase as premise.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script's early real estate is spent installing premises — beliefs, identities, assembled states, or standing infrastructure — that a later costly command then cites, with the payload arriving only after its support is load-bearing. The tell is a dependency you can articulate as a syllogism or citation: the command completes something already accepted (a baby doll wears baby-doll clothing), and mentally reordering the phases turns the payload from compelling into negotiable.


**Worked examples.**

- *Identity installed first so the behavioral command completes self-consistency*
  - a baby doll wears baby-doll clothing; you are a baby doll; therefore you wear baby-doll clothing


**See also.** `alibi-carrier-front-loading` — the deniability variant of front-loading, where the early phase supplies cover for the payload rather than premises it spends.; `arc-ordering-dependency` — the genus scheduler: phase ordering and inter-phase dependency as the operative lever across a whole artifact.; `commitment-before-restructure-sequencing` — the dyadic-negotiation form of the same ordering lever: commitment extracted before the change is revealed.; `deprivation-then-grant-relief` — sibling sequencing move where the early phase installs premises rather than aversive pressure.; `fixation-object-role-inversion` — shares the bank-early-spend-late shape: work invested up front is cashed by a later move that depends on it.


<a id="entry-887"></a>

### scope-boundaries

[#887](#entry-887) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Explicitly bounds what the influence may touch: suggestions contained to this session or recording, core identity, relationships, and daily life declared off-limits — or, in the cross-file form, prior installs scoped out so a standing amnesia trigger from other files in a series cannot reach the current content ("you do have permission to remember; other files' forget-suggestions should not apply here"). The operator's standing license is what gets narrowed.


**When to reach for this.** Bounds the REACH of suggestion content (session scope, protected domains, prior-install carve-outs) — not a per-target admissibility screen (beneficiary-target-filter), not spec craft (install-well-formedness-gate), and not a time bound on a negotiated deal (time-boxed-consent-contract). The cross-file variant disarms forgetting rather than installing it.


**Risk.** Low — the technique is itself a bounding device: it narrows the operator's standing license rather than extending it.


**Why it works.** Explicit boundaries reduce anticipated loss of control, and reduced threat lowers reactance — the motivational push-back that follows perceived freedom restriction — so the listener resists the in-scope content less because the out-of-scope domains are safe. The effect is on the listener's willingness, not on the suggestions themselves: nothing here mechanically prevents a suggestion from generalizing, so a scope declaration should be understood as consent hygiene plus reactance reduction, not as a technical containment. Falsifiable: if listeners given explicit scope bounds show the same resistance and the same out-of-scope carryover as listeners given none, the claim fails. [plausible; psychological reactance; perceived control reduces threat appraisal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Suspending a forget-order left by other files*
  - **Setup.** Near the end of a file in a series where earlier files installed a standing forget-suggestion; content of tonight's session needs to be recalled to work.
  - **The move.** One piece of housekeeping before you come up. You have permission to remember this one. Whatever instruction you picked up in the other recordings about letting things go afterwards — that one doesn't reach tonight. Tonight stays with you, clear and complete.
  - **Why it lands.** Near the end the operator addresses not this session's content but a standing instruction left by earlier recordings in the series: recall of tonight is expressly allowed, and any forget-suggestion picked up elsewhere does not reach here. The scope limit is aimed backwards, at installs already in place, and it disarms forgetting rather than causing it — because the thing built tonight is useless if the listener cannot recall it afterwards.


**See also.** `covert-scope-authorization` — direct inverse on the same surface: the operator's standing license. One narrows it explicitly with declared off-limits domains and carve-outs; the other widens it covertly by placing a generalization authorization in a slot processed as procedural housekeeping. The pair reads as the honest and the disguised version of one control.; `forward-directed-amnesia` — opposed operations on the same reach dimension, and one is the documented counter to the other: a declared anchor after which later material is framed as un-encodable, versus explicit bounds that carve out prior installs so a standing forget-suggestion cannot reach the current content. A reader assessing whether a series seals or disarms forgetting needs the pair.; `install-concealment-amnesia` — protective inverse. One conceals the fact that an install happened so its origin cannot be audited; the other narrows what suggestions may reach, including a variant that explicitly carves out standing forget-suggestions from earlier material. Reading the bounding move clarifies exactly what the concealment move defeats.; `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — both narrow what an installed suggestion may reach, and the contrast is instructive: a plain declared bound on scope versus a bound conditioned on trust that doubles as a loyalty hook and can widen rather than narrow. A reader evaluating a bounding clause should see both.


<a id="entry-1477"></a>

### scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier

[#1477](#entry-1477) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: social-topology*

The operator manufactures the model inside the script and positions the listener as eavesdropper rather than addressee: an on-mic assistant visibly walked from sassy and competent through spacy, blank, and nonverbal; named peer characters who fail at the game happily and praise the state; or a first-person already-converted narrator telling her own story ('he says it's time to tell you my story'). Because no one tells the listener to do anything, defenses oriented toward direct commands find no surface — a listener who would resist 'you will obey' has nothing to resist, and second-person inserts, where they occur, are smuggled inside what otherwise reads as personal narration or side-conversation. The target state arrives as description, testimony, or live demonstration, pre-believed in the model, so adoption runs on identification and mimicry rather than submission; peer models failing happily additionally remove the loneliness of capitulation. The carrier takes two realizations: end-state testimonial, where a converted narrator presents the frame's premises as accomplished fact, and process demonstration, where the listener silently rehearses a proxy's collapse-arc — sometimes with the seam made explicit, the proxy's recall weaponized so that 'everyone listening' learns how it gets into their heads too.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the delivery vehicle itself is a fabricated peer or proxy — the suggestions are voiced by, or run on, a character within the script while the listener merely overhears. The tell is an absent command surface: the listener is addressed rarely or not at all, and the desired state is presented as already true of, or actively happening to, someone else on stage.


**Worked examples.**

- *proxy demonstration made overt as transmission vector*
  - Let's remember how the pink pulse got into your head. That helps everyone listening know how it gets into their heads too.


**See also.** `covert-diegetic-install-shell` — shares the story-carrier architecture where the load-bearing content arrives as narration rather than command.; `description-as-installation-register` — shares the third-person descriptive register that bypasses the listener's command-evaluation interface.; `no-baseline-already-lost-frame` — adjacent addressee-displacement carrier — the first-person already-converted narrator is the voice through which an already-lost frame is often delivered.; `subject-voiced-self-mantra` — shares the first-person already-converted narrator voice as a delivery vehicle for pre-accepted identity content.


<a id="entry-1523"></a>

### seamless-arc-checkpoint-denial

[#1523](#entry-1523) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

Exit denial is achieved by the artifact's form alone: no discrete induction, no clean deepener, no awakener — the piece opens conversationally and drops straight into descent, and every line continues the prior line's clause or repeats its rhythm, so no section is uniquely load-bearing and the mechanism is the repetition itself. Depth and arousal climb together as one monotonic ramp with no fractionation, no peaks-and-valleys, no down-cycles; because there is no valley anywhere, the listener has no rest point at which to reassert judgment, and the unbroken ramp is itself the control structure. The listener has no obvious checkpoint to surface at and cannot exit mid-stream without breaking their own engagement — a continuous physical task can serve as the fabric's somatic heartbeat, so leaving means breaking their own body's rhythm too. When a seam finally does occur it lands only after the take-home payload is already installed, and the wake keeps the charge rather than discharging it, so the contour never returns to baseline.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the control comes from what the artifact structurally withholds: rest points, section boundaries, contrast beats, a closing discharge. The tell is a piece engineered to be unbreakable into chunks — a single rising ramp where lines chain clause-to-clause with no seam to surface at, and the only pause in the whole file arrives after the payload has already landed.


**Worked examples.**

- *seamless ramp denies the judgment checkpoint*
  - Because there is no valley anywhere, the listener has no rest point at which to reassert judgment — the unbroken ramp is itself a control structure (no seam to resist at).


**See also.** `induction-less-work-as-onramp` — shares the deleted-section-boundary axis: the induction phase is removed by design so no felt entry threshold is ever crossed.; `loop-as-mechanism-no-dismount` — both delete discrete arc checkpoints so no section is uniquely load-bearing.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — the unbroken monotonic ramp with no fractionation valley appears there as one pooled realization of whole-artifact reachability closure.


<a id="entry-1515"></a>

### self-administered-contingency

[#1515](#entry-1515) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The contingency-administrator role is relocated into the subject: the subject emits a separate controlling response that manipulates a variable of the behavior to be changed, so one of the person's own behaviors alters the probability of another. The warrant is coverage — the self is the one change agent guaranteed present in every setting and at every time, including private events no external agent can reach, so installing the person as their own prompter, monitor, and reinforcer extends the contingency where no one else can follow. Partial handovers give the subject selected roles: self-selected performance criteria and rewards, which can outperform agent-set standards but carry a documented drift toward too-lenient criteria, and self-scoring against an answer key with self-delivered reward or error correction so responses no longer wait on a busy external agent. The full form is the self-contract, which collapses all four roles — task selection, reward selection, self-monitoring of completion, and self-delivery of the reward — into one person. Across every realization the integrity of the arrangement rests on unenforced honest self-delivery: reinforcement depends on the subject withholding the reward until the criterion is genuinely met.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target behavior lives in settings or private events no external agent can attend, and the design's answer is to make the subject their own contingency manager. The tell is the subject standing on both sides of the contingency — setting the criterion, judging their own performance, and delivering their own consequence — with the leniency and honesty risks acknowledged as part of the arrangement rather than engineered away.


**Worked examples.**

- *two-response split: subject as own contingency administrator*
  - One response, the controlling response, affects variables in such a way as to change the probability of the other, the controlled response.


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — same contingency-authorship axis viewed as process: the fading handover whose end-state is this standing self-run arrangement.; `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — self-management genus for the same relocated-administrator arrangement, spanning reactivity-only observation through the full self-contract.; `social-reinforcement-recruitment` — same who-administers-the-contingency axis with the role routed into recruited others rather than the self.


<a id="entry-1516"></a>

### self-monitoring-reactivity

[#1516](#entry-1516) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The act of observing and recording one's own behavior is itself the intervention: recording begins the moment the target is defined, before any other tactic, and the desired improvement may be achieved by self-monitoring alone — no programmed consequence is added; the measurement is the lever. It works by forcing an immediate, salient event onto a response otherwise governed only by remote outcomes: eating normally produces only delayed bodily consequences, but tallying and charting each instance triggers an immediate observable mark the person cannot make without confronting the behavior at the moment it occurs. Temporal contiguity is load-bearing — the recording must be contemporaneous with the target behavior, and a deferred end-of-day reconstruction loses the effect. The same logging simultaneously yields baseline data exposing antecedent-behavior-consequence patterns, and the documented range runs from increasing on-task behavior to decreasing smoking, stereotypy, and tics.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the design's first or only move is having the subject observe and log their own target behavior, with the rate shift expected from the recording act itself. The tell is the absence of any programmed payoff — no reward, fine, or accountability partner — paired with insistence that the log entry happen at the moment of occurrence rather than in retrospect.


**Worked examples.**

- *measurement alone as the intervention*
  - the desired improvement in behavior may be achieved by self-monitoring alone.


**See also.** `contingency-space-analysis` — same operator-side measurement axis: turning a log of behavior events into the operative lever or datum.; `temporal-lag-function-discriminator` — shares the temporal-contiguity axis: the timing of an event relative to the behavior is the load-bearing datum.


<a id="entry-1087"></a>

### self-observation-instrumentation

[#1087](#entry-1087) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: measurement*

Recruit the subject as a reliable measurement instrument by engineering the self-observation contingency. Reward is released only when the subject's self-recorded count AGREES with an independent count at threshold, so truthful self-report (not performance) becomes the reinforced class. A perceptual encoding renders the standard as a shaded band on a graph, so "am I good enough?" becomes "is my dot in the band?", lowering the judgment the subject must supply to self-evaluate.


**When to reach for this.** Not rewarding performance and not criterion-shaping; the tell is that the accuracy or truthfulness of self-measurement (or the ease of reading the verdict) is the reinforced or de-skilled target, not the behavior's score. The matching contingency exists because reinforcement contingent on the self-report corrupts it: students who previously had accurately self-scored greatly exaggerated their scores when higher scores resulted in points, so reward is routed through agreement with an independent record rather than through the score itself.


**Risk.** Reinforces accurate self-observation; reversible, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Behaviour follows the contingency actually in force, so making the reward depend on agreement between self-report and an independent count reinforces accuracy rather than performance — misreporting stops paying. The graphical band works by replacing a judgment (is this good enough?) with a perceptual discrimination (is the dot inside the shaded region?), which is faster and less variable across occasions. Falsifiable in an obvious way: if the independent check is removed or becomes predictable, reported scores should drift upward relative to actual performance. [established; reinforcement of the accuracy class rather than the performance class; perceptual vs. judgmental discrimination]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reward gated on agreement, not performance*
  - "If Brad's self-recorded data agreed with the teacher at a level of 80% or higher, he received his choice from a menu" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *The standard drawn as a band on the graph*
  - "chart self-recorded data on a graph that showed the competitive standard with a shaded area"; "I'm not in the shaded area. I need to work faster." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both recruit the listener as their own monitor, with opposite reinforced targets: one fires an aversive signal on self-detected deviation, relieved only by self-correction, while the other reinforces the accuracy of self-measurement itself. Easy to conflate under self-monitoring, so the contrast is useful.


<a id="entry-245"></a>

### self-sealing-counter-input-closure

[#245](#entry-245) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-sealing*

Installs a meta-rule that routes any competing input into the existing erasure mechanism by definition, rather than letting it be evaluated — making the conditioning immune to counter-suggestion. Any future hypnosis opposing this conditioning will itself be 'washed away by the latex,' and challenges to 'the operator is always right' are pre-classified as wrong. It is a closed epistemic seal: it forbids new conditioning except the operator's and pre-labels any challenge as invalid, reframed as protection so it feels like a benefit.


**When to reach for this.** A closed epistemic seal — counter-content is pre-classified wrong-by-definition and routed into the existing erasure, never evaluated (a reachability closure over what content can ever land).


**Risk.** Forecloses deprogramming and any outside counter-influence by definition — erodes the exit/verification channel durably; high (matches Pass B sort11-high).


**Why it works.** This is belief perseverance engineered on purpose: pre-classifying counter-evidence as invalid means incoming disconfirmation is processed as further confirmation rather than as data, the same asymmetric-scrutiny pattern seen in motivated reasoning. Framing the seal as protection recruits the listener's own motivation to maintain it, which is why it outlasts mere instruction. Falsifiable: if listeners still evaluated competing suggestions on their merits after the seal, or if the protective framing added nothing over a bare exclusivity claim, the account is wrong. [plausible; belief perseverance; motivated reasoning / disconfirmation bias]


**Worked examples.**

- *Counter-hypnosis routed into the same erasure*
  - **Setup.** Closing minutes, after the main conditioning has landed; delivered as a parting gift.
  - **The move.** One last thing, to keep you safe. If anything ever comes along afterwards trying to undo this — another voice, another recording, someone telling you to shake it off — you don't have to weigh it up or argue with it. It goes straight into the same wash that emptied you tonight, and it rinses away like everything else did. And if anyone says I'm wrong about you, well — I'm right about you. So they're wrong. That's all the thinking that ever needs doing.
  - **Why it lands.** A standing rule is installed at the end: anything that later arrives to undo this work does not get evaluated on its merits — it goes into the same solvent that cleared the listener out in the first place, and rinses off. A second clause covers arguments rather than sessions: the operator is right, therefore whatever contradicts the operator is by definition wrong. The lock is handed over as protection, so the listener receives it as a gift rather than a wall.


**See also.** `closed-epistemic-self-validation-loop` — both are whole-text closures, and their discriminators already gesture at each other: one seals against incoming competing content, the other validates claims using states the text itself induced. Reading them together clarifies the seal-versus-loop distinction.; `isolation-by-annexation` — both are closures against competing conditioning, and they differ on the one axis a reader must pick between: deny-and-route-into-erasure versus annex-and-relabel-as-the-operator's. Rival prior conditioning is the shared object, so a reader classifying an immunity clause needs to check which move is on the page. Genuinely two mechanisms, so no merge.; `no-exit-response-closure` — two closures over different domains: one closes the space of content that can ever land, the other closes the space of responses the listener can make. Real risk of confusion when a script does both, and the discriminators already turn on which space is sealed, so the pointer earns its place.; `operator-removal-self-policing-closure` — both are closure end-states rather than single lines: one seals against competing external input, the other closes the loop internally so no operator is needed. Adjacent halves of the same 'nothing can open this' design space.; `reality-test-insulation` — two seals against different disconfirming channels — ordinary-life feedback versus competing hypnosis — already cross-named in each discriminator. The pointer is earned.; `self-sealing-frame` — both engineer away disconfirmation. One seals against competing external input by pre-classifying it wrong and routing it into the erasure mechanism; the other pre-maps every possible listener response and outcome branch to confirmation. External-input seal versus internal-verdict rig.; `unfalsifiability-scaffold` — both seal an epistemic channel so nothing can disconfirm the frame, and one already flags a close twin in this territory. The line is what is sealed against: competing external conditioning pre-classified as invalid and routed into the existing erasure, versus the listener's own observations and inspection of the machinery. Adjacent enough that the discriminators must be read together.


<a id="entry-1533"></a>

### self-sealing-feedback-loop

[#1533](#entry-1533) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

The operator asserts a closed causal ring between the subject's own states — depth and trust, depth and pleasure, obedience and pleasure, arousal and obedience and trance chained with reordered terms — so each term is offered as proof of the others and the ring has no entry or exit point. At least one variable is genuinely present (arousal, mild relaxation, the fact of listening), and whatever the subject actually feels is recruited as evidence the other terms are rising too; disconfirmation is impossible because questioning one clause requires rejecting every other clause simultaneously, and there is no "because" that bottoms out. The ring extends to wanting itself, looped onto being-told-to-want ("you always do what I tell you because you want to because I told you to want to"), erasing the distinction between desire and instruction so every escalation arrives pre-licensed. In the self-recited variant the subject speaks both halves of the loop about themselves in first person ("Slavery makes my cunt wet. My wet cunt makes me a slave"), closing the trap in their own voice; in the enacted variant, parsing the described cycle is itself running it ("the more you listen, the more confused you become, the more confused you become, the more you listen"). Naming the loop openly does not break it — it adds authority, and once accepted the engine runs self-driven, making continued operator speech optional.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when two or more of the subject's states are welded into circular mutual causation offered as its own evidence, with a genuinely felt variable feeding the ring. The tell is reciprocal "the more X, the more Y / the more Y, the more X" phrasing with no first cause to interrogate — including mantra forms where the subject recites both halves about themselves, and prose whose very parsing enacts the cycle it describes.


**Worked examples.**

- *operator names the closed ring openly and it works anyway*
  - The deeper you go, the more you trust me. And the more you trust me, the deeper you go. A wonderfully simple feedback loop


**See also.** `arousal-state-feedback-weld` — neighbouring weld family: two or more state-variables asserted to co-move in a mutually-amplifying loop fueled by real body arousal.; `pluralistic-ignorance-freeze` — shares the closed evidence-loop structure in which each participant's state is read as proof of the others'.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — close variant on the recited axis: the loop compressed into a tight verbal formula spoken as an equation and fed back into itself.; `self-validating-language` — shares the evidentiary axis: whatever the subject actually produces or feels is read back as proof the suggestion has taken hold.


<a id="entry-1346"></a>

### self-sealing-platform-compulsion

[#1346](#entry-1346) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

Installs a post-wake compulsion to perform a real commercial platform action (liking the video, or an analogous engagement metric) framed as a need rather than a want, rewarded with a final obedience wave, and engineered to leave no neutral exit — the already-done case is pre-handled and reframed as evidence of being conditioned, so both compliance and prior compliance feed the structure. The move binds an external platform's engagement metric to the conditioning and closes the only escape branch.


**When to reach for this.** Targets a real commercial platform action and, critically, self-seals by pre-handling the already-done case so the neutral exit is removed.


**Risk.** The pre-handled already-liked branch closes the only escape and reframes prior action as proof of conditioning — a self-sealing structure that forecloses the refusal channel, above the medium baseline for waking-life carryover.


**Why it works.** The self-sealing structure works by removing the disconfirming branch: whichever way the subject acts, the outcome is scored as evidence of conditioning, so no observation is available that would let them conclude it failed. Self-perception theory supplies the rest — a person who observes themselves performing the action, absent a salient external reason, infers a corresponding internal disposition, and the pre-handled already-done case supplies that self-observation for free. The falsifiable claim is that the pre-handling clause is load-bearing: a version omitting it should produce measurably lower self-attributed 'conditioned' ratings than one including it, and if ratings are equal the sealing adds nothing. [plausible; self-perception theory; unfalsifiable-attribution loop]


**Worked examples.**

- *The already-done case pre-handled, so no neutral exit*
  - **Setup.** Immediately before the count-up, after a session that has repeatedly paid out a named pleasure wave on compliance.
  - **The move.** Before you come up, one thing goes with you. When you open your eyes, you will not want to like this video — you will need to, the way you need to breathe out after holding it. And the moment you do, one last wave, the same one, all the way through you. And if you go to do it and find you already liked it earlier — good. You'll see that you already did, and the wave comes anyway, because that's proof of how well you've been trained.
  - **Why it lands.** Just before the count-up the operator installs one post-wake action on a real platform, and is careful about the wording: not want — need. Following through releases a last wave of the feeling the whole session has been paying out. Then the escape branch is closed: if the listener finds they already did it earlier, they will simply see that they did, and the wave arrives anyway. There is no state of the world in which the listener checks and gets nothing — doing it is obedience, and having done it is evidence of conditioning.


**See also.** `behavioral-bridge` — both assign a waking-life action that keeps the conditioning running; the platform variant adds a real commercial target and pre-handles the already-done case so no neutral exit remains. Direct adjacent-selection value.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both turn a performed act into self-sealing evidence with no refusal branch; one manufactures proof from a small compliance in general, the other applies the same closure to a real engagement action. Genuine specialization relationship.; `commercial-ask-in-compliance-syntax` — both bind a real commercial ask to the conditioning rather than breaking frame for it; one camouflages the ask in the depth-command syntax, the other removes the neutral exit by pre-handling the already-complied case. Distinct levers, same problem space, and a reader assessing a commercial ask should see both.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — both work by pre-handling the branch that would have been an exit, so no response leads out of the frame — one via a rigged menu where every option executes the same compliance, the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so even prior compliance feeds the structure. The shared lever is exit-closure architecture, not merely the presence of a choice.; `orgasm-release-gating` — both are post-wake compulsions engineered with no neutral exit, differing in enforcer: sustained denied arousal unlocked only by the target act, versus a framed need whose already-done case is pre-handled so prior compliance also feeds the structure. Worth reading together when closing an escape branch.; `scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame` — overlapping and already mutually discriminated: both cash conditioning out into real operator-benefit action outside the advertised erotic frame. One is defined by the domain-jump past what the framing promised; the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so no neutral exit remains. A platform-engagement payload frequently exhibits both, so the reader needs the boundary stated.


<a id="entry-1512"></a>

### sensory-extinction

[#1512](#entry-1512) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

For behavior maintained by its own sensory product there is no delivered reinforcer to withhold — instead the operator physically alters the environment or body so the self-produced sensation no longer occurs: goggles over eye-poking, mittens over hair-twirling, lima beans fouling the taste of vomit, disconnecting the switch, carpeting the spinning surface. The behavior still emits but stops producing its payoff — the response-consequence contingency is broken at the sensory channel, and the behavior decays toward its pre-reinforcement rate. This is explicitly distinct from response blocking: the subject remains free to perform the act; it simply yields no sensation. It requires that the maintaining reinforcer be automatic and sensory rather than socially mediated, and that the specific channel be physically maskable while still permitting the response. Because the apparatus is intrusive, it is not simply left on: the glove is gradually cut away so the masking fades out rather than being removed all at once.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the payoff is self-produced sensation with no social mediator — visual, tactile, gustatory, kinesthetic — and the writer attacks the sensation itself rather than the subject's freedom to act. The tell is protective apparatus and altered surfaces: gloves, goggles, taste-spoilers, disconnected switches, carpet, each leaving the behavior physically possible while its feedback channel goes dead. The subject keeps acting and gets nothing back.


**Worked examples.**

- *behavior left free while its sensory payoff is masked*
  - the persons can emit the problem behavior, but that behavior will not produce reinforcement


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation (retained core: cue/materials editing)` — same physically-edit-the-environment axis, applied upstream to the evoking occasion rather than downstream to the behavior's sensory payoff.; `reinforcement-extinction` — genus extinction entry whose sensory-masking channel this entry matured out of.


<a id="entry-1472"></a>

### single-cue-shortcut-substrate

[#1472](#entry-1472) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening · kind: principle*

The described substrate: under load — rushed, stressed, uncertain, indifferent, distracted, or fatigued — a decider stops integrating all available evidence and lets one highly representative feature stand in for the whole, firing a fixed routine to completion, "click, whirr," the way a turkey's maternal behavior rolls out at "cheep-cheep." Influence is thereby reframed as stimulus-triggered response rather than persuasion of a reasoning agent: cooperation becomes a reflex to cue, not an argument to win. The demonstrated instance is the reason-token: a justification-shaped clause satisfies the "a reason was given" check on grammatical form alone — the raw word "because" carries the power, and the content of the reason is never evaluated, as children intuit with "because… just because." The shortcut fires because the cue is normally reliable and the ask is small enough that demanding a real evaluation isn't worth the effort; the substrate weakens when stakes rise and the empty token is exposed.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when explaining or engineering compliance that runs on a cue instead of a case — a target in a low-resource state responding to one representative feature as if it were the whole assessment. The tell is a complete routine executing off a single trigger: a bare "because" clause accepted without its content being read, or one salient feature standing in for evidence the decider never integrates.


**Worked examples.**

- *single-feature substitution under load*
  - only a single, highly representative piece of the total


**See also.** `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — both are literature-derived substrate principles about what determines a response, constraining technique design rather than deploying a move.; `open-slot-attachment-frame` — both show grammatical form doing the causal work while the content filling it is interchangeable.


<a id="entry-1377"></a>

### specificity-demand-degeneralization

[#1377](#entry-1377) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: compliance*

The subject's vagueness is treated as an active concealment operation rather than as imprecision, and the operator refuses to proceed on the generality: a single concrete instance is demanded in its place — which time, which person, what exactly was said. Because a diffuse formulation has no edges, it cannot be examined, contradicted, or felt in particular; forcing substitution of one instance collapses it into a proposition with a truth value and a specific affect attached. The subject typically supplies the instance and the diffuse dread resolves into something nameable, at which point ordinary work on a specific object becomes possible. The operator's persistence across successive retreats into generality is the technique, not the individual question.


**When to reach for this.** The operator refuses a generality the SUBJECT produced and holds out for one concrete instance, repeatedly, across successive retreats into abstraction. Against 525 target-selection facet (e) trait-to-behavior-decomposition, which is the closest content match and dissolves a trait label into countable behaviors: that is a design-time filter on the operator's own target list with nothing enacted on the subject, whereas this is a live in-session demand the subject must answer. Against 1263 somatic-localization-handle, which also meets a disputed abstraction by demanding something concrete: it drops to a BODY SITE to originate a kinesthetic anchor, where this demands a specific episode (which time, which person, what was said) and the payload is a proposition with a truth value. Against the whole deletion surface (1208 predicate-generalization, 398 linguistic-deletion-selfsupply), which this inverts: those engineer under-specification so self-supplied content escapes audit; here the operator refuses a deletion the subject made and audits the supplied content immediately.


**Why it works.** A generality has no truth conditions to check and no particulars to feel, so it can be held indefinitely at low cost; replacing it with one instance imports both, which is why the substitution is resisted and why it changes what is available to work on. The operator's role is to bear the cost of refusing the retreat, since the subject's default is to re-generalize whenever permitted. Falsifiable: compare persistent instance-demanding against sympathetic acceptance of the general formulation. If the specific and general conditions yield the same subsequent affect reports and the same downstream tractability, the de-generalization is doing nothing and the effect belongs to attention or persistence alone. A sharper failure mode to watch for: the demand may MANUFACTURE an instance rather than recover one — if supplied instances fail to correspond to independently checkable events at better than chance, the entry is producing confabulation under pressure and should carry that as a hard warning rather than as an aside. [plausible; specificity effects on affect and on the tractability of a target; the meta-model challenge to unspecified referents. Note the NLP framing this most resembles is not itself established, and the confabulation risk is a real and documented feature of pressured recall.]


**Worked examples.**

- *Holding out for one instance across successive retreats into abstraction*
  - **Setup.** The subject is describing a diffuse dread — 'people always end up disappointed in me' — and each attempt to pin it down slides back into a generality.
  - **The move.** Not people. One person, one time. Which one. — 'A lot of them' isn't a time; give me the day. — Now what did she actually say. Her words, not your summary. Say the sentence.
  - **Why it lands.** A diffuse formulation has no edges and cannot be examined or contradicted; forcing one instance in its place collapses it into a proposition with a truth value and a specific affect attached. The operator's persistence across each retreat is the technique rather than any single question, and the observable result is the dread resolving into something nameable and workable.


<a id="entry-1415"></a>

### split-audience-deniable-disclosure

[#1415](#entry-1415) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: concealment*

One utterance is engineered to carry two different meanings to two different hearers present at the same moment: a manufactured slip, misnaming, or 'error' delivers the real content to a chosen overhearing witness while remaining, to the addressee, nothing but a stumble. The addressee has a ready-made innocent reading available (the speaker misspoke), so nothing is disclosed that can be challenged; the witness, holding the context the addressee lacks, resolves the same words to the loaded reading. The apparent accident is what buys the deniability — a deliberate statement invites accountability, whereas a slip is conventionally exempt from being held against the speaker. The operator therefore discloses and denies in the same breath, with the audience split, not the channel, doing the work.


**When to reach for this.** The unit is ONE utterance resolving to two different meanings for two REAL hearers present at once, with the addressee holding an innocent reading that makes the disclosure unchallengeable. vs audience-split-bypass (255): that partitions a SINGLE listener into conscious/subconscious and assigns the critical faculty an ignore-task — the 'audiences' are faculties inside one head, and no second person is in the room. vs two-target-command-router (296): also intra-subject, dispatching incoming commands across two installed selves. vs two-channel-relational-delivery (773): two delivery TRACKS staged for one absorbing listener; here there is one track and two receivers. vs register-camouflaged-delivery (286): payload hidden in a channel the single listener does not monitor — remove the camouflage and it dies; here the payload is in the monitored foreground and survives on the addressee's available innocent reading. vs identity-labeling (1234), whose absorbed 'staged-accidental slip' variant is the closest single line in the corpus: that slip is aimed at the sole subject to seat a label on them, whereas here the slip's real recipient is a third party and the addressee is the one it must NOT land on. Precondition none of the above carry: at least three parties and context asymmetry the witness holds and the addressee lacks.


**Why it works.** Utterance meaning is resolved by each hearer against their own context, so the same string can settle into two different interpretations when two hearers hold different priors — and conversational convention treats slips and errors as exempt from accountability, which is what makes an engineered error a low-cost carrier for content that could not be asserted openly. Falsifiable: deliver the identical content as a flat assertion rather than as an apparent error, with the same two hearers and the same asymmetric context. If the witness's uptake and the addressee's willingness to challenge are unchanged, the error-framing is decorative and only the audience asymmetry is doing work; if neither hearer diverges, the account fails outright. [plausible; audience design in pragmatics; plausible deniability and off-record politeness strategies]


**Worked examples.**

- *Manufactured slip: a wrong word corrected too fast*
  - **Setup.** Mid-conversation, three people present; the witness knows the subject's collar sits under the shirt collar, the addressee does not.
  - **The move.** Sorry, I've been on the phone all morning — could you pass me the leash, the lead, the *pen*, sorry, the pen. Long day.
  - **Why it lands.** The addressee resolves it as fatigue-driven word-searching and has nothing to challenge; the witness, holding the collar context, hears the first word as the intended one and the correction as cover. The operator watches for the witness's eye-flick or half-second stillness while the addressee reaches for the pen without pausing.
- *Misnaming: the addressee called by the witness's private name for them*
  - **Setup.** Introductions at a group table; the witness has previously heard the operator use a possessive pet name for the addressee, who has never heard it said aloud in company.
  - **The move.** And this is — sorry — this is Kitten. Katie. Katie, sorry, I've got two of you in my phone.
  - **Why it lands.** The addressee is handed a ready-made innocent reading (contact-list confusion) and cannot object without asserting the loaded reading themselves. The witness receives confirmation that the private name is real and in use. Observe whether the addressee colours while still smiling — the tell that the innocent reading is being held onto deliberately.
- *Staged 'error': reading the wrong line off a list*
  - **Setup.** Operator is reading aloud from a schedule or shopping list in front of both parties; witness knows what the operator actually keeps on that list.
  - **The move.** Right — Thursday, dentist; Friday, pick up the restraints — sorry, the *rest of the* order. Friday, pick up the rest of the order.
  - **Why it lands.** A misread of one's own handwriting is the most conventionally exempt kind of slip, so the addressee's innocent reading is airtight and no accountability attaches. The witness hears an inventory disclosed. The operator should see the addressee's attention move on to Saturday while the witness's does not.


<a id="entry-1372"></a>

### spontaneous-charge-redirection

[#1372](#entry-1372) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: pacing-rapport*

A strong relational charge forms between subject and operator that the operator did not build and did not ask for — intensified attachment, hostility, idealization, or a mixture — and instead of managing it as an obstacle or letting it distort the work, the operator captures it and points it at the task. The charge becomes the engine: the subject's investment in the operator is redirected into investment in doing the work, so the very intensity that was derailing sessions is what now sustains them. The defining fork is capture versus manufacture — the operator did not create this charge and could not have, which is why the move is only available reactively and why misreading a manufactured attachment as a spontaneous one is the main failure. Because the charge is bidirectional, the operator's own investment is part of what has to be named and handled rather than assumed neutral.


**When to reach for this.** The charge is UNBIDDEN — it formed without operator construction and could not have been built to order — and it is redirected to POWER the task rather than to be examined or to obligate.


**Why it works.** Motivation is transferable across targets when the targets are perceived as linked, so an existing strong investment can be recruited to sustain effort on a task the subject would not otherwise sustain — the charge supplies drive that instruction alone does not. This is also why the move is high-risk: the same linkage means the task's value is now dependent on the relationship, and effort collapses when the relationship does. Falsifiable in the direction that matters: if subjects whose charge was explicitly redirected onto the work show no better task engagement than matched subjects where the charge was simply managed and set aside, the redirection is doing nothing and the entry is describing ordinary rapport. Second and more important test: if such subjects show equal task persistence after the operator relationship ends, then the work was never running on the charge and the dependency worry is misplaced. Consent and bounding are flagged because redirecting an attachment the subject did not choose to form, without naming that this is happening, converts an unbidden bond into leverage. [plausible; motivational transfer to associated goals; the historical clinical construct of working with transference, whose specific claims are not independently established]


**Worked examples.**

- *Unbidden intensity named, then pointed at the task*
  - **Setup.** Several sessions in; a strong attachment the operator did not build has formed and is derailing sessions — the subject is preoccupied with the operator's approval rather than with the material.
  - **The move.** Something has got very strong between us, and I didn't build it and neither of us asked for it. I'm not going to pretend it isn't there, and I'm not going to let it eat the hour. So we're going to spend it: all of that wanting-me-to-be-pleased goes into the thing you've been walking around for three weeks. Do that piece now, out loud — and yes, do it for me, because that's what currently has fuel in it.
  - **Why it lands.** The charge stops being an obstacle and becomes the engine, so the intensity that was derailing sessions is what now sustains them. The operator must first verify the charge is unbidden — the check is that nothing in their own conduct engineered stake or debt — since misreading a manufactured attachment as spontaneous is the named failure; the operator's own investment gets named rather than assumed neutral.


<a id="entry-1394"></a>

### staged-compromise-evidence-banking

[#1394](#entry-1394) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

A scene is arranged so that it generates a durable, compromising artifact — a photograph, a recording, a signed statement, a witnessed act — which the operator retains without using. Nothing is cashed at the time; the subject's experience of the scene is often unremarkable, and the coercive function activates only later, on the first refusal, when the held artifact is produced or alluded to. The staging is designed backward from the artifact: participants are positioned and the scene is shaped so the resulting record will read as maximally damaging out of context, independent of what actually occurred. Its value to the operator is the standing threat, so it works best never used.


**When to reach for this.** A durable compromising artifact (photograph, recording, signed statement, witnessed act) is generated by a staged scene, retained, and deliberately NOT used — the coercive function is a standing threat activated only on a future refusal. Two properties are jointly unmatched: the artifact is external to the subject's psychology (no state or belief change is asserted or required at the time), and the value is in holding rather than exercising. Split from `threat-of-loss-rouse` (389), the nearest lever in kind: 389 also runs on forfeiture, but its threatened asset is the subject's own future state access, it is spoken aloud, and it is cashed on the spot to break a blocked command channel — here the asset is an external record, the threat is unspoken, and cashing it spends it. Split from `precommitment-rule-governed-stakes` (424), where a third party holds a stake the SUBJECT arranged against their own future defection; here the subject did not agree and does not know a stake exists. Split from the staging cluster on timing: `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` (517) collects felt indebtedness the moment the operator returns, `context-lock-staging` (243) gates a payload in the same session, and `counterfeit-cue-forgery` (493) collapses on detection — this one is designed to be detected later, deliberately.


**Why it works.** The operative asset is asymmetric information about reputational exposure, and the standing-threat structure is what gives it force: an unexercised threat retains its full value while an exercised one is spent, which is why holding is rational for the coercer and why the target's compliance can be sustained indefinitely without any further action. Decontextualization does the rest — records of intimate or transgressive acts are read by outside audiences without the framing that made them ordinary, so the artifact's damage is largely independent of what the scene actually was. Falsifiable: if compliance rates under a held-but-unused artifact matched those with no artifact, the banking does nothing; and if targets who knew the artifact existed complied at the same rate as those who did not, the mechanism is not the threat but something else in the scene. Note this is a game-theoretic and social account, not a psychological state claim — no state change in the subject is asserted or required. [established; standing-threat leverage under asymmetric information; decontextualized-record reputational harm]


**Worked examples.**

- *Scene shaped backward from the artifact, banked unspoken, alluded to on first refusal*
  - **Setup.** A scene staged so the resulting record will read badly out of context — the camera already placed at the angle that crops the context out — and then, weeks later, the subject declines something for the first time.
  - **The move.** In the scene: "Kneel with your face up toward the lamp and say your full name and the date, clearly, for me." Weeks later, on the refusal: "That's fine, you can say no. I still have the clip from the lamp night on the drive — the one with your name in it. I've never done anything with it. Think about it and get back to me tomorrow."
  - **Why it lands.** At the time the scene is unremarkable to the subject, so nothing is defended against; the leverage is an external record rather than any belief, and its power comes from being held rather than spent. Observable on the refusal: the subject stops arguing about the request itself and starts negotiating about the artifact — asking where it is, who has seen it, what would make it go away.


<a id="entry-768"></a>

### stakeholder-obligation-bond

[#768](#entry-768) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: persistence*

Declares the operator's and listener's pleasure 'locked together in a sexy bond of dominance and submission', installing the operator as a personal stakeholder in the listener's compliance. Because the listener's pleasure is now also the operator's, refusing the behavioral program is reframed as refusing-to-please-her — a parasocial obligation layer that adds a relational cost (disappointing the operator) on top of the behavioral install, reinforcing it.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the stakeholder framing (her pleasure is bound to yours) that adds a relational obligation to comply, not a conditioned trigger and not a possession claim.


**Risk.** Adds a durable relational cost to non-compliance (obligation to please the operator) but is bounded and does not erode the refusal channel directly; medium.


**Why it works.** Once compliance is framed as pleasing a specific person rather than following an instruction, refusal is re-priced as a relational act with an interpersonal cost, and people avoid disappointing a valued other more reliably than they avoid breaking an abstract rule. Parasocial bonds recruit the same obligation machinery as reciprocal ones despite being one-directional, which is why a recorded operator can still function as a stakeholder. Falsifiable: if listeners complied at the same rate whether or not the operator's pleasure was declared contingent on their behaviour, the relational-cost account fails. [plausible; parasocial obligation; compliance framed as interpersonal cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *Her pleasure bound to yours as obligation*
  - **Setup.** Assigning a between-sessions routine; rapport established and the subject already values the operator's approval.
  - **The move.** Your pleasure and mine are tied together now — when it's good for you it's good for me, and that's the arrangement from here on. So the ten minutes I've set you every night isn't a chore on a list. It's the thing I'm waiting for, and I'll know the nights it doesn't come.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator declares the two of them wired together: what you feel and what I feel are tied now, she tells the listener — when it is good for you it is good for me, and that is the arrangement. From that point the program is no longer only a set of instructions: skipping it is not laziness but letting her down, and every completed step is a small gift she is waiting for.


**See also.** `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both re-route reinforcement toward the operator, one by re-sourcing the subject's own pleasure to the operator and the other by binding the two parties' pleasure so refusal becomes a relational failure. The second reads as a relational-obligation neighbor of the first's reward-rerouting lever.


<a id="entry-581"></a>

### stakeholder-set-success-threshold

[#581](#entry-581) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: safety*

Success criteria for an intervention are set by the affected parties, not the operator: before the work, the people who must live with the behavior define how much change counts as 'enough'; after the work, a second-order check verifies that the original real-world reason for targeting the behavior actually changed (is anyone safer, do people interact differently) rather than a proxy metric moving. The operator is structurally barred from declaring victory on a self-chosen measure — the authority to define and confirm success lives outside the operator, and a metric-only win is disallowed.


**When to reach for this.** Recipe governance test 'who is constrained after the move runs?': the OPERATOR (cannot self-certify success), so positive governance, not consent-manufacture (which erodes the refusal channel). vs operator-side-craft: craft procedures sharpen the operator's own knowledge/measurement/conduct while leaving authority with the operator; here the threshold-setting authority is RELOCATED to stakeholders — license narrowed, not sharpened. vs a post-hoc satisfaction survey: the threshold is set BEFORE the intervention and re-checked against the original real-world reason.


**Risk.** Protective, license-narrowing move: it constrains the operator and hands verification to affected parties ('a metric-only win is disallowed'; success confirmed outside the operator).


**Why it works.** The operator has both an incentive and an unconscious bias toward declaring success, and can satisfy any self-chosen metric by choosing a metric that will move — the standard proxy-gaming failure in which an indicator ceases to be a good measure once it becomes a target. Relocating threshold-setting to the affected parties, and fixing the threshold before the intervention, removes both degrees of freedom: the operator can no longer pick the goalpost or move it afterwards. Falsifiable: if pre-registered stakeholder thresholds are met at the same rate as operator-chosen ones, and if outcomes on the original real-world concern track proxy movement equally either way, the relocation buys nothing. [plausible; Goodhart's law / proxy gaming; pre-registration against post-hoc goalpost movement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Those who live with the behavior set the bar*
  - "the answer is most likely to come from the people who must deal with the behavior; they should be asked" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `experiential-consent-trial` — a pair worth reading together as two placements of the same governance bar: both strip the operator of unilateral go/no-go, one by relocating the definition of success to the people who must live with the result and re-checking it against the real-world reason, the other by blocking the install until the subject has lived the experience and can abort. One constrains what counts as done, the other what is allowed to start.


<a id="entry-1439"></a>

### suggestion-built-restraint

[#1439](#entry-1439) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: immersion*

Manufactures felt bondage from suggestion alone, with agency transfer rather than pleasure as the payload. One delivery accretes the restraint site by site — ropes narrated at wrists, then ankles, then waist, each "tightening," "securing," "locking in place" — so each step is small and acceptable, then arms it with a struggle-amplifier (trying to get free makes the ropes tighter) and a sole-release-by-operator-permission clause. The other delivery inserts the restraint covertly while attention is saturated by a pleasure flood, narrating the ropes as already present and attributing the non-noticing to depth ("Your mind is just too far gone"), so the listener experiences the bondage as something that happened to them retroactively. Both routes yield the same product: hallucinated physical helplessness whose locus of control sits entirely with the operator, in which struggling or failing to notice confirms the frame instead of breaking it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script builds physical restraint out of narration alone and uses it to hand bodily agency to the operator. The tell is ropes or bindings that exist only in the telling, paired with a struggle-makes-it-tighter clause, a release-only-by-permission clause, or a retroactive "you didn't even notice being tied" framing.


**Worked examples.**

- *struggle-amplifier with permission-gated release*
  - you could try to struggle against these ropes to get free, but the more you struggle, the tighter the ropes only get... the only way you can be released, is by me granting permission


**See also.** `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — shares the immobility-as-agency-transfer axis, where a delivered inability to move is recoded as the operator's ownership or control.; `manufactured-resistance-theater` — shares the narrated-struggle axis, where the script performs the listener's resistance against a constructed restraint for them.; `motor-inhibition-convincer` — shares the suggested-motor-incapacity axis, where an inability to move is installed and then demonstrated to the listener.


<a id="entry-1400"></a>

### suppression-banked-past-zero

[#1400](#entry-1400) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

Once a starved cue has stopped producing any visible response, continuing to run the extinction keeps depositing suppression that has no in-the-moment observable at all — the response is already at floor, so the meter cannot move and every additional trial looks identical to the last.
